views.lean_signature: theorem Finsupp.prod_add_index' [AddZeroClass M] [CommMonoid N] {f g : α →₀ M} {h : α → M → N} (h_zero : ∀ a, h a 0 = 1) (h_add : ∀ a b₁ b₂, h a (b₁ + b₂) = h a b₁ * h a b₂) : (f + g).prod h = f.prod h * g.prod h

views.nl_informal:
For disjoint `f1` and `f2`, and function `g`, the product of the products of `g`
over `f1` and `f2` equals the product of `g` over `f1 + f2`
views.lean_signature: theorem Finsupp.prod_add_index_of_disjoint [AddCommMonoid M] {f1 f2 : α →₀ M} (hd : Disjoint f1.support f2.support) {β : Type*} [CommMonoid β] (g : α → M → β) : (f1 + f2).prod g = f1.prod g * f2.prod g

views.nl_informal: If `0 : ℕ` is not in the support of `f : ℕ →₀ ℕ` then `0 < ∏ x ∈ f.support, x ^ (f x)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.prod_pow_pos_of_zero_not_mem_support {f : ℕ →₀ ℕ} (nhf : 0 ∉ f.support) : 0 < f.prod (· ^ ·)

views.nl_informal:
The product of `f` over `insert a s` is the same as
the product over `s`, as long as `a` is in `s` or `f a = 1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_insert_of_eq_one_if_not_mem [DecidableEq ι] (h : a ∉ s → f a = 1) : ∏ x ∈ insert a s, f x = ∏ x ∈ s, f x

views.nl_informal:
The product of `f` over `insert a s` is the same as
the product over `s`, as long as `f a = 1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_insert_one [DecidableEq ι] (h : f a = 1) : ∏ x ∈ insert a s, f x = ∏ x ∈ s, f x

views.nl_informal: In a monoid whose only unit is `1`, a product is equal to `1` iff all factors are `1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_eq_one_iff [Subsingleton Mˣ] : ∏ i ∈ s, f i = 1 ↔ ∀ i ∈ s, f i = 1

views.nl_informal:
Multiplying the products of a function over `s` and over `sᶜ` gives the whole product.
For a version expressed with subtypes, see `Fintype.prod_subtype_mul_prod_subtype`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_mul_prod_compl [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (s : Finset ι) (f : ι → M) : (∏ i ∈ s, f i) * ∏ i ∈ sᶜ, f i = ∏ i, f i

views.nl_informal:
The products of two functions `f g : ι → M` over finite sets `s₁ s₂ : Finset ι`
are equal if the functions agree on `s₁ ∩ s₂`, `f = 1` and `g = 1` on the respective
set differences.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_congr_of_eq_on_inter {ι M : Type*} {s₁ s₂ : Finset ι} {f g : ι → M} [CommMonoid M] (h₁ : ∀ a ∈ s₁, a ∉ s₂ → f a = 1) (h₂ : ∀ a ∈ s₂, a ∉ s₁ → g a = 1) (h : ∀ a ∈ s₁, a ∈ s₂ → f a = g a) : ∏ a ∈ s₁, f a = ∏ a ∈ s₂, g a

views.nl_informal: A product over `s.subtype p` equals one over `{x ∈ s | p x}`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_subtype_eq_prod_filter (f : ι → M) {p : ι → Prop} [DecidablePred p] : ∏ x ∈ s.subtype p, f x = ∏ x ∈ s with p x, f x

views.nl_informal:
If all elements of a `Finset` satisfy the predicate `p`, a product
over `s.subtype p` equals that product over `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_subtype_of_mem (f : ι → M) {p : ι → Prop} [DecidablePred p] (h : ∀ x ∈ s, p x) : ∏ x ∈ s.subtype p, f x = ∏ x ∈ s, f x

views.nl_informal:
A product of a function over a `Finset` in a subtype equals a
product in the main type of a function that agrees with the first
function on that `Finset`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_subtype_map_embedding {p : ι → Prop} {s : Finset { x // p x }} {f : { x // p x } → M} {g : ι → M} (h : ∀ x : { x // p x }, x ∈ s → g x = f x) : (∏ x ∈ s.map (Function.Embedding.subtype _), g x) = ∏ x ∈ s, f x

views.nl_informal:
The product of a function `g` defined only on a set `s` is equal to
the product of a function `f` defined everywhere,
as long as `f` and `g` agree on `s`, and `f = 1` off `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_congr_set [Fintype ι] (s : Set ι) [DecidablePred (· ∈ s)] (f : ι → M) (g : s → M) (w : ∀ x (hx : x ∈ s), f x = g ⟨x, hx⟩) (w' : ∀ x ∉ s, f x = 1) : ∏ i, f i = ∏ i, g i

views.nl_informal:
For any product along `{0, ..., n - 1}` of a commutative-monoid-valued function, we can verify
that it's equal to a different function just by checking ratios of adjacent terms.

This is a multiplicative discrete analogue of the fundamental theorem of calculus.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_range_induction (f s : ℕ → M) (base : s 0 = 1) (step : ∀ n, s (n + 1) = s n * f n) (n : ℕ) : ∏ k ∈ Finset.range n, f k = s n

views.nl_informal:
The product of the composition of functions `f` and `g`, is the product over `b ∈ s.image g` of
`f b` to the power of the cardinality of the fibre of `b`. See also `Finset.prod_image`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_comp [DecidableEq κ] (f : κ → M) (g : ι → κ) : ∏ a ∈ s, f (g a) = ∏ b ∈ s.image g, f b ^ #{a ∈ s | g a = b}

views.nl_informal: A product can be partitioned into a product of products, each equivalent under a setoid.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_partition (R : Setoid ι) [DecidableRel R.r] : ∏ x ∈ s, f x = ∏ xbar ∈ s.image (Quotient.mk _), ∏ y ∈ s with ⟦y⟧ = xbar, f y

views.nl_informal: If we can partition a product into subsets that cancel out, then the whole product cancels.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_cancels_of_partition_cancels (R : Setoid ι) [DecidableRel R] (h : ∀ x ∈ s, ∏ a ∈ s with R a x, f a = 1) : ∏ x ∈ s, f x = 1

views.nl_informal:
If a product of a `Finset` of size at most 1 has a given value, so
do the terms in that product.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.eq_of_card_le_one_of_prod_eq {s : Finset ι} (hc : #s ≤ 1) {f : ι → M} {b : M} (h : ∏ x ∈ s, f x = b) : ∀ x ∈ s, f x = b

views.nl_informal:
Taking a product over `s : Finset ι` is the same as multiplying the value on a single element
`f a` by the product of `s.erase a`.

See `Multiset.prod_map_erase` for the `Multiset` version.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.mul_prod_erase [DecidableEq ι] (s : Finset ι) (f : ι → M) {a : ι} (h : a ∈ s) : (f a * ∏ x ∈ s.erase a, f x) = ∏ x ∈ s, f x

views.nl_informal:
If a function applied at a point is 1, a product is unchanged by
removing that point, if present, from a `Finset`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_erase [DecidableEq ι] (s : Finset ι) {f : ι → M} {a : ι} (h : f a = 1) : ∏ x ∈ s.erase a, f x = ∏ x ∈ s, f x

views.nl_informal:
If a product is 1 and the function is 1 except possibly at one
point, it is 1 everywhere on the `Finset`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.eq_one_of_prod_eq_one {s : Finset ι} {f : ι → M} {a : ι} (hp : ∏ x ∈ s, f x = 1) (h1 : ∀ x ∈ s, x ≠ a → f x = 1) : ∀ x ∈ s, f x = 1

views.nl_informal:
A telescoping product along `{0, ..., n - 1}` of a commutative group valued function reduces to
the ratio of the last and first factors.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_range_div (f : ℕ → G) (n : ℕ) : (∏ i ∈ range n, f (i + 1) / f i) = f n / f 0

views.nl_informal:
A telescoping sum along `{0, ..., n-1}` of an `ℕ`-valued function reduces to the difference of
the last and first terms when the function we are summing is monotone.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.sum_range_tsub {f : ℕ → M} (h : Monotone f) (n : ℕ) : ∑ i ∈ range n, (f (i + 1) - f i) = f n - f 0

views.nl_informal:
Reorder a product.

The difference with `Finset.prod_bij'` is that the bijection is specified as a surjective injection,
rather than by an inverse function.

The difference with `Finset.prod_nbij` is that the bijection is allowed to use membership of the
domain of the product, rather than being a non-dependent function.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_bij (i : ∀ a ∈ s, κ) (hi : ∀ a ha, i a ha ∈ t) (i_inj : ∀ a₁ ha₁ a₂ ha₂, i a₁ ha₁ = i a₂ ha₂ → a₁ = a₂) (i_surj : ∀ b ∈ t, ∃ a ha, i a ha = b) (h : ∀ a ha, f a = g (i a ha)) : ∏ x ∈ s, f x = ∏ x ∈ t, g x

views.nl_informal:
Reorder a product.

The difference with `Finset.prod_bij` is that the bijection is specified with an inverse, rather
than as a surjective injection.

The difference with `Finset.prod_nbij'` is that the bijection and its inverse are allowed to use
membership of the domains of the products, rather than being non-dependent functions.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_bij' (i : ∀ a ∈ s, κ) (j : ∀ a ∈ t, ι) (hi : ∀ a ha, i a ha ∈ t) (hj : ∀ a ha, j a ha ∈ s) (left_inv : ∀ a ha, j (i a ha) (hi a ha) = a) (right_inv : ∀ a ha, i (j a ha) (hj a ha) = a) (h : ∀ a ha, f a = g (i a ha)) : ∏ x ∈ s, f x = ∏ x ∈ t, g x

views.nl_informal:
Reorder a product.

The difference with `Finset.prod_nbij'` is that the bijection is specified as a surjective
injection, rather than by an inverse function.

The difference with `Finset.prod_bij` is that the bijection is a non-dependent function, rather than
being allowed to use membership of the domain of the product.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_nbij (i : ι → κ) (hi : ∀ a ∈ s, i a ∈ t) (i_inj : (s : Set ι).InjOn i) (i_surj : (s : Set ι).SurjOn i t) (h : ∀ a ∈ s, f a = g (i a)) : ∏ x ∈ s, f x = ∏ x ∈ t, g x

views.nl_informal:
Reorder a product.

The difference with `Finset.prod_nbij` is that the bijection is specified with an inverse, rather
than as a surjective injection.

The difference with `Finset.prod_bij'` is that the bijection and its inverse are non-dependent
functions, rather than being allowed to use membership of the domains of the products.

The difference with `Finset.prod_equiv` is that bijectivity is only required to hold on the domains
of the products, rather than on the entire types.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_nbij' (i : ι → κ) (j : κ → ι) (hi : ∀ a ∈ s, i a ∈ t) (hj : ∀ a ∈ t, j a ∈ s) (left_inv : ∀ a ∈ s, j (i a) = a) (right_inv : ∀ a ∈ t, i (j a) = a) (h : ∀ a ∈ s, f a = g (i a)) : ∏ x ∈ s, f x = ∏ x ∈ t, g x

views.nl_informal:
To prove a property of a product, it suffices to prove that
the property is multiplicative and holds on factors.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_induction {M : Type*} [CommMonoid M] (f : α → M) (p : M → Prop) (hom : ∀ a b, p a → p b → p (a * b)) (unit : p 1) (base : ∀ x ∈ s, p <| f x) : p <| ∏ x ∈ s, f x

views.nl_informal:
To prove a property of a product, it suffices to prove that
the property is multiplicative and holds on factors.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_induction_nonempty {M : Type*} [CommMonoid M] (f : α → M) (p : M → Prop) (hom : ∀ a b, p a → p b → p (a * b)) (nonempty : s.Nonempty) (base : ∀ x ∈ s, p <| f x) : p <| ∏ x ∈ s, f x

views.nl_informal: Moving to the opposite additive commutative monoid commutes with summing.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.op_sum [AddCommMonoid β] {s : Finset α} (f : α → β) : op (∑ x ∈ s, f x) = ∑ x ∈ s, op (f x)

views.nl_informal:
Consider a product of `g i (f i)` over a finset.  Suppose `g` is a function such as
`n ↦ (· ^ n)`, which maps a second argument of `1` to `1`. Then if `f` is replaced by the
corresponding multiplicative indicator function, the finset may be replaced by a possibly larger
finset without changing the value of the product.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_mulIndicator_subset_of_eq_one [One α] (f : ι → α) (g : ι → α → β) {s t : Finset ι} (h : s ⊆ t) (hg : ∀ a, g a 1 = 1) : ∏ i ∈ t, g i (mulIndicator ↑s f i) = ∏ i ∈ s, g i (f i)

views.nl_informal:
Taking the product of an indicator function over a possibly larger finset is the same as
taking the original function over the original finset.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_mulIndicator_subset (f : ι → β) {s t : Finset ι} (h : s ⊆ t) : ∏ i ∈ t, mulIndicator (↑s) f i = ∏ i ∈ s, f i

views.nl_informal:
Taking a product over `univ.pi t` is the same as taking the product over `Fintype.piFinset t`.
`univ.pi t` and `Fintype.piFinset t` are essentially the same `Finset`, but differ
in the type of their element, `univ.pi t` is a `Finset (Π a ∈ univ, t a)` and
`Fintype.piFinset t` is a `Finset (Π a, t a)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_univ_pi [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι] {κ : ι → Type*} (t : ∀ i, Finset (κ i)) (f : (∀ i ∈ (univ : Finset ι), κ i) → β) : ∏ x ∈ univ.pi t, f x = ∏ x ∈ Fintype.piFinset t, f fun a _ ↦ x a

views.nl_informal:
A product taken over a conditional whose condition is an equality test on the index and whose
alternative is `1` has value either the term at that index or `1`.

The difference with `Finset.prod_ite_eq` is that the arguments to `Eq` are swapped.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_ite_eq' [DecidableEq α] (s : Finset α) (a : α) (b : α → β) : (∏ x ∈ s, ite (x = a) (b x) 1) = ite (a ∈ s) (b a) 1

views.nl_informal:
A product over all subsets of `s ∪ {x}` is obtained by multiplying the product over all subsets
of `s`, and over all subsets of `s` to which one adds `x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_powerset_insert [DecidableEq α] (ha : a ∉ s) (f : Finset α → β) : ∏ t ∈ (insert a s).powerset, f t = (∏ t ∈ s.powerset, f t) * ∏ t ∈ s.powerset, f (insert a t)

views.nl_informal:
A product over all subsets of `s ∪ {x}` is obtained by multiplying the product over all subsets
of `s`, and over all subsets of `s` to which one adds `x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_powerset_cons (ha : a ∉ s) (f : Finset α → β) : ∏ t ∈ (s.cons a ha).powerset, f t = (∏ t ∈ s.powerset, f t) * ∏ t ∈ s.powerset.attach, f (cons a t <| not_mem_mono (mem_powerset.1 t.2) ha)

views.nl_informal:
A product over `powerset s` is equal to the double product over sets of subsets of `s` with
`#s = k`, for `k = 1, ..., #s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_powerset (s : Finset α) (f : Finset α → β) : ∏ t ∈ powerset s, f t = ∏ j ∈ range (#s + 1), ∏ t ∈ powersetCard j s, f t

views.nl_informal: A product over `Finset.powersetCard` which only depends on the size of the sets is constant.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_powersetCard (n : ℕ) (s : Finset α) (f : ℕ → β) : ∏ t ∈ powersetCard n s, f #t = f n ^ (#s).choose n

views.nl_informal:
The product over a sigma type equals the product of the fiberwise products.
For rewriting in the reverse direction, use `Finset.prod_sigma'`.

See also `Fintype.prod_sigma` for the product over the whole type.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_sigma {σ : α → Type*} (s : Finset α) (t : ∀ a, Finset (σ a)) (f : Sigma σ → β) : ∏ x ∈ s.sigma t, f x = ∏ a ∈ s, ∏ s ∈ t a, f ⟨a, s⟩

views.nl_informal:
The product over a sigma type equals the product of the fiberwise products. For rewriting
in the reverse direction, use `Finset.prod_sigma`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_sigma' {σ : α → Type*} (s : Finset α) (t : ∀ a, Finset (σ a)) (f : ∀ a, σ a → β) : (∏ a ∈ s, ∏ s ∈ t a, f a s) = ∏ x ∈ s.sigma t, f x.1 x.2

views.nl_informal:
The product over a product set equals the product of the fiberwise products. For rewriting
in the reverse direction, use `Finset.prod_product'`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_product (s : Finset γ) (t : Finset α) (f : γ × α → β) : ∏ x ∈ s ×ˢ t, f x = ∏ x ∈ s, ∏ y ∈ t, f (x, y)

views.nl_informal:
The product over a product set equals the product of the fiberwise products. For rewriting
in the reverse direction, use `Finset.prod_product`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_product' (s : Finset γ) (t : Finset α) (f : γ → α → β) : ∏ x ∈ s ×ˢ t, f x.1 x.2 = ∏ x ∈ s, ∏ y ∈ t, f x y

views.nl_informal: Cyclically permute 3 nested instances of `Finset.prod`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_comm_cycle {s : Finset γ} {t : Finset α} {u : Finset κ} {f : γ → α → κ → β} : (∏ x ∈ s, ∏ y ∈ t, ∏ z ∈ u, f x y z) = ∏ z ∈ u, ∏ x ∈ s, ∏ y ∈ t, f x y z

views.nl_informal: A list with product not one must have positive length.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.length_pos_of_prod_ne_one (L : List M) (h : L.prod ≠ 1) : 0 < L.length

views.nl_informal: A list with product greater than one must have positive length.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.length_pos_of_one_lt_prod [Preorder M] (L : List M) (h : 1 < L.prod) : 0 < L.length

views.nl_informal: A list with product less than one must have positive length.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.length_pos_of_prod_lt_one [Preorder M] (L : List M) (h : L.prod < 1) : 0 < L.length

views.nl_informal:
We'd like to state this as `L.headI * L.tail.prod = L.prod`, but because `L.headI` relies on an
inhabited instance to return a garbage value on the empty list, this is not possible.
Instead, we write the statement in terms of `L[0]?.getD 1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.getElem?_zero_mul_tail_prod (l : List M) : l[0]?.getD 1 * l.tail.prod = l.prod

views.nl_informal: Cancellation of a telescoping product.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.prod_range_div' (n : ℕ) (f : ℕ → G) : ((range n).map fun k ↦ f k / f (k + 1)).prod = f 0 / f n

views.nl_informal: Cancellation of a telescoping product.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.prod_range_div (n : ℕ) (f : ℕ → G) : ((range n).map fun k ↦ f (k + 1) / f k).prod = f n / f 0

views.nl_informal:
In a flatten, taking the first elements up to an index which is the sum of the lengths of the
first `i` sublists, is the same as taking the flatten of the first `i` sublists.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.take_sum_flatten (L : List (List α)) (i : ℕ) : L.flatten.take ((L.map length).take i).sum = (L.take i).flatten

views.nl_informal:
In a flatten, dropping all the elements up to an index which is the sum of the lengths of the
first `i` sublists, is the same as taking the join after dropping the first `i` sublists.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.drop_sum_flatten (L : List (List α)) (i : ℕ) : L.flatten.drop ((L.map length).take i).sum = (L.drop i).flatten

views.nl_informal:
If all elements in a list are bounded below by `1`, then the length of the list is bounded
by the sum of the elements.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.length_le_sum_of_one_le (L : List ℕ) (h : ∀ i ∈ L, 1 ≤ i) : L.length ≤ L.sum

views.nl_informal:
If elements of a list commute with each other, then their product does not
depend on the order of elements.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Perm.prod_eq' (h : l₁ ~ l₂) (hc : l₁.Pairwise Commute) : l₁.prod = l₂.prod

views.nl_informal: Summing the count of `x` over a list filtered by some `p` is just `countP` applied to `p`
views.lean_signature: theorem List.sum_map_count_dedup_filter_eq_countP (p : α → Bool) (l : List α) : ((l.dedup.filter p).map fun x => l.count x).sum = l.countP p

views.nl_informal: The members of `l.ranges` have no duplicate
views.lean_signature: theorem List.ranges_nodup {l s : List ℕ} (hs : s ∈ ranges l) : s.Nodup

views.nl_informal: Any entry of any member of `l.ranges` is strictly smaller than `l.sum`.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.mem_mem_ranges_iff_lt_sum (l : List ℕ) {n : ℕ} : (∃ s ∈ l.ranges, n ∈ s) ↔ n < l.sum

views.nl_informal:
In a flatten of sublists, taking the slice between the indices `A` and `B - 1` gives back the
original sublist of index `i` if `A` is the sum of the lengths of sublists of index `< i`, and
`B` is the sum of the lengths of sublists of index `≤ i`.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.drop_take_succ_flatten_eq_getElem (L : List (List α)) (i : Nat) (h : i < L.length) : (L.flatten.take ((L.map length).take (i + 1)).sum).drop ((L.map length).take i).sum = L[i]

views.nl_informal: If a product of integers is `-1`, then at least one factor must be `-1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.neg_one_mem_of_prod_eq_neg_one {l : List ℤ} (h : l.prod = -1) : (-1 : ℤ) ∈ l

views.nl_informal: A morphism into the opposite monoid acts on the product by acting on the reversed elements.
views.lean_signature: theorem unop_map_list_prod {F : Type*} [FunLike F M Nᵐᵒᵖ] [MonoidHomClass F M Nᵐᵒᵖ] (f : F) (l : List M) : (f l.prod).unop = (l.map (MulOpposite.unop ∘ f)).reverse.prod

views.nl_informal:
If `f = g = h` everywhere but at `i`, where `f i = g i + h i`, then the product of `f` over `s`
is the sum of the products of `g` and `h`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_add_prod_eq {s : Finset ι} {i : ι} {f g h : ι → α} (hi : i ∈ s) (h1 : g i + h i = f i) (h2 : ∀ j ∈ s, j ≠ i → g j = f j) (h3 : ∀ j ∈ s, j ≠ i → h j = f j) : (∏ i ∈ s, g i) + ∏ i ∈ s, h i = ∏ i ∈ s, f i

views.nl_informal:
The product over a sum can be written as a sum over the product of sets, `Finset.Pi`.
`Finset.prod_univ_sum` is an alternative statement when the product is over `univ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_sum (s : Finset ι) (t : ∀ i, Finset (κ i)) (f : ∀ i, κ i → α) : ∏ a ∈ s, ∑ b ∈ t a, f a b = ∑ p ∈ s.pi t, ∏ x ∈ s.attach, f x.1 (p x.1 x.2)

views.nl_informal:
The product over `univ` of a sum can be written as a sum over the product of sets,
`Fintype.piFinset`. `Finset.prod_sum` is an alternative statement when the product is not
over `univ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_univ_sum [Fintype ι] (t : ∀ i, Finset (κ i)) (f : ∀ i, κ i → α) : ∏ i, ∑ j ∈ t i, f i j = ∑ x ∈ piFinset t, ∏ i, f i (x i)

views.nl_informal:
The product of `f a + g a` over all of `s` is the sum over the powerset of `s` of the product of
`f` over a subset `t` times the product of `g` over the complement of `t`
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_add (f g : ι → α) (s : Finset ι) : ∏ i ∈ s, (f i + g i) = ∑ t ∈ s.powerset, (∏ i ∈ t, f i) * ∏ i ∈ s \ t, g i

views.nl_informal: `∏ i, (f i + g i) = (∏ i, f i) + ∑ i, g i * (∏ j < i, f j + g j) * (∏ j > i, f j)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_add_ordered [LinearOrder ι] (s : Finset ι) (f g : ι → α) : ∏ i ∈ s, (f i + g i) = (∏ i ∈ s, f i) + ∑ i ∈ s, g i * (∏ j ∈ s with j < i, (f j + g j)) * ∏ j ∈ s with i < j, f j

views.nl_informal:
Summing `a ^ #t * b ^ (n - #t)` over all finite subsets `t` of a finset `s`
gives `(a + b) ^ #s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.sum_pow_mul_eq_add_pow (a b : α) (s : Finset ι) : (∑ t ∈ s.powerset, a ^ #t * b ^ (#s - #t)) = (a + b) ^ #s

views.nl_informal:
Summing `a^#s * b^(n-#s)` over all finite subsets `s` of a fintype of cardinality `n`
gives `(a + b)^n`. The "good" proof involves expanding along all coordinates using the fact that
`x^n` is multilinear, but multilinear maps are only available now over rings, so we give instead
a proof reducing to the usual binomial theorem to have a result over semirings.
views.lean_signature: theorem Fintype.sum_pow_mul_eq_add_pow (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] (a b : α) : ∑ s : Finset ι, a ^ #s * b ^ (Fintype.card ι - #s) = (a + b) ^ Fintype.card ι

views.nl_informal:
The product of `f i - g i` over all of `s` is the sum over the powerset of `s` of the product of
`g` over a subset `t` times the product of `f` over the complement of `t` times `(-1) ^ #t`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_sub [DecidableEq ι] (f g : ι → α) (s : Finset ι) : ∏ i ∈ s, (f i - g i) = ∑ t ∈ s.powerset, (-1) ^ #t * (∏ i ∈ s \ t, f i) * ∏ i ∈ t, g i

views.nl_informal: `∏ i, (f i - g i) = (∏ i, f i) - ∑ i, g i * (∏ j < i, f j - g j) * (∏ j > i, f j)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_sub_ordered [LinearOrder ι] (s : Finset ι) (f g : ι → α) : ∏ i ∈ s, (f i - g i) = (∏ i ∈ s, f i) - ∑ i ∈ s, g i * (∏ j ∈ s with j < i, (f j - g j)) * ∏ j ∈ s with i < j, f j

views.nl_informal:
`∏ i, (1 - f i) = 1 - ∑ i, f i * (∏ j < i, 1 - f j)`. This formula is useful in construction of
a partition of unity from a collection of “bump” functions.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.prod_one_sub_ordered [LinearOrder ι] (s : Finset ι) (f : ι → α) : ∏ i ∈ s, (1 - f i) = 1 - ∑ i ∈ s, f i * ∏ j ∈ s with j < i, (1 - f j)

views.nl_informal: A product of sums can be written as a sum of products.

views.nl_informal:
In the commutative diagram
```
             f     g
    0 --→ X₁ --→ X₂ --→ X₃
          ↑      ↑      ↑
         v|     u|     w|
          ι  → ι ⊕ ι' ← ι'
```
where the top row is an exact sequence of modules and the maps on the bottom are `Sum.inl` and
`Sum.inr`. If `u` is injective and `v` and `w` are linearly independent, then `u` is linearly
independent.
views.lean_signature: theorem ModuleCat.linearIndependent_leftExact : LinearIndependent R u

views.nl_informal:

views.lean_signature: theorem ModuleCat.linearIndependent_shortExact {w : ι' → S.X₃} (hw : LinearIndependent R w) : LinearIndependent R (Sum.elim (S.f ∘ v) (S.g.hom.toFun.invFun ∘ w))

views.nl_informal:
In the commutative diagram
```
    f     g
 X₁ --→ X₂ --→ X₃
 ↑      ↑      ↑
v|     u|     w|
 ι  → ι ⊕ ι' ← ι'
```
where the top row is an exact sequence of modules and the maps on the bottom are `Sum.inl` and
`Sum.inr`. If `v` spans `X₁` and `w` spans `X₃`, then `u` spans `X₂`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ModuleCat.span_exact {β : Type*} {u : ι ⊕ β → S.X₂} (huv : u ∘ Sum.inl = S.f ∘ v) (hv : ⊤ ≤ span R (range v)) (hw : ⊤ ≤ span R (range (S.g ∘ u ∘ Sum.inr))) : ⊤ ≤ span R (range u)

views.nl_informal:
Given an exact sequence `X₁ ⟶ X₂ ⟶ X₃ ⟶ 0` of `R`-modules and spanning

views.nl_informal:
Describes the counit of the adjunction `M ⊗ - ⊣ Hom(M, -)`. Given an `R`-module `N` this
should give a map `M ⊗ Hom(M, N) ⟶ N`, so we flip the order of the arguments in the identity map

views.nl_informal:

and two ring homs `a : S ⟶ Fᵢ` and `b : S ⟶ Fⱼ` over `R`.
If `a` and `b` agree at `S ⟶ colimit F`,
then there exists `k` such that `a` and `b` are equal at `S ⟶ F_k`.
In other words, the map `colimᵢ Hom_R(S, Fᵢ) ⟶ Hom_R(S, colim F)` is injective.

views.lean_signature: theorem algebraRat.charZero [Ring R] [Algebra ℚ R] : CharZero R

views.nl_informal: If `R` has characteristic `p`, then so does Frac(R).
views.lean_signature: theorem IsFractionRing.charP_of_isFractionRing [CharP R p] : CharP K p

views.nl_informal: If `R` has characteristic `0`, then so does Frac(R).
views.lean_signature: theorem IsFractionRing.charZero_of_isFractionRing [CharZero R] : CharZero K

views.nl_informal:
If a ring `R` is of characteristic `p`, then for any prime number `q` different from `p`,
it is not zero in `R`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CharP.cast_ne_zero_of_ne_of_prime [Nontrivial R] {p q : ℕ} [CharP R p] (hq : q.Prime) (hneq : p ≠ q) : (q : R) ≠ 0

views.nl_informal: We have `2 ≠ 0` in a nontrivial ring whose characteristic is not `2`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Ring.two_ne_zero {R : Type*} [NonAssocSemiring R] [Nontrivial R] (hR : ringChar R ≠ 2) : (2 : R) ≠ 0

views.nl_informal: Characteristic `≠ 2` and nontrivial implies that `-1 ≠ 1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Ring.neg_one_ne_one_of_char_ne_two {R : Type*} [NonAssocRing R] [Nontrivial R] (hR : ringChar R ≠ 2) : (-1 : R) ≠ 1

views.nl_informal: Characteristic `≠ 2` in a domain implies that `-a = a` iff `a = 0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Ring.eq_self_iff_eq_zero_of_char_ne_two {R : Type*} [NonAssocRing R] [Nontrivial R] [NoZeroDivisors R] (hR : ringChar R ≠ 2) {a : R} : -a = a ↔ a = 0

views.nl_informal:
If two integers from `{0, 1, -1}` result in equal elements in a ring `R`
that is nontrivial and of characteristic not `2`, then they are equal.
views.lean_signature: theorem Int.cast_injOn_of_ringChar_ne_two {R : Type*} [NonAssocRing R] [Nontrivial R] (hR : ringChar R ≠ 2) : ({0, 1, -1} : Set ℤ).InjOn ((↑) : ℤ → R)

views.nl_informal:
A prime `p` is a unit in a commutative ring `R` of nonzero characteristic iff it does not divide
the characteristic.
views.lean_signature: theorem isUnit_iff_not_dvd_char_of_ringChar_ne_zero (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hR : ringChar R ≠ 0) : IsUnit (p : R) ↔ ¬p ∣ ringChar R

views.nl_informal:
A prime `p` is a unit in a finite commutative ring `R`
iff it does not divide the characteristic.
views.lean_signature: theorem isUnit_iff_not_dvd_char (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [Finite R] : IsUnit (p : R) ↔ ¬p ∣ ringChar R

views.nl_informal:
The prime divisors of the characteristic of a finite commutative ring are exactly
the prime divisors of its cardinality.
views.lean_signature: theorem prime_dvd_char_iff_dvd_card {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [Fintype R] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] : p ∣ ringChar R ↔ p ∣ Fintype.card R

views.nl_informal:
A prime that divides the cardinality of a finite commutative ring `R`
isn't a unit in `R`.
views.lean_signature: theorem not_isUnit_prime_of_dvd_card {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [Fintype R] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hp : p ∣ Fintype.card R) : ¬IsUnit (p : R)

views.nl_informal: The characteristic is prime if it is non-zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem CharP.char_prime_of_ne_zero {p : ℕ} [CharP R p] (hp : p ≠ 0) : p.Prime

views.nl_informal: The exponential characteristic is unique.
views.lean_signature: theorem ExpChar.eq {p q : ℕ} (hp : ExpChar R p) (hq : ExpChar R q) : p = q

views.nl_informal: The exponential characteristic is one if the characteristic is zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem expChar_one_of_char_zero (q : ℕ) [hp : CharP R 0] [hq : ExpChar R q] : q = 1

views.nl_informal: The characteristic equals the exponential characteristic iff the former is prime.
views.lean_signature: theorem char_eq_expChar_iff (p q : ℕ) [hp : CharP R p] [hq : ExpChar R q] : p = q ↔ p.Prime

views.nl_informal:
The exponential characteristic is a prime number or one.
See also `CharP.char_is_prime_or_zero`.
views.lean_signature: theorem expChar_is_prime_or_one (q : ℕ) [hq : ExpChar R q] : Nat.Prime q ∨ q = 1

views.nl_informal: The exponential characteristic is positive.
views.lean_signature: theorem expChar_pos (q : ℕ) [ExpChar R q] : 0 < q

views.nl_informal: Any power of the exponential characteristic is positive.
views.lean_signature: theorem expChar_pow_pos (q : ℕ) [ExpChar R q] (n : ℕ) : 0 < q ^ n

views.nl_informal: The characteristic is zero if the exponential characteristic is one.
views.lean_signature: theorem charZero_of_expChar_one' [hq : ExpChar R 1] : CharZero R

views.nl_informal: The exponential characteristic is one iff the characteristic is zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem expChar_one_iff_char_zero (p q : ℕ) [CharP R p] [ExpChar R q] : q = 1 ↔ p = 0

views.nl_informal: The Frobenius endomorphism commutes with any ring homomorphism.
views.lean_signature: theorem RingHom.frobenius_comm : g.comp (frobenius R p) = (frobenius S p).comp g

views.nl_informal: The iterated Frobenius endomorphism commutes with any ring homomorphism.
views.lean_signature: theorem RingHom.iterateFrobenius_comm (n : ℕ) : g.comp (iterateFrobenius R p n) = (iterateFrobenius S p n).comp g

views.nl_informal: The characteristic of a finite ring cannot be zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem CharP.char_ne_zero_of_finite (p : ℕ) [CharP R p] [Finite R] : p ≠ 0

views.nl_informal:
For a commutative semiring `R` and a `R`-module `M`, if `M` contains an
element `x` that is not torsion, then the characteristic of `R` is equal to the
characteristic of the `R`-linear endomorphisms of `M`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.charP_end {p : ℕ} [hchar : CharP R p] (htorsion : ∃ x : M, Ideal.torsionOf R M x = ⊥) : CharP (M →ₗ[R] M) p

views.nl_informal: In a local ring the characteristics is either zero or a prime power.
views.lean_signature: theorem charP_zero_or_prime_power (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] (q : ℕ) [char_R_q : CharP R q] : q = 0 ∨ IsPrimePow q

views.nl_informal:
Reduction to `p` prime: When proving any statement `P` about mixed characteristic rings we
can always assume that `p` is prime.
views.lean_signature: theorem MixedCharZero.reduce_to_p_prime {P : Prop} : (∀ p > 0, MixedCharZero R p → P) ↔ ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → MixedCharZero R p → P

views.nl_informal:
Reduction to `I` prime ideal: When proving statements about mixed characteristic rings,
after we reduced to `p` prime, we can assume that the ideal `I` in the definition is maximal.
views.lean_signature: theorem MixedCharZero.reduce_to_maximal_ideal {p : ℕ} (hp : Nat.Prime p) : (∃ I : Ideal R, I ≠ ⊤ ∧ CharP (R ⧸ I) p) ↔ ∃ I : Ideal R, I.IsMaximal ∧ CharP (R ⧸ I) p

views.nl_informal: `ℚ`-algebra implies equal characteristic.
views.lean_signature: theorem EqualCharZero.of_algebraRat [Algebra ℚ R] : ∀ I : Ideal R, I ≠ ⊤ → CharZero (R ⧸ I)

views.nl_informal: Not mixed characteristic implies equal characteristic.
views.lean_signature: theorem EqualCharZero.of_not_mixedCharZero [CharZero R] (h : ∀ p > 0, ¬MixedCharZero R p) : ∀ I : Ideal R, I ≠ ⊤ → CharZero (R ⧸ I)

views.nl_informal: Equal characteristic implies not mixed characteristic.
views.lean_signature: theorem EqualCharZero.to_not_mixedCharZero (h : ∀ I : Ideal R, I ≠ ⊤ → CharZero (R ⧸ I)) : ∀ p > 0, ¬MixedCharZero R p

views.nl_informal:
A ring of characteristic zero has equal characteristic iff it does not
have mixed characteristic for any `p`.
views.lean_signature: theorem EqualCharZero.iff_not_mixedCharZero [CharZero R] : (∀ I : Ideal R, I ≠ ⊤ → CharZero (R ⧸ I)) ↔ ∀ p > 0, ¬MixedCharZero R p

views.nl_informal: A ring is a `ℚ`-algebra iff it has equal characteristic zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem EqualCharZero.nonempty_algebraRat_iff : Nonempty (Algebra ℚ R) ↔ ∀ I : Ideal R, I ≠ ⊤ → CharZero (R ⧸ I)

views.nl_informal: A ring of characteristic zero is not a `ℚ`-algebra iff it has mixed characteristic for some `p`.
views.lean_signature: theorem isEmpty_algebraRat_iff_mixedCharZero [CharZero R] : IsEmpty (Algebra ℚ R) ↔ ∃ p > 0, MixedCharZero R p

views.nl_informal: Split a `Prop` in characteristic zero into equal and mixed characteristic.
views.lean_signature: theorem split_equalCharZero_mixedCharZero [CharZero R] (h_equal : Algebra ℚ R → P) (h_mixed : ∀ p : ℕ, Nat.Prime p → MixedCharZero R p → P) : P

views.nl_informal:
Split any `Prop` over `R` into the three cases:
- positive characteristic.
- equal characteristic zero.
- mixed characteristic `(0, p)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem split_by_characteristic (h_pos : ∀ p : ℕ, p ≠ 0 → CharP R p → P) (h_equal : Algebra ℚ R → P) (h_mixed : ∀ p : ℕ, Nat.Prime p → MixedCharZero R p → P) : P

views.nl_informal:
In an `IsDomain R`, split any `Prop` over `R` into the three cases:
- *prime* characteristic.
- equal characteristic zero.
- mixed characteristic `(0, p)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem split_by_characteristic_domain [IsDomain R] (h_pos : ∀ p : ℕ, Nat.Prime p → CharP R p → P) (h_equal : Algebra ℚ R → P) (h_mixed : ∀ p : ℕ, Nat.Prime p → MixedCharZero R p → P) : P

views.nl_informal:
In a local ring `R`, split any predicate over `R` into the three cases:
- *prime power* characteristic.
- equal characteristic zero.
- mixed characteristic `(0, p)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem split_by_characteristic_localRing [IsLocalRing R] (h_pos : ∀ p : ℕ, IsPrimePow p → CharP R p → P) (h_equal : Algebra ℚ R → P) (h_mixed : ∀ p : ℕ, Nat.Prime p → MixedCharZero R p → P) : P

views.nl_informal:
If an ideal does not contain any coercions of natural numbers other than zero, then its quotient
inherits the characteristic of the underlying ring.
views.lean_signature: theorem CharP.quotient' {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (p : ℕ) [CharP R p] (I : Ideal R) (h : ∀ x : ℕ, (x : R) ∈ I → (x : R) = 0) : CharP (R ⧸ I) p

views.nl_informal:
If `ringChar R = 2`, where `R` is a finite reduced commutative ring,
then every `a : R` is a square.
views.lean_signature: theorem isSquare_of_charTwo' {R : Type*} [Finite R] [CommRing R] [IsReduced R] [CharP R 2] (a : R) : IsSquare a

views.nl_informal:
The characteristic of a division ring is equal to the characteristic
of its center
views.lean_signature: theorem CharP.charP_center_iff {R : Type u} [Ring R] {p : ℕ} : CharP (Subring.center R) p ↔ CharP R p

views.nl_informal: The only hypotheses required to build a `CharP R 2` instance are `1 ≠ 0` and `2 = 0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CharTwo.of_one_ne_zero_of_two_eq_zero (h₁ : (1 : R) ≠ 0) (h₂ : (2 : R) = 0) : CharP R 2

views.nl_informal: `z • r` is a multiple of `p` iff `r` is `pk/z` above a multiple of `p`, where `0 ≤ k < |z|`.
views.lean_signature: theorem AddSubgroup.zsmul_mem_zmultiples_iff_exists_sub_div {r : R} {z : ℤ} (hz : z ≠ 0) : z • r ∈ AddSubgroup.zmultiples p ↔ ∃ k : Fin z.natAbs, r - (k : ℕ) • (p / z : R) ∈ AddSubgroup.zmultiples p

views.nl_informal:
Every element of the direct limit corresponds to some element in
some component of the directed system.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.DirectLimit.exists_of [Nonempty ι] [IsDirected ι (· ≤ ·)] (z : DirectLimit G f) : ∃ i x, of R ι G f i x = z

views.nl_informal:
A component that corresponds to zero in the direct limit is already zero in some
bigger module in the directed system.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.DirectLimit.of.zero_exact {i x} (H : of R ι G f i x = 0) : ∃ j hij, f i j hij x = (0 : G j)

views.nl_informal:
A component that corresponds to zero in the direct limit is already zero in some
bigger module in the directed system.
views.lean_signature: theorem AddCommGroup.DirectLimit.of.zero_exact [IsDirected ι (· ≤ ·)] [DirectedSystem G fun i j h ↦ f i j h] (i x) (h : of G f i x = 0) : ∃ j hij, f i j hij x = 0

views.nl_informal:
Every element of the direct limit corresponds to some element in
some component of the directed system.
views.lean_signature: theorem Ring.DirectLimit.exists_of [Nonempty ι] [IsDirected ι (· ≤ ·)] (z : DirectLimit G f) : ∃ i x, of G f i x = z

views.nl_informal:
A component that corresponds to zero in the direct limit is already zero in some
bigger module in the directed system.
views.lean_signature: theorem Ring.DirectLimit.of.zero_exact {i x} (hix : of G (f' · · ·) i x = 0) : ∃ (j : _) (hij : i ≤ j), f' i j hij x = 0

views.nl_informal:
If the maps in the directed system are injective, then the canonical maps
from the components to the direct limits are injective.
views.lean_signature: theorem Ring.DirectLimit.of_injective [IsDirected ι (· ≤ ·)] [DirectedSystem G fun i j h ↦ f' i j h] (hf : ∀ i j hij, Function.Injective (f' i j hij)) (i) : Function.Injective (of G (fun i j h ↦ f' i j h) i)

views.nl_informal: Shows that `Aₙ = bₙ * Aₙ₋₁ + aₙ * Aₙ₋₂` and `Bₙ = bₙ * Bₙ₋₁ + aₙ * Bₙ₋₂`.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.conts_recurrence {gp ppred pred : Pair K} (succ_nth_s_eq : g.s.get? (n + 1) = some gp) (nth_conts_eq : g.conts n = ppred) (succ_nth_conts_eq : g.conts (n + 1) = pred) : g.conts (n + 2) = ⟨gp.b * pred.a + gp.a * ppred.a, gp.b * pred.b + gp.a * ppred.b⟩

views.nl_informal: Shows that `Aₙ = bₙ * Aₙ₋₁ + aₙ * Aₙ₋₂`.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.nums_recurrence {gp : Pair K} {ppredA predA : K} (succ_nth_s_eq : g.s.get? (n + 1) = some gp) (nth_num_eq : g.nums n = ppredA) (succ_nth_num_eq : g.nums (n + 1) = predA) : g.nums (n + 2) = gp.b * predA + gp.a * ppredA

views.nl_informal: Shows that `Bₙ = bₙ * Bₙ₋₁ + aₙ * Bₙ₋₂`.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.dens_recurrence {gp : Pair K} {ppredB predB : K} (succ_nth_s_eq : g.s.get? (n + 1) = some gp) (nth_den_eq : g.dens n = ppredB) (succ_nth_den_eq : g.dens (n + 1) = predB) : g.dens (n + 2) = gp.b * predB + gp.a * ppredB

views.nl_informal: If the sequence already terminated at position `n + 1`, nothing gets squashed.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.squashSeq_eq_self_of_terminated (terminatedAt_succ_n : s.TerminatedAt (n + 1)) : squashSeq s n = s

views.nl_informal:
If the sequence has not terminated before position `n + 1`, the value at `n + 1` gets
squashed into position `n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.squashSeq_nth_of_not_terminated {gp_n gp_succ_n : Pair K} (s_nth_eq : s.get? n = some gp_n) (s_succ_nth_eq : s.get? (n + 1) = some gp_succ_n) : (squashSeq s n).get? n = some ⟨gp_n.a, gp_n.b + gp_succ_n.a / gp_succ_n.b⟩

views.nl_informal: The values before the squashed position stay the same.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.squashSeq_nth_of_lt {m : ℕ} (m_lt_n : m < n) : (squashSeq s n).get? m = s.get? m

views.nl_informal:
Squashing at position `n + 1` and taking the tail is the same as squashing the tail of the
sequence at position `n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.squashSeq_succ_n_tail_eq_squashSeq_tail_n : (squashSeq s (n + 1)).tail = squashSeq s.tail n

views.nl_informal:
The auxiliary function `convs'Aux` returns the same value for a sequence and the
corresponding squashed sequence at the squashed position.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.succ_succ_nth_conv'Aux_eq_succ_nth_conv'Aux_squashSeq : convs'Aux s (n + 2) = convs'Aux (squashSeq s n) (n + 1)

views.nl_informal: If the gcf already terminated at position `n`, nothing gets squashed.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.squashGCF_eq_self_of_terminated (terminatedAt_n : TerminatedAt g n) : squashGCF g n = g

views.nl_informal: The values before the squashed position stay the same.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.squashGCF_nth_of_lt {m : ℕ} (m_lt_n : m < n) : (squashGCF g (n + 1)).s.get? m = g.s.get? m

views.nl_informal:
`convs'` returns the same value for a gcf and the corresponding squashed gcf at the
squashed position.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.succ_nth_conv'_eq_squashGCF_nth_conv' : g.convs' (n + 1) = (squashGCF g n).convs' n

views.nl_informal: The auxiliary continuants before the squashed position stay the same.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.contsAux_eq_contsAux_squashGCF_of_le {m : ℕ} : m ≤ n → contsAux g m = (squashGCF g n).contsAux m

views.nl_informal:
The convergents coincide in the expected way at the squashed position if the partial denominator
at the squashed position is not zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.succ_nth_conv_eq_squashGCF_nth_conv [Field K] (nth_partDen_ne_zero : ∀ {b : K}, g.partDens.get? n = some b → b ≠ 0) : g.convs (n + 1) = (squashGCF g n).convs n

views.nl_informal:
Shows that the recurrence relation (`convs`) and direct evaluation (`convs'`) of the
generalized continued fraction coincide at position `n` if the sequence of fractions contains
strictly positive values only.
Requiring positivity of all values is just one possible condition to obtain this result.
For example, the dual - sequences with strictly negative values only - would also work.

In practice, one most commonly deals with regular continued fractions, which satisfy the
positivity criterion required here. The analogous result for them
(see `ContFract.convs_eq_convs`) hence follows directly from this theorem.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.convs_eq_convs' [Field K] [LinearOrder K] [IsStrictOrderedRing K] (s_pos : ∀ {gp : Pair K} {m : ℕ}, m < n → g.s.get? m = some gp → 0 < gp.a ∧ 0 < gp.b) : g.convs n = g.convs' n

views.nl_informal:
Shows that the recurrence relation (`convs`) and direct evaluation (`convs'`) of a
(regular) continued fraction coincide.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContFract.convs_eq_convs' [Field K] [LinearOrder K] [IsStrictOrderedRing K] {c : ContFract K} : (↑c : GenContFract K).convs = (↑c : GenContFract K).convs'

views.nl_informal: The determinant formula `Aₙ * Bₙ₊₁ - Bₙ * Aₙ₊₁ = (-1)^(n + 1)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpContFract.determinant (not_terminatedAt_n : ¬(↑s : GenContFract K).TerminatedAt n) : (↑s : GenContFract K).nums n * (↑s : GenContFract K).dens (n + 1) - (↑s : GenContFract K).dens n * (↑s : GenContFract K).nums (n + 1) = (-1) ^ (n + 1)

views.nl_informal: If a gcf terminated at position `n`, it also terminated at `m ≥ n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.terminated_stable (n_le_m : n ≤ m) (terminatedAt_n : g.TerminatedAt n) : g.TerminatedAt m

views.nl_informal:
The recurrence relation for the convergents of the continued fraction expansion
of an element `v` of `K` in terms of the convergents of the inverse of its fractional part.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.convs_succ (n : ℕ) : (of v).convs (n + 1) = ⌊v⌋ + 1 / (of (Int.fract v)⁻¹).convs n

views.nl_informal: Shows that the fractional parts of the stream are in `[0,1)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.IntFractPair.nth_stream_fr_nonneg_lt_one {ifp_n : IntFractPair K} (nth_stream_eq : IntFractPair.stream v n = some ifp_n) : 0 ≤ ifp_n.fr ∧ ifp_n.fr < 1

views.nl_informal: Shows that the fractional parts of the stream are nonnegative.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.IntFractPair.nth_stream_fr_nonneg {ifp_n : IntFractPair K} (nth_stream_eq : IntFractPair.stream v n = some ifp_n) : 0 ≤ ifp_n.fr

views.nl_informal: Shows that the fractional parts of the stream are smaller than one.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.IntFractPair.nth_stream_fr_lt_one {ifp_n : IntFractPair K} (nth_stream_eq : IntFractPair.stream v n = some ifp_n) : ifp_n.fr < 1

views.nl_informal: Shows that the integer parts of the stream are at least one.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.IntFractPair.one_le_succ_nth_stream_b {ifp_succ_n : IntFractPair K} (succ_nth_stream_eq : IntFractPair.stream v (n + 1) = some ifp_succ_n) : 1 ≤ ifp_succ_n.b

views.nl_informal:
Shows that the `n + 1`th integer part `bₙ₊₁` of the stream is smaller or equal than the inverse of
the `n`th fractional part `frₙ` of the stream.
This result is straight-forward as `bₙ₊₁` is defined as the floor of `1 / frₙ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.IntFractPair.succ_nth_stream_b_le_nth_stream_fr_inv {ifp_n ifp_succ_n : IntFractPair K} (nth_stream_eq : IntFractPair.stream v n = some ifp_n) (succ_nth_stream_eq : IntFractPair.stream v (n + 1) = some ifp_succ_n) : (ifp_succ_n.b : K) ≤ ifp_n.fr⁻¹

views.nl_informal: Shows that the integer parts of the continued fraction are at least one.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.of_one_le_get?_partDen {b : K} (nth_partDen_eq : (of v).partDens.get? n = some b) : 1 ≤ b

views.nl_informal:
Shows that the partial numerators `aᵢ` of the continued fraction are equal to one and the partial
denominators `bᵢ` correspond to integers.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.of_partNum_eq_one_and_exists_int_partDen_eq {gp : GenContFract.Pair K} (nth_s_eq : (of v).s.get? n = some gp) : gp.a = 1 ∧ ∃ z : ℤ, gp.b = (z : K)

views.nl_informal: Shows that the partial numerators `aᵢ` are equal to one.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.of_partNum_eq_one {a : K} (nth_partNum_eq : (of v).partNums.get? n = some a) : a = 1

views.nl_informal: Shows that the partial denominators `bᵢ` correspond to an integer.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.exists_int_eq_of_partDen {b : K} (nth_partDen_eq : (of v).partDens.get? n = some b) : ∃ z : ℤ, b = (z : K)

views.nl_informal:
Shows that the `n`th denominator is greater than or equal to the `n + 1`th fibonacci number,
that is `Nat.fib (n + 1) ≤ Bₙ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.succ_nth_fib_le_of_nth_den (hyp : n = 0 ∨ ¬(of v).TerminatedAt (n - 1)) : (fib (n + 1) : K) ≤ (of v).dens n

views.nl_informal: Shows that all denominators are nonnegative.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.zero_le_of_den : 0 ≤ (of v).dens n

views.nl_informal:
Shows that `bₙ * Bₙ ≤ Bₙ₊₁`, where `bₙ` is the `n`th partial denominator and `Bₙ₊₁` and `Bₙ` are
the `n + 1`th and `n`th denominator of the continued fraction.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.le_of_succ_get?_den {b : K} (nth_partDenom_eq : (of v).partDens.get? n = some b) : b * (of v).dens n ≤ (of v).dens (n + 1)

views.nl_informal: Shows that the sequence of denominators is monotone, that is `Bₙ ≤ Bₙ₊₁`.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.of_den_mono : (of v).dens n ≤ (of v).dens (n + 1)

views.nl_informal: Shows that `|v - Aₙ / Bₙ| ≤ 1 / (Bₙ * Bₙ₊₁)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.abs_sub_convs_le (not_terminatedAt_n : ¬(of v).TerminatedAt n) : |v - (of v).convs n| ≤ 1 / ((of v).dens n * ((of v).dens <| n + 1))

views.nl_informal:
Shows that `|v - Aₙ / Bₙ| ≤ 1 / (bₙ * Bₙ * Bₙ)`. This bound is worse than the one shown in
`GenContFract.abs_sub_convs_le`, but sometimes it is easier to apply and
sufficient for one's use case.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.abs_sub_convergents_le' {b : K} (nth_partDen_eq : (of v).partDens.get? n = some b) : |v - (of v).convs n| ≤ 1 / (b * (of v).dens n * (of v).dens n)

views.nl_informal:
Shows that `IntFractPair.stream` has the sequence property, that is once we return `none` at
position `n`, we also return `none` at `n + 1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.IntFractPair.stream_isSeq (v : K) : (IntFractPair.stream v).IsSeq

views.nl_informal:
Shows the correctness of `compExactValue` in case the continued fraction
`GenContFract.of v` did not terminate at position `n`. That is, we obtain the
value `v` if we pass the two successive (auxiliary) continuants at positions `n` and `n + 1` as well
as the fractional part at `IntFractPair.stream n` to `compExactValue`.

The correctness might be seen more readily if one uses `convs'` to evaluate the continued
fraction. Here is an example to illustrate the idea:

Let `(v : ℚ) := 3.4`. We have
- `GenContFract.IntFractPair.stream v 0 = some ⟨3, 0.4⟩`, and
- `GenContFract.IntFractPair.stream v 1 = some ⟨2, 0.5⟩`.
Now `(GenContFract.of v).convs' 1 = 3 + 1/2`, and our fractional term at position `2` is `0.5`.
We hence have `v = 3 + 1/(2 + 0.5) = 3 + 1/2.5 = 3.4`.
This computation corresponds exactly to the one using the recurrence equation in `compExactValue`.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.compExactValue_correctness_of_stream_eq_some : ∀ {ifp_n : IntFractPair K}, IntFractPair.stream v n = some ifp_n → v = compExactValue ((of v).contsAux n) ((of v).contsAux <| n + 1) ifp_n.fr

views.nl_informal:
The convergent of `GenContFract.of v` at step `n - 1` is exactly `v` if the
`IntFractPair.stream` of the corresponding continued fraction terminated at step `n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.of_correctness_of_nth_stream_eq_none (nth_stream_eq_none : IntFractPair.stream v n = none) : v = (of v).convs (n - 1)

views.nl_informal: If `GenContFract.of v` terminated at step `n`, then the `n`th convergent is exactly `v`.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.of_correctness_of_terminatedAt (terminatedAt_n : (of v).TerminatedAt n) : v = (of v).convs n

views.nl_informal:
If `GenContFract.of v` terminates, then there is `n : ℕ` such that the `n`th convergent is
exactly `v`.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.of_correctness_of_terminates (terminates : (of v).Terminates) : ∃ n : ℕ, v = (of v).convs n

views.nl_informal: If `GenContFract.of v` terminates, then its convergents will eventually always be `v`.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.of_correctness_atTop_of_terminates (terminates : (of v).Terminates) : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, v = (of v).convs n

views.nl_informal: Every finite convergent corresponds to a rational number.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.exists_rat_eq_nth_conv : ∃ q : ℚ, (of v).convs n = (q : K)

views.nl_informal: Every terminating continued fraction corresponds to a rational number.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.exists_rat_eq_of_terminates (terminates : (of v).Terminates) : ∃ q : ℚ, v = ↑q

views.nl_informal: Given `(v : K), (q : ℚ), and v = q`, we have that `of q = of v`
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.coe_of_rat_eq (v_eq_q : v = (↑q : K)) : (⟨(of q).h, (of q).s.map (Pair.map (↑))⟩ : GenContFract K) = of v

views.nl_informal:
Shows that for any `q : ℚ` with `0 < q < 1`, the numerator of the fractional part of
`IntFractPair.of q⁻¹` is smaller than the numerator of `q`.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.IntFractPair.of_inv_fr_num_lt_num_of_pos (q_pos : 0 < q) : (IntFractPair.of q⁻¹).fr.num < q.num

views.nl_informal:
Shows that the sequence of numerators of the fractional parts of the stream is strictly
antitone.

views.nl_informal: The continued fraction of a rational number terminates.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.terminates_of_rat (q : ℚ) : (of q).Terminates

views.nl_informal: The continued fraction `GenContFract.of v` terminates if and only if `v ∈ ℚ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.terminates_iff_rat (v : K) : (of v).Terminates ↔ ∃ q : ℚ, v = (q : K)

views.nl_informal:
Gives a recurrence to compute the `n + 1`th value of the sequence of integer and fractional
parts of a value in case of termination.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.IntFractPair.succ_nth_stream_eq_none_iff : IntFractPair.stream v (n + 1) = none ↔ IntFractPair.stream v n = none ∨ ∃ ifp, IntFractPair.stream v n = some ifp ∧ ifp.fr = 0

views.nl_informal:
Gives a recurrence to compute the `n + 1`th value of the sequence of integer and fractional
parts of a value in case of non-termination.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.IntFractPair.succ_nth_stream_eq_some_iff {ifp_succ_n : IntFractPair K} : IntFractPair.stream v (n + 1) = some ifp_succ_n ↔ ∃ ifp_n : IntFractPair K, IntFractPair.stream v n = some ifp_n ∧ ifp_n.fr ≠ 0 ∧ IntFractPair.of ifp_n.fr⁻¹ = ifp_succ_n

views.nl_informal: The stream of `IntFractPair`s of an integer stops after the first term.

views.nl_informal:
A recurrence relation that expresses the `(n+1)`th term of the stream of `IntFractPair`s
of `v` for non-integer `v` in terms of the `n`th term of the stream associated to
the inverse of the fractional part of `v`.

views.nl_informal: The head term of the sequence with head of `v` is just the integer part of `v`.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.IntFractPair.seq1_fst_eq_of : (IntFractPair.seq1 v).fst = IntFractPair.of v

views.nl_informal: The head term of the gcf of `v` is `⌊v⌋`.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.of_h_eq_floor : (of v).h = ⌊v⌋

views.nl_informal:
Shows how the entries of the sequence of the computed continued fraction can be obtained by the
integer parts of the stream of integer and fractional parts.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.get?_of_eq_some_of_succ_get?_intFractPair_stream {ifp_succ_n : IntFractPair K} (stream_succ_nth_eq : IntFractPair.stream v (n + 1) = some ifp_succ_n) : (of v).s.get? n = some ⟨1, ifp_succ_n.b⟩

views.nl_informal:
Shows how the entries of the sequence of the computed continued fraction can be obtained by the
fractional parts of the stream of integer and fractional parts.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.get?_of_eq_some_of_get?_intFractPair_stream_fr_ne_zero {ifp_n : IntFractPair K} (stream_nth_eq : IntFractPair.stream v n = some ifp_n) (nth_fr_ne_zero : ifp_n.fr ≠ 0) : (of v).s.get? n = some ⟨1, (IntFractPair.of ifp_n.fr⁻¹).b⟩

views.nl_informal: This gives the first pair of coefficients of the continued fraction of a non-integer `v`.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.of_s_head (h : fract v ≠ 0) : (of v).s.head = some ⟨1, ⌊(fract v)⁻¹⌋⟩

views.nl_informal: If `a` is an integer, then the coefficient sequence of its continued fraction is empty.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.of_s_of_int (a : ℤ) : (of (a : K)).s = Stream'.Seq.nil

views.nl_informal:
Recurrence for the `GenContFract.of` an element `v` of `K` in terms of that of the inverse of
the fractional part of `v`.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.of_s_succ (n : ℕ) : (of v).s.get? (n + 1) = (of (fract v)⁻¹).s.get? n

views.nl_informal:
This expresses the tail of the coefficient sequence of the `GenContFract.of` an element `v` of
`K` as the coefficient sequence of that of the inverse of the fractional part of `v`.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.of_s_tail : (of v).s.tail = (of (fract v)⁻¹).s

views.nl_informal:
If `a` is an integer, then the `convs'` of its continued fraction expansion
are all equal to `a`.
views.lean_signature: theorem GenContFract.convs'_of_int (a : ℤ) : (of (a : K)).convs' n = a

views.nl_informal:

of an element `v` of `K` in terms of the convergents of the inverse of its fractional part.

views.nl_informal:
If a linear map `f : M₁ → M₂` respects direct sum decompositions of `M₁` and `M₂`, then it has a
block diagonal matrix with respect to bases compatible with the direct sum decompositions.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.toMatrix_directSum_collectedBasis_eq_blockDiagonal' {R M₁ M₂ : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [AddCommMonoid M₁] [Module R M₁] {N₁ : ι → Submodule R M₁} (h₁ : IsInternal N₁) [AddCommMonoid M₂] [Module R M₂] {N₂ : ι → Submodule R M₂} (h₂ : IsInternal N₂) {κ₁ κ₂ : ι → Type*} [∀ i, Fintype (κ₁ i)] [∀ i, Finite (κ₂ i)] [∀ i, DecidableEq (κ₁ i)] [Fintype ι] (b₁ : (i : ι) → Basis (κ₁ i) R (N₁ i)) (b₂ : (i : ι) → Basis (κ₂ i) R (N₂ i)) {f : M₁ →ₗ[R] M₂} (hf : ∀ i, MapsTo f (N₁ i) (N₂ i)) : toMatrix (h₁.collectedBasis b₁) (h₂.collectedBasis b₂) f = Matrix.blockDiagonal' fun i ↦ toMatrix (b₁ i) (b₂ i) (f.restrict (hf i))

views.nl_informal:

If `f` and `g` are commuting endomorphisms of a finite, free `R`-module `M`, such that `f`
is triangularizable, then to prove that the trace of `g ∘ f` vanishes, it is sufficient to prove
that the trace of `g` vanishes on each generalized eigenspace of `f`.

views.nl_informal:
The trace of an endomorphism of a direct sum is the sum of the traces on each component.

views.nl_informal:
**Vertical line test** for monoid homomorphisms.

Let `f : G → H × I` be a homomorphism to a product of monoids. Assume that `f` is surjective on the
first factor and that the image of `f` intersects every "vertical line" `{(h, i) | i : I}` at most

views.nl_informal:
**Line test** for monoid isomorphisms.

Let `f : G → H × I` be a homomorphism to a product of monoids. Assume that `f` is surjective on both
factors and that the image of `f` intersects every "vertical line" `{(h, i) | i : I}` and every
"horizontal line" `{(h, i) | h : H}` at most once. Then the image of `f` is the graph of some monoid
isomorphism `f' : H ≃ I`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MonoidHom.exists_mulEquiv_mrange_eq_mgraph {f : G →* H × I} (hf₁ : Surjective (Prod.fst ∘ f)) (hf₂ : Surjective (Prod.snd ∘ f)) (hf : ∀ g₁ g₂, (f g₁).1 = (f g₂).1 ↔ (f g₁).2 = (f g₂).2) : ∃ e : H ≃* I, mrange f = e.toMonoidHom.mgraph

views.nl_informal:
For an addivite functor `F : C ⥤ D` between abelian categories, the following are equivalent:
- `F` preserves short exact sequences on the left hand side, i.e. if `0 ⟶ A ⟶ B ⟶ C ⟶ 0` is exact
  then `0 ⟶ F(A) ⟶ F(B) ⟶ F(C)` is exact.
- `F` preserves exact sequences on the left hand side, i.e. if `A ⟶ B ⟶ C` is exact where `A ⟶ B`
  is mono, then `F(A) ⟶ F(B) ⟶ F(C)` is exact and `F(A) ⟶ F(B)` is mono as well.
- `F` preserves kernels.
- `F` preserves finite limits.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Functor.preservesFiniteLimits_tfae : List.TFAE [ ∀ (S : ShortComplex C), S.ShortExact → (S.map F).Exact ∧ Mono (F.map S.f), ∀ (S : ShortComplex C), S.Exact ∧ Mono S.f → (S.map F).Exact ∧ Mono (F.map S.f), ∀ ⦃X Y : C⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y), PreservesLimit (parallelPair f 0) F, PreservesFiniteLimits F ]
theorem CategoryTheory.Functor.preservesEpimorphisms_of_preserves_shortExact_right (h : ∀ (S : ShortComplex C), S.ShortExact → (S.map F).Exact ∧ Epi (F.map S.g)) : F.PreservesEpimorphisms

views.nl_informal:
For an addivite functor `F : C ⥤ D` between abelian categories, the following are equivalent:
- `F` preserves short exact sequences on the right hand side, i.e. if `0 ⟶ A ⟶ B ⟶ C ⟶ 0` is
  exact then `F(A) ⟶ F(B) ⟶ F(C) ⟶ 0` is exact.
- `F` preserves exact sequences on the right hand side, i.e. if `A ⟶ B ⟶ C` is exact where `B ⟶ C`
  is epi, then `F(A) ⟶ F(B) ⟶ F(C) ⟶ 0` is exact and `F(B) ⟶ F(C)` is epi as well.
- `F` preserves cokernels.
- `F` preserves finite colimits.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Functor.preservesFiniteColimits_tfae : List.TFAE [ ∀ (S : ShortComplex C), S.ShortExact → (S.map F).Exact ∧ Epi (F.map S.g), ∀ (S : ShortComplex C), S.Exact ∧ Epi S.g → (S.map F).Exact ∧ Epi (F.map S.g), ∀ ⦃X Y : C⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y), PreservesColimit (parallelPair f 0) F, PreservesFiniteColimits F ]

views.nl_informal:
For an additive functor `F : C ⥤ D` between abelian categories, the following are equivalent:
- `F` preserves short exact sequences, i.e. if `0 ⟶ A ⟶ B ⟶ C ⟶ 0` is exact then
  `0 ⟶ F(A) ⟶ F(B) ⟶ F(C) ⟶ 0` is exact.
- `F` preserves exact sequences, i.e. if `A ⟶ B ⟶ C` is exact then `F(A) ⟶ F(B) ⟶ F(C)` is exact.
- `F` preserves homology.
- `F` preserves both finite limits and finite colimits.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Functor.exact_tfae : List.TFAE [ ∀ (S : ShortComplex C), S.ShortExact → (S.map F).ShortExact, ∀ (S : ShortComplex C), S.Exact → (S.map F).Exact, PreservesHomology F, PreservesFiniteLimits F ∧ PreservesFiniteColimits F ]

views.nl_informal:
Let `L` be a Lie algebra of dimension `n` over a field `K` with at least `n` elements.
Given a Lie subalgebra `U` of `L`, and an element `x ∈ U` such that `U ≤ engel K x`.
Suppose that `engel K x` is minimal amongst the Engel subalgebras `engel K y` for `y ∈ U`.
Then `engel K x ≤ engel K y` for all `y ∈ U`.

Lemma 2 in [barnes1967].
views.lean_signature: theorem LieAlgebra.engel_isBot_of_isMin (hLK : finrank K L ≤ #K) (U : LieSubalgebra K L) (E : {engel K x | x ∈ U}) (hUle : U ≤ E) (hmin : IsMin E) : IsBot E

*Engel's theorem*.

`LieModule.nontrivial_max_triv_of_isNilpotent`, `LieModule.isNilpotent_iff_forall`,
`LieAlgebra.isNilpotent_iff_forall`.
views.lean_signature: theorem LieAlgebra.isEngelian_of_isNoetherian [IsNoetherian R L] : LieAlgebra.IsEngelian R L

views.nl_informal:
Engel's theorem.

views.nl_informal: Engel's theorem.
views.lean_signature: theorem LieModule.isNilpotent_iff_forall' [IsNoetherian R M] : LieModule.IsNilpotent L M ↔ ∀ x, _root_.IsNilpotent <| toEnd R L M x

views.nl_informal:
Engel subalgebras are self-normalizing.

containing an Engel subalgebra are also self-normalizing,
provided that the ambient Lie algebra is artinina.
views.lean_signature: theorem LieSubalgebra.normalizer_engel (x : L) : normalizer (engel R x) = engel R x

views.nl_informal:
A Lie-subalgebra of an Artinian Lie algebra is self-normalizing
if it contains an Engel subalgebra.
See `LieSubalgebra.normalizer_engel` for a proof that Engel subalgebras are self-normalizing,
avoiding the Artinian condition.
views.lean_signature: theorem LieSubalgebra.normalizer_eq_self_of_engel_le [IsArtinian R L] (H : LieSubalgebra R L) (x : L) (h : engel R x ≤ H) : normalizer H = H

views.nl_informal:

if it is contained in the Engel subalgebra of all its elements.

if it does not have non-trivial abelian ideals and it admits a
non-degenerate reflexive invariant bilinear form.

have a common eigenvector for the action of all elements of the Lie algebra.

See `LieModule.exists_nontrivial_weightSpace_of_isNilpotent` for the variant that
assumes that `L` is nilpotent and drops the condition that `k` is of characteristic zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem LieModule.exists_nontrivial_weightSpace_of_isSolvable [IsSolvable L] [LieModule.IsTriangularizable k L V] : ∃ χ : Module.Dual k L, Nontrivial (weightSpace V χ)

views.nl_informal:
If the quotient of a Lie module `M` by a Lie submodule on which the Lie algebra acts trivially
is nilpotent then `M` is nilpotent.

This is essentially the Lie module equivalent of the fact that a central
extension of nilpotent Lie algebras is nilpotent. See `LieAlgebra.nilpotent_of_nilpotent_quotient`
below for the corresponding result for Lie algebras.

views.nl_informal:
For a nilpotent Lie module `M` of a Lie algebra `L`, the first term in the lower central series
of `M` contains a non-zero element on which `L` acts trivially unless the entire action is trivial.

Taking `M = L`, this provides a useful characterisation of Abelian-ness for nilpotent Lie
algebras.
views.lean_signature: theorem LieModule.disjoint_lowerCentralSeries_maxTrivSubmodule_iff [IsNilpotent L M] : Disjoint (lowerCentralSeries R L M 1) (maxTrivSubmodule R L M) ↔ IsTrivial L M

views.nl_informal:
If a Lie module `M` contains a self-normalizing Lie submodule `N`, then all terms of the upper
central series of `M` are contained in `N`.

An important instance of this situation arises from a Cartan subalgebra `H ⊆ L` with the roles of
`L`, `M`, `N` played by `H`, `L`, `H`, respectively.

views.nl_informal:
Given an ideal `I` of a Lie algebra `L`, the lower central series of `L ⧸ I` is the same
whether we regard `L ⧸ I` as an `L` module or an `L ⧸ I` module.

TODO: This result obviously generalises but the generalisation requires the missing definition of
morphisms between Lie modules over different Lie algebras.
views.lean_signature: theorem coe_lowerCentralSeries_ideal_quot_eq {I : LieIdeal R L} (k : ℕ) : LieSubmodule.toSubmodule (lowerCentralSeries R L (L ⧸ I) k) = LieSubmodule.toSubmodule (lowerCentralSeries R (L ⧸ I) (L ⧸ I) k)

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:
A useful alternative characterisation of Lie ideal operations on Lie submodules.

Given a Lie ideal `I ⊆ L` and a Lie submodule `N ⊆ M`, by tensoring the inclusion maps and then

views.nl_informal:
In a semisimple Lie algebra,
Lie ideals that are contained in the supremum of a finite collection of atoms
are themselves the supremum of a finite subcollection of those atoms.

By a compactness argument, this statement can be extended to arbitrary sets of atoms.
See `atomistic`.

The proof is by induction on the finite set of atoms.
views.lean_signature: theorem LieAlgebra.IsSemisimple.finitelyAtomistic : ∀ s : Finset (LieIdeal R L), ↑s ⊆ {I : LieIdeal R L | IsAtom I} → ∀ I : LieIdeal R L, I ≤ s.sup id → ∃ t ⊆ s, I = t.sup id

views.lean_signature: theorem LieAlgebra.subsingleton_of_hasTrivialRadical_lie_abelian [HasTrivialRadical R L] [h : IsLieAbelian L] : Subsingleton L

views.nl_informal: This is the Fitting decomposition of the Lie module `M`.

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:
If the zero root subalgebra of a nilpotent Lie subalgebra `H` is just `H` then `H` is a Cartan
subalgebra.

When `L` is Noetherian, it follows from Engel's theorem that the converse holds. See
`LieAlgebra.zeroRootSubalgebra_eq_iff_is_cartan`
views.lean_signature: theorem LieAlgebra.is_cartan_of_zeroRootSubalgebra_eq (h : zeroRootSubalgebra R L H = H) : H.IsCartanSubalgebra

views.nl_informal:
Given a (potential) root `α` relative to a Cartan subalgebra `H`, if we restrict to the ideal
`I = corootSpace α` of `H` (informally, `I = ⁅H(α), H(-α)⁆`), we may find an
integral linear combination between `α` and any weight `χ` of a representation.

This is Proposition 4.4 from [carter2005] and is a key step in the proof that the roots of a
semisimple Lie algebra form a root system. It shows that the restriction of `α` to `I` vanishes iff
the restriction of every root to `I` vanishes (which cannot happen in a semisimple Lie algebra).
views.lean_signature: theorem LieModule.exists_forall_mem_corootSpace_smul_add_eq_zero [IsDomain R] [IsPrincipalIdealRing R] [CharZero R] [NoZeroSMulDivisors R M] [IsNoetherian R M] (hα : α ≠ 0) (hχ : genWeightSpace M χ ≠ ⊥) : ∃ a b : ℤ, 0 < b ∧ ∀ x ∈ corootSpace α, (a • α + b • χ) x = 0

views.nl_informal:
If the Killing form of a Lie algebra is non-singular, it remains non-singular when restricted
to a Cartan subalgebra.

views.nl_informal:

form, provided `α + β ≠ 0`.

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:
If a Lie algebra `L` has non-degenerate Killing form, the only element of a Cartan subalgebra

If `(M', f : M ⟶ M')` is a localized module then it satisfies the following universal property:
For every `R`-module `M''` which every `s : S`-scalar multiplication is invertible and for every
`R`-linear map `g : M ⟶ M''`, there is a unique `R`-linear map `l : M' ⟶ M''` such that

|           /
|g       /
|     /   l
v   /
M''

* `φ` maps each monomial `m` in `R[x]` to a polynomial `φ m` of degree `fu (deg m)`.

Vieta's formula for a quadratic equation, relating the coefficients of the polynomial with
its roots. This particular version states that if we have a root `x` of a monic quadratic
polynomial, then there is another root `y` such that `x + y` is negative the `a_1` coefficient
and `x * y` is the `a_0` coefficient.

views.nl_informal:

implies the mere existence of such an inverse.

views.nl_informal:

the common vertices will agree with those of the original path `f`. In particular,
a vertex `i` with `i < j` can be identified with the same vertex in `f`.

views.nl_informal:
If we take the path along the spine of the `j`th face of a `spineToSimplex`,
a vertex `i` with `j ≤ i` can be identified with vertex `i + 1` in the original
path.
views.lean_signature: theorem SSet.Truncated.StrictSegal.spine_δ_vertex_ge (hij : j ≤ i.castSucc) : (X.spine m _ (X.map (tr (δ j)).op (sx.spineToSimplex (m + 1) _ f))).vertex i = f.vertex i.succ

the common arrows will agree with those of the original path `f`. In particular,
an arrow `i` with `i + 1 < j` can be identified with the same arrow in `f`.

views.nl_informal:

an arrow `i` with `i + 1 > j` can be identified with arrow `i + 1` in the
original path.

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:
If we take the path along the spine of the `j`th face of a `spineToSimplex`,

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:
If we take the path along the spine of the `j`th face of a `spineToSimplex`,

views.nl_informal:
If we take the path along the spine of the `j`th face of a `spineToSimplex`,
an arrow `i` with `i + 1 > j` can be identified with arrow `i + 1` in the
original path.
views.lean_signature: theorem SSet.StrictSegal.spine_δ_arrow_gt (h : j < i.succ.castSucc) : (X.spine n (X.δ j (sx.spineToSimplex f))).arrow i = f.arrow i.succ

views.nl_informal:
If we take the path along the spine of a face of a `spineToSimplex`, the
arrows not contained in the original path can be recovered as the diagonal edge
of the `spineToSimplex` that "composes" arrows `i` and `i + 1`.

A sufficient condition to prove that `f ⋆[L, μ] g` exists.

views.nl_informal: If `‖f‖ *[μ] ‖g‖` exists, then `f *[L, μ] g` exists.

views.nl_informal:
A sufficient condition to prove that `f ⋆[L, μ] g` exists.
We assume that the integrand has compact support and `g` is bounded on this support (note that
both properties hold if `g` is continuous with compact support). We also require that `f` is
integrable on the support of the integrand, and that both functions are strongly measurable.

This is a variant of `BddAbove.convolutionExistsAt'` in an abelian group with a left-invariant
measure. This allows us to state the boundedness and measurability of `g` in a more natural way.
views.lean_signature: theorem BddAbove.convolutionExistsAt [MeasurableAdd₂ G] [SFinite μ] {x₀ : G} {s : Set G} (hbg : BddAbove ((fun i => ‖g i‖) '' ((fun t => x₀ - t) ⁻¹' s))) (hs : MeasurableSet s) (h2s : (support fun t => L (f t) (g (x₀ - t))) ⊆ s) (hf : IntegrableOn f s μ) (hmg : AEStronglyMeasurable g μ) : ConvolutionExistsAt f g x₀ L μ

views.nl_informal:
If `f` has formal power series `∑ n, pₙ` on a ball of radius `r`, then for `y, z` in any smaller
ball, the norm of the difference `f y - f z - p 1 (fun _ ↦ y - z)` is bounded above by
`C * (max ‖y - x‖ ‖z - x‖) * ‖y - z‖`. This lemma formulates this property using `IsBigO` and
`Filter.principal` on `E × E`.
views.lean_signature: theorem HasFPowerSeriesOnBall.isBigO_image_sub_image_sub_deriv_principal (hf : HasFPowerSeriesOnBall f p x r) (hr : r' < r) : (fun y : E × E => f y.1 - f y.2 - p 1 fun _ => y.1 - y.2) =O[𝓟 (EMetric.ball (x, x) r')] fun y => ‖y - (x, x)‖ * ‖y.1 - y.2‖

views.nl_informal:
If `f` has formal power series `∑ n, pₙ` within a set, on a ball of radius `r`, then for `y, z`
in any smaller ball, the norm of the difference `f y - f z - p 1 (fun _ ↦ y - z)` is bounded above
by `C * (max ‖y - x‖ ‖z - x‖) * ‖y - z‖`.
views.lean_signature: theorem HasFPowerSeriesWithinOnBall.image_sub_sub_deriv_le (hf : HasFPowerSeriesWithinOnBall f p s x r) (hr : r' < r) : ∃ C, ∀ᵉ (y ∈ insert x s ∩ EMetric.ball x r') (z ∈ insert x s ∩ EMetric.ball x r'), ‖f y - f z - p 1 fun _ => y - z‖ ≤ C * max ‖y - x‖ ‖z - x‖ * ‖y - z‖

views.nl_informal:
If `f` has formal power series `∑ n, pₙ` on a ball of radius `r`, then for `y, z` in any smaller
ball, the norm of the difference `f y - f z - p 1 (fun _ ↦ y - z)` is bounded above by
`C * (max ‖y - x‖ ‖z - x‖) * ‖y - z‖`.
views.lean_signature: theorem HasFPowerSeriesOnBall.image_sub_sub_deriv_le (hf : HasFPowerSeriesOnBall f p x r) (hr : r' < r) : ∃ C, ∀ᵉ (y ∈ EMetric.ball x r') (z ∈ EMetric.ball x r'), ‖f y - f z - p 1 fun _ => y - z‖ ≤ C * max ‖y - x‖ ‖z - x‖ * ‖y - z‖

views.nl_informal:
If `f` has formal power series `∑ n, pₙ` at `x` within a set `s`, then
`f y - f z - p 1 (fun _ ↦ y - z) = O(‖(y, z) - (x, x)‖ * ‖y - z‖)` as `(y, z) → (x, x)`
within `s × s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem HasFPowerSeriesWithinAt.isBigO_image_sub_norm_mul_norm_sub (hf : HasFPowerSeriesWithinAt f p s x) : (fun y : E × E => f y.1 - f y.2 - p 1 fun _ => y.1 - y.2) =O[𝓝[(insert x s) ×ˢ (insert x s)] (x, x)] fun y => ‖y - (x, x)‖ * ‖y.1 - y.2‖

views.nl_informal:
If `f` has formal power series `∑ n, pₙ` at `x`, then
`f y - f z - p 1 (fun _ ↦ y - z) = O(‖(y, z) - (x, x)‖ * ‖y - z‖)` as `(y, z) → (x, x)`.
In particular, `f` is strictly differentiable at `x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem HasFPowerSeriesAt.isBigO_image_sub_norm_mul_norm_sub (hf : HasFPowerSeriesAt f p x) : (fun y : E × E => f y.1 - f y.2 - p 1 fun _ => y.1 - y.2) =O[𝓝 (x, x)] fun y => ‖y - (x, x)‖ * ‖y.1 - y.2‖

views.nl_informal:
If a function admits a power series expansion within a set at `x`, then it is the uniform limit
of the partial sums of this power series on strict subdisks of the disk of convergence, i.e.,
`f (x + y)` is the uniform limit of `p.partialSum n y` there.
