views.nl_informal:
If a function admits a power series expansion within a set on a ball, then it is
continuous there.
views.lean_signature: theorem HasFPowerSeriesWithinOnBall.continuousOn (hf : HasFPowerSeriesWithinOnBall f p s x r) : ContinuousOn f (insert x s ∩ EMetric.ball x r)

views.nl_informal: If a function admits a power series expansion on a ball, then it is continuous there.
views.lean_signature: theorem HasFPowerSeriesOnBall.continuousOn (hf : HasFPowerSeriesOnBall f p x r) : ContinuousOn f (EMetric.ball x r)

views.nl_informal: Analytic everywhere implies continuous
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticOnNhd.continuous {f : E → F} (fa : AnalyticOnNhd 𝕜 f univ) : Continuous f

views.nl_informal:
In a complete space, the sum of a converging power series `p` admits `p` as a power series.
This is not totally obvious as we need to check the convergence of the series.
views.lean_signature: theorem FormalMultilinearSeries.hasFPowerSeriesOnBall [CompleteSpace F] (p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F) (h : 0 < p.radius) : HasFPowerSeriesOnBall p.sum p 0 p.radius

views.nl_informal: The sum of a converging power series is continuous in its disk of convergence.
views.lean_signature: theorem FormalMultilinearSeries.continuousOn [CompleteSpace F] : ContinuousOn p.sum (EMetric.ball 0 p.radius)

views.nl_informal:
A function `f : 𝕜 → E` has `p` as power series expansion at a point `z₀` iff it is the sum of
`p` in a neighborhood of `z₀`. This makes some proofs easier by hiding the fact that
`HasFPowerSeriesAt` depends on `p.radius`.
views.lean_signature: theorem hasFPowerSeriesAt_iff : HasFPowerSeriesAt f p z₀ ↔ ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝 0, HasSum (fun n => z ^ n • p.coeff n) (f (z₀ + z))

views.nl_informal:
If a function `f` has a finite power series `p` around `x`, then the function
`z ↦ f (z - y)` has the same finite power series around `x + y`.
views.lean_signature: theorem HasFiniteFPowerSeriesOnBall.comp_sub (hf : HasFiniteFPowerSeriesOnBall f p x n r) (y : E) : HasFiniteFPowerSeriesOnBall (fun z => f (z - y)) p (x + y) n r

views.nl_informal:
If a function `f` has a finite power series `p` on a ball and `g` is a continuous linear map,
then `g ∘ f` has the finite power series `g ∘ p` on the same ball.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContinuousLinearMap.comp_hasFiniteFPowerSeriesOnBall (g : F →L[𝕜] G) (h : HasFiniteFPowerSeriesOnBall f p x n r) : HasFiniteFPowerSeriesOnBall (g ∘ f) (g.compFormalMultilinearSeries p) x n r

views.nl_informal:
If a function `f` is continuously polynomial on a set `s` and `g` is a continuous linear map,
then `g ∘ f` is continuously polynomial on `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContinuousLinearMap.comp_cpolynomialOn {s : Set E} (g : F →L[𝕜] G) (h : CPolynomialOn 𝕜 f s) : CPolynomialOn 𝕜 (g ∘ f) s

views.nl_informal:
If a function admits a finite power series expansion bounded by `n`, then it is equal to
the `m`th partial sums of this power series at every point of the disk for `n ≤ m`.
views.lean_signature: theorem HasFiniteFPowerSeriesOnBall.eq_partialSum (hf : HasFiniteFPowerSeriesOnBall f p x n r) : ∀ y ∈ EMetric.ball (0 : E) r, ∀ m, n ≤ m → f (x + y) = p.partialSum m y

views.nl_informal:
If `f` has a formal power series on a ball bounded by `0`, then `f` is equal to `0` on
the ball.
views.lean_signature: theorem HasFiniteFPowerSeriesOnBall.eq_zero_of_bound_zero (hf : HasFiniteFPowerSeriesOnBall f pf x 0 r) : ∀ y ∈ EMetric.ball x r, f y = 0

views.nl_informal:
If `f` has a formal power series at `x` bounded by `0`, then `f` is equal to `0` in a
neighborhood of `x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem HasFiniteFPowerSeriesAt.eventually_zero_of_bound_zero (hf : HasFiniteFPowerSeriesAt f pf x 0) : f =ᶠ[𝓝 x] 0

views.nl_informal:
If `f` has a formal power series on a ball bounded by `1`, then `f` is constant equal
to `f x` on the ball.
views.lean_signature: theorem HasFiniteFPowerSeriesOnBall.eq_const_of_bound_one (hf : HasFiniteFPowerSeriesOnBall f pf x 1 r) : ∀ y ∈ EMetric.ball x r, f y = f x

views.nl_informal:
If `f` has a formal power series at x bounded by `1`, then `f` is constant equal
to `f x` in a neighborhood of `x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem HasFiniteFPowerSeriesAt.eventually_const_of_bound_one (hf : HasFiniteFPowerSeriesAt f pf x 1) : f =ᶠ[𝓝 x] (fun _ => f x)

views.nl_informal: If a function admits a finite power series expansion on a disk, then it is continuous there.
views.lean_signature: theorem HasFiniteFPowerSeriesOnBall.continuousOn (hf : HasFiniteFPowerSeriesOnBall f p x n r) : ContinuousOn f (EMetric.ball x r)

views.nl_informal: Continuously polynomial everywhere implies continuous
views.lean_signature: theorem CPolynomialOn.continuous {f : E → F} (fa : CPolynomialOn 𝕜 f univ) : Continuous f

views.nl_informal: A finite formal multilinear series sums to its sum at every point.
views.lean_signature: theorem FormalMultilinearSeries.hasSum_of_finite (p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F) {n : ℕ} (hn : ∀ m, n ≤ m → p m = 0) (x : E) : HasSum (fun n : ℕ => p n fun _ => x) (p.sum x)

views.nl_informal: The sum of a finite power series `p` admits `p` as a power series.
views.lean_signature: theorem FormalMultilinearSeries.hasFiniteFPowerSeriesOnBall_of_finite (p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F) {n : ℕ} (hn : ∀ m, n ≤ m → p m = 0) : HasFiniteFPowerSeriesOnBall p.sum p 0 n ⊤

views.nl_informal: The sum of a finite power series is continuous.
views.lean_signature: theorem FormalMultilinearSeries.continuousOn_of_finite (p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F) {n : ℕ} (hn : ∀ m, n ≤ m → p m = 0) : Continuous p.sum

views.nl_informal:
If `p` is a formal multilinear series such that `p m = 0` for `n ≤ m`, then
`p.changeOriginSeriesTerm k l = 0` for `n ≤ k + l`.
views.lean_signature: theorem FormalMultilinearSeries.changeOriginSeriesTerm_bound (p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F) {n : ℕ} (hn : ∀ (m : ℕ), n ≤ m → p m = 0) (k l : ℕ) {s : Finset (Fin (k + l))} (hs : s.card = l) (hkl : n ≤ k + l) : p.changeOriginSeriesTerm k l s hs = 0

views.nl_informal:
If `p` is a finite formal multilinear series, then so is `p.changeOriginSeries k` for every
`k` in `ℕ`. More precisely, if `p m = 0` for `n ≤ m`, then `p.changeOriginSeries k m = 0` for
`n ≤ k + m`.
views.lean_signature: theorem FormalMultilinearSeries.changeOriginSeries_finite_of_finite (p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F) {n : ℕ} (hn : ∀ (m : ℕ), n ≤ m → p m = 0) (k : ℕ) : ∀ {m : ℕ}, n ≤ k + m → p.changeOriginSeries k m = 0

views.nl_informal:
If `p` is a formal multilinear series such that `p m = 0` for `n ≤ m`, then
`p.changeOrigin x k = 0` for `n ≤ k`.
views.lean_signature: theorem FormalMultilinearSeries.changeOrigin_finite_of_finite (p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F) {n : ℕ} (hn : ∀ (m : ℕ), n ≤ m → p m = 0) {k : ℕ} (hk : n ≤ k) : p.changeOrigin x k = 0

views.nl_informal:
The terms of the formal multilinear series `p.changeOrigin` are continuously polynomial
as we vary the origin
views.lean_signature: theorem FormalMultilinearSeries.cpolynomialAt_changeOrigin_of_finite (p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F) {n : ℕ} (hn : ∀ (m : ℕ), n ≤ m → p m = 0) (k : ℕ) : CPolynomialAt 𝕜 (p.changeOrigin · k) 0

views.nl_informal:
If a function admits a finite power series expansion `p` on an open ball `B (x, r)`, then
it is continuously polynomial at every point of this ball.
views.lean_signature: theorem HasFiniteFPowerSeriesOnBall.cpolynomialAt_of_mem (hf : HasFiniteFPowerSeriesOnBall f p x n r) (h : y ∈ EMetric.ball x r) : CPolynomialAt 𝕜 f y

views.nl_informal:
For any function `f` from a normed vector space to a normed vector space, the set of points
`x` such that `f` is continuously polynomial at `x` is open.
views.lean_signature: theorem isOpen_cpolynomialAt : IsOpen { x | CPolynomialAt 𝕜 f x }

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is continuously polynomial at a point, then it is continuously polynomial in a
nonempty ball around that point.
views.lean_signature: theorem CPolynomialAt.exists_ball_cpolynomialOn {f : E → F} {x : E} (h : CPolynomialAt 𝕜 f x) : ∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ CPolynomialOn 𝕜 f (Metric.ball x r)

views.nl_informal:
The radius of convergence of `p.changeOrigin x` is at least `p.radius - ‖x‖`. In other words,
`p.changeOrigin x` is well defined on the largest ball contained in the original ball of
convergence.
views.lean_signature: theorem FormalMultilinearSeries.changeOrigin_radius : p.radius - ‖x‖₊ ≤ (p.changeOrigin x).radius

views.nl_informal: Summing the series `p.changeOrigin x` at a point `y` gives back `p (x + y)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem FormalMultilinearSeries.changeOrigin_eval (h : (‖x‖₊ + ‖y‖₊ : ℝ≥0∞) < p.radius) : (p.changeOrigin x).sum y = p.sum (x + y)

views.nl_informal: Power series terms are analytic as we vary the origin
views.lean_signature: theorem FormalMultilinearSeries.analyticAt_changeOrigin (p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F) (rp : p.radius > 0) (n : ℕ) : AnalyticAt 𝕜 (fun x ↦ p.changeOrigin x n) 0

views.nl_informal:
If a function admits a power series expansion `p` within a set `s` on a ball `B (x, r)`, then
it also admits a power series on any subball of this ball (even with a different center provided
it belongs to `s`), given by `p.changeOrigin`.
views.lean_signature: theorem HasFPowerSeriesWithinOnBall.changeOrigin (hf : HasFPowerSeriesWithinOnBall f p s x r) (h : ‖y‖ₑ < r) (hy : x + y ∈ insert x s) : HasFPowerSeriesWithinOnBall f (p.changeOrigin y) s (x + y) (r - ‖y‖ₑ)

views.nl_informal:
If a function admits a power series expansion `p` on a ball `B (x, r)`, then it also admits a
power series on any subball of this ball (even with a different center), given by `p.changeOrigin`.
views.lean_signature: theorem HasFPowerSeriesOnBall.changeOrigin (hf : HasFPowerSeriesOnBall f p x r) (h : (‖y‖₊ : ℝ≥0∞) < r) : HasFPowerSeriesOnBall f (p.changeOrigin y) (x + y) (r - ‖y‖₊)

views.nl_informal:
If a function admits a power series expansion `p` on an open ball `B (x, r)`, then
it is analytic at every point of this ball.
views.lean_signature: theorem HasFPowerSeriesWithinOnBall.analyticWithinAt_of_mem (hf : HasFPowerSeriesWithinOnBall f p s x r) (h : y ∈ insert x s ∩ EMetric.ball x r) : AnalyticWithinAt 𝕜 f s y

views.nl_informal:
If a function admits a power series expansion `p` on an open ball `B (x, r)`, then
it is analytic at every point of this ball.
views.lean_signature: theorem HasFPowerSeriesOnBall.analyticAt_of_mem (hf : HasFPowerSeriesOnBall f p x r) (h : y ∈ EMetric.ball x r) : AnalyticAt 𝕜 f y

views.nl_informal:
For any function `f` from a normed vector space to a Banach space, the set of points `x` such
that `f` is analytic at `x` is open.
views.lean_signature: theorem isOpen_analyticAt : IsOpen { x | AnalyticAt 𝕜 f x }

views.nl_informal: If we're analytic at a point, we're analytic in a nonempty ball
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticAt.exists_ball_analyticOnNhd (h : AnalyticAt 𝕜 f x) : ∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ AnalyticOnNhd 𝕜 f (Metric.ball x r)

views.nl_informal:
Technical lemma stating how `p.applyComposition` commutes with updating variables. This
will be the key point to show that functions constructed from `applyComposition` retain
multilinearity.
views.lean_signature: theorem FormalMultilinearSeries.applyComposition_update (p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F) {n : ℕ} (c : Composition n) (j : Fin n) (v : Fin n → E) (z : E) : p.applyComposition c (Function.update v j z) = Function.update (p.applyComposition c v) (c.index j) (p (c.blocksFun (c.index j)) (Function.update (v ∘ c.embedding (c.index j)) (c.invEmbedding j) z))

views.nl_informal:
The `0`-th coefficient of `q.comp p` is `q 0`. Since these maps are multilinear maps in zero
variables, but on different spaces, we can not state this directly, so we state it when applied to
arbitrary vectors (which have to be the zero vector).
views.lean_signature: theorem FormalMultilinearSeries.comp_coeff_zero (q : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 F G) (p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F) (v : Fin 0 → E) (v' : Fin 0 → F) : (q.comp p) 0 v = q 0 v'

views.nl_informal:
The `0`-th coefficient of `q.comp p` is `q 0`. When `p` goes from `E` to `E`, this can be
expressed as a direct equality
views.lean_signature: theorem FormalMultilinearSeries.comp_coeff_zero'' (q : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F) (p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E E) : (q.comp p) 0 = q 0

views.nl_informal:
The first coefficient of a composition of formal multilinear series is the composition of the
first coefficients seen as continuous linear maps.
views.lean_signature: theorem FormalMultilinearSeries.comp_coeff_one (q : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 F G) (p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F) (v : Fin 1 → E) : (q.comp p) 1 v = q 1 fun _i => p 1 v

views.nl_informal: Only `0`-th coefficient of `q.comp p` depends on `q 0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem FormalMultilinearSeries.removeZero_comp_of_pos (q : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 F G) (p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F) {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) : q.removeZero.comp p n = q.comp p n

views.nl_informal:
The norm of `f.compAlongComposition p c` is controlled by the product of
the norms of the relevant bits of `f` and `p`.
views.lean_signature: theorem FormalMultilinearSeries.compAlongComposition_bound {n : ℕ} (p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F) (c : Composition n) (f : F [×c.length]→L[𝕜] G) (v : Fin n → E) : ‖f.compAlongComposition p c v‖ ≤ (‖f‖ * ∏ i, ‖p (c.blocksFun i)‖) * ∏ i : Fin n, ‖v i‖

views.nl_informal:
The norm of `q.compAlongComposition p c` is controlled by the product of
the norms of the relevant bits of `q` and `p`.
views.lean_signature: theorem FormalMultilinearSeries.compAlongComposition_norm {n : ℕ} (q : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 F G) (p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F) (c : Composition n) : ‖q.compAlongComposition p c‖ ≤ ‖q c.length‖ * ∏ i, ‖p (c.blocksFun i)‖

views.nl_informal: The first coefficient of `id 𝕜 E` is the identity.
views.lean_signature: theorem FormalMultilinearSeries.id_apply_one (x : E) (v : Fin 1 → E) : (FormalMultilinearSeries.id 𝕜 E x) 1 v = v 0

views.nl_informal:
The `n`th coefficient of `id 𝕜 E` is the identity when `n = 1`. We state this in a dependent
way, as it will often appear in this form.
views.lean_signature: theorem FormalMultilinearSeries.id_apply_one' (x : E) {n : ℕ} (h : n = 1) (v : Fin n → E) : (id 𝕜 E x) n v = v ⟨0, h.symm ▸ zero_lt_one⟩

views.nl_informal: For `n ≠ 1`, the `n`-th coefficient of `id 𝕜 E` is zero, by definition.
views.lean_signature: theorem FormalMultilinearSeries.id_apply_of_one_lt (x : E) {n : ℕ} (h : 1 < n) : (FormalMultilinearSeries.id 𝕜 E x) n = 0

views.nl_informal:
If two formal multilinear series have positive radius of convergence, then the terms appearing
in the definition of their composition are also summable (when multiplied by a suitable positive
geometric term).

views.nl_informal:
`compChangeOfVariables m M N` is a bijection between `compPartialSumSource m M N`
and `compPartialSumTarget m M N`, yielding equal sums for functions that correspond to each
other under the bijection. As `compChangeOfVariables m M N` is a dependent function, stating
that it is a bijection is not directly possible, but the consequence on sums can be stated
more easily.

views.nl_informal:
Auxiliary lemma to prove that the composition of formal multilinear series is associative.

Consider a composition `a` of `n` and a composition `b` of `a.length`. Grouping together some
blocks of `a` according to `b` as in `a.gather b`, one can compute the total size of the blocks
of `a` up to an index `sizeUpTo b i + j` (where the `j` corresponds to a set of blocks of `a`
that do not fill a whole block of `a.gather b`). The first part corresponds to a sum of blocks
in `a.gather b`, and the second one to a sum of blocks in the next block of
`sigmaCompositionAux a b`. This is the content of this lemma.
views.lean_signature: theorem Composition.sizeUpTo_sizeUpTo_add (a : Composition n) (b : Composition a.length) {i j : ℕ} (hi : i < b.length) (hj : j < blocksFun b ⟨i, hi⟩) : sizeUpTo a (sizeUpTo b i + j) = sizeUpTo (a.gather b) i + sizeUpTo (sigmaCompositionAux a b ⟨i, (length_gather a b).symm ▸ hi⟩) j

The right inverse to a formal multilinear series is indeed a right inverse, provided its linear

views.nl_informal:
First technical lemma to control the growth of coefficients of the inverse. Bound the explicit
expression for `∑_{k<n+1} aᵏ Qₖ` in terms of a sum of powers of the same sum one step before,
in a general abstract setup.
views.lean_signature: theorem FormalMultilinearSeries.radius_right_inv_pos_of_radius_pos_aux1 (n : ℕ) (p : ℕ → ℝ) (hp : ∀ k, 0 ≤ p k) {r a : ℝ} (hr : 0 ≤ r) (ha : 0 ≤ a) : ∑ k ∈ Ico 2 (n + 1), a ^ k * ∑ c ∈ ({c | 1 < Composition.length c}.toFinset : Finset (Composition k)), r ^ c.length * ∏ j, p (c.blocksFun j) ≤ ∑ j ∈ Ico 2 (n + 1), r ^ j * (∑ k ∈ Ico 1 n, a ^ k * p k) ^ j

views.nl_informal:
Second technical lemma to control the growth of coefficients of the inverse. Bound the explicit
expression for `∑_{k<n+1} aᵏ Qₖ` in terms of a sum of powers of the same sum one step before,
in the specific setup we are interesting in, by reducing to the general bound in
`radius_rightInv_pos_of_radius_pos_aux1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem FormalMultilinearSeries.radius_rightInv_pos_of_radius_pos_aux2 {x : E} {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n + 1) (p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F) (i : E ≃L[𝕜] F) {r a C : ℝ} (hr : 0 ≤ r) (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hC : 0 ≤ C) (hp : ∀ n, ‖p n‖ ≤ C * r ^ n) : ∑ k ∈ Ico 1 (n + 1), a ^ k * ‖p.rightInv i x k‖ ≤ ‖(i.symm : F →L[𝕜] E)‖ * a + ‖(i.symm : F →L[𝕜] E)‖ * C * ∑ k ∈ Ico 2 (n + 1), (r * ∑ j ∈ Ico 1 n, a ^ j * ‖p.rightInv i x j‖) ^ k

views.nl_informal:
The *principle of isolated zeros* for an analytic function, local version: if a function is
analytic at `z₀`, then either it is identically zero in a neighborhood of `z₀`, or it does not
vanish in a punctured neighborhood of `z₀`.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticAt.eventually_eq_zero_or_eventually_ne_zero (hf : AnalyticAt 𝕜 f z₀) : (∀ᶠ z in 𝓝 z₀, f z = 0) ∨ ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝[≠] z₀, f z ≠ 0

views.nl_informal:
For a function `f` on `𝕜`, and `z₀ ∈ 𝕜`, there exists at most one `n` such that on a punctured
neighbourhood of `z₀` we have `f z = (z - z₀) ^ n • g z`, with `g` analytic and nonvanishing at
`z₀`. We formulate this with `n : ℤ`, and deduce the case `n : ℕ` later, for applications to
meromorphic functions.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticAt.unique_eventuallyEq_zpow_smul_nonzero {m n : ℤ} (hm : ∃ g, AnalyticAt 𝕜 g z₀ ∧ g z₀ ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝[≠] z₀, f z = (z - z₀) ^ m • g z) (hn : ∃ g, AnalyticAt 𝕜 g z₀ ∧ g z₀ ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝[≠] z₀, f z = (z - z₀) ^ n • g z) : m = n

views.nl_informal:
For a function `f` on `𝕜`, and `z₀ ∈ 𝕜`, there exists at most one `n` such that on a
neighbourhood of `z₀` we have `f z = (z - z₀) ^ n • g z`, with `g` analytic and nonvanishing at
`z₀`.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticAt.unique_eventuallyEq_pow_smul_nonzero {m n : ℕ} (hm : ∃ g, AnalyticAt 𝕜 g z₀ ∧ g z₀ ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝 z₀, f z = (z - z₀) ^ m • g z) (hn : ∃ g, AnalyticAt 𝕜 g z₀ ∧ g z₀ ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝 z₀, f z = (z - z₀) ^ n • g z) : m = n

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is analytic at `z₀`, then exactly one of the following two possibilities occurs: either
`f` vanishes identically near `z₀`, or locally around `z₀` it has the form `z ↦ (z - z₀) ^ n • g z`
for some `n` and some `g` which is analytic and non-vanishing at `z₀`.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticAt.exists_eventuallyEq_pow_smul_nonzero_iff (hf : AnalyticAt 𝕜 f z₀) : (∃ (n : ℕ), ∃ (g : 𝕜 → E), AnalyticAt 𝕜 g z₀ ∧ g z₀ ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝 z₀, f z = (z - z₀) ^ n • g z) ↔ (¬∀ᶠ z in 𝓝 z₀, f z = 0)

views.nl_informal:
The *principle of isolated zeros* for an analytic function, global version: if a function is
analytic on a connected set `U` and vanishes in arbitrary neighborhoods of a point `z₀ ∈ U`, then
it is identically zero in `U`.
For higher-dimensional versions requiring that the function vanishes in a neighborhood of `z₀`,
see `AnalyticOnNhd.eqOn_zero_of_preconnected_of_eventuallyEq_zero`.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticOnNhd.eqOn_zero_of_preconnected_of_frequently_eq_zero (hf : AnalyticOnNhd 𝕜 f U) (hU : IsPreconnected U) (h₀ : z₀ ∈ U) (hfw : ∃ᶠ z in 𝓝[≠] z₀, f z = 0) : EqOn f 0 U

views.nl_informal:
The *identity principle* for analytic functions, global version: if two functions are
analytic on a connected set `U` and coincide at points which accumulate to a point `z₀ ∈ U`, then
they coincide globally in `U`.
For higher-dimensional versions requiring that the functions coincide in a neighborhood of `z₀`,
see `AnalyticOnNhd.eqOn_of_preconnected_of_eventuallyEq`.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticOnNhd.eqOn_of_preconnected_of_frequently_eq (hf : AnalyticOnNhd 𝕜 f U) (hg : AnalyticOnNhd 𝕜 g U) (hU : IsPreconnected U) (h₀ : z₀ ∈ U) (hfg : ∃ᶠ z in 𝓝[≠] z₀, f z = g z) : EqOn f g U

views.nl_informal:
The *identity principle* for analytic functions, global version: if two functions on a normed
field `𝕜` are analytic everywhere and coincide at points which accumulate to a point `z₀`, then
they coincide globally.
For higher-dimensional versions requiring that the functions coincide in a neighborhood of `z₀`,
see `AnalyticOnNhd.eq_of_eventuallyEq`.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticOnNhd.eq_of_frequently_eq [ConnectedSpace 𝕜] (hf : AnalyticOnNhd 𝕜 f univ) (hg : AnalyticOnNhd 𝕜 g univ) (hfg : ∃ᶠ z in 𝓝[≠] z₀, f z = g z) : f = g

views.nl_informal:
If `f, g` are analytic on a neighbourhood of the preconnected open set `U`, and `f • g = 0`
on `U`, then either `f = 0` on `U` or `g = 0` on `U`.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticOnNhd.eq_zero_or_eq_zero_of_smul_eq_zero [NoZeroSMulDivisors A B] {f : 𝕜 → A} {g : 𝕜 → B} (hf : AnalyticOnNhd 𝕜 f U) (hg : AnalyticOnNhd 𝕜 g U) (hfg : ∀ z ∈ U, f z • g z = 0) (hU : IsPreconnected U) : (∀ z ∈ U, f z = 0) ∨ (∀ z ∈ U, g z = 0)

views.nl_informal:
If `f, g` are analytic on a neighbourhood of the preconnected open set `U`, and `f * g = 0`
on `U`, then either `f = 0` on `U` or `g = 0` on `U`.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticOnNhd.eq_zero_or_eq_zero_of_mul_eq_zero [NoZeroDivisors A] {f g : 𝕜 → A} (hf : AnalyticOnNhd 𝕜 f U) (hg : AnalyticOnNhd 𝕜 g U) (hfg : ∀ z ∈ U, f z * g z = 0) (hU : IsPreconnected U) : (∀ z ∈ U, f z = 0) ∨ (∀ z ∈ U, g z = 0)

views.nl_informal:
Preimages of codiscrete sets, local version: if `f` is analytic at `x` and not locally constant,
then the preimage of any punctured neighbourhood of `f x` is a punctured neighbourhood of `x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticAt.preimage_of_nhdsNE {x : 𝕜} {f : 𝕜 → E} {s : Set E} (hfx : AnalyticAt 𝕜 f x) (h₂f : ¬EventuallyConst f (𝓝 x)) (hs : s ∈ 𝓝[≠] f x) : f ⁻¹' s ∈ 𝓝[≠] x

views.nl_informal:
Preimages of codiscrete sets, local filter version: if `f` is analytic at `x` and not locally
constant, then the push-forward of the punctured neighbourhood filter `𝓝[≠] x` is less than or
equal to the punctured neighbourhood filter `𝓝[≠] f x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticAt.map_nhdsNE {x : 𝕜} {f : 𝕜 → E} (hfx : AnalyticAt 𝕜 f x) (h₂f : ¬EventuallyConst f (𝓝 x)) : (𝓝[≠] x).map f ≤ (𝓝[≠] f x)

views.nl_informal:
Preimages of codiscrete sets: if `f` is analytic on a neighbourhood of `U` and not locally
constant, then the preimage of any subset codiscrete within `f '' U` is codiscrete within `U`.

Applications might want to use the theorem `Filter.codiscreteWithin.mono`.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticOnNhd.preimage_mem_codiscreteWithin {U : Set 𝕜} {s : Set E} {f : 𝕜 → E} (hfU : AnalyticOnNhd 𝕜 f U) (h₂f : ∀ x ∈ U, ¬EventuallyConst f (𝓝 x)) (hs : s ∈ codiscreteWithin (f '' U)) : f ⁻¹' s ∈ codiscreteWithin U

views.nl_informal:
Preimages of codiscrete sets, filter version: if `f` is analytic on a neighbourhood of `U` and
not locally constant, then the push-forward of the filter of sets codiscrete within `U` is less
than or equal to the filter of sets codiscrete within `f '' U`.

Applications might want to use the theorem `Filter.codiscreteWithin.mono`.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticOnNhd.map_codiscreteWithin {U : Set 𝕜} {f : 𝕜 → E} (hfU : AnalyticOnNhd 𝕜 f U) (h₂f : ∀ x ∈ U, ¬EventuallyConst f (𝓝 x)) : map f (codiscreteWithin U) ≤ (codiscreteWithin (f '' U))

views.nl_informal:
If a function has a power series in a ball, then its `n`-th iterated derivative is given by

The radius of convergence of a scalar series is the inverse of the non-zero limit
`fun n ↦ ‖c n.succ‖ / ‖c n‖`.

views.nl_informal:
The ratio test stating that if `‖c n.succ‖ / ‖c n‖` tends to zero, the radius is unbounded.
This requires that the coefficients are eventually non-zero as
`‖c n.succ‖ / 0 = 0` by convention.
views.lean_signature: theorem FormalMultilinearSeries.ofScalars_radius_eq_top_of_tendsto (hc : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, c n ≠ 0) (hc' : Tendsto (fun n ↦ ‖c n.succ‖ / ‖c n‖) atTop (𝓝 0)) : (ofScalars E c).radius = ⊤

views.lean_signature: theorem FormalMultilinearSeries.ofScalars_radius_eq_zero_of_tendsto [NormOneClass E] (hc : Tendsto (fun n ↦ ‖c n.succ‖ / ‖c n‖) atTop atTop) : (ofScalars E c).radius = 0

views.nl_informal:
The order of an analytic function `f` at a `z₀` is infinity iff `f` vanishes locally around
`z₀`.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticAt.order_eq_top_iff (hf : AnalyticAt 𝕜 f z₀) : hf.order = ⊤ ↔ ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝 z₀, f z = 0

views.nl_informal:
The order of an analytic function `f` at `z₀` equals a natural number `n` iff `f` can locally
be written as `f z = (z - z₀) ^ n • g z`, where `g` is analytic and does not vanish at `z₀`.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticAt.order_eq_nat_iff {n : ℕ} (hf : AnalyticAt 𝕜 f z₀) : hf.order = ↑n ↔ ∃ (g : 𝕜 → E), AnalyticAt 𝕜 g z₀ ∧ g z₀ ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝 z₀, f z = (z - z₀) ^ n • g z

views.nl_informal:
The order of an analytic function `f` at `z₀` is finite iff `f` can locally be written as `f z =
  (z - z₀) ^ order • g z`, where `g` is analytic and does not vanish at `z₀`.

See `MeromorphicNFAt.order_eq_zero_iff` for an analogous statement about meromorphic functions in
normal form.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticAt.order_ne_top_iff (hf : AnalyticAt 𝕜 f z₀) : hf.order ≠ ⊤ ↔ ∃ (g : 𝕜 → E), AnalyticAt 𝕜 g z₀ ∧ g z₀ ≠ 0 ∧ f =ᶠ[𝓝 z₀] fun z ↦ (z - z₀) ^ (hf.order.toNat) • g z

views.nl_informal: The order of an analytic function `f` at `z₀` is zero iff `f` does not vanish at `z₀`.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticAt.order_eq_zero_iff (hf : AnalyticAt 𝕜 f z₀) : hf.order = 0 ↔ f z₀ ≠ 0

views.nl_informal: An analytic function vanishes at a point if its order is nonzero when converted to ℕ.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticAt.apply_eq_zero_of_order_toNat_ne_zero (hf : AnalyticAt 𝕜 f z₀) : hf.order.toNat ≠ 0 → f z₀ = 0

views.nl_informal:
Characterization of which natural numbers are `≤ hf.order`. Useful for avoiding case splits,
since it applies whether or not the order is `∞`.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticAt.natCast_le_order_iff (hf : AnalyticAt 𝕜 f z₀) {n : ℕ} : n ≤ hf.order ↔ ∃ g, AnalyticAt 𝕜 g z₀ ∧ ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝 z₀, f z = (z - z₀) ^ n • g z

views.nl_informal: If two functions agree in a neighborhood of `z₀`, then their orders at `z₀` agree.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticAt.order_congr (hf₁ : AnalyticAt 𝕜 f₁ z₀) (h : f₁ =ᶠ[𝓝 z₀] f₂) : (hf₁.congr h).order = hf₁.order

views.nl_informal: The order is additive when scalar multiplying analytic functions.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticAt.order_smul {f : 𝕜 → 𝕜} {g : 𝕜 → E} (hf : AnalyticAt 𝕜 f z₀) (hg : AnalyticAt 𝕜 g z₀) : (hf.smul hg).order = hf.order + hg.order

views.nl_informal: The order is additive when multiplying analytic functions.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticAt.order_mul {f g : 𝕜 → 𝕜} (hf : AnalyticAt 𝕜 f z₀) (hg : AnalyticAt 𝕜 g z₀) : (hf.mul hg).order = hf.order + hg.order

views.nl_informal: The order multiplies by `n` when taking an analytic function to its `n`th power.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticAt.order_pow {f : 𝕜 → 𝕜} (hf : AnalyticAt 𝕜 f z₀) {n : ℕ} : (hf.pow n).order = n • hf.order

views.nl_informal: The order of a sum is at least the minimum of the orders of the summands.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticAt.order_add (hf₁ : AnalyticAt 𝕜 f₁ z₀) (hf₂ : AnalyticAt 𝕜 f₂ z₀) : min hf₁.order hf₂.order ≤ (hf₁.add hf₂).order

views.nl_informal:
If two functions have unequal orders, then the order of their sum is exactly the minimum
of the orders of the summands.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticAt.order_add_of_order_ne_order (hf₁ : AnalyticAt 𝕜 f₁ z₀) (hf₂ : AnalyticAt 𝕜 f₂ z₀) (h : hf₁.order ≠ hf₂.order) : (hf₁.add hf₂).order = min hf₁.order hf₂.order

views.nl_informal: The set where an analytic function has infinite order is clopen in its domain of analyticity.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticOnNhd.isClopen_setOf_order_eq_top : IsClopen { u : U | (hf u.1 u.2).order = ⊤ }

views.nl_informal:
On a connected set, there exists a point where a meromorphic function `f` has finite order iff
`f` has finite order at every point.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticOnNhd.exists_order_ne_top_iff_forall (hU : IsConnected U) : (∃ u : U, (hf u u.2).order ≠ ⊤) ↔ (∀ u : U, (hf u u.2).order ≠ ⊤)

views.nl_informal:
On a preconnected set, a meromorphic function has finite order at one point if it has finite
order at another point.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticOnNhd.order_ne_top_of_isPreconnected {x y : 𝕜} (hU : IsPreconnected U) (h₁x : x ∈ U) (hy : y ∈ U) (h₂x : (hf x h₁x).order ≠ ⊤) : (hf y hy).order ≠ ⊤

views.nl_informal:
The set where an analytic function has zero or infinite order is discrete within its domain of
analyticity.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticOnNhd.codiscrete_setOf_order_eq_zero_or_top : {u : U | (hf u u.2).order = 0 ∨ (hf u u.2).order = ⊤} ∈ Filter.codiscrete U

views.nl_informal:
The radius of a formal multilinear series is equal to
$\liminf_{n\to\infty} \frac{1}{\sqrt[n]{‖p n‖}}$. The actual statement uses `ℝ≥0` and some
coercions.
views.lean_signature: theorem FormalMultilinearSeries.radius_eq_liminf : p.radius = liminf (fun n => (1 / (‖p n‖₊ ^ (1 / (n : ℝ)) : ℝ≥0) : ℝ≥0∞)) atTop

views.nl_informal:
If a formal multilinear series `p` represents the zero function at `x : E`, then the
terms `p n (fun i ↦ y)` appearing in the sum are zero for any `n : ℕ`, `y : E`.
views.lean_signature: theorem HasFPowerSeriesAt.apply_eq_zero {p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F} {x : E} (h : HasFPowerSeriesAt 0 p x) (n : ℕ) : ∀ y : E, (p n fun _ => y) = 0

views.nl_informal: A one-dimensional formal multilinear series representing the zero function is zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem HasFPowerSeriesAt.eq_zero {p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 𝕜 E} {x : 𝕜} (h : HasFPowerSeriesAt 0 p x) : p = 0

views.nl_informal: One-dimensional formal multilinear series representing the same function are equal.
views.lean_signature: theorem HasFPowerSeriesAt.eq_formalMultilinearSeries {p₁ p₂ : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 𝕜 E} {f : 𝕜 → E} {x : 𝕜} (h₁ : HasFPowerSeriesAt f p₁ x) (h₂ : HasFPowerSeriesAt f p₂ x) : p₁ = p₂

views.nl_informal: A one-dimensional formal multilinear series representing a locally zero function is zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem HasFPowerSeriesAt.eq_zero_of_eventually {p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 𝕜 E} {f : 𝕜 → E} {x : 𝕜} (hp : HasFPowerSeriesAt f p x) (hf : f =ᶠ[𝓝 x] 0) : p = 0

views.nl_informal:
If a function `f : 𝕜 → E` has two power series representations at `x`, then the given radii in
which convergence is guaranteed may be interchanged. This can be useful when the formal multilinear
series in one representation has a particularly nice form, but the other has a larger radius.
views.lean_signature: theorem HasFPowerSeriesOnBall.exchange_radius {p₁ p₂ : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 𝕜 E} {f : 𝕜 → E} {r₁ r₂ : ℝ≥0∞} {x : 𝕜} (h₁ : HasFPowerSeriesOnBall f p₁ x r₁) (h₂ : HasFPowerSeriesOnBall f p₂ x r₂) : HasFPowerSeriesOnBall f p₁ x r₂

views.nl_informal:
If a function `f : 𝕜 → E` has power series representation `p` on a ball of some radius and for
each positive radius it has some power series representation, then `p` converges to `f` on the whole
`𝕜`.
views.lean_signature: theorem HasFPowerSeriesOnBall.r_eq_top_of_exists {f : 𝕜 → E} {r : ℝ≥0∞} {x : 𝕜} {p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 𝕜 E} (h : HasFPowerSeriesOnBall f p x r) (h' : ∀ (r' : ℝ≥0) (_ : 0 < r'), ∃ p' : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 𝕜 E, HasFPowerSeriesOnBall f p' x r') : HasFPowerSeriesOnBall f p x ∞

views.nl_informal:
If an analytic function vanishes around a point, then it is uniformly zero along
a connected set. Superseded by `eqOn_zero_of_preconnected_of_locally_zero` which does not assume
completeness of the target space.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticOnNhd.eqOn_zero_of_preconnected_of_eventuallyEq_zero_aux [CompleteSpace F] {f : E → F} {U : Set E} (hf : AnalyticOnNhd 𝕜 f U) (hU : IsPreconnected U) {z₀ : E} (h₀ : z₀ ∈ U) (hfz₀ : f =ᶠ[𝓝 z₀] 0) : EqOn f 0 U

views.nl_informal:
The *identity principle* for analytic functions: If an analytic function vanishes in a whole
neighborhood of a point `z₀`, then it is uniformly zero along a connected set. For a one-dimensional
version assuming only that the function vanishes at some points arbitrarily close to `z₀`, see
`eqOn_zero_of_preconnected_of_frequently_eq_zero`.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticOnNhd.eqOn_zero_of_preconnected_of_eventuallyEq_zero {f : E → F} {U : Set E} (hf : AnalyticOnNhd 𝕜 f U) (hU : IsPreconnected U) {z₀ : E} (h₀ : z₀ ∈ U) (hfz₀ : f =ᶠ[𝓝 z₀] 0) : EqOn f 0 U

views.nl_informal:
The *identity principle* for analytic functions: If two analytic functions coincide in a whole
neighborhood of a point `z₀`, then they coincide globally along a connected set.
For a one-dimensional version assuming only that the functions coincide at some points
arbitrarily close to `z₀`, see `eqOn_of_preconnected_of_frequently_eq`.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticOnNhd.eqOn_of_preconnected_of_eventuallyEq {f g : E → F} {U : Set E} (hf : AnalyticOnNhd 𝕜 f U) (hg : AnalyticOnNhd 𝕜 g U) (hU : IsPreconnected U) {z₀ : E} (h₀ : z₀ ∈ U) (hfg : f =ᶠ[𝓝 z₀] g) : EqOn f g U

views.nl_informal:
The *identity principle* for analytic functions: If two analytic functions on a normed space
coincide in a neighborhood of a point `z₀`, then they coincide everywhere.
For a one-dimensional version assuming only that the functions coincide at some points
arbitrarily close to `z₀`, see `eq_of_frequently_eq`.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticOnNhd.eq_of_eventuallyEq {f g : E → F} [PreconnectedSpace E] (hf : AnalyticOnNhd 𝕜 f univ) (hg : AnalyticOnNhd 𝕜 g univ) {z₀ : E} (hfg : f =ᶠ[𝓝 z₀] g) : f = g

views.nl_informal: On open sets, `AnalyticOnNhd` and `AnalyticOn` coincide
views.lean_signature: theorem IsOpen.analyticOn_iff_analyticOnNhd {f : E → F} {s : Set E} (hs : IsOpen s) : AnalyticOn 𝕜 f s ↔ AnalyticOnNhd 𝕜 f s

views.nl_informal: `f` has power series `p` at `x` iff some local extension of `f` has that series
views.lean_signature: theorem hasFPowerSeriesWithinOnBall_iff_exists_hasFPowerSeriesOnBall [CompleteSpace F] {f : E → F} {p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F} {s : Set E} {x : E} {r : ℝ≥0∞} : HasFPowerSeriesWithinOnBall f p s x r ↔ ∃ g, EqOn f g (insert x s ∩ EMetric.ball x r) ∧ HasFPowerSeriesOnBall g p x r

views.nl_informal: `f` has power series `p` at `x` iff some local extension of `f` has that series
views.lean_signature: theorem hasFPowerSeriesWithinAt_iff_exists_hasFPowerSeriesAt [CompleteSpace F] {f : E → F} {p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F} {s : Set E} {x : E} : HasFPowerSeriesWithinAt f p s x ↔ ∃ g, f =ᶠ[𝓝[insert x s] x] g ∧ HasFPowerSeriesAt g p x

views.nl_informal: `f` is analytic within `s` at `x` iff some local extension of `f` is analytic at `x`
views.lean_signature: theorem analyticWithinAt_iff_exists_analyticAt [CompleteSpace F] {f : E → F} {s : Set E} {x : E} : AnalyticWithinAt 𝕜 f s x ↔ ∃ g, f =ᶠ[𝓝[insert x s] x] g ∧ AnalyticAt 𝕜 g x

views.nl_informal:
`f` is analytic within `s` at `x` iff some local extension of `f` is analytic at `x`. In this
version, we make sure that the extension coincides with `f` on all of `insert x s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem analyticWithinAt_iff_exists_analyticAt' [CompleteSpace F] {f : E → F} {s : Set E} {x : E} : AnalyticWithinAt 𝕜 f s x ↔ ∃ g, f x = g x ∧ EqOn f g (insert x s) ∧ AnalyticAt 𝕜 g x

views.nl_informal: Definition of `IsBigOWith`. We record it in a lemma as `IsBigOWith` is irreducible.
views.lean_signature: theorem Asymptotics.isBigOWith_iff : IsBigOWith c l f g ↔ ∀ᶠ x in l, ‖f x‖ ≤ c * ‖g x‖

views.nl_informal:
Definition of `IsBigO` in terms of `IsBigOWith`. We record it in a lemma as `IsBigO` is
irreducible.
views.lean_signature: theorem Asymptotics.isBigO_iff_isBigOWith : f =O[l] g ↔ ∃ c : ℝ, IsBigOWith c l f g

views.nl_informal: Definition of `IsBigO` in terms of filters.
views.lean_signature: theorem Asymptotics.isBigO_iff : f =O[l] g ↔ ∃ c : ℝ, ∀ᶠ x in l, ‖f x‖ ≤ c * ‖g x‖

views.nl_informal: Definition of `IsBigO` in terms of filters, with a positive constant.
views.lean_signature: theorem Asymptotics.isBigO_iff' {g : α → E'''} : f =O[l] g ↔ ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ x in l, ‖f x‖ ≤ c * ‖g x‖

views.nl_informal: Definition of `IsBigO` in terms of filters, with the constant in the lower bound.
views.lean_signature: theorem Asymptotics.isBigO_iff'' {g : α → E'''} : f =O[l] g ↔ ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ x in l, c * ‖f x‖ ≤ ‖g x‖

views.nl_informal: Definition of `IsLittleO` in terms of `IsBigOWith`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Asymptotics.isLittleO_iff_forall_isBigOWith : f =o[l] g ↔ ∀ ⦃c : ℝ⦄, 0 < c → IsBigOWith c l f g

views.nl_informal: Definition of `IsLittleO` in terms of filters.
views.lean_signature: theorem Asymptotics.isLittleO_iff : f =o[l] g ↔ ∀ ⦃c : ℝ⦄, 0 < c → ∀ᶠ x in l, ‖f x‖ ≤ c * ‖g x‖

views.nl_informal: `f = O(g)` if and only if `IsBigOWith c f g` for all sufficiently large `c`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Asymptotics.isBigO_iff_eventually_isBigOWith : f =O[l] g' ↔ ∀ᶠ c in atTop, IsBigOWith c l f g'

views.nl_informal: `f = O(g)` if and only if `∀ᶠ x in l, ‖f x‖ ≤ c * ‖g x‖` for all sufficiently large `c`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Asymptotics.isBigO_iff_eventually : f =O[l] g' ↔ ∀ᶠ c in atTop, ∀ᶠ x in l, ‖f x‖ ≤ c * ‖g' x‖

views.nl_informal: If `u = O(v)` along `l`, then `(u / v) * v = u` eventually at `l`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Asymptotics.IsBigO.eventually_mul_div_cancel (h : u =O[l] v) : u / v * v =ᶠ[l] u

views.nl_informal: If `u = o(v)` along `l`, then `(u / v) * v = u` eventually at `l`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Asymptotics.IsLittleO.eventually_mul_div_cancel (h : u =o[l] v) : u / v * v =ᶠ[l] u

views.nl_informal: The condition `f = O[𝓝[≠] a] 1` is equivalent to `f = O[𝓝 a] 1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Asymptotics.isBigO_one_nhds_ne_iff [TopologicalSpace α] {a : α} : f =O[𝓝[≠] a] (fun _ ↦ 1 : α → F) ↔ f =O[𝓝 a] (fun _ ↦ 1 : α → F)

views.nl_informal: `(fun x ↦ c) =O[l] f` if and only if `f` is bounded away from zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Asymptotics.isBigO_const_left_iff_pos_le_norm {c : E''} (hc : c ≠ 0) : (fun _x => c) =O[l] f' ↔ ∃ b, 0 < b ∧ ∀ᶠ x in l, b ≤ ‖f' x‖

views.nl_informal:
If `‖φ‖` is eventually bounded by `c`, and `u =ᶠ[l] φ * v`, then we have `IsBigOWith c u v l`.
This does not require any assumptions on `c`, which is why we keep this version along with
`IsBigOWith_iff_exists_eq_mul`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Asymptotics.isBigOWith_of_eq_mul {u v : α → R} (φ : α → R) (hφ : ∀ᶠ x in l, ‖φ x‖ ≤ c) (h : u =ᶠ[l] φ * v) : IsBigOWith c l u v

views.nl_informal:
If `f x = O(g x)` along `cofinite`, then there exists a positive constant `C` such that
`‖f x‖ ≤ C * ‖g x‖` whenever `g x ≠ 0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Asymptotics.bound_of_isBigO_cofinite (h : f =O[cofinite] g'') : ∃ C > 0, ∀ ⦃x⦄, g'' x ≠ 0 → ‖f x‖ ≤ C * ‖g'' x‖

views.nl_informal: Transfer `IsBigOWith` over a `PartialHomeomorph`.
views.lean_signature: theorem PartialHomeomorph.isBigOWith_congr (e : PartialHomeomorph α β) {b : β} (hb : b ∈ e.target) {f : β → E} {g : β → F} {C : ℝ} : IsBigOWith C (𝓝 b) f g ↔ IsBigOWith C (𝓝 (e.symm b)) (f ∘ e) (g ∘ e)

views.nl_informal: Transfer `IsBigO` over a `PartialHomeomorph`.

views.nl_informal:
**Henstock-Sacks inequality**. Let `r₁ r₂ : ℝⁿ → (0, ∞)` be a function such that for any tagged
*partition* of `I` subordinate to `rₖ`, `k=1,2`, the integral sum of `f` over this partition differs
from the integral of `f` by at most `εₖ`. Then for any two tagged *prepartition* `π₁ π₂` subordinate
to `r₁` and `r₂` respectively and covering the same part of `I`, the integral sums of `f` over these
prepartitions differ from each other by at most `ε₁ + ε₂`.

The actual statement

- uses `BoxIntegral.Integrable.convergenceR` instead of a predicate assumption on `r`;
- uses `BoxIntegral.IntegrationParams.MemBaseSet` instead of “subordinate to `r`” to
  account for additional requirements like being a Henstock partition or having a bounded
  distortion.

See also `BoxIntegral.Integrable.dist_integralSum_sum_integral_le_of_memBaseSet_of_iUnion_eq` and
`BoxIntegral.Integrable.dist_integralSum_sum_integral_le_of_memBaseSet`.

views.nl_informal:
**Henstock-Sacks inequality**. Let `r : ℝⁿ → (0, ∞)` be a function such that for any tagged
*partition* of `I` subordinate to `r`, the integral sum of `f` over this partition differs from the

views.nl_informal:
A function `f` has Henstock (or `⊥`) integral over `I` is equal to the value of a box-additive
function `g` on `I` provided that `vol J (f x)` is sufficiently close to `g J` for sufficiently
small boxes `J ∋ x`. This lemma is useful to prove, e.g., to prove the Divergence theorem for
integral along `⊥`.

Let `l` be either `BoxIntegral.IntegrationParams.Henstock` or `⊥`. Let `g` a box-additive function
on subboxes of `I`. Suppose that there exists a nonnegative box-additive function `B` and a
countable set `s` with the following property.

For every `c : ℝ≥0`, a point `x ∈ I.Icc`, and a positive `ε` there exists `δ > 0` such that for any
box `J ≤ I` such that

- `x ∈ J.Icc ⊆ Metric.closedBall x δ`;
- if `l.bDistortion` (i.e., `l = ⊥`), then the distortion of `J` is less than or equal to `c`,

the distance between the term `vol J (f x)` of an integral sum corresponding to `J` and `g J` is
less than or equal to `ε` if `x ∈ s` and is less than or equal to `ε * B J` otherwise.

Then `f` is integrable on `I` along `l` with integral `g I`.

views.nl_informal:
Suppose that there exists a nonnegative box-additive function `B` with the following property.

For every `c : ℝ≥0`, a point `x ∈ I.Icc`, and a positive `ε` there exists `δ > 0` such that for any
box `J ≤ I` such that

- `J.Icc ⊆ Metric.closedBall x δ`;
- if `l.bDistortion` (i.e., `l = ⊥`), then the distortion of `J` is less than or equal to `c`,

the distance between the term `vol J (f x)` of an integral sum corresponding to `J` and `g J` is

Then `f` is McShane integrable on `I` with integral `g I`.

views.nl_informal:
If `f : ℝⁿ⁺¹ → E` is differentiable on a closed rectangular box `I` with derivative `f'`, then
the partial derivative `fun x ↦ f' x (Pi.single i 1)` is Henstock-Kurzweil integrable with integral
equal to the difference of integrals of `f` over the faces `x i = I.upper i` and `x i = I.lower i`.

More precisely, we use a non-standard generalization of the Henstock-Kurzweil integral and
we allow `f` to be non-differentiable (but still continuous) at a countable set of points.

TODO: If `n > 0`, then the condition at `x ∈ s` can be replaced by a much weaker estimate but this
requires either better integrability theorems, or usage of a filter depending on the countable set
`s` (we need to ensure that none of the faces of a partition contain a point from `s`).
views.lean_signature: theorem BoxIntegral.hasIntegral_GP_pderiv (f : (Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) → E) (f' : (Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) → (Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) →L[ℝ] E) (s : Set (Fin (n + 1) → ℝ)) (hs : s.Countable) (Hs : ∀ x ∈ s, ContinuousWithinAt f (Box.Icc I) x) (Hd : ∀ x ∈ (Box.Icc I) \ s, HasFDerivWithinAt f (f' x) (Box.Icc I) x) (i : Fin (n + 1)) : HasIntegral.{0, u, u} I GP (fun x => f' x (Pi.single i 1)) BoxAdditiveMap.volume (integral.{0, u, u} (I.face i) GP (fun x => f (i.insertNth (I.upper i) x)) BoxAdditiveMap.volume - integral.{0, u, u} (I.face i) GP (fun x => f (i.insertNth (I.lower i) x)) BoxAdditiveMap.volume)

views.nl_informal:
Divergence theorem for a Henstock-Kurzweil style integral.

If `f : ℝⁿ⁺¹ → Eⁿ⁺¹` is differentiable on a closed rectangular box `I` with derivative `f'`, then
the divergence `∑ i, f' x (Pi.single i 1) i` is Henstock-Kurzweil integrable with integral equal to
the sum of integrals of `f` over the faces of `I` taken with appropriate signs.

More precisely, we use a non-standard generalization of the Henstock-Kurzweil integral and
we allow `f` to be non-differentiable (but still continuous) at a countable set of points.

hold true.

* `H_ind` : Consider a smaller box `J ≤ I`. The hyperplanes passing through the center of `J` split
  it into `2 ^ n` boxes. If `p` holds true on each of these boxes, then it true on `J`.

* `H_nhds` : For each `z` in the closed box `I.Icc` there exists a neighborhood `U` of `z` within
  `I.Icc` such that for every box `J ≤ I` such that `z ∈ J.Icc ⊆ U`, if `J` is homothetic to `I`
  with a coefficient of the form `1 / 2 ^ m`, then `p` is true on `J`.

Then `p I` is true. See also `BoxIntegral.Box.subbox_induction_on` for a version using
`BoxIntegral.Prepartition.splitCenter` instead of `BoxIntegral.Box.splitCenterBox`.

The proof still works if we assume `H_ind` only for subboxes `J ≤ I` that are homothetic to `I` with
a coefficient of the form `2⁻ᵐ` but we do not need this generalization yet.

Consider the contravariant functors between compact Hausdorff spaces and commutative unital
C⋆algebras `F : Cpct → CommCStarAlg := X ↦ C(X, ℂ)` and
`G : CommCStarAlg → Cpct := A → characterSpace ℂ A` whose actions on morphisms are given by
`WeakDual.CharacterSpace.compContinuousMap` and `ContinuousMap.compStarAlgHom'`, respectively.

Then `η : id → F ∘ G := gelfandStarTransform` is a natural isomorphism implementing (half of)
the duality between these categories. That is, for commutative unital C⋆-algebras `A` and `B` and
`φ : A →⋆ₐ[ℂ] B` the following diagram commutes:

```
A  --- η A ---> C(characterSpace ℂ A, ℂ)

|                     |

φ                  (F ∘ G) φ

|                     |
V                     V

B  --- η B ---> C(characterSpace ℂ B, ℂ)
```

Lagrange multipliers theorem: if `φ : E → ℝ` has a local extremum on the set `{x | f x = f x₀}`
at `x₀`, both `f : E → F` and `φ` are strictly differentiable at `x₀`, and the codomain of `f` is
a complete space, then the linear map `x ↦ (f' x, φ' x)` is not surjective.

views.nl_informal:
Lagrange multipliers theorem: if `φ : E → ℝ` has a local extremum on the set `{x | f x = f x₀}`
at `x₀`, both `f : E → F` and `φ` are strictly differentiable at `x₀`, and the codomain of `f` is
a complete space, then there exist `Λ : dual ℝ F` and `Λ₀ : ℝ` such that `(Λ, Λ₀) ≠ 0` and
`Λ (f' x) + Λ₀ • φ' x = 0` for all `x`.

views.nl_informal:
Lagrange multipliers theorem, 1d version. Let `f : ι → E → ℝ` be a finite family of functions.
Suppose that `φ : E → ℝ` has a local extremum on the set `{x | ∀ i, f i x = f i x₀}` at `x₀`.
Suppose that all functions `f i` as well as `φ` are strictly differentiable at `x₀`.
Then the derivatives `f' i : E → L[ℝ] ℝ` and `φ' : E →L[ℝ] ℝ` are linearly dependent:
there exist `Λ : ι → ℝ` and `Λ₀ : ℝ`, `(Λ, Λ₀) ≠ 0`, such that `∑ i, Λ i • f' i + Λ₀ • φ' = 0`.

states `¬LinearIndependent ℝ _` instead of existence of `Λ` and `Λ₀`.

views.nl_informal:
**Taylor's theorem** with the general mean value form of the remainder.

We assume that `f` is `n+1`-times continuously differentiable in the closed set `Icc x₀ x` and
`n+1`-times differentiable on the open set `Ioo x₀ x`, and `g` is a differentiable function on
`Ioo x₀ x` and continuous on `Icc x₀ x`. Then there exists an `x' ∈ Ioo x₀ x` such that
$$f(x) - (P_n f)(x₀, x) = \frac{(x - x')^n}{n!} \frac{g(x) - g(x₀)}{g' x'},$$
where $P_n f$ denotes the Taylor polynomial of degree $n$.
views.lean_signature: theorem taylor_mean_remainder {f : ℝ → ℝ} {g g' : ℝ → ℝ} {x x₀ : ℝ} {n : ℕ} (hx : x₀ < x) (hf : ContDiffOn ℝ n f (Icc x₀ x)) (hf' : DifferentiableOn ℝ (iteratedDerivWithin n f (Icc x₀ x)) (Ioo x₀ x)) (gcont : ContinuousOn g (Icc x₀ x)) (gdiff : ∀ x_1 : ℝ, x_1 ∈ Ioo x₀ x → HasDerivAt g (g' x_1) x_1) (g'_ne : ∀ x_1 : ℝ, x_1 ∈ Ioo x₀ x → g' x_1 ≠ 0) : ∃ x' ∈ Ioo x₀ x, f x - taylorWithinEval f n (Icc x₀ x) x₀ x = ((x - x') ^ n / n ! * (g x - g x₀) / g' x') • iteratedDerivWithin (n + 1) f (Icc x₀ x) x'

views.nl_informal:
**Taylor's theorem** with the Lagrange form of the remainder.

We assume that `f` is `n+1`-times continuously differentiable in the closed set `Icc x₀ x` and
`n+1`-times differentiable on the open set `Ioo x₀ x`. Then there exists an `x' ∈ Ioo x₀ x` such
that $$f(x) - (P_n f)(x₀, x) = \frac{f^{(n+1)}(x') (x - x₀)^{n+1}}{(n+1)!},$$
where $P_n f$ denotes the Taylor polynomial of degree $n$ and $f^{(n+1)}$ is the $n+1$-th iterated
derivative.
views.lean_signature: theorem taylor_mean_remainder_lagrange {f : ℝ → ℝ} {x x₀ : ℝ} {n : ℕ} (hx : x₀ < x) (hf : ContDiffOn ℝ n f (Icc x₀ x)) (hf' : DifferentiableOn ℝ (iteratedDerivWithin n f (Icc x₀ x)) (Ioo x₀ x)) : ∃ x' ∈ Ioo x₀ x, f x - taylorWithinEval f n (Icc x₀ x) x₀ x = iteratedDerivWithin (n + 1) f (Icc x₀ x) x' * (x - x₀) ^ (n + 1) / (n + 1)!

views.nl_informal:
**Taylor's theorem** with the Cauchy form of the remainder.

We assume that `f` is `n+1`-times continuously differentiable on the closed set `Icc x₀ x` and
`n+1`-times differentiable on the open set `Ioo x₀ x`. Then there exists an `x' ∈ Ioo x₀ x` such
that $$f(x) - (P_n f)(x₀, x) = \frac{f^{(n+1)}(x') (x - x')^n (x-x₀)}{n!},$$
where $P_n f$ denotes the Taylor polynomial of degree $n$ and $f^{(n+1)}$ is the $n+1$-th iterated
derivative.
views.lean_signature: theorem taylor_mean_remainder_cauchy {f : ℝ → ℝ} {x x₀ : ℝ} {n : ℕ} (hx : x₀ < x) (hf : ContDiffOn ℝ n f (Icc x₀ x)) (hf' : DifferentiableOn ℝ (iteratedDerivWithin n f (Icc x₀ x)) (Ioo x₀ x)) : ∃ x' ∈ Ioo x₀ x, f x - taylorWithinEval f n (Icc x₀ x) x₀ x = iteratedDerivWithin (n + 1) f (Icc x₀ x) x' * (x - x') ^ n / n ! * (x - x₀)

**Taylor's theorem** with a polynomial bound on the remainder

We assume that `f` is `n+1`-times continuously differentiable on the closed set `Icc a b`.
The difference of `f` and its `n`-th Taylor polynomial can be estimated by

We assume that `f` is `n+1`-times continuously differentiable on the closed set `Icc a b`.

views.nl_informal:
One direction of `contDiffWithinAt_succ_iff_hasFDerivWithinAt`, but where all derivatives are
taken within the same set. Version for partial derivatives / functions with parameters. If `f x` is
a `C^n+1` family of functions and `g x` is a `C^n` family of points, then the derivative of `f x` at
`g x` depends in a `C^n` way on `x`. We give a general version of this fact relative to sets which
may not have unique derivatives, in the following form.  If `f : E × F → G` is `C^n+1` at
`(x₀, g(x₀))` in `(s ∪ {x₀}) × t ⊆ E × F` and `g : E → F` is `C^n` at `x₀` within some set `s ⊆ E`,
then there is a function `f' : E → F →L[𝕜] G` that is `C^n` at `x₀` within `s` such that for all `x`
sufficiently close to `x₀` within `s ∪ {x₀}` the function `y ↦ f x y` has derivative `f' x` at `g x`
within `t ⊆ F`.  For convenience, we return an explicit set of `x`'s where this holds that is a
subset of `s ∪ {x₀}`.  We need one additional condition, namely that `t` is a neighborhood of
`g(x₀)` within `g '' s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContDiffWithinAt.hasFDerivWithinAt_nhds {f : E → F → G} {g : E → F} {t : Set F} (hn : n ≠ ∞) {x₀ : E} (hf : ContDiffWithinAt 𝕜 (n + 1) (uncurry f) (insert x₀ s ×ˢ t) (x₀, g x₀)) (hg : ContDiffWithinAt 𝕜 n g s x₀) (hgt : t ∈ 𝓝[g '' s] g x₀) : ∃ v ∈ 𝓝[insert x₀ s] x₀, v ⊆ insert x₀ s ∧ ∃ f' : E → F →L[𝕜] G, (∀ x ∈ v, HasFDerivWithinAt (f x) (f' x) t (g x)) ∧ ContDiffWithinAt 𝕜 n (fun x => f' x) s x₀

iterated derivatives of `f` and `g` when `B` is bilinear. This lemma is an auxiliary version
assuming all spaces live in the same universe, to enable an induction. Use instead

views.lean_signature: theorem ContinuousLinearMap.norm_iteratedFDerivWithin_le_of_bilinear_aux {Du Eu Fu Gu : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup Du] [NormedSpace 𝕜 Du] [NormedAddCommGroup Eu] [NormedSpace 𝕜 Eu] [NormedAddCommGroup Fu] [NormedSpace 𝕜 Fu] [NormedAddCommGroup Gu] [NormedSpace 𝕜 Gu] (B : Eu →L[𝕜] Fu →L[𝕜] Gu) {f : Du → Eu} {g : Du → Fu} {n : ℕ} {s : Set Du} {x : Du} (hf : ContDiffOn 𝕜 n f s) (hg : ContDiffOn 𝕜 n g s) (hs : UniqueDiffOn 𝕜 s) (hx : x ∈ s) : ‖iteratedFDerivWithin 𝕜 n (fun y => B (f y) (g y)) s x‖ ≤ ‖B‖ * ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), (n.choose i : ℝ) * ‖iteratedFDerivWithin 𝕜 i f s x‖ * ‖iteratedFDerivWithin 𝕜 (n - i) g s x‖

iterated derivatives of `f` and `g` when `B` is bilinear:
`‖D^n (x ↦ B (f x) (g x))‖ ≤ ‖B‖ ∑_{k ≤ n} n.choose k ‖D^k f‖ ‖D^{n-k} g‖`

views.nl_informal:
Bounding the norm of the iterated derivative of `B (f x) (g x)` in terms of the
iterated derivatives of `f` and `g` when `B` is bilinear:
`‖D^n (x ↦ B (f x) (g x))‖ ≤ ‖B‖ ∑_{k ≤ n} n.choose k ‖D^k f‖ ‖D^{n-k} g‖`

views.nl_informal:
Bounding the norm of the iterated derivative of `B (f x) (g x)` in terms of the
iterated derivatives of `f` and `g` when `B` is bilinear of norm at most `1`:

views.nl_informal:
If the derivatives within a set of `g` at `f x` are bounded by `C`, and the `i`-th derivative
within a set of `f` at `x` is bounded by `D^i` for all `1 ≤ i ≤ n`, then the `n`-th derivative
of `g ∘ f` is bounded by `n! * C * D^n`.
This lemma proves this estimate assuming additionally that two of the spaces live in the same
universe, to make an induction possible. Use instead `norm_iteratedFDerivWithin_comp_le` that
removes this assumption.
views.lean_signature: theorem norm_iteratedFDerivWithin_comp_le_aux {Fu Gu : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup Fu] [NormedSpace 𝕜 Fu] [NormedAddCommGroup Gu] [NormedSpace 𝕜 Gu] {g : Fu → Gu} {f : E → Fu} {n : ℕ} {s : Set E} {t : Set Fu} {x : E} (hg : ContDiffOn 𝕜 n g t) (hf : ContDiffOn 𝕜 n f s) (ht : UniqueDiffOn 𝕜 t) (hs : UniqueDiffOn 𝕜 s) (hst : MapsTo f s t) (hx : x ∈ s) {C : ℝ} {D : ℝ} (hC : ∀ i, i ≤ n → ‖iteratedFDerivWithin 𝕜 i g t (f x)‖ ≤ C) (hD : ∀ i, 1 ≤ i → i ≤ n → ‖iteratedFDerivWithin 𝕜 i f s x‖ ≤ D ^ i) : ‖iteratedFDerivWithin 𝕜 n (g ∘ f) s x‖ ≤ n ! * C * D ^ n

views.nl_informal:
If the derivatives within a set of `g` at `f x` are bounded by `C`, and the `i`-th derivative
within a set of `f` at `x` is bounded by `D^i` for all `1 ≤ i ≤ n`, then the `n`-th derivative
of `g ∘ f` is bounded by `n! * C * D^n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem norm_iteratedFDerivWithin_comp_le {g : F → G} {f : E → F} {n : ℕ} {s : Set E} {t : Set F} {x : E} {N : WithTop ℕ∞} (hg : ContDiffOn 𝕜 N g t) (hf : ContDiffOn 𝕜 N f s) (hn : n ≤ N) (ht : UniqueDiffOn 𝕜 t) (hs : UniqueDiffOn 𝕜 s) (hst : MapsTo f s t) (hx : x ∈ s) {C : ℝ} {D : ℝ} (hC : ∀ i, i ≤ n → ‖iteratedFDerivWithin 𝕜 i g t (f x)‖ ≤ C) (hD : ∀ i, 1 ≤ i → i ≤ n → ‖iteratedFDerivWithin 𝕜 i f s x‖ ≤ D ^ i) : ‖iteratedFDerivWithin 𝕜 n (g ∘ f) s x‖ ≤ n ! * C * D ^ n

views.nl_informal:
If the derivatives of `g` at `f x` are bounded by `C`, and the `i`-th derivative
of `f` at `x` is bounded by `D^i` for all `1 ≤ i ≤ n`, then the `n`-th derivative
of `g ∘ f` is bounded by `n! * C * D^n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem norm_iteratedFDeriv_comp_le {g : F → G} {f : E → F} {n : ℕ} {N : WithTop ℕ∞} (hg : ContDiff 𝕜 N g) (hf : ContDiff 𝕜 N f) (hn : n ≤ N) (x : E) {C : ℝ} {D : ℝ} (hC : ∀ i, i ≤ n → ‖iteratedFDeriv 𝕜 i g (f x)‖ ≤ C) (hD : ∀ i, 1 ≤ i → i ≤ n → ‖iteratedFDeriv 𝕜 i f x‖ ≤ D ^ i) : ‖iteratedFDeriv 𝕜 n (g ∘ f) x‖ ≤ n ! * C * D ^ n

views.nl_informal: A polynomial function is infinitely differentiable.
views.lean_signature: theorem CPolynomialOn.contDiffOn (h : CPolynomialOn 𝕜 f s) {n : WithTop ℕ∞} : ContDiffOn 𝕜 n f s

views.nl_informal:
When `n` is either a natural number or `ω`, one can characterize the property of being `C^n`
as the existence of a neighborhood on which there is a Taylor series up to order `n`,
requiring in addition that its terms are analytic in the `ω` case.
views.lean_signature: theorem contDiffWithinAt_iff_of_ne_infty (hn : n ≠ ∞) : ContDiffWithinAt 𝕜 n f s x ↔ ∃ u ∈ 𝓝[insert x s] x, ∃ p : E → FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F, HasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn n f p u ∧ (n = ω → ∀ i, AnalyticOn 𝕜 (fun x ↦ p x i) u)

views.nl_informal:
In a complete space, a function which is analytic within a set at a point is also `C^ω` there.
Note that the same statement for `AnalyticOn` does not require completeness, see
`AnalyticOn.contDiffOn`.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticWithinAt.contDiffWithinAt [CompleteSpace F] (h : AnalyticWithinAt 𝕜 f s x) : ContDiffWithinAt 𝕜 n f s x

views.nl_informal:
If a function is `C^n` within a set at a point, with `n ≥ 1`, then it is differentiable
within this set at this point.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContDiffWithinAt.differentiableWithinAt' (h : ContDiffWithinAt 𝕜 n f s x) (hn : 1 ≤ n) : DifferentiableWithinAt 𝕜 f (insert x s) x

views.nl_informal:
A function is `C^(n + 1)` on a domain iff locally, it has a derivative which is `C^n`
(and moreover the function is analytic when `n = ω`).
views.lean_signature: theorem contDiffWithinAt_succ_iff_hasFDerivWithinAt (hn : n ≠ ∞) : ContDiffWithinAt 𝕜 (n + 1) f s x ↔ ∃ u ∈ 𝓝[insert x s] x, (n = ω → AnalyticOn 𝕜 f u) ∧ ∃ f' : E → E →L[𝕜] F, (∀ x ∈ u, HasFDerivWithinAt f (f' x) u x) ∧ ContDiffWithinAt 𝕜 n f' u x

views.nl_informal:
A function is `C^n` within a set at a point, for `n : ℕ`, if and only if it is `C^n` on
a neighborhood of this point.
views.lean_signature: theorem contDiffWithinAt_iff_contDiffOn_nhds (hn : n ≠ ∞) : ContDiffWithinAt 𝕜 n f s x ↔ ∃ u ∈ 𝓝[insert x s] x, ContDiffOn 𝕜 n f u

views.nl_informal: If a function is `C^n` on a set with `n ≥ 1`, then it is differentiable there.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContDiffOn.differentiableOn (h : ContDiffOn 𝕜 n f s) (hn : 1 ≤ n) : DifferentiableOn 𝕜 f s

views.nl_informal: If a function is `C^n` around each point in a set, then it is `C^n` on the set.
views.lean_signature: theorem contDiffOn_of_locally_contDiffOn (h : ∀ x ∈ s, ∃ u, IsOpen u ∧ x ∈ u ∧ ContDiffOn 𝕜 n f (s ∩ u)) : ContDiffOn 𝕜 n f s

views.nl_informal: A function is `C^(n + 1)` on a domain iff locally, it has a derivative which is `C^n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem contDiffOn_succ_iff_hasFDerivWithinAt (hn : n ≠ ∞) : ContDiffOn 𝕜 (n + 1) f s ↔ ∀ x ∈ s, ∃ u ∈ 𝓝[insert x s] x, (n = ω → AnalyticOn 𝕜 f u) ∧ ∃ f' : E → E →L[𝕜] F, (∀ x ∈ u, HasFDerivWithinAt f (f' x) u x) ∧ ContDiffOn 𝕜 n f' u

views.nl_informal:
When a function is `C^n` in a set `s` of unique differentiability, it admits
`ftaylorSeriesWithin 𝕜 f s` as a Taylor series up to order `n` in `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContDiffOn.ftaylorSeriesWithin (h : ContDiffOn 𝕜 n f s) (hs : UniqueDiffOn 𝕜 s) : HasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn n f (ftaylorSeriesWithin 𝕜 f s) s

views.nl_informal:
On a set with unique differentiability, an analytic function is automatically `C^ω`, as its
successive derivatives are also analytic. This does not require completeness of the space. See
also `AnalyticOn.contDiffOn_of_completeSpace`.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticOn.contDiffOn (h : AnalyticOn 𝕜 f s) (hs : UniqueDiffOn 𝕜 s) : ContDiffOn 𝕜 n f s

views.nl_informal:
On a set with unique differentiability, an analytic function is automatically `C^ω`, as its
successive derivatives are also analytic. This does not require completeness of the space. See
also `AnalyticOnNhd.contDiffOn_of_completeSpace`.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticOnNhd.contDiffOn (h : AnalyticOnNhd 𝕜 f s) (hs : UniqueDiffOn 𝕜 s) : ContDiffOn 𝕜 n f s

views.nl_informal: An analytic function is automatically `C^ω` in a complete space
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticOn.contDiffOn_of_completeSpace [CompleteSpace F] (h : AnalyticOn 𝕜 f s) : ContDiffOn 𝕜 n f s

views.nl_informal: An analytic function is automatically `C^ω` in a complete space
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticOnNhd.contDiffOn_of_completeSpace [CompleteSpace F] (h : AnalyticOnNhd 𝕜 f s) : ContDiffOn 𝕜 n f s

views.nl_informal:
A function is `C^(n + 1)` on a domain with unique derivatives if and only if it is
differentiable there, and its derivative (expressed with `fderivWithin`) is `C^n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem contDiffOn_succ_iff_fderivWithin (hs : UniqueDiffOn 𝕜 s) : ContDiffOn 𝕜 (n + 1) f s ↔ DifferentiableOn 𝕜 f s ∧ (n = ω → AnalyticOn 𝕜 f s) ∧ ContDiffOn 𝕜 n (fderivWithin 𝕜 f s) s

views.nl_informal:
A function is `C^(n + 1)` on an open domain if and only if it is
differentiable there, and its derivative (expressed with `fderiv`) is `C^n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem contDiffOn_succ_iff_fderiv_of_isOpen (hs : IsOpen s) : ContDiffOn 𝕜 (n + 1) f s ↔ DifferentiableOn 𝕜 f s ∧ (n = ω → AnalyticOn 𝕜 f s) ∧ ContDiffOn 𝕜 n (fderiv 𝕜 f) s

views.nl_informal:
In a complete space, a function which is analytic at a point is also `C^ω` there.
Note that the same statement for `AnalyticOn` does not require completeness, see
`AnalyticOn.contDiffOn`.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticAt.contDiffAt [CompleteSpace F] (h : AnalyticAt 𝕜 f x) : ContDiffAt 𝕜 n f x

views.nl_informal: If a function is `C^n` with `n ≥ 1` at a point, then it is differentiable there.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContDiffAt.differentiableAt (h : ContDiffAt 𝕜 n f x) (hn : 1 ≤ n) : DifferentiableAt 𝕜 f x

views.nl_informal: A function is `C^(n + 1)` at a point iff locally, it has a derivative which is `C^n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem contDiffAt_succ_iff_hasFDerivAt {n : ℕ} : ContDiffAt 𝕜 (n + 1) f x ↔ ∃ f' : E → E →L[𝕜] F, (∃ u ∈ 𝓝 x, ∀ x ∈ u, HasFDerivAt f (f' x) x) ∧ ContDiffAt 𝕜 n f' x

views.nl_informal: If `f` has a Taylor series up to `n`, then it is `C^n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem HasFTaylorSeriesUpTo.contDiff {n : ℕ∞} {f' : E → FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F} (hf : HasFTaylorSeriesUpTo n f f') : ContDiff 𝕜 n f

views.nl_informal: If a function is `C^n` with `n ≥ 1`, then it is differentiable.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContDiff.differentiable (h : ContDiff 𝕜 n f) (hn : 1 ≤ n) : Differentiable 𝕜 f

views.nl_informal: A function is `C^(n+1)` iff it has a `C^n` derivative.
views.lean_signature: theorem contDiff_succ_iff_hasFDerivAt {n : ℕ} : ContDiff 𝕜 (n + 1) f ↔ ∃ f' : E → E →L[𝕜] F, ContDiff 𝕜 n f' ∧ ∀ x, HasFDerivAt f (f' x) x

views.nl_informal:
When a function is `C^n`, it admits `ftaylorSeries 𝕜 f` as a Taylor series up
to order `n` in `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContDiff.ftaylorSeries (hf : ContDiff 𝕜 n f) : HasFTaylorSeriesUpTo n f (ftaylorSeries 𝕜 f)

views.nl_informal:
For `n : ℕ∞`, a function is `C^n` iff it admits `ftaylorSeries 𝕜 f`
as a Taylor series up to order `n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem contDiff_iff_ftaylorSeries {n : ℕ∞} : ContDiff 𝕜 n f ↔ HasFTaylorSeriesUpTo n f (ftaylorSeries 𝕜 f)

views.nl_informal: If `f` is `C^n` then its `m`-times iterated derivative is continuous for `m ≤ n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContDiff.continuous_iteratedFDeriv {m : ℕ} (hm : m ≤ n) (hf : ContDiff 𝕜 n f) : Continuous fun x => iteratedFDeriv 𝕜 m f x

views.nl_informal: If `f` is `C^n` then its `m`-times iterated derivative is differentiable for `m < n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContDiff.differentiable_iteratedFDeriv {m : ℕ} (hm : m < n) (hf : ContDiff 𝕜 n f) : Differentiable 𝕜 fun x => iteratedFDeriv 𝕜 m f x

views.nl_informal:
A function is `C^(n + 1)` if and only if it is differentiable,
and its derivative (formulated in terms of `fderiv`) is `C^n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem contDiff_succ_iff_fderiv : ContDiff 𝕜 (n + 1) f ↔ Differentiable 𝕜 f ∧ (n = ω → AnalyticOnNhd 𝕜 f univ) ∧ ContDiff 𝕜 n (fderiv 𝕜 f)

views.nl_informal:
If a function is at least `C^1`, its bundled derivative (mapping `(x, v)` to `Df(x) v`) is
continuous.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContDiff.continuous_fderiv_apply (h : ContDiff 𝕜 n f) (hn : 1 ≤ n) : Continuous fun p : E × E => (fderiv 𝕜 f p.1 : E → F) p.2

views.nl_informal:
If two functions coincide on a set `s`, then a Taylor series for the first one is as well a
Taylor series for the second one.
views.lean_signature: theorem HasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn.congr (h : HasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn n f p s) (h₁ : ∀ x ∈ s, f₁ x = f x) : HasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn n f₁ p s

views.nl_informal:
In the case that `n = ∞` we don't need the continuity assumption in
`HasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn`.
views.lean_signature: theorem hasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn_top_iff' (hN : ∞ ≤ N) : HasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn N f p s ↔ (∀ x ∈ s, (p x 0).curry0 = f x) ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, ∀ x ∈ s, HasFDerivWithinAt (fun y => p y m) (p x m.succ).curryLeft s x

views.nl_informal:
If a function has a Taylor series at order at least `1`, then the term of order `1` of this
series is a derivative of `f`.
views.lean_signature: theorem HasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn.hasFDerivWithinAt (h : HasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn n f p s) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (hx : x ∈ s) : HasFDerivWithinAt f (continuousMultilinearCurryFin1 𝕜 E F (p x 1)) s x

views.nl_informal:
If a function has a Taylor series at order at least `1` on a neighborhood of `x`, then the term
of order `1` of this series is a derivative of `f` at `x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem HasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn.hasFDerivAt (h : HasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn n f p s) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (hx : s ∈ 𝓝 x) : HasFDerivAt f (continuousMultilinearCurryFin1 𝕜 E F (p x 1)) x

views.nl_informal:
If a function has a Taylor series at order at least `1` on a neighborhood of `x`, then
in a neighborhood of `x`, the term of order `1` of this series is a derivative of `f`.
views.lean_signature: theorem HasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn.eventually_hasFDerivAt (h : HasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn n f p s) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (hx : s ∈ 𝓝 x) : ∀ᶠ y in 𝓝 x, HasFDerivAt f (continuousMultilinearCurryFin1 𝕜 E F (p y 1)) y

views.nl_informal:
If a function has a Taylor series at order at least `1` on a neighborhood of `x`, then
it is differentiable at `x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem HasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn.differentiableAt (h : HasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn n f p s) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (hx : s ∈ 𝓝 x) : DifferentiableAt 𝕜 f x

views.nl_informal:
`p` is a Taylor series of `f` up to `n+1` if and only if `p` is a Taylor series up to `n`, and
`p (n + 1)` is a derivative of `p n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem hasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn_succ_iff_left {n : ℕ} : HasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn (n + 1) f p s ↔ HasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn n f p s ∧ (∀ x ∈ s, HasFDerivWithinAt (fun y => p y n) (p x n.succ).curryLeft s x) ∧ ContinuousOn (fun x => p x (n + 1)) s

views.nl_informal:
`p` is a Taylor series of `f` up to `n+1` if and only if `p.shift` is a Taylor series up to `n`
for `p 1`, which is a derivative of `f`. Version for `n : ℕ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem hasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn_succ_nat_iff_right {n : ℕ} : HasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn (n + 1 : ℕ) f p s ↔ (∀ x ∈ s, (p x 0).curry0 = f x) ∧ (∀ x ∈ s, HasFDerivWithinAt (fun y => p y 0) (p x 1).curryLeft s x) ∧ HasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn n (fun x => continuousMultilinearCurryFin1 𝕜 E F (p x 1)) (fun x => (p x).shift) s

views.nl_informal:
`p` is a Taylor series of `f` up to `⊤` if and only if `p.shift` is a Taylor series up to `⊤`
for `p 1`, which is a derivative of `f`.
views.lean_signature: theorem hasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn_top_iff_right (hN : ∞ ≤ N) : HasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn N f p s ↔ (∀ x ∈ s, (p x 0).curry0 = f x) ∧ (∀ x ∈ s, HasFDerivWithinAt (fun y => p y 0) (p x 1).curryLeft s x) ∧ HasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn N (fun x => continuousMultilinearCurryFin1 𝕜 E F (p x 1)) (fun x => (p x).shift) s

views.nl_informal:
`p` is a Taylor series of `f` up to `n+1` if and only if `p.shift` is a Taylor series up to `n`
for `p 1`, which is a derivative of `f`. Version for `n : WithTop ℕ∞`.
views.lean_signature: theorem hasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn_succ_iff_right : HasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn (n + 1) f p s ↔ (∀ x ∈ s, (p x 0).curry0 = f x) ∧ (∀ x ∈ s, HasFDerivWithinAt (fun y => p y 0) (p x 1).curryLeft s x) ∧ HasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn n (fun x => continuousMultilinearCurryFin1 𝕜 E F (p x 1)) (fun x => (p x).shift) s

views.nl_informal:
Writing explicitly the `n+1`-th derivative as the composition of a currying linear equiv,
and the derivative of the `n`-th derivative.
views.lean_signature: theorem iteratedFDerivWithin_succ_eq_comp_left {n : ℕ} : iteratedFDerivWithin 𝕜 (n + 1) f s = (continuousMultilinearCurryLeftEquiv 𝕜 (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => E) F).symm ∘ fderivWithin 𝕜 (iteratedFDerivWithin 𝕜 n f s) s

views.nl_informal:
Writing explicitly the `n+1`-th derivative as the composition of a currying linear equiv,
and the `n`-th derivative of the derivative.
views.lean_signature: theorem iteratedFDerivWithin_succ_eq_comp_right {n : ℕ} (hs : UniqueDiffOn 𝕜 s) (hx : x ∈ s) : iteratedFDerivWithin 𝕜 (n + 1) f s x = ((continuousMultilinearCurryRightEquiv' 𝕜 n E F).symm ∘ iteratedFDerivWithin 𝕜 n (fun y => fderivWithin 𝕜 f s y) s) x

views.nl_informal:
On a set of unique differentiability, the second derivative is obtained by taking the
derivative of the derivative.
views.lean_signature: theorem iteratedFDerivWithin_two_apply (f : E → F) {z : E} (hs : UniqueDiffOn 𝕜 s) (hz : z ∈ s) (m : Fin 2 → E) : iteratedFDerivWithin 𝕜 2 f s z m = fderivWithin 𝕜 (fderivWithin 𝕜 f s) s z (m 0) (m 1)

views.nl_informal:

new atom to the left corresponds to applying `p 1` on the first coordinates, and the initial
ordered partition on the other coordinates.

If `f` has derivative `f'` within `s` at `x`, then for any `r > ‖f'‖` the ratio
`‖f z - f x‖ / ‖z - x‖` is less than `r` in some neighborhood of `x` within `s`.
In other words, the limit superior of this ratio as `z` tends to `x` along `s`
is less than or equal to `‖f'‖`.

views.nl_informal:
If `f` has derivative `f'` within `s` at `x`, then for any `r > ‖f'‖` the ratio
`(‖f z‖ - ‖f x‖) / ‖z - x‖` is less than `r` in some neighborhood of `x` within `s`.
In other words, the limit superior of this ratio as `z` tends to `x` along `s`
is less than or equal to `‖f'‖`.

where `‖f z‖ - ‖f x‖` is replaced by `‖f z - f x‖`.

views.nl_informal:
If `f` has derivative `f'` within `(x, +∞)` at `x`, then for any `r > ‖f'‖` the ratio
`‖f z - f x‖ / ‖z - x‖` is frequently less than `r` as `z → x+0`.
In other words, the limit inferior of this ratio as `z` tends to `x+0`
is less than or equal to `‖f'‖`. See also `HasDerivWithinAt.limsup_norm_slope_le`
for a stronger version using limit superior and any set `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem HasDerivWithinAt.liminf_right_norm_slope_le (hf : HasDerivWithinAt f f' (Ici x) x) (hr : ‖f'‖ < r) : ∃ᶠ z in 𝓝[>] x, ‖z - x‖⁻¹ * ‖f z - f x‖ < r

views.nl_informal:

In other words, the limit inferior of this ratio as `z` tends to `x+0`
is less than or equal to `‖f'‖`.

See also

* `HasDerivWithinAt.limsup_norm_slope_le` for a stronger version using
  limit superior and any set `s`;
* `HasDerivWithinAt.liminf_right_norm_slope_le` for a stronger version using
  `‖f z - f xp‖` instead of `‖f z‖ - ‖f x‖`.
views.lean_signature: theorem HasDerivWithinAt.liminf_right_slope_norm_le (hf : HasDerivWithinAt f f' (Ici x) x) (hr : ‖f'‖ < r) : ∃ᶠ z in 𝓝[>] x, (z - x)⁻¹ * (‖f z‖ - ‖f x‖) < r

i.e., `n (f (x + (1/n) v) - f x)` converges to `f' v`. More generally, if `c n` tends to infinity
and `c n * d n` tends to `v`, then `c n * (f (x + d n) - f x)` tends to `f' v`. This lemma expresses
this fact, for functions having a derivative within a set. Its specific formulation is useful for
tangent cone related discussions.

views.nl_informal:
Assume that `f` is differentiable inside a convex set `s`, and that its derivative `f'` is
differentiable at a point `x`. Then, given two vectors `v` and `w` pointing inside `s`, one can
Taylor-expand to order two the function `f` on the segment `[x + h v, x + h (v + w)]`, giving a
bilinear estimate for `f (x + hv + hw) - f (x + hv)` in terms of `f' w` and of `f'' ⬝ w`, up to
`o(h^2)`.

This is a technical statement used to show that the second derivative is symmetric.
views.lean_signature: theorem Convex.taylor_approx_two_segment {v w : E} (hv : x + v ∈ interior s) (hw : x + v + w ∈ interior s) : (fun h : ℝ => f (x + h • v + h • w) - f (x + h • v) - h • f' x w - h ^ 2 • f'' v w - (h ^ 2 / 2) • f'' w w) =o[𝓝[>] 0] fun h => h ^ 2

views.nl_informal:
One can get `f'' v w` as the limit of `h ^ (-2)` times the alternate sum of the values of `f`
along the vertices of a quadrilateral with sides `h v` and `h w` based at `x`.
In a setting where `f` is not guaranteed to be continuous at `f`, we can still
get this if we use a quadrilateral based at `h v + h w`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Convex.isLittleO_alternate_sum_square {v w : E} (h4v : x + (4 : ℝ) • v ∈ interior s) (h4w : x + (4 : ℝ) • w ∈ interior s) : (fun h : ℝ => f (x + h • (2 • v + 2 • w)) + f (x + h • (v + w)) - f (x + h • (2 • v + w)) - f (x + h • (v + 2 • w)) - h ^ 2 • f'' v w) =o[𝓝[>] 0] fun h => h ^ 2

views.nl_informal:

differentiable at a point `x`. Then, given two vectors `v` and `w` pointing inside `s`, one
has `f'' v w = f'' w v`. Superseded by `Convex.second_derivative_within_at_symmetric`, which
removes the assumption that `v` and `w` point inside `s`.

of `z₀`, or behaves locally like an open function (in the sense that the image of every neighborhood
of `z₀` is a neighborhood of `f z₀`, as in `isOpenMap_iff_nhds_le`). For a function `f : E → ℂ`

views.nl_informal:

is analytic at a point `z₀`, then either it is constant in a neighborhood of `z₀`, or it maps every
neighborhood of `z₀` to a neighborhood of `z₀`. For the particular case of a holomorphic function on

views.nl_informal:

Let `f : ℂ → E` be a function such that

* `f` is differentiable on `U` and is continuous on its closure;
* `‖f z‖` is bounded from above by `A * exp(B * exp(c * |re z|))` on `U` for some `c < π / (b - a)`;
* `‖f z‖` is bounded from above by a constant `C` on the boundary of `U`.

`{z : ℂ | a ≤ im z ≤ b}`. Moreover, it suffices to verify the second assumption
only for sufficiently large values of `|re z|`.

views.nl_informal:
If M is a positive scalar multiple of a doubly stochastic matrix, then there is a permutation matrix
whose support is contained in the support of M.
views.lean_signature: theorem exists_perm_eq_zero_implies_eq_zero [Nonempty n] {s : R} (hs : 0 < s) (hM : ∃ M' ∈ doublyStochastic R n, M = s • M') : ∃ σ : Equiv.Perm n, ∀ i j, M i j = 0 → σ.permMatrix R i j = 0

views.nl_informal:
If M is a scalar multiple of a doubly stochastic matrix, then it is a conical combination of
permutation matrices. This is most useful when M is a doubly stochastic matrix, in which case
the combination is convex.

This particular formulation is chosen to make the inductive step easier: we no longer need to
rescale each time a permutation matrix is subtracted.
views.lean_signature: theorem doublyStochastic_sum_perm_aux (M : Matrix n n R) (s : R) (hs : 0 ≤ s) (hM : ∃ M' ∈ doublyStochastic R n, M = s • M') : ∃ w : Equiv.Perm n → R, (∀ σ, 0 ≤ w σ) ∧ ∑ σ, w σ • σ.permMatrix R = M

views.nl_informal:
If M is a doubly stochastic matrix, then it is an convex combination of permutation matrices. Note
`doublyStochastic_eq_convexHull_permMatrix` shows `doublyStochastic n` is exactly the convex hull of
the permutation matrices, and this lemma is instead most useful for accessing the coefficients of
each permutation matrices directly.
views.lean_signature: theorem exists_eq_sum_perm_of_mem_doublyStochastic (hM : M ∈ doublyStochastic R n) : ∃ w : Equiv.Perm n → R, (∀ σ, 0 ≤ w σ) ∧ ∑ σ, w σ = 1 ∧ ∑ σ, w σ • σ.permMatrix R = M

views.nl_informal:
**Birkhoff's theorem**
The set of doubly stochastic matrices is the convex hull of the permutation matrices.  Note
`exists_eq_sum_perm_of_mem_doublyStochastic` gives a convex weighting of each permutation matrix
directly.  To show `doublyStochastic n` is convex, use `convex_doublyStochastic`.
views.lean_signature: theorem doublyStochastic_eq_convexHull_permMatrix : doublyStochastic R n = convexHull R {σ.permMatrix R | σ : Equiv.Perm n}

views.nl_informal: The set of extreme points of the doubly stochastic matrices is the set of permutation matrices.

deals with two different index types.

A convex combination of two centers of mass is a center of mass as well. This version

nonnegative weights with sum one and `z : ι → E` is a family of elements of a module over `R` such

views.nl_informal:
The extended gauge of a point `(a, b)` with respect to the product of balanced sets `U` and `V`
is equal to the maximum of the extended gauges of `a` with respect to `U`
and `b` with respect to `V`.

views.nl_informal:

with respect to a product of finitely many balanced sets `U i`, `i ∈ I`,
(and the whole spaces for the other indices)
is the supremum of the extended gauges of the components of `x`
with respect to the corresponding balanced set.

- either `I` is the universal set;
- or one of `x i`, `i ∈ I`, is nonzero;
- or `𝕜` is nontrivially normed.

views.nl_informal:

with respect to the corresponding balanced set.

and for any `x₁`, `x₂` such that `x` belongs to the open segment `(x₁, x₂)`, we have `x₁ = x`.

to verify the inequality `a • f x + b • f y < f (a • x + b • y)` for `x < y` and positive `a`, `b`.
The main use case is `E = 𝕜` however one can apply it, e.g., to `𝕜^n` with lexicographic order.
