With our definitions, `MeromorphicAt f x` depends only on the values of `f` on a punctured
neighbourhood of `x` (not on `f x`)
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicAt.congr {f g : 𝕜 → E} {x : 𝕜} (hf : MeromorphicAt f x) (hfg : f =ᶠ[𝓝[≠] x] g) : MeromorphicAt g x

views.nl_informal: If two functions agree on a punctured neighborhood, then one is meromorphic iff the other is so.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicAt.meromorphicAt_congr {f g : 𝕜 → E} {x : 𝕜} (h : f =ᶠ[𝓝[≠] x] g) : MeromorphicAt f x ↔ MeromorphicAt g x

views.nl_informal: If a function is meromorphic at a point, then it is continuous at nearby points.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicAt.eventually_continuousAt {f : 𝕜 → E} {x : 𝕜} (h : MeromorphicAt f x) : ∀ᶠ y in 𝓝[≠] x, ContinuousAt f y

views.nl_informal:
In a complete space, a function which is meromorphic at a point is analytic at all nearby
points. The completeness assumption can be dispensed with if one assumes that `f` is meromorphic
on a set around `x`, see `MeromorphicOn.eventually_analyticAt`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicAt.eventually_analyticAt [CompleteSpace E] {f : 𝕜 → E} {x : 𝕜} (h : MeromorphicAt f x) : ∀ᶠ y in 𝓝[≠] x, AnalyticAt 𝕜 f y

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is meromorphic on `U`, if `g` agrees with `f` on a codiscrete subset of `U` and outside of
`U`, then `g` is also meromorphic on `U`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicOn.congr_codiscreteWithin_of_eqOn_compl (hf : MeromorphicOn f U) (h₁ : f =ᶠ[codiscreteWithin U] g) (h₂ : Set.EqOn f g Uᶜ) : MeromorphicOn g U

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is meromorphic on an open set `U`, if `g` agrees with `f` on a codiscrete subset of `U`, then
`g` is also meromorphic on `U`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicOn.congr_codiscreteWithin (hf : MeromorphicOn f U) (h₁ : f =ᶠ[codiscreteWithin U] g) (h₂ : IsOpen U) : MeromorphicOn g U

views.nl_informal: Definition of the divisor
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicOn.divisor_def (f : 𝕜 → E) (U : Set 𝕜) : divisor f U z = if h : MeromorphicOn f U ∧ z ∈ U then (h.1 z h.2).order.untop₀ else 0

views.nl_informal:
Simplifier lemma: on `U`, the divisor of a function `f` that is meromorphic on `U` evaluates to
`order.untop₀`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicOn.divisor_apply {f : 𝕜 → E} (hf : MeromorphicOn f U) (hz : z ∈ U) : divisor f U z = (hf z hz).order.untop₀

views.nl_informal:
If `f₁` is meromorphic on `U`, if `f₂` agrees with `f₁` on a codiscrete subset of `U` and outside of
`U`, then `f₁` and `f₂` induce the same divisors on `U`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicOn.divisor_congr_codiscreteWithin_of_eqOn_compl {f₁ f₂ : 𝕜 → E} (hf₁ : MeromorphicOn f₁ U) (h₁ : f₁ =ᶠ[Filter.codiscreteWithin U] f₂) (h₂ : Set.EqOn f₁ f₂ Uᶜ) : divisor f₁ U = divisor f₂ U

views.nl_informal:
If `f₁` is meromorphic on an open set `U`, if `f₂` agrees with `f₁` on a codiscrete subset of `U`,
then `f₁` and `f₂` induce the same divisors on`U`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicOn.divisor_congr_codiscreteWithin {f₁ f₂ : 𝕜 → E} (hf₁ : MeromorphicOn f₁ U) (h₁ : f₁ =ᶠ[Filter.codiscreteWithin U] f₂) (h₂ : IsOpen U) : divisor f₁ U = divisor f₂ U

views.nl_informal: Analytic functions have non-negative divisors.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicOn.AnalyticOnNhd.divisor_nonneg {f : 𝕜 → E} (hf : AnalyticOnNhd 𝕜 f U) : 0 ≤ MeromorphicOn.divisor f U

views.nl_informal:
If orders are finite, the divisor of the scalar product of two meromorphic functions is the sum of
the divisors.

See `MeromorphicOn.exists_order_ne_top_iff_forall` and
`MeromorphicOn.order_ne_top_of_isPreconnected` for two convenient criteria to guarantee conditions
`h₂f₁` and `h₂f₂`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicOn.divisor_smul {f₁ : 𝕜 → 𝕜} {f₂ : 𝕜 → E} (h₁f₁ : MeromorphicOn f₁ U) (h₁f₂ : MeromorphicOn f₂ U) (h₂f₁ : ∀ z, (hz : z ∈ U) → (h₁f₁ z hz).order ≠ ⊤) (h₂f₂ : ∀ z, (hz : z ∈ U) → (h₁f₂ z hz).order ≠ ⊤) : divisor (f₁ • f₂) U = divisor f₁ U + divisor f₂ U

views.nl_informal:
If orders are finite, the divisor of the product of two meromorphic functions is the sum of the
divisors.

See `MeromorphicOn.exists_order_ne_top_iff_forall` and
`MeromorphicOn.order_ne_top_of_isPreconnected` for two convenient criteria to guarantee conditions
`h₂f₁` and `h₂f₂`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicOn.divisor_mul {f₁ f₂ : 𝕜 → 𝕜} (h₁f₁ : MeromorphicOn f₁ U) (h₁f₂ : MeromorphicOn f₂ U) (h₂f₁ : ∀ z, (hz : z ∈ U) → (h₁f₁ z hz).order ≠ ⊤) (h₂f₂ : ∀ z, (hz : z ∈ U) → (h₁f₂ z hz).order ≠ ⊤) : divisor (f₁ * f₂) U = divisor f₁ U + divisor f₂ U

views.nl_informal: The divisor of the inverse is the negative of the divisor.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicOn.divisor_inv {f : 𝕜 → 𝕜} : divisor f⁻¹ U = -divisor f U

views.nl_informal: Taking the divisor of a meromorphic function commutes with restriction.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicOn.divisor_restrict {f : 𝕜 → E} {V : Set 𝕜} (hf : MeromorphicOn f U) (hV : V ⊆ U) : (divisor f U).restrict hV = divisor f V

views.nl_informal: Adding an analytic function to a meromorphic one does not change the pole divisor.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicOn.negPart_divisor_add_of_analyticNhdOn_right {f₁ f₂ : 𝕜 → E} (hf₁ : MeromorphicOn f₁ U) (hf₂ : AnalyticOnNhd 𝕜 f₂ U) : (divisor (f₁ + f₂) U)⁻ = (divisor f₁ U)⁻

views.nl_informal: Adding an analytic function to a meromorphic one does not change the pole divisor.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicOn.negPart_divisor_add_of_analyticNhdOn_left {f₁ f₂ : 𝕜 → E} (hf₁ : AnalyticOnNhd 𝕜 f₁ U) (hf₂ : MeromorphicOn f₂ U) : (divisor (f₁ + f₂) U)⁻ = (divisor f₂ U)⁻

views.nl_informal:
A meromorphic function has normal form at `x` iff it is either analytic
there, or if it has a pole at `x` and takes the default value `0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem meromorphicNFAt_iff_analyticAt_or : MeromorphicNFAt f x ↔ AnalyticAt 𝕜 f x ∨ ∃ hf : MeromorphicAt f x, hf.order < 0 ∧ f x = 0

views.nl_informal: If a function is meromorphic in normal form at `x`, then it is meromorphic at `x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicNFAt.meromorphicAt (hf : MeromorphicNFAt f x) : MeromorphicAt f x

views.nl_informal:
If a function is meromorphic in normal form at `x`, then it has non-negative order iff it is
analytic.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicNFAt.order_nonneg_iff_analyticAt (hf : MeromorphicNFAt f x) : 0 ≤ hf.meromorphicAt.order ↔ AnalyticAt 𝕜 f x

views.nl_informal: Analytic functions are meromorphic in normal form.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticAt.meromorphicNFAt (hf : AnalyticAt 𝕜 f x) : MeromorphicNFAt f x

views.nl_informal:
Meromorphic functions have normal form outside of a discrete subset in the domain of
meromorphicity.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicOn.meromorphicNFAt_mem_codiscreteWithin {U : Set 𝕜} (hf : MeromorphicOn f U) : { x | MeromorphicNFAt f x } ∈ Filter.codiscreteWithin U

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is meromorphic in normal form at `x`, then `f` has order zero iff it does not vanish at
`x`.

See `AnalyticAt.order_eq_zero_iff` for an analogous statement about analytic functions.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicNFAt.order_eq_zero_iff (hf : MeromorphicNFAt f x) : hf.meromorphicAt.order = 0 ↔ f x ≠ 0

views.nl_informal:
**Local identity theorem**: two meromorphic functions in normal form agree in a
neighborhood iff they agree in a pointed neighborhood.

See `ContinuousAt.eventuallyEq_nhd_iff_eventuallyEq_nhdNE` for the analogous
statement for continuous functions.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicNFAt.eventuallyEq_nhdNE_iff_eventuallyEq_nhd {g : 𝕜 → E} (hf : MeromorphicNFAt f x) (hg : MeromorphicNFAt g x) : f =ᶠ[𝓝[≠] x] g ↔ f =ᶠ[𝓝 x] g

views.nl_informal: Meromorphicity in normal form is a local property.
views.lean_signature: theorem meromorphicNFAt_congr {g : 𝕜 → E} (hfg : f =ᶠ[𝓝 x] g) : MeromorphicNFAt f x ↔ MeromorphicNFAt g x

views.nl_informal:
Helper lemma for `meromorphicNFAt_iff_meromorphicNFAt_of_smul_analytic`: if
`f` is meromorphic in normal form at `x` and `g` is analytic without zero at
`x`, then `g • f` is meromorphic in normal form at `x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicNFAt.smul_analytic (hf : MeromorphicNFAt f x) (h₁g : AnalyticAt 𝕜 g x) (h₂g : g x ≠ 0) : MeromorphicNFAt (g • f) x

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is any function and `g` is analytic without zero at `z₀`, then `f` is meromorphic in
normal form at `z₀` iff `g • f` is meromorphic in normal form at `z₀`.
views.lean_signature: theorem meromorphicNFAt_smul_iff_right_of_analyticAt (h₁g : AnalyticAt 𝕜 g x) (h₂g : g x ≠ 0) : MeromorphicNFAt (g • f) x ↔ MeromorphicNFAt f x

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is any function and `g` is analytic without zero at `z₀`, then `f` is meromorphic in
normal form at `z₀` iff `g * f` is meromorphic in normal form at `z₀`.
views.lean_signature: theorem meromorphicNFAt_mul_iff_right {f : 𝕜 → 𝕜} (h₁g : AnalyticAt 𝕜 g x) (h₂g : g x ≠ 0) : MeromorphicNFAt (g * f) x ↔ MeromorphicNFAt f x

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is any function and `g` is analytic without zero at `z₀`, then `f` is meromorphic in
normal form at `z₀` iff `f * g` is meromorphic in normal form at `z₀`.
views.lean_signature: theorem meromorphicNFAt_mul_iff_left {f : 𝕜 → 𝕜} (h₁g : AnalyticAt 𝕜 g x) (h₂g : g x ≠ 0) : MeromorphicNFAt (f * g) x ↔ MeromorphicNFAt f x

views.nl_informal: Conversion to normal form at `x` changes the value only at x.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicAt.eqOn_compl_singleton_toMermomorphicNFAt (hf : MeromorphicAt f x) : Set.EqOn f (toMeromorphicNFAt f x) {x}ᶜ

views.nl_informal: If `f` is not meromorphic, conversion to normal form at `x` maps the function to `0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem toMeromorphicNFAt_of_not_meromorphicAt (hf : ¬MeromorphicAt f x) : toMeromorphicNFAt f x = 0

views.nl_informal: Conversion to normal form at `x` changes the value only at x.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicAt.eq_nhdNE_toMeromorphicNFAt (hf : MeromorphicAt f x) : f =ᶠ[𝓝[≠] x] toMeromorphicNFAt f x

views.nl_informal: Two analytic functions agree on a punctured neighborhood iff they agree on a neighborhood.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticAt.eventuallyEq_nhdNE_iff_eventuallyEq_nhd {g : 𝕜 → E} {z₀ : 𝕜} (hf : AnalyticAt 𝕜 f z₀) (hg : AnalyticAt 𝕜 g z₀) (hfg : f =ᶠ[𝓝[≠] z₀] g) : f =ᶠ[𝓝 z₀] g

views.nl_informal: After conversion to normal form at `x`, the function has normal form.
views.lean_signature: theorem meromorphicNFAt_toMeromorphicNFAt : MeromorphicNFAt (toMeromorphicNFAt f x) x

views.nl_informal: If `f` has normal form at `x`, then `f` equals `f.toNF`.
views.lean_signature: theorem toMeromorphicNFAt_eq_self : toMeromorphicNFAt f x = f ↔ MeromorphicNFAt f x

views.nl_informal: If `f` is meromorphic in normal form, then so is its inverse.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicNFAt.inv {f : 𝕜 → 𝕜} (hf : MeromorphicNFAt f x) : MeromorphicNFAt f⁻¹ x

views.nl_informal: A function to 𝕜 is meromorphic in normal form at a point iff its inverse is.
views.lean_signature: theorem meromorphicNFAt_inv {f : 𝕜 → 𝕜} : MeromorphicNFAt f⁻¹ x ↔ MeromorphicNFAt f x

views.nl_informal:
If a function is meromorphic in normal form on `U`, then it is meromorphic on
`U`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicNFOn.meromorphicOn (hf : MeromorphicNFOn f U) : MeromorphicOn f U

views.nl_informal:
If a function is meromorphic in normal form on `U`, then its divisor is
non-negative iff it is analytic.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicNFOn.divisor_nonneg_iff_analyticOnNhd (h₁f : MeromorphicNFOn f U) : 0 ≤ MeromorphicOn.divisor f U ↔ AnalyticOnNhd 𝕜 f U

views.nl_informal: Analytic functions are meromorphic in normal form.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticOnNhd.meromorphicNFOn (h₁f : AnalyticOnNhd 𝕜 f U) : MeromorphicNFOn f U

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is meromorphic in normal form on `U` and nowhere locally constant zero,
then its zero set equals the support of the associated divisor.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicNFOn.zero_set_eq_divisor_support (h₁f : MeromorphicNFOn f U) (h₂f : ∀ u : U, (h₁f u.2).meromorphicAt.order ≠ ⊤) : U ∩ f⁻¹' {0} = Function.support (MeromorphicOn.divisor f U)

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is any function and `g` is analytic without zero on `U`, then `f` is
meromorphic in normal form on `U` iff `g • f` is meromorphic in normal form on
`U`.
views.lean_signature: theorem meromorphicNFOn_smul_iff_right_of_analyticOnNhd {g : 𝕜 → 𝕜} (h₁g : AnalyticOnNhd 𝕜 g U) (h₂g : ∀ u ∈ U, g u ≠ 0) : MeromorphicNFOn (g • f) U ↔ MeromorphicNFOn f U

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is any function and `g` is analytic without zero in `U`, then `f` is
meromorphic in normal form on `U` iff `g * f` is meromorphic in normal form on
`U`.
views.lean_signature: theorem meromorphicNFOn_mul_iff_right_of_analyticOnNhd {f g : 𝕜 → 𝕜} (h₁g : AnalyticOnNhd 𝕜 g U) (h₂g : ∀ u ∈ U, g u ≠ 0) : MeromorphicNFOn (g * f) U ↔ MeromorphicNFOn f U

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is any function and `g` is analytic without zero in `U`, then `f` is
meromorphic in normal form on `U` iff `f * g` is meromorphic in normal form on
`U`.
views.lean_signature: theorem meromorphicNFOn_mul_iff_left_of_analyticOnNhd {f g : 𝕜 → 𝕜} (h₁g : AnalyticOnNhd 𝕜 g U) (h₂g : ∀ u ∈ U, g u ≠ 0) : MeromorphicNFOn (f * g) U ↔ MeromorphicNFOn f U

views.nl_informal: A function to 𝕜 is meromorphic in normal form on `U` iff its inverse is.
views.lean_signature: theorem meromorphicNFOn_inv {f : 𝕜 → 𝕜} : MeromorphicNFOn f⁻¹ U ↔ MeromorphicNFOn f U

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is not meromorphic on `U`, conversion to normal form  maps the function
to `0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem toMeromorphicNFOn_of_not_meromorphicOn (hf : ¬MeromorphicOn f U) : toMeromorphicNFOn f U = 0

views.nl_informal: Conversion to normal form on `U` does not change values outside of `U`.
views.lean_signature: theorem toMeromorphicNFOn_eq_self_on_compl (hf : MeromorphicOn f U) : Set.EqOn (toMeromorphicNFOn f U) f Uᶜ

views.nl_informal:
Conversion to normal form on `U` changes the value only along a discrete subset
of `U`.
views.lean_signature: theorem toMeromorphicNFOn_eqOn_codiscrete (hf : MeromorphicOn f U) : f =ᶠ[Filter.codiscreteWithin U] toMeromorphicNFOn f U

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is meromorphic on `U` and `x ∈ U`, then `f` and its conversion to normal
form on `U` agree in a punctured neighborhood of `x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicOn.toMeromorphicNFOn_eq_self_on_nhdNE (hf : MeromorphicOn f U) (hx : x ∈ U) : toMeromorphicNFOn f U =ᶠ[𝓝[≠] x] f

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is meromorphic on `U` and `x ∈ U`, then conversion to normal form at `x`
and conversion to normal form on `U` agree in a neighborhood of `x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem toMeromorphicNFOn_eq_toMeromorphicNFAt_on_nhd (hf : MeromorphicOn f U) (hx : x ∈ U) : toMeromorphicNFOn f U =ᶠ[𝓝 x] toMeromorphicNFAt f x

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is meromorphic on `U` and `x ∈ U`, then conversion to normal form at `x`
and conversion to normal form on `U` agree at `x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem toMeromorphicNFOn_eq_toMeromorphicNFAt (hf : MeromorphicOn f U) (hx : x ∈ U) : toMeromorphicNFOn f U x = toMeromorphicNFAt f x x

views.nl_informal: After conversion to normal form on `U`, the function has normal form.
views.lean_signature: theorem meromorphicNFOn_toMeromorphicNFOn : MeromorphicNFOn (toMeromorphicNFOn f U) U

views.nl_informal: If `f` has normal form on `U`, then `f` equals `toMeromorphicNFOn f U`.
views.lean_signature: theorem toMeromorphicNFOn_eq_self : toMeromorphicNFOn f U = f ↔ MeromorphicNFOn f U

views.nl_informal: Conversion of normal form does not affect orders.
views.lean_signature: theorem order_toMeromorphicNFOn (hf : MeromorphicOn f U) (hx : x ∈ U) : ((meromorphicNFOn_toMeromorphicNFOn f U) hx).meromorphicAt.order = (hf x hx).order

views.nl_informal: Conversion of normal form does not affect divisors.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicOn.divisor_of_toMeromorphicNFOn (hf : MeromorphicOn f U) : divisor (toMeromorphicNFOn f U) U = divisor f U

views.nl_informal:
The order of a meromorphic function `f` at a `z₀` is infinity iff `f` vanishes locally around
`z₀`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicAt.order_eq_top_iff (hf : MeromorphicAt f x) : hf.order = ⊤ ↔ ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝[≠] x, f z = 0

views.nl_informal:
The order of a meromorphic function `f` at `z₀` equals an integer `n` iff `f` can locally be
written as `f z = (z - z₀) ^ n • g z`, where `g` is analytic and does not vanish at `z₀`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicAt.order_eq_int_iff {n : ℤ} (hf : MeromorphicAt f x) : hf.order = n ↔ ∃ g : 𝕜 → E, AnalyticAt 𝕜 g x ∧ g x ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝[≠] x, f z = (z - x) ^ n • g z

views.nl_informal:
If the order of a meromorphic function is negative, then this function converges to infinity
at this point. See also the iff version `tendsto_cobounded_iff_order_neg`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicAt.tendsto_cobounded_of_order_neg (hf : MeromorphicAt f x) (ho : hf.order < 0) : Tendsto f (𝓝[≠] x) (Bornology.cobounded E)

views.nl_informal:
If the order of a meromorphic function is zero, then this function converges to a nonzero
limit at this point. See also the iff version `tendsto_ne_zero_iff_order_eq_zero`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicAt.tendsto_ne_zero_of_order_eq_zero (hf : MeromorphicAt f x) (ho : hf.order = 0) : ∃ c ≠ 0, Tendsto f (𝓝[≠] x) (𝓝 c)

views.nl_informal:
If the order of a meromorphic function is positive, then this function converges to zero
at this point. See also the iff version `tendsto_zero_iff_order_pos`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicAt.tendsto_zero_of_order_pos (hf : MeromorphicAt f x) (ho : 0 < hf.order) : Tendsto f (𝓝[≠] x) (𝓝 0)

views.nl_informal:
If the order of a meromorphic function is nonnegative, then this function converges
at this point. See also the iff version `tendsto_nhds_iff_order_nonneg`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicAt.tendsto_nhds_of_order_nonneg (hf : MeromorphicAt f x) (ho : 0 ≤ hf.order) : ∃ c, Tendsto f (𝓝[≠] x) (𝓝 c)

views.nl_informal: A meromorphic function converges to infinity iff its order is negative.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicAt.tendsto_cobounded_iff_order_neg (hf : MeromorphicAt f x) : Tendsto f (𝓝[≠] x) (Bornology.cobounded E) ↔ hf.order < 0

views.nl_informal: A meromorphic function converges to a limit iff its order is nonnegative.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicAt.tendsto_nhds_iff_order_nonneg (hf : MeromorphicAt f x) : (∃ c, Tendsto f (𝓝[≠] x) (𝓝 c)) ↔ 0 ≤ hf.order

views.nl_informal: A meromorphic function converges to a nonzero limit iff its order is zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicAt.tendsto_ne_zero_iff_order_eq_zero (hf : MeromorphicAt f x) : (∃ c ≠ 0, Tendsto f (𝓝[≠] x) (𝓝 c)) ↔ hf.order = 0

views.nl_informal: A meromorphic function converges to zero iff its order is positive.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicAt.tendsto_zero_iff_order_pos (hf : MeromorphicAt f x) : (Tendsto f (𝓝[≠] x) (𝓝 0)) ↔ 0 < hf.order

views.nl_informal:
Meromorphic functions that agree in a punctured neighborhood of `z₀` have the same order at
`z₀`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicAt.order_congr (hf₁ : MeromorphicAt f₁ x) (hf₁₂ : f₁ =ᶠ[𝓝[≠] x] f₂) : hf₁.order = (hf₁.congr hf₁₂).order

views.nl_informal: Compatibility of notions of `order` for analytic and meromorphic functions.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticAt.meromorphicAt_order (hf : AnalyticAt 𝕜 f x) : hf.meromorphicAt.order = hf.order.map (↑)

views.nl_informal: When seen as meromorphic functions, analytic functions have nonnegative order.
views.lean_signature: theorem AnalyticAt.meromorphicAt_order_nonneg (hf : AnalyticAt 𝕜 f x) : 0 ≤ hf.meromorphicAt.order

views.nl_informal: If a function is both meromorphic and continuous at a point, then it is analytic there.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicAt.analyticAt {f : 𝕜 → E} {x : 𝕜} (h : MeromorphicAt f x) (h' : ContinuousAt f x) : AnalyticAt 𝕜 f x

views.nl_informal: The order is additive when multiplying scalar-valued and vector-valued meromorphic functions.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicAt.order_smul {f : 𝕜 → 𝕜} {g : 𝕜 → E} (hf : MeromorphicAt f x) (hg : MeromorphicAt g x) : (hf.smul hg).order = hf.order + hg.order

views.nl_informal: The order is additive when multiplying meromorphic functions.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicAt.order_mul {f g : 𝕜 → 𝕜} (hf : MeromorphicAt f x) (hg : MeromorphicAt g x) : (hf.mul hg).order = hf.order + hg.order

views.nl_informal: The order of the inverse is the negative of the order.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicAt.order_inv {f : 𝕜 → 𝕜} (hf : MeromorphicAt f x) : hf.inv.order = -hf.order

views.nl_informal: The order of a sum is at least the minimum of the orders of the summands.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicAt.order_add (hf₁ : MeromorphicAt f₁ x) (hf₂ : MeromorphicAt f₂ x) : min hf₁.order hf₂.order ≤ (hf₁.add hf₂).order

views.nl_informal:
If two meromorphic functions have unequal orders, then the order of their sum is
exactly the minimum of the orders of the summands.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicAt.order_add_of_order_ne (hf₁ : MeromorphicAt f₁ x) (hf₂ : MeromorphicAt f₂ x) (h : hf₁.order ≠ hf₂.order) : (hf₁.add hf₂).order = min hf₁.order hf₂.order

views.nl_informal: The set where a meromorphic function has infinite order is clopen in its domain of meromorphy.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicOn.isClopen_setOf_order_eq_top : IsClopen { u : U | (hf u.1 u.2).order = ⊤ }

views.nl_informal:
On a connected set, there exists a point where a meromorphic function `f` has finite order iff
`f` has finite order at every point.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicOn.exists_order_ne_top_iff_forall (hU : IsConnected U) : (∃ u : U, (hf u u.2).order ≠ ⊤) ↔ (∀ u : U, (hf u u.2).order ≠ ⊤)

views.nl_informal:
On a preconnected set, a meromorphic function has finite order at one point if it has finite
order at another point.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicOn.order_ne_top_of_isPreconnected {y : 𝕜} (hU : IsPreconnected U) (h₁x : x ∈ U) (hy : y ∈ U) (h₂x : (hf x h₁x).order ≠ ⊤) : (hf y hy).order ≠ ⊤

views.nl_informal:
If a function is meromorphic on a set `U`, then for each point in `U`, it is analytic at nearby
points in `U`. When the target space is complete, this can be strengthened to analyticity at all
nearby points, see `MeromorphicAt.eventually_analyticAt`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicOn.eventually_analyticAt {f : 𝕜 → E} {x : 𝕜} (h : MeromorphicOn f U) (hx : x ∈ U) : ∀ᶠ y in 𝓝[U \ {x}] x, AnalyticAt 𝕜 f y

views.nl_informal: Meromorphic functions on `U` are analytic on `U`, outside of a discrete subset.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicOn.analyticAt_mem_codiscreteWithin (hf : MeromorphicOn f U) : { x | AnalyticAt 𝕜 f x } ∈ Filter.codiscreteWithin U

views.nl_informal:
The set where a meromorphic function has zero or infinite
order is codiscrete within its domain of meromorphicity.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeromorphicOn.codiscrete_setOf_order_eq_zero_or_top : {u : U | (hf u u.2).order = 0 ∨ (hf u u.2).order = ⊤} ∈ Filter.codiscrete U

views.nl_informal: The midpoint of the segment AB is the same distance from A as it is from B.
views.lean_signature: theorem dist_left_midpoint_eq_dist_right_midpoint (p₁ p₂ : P) : dist p₁ (midpoint 𝕜 p₁ p₂) = dist p₂ (midpoint 𝕜 p₁ p₂)

views.nl_informal:
Given a finite-dimensional normed real vector space, the interior of the convex hull of an
affine basis is the set of points whose barycentric coordinates are strictly positive with respect
to this basis.

TODO Restate this result for affine spaces (instead of vector spaces) once the definition of
convexity is generalised to this setting.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineBasis.interior_convexHull {ι E : Type*} [Finite ι] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] (b : AffineBasis ι ℝ E) : interior (convexHull ℝ (range b)) = {x | ∀ i, 0 < b.coord i x}

views.nl_informal:
Given a set `s` of affine-independent points belonging to an open set `u`, we may extend `s` to
an affine basis, all of whose elements belong to `u`.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsOpen.exists_between_affineIndependent_span_eq_top {s u : Set P} (hu : IsOpen u) (hsu : s ⊆ u) (hne : s.Nonempty) (h : AffineIndependent ℝ ((↑) : s → P)) : ∃ t : Set P, s ⊆ t ∧ t ⊆ u ∧ AffineIndependent ℝ ((↑) : t → P) ∧ affineSpan ℝ t = ⊤

views.nl_informal: The affine span of a nonempty open set is `⊤`.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsOpen.affineSpan_eq_top {u : Set P} (hu : IsOpen u) (hne : u.Nonempty) : affineSpan ℝ u = ⊤

views.nl_informal: We can intercalate a simplex between a point and one of its neighborhoods.
views.lean_signature: theorem exists_mem_interior_convexHull_affineBasis (hs : s ∈ 𝓝 x) : ∃ b : AffineBasis (Fin (finrank ℝ E + 1)) ℝ E, x ∈ interior (convexHull ℝ (range b)) ∧ convexHull ℝ (range b) ⊆ s

views.nl_informal:
The map `g` from `V` to `V₂` corresponding to a map `f` from `P` to `P₂`, at a base point `p`,
is an isometry if `f` is one.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineIsometryEquiv.vadd_vsub {f : P → P₂} (hf : Isometry f) {p : P} {g : V → V₂} (hg : ∀ v, g v = f (v +ᵥ p) -ᵥ f p) : Isometry g

views.nl_informal: If `f` is an affine map, then its linear part is continuous iff `f` is continuous.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineMap.continuous_linear_iff {f : P →ᵃ[𝕜] P₂} : Continuous f.linear ↔ Continuous f

views.nl_informal: If `f` is an affine map, then its linear part is an open map iff `f` is an open map.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineMap.isOpenMap_linear_iff {f : P →ᵃ[𝕜] P₂} : IsOpenMap f.linear ↔ IsOpenMap f

views.nl_informal:
If an isometric self-homeomorphism of a normed vector space over `ℝ` fixes `x` and `y`,
then it fixes the midpoint of `[x, y]`. This is a lemma for a more general Mazur-Ulam theorem,
see below.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsometryEquiv.midpoint_fixed {x y : PE} : ∀ e : PE ≃ᵢ PE, e x = x → e y = y → e (midpoint ℝ x y) = midpoint ℝ x y

views.nl_informal: A bijective isometry sends midpoints to midpoints.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsometryEquiv.map_midpoint (f : PE ≃ᵢ PF) (x y : PE) : f (midpoint ℝ x y) = midpoint ℝ (f x) (f y)

views.nl_informal: The exponential series as an `ofScalars` series.
views.lean_signature: theorem NormedSpace.expSeries_eq_ofScalars : expSeries 𝕂 𝔸 = ofScalars 𝔸 fun n ↦ (n !⁻¹ : 𝕂)

views.nl_informal: The exponential sum as an `ofScalarsSum`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NormedSpace.exp_eq_ofScalarsSum : exp 𝕂 = ofScalarsSum (E := 𝔸) fun n ↦ (n !⁻¹ : 𝕂)

views.nl_informal:
In a Banach-algebra `𝔸` over a normed field `𝕂` of characteristic zero, if `x` and `y` are
in the disk of convergence and commute, then
`NormedSpace.exp 𝕂 (x + y) = (NormedSpace.exp 𝕂 x) * (NormedSpace.exp 𝕂 y)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NormedSpace.exp_add_of_commute_of_mem_ball [CharZero 𝕂] {x y : 𝔸} (hxy : Commute x y) (hx : x ∈ EMetric.ball (0 : 𝔸) (expSeries 𝕂 𝔸).radius) (hy : y ∈ EMetric.ball (0 : 𝔸) (expSeries 𝕂 𝔸).radius) : exp 𝕂 (x + y) = exp 𝕂 x * exp 𝕂 y

views.nl_informal: Any continuous ring homomorphism commutes with `NormedSpace.exp`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NormedSpace.map_exp_of_mem_ball {F} [FunLike F 𝔸 𝔹] [RingHomClass F 𝔸 𝔹] (f : F) (hf : Continuous f) (x : 𝔸) (hx : x ∈ EMetric.ball (0 : 𝔸) (expSeries 𝕂 𝔸).radius) : f (exp 𝕂 x) = exp 𝕂 (f x)

views.nl_informal:
In a commutative Banach-algebra `𝔸` over a normed field `𝕂` of characteristic zero,
`NormedSpace.exp 𝕂 (x+y) = (NormedSpace.exp 𝕂 x) * (NormedSpace.exp 𝕂 y)`
for all `x`, `y` in the disk of convergence.
views.lean_signature: theorem NormedSpace.exp_add_of_mem_ball [CharZero 𝕂] {x y : 𝔸} (hx : x ∈ EMetric.ball (0 : 𝔸) (expSeries 𝕂 𝔸).radius) (hy : y ∈ EMetric.ball (0 : 𝔸) (expSeries 𝕂 𝔸).radius) : exp 𝕂 (x + y) = exp 𝕂 x * exp 𝕂 y

views.nl_informal:
In a normed algebra `𝔸` over `𝕂 = ℝ` or `𝕂 = ℂ`, the series defining the exponential map
has an infinite radius of convergence.
views.lean_signature: theorem NormedSpace.expSeries_radius_eq_top : (expSeries 𝕂 𝔸).radius = ∞

views.nl_informal:
In a Banach-algebra `𝔸` over `𝕂 = ℝ` or `𝕂 = ℂ`, if `x` and `y` commute, then
`NormedSpace.exp 𝕂 (x+y) = (NormedSpace.exp 𝕂 x) * (NormedSpace.exp 𝕂 y)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NormedSpace.exp_add_of_commute {x y : 𝔸} (hxy : Commute x y) : exp 𝕂 (x + y) = exp 𝕂 x * exp 𝕂 y

views.nl_informal:
In a Banach-algebra `𝔸` over `𝕂 = ℝ` or `𝕂 = ℂ`, if a family of elements `f i` mutually
commute then `NormedSpace.exp 𝕂 (∑ i, f i) = ∏ i, NormedSpace.exp 𝕂 (f i)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NormedSpace.exp_sum_of_commute {ι} (s : Finset ι) (f : ι → 𝔸) (h : (s : Set ι).Pairwise (Commute on f)) : exp 𝕂 (∑ i ∈ s, f i) = s.noncommProd (fun i => exp 𝕂 (f i)) fun _ hi _ hj _ => (h.of_refl hi hj).exp 𝕂

views.nl_informal: Any continuous ring homomorphism commutes with `NormedSpace.exp`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NormedSpace.map_exp {F} [FunLike F 𝔸 𝔹] [RingHomClass F 𝔸 𝔹] (f : F) (hf : Continuous f) (x : 𝔸) : f (exp 𝕂 x) = exp 𝕂 (f x)

views.nl_informal:
In a commutative Banach-algebra `𝔸` over `𝕂 = ℝ` or `𝕂 = ℂ`,
`NormedSpace.exp 𝕂 (x+y) = (NormedSpace.exp 𝕂 x) * (NormedSpace.exp 𝕂 y)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NormedSpace.exp_add {x y : 𝔸} : exp 𝕂 (x + y) = exp 𝕂 x * exp 𝕂 y

views.nl_informal:
If a normed ring `𝔸` is a normed algebra over two fields, then they define the same
`expSeries` on `𝔸`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NormedSpace.expSeries_eq_expSeries (n : ℕ) (x : 𝔸) : (expSeries 𝕂 𝔸 n fun _ => x) = expSeries 𝕂' 𝔸 n fun _ => x

views.nl_informal:
If a normed ring `𝔸` is a normed algebra over two fields, then they define the same
exponential function on `𝔸`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NormedSpace.exp_eq_exp : (exp 𝕂 : 𝔸 → 𝔸) = exp 𝕂'

views.nl_informal: The even terms of `expSeries` are real, and correspond to the series for $\cos ‖q‖$.
views.lean_signature: theorem Quaternion.expSeries_even_of_imaginary {q : Quaternion ℝ} (hq : q.re = 0) (n : ℕ) : expSeries ℝ (Quaternion ℝ) (2 * n) (fun _ => q) = ↑((-1 : ℝ) ^ n * ‖q‖ ^ (2 * n) / (2 * n)!)

views.nl_informal:
The odd terms of `expSeries` are real, and correspond to the series for
$\frac{q}{‖q‖} \sin ‖q‖$.
views.lean_signature: theorem Quaternion.expSeries_odd_of_imaginary {q : Quaternion ℝ} (hq : q.re = 0) (n : ℕ) : expSeries ℝ (Quaternion ℝ) (2 * n + 1) (fun _ => q) = (((-1 : ℝ) ^ n * ‖q‖ ^ (2 * n + 1) / (2 * n + 1)!) / ‖q‖) • q

views.nl_informal:
Auxiliary result; if the power series corresponding to `Real.cos` and `Real.sin` evaluated
at `‖q‖` tend to `c` and `s`, then the exponential series tends to `c + (s / ‖q‖)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Quaternion.hasSum_expSeries_of_imaginary {q : Quaternion ℝ} (hq : q.re = 0) {c s : ℝ} (hc : HasSum (fun n => (-1 : ℝ) ^ n * ‖q‖ ^ (2 * n) / (2 * n)!) c) (hs : HasSum (fun n => (-1 : ℝ) ^ n * ‖q‖ ^ (2 * n + 1) / (2 * n + 1)!) s) : HasSum (fun n => expSeries ℝ (Quaternion ℝ) n fun _ => q) (↑c + (s / ‖q‖) • q)

views.nl_informal: The closed form for the quaternion exponential on imaginary quaternions.
views.lean_signature: theorem Quaternion.exp_of_re_eq_zero (q : Quaternion ℝ) (hq : q.re = 0) : exp ℝ q = ↑(Real.cos ‖q‖) + (Real.sin ‖q‖ / ‖q‖) • q

views.nl_informal: The closed form for the quaternion exponential on arbitrary quaternions.
views.lean_signature: theorem Quaternion.exp_eq (q : Quaternion ℝ) : exp ℝ q = exp ℝ q.re • (↑(Real.cos ‖q.im‖) + (Real.sin ‖q.im‖ / ‖q.im‖) • q.im)

views.nl_informal:
In a Banach algebra `A` over a nontrivially normed field `𝕜`, for any `a : A` the
power series with coefficients `a ^ n` represents the function `(1 - z • a)⁻¹` in a disk of
radius `‖a‖₊⁻¹`.
views.lean_signature: theorem spectrum.hasFPowerSeriesOnBall_inverse_one_sub_smul [HasSummableGeomSeries A] (a : A) : HasFPowerSeriesOnBall (fun z : 𝕜 => Ring.inverse (1 - z • a)) (fun n => ContinuousMultilinearMap.mkPiRing 𝕜 (Fin n) (a ^ n)) 0 ‖a‖₊⁻¹

views.nl_informal:
In a Banach algebra `A` over `𝕜`, for `a : A` the function `fun z ↦ (1 - z • a)⁻¹` is
differentiable on any closed ball centered at zero of radius `r < (spectralRadius 𝕜 a)⁻¹`.
views.lean_signature: theorem spectrum.differentiableOn_inverse_one_sub_smul [CompleteSpace A] {a : A} {r : ℝ≥0} (hr : (r : ℝ≥0∞) < (spectralRadius 𝕜 a)⁻¹) : DifferentiableOn 𝕜 (fun z : 𝕜 => Ring.inverse (1 - z • a)) (Metric.closedBall 0 r)

views.nl_informal: The `limsup` relationship for the spectral radius used to prove `spectrum.gelfand_formula`.
views.lean_signature: theorem spectrum.limsup_pow_nnnorm_pow_one_div_le_spectralRadius (a : A) : limsup (fun n : ℕ => (‖a ^ n‖₊ : ℝ≥0∞) ^ (1 / n : ℝ)) atTop ≤ spectralRadius ℂ a

views.nl_informal:
**Gelfand's formula**: Given an element `a : A` of a complex Banach algebra, the
`spectralRadius` of `a` is the limit of the sequence `‖a ^ n‖₊ ^ (1 / n)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem spectrum.pow_nnnorm_pow_one_div_tendsto_nhds_spectralRadius (a : A) : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (‖a ^ n‖₊ : ℝ≥0∞) ^ (1 / n : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 (spectralRadius ℂ a))

views.nl_informal:
**Gelfand's formula**: Given an element `a : A` of a complex Banach algebra, the
`spectralRadius` of `a` is the limit of the sequence `‖a ^ n‖₊ ^ (1 / n)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem spectrum.pow_norm_pow_one_div_tendsto_nhds_spectralRadius (a : A) : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => ENNReal.ofReal (‖a ^ n‖ ^ (1 / n : ℝ))) atTop (𝓝 (spectralRadius ℂ a))

views.nl_informal: In a (nontrivial) complex Banach algebra, every element has nonempty spectrum.
views.lean_signature: theorem spectrum.nonempty : (spectrum ℂ a).Nonempty

views.nl_informal:
In a complex Banach algebra, the spectral radius is always attained by some element of the
spectrum.
views.lean_signature: theorem spectrum.exists_nnnorm_eq_spectralRadius : ∃ z ∈ spectrum ℂ a, (‖z‖₊ : ℝ≥0∞) = spectralRadius ℂ a

views.nl_informal:
In a complex Banach algebra, if every element of the spectrum has norm strictly less than
`r : ℝ≥0`, then the spectral radius is also strictly less than `r`.
views.lean_signature: theorem spectrum.spectralRadius_lt_of_forall_lt {r : ℝ≥0} (hr : ∀ z ∈ spectrum ℂ a, ‖z‖₊ < r) : spectralRadius ℂ a < r

views.nl_informal: The **spectral mapping theorem** for polynomials in a Banach algebra over `ℂ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem spectrum.map_polynomial_aeval (p : ℂ[X]) : spectrum ℂ (aeval a p) = (fun k => eval k p) '' spectrum ℂ a

views.nl_informal:
A specialization of the spectral mapping theorem for polynomials in a Banach algebra over `ℂ`
to monic monomials.
views.lean_signature: theorem spectrum.map_pow (n : ℕ) : spectrum ℂ (a ^ n) = (· ^ n) '' spectrum ℂ a

views.nl_informal: For `𝕜 = ℝ` or `𝕜 = ℂ`, `exp 𝕜` maps the spectrum of `a` into the spectrum of `exp 𝕜 a`.
views.lean_signature: theorem spectrum.exp_mem_exp [RCLike 𝕜] [NormedRing A] [NormedAlgebra 𝕜 A] [CompleteSpace A] (a : A) {z : 𝕜} (hz : z ∈ spectrum 𝕜 a) : exp 𝕜 z ∈ spectrum 𝕜 (exp 𝕜 a)

views.nl_informal:
Let `S` be a closed subalgebra of a Banach algebra `A`. If `a : S` is invertible in `A`,
and for all `x : S` sufficiently close to `a` within some filter `l`, `x` is invertible in `S`,
then `a` is invertible in `S` as well.
views.lean_signature: theorem Subalgebra.isUnit_of_isUnit_val_of_eventually {l : Filter S} {a : S} (ha : IsUnit (a : A)) (hla : l ≤ 𝓝 a) (hl : ∀ᶠ x in l, IsUnit x) (hl' : l.NeBot) : IsUnit a

views.nl_informal:
If `S : Subalgebra 𝕜 A` is a closed subalgebra of a Banach algebra `A`, then for any
`x : S`, the boundary of the spectrum of `x` relative to `S` is a subset of the spectrum of
`↑x : A` relative to `A`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Subalgebra.frontier_spectrum : frontier (σ 𝕜 x) ⊆ σ 𝕜 (x : A)

views.nl_informal:
If `S` is a closed subalgebra of a Banach algebra `A`, then for any `x : S`, the boundary of
the spectrum of `x` relative to `S` is a subset of the boundary of the spectrum of `↑x : A`
relative to `A`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Subalgebra.frontier_subset_frontier : frontier (σ 𝕜 x) ⊆ frontier (σ 𝕜 (x : A))

views.nl_informal:
If `S` is a closed subalgebra of a Banach algebra `A`, then for any `x : S`, the spectrum of `x`
is the spectrum of `↑x : A` along with the connected components of the complement of the spectrum of
`↑x : A` which contain an element of the spectrum of `x : S`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Subalgebra.spectrum_sUnion_connectedComponentIn : σ 𝕜 x = σ 𝕜 (x : A) ∪ (⋃ z ∈ (σ 𝕜 x \ σ 𝕜 (x : A)), connectedComponentIn (σ 𝕜 (x : A))ᶜ z)

views.nl_informal:
Let `S` be a closed subalgebra of a Banach algebra `A`, and let `x : S`. If `z` is in the
spectrum of `x`, then the connected component of `z` in the complement of the spectrum of `↑x : A`
is bounded (or else `z` actually belongs to the spectrum of `↑x : A`).
views.lean_signature: theorem Subalgebra.spectrum_isBounded_connectedComponentIn {z : 𝕜} (hz : z ∈ σ 𝕜 x) : Bornology.IsBounded (connectedComponentIn (σ 𝕜 (x : A))ᶜ z)

views.nl_informal:
Let `S` be a closed subalgebra of a Banach algebra `A`. If for `x : S` the complement of the
spectrum of `↑x : A` is connected, then `spectrum 𝕜 x = spectrum 𝕜 (x : A)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Subalgebra.spectrum_eq_of_isPreconnected_compl (h : IsPreconnected (σ 𝕜 (x : A))ᶜ) : σ 𝕜 x = σ 𝕜 (x : A)

views.nl_informal:
If `𝕜₁` is a normed field contained as subfield of a larger normed field `𝕜₂`, and if `a : A`
is an element whose `𝕜₂` spectrum restricts to `𝕜₁`, then the spectral radii over each scalar
field coincide.
views.lean_signature: theorem SpectrumRestricts.spectralRadius_eq {𝕜₁ 𝕜₂ A : Type*} [NormedField 𝕜₁] [NormedField 𝕜₂] [NormedRing A] [NormedAlgebra 𝕜₁ A] [NormedAlgebra 𝕜₂ A] [NormedAlgebra 𝕜₁ 𝕜₂] [IsScalarTower 𝕜₁ 𝕜₂ A] {f : 𝕜₂ → 𝕜₁} {a : A} (h : SpectrumRestricts a f) : spectralRadius 𝕜₁ a = spectralRadius 𝕜₂ a

views.nl_informal:
If `NormedSpace.exp R x.fst` converges to `e`
then `(NormedSpace.exp R x).snd` converges to `e • x.snd`.
views.lean_signature: theorem TrivSqZeroExt.hasSum_snd_expSeries_of_smul_comm (x : tsze R M) (hx : MulOpposite.op x.fst • x.snd = x.fst • x.snd) {e : R} (h : HasSum (fun n => expSeries 𝕜 R n fun _ => x.fst) e) : HasSum (fun n => snd (expSeries 𝕜 (tsze R M) n fun _ => x)) (e • x.snd)

views.nl_informal:
If `NormedSpace.exp R x.fst` converges to `e`
then `NormedSpace.exp R x` converges to `inl e + inr (e • x.snd)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem TrivSqZeroExt.hasSum_expSeries_of_smul_comm (x : tsze R M) (hx : MulOpposite.op x.fst • x.snd = x.fst • x.snd) {e : R} (h : HasSum (fun n => expSeries 𝕜 R n fun _ => x.fst) e) : HasSum (fun n => expSeries 𝕜 (tsze R M) n fun _ => x) (inl e + inr (e • x.snd))

views.nl_informal: Polar form of trivial-square-zero extension.
views.lean_signature: theorem TrivSqZeroExt.eq_smul_exp_of_invertible (x : tsze R M) [Invertible x.fst] : x = x.fst • exp 𝕜 (⅟ x.fst • inr x.snd)

views.nl_informal:
The other direction of `IsUltrametricDist.of_normedAlgebra`.
Let `K` be a normed field. If a seminormed ring `L` is a normed `K`-algebra, and `‖1‖ = 1` in `L`,
then `K` is ultrametric (i.e. the norm on `L` is nonarchimedean) if `F` is.
This can be further generalized to the case where `‖1‖ ≠ 0` in `L`.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsUltrametricDist.of_normedAlgebra' [SeminormedRing L] [NormOneClass L] [NormedAlgebra K L] [h : IsUltrametricDist L] : IsUltrametricDist K

views.nl_informal:
Let `K` be a normed field. If a normed division ring `L` is a normed `K`-algebra,
then `L` is ultrametric (i.e. the norm on `L` is nonarchimedean) if `K` is.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsUltrametricDist.of_normedAlgebra [NormedDivisionRing L] [NormedAlgebra K L] [h : IsUltrametricDist K] : IsUltrametricDist L

views.nl_informal:
Let `K` be a normed field. If a normed division ring `L` is a normed `K`-algebra,
then `L` is ultrametric (i.e. the norm on `L` is nonarchimedean) if and only if `K` is.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsUltrametricDist.normedAlgebra_iff [NormedDivisionRing L] [NormedAlgebra K L] : IsUltrametricDist L ↔ IsUltrametricDist K

views.nl_informal:
this lemma establishes that if `ContinuousLinearMap.mul 𝕜 A` is injective, then so is
`Unitization.splitMul 𝕜 A`. When `A` is a `RegularNormedAlgebra`, then
`ContinuousLinearMap.mul 𝕜 A` is an isometry, and is therefore automatically injective.
views.lean_signature: theorem Unitization.splitMul_injective_of_clm_mul_injective (h : Function.Injective (mul 𝕜 A)) : Function.Injective (splitMul 𝕜 A)

views.nl_informal:
In a `RegularNormedAlgebra`, the map `Unitization.splitMul 𝕜 A` is injective.
We will use this to pull back the norm from `𝕜 × (A →L[𝕜] A)` to `Unitization 𝕜 A`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Unitization.splitMul_injective : Function.Injective (splitMul 𝕜 A)

views.nl_informal:
Multiplication on the left by a nonzero element of a normed division ring tends to infinity at
infinity.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.tendsto_mul_left_cobounded {a : α} (ha : a ≠ 0) : Tendsto (a * ·) (cobounded α) (cobounded α)

views.nl_informal:
Multiplication on the right by a nonzero element of a normed division ring tends to infinity at
infinity.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.tendsto_mul_right_cobounded {a : α} (ha : a ≠ 0) : Tendsto (· * a) (cobounded α) (cobounded α)

views.nl_informal:
A normed field is either nontrivially normed or has a discrete topology.
In the discrete topology case, all the norms are 1, by `norm_eq_one_iff_ne_zero_of_discrete`.
The nontrivially normed field instance is provided by a subtype with a proof that the
forgetful inheritance to the existing `NormedField` instance is definitionally true.
This allows one to have the new `NontriviallyNormedField` instance without data clashes.
views.lean_signature: theorem NormedField.discreteTopology_or_nontriviallyNormedField (𝕜 : Type*) [h : NormedField 𝕜] : DiscreteTopology 𝕜 ∨ Nonempty ({h' : NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜 // h'.toNormedField = h})

views.nl_informal:
A weakly locally compact normed field is proper.
This is a specialization of `ProperSpace.of_locallyCompactSpace`
which holds for `NormedSpace`s but requires more imports.
views.lean_signature: theorem ProperSpace.of_nontriviallyNormedField_of_weaklyLocallyCompactSpace (𝕜 : Type*) [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [WeaklyLocallyCompactSpace 𝕜] : ProperSpace 𝕜

views.nl_informal:
To prove that a normed division ring is nonarchimedean, it suffices to prove that the norm
of the image of any natural is less than or equal to one.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsUltrametricDist.isUltrametricDist_of_forall_norm_natCast_le_one (h : ∀ n : ℕ, ‖(n : R)‖ ≤ 1) : IsUltrametricDist R

views.nl_informal:
If the absolute value `v` factors through an embedding `f` into a normed field, then
`f` is an isometry.
views.lean_signature: theorem WithAbs.isometry_of_comp (h : ∀ x, ‖f x‖ = v x) : Isometry f

views.nl_informal:
If the absolute value `v` factors through an embedding `f` into a normed field, then
the pseudo metric space associated to the absolute value is the same as the pseudo metric space
induced by `f`.
views.lean_signature: theorem WithAbs.pseudoMetricSpace_induced_of_comp (h : ∀ x, ‖f x‖ = v x) : PseudoMetricSpace.induced f inferInstance = (normedField v).toPseudoMetricSpace

views.nl_informal:
If the absolute value `v` factors through an embedding `f` into a normed field, then
the uniform structure associated to the absolute value is the same as the uniform structure
induced by `f`.
views.lean_signature: theorem WithAbs.uniformSpace_comap_eq_of_comp (h : ∀ x, ‖f x‖ = v x) : UniformSpace.comap f inferInstance = (normedField v).toUniformSpace

views.nl_informal:
If the absolute value `v` factors through an embedding `f` into a normed field, then
`f` is uniform inducing.
views.lean_signature: theorem WithAbs.isUniformInducing_of_comp (h : ∀ x, ‖f x‖ = v x) : IsUniformInducing f

views.nl_informal:
If the absolute value of a normed field factors through an embedding into another normed field,
then the extended embedding `v.Completion →+* L` preserves distances.
views.lean_signature: theorem AbsoluteValue.Completion.extensionEmbedding_dist_eq_of_comp (h : ∀ x, ‖f x‖ = v x) (x y : v.Completion) : dist (extensionEmbedding_of_comp h x) (extensionEmbedding_of_comp h y) = dist x y

views.nl_informal:
If the absolute value of a normed field factors through an embedding into another normed field,
then the extended embedding `v.Completion →+* L` is an isometry.
views.lean_signature: theorem AbsoluteValue.Completion.isometry_extensionEmbedding_of_comp (h : ∀ x, ‖f x‖ = v x) : Isometry (extensionEmbedding_of_comp h)

views.nl_informal:
If the absolute value of a normed field factors through an embedding into another normed field,
then the extended embedding `v.Completion →+* L` is a closed embedding.
views.lean_signature: theorem AbsoluteValue.Completion.isClosedEmbedding_extensionEmbedding_of_comp (h : ∀ x, ‖f x‖ = v x) : IsClosedEmbedding (extensionEmbedding_of_comp h)

views.nl_informal:
If the absolute value of a normed field factors through an embedding into another normed field
that is locally compact, then the completion of the first normed field is also locally compact.
views.lean_signature: theorem AbsoluteValue.Completion.locallyCompactSpace [LocallyCompactSpace L] (h : ∀ x, ‖f x‖ = v x) : LocallyCompactSpace (v.Completion)

views.nl_informal:
The distance equals the norm of subtracting two points. In this
lemma, it is necessary to have `V` as an explicit argument; otherwise
`rw dist_eq_norm_vsub` sometimes doesn't work.
views.lean_signature: theorem dist_eq_norm_vsub (x y : P) : dist x y = ‖x -ᵥ y‖

views.nl_informal:
The distance equals the norm of subtracting two points. In this
lemma, it is necessary to have `V` as an explicit argument; otherwise
`rw dist_eq_norm_vsub'` sometimes doesn't work.
views.lean_signature: theorem dist_eq_norm_vsub' (x y : P) : dist x y = ‖y -ᵥ x‖

views.nl_informal: **Triangle inequality** for the norm.
views.lean_signature: theorem norm_mul_le' (a b : E) : ‖a * b‖ ≤ ‖a‖ + ‖b‖

views.nl_informal: **Triangle inequality** for the norm.
views.lean_signature: theorem norm_mul_le_of_le' (h₁ : ‖a₁‖ ≤ r₁) (h₂ : ‖a₂‖ ≤ r₂) : ‖a₁ * a₂‖ ≤ r₁ + r₂

views.nl_informal: **Triangle inequality** for the norm.
views.lean_signature: theorem norm_mul₃_le' : ‖a * b * c‖ ≤ ‖a‖ + ‖b‖ + ‖c‖

views.nl_informal: The non negative norm seen as an `ENNReal` and then as a `Real` is equal to the norm.
views.lean_signature: theorem toReal_coe_nnnorm' (a : E) : (‖a‖₊ : ℝ≥0∞).toReal = ‖a‖

views.nl_informal: In a (semi)normed group, inversion `x ↦ x⁻¹` tends to infinity at infinity.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.tendsto_inv_cobounded : Tendsto Inv.inv (cobounded E) (cobounded E)

views.nl_informal:
A helper lemma used to prove that the (scalar or usual) product of a function that tends to one
and a bounded function tends to one. This lemma is formulated for any binary operation
`op : E → F → G` with an estimate `‖op x y‖ ≤ A * ‖x‖ * ‖y‖` for some constant A instead of
multiplication so that it can be applied to `(*)`, `flip (*)`, `(•)`, and `flip (•)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.Tendsto.op_one_isBoundedUnder_le' {f : α → E} {g : α → F} {l : Filter α} (hf : Tendsto f l (𝓝 1)) (hg : IsBoundedUnder (· ≤ ·) l (Norm.norm ∘ g)) (op : E → F → G) (h_op : ∃ A, ∀ x y, ‖op x y‖ ≤ A * ‖x‖ * ‖y‖) : Tendsto (fun x => op (f x) (g x)) l (𝓝 1)

views.nl_informal:
A helper lemma used to prove that the (scalar or usual) product of a function that tends to one
and a bounded function tends to one. This lemma is formulated for any binary operation
`op : E → F → G` with an estimate `‖op x y‖ ≤ ‖x‖ * ‖y‖` instead of multiplication so that it
can be applied to `(*)`, `flip (*)`, `(•)`, and `flip (•)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.Tendsto.op_one_isBoundedUnder_le {f : α → E} {g : α → F} {l : Filter α} (hf : Tendsto f l (𝓝 1)) (hg : IsBoundedUnder (· ≤ ·) l (Norm.norm ∘ g)) (op : E → F → G) (h_op : ∀ x y, ‖op x y‖ ≤ ‖x‖ * ‖y‖) : Tendsto (fun x => op (f x) (g x)) l (𝓝 1)

views.nl_informal:
A normed additive group is complete if any absolutely convergent series converges in the
space.
views.lean_signature: theorem NormedAddCommGroup.completeSpace_of_summable_imp_tendsto (h : ∀ u : ℕ → E, Summable (‖u ·‖) → ∃ a, Tendsto (fun n => ∑ i ∈ range n, u i) atTop (𝓝 a)) : CompleteSpace E

views.nl_informal:
In a complete normed additive group, every absolutely convergent series converges in the
space.
views.lean_signature: theorem NormedAddCommGroup.summable_imp_tendsto_of_complete [CompleteSpace E] (u : ℕ → E) (hu : Summable (‖u ·‖)) : ∃ a, Tendsto (fun n => ∑ i ∈ range n, u i) atTop (𝓝 a)

views.nl_informal:
In a normed additive group, every absolutely convergent series converges in the
space iff the space is complete.
views.lean_signature: theorem NormedAddCommGroup.summable_imp_tendsto_iff_completeSpace : (∀ u : ℕ → E, Summable (‖u ·‖) → ∃ a, Tendsto (fun n => ∑ i ∈ range n, u i) atTop (𝓝 a)) ↔ CompleteSpace E

views.nl_informal:
The seminorm of an element in a product space is `≤ r` if and only if the norm of each
component is.
views.lean_signature: theorem pi_norm_le_iff_of_nonneg' (hr : 0 ≤ r) : ‖x‖ ≤ r ↔ ∀ i, ‖x i‖ ≤ r

views.nl_informal:
The seminorm of an element in a product space is `< r` if and only if the norm of each
component is.
views.lean_signature: theorem pi_norm_lt_iff' (hr : 0 < r) : ‖x‖ < r ↔ ∀ i, ‖x i‖ < r

views.nl_informal: The $L^1$ norm is less than the $L^\infty$ norm scaled by the cardinality.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pi.sum_norm_apply_le_norm' : ∑ i, ‖f i‖ ≤ Fintype.card ι • ‖f‖

views.nl_informal: The $L^1$ norm is less than the $L^\infty$ norm scaled by the cardinality.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pi.sum_nnnorm_apply_le_nnnorm' : ∑ i, ‖f i‖₊ ≤ Fintype.card ι • ‖f‖₊

views.nl_informal:
Special case of the sandwich theorem: if the norm of `f` is eventually bounded by a real
function `a` which tends to `0`, then `f` tends to `1` (neutral element of `SeminormedGroup`).
In this pair of lemmas (`squeeze_one_norm'` and `squeeze_one_norm`), following a convention of
similar lemmas in `Topology.MetricSpace.Basic` and `Topology.Algebra.Order`, the `'` version is
phrased using "eventually" and the non-`'` version is phrased absolutely.
views.lean_signature: theorem squeeze_one_norm' {f : α → E} {a : α → ℝ} {t₀ : Filter α} (h : ∀ᶠ n in t₀, ‖f n‖ ≤ a n) (h' : Tendsto a t₀ (𝓝 0)) : Tendsto f t₀ (𝓝 1)

views.nl_informal:
Special case of the sandwich theorem: if the norm of `f` is bounded by a real function `a` which
tends to `0`, then `f` tends to `1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem squeeze_one_norm {f : α → E} {a : α → ℝ} {t₀ : Filter α} (h : ∀ n, ‖f n‖ ≤ a n) : Tendsto a t₀ (𝓝 0) → Tendsto f t₀ (𝓝 1)

views.nl_informal: If `‖y‖ → ∞`, then we can assume `y ≠ x` for any fixed `x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem eventually_ne_of_tendsto_norm_atTop' {l : Filter α} {f : α → E} (h : Tendsto (fun y => ‖f y‖) l atTop) (x : E) : ∀ᶠ y in l, f y ≠ x

views.nl_informal:
Given `f : NormedAddGroupHom G H` for some complete `G` and a subgroup `K` of `H`, if every
element `x` of `K` has a preimage under `f` whose norm is at most `C*‖x‖` then the same holds for
elements of the (topological) closure of `K` with constant `C+ε` instead of `C`, for any
positive `ε`.
views.lean_signature: theorem controlled_closure_of_complete {f : NormedAddGroupHom G H} {K : AddSubgroup H} {C ε : ℝ} (hC : 0 < C) (hε : 0 < ε) (hyp : f.SurjectiveOnWith K C) : f.SurjectiveOnWith K.topologicalClosure (C + ε)

views.nl_informal:
Given `f : NormedAddGroupHom G H` for some complete `G`, if every element `x` of the image of
an isometric immersion `j : NormedAddGroupHom K H` has a preimage under `f` whose norm is at most
`C*‖x‖` then the same holds for elements of the (topological) closure of this image with constant
`C+ε` instead of `C`, for any positive `ε`.
This is useful in particular if `j` is the inclusion of a normed group into its completion
(in this case the closure is the full target group).
views.lean_signature: theorem controlled_closure_range_of_complete {f : NormedAddGroupHom G H} {K : Type*} [SeminormedAddCommGroup K] {j : NormedAddGroupHom K H} (hj : ∀ x, ‖j x‖ = ‖x‖) {C ε : ℝ} (hC : 0 < C) (hε : 0 < ε) (hyp : ∀ k, ∃ g, f g = j k ∧ ‖g‖ ≤ C * ‖k‖) : f.SurjectiveOnWith j.range.topologicalClosure (C + ε)

views.nl_informal: The fundamental property of the operator norm: `‖f x‖ ≤ ‖f‖ * ‖x‖`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NormedAddGroupHom.le_opNorm (x : V₁) : ‖f x‖ ≤ ‖f‖ * ‖x‖

views.nl_informal: continuous linear maps are Lipschitz continuous.
views.lean_signature: theorem NormedAddGroupHom.lipschitz : LipschitzWith ⟨‖f‖, opNorm_nonneg f⟩ f

views.nl_informal: If one controls the norm of every `f x`, then one controls the norm of `f`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NormedAddGroupHom.opNorm_le_bound {M : ℝ} (hMp : 0 ≤ M) (hM : ∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ M * ‖x‖) : ‖f‖ ≤ M

views.nl_informal:
If a bounded group homomorphism map is constructed from a group homomorphism via the constructor
`AddMonoidHom.mkNormedAddGroupHom`, then its norm is bounded by the bound given to the constructor
if it is nonnegative.
views.lean_signature: theorem NormedAddGroupHom.mkNormedAddGroupHom_norm_le (f : V₁ →+ V₂) {C : ℝ} (hC : 0 ≤ C) (h : ∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ C * ‖x‖) : ‖f.mkNormedAddGroupHom C h‖ ≤ C

views.nl_informal:
If a bounded group homomorphism map is constructed from a group homomorphism via the constructor
`NormedAddGroupHom.ofLipschitz`, then its norm is bounded by the bound given to the constructor.
views.lean_signature: theorem NormedAddGroupHom.ofLipschitz_norm_le (f : V₁ →+ V₂) {K : ℝ≥0} (h : LipschitzWith K f) : ‖ofLipschitz f h‖ ≤ K

views.nl_informal:
If a bounded group homomorphism map is constructed from a group homomorphism
via the constructor `AddMonoidHom.mkNormedAddGroupHom`, then its norm is bounded by the bound
given to the constructor or zero if this bound is negative.
views.lean_signature: theorem NormedAddGroupHom.mkNormedAddGroupHom_norm_le' (f : V₁ →+ V₂) {C : ℝ} (h : ∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ C * ‖x‖) : ‖f.mkNormedAddGroupHom C h‖ ≤ max C 0

views.nl_informal: The operator norm satisfies the triangle inequality.
views.lean_signature: theorem NormedAddGroupHom.opNorm_add_le : ‖f + g‖ ≤ ‖f‖ + ‖g‖

views.nl_informal: The norm of the `0` operator is `0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NormedAddGroupHom.opNorm_zero : ‖(0 : NormedAddGroupHom V₁ V₂)‖ = 0

views.nl_informal: For normed groups, an operator is zero iff its norm vanishes.
views.lean_signature: theorem NormedAddGroupHom.opNorm_zero_iff {V₁ V₂ : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V₁] [NormedAddCommGroup V₂] {f : NormedAddGroupHom V₁ V₂} : ‖f‖ = 0 ↔ f = 0

views.nl_informal:
The norm of the identity is at most `1`. It is in fact `1`, except when the norm of every
element vanishes, where it is `0`. (Since we are working with seminorms this can happen even if the
space is non-trivial.) It means that one can not do better than an inequality in general.
views.lean_signature: theorem NormedAddGroupHom.norm_id_le : ‖(id V : NormedAddGroupHom V V)‖ ≤ 1

views.nl_informal:
If there is an element with norm different from `0`, then the norm of the identity equals `1`.
(Since we are working with seminorms supposing that the space is non-trivial is not enough.)
views.lean_signature: theorem NormedAddGroupHom.norm_id_of_nontrivial_seminorm (h : ∃ x : V, ‖x‖ ≠ 0) : ‖id V‖ = 1

views.nl_informal: If a normed space is non-trivial, then the norm of the identity equals `1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NormedAddGroupHom.norm_id {V : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [Nontrivial V] : ‖id V‖ = 1

views.nl_informal: The lifting of a norm nonincreasing morphism is norm nonincreasing.
views.lean_signature: theorem NormedAddGroupHom.Equalizer.lift_normNoninc (φ : NormedAddGroupHom V₁ V) (h : f.comp φ = g.comp φ) (hφ : φ.NormNoninc) : (lift φ h).NormNoninc

views.nl_informal: If `φ` satisfies `‖φ‖ ≤ C`, then the same is true for the lifted morphism.
views.lean_signature: theorem NormedAddGroupHom.Equalizer.norm_lift_le (φ : NormedAddGroupHom V₁ V) (h : f.comp φ = g.comp φ) (C : ℝ) (hφ : ‖φ‖ ≤ C) : ‖lift φ h‖ ≤ C

views.nl_informal:
A version of the **direct comparison test** for conditionally convergent series.
See `cauchySeq_finset_of_norm_bounded` for the same statement about absolutely convergent ones.
views.lean_signature: theorem cauchySeq_range_of_norm_bounded {f : ℕ → E} (g : ℕ → ℝ) (hg : CauchySeq fun n => ∑ i ∈ range n, g i) (hf : ∀ i, ‖f i‖ ≤ g i) : CauchySeq fun n => ∑ i ∈ range n, f i

views.nl_informal:
If a function `f` is summable in norm, and along some sequence of finsets exhausting the space
its sum is converging to a limit `a`, then this holds along all finsets, i.e., `f` is summable
with sum `a`.
views.lean_signature: theorem hasSum_of_subseq_of_summable {f : ι → E} (hf : Summable fun a => ‖f a‖) {s : α → Finset ι} {p : Filter α} [NeBot p] (hs : Tendsto s p atTop) {a : E} (ha : Tendsto (fun b => ∑ i ∈ s b, f i) p (𝓝 a)) : HasSum f a

views.nl_informal:
The direct comparison test for series:  if the norm of `f` is bounded by a real function `g`
which is summable, then `f` is summable.
views.lean_signature: theorem Summable.of_norm_bounded [CompleteSpace E] {f : ι → E} (g : ι → ℝ) (hg : Summable g) (h : ∀ i, ‖f i‖ ≤ g i) : Summable f

views.nl_informal:
Quantitative result associated to the direct comparison test for series:  If `∑' i, g i` is
summable, and for all `i`, `‖f i‖ ≤ g i`, then `‖∑' i, f i‖ ≤ ∑' i, g i`. Note that we do not
assume that `∑' i, f i` is summable, and it might not be the case if `α` is not a complete space.
views.lean_signature: theorem tsum_of_norm_bounded {f : ι → E} {g : ι → ℝ} {a : ℝ} (hg : HasSum g a) (h : ∀ i, ‖f i‖ ≤ g i) : ‖∑' i : ι, f i‖ ≤ a

views.nl_informal:
If `∑' i, ‖f i‖` is summable, then `‖∑' i, f i‖ ≤ (∑' i, ‖f i‖)`. Note that we do not assume
that `∑' i, f i` is summable, and it might not be the case if `α` is not a complete space.
views.lean_signature: theorem norm_tsum_le_tsum_norm {f : ι → E} (hf : Summable fun i => ‖f i‖) : ‖∑' i, f i‖ ≤ ∑' i, ‖f i‖

views.nl_informal:
Quantitative result associated to the direct comparison test for series: If `∑' i, g i` is
summable, and for all `i`, `‖f i‖₊ ≤ g i`, then `‖∑' i, f i‖₊ ≤ ∑' i, g i`. Note that we
do not assume that `∑' i, f i` is summable, and it might not be the case if `α` is not a complete
space.
views.lean_signature: theorem tsum_of_nnnorm_bounded {f : ι → E} {g : ι → ℝ≥0} {a : ℝ≥0} (hg : HasSum g a) (h : ∀ i, ‖f i‖₊ ≤ g i) : ‖∑' i : ι, f i‖₊ ≤ a

views.nl_informal:
If `∑' i, ‖f i‖₊` is summable, then `‖∑' i, f i‖₊ ≤ ∑' i, ‖f i‖₊`. Note that
we do not assume that `∑' i, f i` is summable, and it might not be the case if `α` is not a complete
space.
views.lean_signature: theorem nnnorm_tsum_le {f : ι → E} (hf : Summable fun i => ‖f i‖₊) : ‖∑' i, f i‖₊ ≤ ∑' i, ‖f i‖₊

views.nl_informal:
Variant of the direct comparison test for series:  if the norm of `f` is eventually bounded by a
real function `g` which is summable, then `f` is summable.
views.lean_signature: theorem Summable.of_norm_bounded_eventually {f : ι → E} (g : ι → ℝ) (hg : Summable g) (h : ∀ᶠ i in cofinite, ‖f i‖ ≤ g i) : Summable f

views.nl_informal:
Variant of the direct comparison test for series:  if the norm of `f` is eventually bounded by a
real function `g` which is summable, then `f` is summable.
views.lean_signature: theorem Summable.of_norm_bounded_eventually_nat {f : ℕ → E} (g : ℕ → ℝ) (hg : Summable g) (h : ∀ᶠ i in atTop, ‖f i‖ ≤ g i) : Summable f

views.nl_informal:
An alternative definition of the norm on the quotient group: the norm of `((x : M) : M ⧸ S)` is
equal to the distance from `x` to `S`.
views.lean_signature: theorem QuotientGroup.norm_mk (x : M) : ‖(x : M ⧸ S)‖ = infDist x S

views.nl_informal: The norm of the projection is smaller or equal to the norm of the original element.
views.lean_signature: theorem QuotientGroup.norm_mk_le_norm : ‖(m : M ⧸ S)‖ ≤ ‖m‖

views.nl_informal:
The norm of the image of `m : M` in the quotient by `S` is zero if and only if `m` belongs
to the closure of `S`.
views.lean_signature: theorem QuotientGroup.norm_mk_eq_zero_iff_mem_closure : ‖(m : M ⧸ S)‖ = 0 ↔ m ∈ closure (S : Set M)

views.nl_informal:
The norm of the image of `m : M` in the quotient by a closed subgroup `S` is zero if and only if
`m ∈ S`.
views.lean_signature: theorem QuotientGroup.norm_mk_eq_zero [hS : IsClosed (S : Set M)] : ‖(m : M ⧸ S)‖ = 0 ↔ m ∈ S

views.nl_informal:
For any `x : M ⧸ S` and any `0 < ε`, there is `m : M` such that `mk' S m = x`
and `‖m‖ < ‖x‖ + ε`.

views.nl_informal:
**Tannery's theorem**: topological sums commute with termwise limits, when the norms of the
summands are eventually uniformly bounded by a summable function.

(This is the special case of the Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem for the counting measure
on a discrete set. However, we prove it under somewhat weaker assumptions than the general
measure-theoretic result, e.g. `G` is not assumed to be an `ℝ`-vector space or second countable,
and the limit is along an arbitrary filter rather than `atTop ℕ`.)

See also:
* `MeasureTheory.tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence` (for general integrals, but
  with more assumptions on `G`)
* `continuous_tsum` (continuity of infinite sums in a parameter)
views.lean_signature: theorem tendsto_tsum_of_dominated_convergence {α β G : Type*} {𝓕 : Filter α} [NormedAddCommGroup G] [CompleteSpace G] {f : α → β → G} {g : β → G} {bound : β → ℝ} (h_sum : Summable bound) (hab : ∀ k : β, Tendsto (f · k) 𝓕 (𝓝 (g k))) (h_bound : ∀ᶠ n in 𝓕, ∀ k, ‖f n k‖ ≤ bound k) : Tendsto (∑' k, f · k) 𝓕 (𝓝 (∑' k, g k))

Rescaling everything, it follows that any `y ∈ F` is arbitrarily well approached by
images of elements of norm at most `C * ‖y‖`.

is within distance `‖y‖/2` of `y`, to apply an iterative process.
