See also `norm_pow_le'`.
views.lean_signature: theorem norm_pow_le [NormOneClass α] (a : α) (n : ℕ) : ‖a ^ n‖ ≤ ‖a‖ ^ n

views.nl_informal: The restriction of a power-multiplicative function to a subalgebra is power-multiplicative.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsPowMul.restriction {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [Ring S] [Algebra R S] (A : Subalgebra R S) {f : S → ℝ} (hf_pm : IsPowMul f) : IsPowMul fun x : A => f x.val

views.nl_informal:
Deduce `NormOneClass` from `NormMulClass` under a suitable nontriviality hypothesis. Not
an instance, in order to avoid loops with `NormOneClass.nontrivial`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NormMulClass.toNormOneClass : NormOneClass α

views.nl_informal:
A ring homomorphism from a `Ring R` to a `SeminormedRing S` which induces the norm structure
`SeminormedRing.induced` makes `R` satisfy `‖(1 : R)‖ = 1` whenever `‖(1 : S)‖ = 1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NormOneClass.induced {F : Type*} (R S : Type*) [Ring R] [SeminormedRing S] [NormOneClass S] [FunLike F R S] [RingHomClass F R S] (f : F) : @NormOneClass R (SeminormedRing.induced R S f).toNorm _

views.nl_informal:
Product of two infinite sums indexed by arbitrary types.
See also `tsum_mul_tsum` if `f` and `g` are *not* absolutely summable, and
`tsum_mul_tsum_of_summable_norm'` when the space is not complete.
views.lean_signature: theorem tsum_mul_tsum_of_summable_norm [CompleteSpace R] {f : ι → R} {g : ι' → R} (hf : Summable fun x => ‖f x‖) (hg : Summable fun x => ‖g x‖) : ((∑' x, f x) * ∑' y, g y) = ∑' z : ι × ι', f z.1 * g z.2

views.nl_informal:
The Cauchy product formula for the product of two infinite sums indexed by `ℕ`,
expressed by summing on `Finset.antidiagonal`.
See also `tsum_mul_tsum_eq_tsum_sum_antidiagonal` if `f` and `g` are
*not* absolutely summable, and `tsum_mul_tsum_eq_tsum_sum_antidiagonal_of_summable_norm'`
when the space is not complete.
views.lean_signature: theorem tsum_mul_tsum_eq_tsum_sum_antidiagonal_of_summable_norm [CompleteSpace R] {f g : ℕ → R} (hf : Summable fun x => ‖f x‖) (hg : Summable fun x => ‖g x‖) : ((∑' n, f n) * ∑' n, g n) = ∑' n, ∑ kl ∈ antidiagonal n, f kl.1 * g kl.2

views.nl_informal:
The Cauchy product formula for the product of two infinite sums indexed by `ℕ`,
expressed by summing on `Finset.range`.
See also `tsum_mul_tsum_eq_tsum_sum_range` if `f` and `g` are
*not* absolutely summable, and `tsum_mul_tsum_eq_tsum_sum_range_of_summable_norm'` when the
space is not complete.
views.lean_signature: theorem tsum_mul_tsum_eq_tsum_sum_range_of_summable_norm [CompleteSpace R] {f g : ℕ → R} (hf : Summable fun x => ‖f x‖) (hg : Summable fun x => ‖g x‖) : ((∑' n, f n) * ∑' n, g n) = ∑' n, ∑ k ∈ range (n + 1), f k * g (n - k)

views.nl_informal:
The group of units of a normed ring with summable geometric series is an open subset
of the ring.
views.lean_signature: theorem Units.isOpen : IsOpen { x : R | IsUnit x }

views.nl_informal:
The `nonunits` in a normed ring with summable geometric series are contained in the
complement of the ball of radius `1` centered at `1 : R`.
views.lean_signature: theorem nonunits.subset_compl_ball : nonunits R ⊆ (Metric.ball (1 : R) 1)ᶜ

views.nl_informal:
The formula `Ring.inverse (x + t) = Ring.inverse (1 + x⁻¹ * t) * x⁻¹` holds for `t` sufficiently
small.
views.lean_signature: theorem NormedRing.inverse_add (x : Rˣ) : ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝 0, inverse ((x : R) + t) = inverse (1 + ↑x⁻¹ * t) * ↑x⁻¹

views.nl_informal:
The formula
`Ring.inverse (x + t) =
  (∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, (- x⁻¹ * t) ^ i) * x⁻¹ + (- x⁻¹ * t) ^ n * Ring.inverse (x + t)`
holds for `t` sufficiently small.
views.lean_signature: theorem NormedRing.inverse_add_nth_order (x : Rˣ) (n : ℕ) : ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝 0, inverse ((x : R) + t) = (∑ i ∈ range n, (-↑x⁻¹ * t) ^ i) * ↑x⁻¹ + (-↑x⁻¹ * t) ^ n * inverse (x + t)

views.nl_informal: The function `fun t ↦ inverse (x + t)` is O(1) as `t → 0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NormedRing.inverse_add_norm (x : Rˣ) : (fun t : R => inverse (↑x + t)) =O[𝓝 0] fun _t => (1 : ℝ)

views.nl_informal:
The function
`fun t ↦ Ring.inverse (x + t) - (∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, (- x⁻¹ * t) ^ i) * x⁻¹`
is `O(t ^ n)` as `t → 0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NormedRing.inverse_add_norm_diff_nth_order (x : Rˣ) (n : ℕ) : (fun t : R => inverse (↑x + t) - (∑ i ∈ range n, (-↑x⁻¹ * t) ^ i) * ↑x⁻¹) =O[𝓝 (0 : R)] fun t => ‖t‖ ^ n

views.nl_informal: The function `fun t ↦ Ring.inverse (x + t) - x⁻¹` is `O(t)` as `t → 0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NormedRing.inverse_add_norm_diff_first_order (x : Rˣ) : (fun t : R => inverse (↑x + t) - ↑x⁻¹) =O[𝓝 0] fun t => ‖t‖

views.nl_informal: The function `fun t ↦ Ring.inverse (x + t) - x⁻¹ + x⁻¹ * t * x⁻¹` is `O(t ^ 2)` as `t → 0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NormedRing.inverse_add_norm_diff_second_order (x : Rˣ) : (fun t : R => inverse (↑x + t) - ↑x⁻¹ + ↑x⁻¹ * t * ↑x⁻¹) =O[𝓝 0] fun t => ‖t‖ ^ 2

views.nl_informal: The function `Ring.inverse` is continuous at each unit of `R`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NormedRing.inverse_continuousAt (x : Rˣ) : ContinuousAt inverse (x : R)

views.nl_informal:
In a normed ring with summable geometric series, the coercion from `Rˣ` (equipped with the
induced topology from the embedding in `R × R`) to `R` is an open embedding.
views.lean_signature: theorem Units.isOpenEmbedding_val : IsOpenEmbedding (val : Rˣ → R)

views.nl_informal:
In a normed ring with summable geometric series, the coercion from `Rˣ` (equipped with the
induced topology from the embedding in `R × R`) to `R` is an open map.
views.lean_signature: theorem Units.isOpenMap_val : IsOpenMap (val : Rˣ → R)

views.nl_informal: An ideal which contains an element within `1` of `1 : R` is the unit ideal.
views.lean_signature: theorem Ideal.eq_top_of_norm_lt_one (I : Ideal R) {x : R} (hxI : x ∈ I) (hx : ‖1 - x‖ < 1) : I = ⊤

views.nl_informal:
The `Ideal.closure` of a proper ideal in a normed ring with summable
geometric series is proper.
views.lean_signature: theorem Ideal.closure_ne_top (I : Ideal R) (hI : I ≠ ⊤) : I.closure ≠ ⊤

views.nl_informal:
The `Ideal.closure` of a maximal ideal in a normed ring with summable
geometric series is the ideal itself.
views.lean_signature: theorem Ideal.IsMaximal.closure_eq {I : Ideal R} (hI : I.IsMaximal) : I.closure = I

views.nl_informal: An `R`-algebra norm such that `f 1 = 1` extends the norm on `R`.
views.lean_signature: theorem AlgebraNorm.extends_norm' (hf1 : f 1 = 1) (a : R) : f (a • (1 : S)) = ‖a‖

views.nl_informal: An `R`-algebra norm such that `f 1 = 1` extends the norm on `R`.
views.lean_signature: theorem AlgebraNorm.extends_norm (hf1 : f 1 = 1) (a : R) : f (algebraMap R S a) = ‖a‖

views.nl_informal: A multiplicative `R`-algebra norm extends the norm on `R`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MulAlgebraNorm.extends_norm' (f : MulAlgebraNorm R S) (a : R) : f (a • (1 : S)) = ‖a‖

views.nl_informal: A multiplicative `R`-algebra norm extends the norm on `R`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MulAlgebraNorm.extends_norm (f : MulAlgebraNorm R S) (a : R) : f (algebraMap R S a) = ‖a‖

views.nl_informal: A multiplicative ring norm is power-multiplicative.
views.lean_signature: theorem MulRingNorm.isPowMul {A : Type*} [Ring A] (f : MulRingNorm A) : IsPowMul f

views.nl_informal: The norm of a coefficient `x_i` is less than or equal to the norm of `x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Basis.norm_repr_le_norm {x : L} (i : ι) : ‖B.repr x i‖ ≤ B.norm x

views.nl_informal: For any `K`-basis of `L`, we have `B.norm 0 = 0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Basis.norm_zero : B.norm 0 = 0

views.nl_informal: For any `K`-basis of `L`, and any `x : L`, we have `B.norm (-x) = B.norm x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Basis.norm_neg (x : L) : B.norm (-x) = B.norm x

views.nl_informal: For any `K`-basis of `L`, and any `x : L`, we have `0 ≤ B.norm x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Basis.norm_nonneg (x : L) : 0 ≤ B.norm x

views.nl_informal: For any `K`-basis `B` of `L` containing `1`, `B.norm` extends the norm on `K`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Basis.norm_extends {i : ι} (hBi : B i = (1 : L)) (x : K) : B.norm ((algebraMap K L) x) = ‖x‖

views.nl_informal: For any `K`-basis of `L`, if the norm on `K` is nonarchimedean, then so is `B.norm`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Basis.norm_isNonarchimedean (hna : IsNonarchimedean (Norm.norm : K → ℝ)) : IsNonarchimedean B.norm

views.nl_informal:
For any `K`-basis of `L`, `B.norm` is bounded with respect to multiplication. That is,
`∃ (c : ℝ), c > 0` such that ` ∀ (x y : L), B.norm (x * y) ≤ c * B.norm x * B.norm y`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Basis.norm_mul_le_const_mul_norm {i : ι} (hBi : B i = (1 : L)) (hna : IsNonarchimedean (Norm.norm : K → ℝ)) : ∃ (c : ℝ) (_ : 0 < c), ∀ x y : L, B.norm (x * y) ≤ c * B.norm x * B.norm y

views.nl_informal:
For any `k : K`, `y : L`, we have
`B.norm ((algebra_map K L) k * y) = B.norm ((algebra_map K L) k) * B.norm y`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Basis.norm_smul {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] {B : Basis ι K L} {i : ι} (hBi : B i = (1 : L)) (k : K) (y : L) : B.norm ((algebraMap K L) k * y) = B.norm ((algebraMap K L) k) * B.norm y

views.nl_informal:
If `K` is a nonarchimedean normed field `L/K` is a finite extension, then there exists a
power-multiplicative nonarchimedean `K`-algebra norm on `L` extending the norm on `K`.
views.lean_signature: theorem exists_nonarchimedean_pow_mul_seminorm_of_finiteDimensional (hfd : FiniteDimensional K L) (hna : IsNonarchimedean (norm : K → ℝ)) : ∃ f : AlgebraNorm K L, IsPowMul f ∧ (∀ (x : K), f ((algebraMap K L) x) = ‖x‖) ∧ IsNonarchimedean f

views.nl_informal:
If `f : α →+* β` is bounded with respect to a ring seminorm `nα` on `α` and a
power-multiplicative function `nβ : β → ℝ`, then `∀ x : α, nβ (f x) ≤ nα x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem contraction_of_isPowMul_of_boundedWrt {F : Type*} {α : outParam (Type*)} [Ring α] [FunLike F α ℝ] [RingSeminormClass F α ℝ] {β : Type*} [Ring β] (nα : F) {nβ : β → ℝ} (hβ : IsPowMul nβ) {f : α →+* β} (hf : f.IsBoundedWrt nα nβ) (x : α) : nβ (f x) ≤ nα x

views.nl_informal:
Given a bounded `f : α →+* β` between seminormed rings, is the seminorm on `β` is
power-multiplicative, then `f` is a contraction.
views.lean_signature: theorem contraction_of_isPowMul {α β : Type*} [SeminormedRing α] [SeminormedRing β] (hβ : IsPowMul (norm : β → ℝ)) {f : α →+* β} (hf : f.IsBounded) (x : α) : norm (f x) ≤ norm x

views.nl_informal:
Given two power-multiplicative ring seminorms `f, g` on `α`, if `f` is bounded by a positive
multiple of `g` and vice versa, then `f = g`.
views.lean_signature: theorem eq_seminorms {F : Type*} {α : outParam (Type*)} [Ring α] [FunLike F α ℝ] [RingSeminormClass F α ℝ] {f g : F} (hfpm : IsPowMul f) (hgpm : IsPowMul g) (hfg : ∃ (r : ℝ) (_ : 0 < r), ∀ a : α, f a ≤ r * g a) (hgf : ∃ (r : ℝ) (_ : 0 < r), ∀ a : α, g a ≤ r * f a) : f = g

views.nl_informal:
If `R` is a normed commutative ring and `f₁` and `f₂` are two power-multiplicative `R`-algebra
norms on `S`, then if `f₁` and `f₂` are equivalent on every  subring `R[y]` for `y : S`, it
follows that `f₁ = f₂` [BGR, Proposition 3.1.5/1][bosch-guntzer-remmert].
views.lean_signature: theorem eq_of_powMul_faithful (f₁ : AlgebraNorm R S) (hf₁_pm : IsPowMul f₁) (f₂ : AlgebraNorm R S) (hf₂_pm : IsPowMul f₂) (h_eq : ∀ y : S, ∃ (C₁ C₂ : ℝ) (_ : 0 < C₁) (_ : 0 < C₂), ∀ x : Algebra.adjoin R {y}, f₁ x.val ≤ C₁ * f₂ x.val ∧ f₂ x.val ≤ C₂ * f₁ x.val) : f₁ = f₂

views.nl_informal: If `f` is a ring seminorm on `a`, then `∀ {n : ℕ}, n ≠ 0 → f (a ^ n) ≤ f a ^ n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem map_pow_le_pow {F α : Type*} [Ring α] [FunLike F α ℝ] [RingSeminormClass F α ℝ] (f : F) (a : α) : ∀ {n : ℕ}, n ≠ 0 → f (a ^ n) ≤ f a ^ n

views.nl_informal: If `f` is a ring seminorm on `a` with `f 1 ≤ 1`, then `∀ (n : ℕ), f (a ^ n) ≤ f a ^ n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem map_pow_le_pow' {F α : Type*} [Ring α] [FunLike F α ℝ] [RingSeminormClass F α ℝ] {f : F} (hf1 : f 1 ≤ 1) (a : α) : ∀ n : ℕ, f (a ^ n) ≤ f a ^ n

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is a ring seminorm on `R` with `f 1 ≤ 1` and `s : ℕ → ℕ` is bounded by `n`, then
`f (x ^ s (ψ n)) ^ (1 / (ψ n : ℝ))` is eventually bounded.
views.lean_signature: theorem RingSeminorm.isBoundedUnder (hp : p 1 ≤ 1) {s : ℕ → ℕ} (hs_le : ∀ n : ℕ, s n ≤ n) {x : R} (ψ : ℕ → ℕ) : IsBoundedUnder LE.le atTop fun n : ℕ => p (x ^ s (ψ n)) ^ (1 / (ψ n : ℝ))

views.nl_informal: Equivalence of multiplicative ring norms is reflexive.
views.lean_signature: theorem MulRingNorm.equiv_refl (f : MulRingNorm R) : equiv f f

views.nl_informal: Equivalence of multiplicative ring norms is symmetric.
views.lean_signature: theorem MulRingNorm.equiv_symm {f g : MulRingNorm R} (hfg : equiv f g) : equiv g f

views.nl_informal: Equivalence of multiplicative ring norms is transitive.
views.lean_signature: theorem MulRingNorm.equiv_trans {f g k : MulRingNorm R} (hfg : equiv f g) (hgk : equiv g k) : equiv f k

views.nl_informal: A multiplicative ring norm satisfies `f n ≤ n` for every `n : ℕ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MulRingNorm_nat_le_nat {R : Type*} [Ring R] (n : ℕ) (f : MulRingNorm R) : f n ≤ n

views.nl_informal: A multiplicative norm composed with the absolute value on integers equals the norm itself.
views.lean_signature: theorem MulRingNorm.apply_natAbs_eq {R : Type*} [Ring R] (x : ℤ) (f : MulRingNorm R) : f (natAbs x) = f x

views.nl_informal: Triangle inequality for `MulRingNorm` applied to a list.
views.lean_signature: theorem mulRingNorm_sum_le_sum_mulRingNorm {R : Type*} [NonAssocRing R] (l : List R) (f : MulRingNorm R) : f l.sum ≤ (l.map f).sum

views.nl_informal: If `f : R → ℝ` is a nonzero, nonnegative, multiplicatively bounded function, then `f 1 ≠ 0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem map_one_ne_zero (f_ne_zero : f ≠ 0) (f_nonneg : 0 ≤ f) (f_mul : ∀ x y : R, f (x * y) ≤ c * f x * f y) : f 1 ≠ 0

views.nl_informal:
If `f : R → ℝ` is a nonnegative multiplicatively bounded function and `x : R` is a unit with
`f x ≠ 0`, then for every `n : ℕ`, we have `f (x ^ n) ≠ 0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem map_pow_ne_zero (f_nonneg : 0 ≤ f) {x : R} (hx : IsUnit x) (hfx : f x ≠ 0) (n : ℕ) (f_mul : ∀ x y : R, f (x * y) ≤ c * f x * f y) : f (x ^ n) ≠ 0

views.nl_informal:
If `f : R → ℝ` is a nonnegative, multiplicatively bounded function, then given `x y : R` with
`f x = 0`, we have `f (x * y) = 0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem map_mul_zero_of_map_zero (f_nonneg : 0 ≤ f) (f_mul : ∀ x y : R, f (x * y) ≤ c * f x * f y) {x : R} (hx : f x = 0) (y : R) : f (x * y) = 0

views.nl_informal: `seminormFromBounded' f` preserves `0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem seminormFromBounded_zero (f_zero : f 0 = 0) : seminormFromBounded' f (0 : R) = 0

views.nl_informal:
If `f : R → ℝ` is a nonnegative, multiplicatively bounded function, then for every `x : R`,
the image of `y ↦ f (x * y) / f y` is bounded above.
views.lean_signature: theorem seminormFromBounded_bddAbove_range (f_nonneg : 0 ≤ f) (f_mul : ∀ x y : R, f (x * y) ≤ c * f x * f y) (x : R) : BddAbove (Set.range fun y ↦ f (x * y) / f y)

views.nl_informal:
If `f : R → ℝ` is a nonnegative, multiplicatively bounded function, then for every `x : R`,
`seminormFromBounded' f x` is bounded above by some multiple of `f x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem seminormFromBounded_le (f_nonneg : 0 ≤ f) (f_mul : ∀ x y : R, f (x * y) ≤ c * f x * f y) (x : R) : seminormFromBounded' f x ≤ c * f x

views.nl_informal:
If `f : R → ℝ` is a nonnegative, multiplicatively bounded function, then for every `x : R`,
`f x ≤ f 1 * seminormFromBounded' f x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem seminormFromBounded_ge (f_nonneg : 0 ≤ f) (f_mul : ∀ x y : R, f (x * y) ≤ c * f x * f y) (x : R) : f x ≤ f 1 * seminormFromBounded' f x

views.nl_informal:
If `f : R → ℝ` is a nonnegative, multiplicatively bounded function, then
`seminormFromBounded' f` is nonnegative.
views.lean_signature: theorem seminormFromBounded_nonneg (f_nonneg : 0 ≤ f) (f_mul : ∀ x y : R, f (x * y) ≤ c * f x * f y) : 0 ≤ seminormFromBounded' f

views.nl_informal:
If `f : R → ℝ` is a nonnegative, multiplicatively bounded function, then
`seminormFromBounded' f x = 0` if and only if `f x = 0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem seminormFromBounded_eq_zero_iff (f_nonneg : 0 ≤ f) (f_mul : ∀ x y : R, f (x * y) ≤ c * f x * f y) (x : R) : seminormFromBounded' f x = 0 ↔ f x = 0

views.nl_informal: If `f` is invariant under negation of `x`, then so is `seminormFromBounded'`.
views.lean_signature: theorem seminormFromBounded_neg (f_neg : ∀ x : R, f (-x) = f x) (x : R) : seminormFromBounded' f (-x) = seminormFromBounded' f x

views.nl_informal:
If `f : R → ℝ` is a nonnegative, multiplicatively bounded function, then
`seminormFromBounded' f` is submultiplicative.
views.lean_signature: theorem seminormFromBounded_mul (f_nonneg : 0 ≤ f) (f_mul : ∀ x y : R, f (x * y) ≤ c * f x * f y) (x y : R) : seminormFromBounded' f (x * y) ≤ seminormFromBounded' f x * seminormFromBounded' f y

views.nl_informal:
If `f : R → ℝ` is a nonzero, nonnegative, multiplicatively bounded function, then
`seminormFromBounded' f 1 = 1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem seminormFromBounded_one (f_ne_zero : f ≠ 0) (f_nonneg : 0 ≤ f) (f_mul : ∀ x y : R, f (x * y) ≤ c * f x * f y) : seminormFromBounded' f 1 = 1

views.nl_informal:
If `f : R → ℝ` is a nonnegative, multiplicatively bounded function, then
`seminormFromBounded' f 1 ≤ 1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem seminormFromBounded_one_le (f_nonneg : 0 ≤ f) (f_mul : ∀ x y : R, f (x * y) ≤ c * f x * f y) : seminormFromBounded' f 1 ≤ 1

views.nl_informal:
If `f : R → ℝ` is a nonnegative, multiplicatively bounded, subadditive function, then
`seminormFromBounded' f` is subadditive.
views.lean_signature: theorem seminormFromBounded_add (f_nonneg : 0 ≤ f) (f_mul : ∀ x y : R, f (x * y) ≤ c * f x * f y) (f_add : ∀ a b, f (a + b) ≤ f a + f b) (x y : R) : seminormFromBounded' f (x + y) ≤ seminormFromBounded' f x + seminormFromBounded' f y

views.nl_informal:
If `f : R → ℝ` is a nonnegative, multiplicatively bounded, nonarchimedean function, then
`seminormFromBounded' f` is nonarchimedean.
views.lean_signature: theorem seminormFromBounded_isNonarchimedean (f_nonneg : 0 ≤ f) (f_mul : ∀ x y : R, f (x * y) ≤ c * f x * f y) (hna : IsNonarchimedean f) : IsNonarchimedean (seminormFromBounded' f)

views.nl_informal:
If `f : R → ℝ` is a nonnegative, multiplicatively bounded function and `x : R` is
multiplicative for `f`, then `seminormFromBounded' f x = f x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem seminormFromBounded_of_mul_apply (f_nonneg : 0 ≤ f) (f_mul : ∀ x y : R, f (x * y) ≤ c * f x * f y) {x : R} (hx : ∀ y : R, f (x * y) = f x * f y) : seminormFromBounded' f x = f x

views.nl_informal:
If `f : R → ℝ` is a nonnegative function and `x : R` is submultiplicative for `f`, then
`seminormFromBounded' f x = f x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem seminormFromBounded_of_mul_le (f_nonneg : 0 ≤ f) {x : R} (hx : ∀ y : R, f (x * y) ≤ f x * f y) (h_one : f 1 ≤ 1) : seminormFromBounded' f x = f x

views.nl_informal:
If `f : R → ℝ` is a nonzero, nonnegative, multiplicatively bounded function, then
`seminormFromBounded' f` is nonzero.
views.lean_signature: theorem seminormFromBounded_nonzero (f_ne_zero : f ≠ 0) (f_nonneg : 0 ≤ f) (f_mul : ∀ x y : R, f (x * y) ≤ c * f x * f y) : seminormFromBounded' f ≠ 0

views.nl_informal:
If `f : R → ℝ` is a nonnegative, multiplicatively bounded function, then the kernel of

views.nl_informal:
Riesz's lemma, which usually states that it is possible to find a
vector with norm 1 whose distance to a closed proper subspace is
arbitrarily close to 1. The statement here is in terms of multiples of
norms, since in general the existence of an element of norm exactly 1
is not guaranteed. For a variant giving an element with norm in `[1, R]`, see
`riesz_lemma_of_norm_lt`.

views.nl_informal:
A version of Riesz lemma: given a strict closed subspace `F`, one may find an element of norm `≤ R`
which is at distance at least `1` of every element of `F`. Here, `R` is any given constant
strictly larger than the norm of an element of norm `> 1`. For a version without an `R`, see
`riesz_lemma`.

Since we are considering a general nontrivially normed field, there may be a gap in possible norms
(for instance no element of norm in `(1,2)`). Hence, we can not allow `R` arbitrarily close to `1`,
and require `R > ‖c‖` for some `c : 𝕜` with norm `> 1`.

views.nl_informal:
**Hahn-Banach theorem** for continuous linear functions over `ℝ`.

that works both for `ℝ` and `ℂ`.

views.nl_informal:
**Hahn-Banach theorem** for continuous linear functions over `𝕜`
satisfying `IsRCLikeNormedField 𝕜`.

views.nl_informal:
Corollary of the **Hahn-Banach theorem**: if `f : p → F` is a continuous linear map
from a submodule of a normed space `E` over `𝕜`, `𝕜 = ℝ` or `𝕜 = ℂ`,
with a finite dimensional range, then `f` admits an extension to a continuous linear map `E → F`.

we provide no estimates on the norm of the extension.

views.nl_informal:
Corollary of Hahn-Banach. Given a nonzero element `x` of a normed space, there exists an
element of the dual space, of norm `1`, whose value on `x` is `‖x‖`.

the dual element arbitrarily when `x = 0`.

views.nl_informal:

all of `s` to values strictly below `1`.

views.nl_informal:

If a continuous multilinear map in finitely many variables on normed spaces satisfies
the inequality `‖f m‖ ≤ C * ∏ i, ‖m i‖` on a shell `ε i / ‖c i‖ < ‖m i‖ < ε i` for some positive
numbers `ε i` and elements `c i : 𝕜`, `1 < ‖c i‖`, then it satisfies this inequality for all `m`.

views.nl_informal:
If a multilinear map `f` satisfies a boundedness property around `0`,
one can deduce a bound on `f m₁ - f m₂` using the multilinearity.
Here, we give a precise but hard to use version.
See `norm_image_sub_le_of_bound` for a less precise but more usable version.
The bound reads
`‖f m - f m'‖ ≤
  C * ‖m 1 - m' 1‖ * max ‖m 2‖ ‖m' 2‖ * max ‖m 3‖ ‖m' 3‖ * ... * max ‖m n‖ ‖m' n‖ + ...`,
where the other terms in the sum are the same products where `1` is replaced by any `i`.

views.nl_informal:
If `f` satisfies a boundedness property around `0`, one can deduce a bound on `f m₁ - f m₂`
using the multilinearity. Here, we give a usable but not very precise version. See
`norm_image_sub_le_of_bound'` for a more precise but less usable version. The bound is
`‖f m - f m'‖ ≤ C * card ι * ‖m - m'‖ * (max ‖m‖ ‖m'‖) ^ (card ι - 1)`.

views.nl_informal:

If a multilinear map in finitely many variables on normed spaces satisfies the inequality

then its norm is bounded by the bound given to the constructor if it is nonnegative.

views.nl_informal:
If a continuous linear map is constructed from a linear map via the constructor `mkContinuous`,
then its norm is bounded by the bound or zero if bound is negative.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.mkContinuous_norm_le' (f : E →ₛₗ[σ₁₂] F) {C : ℝ} (h : ∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ C * ‖x‖) : ‖f.mkContinuous C h‖ ≤ max C 0

views.nl_informal:
The norm of the tensor product of a scalar linear map and of an element of a normed space
is the product of the norms.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContinuousLinearMap.norm_smulRight_apply (c : E →L[𝕜] 𝕜) (f : Fₗ) : ‖smulRight c f‖ = ‖c‖ * ‖f‖

views.nl_informal:
The non-negative norm of the tensor product of a scalar linear map and of an element of a normed
space is the product of the non-negative norms.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContinuousLinearMap.nnnorm_smulRight_apply (c : E →L[𝕜] 𝕜) (f : Fₗ) : ‖smulRight c f‖₊ = ‖c‖₊ * ‖f‖₊

views.nl_informal:
If a Cauchy sequence of continuous linear map converges to a continuous linear map pointwise,
then it converges to the same map in norm. This lemma is used to prove that the space of continuous
linear maps is complete provided that the codomain is a complete space.

views.nl_informal:
Let `s` be a bounded set in the space of continuous (semi)linear maps `E →SL[σ] F` taking values
in a proper space. Then `s` interpreted as a set in the space of maps `E → F` with topology of
pointwise convergence is precompact: its closure is a compact set.

views.nl_informal:
Let `s` be a bounded set in the space of continuous (semi)linear maps `E →SL[σ] F` taking values
in a proper space. If `s` interpreted as a set in the space of maps `E → F` with topology of
pointwise convergence is closed, then it is compact.

image under coercion to functions `E → F` is a closed set. We don't have a name for `E →SL[σ] F`
with weak-* topology in `mathlib`, so we use an equivalent condition (see `isClosed_induced_iff'`).

views.nl_informal:
If a set `s` of semilinear functions is bounded and is closed in the weak-* topology, then its

views.nl_informal:
The set of functions `f : E → F` that represent continuous linear maps `f : E →SL[σ₁₂] F`
at distance `≤ r` from `f₀ : E →SL[σ₁₂] F` is closed in the topology of pointwise convergence.

maps `f : E →SL[σ₁₂] F` at distance `≤ r` from `f₀ : E →SL[σ₁₂] F` is compact in the topology of

`Analysis.Normed.Module.WeakDual`.

views.nl_informal:
A Grönwall-like inequality: if `f : ℝ → ℝ` is continuous on `[a, b]` and satisfies
the inequalities `f a ≤ δ` and
`∀ x ∈ [a, b), liminf_{z→x+0} (f z - f x)/(z - x) ≤ K * (f x) + ε`, then `f x`
is bounded by `gronwallBound δ K ε (x - a)` on `[a, b]`.

See also `norm_le_gronwallBound_of_norm_deriv_right_le` for a version bounding `‖f x‖`,
`f : ℝ → E`.
views.lean_signature: theorem le_gronwallBound_of_liminf_deriv_right_le {f f' : ℝ → ℝ} {δ K ε : ℝ} {a b : ℝ} (hf : ContinuousOn f (Icc a b)) (hf' : ∀ x ∈ Ico a b, ∀ r, f' x < r → ∃ᶠ z in 𝓝[>] x, (z - x)⁻¹ * (f z - f x) < r) (ha : f a ≤ δ) (bound : ∀ x ∈ Ico a b, f' x ≤ K * f x + ε) : ∀ x ∈ Icc a b, f x ≤ gronwallBound δ K ε (x - a)

views.nl_informal:
A Grönwall-like inequality: if `f : ℝ → E` is continuous on `[a, b]`, has right derivative
`f' x` at every point `x ∈ [a, b)`, and satisfies the inequalities `‖f a‖ ≤ δ`,
`∀ x ∈ [a, b), ‖f' x‖ ≤ K * ‖f x‖ + ε`, then `‖f x‖` is bounded by `gronwallBound δ K ε (x - a)`
on `[a, b]`.
views.lean_signature: theorem norm_le_gronwallBound_of_norm_deriv_right_le {f f' : ℝ → E} {δ K ε : ℝ} {a b : ℝ} (hf : ContinuousOn f (Icc a b)) (hf' : ∀ x ∈ Ico a b, HasDerivWithinAt f (f' x) (Ici x) x) (ha : ‖f a‖ ≤ δ) (bound : ∀ x ∈ Ico a b, ‖f' x‖ ≤ K * ‖f x‖ + ε) : ∀ x ∈ Icc a b, ‖f x‖ ≤ gronwallBound δ K ε (x - a)

views.nl_informal:
If `f` and `g` are two approximate solutions of the same ODE, then the distance between them
can't grow faster than exponentially. This is a simple corollary of Grönwall's inequality, and some
people call this Grönwall's inequality too.

This version assumes all inequalities to be true in some time-dependent set `s t`,
and assumes that the solutions never leave this set.

views.nl_informal:
If `f` and `g` are two approximate solutions of the same ODE, then the distance between them

people call this Grönwall's inequality too.

This version assumes all inequalities to be true in the whole space.

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal: The function `log⁺` is even.

views.lean_signature: theorem Real.posLog_mul {a b : ℝ} : log⁺ (a * b) ≤ log⁺ a + log⁺ b

views.nl_informal:
Although `fun x => x ^ r` for fixed `r` is *not* complex-differentiable along the negative real

views.nl_informal:
An application of the layer cake formula / Cavalieri's principle / tail probability formula:

For a nonnegative function `f` on a measure space, the Lebesgue integral of `f` can
be written (roughly speaking) as: `∫⁻ f^p ∂μ = p * ∫⁻ t in 0..∞, t^(p-1) * μ {ω | f(ω) ≥ t}`.

See `MeasureTheory.lintegral_rpow_eq_lintegral_meas_lt_mul` for a version with sets of the form
`{ω | f(ω) > t}` instead.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.lintegral_rpow_eq_lintegral_meas_le_mul : ∫⁻ ω, ENNReal.ofReal (f ω ^ p) ∂μ = ENNReal.ofReal p * ∫⁻ t in Ioi 0, μ {a : α | t ≤ f a} * ENNReal.ofReal (t ^ (p - 1))

views.nl_informal:
An application of the layer cake formula / Cavalieri's principle / tail probability formula:

For a nonnegative function `f` on a measure space, the Lebesgue integral of `f` can
be written (roughly speaking) as: `∫⁻ f^p ∂μ = p * ∫⁻ t in 0..∞, t^(p-1) * μ {ω | f(ω) > t}`.

See `MeasureTheory.lintegral_rpow_eq_lintegral_meas_le_mul` for a version with sets of the form
`{ω | f(ω) ≥ t}` instead.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.lintegral_rpow_eq_lintegral_meas_lt_mul : ∫⁻ ω, ENNReal.ofReal (f ω ^ p) ∂μ = ENNReal.ofReal p * ∫⁻ t in Ioi 0, μ {a : α | t < f a} * ENNReal.ofReal (t ^ (p - 1))

views.nl_informal:
For `0 ≤ x`, the only problematic case in the equality `x ^ y * x ^ z = x ^ (y + z)` is for

The inequality is always true, though, and given in this lemma.
views.lean_signature: theorem Real.le_rpow_add {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 ≤ x) (y z : ℝ) : x ^ y * x ^ z ≤ x ^ (y + z)

views.lean_signature: theorem Real.abs_log_mul_self_rpow_lt (x t : ℝ) (h1 : 0 < x) (h2 : x ≤ 1) (ht : 0 < t) : |log x * x ^ t| < 1 / t

views.nl_informal: `log x` is bounded above by a multiple of every power of `x` with positive exponent.
views.lean_signature: theorem Real.log_le_rpow_div {x ε : ℝ} (hx : 0 ≤ x) (hε : 0 < ε) : log x ≤ x ^ ε / ε

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:
A supporting lemma for the **Phragmen-Lindelöf principle** in a horizontal strip. If `z : ℂ`
belongs to a horizontal strip `|Complex.im z| ≤ b`, `b ≤ π / 2`, and `a ≤ 0`, then
$$\left|exp^{a\left(e^{z}+e^{-z}\right)}\right| \le e^{a\cos b \exp^{|re z|}}.$$
views.lean_signature: theorem Complex.norm_exp_mul_exp_add_exp_neg_le_of_abs_im_le {a b : ℝ} (ha : a ≤ 0) {z : ℂ} (hz : |z.im| ≤ b) (hb : b ≤ π / 2) : ‖exp (a * (exp z + exp (-z)))‖ ≤ Real.exp (a * Real.cos b * Real.exp |z.re|)

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal: Half of **Jordan's inequality** for `cos`.

views.nl_informal:
For 0 < x ≤ 1 we have x - x ^ 3 / 4 < sin x.

This is also true for x > 1, but it's nontrivial for x just above 1. This inequality is not
tight; the tighter inequality is sin x > x - x ^ 3 / 6 for all x > 0, but this inequality has
a simpler proof.
views.lean_signature: theorem Real.sin_gt_sub_cube {x : ℝ} (h : 0 < x) (h' : x ≤ 1) : x - x ^ 3 / 4 < sin x

views.nl_informal:
For all `0 < x < π/2` we have `x < tan x`.

If `J` is connected, then given any function `F` such that the presence of a
morphism `j₁ ⟶ j₂` implies `F j₁ = F j₂`, we have that `F` is constant.

This can be thought of as a local-to-global property.

views.nl_informal:
`J` is connected if: given any function `F : J → α` which is constant for any
`j₁, j₂` for which there is a morphism `j₁ ⟶ j₂`, then `F` is constant.
This can be thought of as a local-to-global property.

views.nl_informal:
An inductive-like property for the objects of a connected category.
If the set `p` is nonempty, and `p` is closed under morphisms of `J`,
then `p` contains all of `J`.

views.nl_informal:
Given a pushout square in an abelian category
```
X₁ ⟶ X₂
|    |
v    v
X₃ ⟶ X₄
```
the morphism `X₂ ⊞ X₃ ⟶ X₄` is an epimorphism. This lemma translates this
as the existence of liftings up to refinements: a morphism `z : T ⟶ X₄`
can be written as a sum of a morphism to `X₂` and a morphism to `X₃`,
at least if we allow a precomposition with an epimorphism `π : T' ⟶ T`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.IsPushout.hom_eq_add_up_to_refinements (h : IsPushout t l r b) {T : C} (x₄ : T ⟶ X₄) : ∃ (T' : C) (π : T' ⟶ T) (_ : Epi π) (x₂ : T' ⟶ X₂) (x₃ : T' ⟶ X₃), π ≫ x₄ = x₂ ≫ r + x₃ ≫ b

views.nl_informal:
Given a commutative diagram in an abelian category
```
X₁ ⟶ X₂
|    |  \
v    v   \
X₃ ⟶ X₄   \
 \     \   v
  \     \> X₅
   \_____>
```
where the top/left square is a pushout square,
the outer square involving `X₁`, `X₂`, `X₃` and `X₅`
is a pullback square, and `X₂ ⟶ X₅` is mono,
then `X₄ ⟶ X₅` is a mono.

between the points of cocones `c₁` and `c₂` for `X₁` and `X₂`, in such
a way that `c₂` is colimit and `f` is compatible with `φ`, then `f` is an epimorphism.

views.nl_informal:
Assume that a functor `X : J ⥤ C` maps any morphism to a monomorphism,
that `J` is filtered. Then the "inclusion" map `c.ι.app j₀` of a colimit cocone for `X`
is a monomorphism if `colim : (Under j₀ ⥤ C) ⥤ C` preserves monomorphisms
(e.g. when `C` satisfies AB5).
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.mono_ι_app_of_isFiltered {X : J ⥤ C} [∀ (j j' : J) (φ : j ⟶ j'), Mono (X.map φ)] {c : Cocone X} (hc : IsColimit c) [IsFiltered J] (j₀ : J) [HasColimitsOfShape (Under j₀) C] [(colim : (Under j₀ ⥤ C) ⥤ C).PreservesMonomorphisms] : Mono (c.ι.app j₀)

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:

the inclusions of the colimit.

views.nl_informal:
If `X` is an object in a Grothendieck abelian category, then
the functor `coyoneda.obj (op X)` commutes with colimits corresponding
to diagrams of monomorphisms indexed by `κ`-filtered categories
for a big enough regular cardinal `κ`.

views.nl_informal:
If `p : X ⟶ Y` is a monomorphism that is not an isomorphism, there exists
a subobject `X'` of `Y` containing `X` (but different from `X`) such that
the inclusion `X ⟶ X'` is a pushout of a monomorphism in the family
`generatingMonomorphisms G`.

is an isomorphism, then `α` is an isomorphism. The converse is given in `Conjugate_iso`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.conjugateEquiv_of_iso (α : L₂ ⟶ L₁) [IsIso (conjugateEquiv adj₁ adj₂ α)] : IsIso α

views.nl_informal:
If `α` is a natural transformation between right adjoints whose conjugate natural transformation is
an isomorphism, then `α` is an isomorphism. The converse is given in `conjugateEquiv_symm_iso`.

views.nl_informal:
When all four functors in a sequare are left adjoints, the mates operation can be iterated:

```
         L₁                  R₁                  R₁
      C --→ D             C ←-- D             C ←-- D
   F₁ ↓  ↗  ↓  F₂      F₁ ↓  ↘  ↓ F₂       U₁ ↑  ↙  ↑ U₂
      E --→ F             E ←-- F             E ←-- F
         L₂                  R₂                  R₂
```

In this case the iterated mate equals the conjugate of the original transformation and is thus an
isomorphism if and only if the original transformation is. This explains why some Beck-Chevalley
natural transformations are natural isomorphisms.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.iterated_mateEquiv_conjugateEquiv (α : TwoSquare F₁ L₁ L₂ F₂) : (mateEquiv adj₄ adj₃ (mateEquiv adj₁ adj₂ α)).natTrans = conjugateEquiv (adj₁.comp adj₄) (adj₃.comp adj₂) α

views.nl_informal: The mates equivalence commutes with this composition, essentially by `mateEquiv_vcomp`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.mateEquiv_conjugateEquiv_vcomp {L₁ : A ⥤ B} {R₁ : B ⥤ A} {L₂ : C ⥤ D} {R₂ : D ⥤ C} {L₃ : C ⥤ D} {R₃ : D ⥤ C} (adj₁ : L₁ ⊣ R₁) (adj₂ : L₂ ⊣ R₂) (adj₃ : L₃ ⊣ R₃) (α : TwoSquare G L₁ L₂ H) (β : L₃ ⟶ L₂) : (mateEquiv adj₁ adj₃) (α.whiskerRight β) = (mateEquiv adj₁ adj₂ α).whiskerBottom (conjugateEquiv adj₂ adj₃ β)

views.nl_informal: The mates equivalence commutes with this composition, essentially by `mateEquiv_vcomp`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.conjugateEquiv_mateEquiv_vcomp {L₁ : A ⥤ B} {R₁ : B ⥤ A} {L₂ : A ⥤ B} {R₂ : B ⥤ A} {L₃ : C ⥤ D} {R₃ : D ⥤ C} (adj₁ : L₁ ⊣ R₁) (adj₂ : L₂ ⊣ R₂) (adj₃ : L₃ ⊣ R₃) (α : L₂ ⟶ L₁) (β : TwoSquare G L₂ L₃ H) : (mateEquiv adj₁ adj₃) (β.whiskerLeft α) = (mateEquiv adj₂ adj₃ β).whiskerTop (conjugateEquiv adj₁ adj₂ α)

If `A` is essentially in the image of a reflective functor `i`, then `η_A` is an isomorphism.
This gives that the "witness" for `A` being in the essential image can instead be given as the
reflection of `A`, with the isomorphism as `η_A`.

(For any `B` in the reflective subcategory, we automatically have that `ε_B` is an iso.)

views.nl_informal:
The adjoint triangle theorem: Suppose `U : B ⥤ C` has a left adjoint `F` such that each counit
`ε_X : FUX ⟶ X` is a regular epimorphism. Then if a category `A` has coequalizers of reflexive
pairs, then a functor `R : A ⥤ B` has a left adjoint if the composite `R ⋙ U` does.

Note the converse is true (with weaker assumptions), by `Adjunction.comp`.
See https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/adjoint+triangle+theorem
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.isRightAdjoint_triangle_lift {U : B ⥤ C} {F : C ⥤ B} (R : A ⥤ B) (adj₁ : F ⊣ U) [∀ X : B, RegularEpi (adj₁.counit.app X)] [HasReflexiveCoequalizers A] [(R ⋙ U).IsRightAdjoint ] : R.IsRightAdjoint

views.nl_informal:
If `R ⋙ U` has a left adjoint, the domain of `R` has reflexive coequalizers and `U` is a monadic
functor, then `R` has a left adjoint.
This is a special case of `isRightAdjoint_triangle_lift` which is often more useful in practice.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.isRightAdjoint_triangle_lift_monadic (U : B ⥤ C) [MonadicRightAdjoint U] {R : A ⥤ B} [HasReflexiveCoequalizers A] [(R ⋙ U).IsRightAdjoint] : R.IsRightAdjoint

views.nl_informal:
Suppose we have a commutative square of functors

```
      Q
    A → B
  U ↓   ↓ V
    C → D
      R
```

where `U` has a left adjoint, `A` has reflexive coequalizers and `V` has a left adjoint such that
each component of the counit is a regular epi.
Then `Q` has a left adjoint if `R` has a left adjoint.

See https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/adjoint+lifting+theorem
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.isRightAdjoint_square_lift (Q : A ⥤ B) (V : B ⥤ D) (U : A ⥤ C) (R : C ⥤ D) (comm : U ⋙ R ≅ Q ⋙ V) [U.IsRightAdjoint] [V.IsRightAdjoint] [R.IsRightAdjoint] [∀ X, RegularEpi ((Adjunction.ofIsRightAdjoint V).counit.app X)] [HasReflexiveCoequalizers A] : Q.IsRightAdjoint

views.nl_informal:
Suppose we have a commutative square of functors

```
  U ↓   ↓ V
    C → D
      R
```

where `U` has a left adjoint, `A` has reflexive coequalizers and `V` is monadic.

views.nl_informal:
The adjoint triangle theorem: Suppose `U : A ⥤ B` has a left adjoint `F` such that each unit
`η_X : X ⟶ UFX` is a regular monomorphism. Then if a category `C` has equalizers of coreflexive
pairs, then a functor `L : C ⥤ B` has a right adjoint if the composite `L ⋙ F` does.

Note the converse is true (with weaker assumptions), by `Adjunction.comp`.

views.nl_informal:
When all four morphisms in a square are left adjoints, the mates operation can be iterated:
         l₁                  r₁                  r₁
      c --→ d             c ←-- d             c ←-- d
   f₁ ↓  ↗  ↓  f₂      f₁ ↓  ↘  ↓ f₂       u₁ ↑  ↙  ↑ u₂

views.nl_informal:
Suppose we have a monoidal equivalence `F : C ≌ D`, with `D` monoidal closed. We can pull the
monoidal closed instance back along the equivalence. For `X, Y, Z : C`, this lemma describes the
resulting currying map `Hom(X ⊗ Y, Z) → Hom(Y, (X ⟶[C] Z))`. (`X ⟶[C] Z` is defined to be
`F⁻¹(F(X) ⟶[D] F(Z))`, so currying in `C` is given by essentially conjugating currying in
`D` by `F.`)
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.MonoidalClosed.ofEquiv_curry_def {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⊗ Y ⟶ Z) : letI

views.nl_informal:
Suppose we have a monoidal equivalence `F : C ≌ D`, with `D` monoidal closed. We can pull the
monoidal closed instance back along the equivalence. For `X, Y, Z : C`, this lemma describes the
resulting uncurrying map `Hom(Y, (X ⟶[C] Z)) → Hom(X ⊗ Y ⟶ Z)`. (`X ⟶[C] Z` is
defined to be `F⁻¹(F(X) ⟶[D] F(Z))`, so uncurrying in `C` is given by essentially conjugating
uncurrying in `D` by `F.`)
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.MonoidalClosed.ofEquiv_uncurry_def {X Y Z : C} : letI

views.nl_informal:
Let the following diagram commute up to isomorphism:

```
      L       R
  A  ---→ T  ←--- B
  |       |       |
  | F     | H     | G
  ↓       ↓       ↓
  A' ---→ T' ←--- B'
      L'      R'
```

Let `F`, `G`, `R` and `R'` be final and `B` be filtered. Then, the induced functor between the comma
categories of the first and second row of the diagram is final.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Comma.map_final {A : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} A] {B : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} B] {T : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃} T] {L : A ⥤ T} {R : B ⥤ T} {A' : Type u₄} [Category.{v₄} A'] {B' : Type u₅} [Category.{v₅} B'] {T' : Type u₆} [Category.{v₆} T'] {L' : A' ⥤ T'} {R' : B' ⥤ T'} {F : A ⥤ A'} {G : B ⥤ B'} {H : T ⥤ T'} (iL : F ⋙ L' ≅ L ⋙ H) (iR : G ⋙ R' ≅ R ⋙ H) [IsFiltered B] [R.Final] [R'.Final] [F.Final] [G.Final] : (Comma.map iL.hom iR.inv).Final

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:
To show a category is cartesian distributive it is enough to show it is left distributive.
The right distributivity is inferred from symmetry of the cartesian monoidal structure.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.IsCartesianDistributive.of_isMonoidalLeftDistrib [IsMonoidalLeftDistrib C] : IsCartesianDistributive C

views.nl_informal:
The forward direction of the left distributivity isomorphism is the cogap morphism
`coprod.desc (_ ◁ coprod.inl) (_ ◁ coprod.inr) : (X ⊗ Y) ⨿ (X ⊗ Z) ⟶ X ⊗ (Y ⨿ Z)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.leftDistrib_hom [IsMonoidalLeftDistrib C] {X Y Z : C} : (∂L X Y Z).hom = coprod.desc (_ ◁ coprod.inl) (_ ◁ coprod.inr)

views.nl_informal:
The composite of `(X ◁ coprod.inl) : X ⊗ Y ⟶ X ⊗ (Y ⨿ Z)` and
`(∂L X Y Z).inv :  X ⊗ (Y ⨿ Z) ⟶ (X ⊗ Y) ⨿ (X ⊗ Z)`
is equal to the left coprojection `coprod.inl : X ⊗ Y ⟶ (X ⊗ Y) ⨿ (X ⊗ Z)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.whiskerLeft_coprod_inl_leftDistrib_inv [IsMonoidalLeftDistrib C] {X Y Z : C} : (X ◁ coprod.inl) ≫ (∂L X Y Z).inv = coprod.inl

views.nl_informal:
The composite of `(X ◁ coprod.inr) : X ⊗ Z ⟶ X ⊗ (Y ⨿ Z)` and
`(∂L X Y Z).inv :  X ⊗ (Y ⨿ Z) ⟶ (X ⊗ Y) ⨿ (X ⊗ Z)`
is equal to the right coprojection `coprod.inr : X ⊗ Z ⟶ (X ⊗ Y) ⨿ (X ⊗ Z)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.whiskerLeft_coprod_inr_leftDistrib_inv [IsMonoidalLeftDistrib C] {X Y Z : C} : (X ◁ coprod.inr) ≫ (∂L X Y Z).inv = coprod.inr

views.nl_informal:
The forward direction of the right distributivity isomorphism is equal to the cogap morphism
`coprod.desc (coprod.inl ▷ _) (coprod.inr ▷ _) : (Y ⊗ X) ⨿ (Z ⊗ X) ⟶ (Y ⨿ Z) ⊗ X`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.rightDistrib_hom [IsMonoidalRightDistrib C] {X Y Z : C} : (∂R X Y Z).hom = coprod.desc (coprod.inl ▷ _) (coprod.inr ▷ _)

views.nl_informal:
The composite of `(coprod.inl ▷ X) : Y ⊗ X ⟶ (Y ⨿ Z) ⊗ X` and
`(∂R X Y Z).inv :  (Y ⨿ Z) ⊗ X ⟶ (Y ⊗ X) ⨿ (Z ⊗ X)` is equal to the left coprojection
`coprod.inl : Y ⊗ X ⟶ (Y ⊗ X) ⨿ (Z ⊗ X)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.whiskerRight_coprod_inl_rightDistrib_inv [IsMonoidalRightDistrib C] {X Y Z : C} : (coprod.inl ▷ X) ≫ (∂R X Y Z).inv = coprod.inl

views.nl_informal:
The composite of `(coprod.inr ▷ X) : Z ⊗ X ⟶ (Y ⨿ Z) ⊗ X` and
`(∂R X Y Z).inv :  (Y ⨿ Z) ⊗ X ⟶ (Y ⊗ X) ⨿ (Z ⊗ X)` is equal to the right coprojection
`coprod.inr : Z ⊗ X ⟶ (Y ⊗ X) ⨿ (Z ⊗ X)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.whiskerRight_coprod_inr_rightDistrib_inv [IsMonoidalRightDistrib C] {X Y Z : C} : (coprod.inr ▷ X) ≫ (∂R X Y Z).inv = coprod.inr

views.nl_informal: The identity in the "underlying" category of an enriched category.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.forgetEnrichment_id (X : ForgetEnrichment W C) : ForgetEnrichment.homTo W (𝟙 X) = eId W (ForgetEnrichment.to W X : C)

views.nl_informal: Composition in the "underlying" category of an enriched category.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.forgetEnrichment_comp {X Y Z : ForgetEnrichment W C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) : ForgetEnrichment.homTo W (f ≫ g) = ((λ_ (𝟙_ W)).inv ≫ (ForgetEnrichment.homTo W f ⊗ ForgetEnrichment.homTo W g)) ≫ eComp W _ _ _

views.nl_informal:
`eHomCongr` respects composition of morphisms. Recall that for any
composable pair of arrows `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` in `C`, the composite
`f ≫ g` in `C` defines a morphism `𝟙_ V ⟶ (X ⟶[V] Z)` in `V`. Composing with
the isomorphism `eHomCongr V α γ` yields a morphism in `V` that can be factored
through the enriched composition map as shown:
`𝟙_ V ⟶ 𝟙_ V ⊗ 𝟙_ V ⟶ (X₁ ⟶[V] Y₁) ⊗ (Y₁ ⟶[V] Z₁) ⟶ (X₁ ⟶[V] Z₁)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Iso.eHomCongr_comp {X Y Z X₁ Y₁ Z₁ : C} (α : X ≅ X₁) (β : Y ≅ Y₁) (γ : Z ≅ Z₁) (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) : eHomEquiv V (f ≫ g) ≫ (eHomCongr V α γ).hom = (λ_ _).inv ≫ (eHomEquiv V f ≫ (eHomCongr V α β).hom) ▷ _ ≫ _ ◁ (eHomEquiv V g ≫ (eHomCongr V β γ).hom) ≫ eComp V X₁ Y₁ Z₁

views.nl_informal: The inverse map defined by `eHomCongr` respects composition of morphisms.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Iso.eHomCongr_inv_comp {X Y Z X₁ Y₁ Z₁ : C} (α : X ≅ X₁) (β : Y ≅ Y₁) (γ : Z ≅ Z₁) (f : X₁ ⟶ Y₁) (g : Y₁ ⟶ Z₁) : eHomEquiv V (f ≫ g) ≫ (eHomCongr V α γ).inv = (λ_ _).inv ≫ (eHomEquiv V f ≫ (eHomCongr V α β).inv) ▷ _ ≫ _ ◁ (eHomEquiv V g ≫ (eHomCongr V β γ).inv) ≫ eComp V X Y Z

views.nl_informal: Unfold the definition of composition in the enriched opposite category.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.eComp_op_eq {C : Type u} [EnrichedCategory V C] (x y z : Cᵒᵖ) : eComp V z y x = (β_ _ _).hom ≫ eComp V x.unop y.unop z.unop

views.nl_informal:
When composing a tensor product of morphisms with the `V`-composition morphism in `Cᵒᵖ`,
this re-writes the `V`-composition to be in `C` and moves the braiding to the left.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.tensorHom_eComp_op_eq {C : Type u} [EnrichedCategory V C] {x y z : Cᵒᵖ} {v w : V} (f : v ⟶ EnrichedCategory.Hom z y) (g : w ⟶ EnrichedCategory.Hom y x) : (f ⊗ g) ≫ eComp V z y x = (β_ v w).hom ≫ (g ⊗ f) ≫ eComp V x.unop y.unop z.unop

views.nl_informal: If a functor `F` has a conical limit, so does any naturally isomorphic functor.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Enriched.HasConicalLimit.of_iso {F G : J ⥤ C} [HasConicalLimit V F] (e : F ≅ G) : HasConicalLimit V G

views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Enriched.HasConicalLimit.of_equiv_comp (F : J ⥤ C) (G : J' ⥤ J) [G.IsEquivalence] [HasConicalLimit V (G ⋙ F)] : HasConicalLimit V F

views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Enriched.HasConicalLimitsOfShape.of_equiv [HasConicalLimitsOfShape J' V C] (G : J' ⥤ J) [G.IsEquivalence] : HasConicalLimitsOfShape J V C

views.nl_informal: Whiskering commutes with the enriched composition.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.eComp_eHomWhiskerRight {X X' : C} (f : X ⟶ X') (Y Z : C) : eComp V X' Y Z ≫ eHomWhiskerRight V f Z = eHomWhiskerRight V f Y ▷ _ ≫ eComp V X Y Z

views.nl_informal: Whiskering commutes with the enriched composition.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.eComp_eHomWhiskerLeft (X Y : C) {Z Z' : C} (g : Z ⟶ Z') : eComp V X Y Z ≫ eHomWhiskerLeft V X g = _ ◁ eHomWhiskerLeft V Y g ≫ eComp V X Y Z'

views.nl_informal:
Given an isomorphism `α : Y ≅ Y₁` in C, the enriched composition map
`eComp V X Y Z : (X ⟶[V] Y) ⊗ (Y ⟶[V] Z) ⟶ (X ⟶[V] Z)` factors through the `V`
object `(X ⟶[V] Y₁) ⊗ (Y₁ ⟶[V] Z)` via the map defined by whiskering in the
middle with `α.hom` and `α.inv`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.eHom_whisker_cancel {X Y Y₁ Z : C} (α : Y ≅ Y₁) : eHomWhiskerLeft V X α.hom ▷ _ ≫ _ ◁ eHomWhiskerRight V α.inv Z ≫ eComp V X Y₁ Z = eComp V X Y Z

views.nl_informal:
For a based functor `F : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴`, and an arrow `φ` in `𝒳`, then `φ` lifts an arrow `f` in `𝒮`

views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.BasedFunctor.isHomLift_map [IsHomLift 𝒴.p f (F.map φ)] : IsHomLift 𝒳.p f φ

views.nl_informal:
Given a cartesian morphism `φ : a ⟶ b` lying over `f : R ⟶ S` in `𝒳`, and another morphism
`φ' : a' ⟶ b` which also lifts `f`. Then any morphism `ψ : a' ⟶ a` lifting `𝟙 R` such that
`g ≫ ψ = φ'` must equal the map induced from the universal property of `φ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Functor.IsCartesian.map_uniq (ψ : a' ⟶ a) [IsHomLift p (𝟙 R) ψ] (hψ : ψ ≫ φ = φ') : ψ = IsCartesian.map p f φ φ'

views.nl_informal:
Given a cartesian morphism `φ : a ⟶ b` lying over `f : R ⟶ S` in `𝒳`, and two morphisms
`ψ ψ' : a' ⟶ a` such that `ψ ≫ φ = ψ' ≫ φ`. Then we must have `ψ = ψ'`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Functor.IsCartesian.ext (φ : a ⟶ b) [IsCartesian p f φ] {a' : 𝒳} (ψ ψ' : a' ⟶ a) [IsHomLift p (𝟙 R) ψ] [IsHomLift p (𝟙 R) ψ'] (h : ψ ≫ φ = ψ' ≫ φ) : ψ = ψ'

views.nl_informal:
The universal property of a strongly cartesian morphism.

This lemma is more flexible with respect to non-definitional equalities than the field
`universal_property'` of `IsStronglyCartesian`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Functor.IsStronglyCartesian.universal_property {R' : 𝒮} {a' : 𝒳} (g : R' ⟶ R) (f' : R' ⟶ S) (hf' : f' = g ≫ f) (φ' : a' ⟶ b) [IsHomLift p f' φ'] : ∃! χ : a' ⟶ a, IsHomLift p g χ ∧ χ ≫ φ = φ'

views.nl_informal:
Given a diagram
```
a'        a --φ--> b
|         |        |
v         v        v
R' --g--> R --f--> S
```
such that `φ` is strongly cartesian, and morphisms `φ' : a' ⟶ b`, `ψ : a' ⟶ a` such that
`ψ ≫ φ = φ'`. Then `ψ` is the map induced by the universal property.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Functor.IsStronglyCartesian.map_uniq (ψ : a' ⟶ a) [IsHomLift p g ψ] (hψ : ψ ≫ φ = φ') : ψ = map p f φ hf' φ'

views.nl_informal:
Given a diagram
```
a'        a --φ--> b
|         |        |
v         v        v
R' --g--> R --f--> S
```
such that `φ` is strongly cartesian, and morphisms `ψ ψ' : a' ⟶ a` such that
`g ≫ ψ = φ' = g ≫ ψ'`. Then we have that `ψ = ψ'`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Functor.IsStronglyCartesian.ext (φ : a ⟶ b) [IsStronglyCartesian p f φ] {R' : 𝒮} {a' : 𝒳} (g : R' ⟶ R) {ψ ψ' : a' ⟶ a} [IsHomLift p g ψ] [IsHomLift p g ψ'] (h : ψ ≫ φ = ψ' ≫ φ) : ψ = ψ'

views.nl_informal:
When its possible to compare the two, the composition of two `IsStronglyCartesian.map` will also
be given by a `IsStronglyCartesian.map`. In other words, given diagrams
```
a''         a'        a --φ--> b
|           |         |        |
v           v         v        v
R'' --g'--> R' --g--> R --f--> S
```
and
```
a' --φ'--> b
|          |
v          v
R' --f'--> S
```
and
```
a'' --φ''--> b
|            |
v            v
R'' --f''--> S
```
such that `φ` and `φ'` are strongly cartesian morphisms, and such that `f' = g ≫ f` and
`f'' = g' ≫ f'`. Then composing the induced map from `a'' ⟶ a'` with the induced map from
`a' ⟶ a` gives the induced map from `a'' ⟶ a`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Functor.IsStronglyCartesian.map_comp_map {R' R'' : 𝒮} {a' a'' : 𝒳} {f' : R' ⟶ S} {f'' : R'' ⟶ S} {g : R' ⟶ R} {g' : R'' ⟶ R'} (H : f' = g ≫ f) (H' : f'' = g' ≫ f') (φ' : a' ⟶ b) (φ'' : a'' ⟶ b) [IsStronglyCartesian p f' φ'] [IsHomLift p f'' φ''] : map p f' φ' H' φ'' ≫ map p f φ H φ' = map p f φ (show f'' = (g' ≫ g) ≫ f by rwa [assoc, ← H]) φ''

views.nl_informal:
Given two commutative squares
```
a --φ--> b --ψ--> c
|        |        |
v        v        v
R --f--> S --g--> T
```
such that `φ ≫ ψ` and `ψ` are strongly cartesian, then so is `φ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Functor.IsStronglyCartesian.of_comp [IsStronglyCartesian p g ψ] [IsStronglyCartesian p (f ≫ g) (φ ≫ ψ)] [IsHomLift p f φ] : IsStronglyCartesian p f φ

views.nl_informal: A strongly cartesian morphism lying over an isomorphism is an isomorphism.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Functor.IsStronglyCartesian.isIso_of_base_isIso (φ : a ⟶ b) [IsStronglyCartesian p f φ] [IsIso f] : IsIso φ

views.nl_informal:
Given a cocartesian morphism `φ : a ⟶ b` lying over `f : R ⟶ S` in `𝒳`, and another morphism
`φ' : a ⟶ b'` which also lifts `f`. Then any morphism `ψ : b ⟶ b'` lifting `𝟙 S` such that

views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Functor.IsCocartesian.map_uniq (ψ : b ⟶ b') [IsHomLift p (𝟙 S) ψ] (hψ : φ ≫ ψ = φ') : ψ = IsCocartesian.map p f φ φ'

views.nl_informal:
Given a cocartesian morphism `φ : a ⟶ b` lying over `f : R ⟶ S` in `𝒳`, and two morphisms
`ψ ψ' : b ⟶ b'` lifting `𝟙 S` such that `φ ≫ ψ = φ ≫ ψ'`. Then we must have `ψ = ψ'`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Functor.IsCocartesian.ext (φ : a ⟶ b) [IsCocartesian p f φ] {b' : 𝒳} (ψ ψ' : b ⟶ b') [IsHomLift p (𝟙 S) ψ] [IsHomLift p (𝟙 S) ψ'] (h : φ ≫ ψ = φ ≫ ψ') : ψ = ψ'

views.nl_informal:
The universal property of a strongly cocartesian morphism.

This lemma is more flexible with respect to non-definitional equalities than the field
`universal_property'` of `IsStronglyCocartesian`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Functor.IsStronglyCocartesian.universal_property {S' : 𝒮} {b' : 𝒳} (g : S ⟶ S') (f' : R ⟶ S') (hf' : f' = f ≫ g) (φ' : a ⟶ b') [IsHomLift p f' φ'] : ∃! χ : b ⟶ b', IsHomLift p g χ ∧ φ ≫ χ = φ'

views.nl_informal:
Given a diagram
```
a --φ--> b        b'
|        |        |
v        v        v
R --f--> S --g--> S'
```
such that `φ` is strongly cocartesian, and morphisms `φ' : a ⟶ b'`, `ψ : b ⟶ b'` such that

views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Functor.IsStronglyCocartesian.map_uniq (ψ : b ⟶ b') [IsHomLift p g ψ] (hψ : φ ≫ ψ = φ') : ψ = map p f φ hf' φ'

views.nl_informal:
Given a diagram
```
a --φ--> b        b'
|        |        |
v        v        v
R --f--> S --g--> S'
```
such that `φ` is strongly cocartesian, and morphisms `ψ ψ' : b ⟶ b'` such that
`g ≫ ψ = φ' = g ≫ ψ'`. Then we have that `ψ = ψ'`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Functor.IsStronglyCocartesian.ext (φ : a ⟶ b) [IsStronglyCocartesian p f φ] {S' : 𝒮} {b' : 𝒳} (g : S ⟶ S') {ψ ψ' : b ⟶ b'} [IsHomLift p g ψ] [IsHomLift p g ψ'] (h : φ ≫ ψ = φ ≫ ψ') : ψ = ψ'

views.nl_informal:
When its possible to compare the two, the composition of two `IsStronglyCocartesian.map` will
also be given by a `IsStronglyCocartesian.map`. In other words, given diagrams
```
a --φ--> b        b'         b''
|        |        |          |
v        v        v          v
R --f--> S --g--> S' --g'--> S'
```
and
```
a --φ'--> b'
|         |
v         v
R --f'--> S'

```
and
```
a --φ''--> b''
|          |
v          v
R --f''--> S''
```
such that `φ` and `φ'` are strongly cocartesian morphisms, and such that `f' = f ≫ g` and
`f'' = f' ≫ g'`. Then composing the induced map from `b ⟶ b'` with the induced map from
`b' ⟶ b''` gives the induced map from `b ⟶ b''`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Functor.IsStronglyCocartesian.map_comp_map {S' S'' : 𝒮} {b' b'' : 𝒳} {f' : R ⟶ S'} {f'' : R ⟶ S''} {g : S ⟶ S'} {g' : S' ⟶ S''} (H : f' = f ≫ g) (H' : f'' = f' ≫ g') (φ' : a ⟶ b') (φ'' : a ⟶ b'') [IsStronglyCocartesian p f' φ'] [IsHomLift p f'' φ''] : map p f φ H φ' ≫ map p f' φ' H' φ'' = map p f φ (show f'' = f ≫ (g ≫ g') by rwa [← assoc, ← H]) φ''

views.nl_informal:
Given two commutative squares
```
a --φ--> b --ψ--> c
|        |        |
v        v        v
R --f--> S --g--> T
```
such that `φ ≫ ψ` and `φ` are strongly cocartesian, then so is `ψ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Functor.IsStronglyCocartesian.of_comp [IsStronglyCocartesian p f φ] [IsStronglyCocartesian p (f ≫ g) (φ ≫ ψ)] [IsHomLift p g ψ] : IsStronglyCocartesian p g ψ

views.nl_informal: A strongly cocartesian arrow lying over an isomorphism is an isomorphism.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Functor.IsStronglyCocartesian.isIso_of_base_isIso (φ : a ⟶ b) [IsStronglyCocartesian p f φ] [IsIso f] : IsIso φ

views.nl_informal:
In a category which admits strongly cartesian pullbacks, any cartesian morphism is

views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Functor.IsFibered.isStronglyCartesian_of_exists_isCartesian (p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮) (h : ∀ (a : 𝒳) (R : 𝒮) (f : R ⟶ p.obj a), ∃ (b : 𝒳) (φ : b ⟶ a), IsStronglyCartesian p f φ) {R S : 𝒮} (f : R ⟶ S) {a b : 𝒳} (φ : a ⟶ b) [p.IsCartesian f φ] : p.IsStronglyCartesian f φ

views.nl_informal:
If `C` is filtered or empty, and we have a right adjoint functor `R : C ⥤ D`, then `D` is

views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.IsFilteredOrEmpty.of_isRightAdjoint (R : C ⥤ D) [R.IsRightAdjoint] : IsFilteredOrEmpty D

views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.IsFilteredOrEmpty.of_equivalence (h : C ≌ D) : IsFilteredOrEmpty D

views.nl_informal: Any finite collection of objects in a filtered category has an object "to the right".
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.IsFiltered.sup_objs_exists (O : Finset C) : ∃ S : C, ∀ {X}, X ∈ O → Nonempty (X ⟶ S)

views.nl_informal:
Given any `Finset` of objects `{X, ...}` and
indexed collection of `Finset`s of morphisms `{f, ...}` in `C`,
there exists an object `S`, with a morphism `T X : X ⟶ S` from each `X`,
such that the triangles commute: `f ≫ T Y = T X`, for `f : X ⟶ Y` in the `Finset`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.IsFiltered.sup_exists : ∃ (S : C) (T : ∀ {X : C}, X ∈ O → (X ⟶ S)), ∀ {X Y : C} (mX : X ∈ O) (mY : Y ∈ O) {f : X ⟶ Y}, (⟨X, Y, mX, mY, f⟩ : Σ' (X Y : C) (_ : X ∈ O) (_ : Y ∈ O), X ⟶ Y) ∈ H → f ≫ T mY = T mX

views.nl_informal: The triangles of consisting of a morphism in `H` and the maps to `sup O H` commute.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.IsFiltered.toSup_commutes {X Y : C} (mX : X ∈ O) (mY : Y ∈ O) {f : X ⟶ Y} (mf : (⟨X, Y, mX, mY, f⟩ : Σ' (X Y : C) (_ : X ∈ O) (_ : Y ∈ O), X ⟶ Y) ∈ H) : f ≫ toSup O H mY = toSup O H mX

If we have `IsFiltered C`, then for any functor `F : J ⥤ C` with `FinCategory J`,

views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.IsFiltered.of_isRightAdjoint (R : C ⥤ D) [R.IsRightAdjoint] : IsFiltered D

views.nl_informal:
