views.nl_informal:
Day's reflection theorem.

Let `D` be a symmetric monoidal closed category and let `C` be a reflective subcategory. Denote by
`R : C ⥤ D` the inclusion functor and by `L : D ⥤ C` the reflector. Let `u` denote the unit of the
adjunction `L ⊣ R`. Denote the internal hom by `[-,-]`. The following are equivalent:

1. `u : [d, Rc] ⟶ RL[d, Rc]` is an isomorphism,
2. `[u, 𝟙] : [RLd, Rc] ⟶ [d, Rc]` is an isomorphism,
3. `L(u ▷ d') : L(d ⊗ d') ⟶ L(RLd ⊗ d')` is an isomorphism,
4. `L(u ⊗ u) : L(d ⊗ d') ⟶ L(RLd ⊗ RLd')` is an isomorphism,

where `c, d, d'` are arbitrary objects of `C`/`D`, quantified over separately in each condition.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Reflective.isIso_tfae : List.TFAE [ ∀ (c : C) (d : D), IsIso (adj.unit.app ((ihom d).obj (R.obj c))) , ∀ (c : C) (d : D), IsIso ((pre (adj.unit.app d)).app (R.obj c)) , ∀ (d d' : D), IsIso (L.map ((adj.unit.app d) ▷ d')) , ∀ (d d' : D), IsIso (L.map ((adj.unit.app d) ⊗ (adj.unit.app d')))]

Assume that we have a diagram of categories
```
C₁ ⥤ D₁
‖     ‖
v     v
C₂ ⥤ D₂
‖     ‖
v     v
C₃ ⥤ D₃
```
with functors `F₁₂ : C₁ ⥤ C₂`, `F₂₃ : C₂ ⥤ C₃` and `F₁₃ : C₁ ⥤ C₃` on the first
column that are related by a natural transformation `α : F₁₃ ⟶ F₁₂ ⋙ F₂₃`
and similarly `β : G₁₂ ⋙ G₂₃ ⟶ G₁₃` on the second column. Assume that we have
natural transformations
`e₁₂ : F₁₂ ⋙ L₂ ⟶ L₁ ⋙ G₁₂` (top square), `e₂₃ : F₂₃ ⋙ L₃ ⟶ L₂ ⋙ G₂₃` (bottom square),
and `e₁₃ : F₁₃ ⋙ L₃ ⟶ L₁ ⋙ G₁₃` (outer square), where the horizontal functors
are denoted `L₁`, `L₂` and `L₃`. Assume that `e₁₃` is determined by the other
natural transformations `α`, `e₂₃`, `e₁₂` and `β`. Then, if all these categories
are equipped with a shift by an additive monoid `A`, and all these functors commute with
these shifts, then the natural transformation `e₁₃` of the outer square commutes with the
shift if all `α`, `e₂₃`, `e₁₂` and `β` do.

When `f : X ⟶ Y⟦m⟧`, `m + n = mn`, `n + a = a'` and `ha'' : m + a' = a''`, this lemma
relates the two morphisms `F.shiftMap f a' a'' ha''` and `(F.shift a).map (f⟦n⟧')`. Indeed,
via canonical isomorphisms, they both identity to morphisms
`(F.shift a').obj X ⟶ (F.shift a'').obj Y`.

`(F.shift a).obj X ⟶ (F.shift a').obj Y`.

`U`, that `P` is a sheaf for each sieve in `B`, and that it is separated for any pullback of any
sieve in `B`.

* `P` is a sheaf for `R`
* `P` is a sheaf for the pullback of `S` along any arrow in `R`
* `P` is separated for the pullback of `R` along any arrow in `S`.

views.nl_informal: Check that if `P ∈ Ps`, then `P` is indeed a sheaf for the finest topology on `Ps`.

views.nl_informal: Check that if each `P ∈ Ps` is a sheaf for `J`, then `J` is a subtopology of `finestTopology Ps`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Sheaf.le_finestTopology (Ps : Set (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v)) (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (hJ : ∀ P ∈ Ps, Presieve.IsSheaf J P) : J ≤ finestTopology Ps

views.nl_informal: `yoneda.obj X` is a sheaf for the canonical topology.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Sheaf.isSheaf_yoneda_obj (X : C) : Presieve.IsSheaf (canonicalTopology C) (yoneda.obj X)

views.nl_informal: A representable functor is a sheaf for the canonical topology.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Sheaf.isSheaf_of_isRepresentable (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v) [P.IsRepresentable] : Presieve.IsSheaf (canonicalTopology C) P

views.nl_informal: If every functor `yoneda.obj X` is a `J`-sheaf, then `J` is subcanonical.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Subcanonical.of_isSheaf_yoneda_obj (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (h : ∀ X, Presieve.IsSheaf J (yoneda.obj X)) : Subcanonical J

views.nl_informal: If `J` is subcanonical, then any representable is a `J`-sheaf.

views.nl_informal: Any sieve is smaller than its closure.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.le_close {X : C} (S : Sieve X) : S ≤ J₁.close S

views.nl_informal: If `S` is `J₁`-closed, then `S` covers exactly the arrows it contains.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.covers_iff_mem_of_isClosed {X : C} {S : Sieve X} (h : J₁.IsClosed S) {Y : C} (f : Y ⟶ X) : J₁.Covers S f ↔ S f

views.nl_informal: Being `J`-closed is stable under pullback.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.isClosed_pullback {X Y : C} (f : Y ⟶ X) (S : Sieve X) : J₁.IsClosed S → J₁.IsClosed (S.pullback f)

views.nl_informal:
The closure of a sieve `S` is the largest closed sieve which contains `S` (justifying the name
"closure").
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.le_close_of_isClosed {X : C} {S T : Sieve X} (h : S ≤ T) (hT : J₁.IsClosed T) : J₁.close S ≤ T

views.nl_informal: The closure of a sieve is closed.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.close_isClosed {X : C} (S : Sieve X) : J₁.IsClosed (J₁.close S)

views.nl_informal: The sieve `S` is closed iff its closure is equal to itself.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.isClosed_iff_close_eq_self {X : C} (S : Sieve X) : J₁.IsClosed S ↔ J₁.close S = S

views.nl_informal: Closing under `J` is stable under pullback.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.pullback_close {X Y : C} (f : Y ⟶ X) (S : Sieve X) : J₁.close (S.pullback f) = (J₁.close S).pullback f

views.nl_informal:
The sieve `S` is in the topology iff its closure is the maximal sieve. This shows that the closure
operator determines the topology.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.close_eq_top_iff_mem {X : C} (S : Sieve X) : J₁.close S = ⊤ ↔ S ∈ J₁ X

views.nl_informal:
The presheaf of `J`-closed sieves is a `J`-sheaf.
The proof of this is adapted from [MM92], Chapter III, Section 7, Lemma 1.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.classifier_isSheaf : Presieve.IsSheaf J₁ (Functor.closedSieves J₁)

views.nl_informal:
If presheaf of `J₁`-closed sieves is a `J₂`-sheaf then `J₁ ≤ J₂`. Note the converse is true by
`classifier_isSheaf` and `isSheaf_of_le`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.le_topology_of_closedSieves_isSheaf {J₁ J₂ : GrothendieckTopology C} (h : Presieve.IsSheaf J₁ (Functor.closedSieves J₂)) : J₁ ≤ J₂

views.nl_informal: If being a sheaf for `J₁` is equivalent to being a sheaf for `J₂`, then `J₁ = J₂`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.topology_eq_iff_same_sheaves {J₁ J₂ : GrothendieckTopology C} : J₁ = J₂ ↔ ∀ P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type max v u, Presieve.IsSheaf J₁ P ↔ Presieve.IsSheaf J₂ P

views.nl_informal: The topology given by the closure operator `J.close` on a Grothendieck topology is the same as `J`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.topologyOfClosureOperator_self : (topologyOfClosureOperator J₁.closureOperator fun _ _ => J₁.pullback_close) = J₁

views.nl_informal: `P⁺` is always separated.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Plus.sep {X : C} (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D) (S : J.Cover X) (x y : ToType ((J.plusObj P).obj (op X))) (h : ∀ I : S.Arrow, (J.plusObj P).map I.f.op x = (J.plusObj P).map I.f.op y) : x = y

views.nl_informal: If `P` is separated, then `P⁺` is a sheaf.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Plus.isSheaf_of_sep (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D) (hsep : ∀ (X : C) (S : J.Cover X) (x y : ToType (P.obj (op X))), (∀ I : S.Arrow, P.map I.f.op x = P.map I.f.op y) → x = y) : Presheaf.IsSheaf J (J.plusObj P)

views.nl_informal: `P⁺⁺` is always a sheaf.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Plus.isSheaf_plus_plus (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D) : Presheaf.IsSheaf J (J.plusObj (J.plusObj P))

views.nl_informal:
If the constant sheaf functor is fully faithful, then a sheaf is constant if and only if the
counit of the constant sheaf adjunction applied to it is an isomorphism.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Sheaf.isConstant_iff_isIso_counit_app [(constantSheaf J D).Faithful] [(constantSheaf J D).Full] (F : Sheaf J D) {T : C} (hT : IsTerminal T) : IsConstant J F ↔ (IsIso <| (constantSheafAdj J D hT).counit.app F)

views.nl_informal:
The property of a sheaf of being constant is invariant under equivalence of sheaf
categories.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Sheaf.isConstant_iff_of_equivalence (F : Sheaf K D) : ((sheafEquiv G J K D).inverse.obj F).IsConstant J ↔ IsConstant K F

views.nl_informal: The counit of `constantSheafAdj` factors through the isomorphism `constantCommuteCompose`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.constantSheafAdj_counit_w {T : C} (hT : IsTerminal T) : ((constantCommuteCompose J U).hom.app (F.val.obj ⟨T⟩)) ≫ ((constantSheafAdj J B hT).counit.app ((sheafCompose J U).obj F)) = ((sheafCompose J U).map ((constantSheafAdj J D hT).counit.app F))

views.nl_informal: The composition of two cocontinuous functors is cocontinuous.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.isCocontinuous_comp [G.IsCocontinuous J K] [G'.IsCocontinuous K L] : (G ⋙ G').IsCocontinuous J L

views.nl_informal:
If `G` is cocontinuous, then `G.op.ran` pushes sheaves to sheaves.

This is SGA 4 III 2.2.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.ran_isSheaf_of_isCocontinuous (ℱ : Sheaf J A) : Presheaf.IsSheaf K (G.op.ran.obj ℱ.val)

views.nl_informal: The identity functor on a site is cover-preserving.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.idCoverPreserving : CoverPreserving J J (𝟭 _)

views.nl_informal: The composition of two cover-preserving functors is cover-preserving.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.CoverPreserving.comp {F} (hF : CoverPreserving J K F) {G} (hG : CoverPreserving K L G) : CoverPreserving J L (F ⋙ G)

views.nl_informal: `CompatiblePreserving` functors indeed preserve compatible families.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presieve.FamilyOfElements.Compatible.functorPushforward : (x.functorPushforward G).Compatible

views.nl_informal: If `F` is cover-preserving and compatible-preserving, then `F` is a continuous functor.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Functor.isContinuous_of_coverPreserving (hF₁ : CompatiblePreserving.{w} K F) (hF₂ : CoverPreserving J K F) : Functor.IsContinuous.{w} F J K

views.nl_informal:
An alternative characterization of the Grothendieck topology associated to a coverage `K`:
it is the infimum of all Grothendieck topologies whose associated coverage contains `K`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Coverage.toGrothendieck_eq_sInf (K : Coverage C) : toGrothendieck _ K = sInf {J | K ≤ ofGrothendieck _ J }

views.nl_informal:
Any sieve that contains a covering presieve for a coverage is a covering sieve for the associated
Grothendieck topology.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Coverage.mem_toGrothendieck_sieves_of_superset (K : Coverage C) {X : C} {S : Sieve X} {R : Presieve X} (h : R ≤ S) (hR : R ∈ K.covering X) : S ∈ (K.toGrothendieck C) X

views.nl_informal:
The main theorem of this file: Given a coverage `K` on `C`,
a `Type*`-valued presheaf on `C` is a sheaf for `K` if and only if it is a sheaf for
the associated Grothendieck topology.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presieve.isSheaf_coverage (K : Coverage C) (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type*) : Presieve.IsSheaf (toGrothendieck _ K) P ↔ (∀ {X : C} (R : Presieve X), R ∈ K X → Presieve.IsSheafFor P R)

views.nl_informal:
A presheaf is a sheaf for the Grothendieck topology generated by a union of coverages iff it is a
sheaf for the Grothendieck topology generated by each coverage separately.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presieve.isSheaf_sup (K L : Coverage C) (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type*) : (Presieve.IsSheaf ((K ⊔ L).toGrothendieck C)) P ↔ (Presieve.IsSheaf (K.toGrothendieck C)) P ∧ (Presieve.IsSheaf (L.toGrothendieck C)) P

views.nl_informal:
The family of elements given by `x : FirstObj P S` is compatible iff `firstMap` and `secondMap`
map it to the same point.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Equalizer.Sieve.compatible_iff (x : FirstObj P S.arrows) : ((firstObjEqFamily P S.arrows).hom x).Compatible ↔ firstMap P S x = secondMap P S x

views.nl_informal: `P` is a sheaf for `S`, iff the fork given by `w` is an equalizer.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Equalizer.Sieve.equalizer_sheaf_condition : Presieve.IsSheafFor P (S : Presieve X) ↔ Nonempty (IsLimit (Fork.ofι _ (w P S)))

views.nl_informal:
The family of elements given by `x : FirstObj P S` is compatible iff `firstMap` and `secondMap`
map it to the same point.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Equalizer.Presieve.compatible_iff (x : FirstObj P R) : ((firstObjEqFamily P R).hom x).Compatible ↔ firstMap P R x = secondMap P R x

views.nl_informal: `P` is a sheaf for `R`, iff the fork given by `w` is an equalizer.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Equalizer.Presieve.sheaf_condition : R.IsSheafFor P ↔ Nonempty (IsLimit (Fork.ofι _ (w P R)))

views.nl_informal:
The family of elements given by `x : FirstObj P S` is compatible iff `firstMap` and `secondMap`
map it to the same point.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Equalizer.Presieve.Arrows.compatible_iff (x : FirstObj P X) : (Arrows.Compatible P π ((Types.productIso _).hom x)) ↔ firstMap P X π x = secondMap P X π x

views.nl_informal: `P` is a sheaf for `Presieve.ofArrows X π`, iff the fork given by `w` is an equalizer.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Equalizer.Presieve.Arrows.sheaf_condition : (Presieve.ofArrows X π).IsSheafFor P ↔ Nonempty (IsLimit (Fork.ofι (forkMap P X π) (w P X π)))

views.nl_informal: Transport `HasSheafify` along an equivalence of sites.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Equivalence.hasSheafify : HasSheafify J A

views.nl_informal:
An extensionality lemma in terms of the coercion to a pi-type.
We prove this explicitly rather than deriving it so that it is in terms of the coercion rather than
the projection `.sieves`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.ext {J₁ J₂ : GrothendieckTopology C} (h : (J₁ : ∀ X : C, Set (Sieve X)) = J₂) : J₁ = J₂

views.nl_informal: Also known as the maximality axiom.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.top_mem (X : C) : ⊤ ∈ J X

views.nl_informal: Also known as the stability axiom.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.pullback_stable (f : Y ⟶ X) (hS : S ∈ J X) : S.pullback f ∈ J Y

views.nl_informal:
If `S` is a subset of `R`, and `S` is covering, then `R` is covering as well.

See also discussion after [MM92] Chapter III, Section 2, Definition 1.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.superset_covering (Hss : S ≤ R) (sjx : S ∈ J X) : R ∈ J X

views.nl_informal:
The intersection of two covering sieves is covering.

See also [MM92] Chapter III, Section 2, Definition 1 (iv).
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.intersection_covering (rj : R ∈ J X) (sj : S ∈ J X) : R ⊓ S ∈ J X

views.nl_informal: The maximality axiom in 'arrow' form: Any arrow `f` in `S` is covered by `S`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.arrow_max (f : Y ⟶ X) (S : Sieve X) (hf : S f) : J.Covers S f

views.nl_informal: The stability axiom in 'arrow' form: If `S` covers `f` then `S` covers `g ≫ f` for any `g`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.arrow_stable (f : Y ⟶ X) (S : Sieve X) (h : J.Covers S f) {Z : C} (g : Z ⟶ Y) : J.Covers S (g ≫ f)

views.nl_informal:
The transitivity axiom in 'arrow' form: If `S` covers `f` and every arrow in `S` is covered by
`R`, then `R` covers `f`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.arrow_trans (f : Y ⟶ X) (S R : Sieve X) (h : J.Covers S f) : (∀ {Z : C} (g : Z ⟶ X), S g → J.Covers R g) → J.Covers R f

views.nl_informal: The restriction of a compatible family is compatible.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presieve.FamilyOfElements.Compatible.restrict {R₁ R₂ : Presieve X} (h : R₁ ≤ R₂) {x : FamilyOfElements P R₂} : x.Compatible → (x.restrict h).Compatible

views.nl_informal: The extension of a compatible family to the generated sieve is compatible.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presieve.FamilyOfElements.Compatible.sieveExtend {x : FamilyOfElements P R} (hx : x.Compatible) : x.sieveExtend.Compatible

views.nl_informal: The extension of a family agrees with the original family.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presieve.extend_agrees {x : FamilyOfElements P R} (t : x.Compatible) {f : Y ⟶ X} (hf : R f) : x.sieveExtend f (le_generate R Y hf) = x f hf

views.nl_informal: The restriction of an extension is the original.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presieve.restrict_extend {x : FamilyOfElements P R} (t : x.Compatible) : x.sieveExtend.restrict (le_generate R) = x

views.nl_informal:
Given a family of elements `x` for the sieve `S` generated by a presieve `R`, if `x` is restricted
to `R` and then extended back up to `S`, the resulting extension equals `x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presieve.extend_restrict {x : FamilyOfElements P (generate R).arrows} (t : x.Compatible) : (x.restrict (le_generate R)).sieveExtend = x

views.nl_informal:
Two compatible families on the sieve generated by a presieve `R` are equal if and only if they are
equal when restricted to `R`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presieve.restrict_inj {x₁ x₂ : FamilyOfElements P (generate R).arrows} (t₁ : x₁.Compatible) (t₂ : x₂.Compatible) : x₁.restrict (le_generate R) = x₂.restrict (le_generate R) → x₁ = x₂

views.nl_informal:
The yoneda version of the sheaf condition is equivalent to the sheaf condition.

C2.1.4 of [Elephant].
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presieve.isSheafFor_iff_yonedaSheafCondition {P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v₁} : IsSheafFor P (S : Presieve X) ↔ YonedaSheafCondition P S

views.nl_informal:
Show that the extension of `f : S.functor ⟶ P` to all of `yoneda.obj X` is in fact an extension, ie
that the triangle below commutes, provided `P` is a sheaf for `S`

      f
   S  →  P
   ↓  ↗
   yX
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presieve.IsSheafFor.functorInclusion_comp_extend {P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v₁} (h : IsSheafFor P S.arrows) (f : S.functor ⟶ P) : S.functorInclusion ≫ h.extend f = f

views.nl_informal: The extension of `f` to `yoneda.obj X` is unique.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presieve.IsSheafFor.unique_extend {P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v₁} (h : IsSheafFor P S.arrows) {f : S.functor ⟶ P} (t : yoneda.obj X ⟶ P) (ht : S.functorInclusion ≫ t = f) : t = h.extend f

views.nl_informal:
If `P` is a sheaf for the sieve `S` on `X`, then if two natural transformations from `yoneda.obj X`
to `P` agree when restricted to the subfunctor given by `S`, they are equal.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presieve.IsSheafFor.hom_ext {P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v₁} (h : IsSheafFor P (S : Presieve X)) (t₁ t₂ : yoneda.obj X ⟶ P) (ht : S.functorInclusion ≫ t₁ = S.functorInclusion ≫ t₂) : t₁ = t₂

views.nl_informal: `P` is a sheaf for `R` iff it is separated for `R` and there exists an amalgamation.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presieve.isSeparatedFor_and_exists_isAmalgamation_iff_isSheafFor : (IsSeparatedFor P R ∧ ∀ x : FamilyOfElements P R, x.Compatible → ∃ t, x.IsAmalgamation t) ↔ IsSheafFor P R

views.nl_informal: If `P` is separated for `R` and every family has an amalgamation, then `P` is a sheaf for `R`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presieve.IsSeparatedFor.isSheafFor (t : IsSeparatedFor P R) : (∀ x : FamilyOfElements P R, x.Compatible → ∃ t, x.IsAmalgamation t) → IsSheafFor P R

views.nl_informal: If `P` is a sheaf for `R`, it is separated for `R`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presieve.IsSheafFor.isSeparatedFor : IsSheafFor P R → IsSeparatedFor P R

views.nl_informal:
Every presheaf is a sheaf for the family {𝟙 X}.

[Elephant] C2.1.5(i)
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presieve.isSheafFor_singleton_iso (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w) : IsSheafFor P (Presieve.singleton (𝟙 X))

views.nl_informal:
Every presheaf is a sheaf for the maximal sieve.

[Elephant] C2.1.5(ii)
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presieve.isSheafFor_top_sieve (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w) : IsSheafFor P ((⊤ : Sieve X) : Presieve X)

views.nl_informal:
If `P₁ : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w` and `P₂  : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w` are two naturally equivalent
presheaves, and `P₁` is a sheaf for a presieve `R`, then `P₂` is also a sheaf for `R`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presieve.isSheafFor_of_nat_equiv {P₁ : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w} {P₂ : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w'} (e : ∀ ⦃X : C⦄, P₁.obj (op X) ≃ P₂.obj (op X)) (he : ∀ ⦃X Y : C⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y) (x : P₁.obj (op Y)), e (P₁.map f.op x) = P₂.map f.op (e x)) {X : C} {R : Presieve X} (hP₁ : IsSheafFor P₁ R) : IsSheafFor P₂ R

views.nl_informal:
If `P` is a sheaf for `S`, and it is iso to `P'`, then `P'` is a sheaf for `S`. This shows that
"being a sheaf for a presieve" is a mathematical or hygienic property.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presieve.isSheafFor_iso {P' : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w} (i : P ≅ P') (hP : IsSheafFor P R) : IsSheafFor P' R

views.nl_informal:
If a presieve `R` on `X` has a subsieve `S` such that:

* `P` is a sheaf for `S`.
* For every `f` in `R`, `P` is separated for the pullback of `S` along `f`,

then `P` is a sheaf for `R`.

This is closely related to [Elephant] C2.1.6(i).
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presieve.isSheafFor_subsieve_aux (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w) {S : Sieve X} {R : Presieve X} (h : (S : Presieve X) ≤ R) (hS : IsSheafFor P (S : Presieve X)) (trans : ∀ ⦃Y⦄ ⦃f : Y ⟶ X⦄, R f → IsSeparatedFor P (S.pullback f : Presieve Y)) : IsSheafFor P R

views.nl_informal:
If `P` is a sheaf for every pullback of the sieve `S`, then `P` is a sheaf for any presieve which
contains `S`.
This is closely related to [Elephant] C2.1.6.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presieve.isSheafFor_subsieve (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w) {S : Sieve X} {R : Presieve X} (h : (S : Presieve X) ≤ R) (trans : ∀ ⦃Y⦄ (f : Y ⟶ X), IsSheafFor P (S.pullback f : Presieve Y)) : IsSheafFor P R

views.nl_informal:
If `E` is a cone which is a limit on the level of presheaves,
then the limit presheaf is again a sheaf.

This is used to show that the forgetful functor from sheaves to presheaves creates limits.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Sheaf.isSheaf_of_isLimit (F : K ⥤ Sheaf J D) (E : Cone (F ⋙ sheafToPresheaf J D)) (hE : IsLimit E) : Presheaf.IsSheaf J E.pt

views.nl_informal:
A morphism of sheaves of types is locally bijective iff it is an isomorphism.
(This is generalized below as `isLocallyBijective_iff_isIso`.)
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Sheaf.isLocallyBijective_iff_isIso' : IsLocallyInjective f ∧ IsLocallySurjective f ↔ IsIso f
theorem CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.plusMap_toPlus : J.plusMap (J.toPlus P) = J.toPlus (J.plusObj P)

views.nl_informal:
If `F` is a presheaf which satisfies the sheaf condition with respect to the empty presieve on the
initial object, then `F` preserves terminal objects.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presieve.preservesTerminal_of_isSheaf_for_empty (hI : IsInitial I) : PreservesLimit (Functor.empty.{0} Cᵒᵖ) F

views.nl_informal: If `F` preserves a particular product, then it `IsSheafFor` the corresponding presieve of arrows.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presieve.isSheafFor_of_preservesProduct [PreservesLimit (Discrete.functor (fun x ↦ op (X x))) F] : (ofArrows X c.inj).IsSheafFor F

views.nl_informal:
The two parallel maps in the equalizer diagram for the sheaf condition corresponding to the
inclusion maps in a disjoint coproduct are equal.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presieve.firstMap_eq_secondMap : Equalizer.Presieve.Arrows.firstMap F X c.inj = Equalizer.Presieve.Arrows.secondMap F X c.inj

views.nl_informal:
If `F` is a presheaf which `IsSheafFor` a presieve of arrows and the empty presieve, then it
preserves the product corresponding to the presieve of arrows.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presieve.preservesProduct_of_isSheafFor (hF' : (ofArrows X c.inj).IsSheafFor F) : PreservesLimit (Discrete.functor (fun x ↦ op (X x))) F

views.nl_informal: The trivial pretopology induces the trivial grothendieck topology.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Pretopology.toGrothendieck_bot : toGrothendieck C ⊥ = ⊥

views.nl_informal:
Given sieve `S` and presheaf `P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A`, their natural associated cone is a limit cone
iff `Hom (E, P -)` is a sheaf of types for the sieve `S` and all `E : A`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presheaf.isLimit_iff_isSheafFor : Nonempty (IsLimit (P.mapCone S.arrows.cocone.op)) ↔ ∀ E : Aᵒᵖ, IsSheafFor (P ⋙ coyoneda.obj E) S.arrows

views.nl_informal:
Given sieve `S` and presheaf `P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A`, their natural associated cone admits at most one
morphism from every cone in the same category (i.e. over the same diagram),
iff `Hom (E, P -)`is separated for the sieve `S` and all `E : A`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presheaf.subsingleton_iff_isSeparatedFor : (∀ c, Subsingleton (c ⟶ P.mapCone S.arrows.cocone.op)) ↔ ∀ E : Aᵒᵖ, IsSeparatedFor (P ⋙ coyoneda.obj E) S.arrows

views.nl_informal:
A presheaf `P` is a sheaf for the Grothendieck topology `J` iff for every covering sieve
`S` of `J`, the natural cone associated to `P` and `S` is a limit cone.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isLimit : IsSheaf J P ↔ ∀ ⦃X : C⦄ (S : Sieve X), S ∈ J X → Nonempty (IsLimit (P.mapCone S.arrows.cocone.op))

views.nl_informal:
A presheaf `P` is separated for the Grothendieck topology `J` iff for every covering sieve
`S` of `J`, the natural cone associated to `P` and `S` admits at most one morphism from every
cone in the same category.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presheaf.isSeparated_iff_subsingleton : (∀ E : A, Presieve.IsSeparated J (P ⋙ coyoneda.obj (op E))) ↔ ∀ ⦃X : C⦄ (S : Sieve X), S ∈ J X → ∀ c, Subsingleton (c ⟶ P.mapCone S.arrows.cocone.op)

views.nl_informal:
Given presieve `R` and presheaf `P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A`, the natural cone associated to `P` and
the sieve `Sieve.generate R` generated by `R` is a limit cone iff `Hom (E, P -)` is a
sheaf of types for the presieve `R` and all `E : A`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presheaf.isLimit_iff_isSheafFor_presieve : Nonempty (IsLimit (P.mapCone (generate R).arrows.cocone.op)) ↔ ∀ E : Aᵒᵖ, IsSheafFor (P ⋙ coyoneda.obj E) R

views.nl_informal:
A presheaf `P` is a sheaf for the Grothendieck topology generated by a pretopology `K`
iff for every covering presieve `R` of `K`, the natural cone associated to `P` and
`Sieve.generate R` is a limit cone.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isLimit_pretopology [HasPullbacks C] (K : Pretopology C) : IsSheaf (K.toGrothendieck C) P ↔ ∀ ⦃X : C⦄ (R : Presieve X), R ∈ K X → Nonempty (IsLimit (P.mapCone (generate R).arrows.cocone.op))

views.nl_informal:
This is stated as a lemma to prevent class search from forming a loop since a sheaf morphism is
monic if and only if it is monic as a presheaf morphism (under suitable assumption).
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Sheaf.Hom.mono_of_presheaf_mono {F G : Sheaf J A} (f : F ⟶ G) [h : Mono f.1] : Mono f

views.nl_informal: The equalizer definition of a sheaf given by `isSheaf'` is equivalent to `isSheaf`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf' : IsSheaf J P' ↔ IsSheaf' J P'

views.nl_informal:
For a concrete category `(A, s)` where the forgetful functor `s : A ⥤ Type v` preserves limits and
reflects isomorphisms, and `A` has limits, an `A`-valued presheaf `P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A` is a sheaf iff its
underlying `Type`-valued presheaf `P ⋙ s : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type` is a sheaf.

Note this lemma applies for "algebraic" categories, eg groups, abelian groups and rings, but not
for the category of topological spaces, topological rings, etc since reflecting isomorphisms doesn't
hold.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_forget (s : A' ⥤ Type max v₁ u₁) [HasLimits A'] [PreservesLimits s] [s.ReflectsIsomorphisms] : IsSheaf J P' ↔ IsSheaf J (P' ⋙ s)

views.nl_informal:
Equational lemma for the presheaf structure on `presheafHom`.
It is advisable to use this lemma rather than `dsimp [presheafHom]` which may result
in the need to prove equalities of objects in an `Over` category.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.presheafHom_map_app {X Y Z : C} (f : Z ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ X) (h : Z ⟶ X) (w : f ≫ g = h) (α : (presheafHom F G).obj (op X)) : ((presheafHom F G).map g.op α).app (op (Over.mk f)) = α.app (op (Over.mk h))

views.nl_informal: The property of being a sheaf is preserved by isomorphism.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presieve.isSheaf_iso {P' : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w} (i : P ≅ P') (h : IsSheaf J P) : IsSheaf J P'

views.nl_informal:
For a topology generated by a basis, it suffices to check the sheaf condition on the basis
presieves only.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presieve.isSheaf_pretopology [HasPullbacks C] (K : Pretopology C) : IsSheaf (K.toGrothendieck C) P ↔ ∀ {X : C} (R : Presieve X), R ∈ K X → IsSheafFor P R

views.nl_informal: Any presheaf is a sheaf for the bottom (trivial) grothendieck topology.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presieve.isSheaf_bot : IsSheaf (⊥ : GrothendieckTopology C) P

views.nl_informal:
The base of a sieve `S` is a colimit of `S` iff all Yoneda-presheaves satisfy
the sheaf condition for `S`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Sieve.forallYonedaIsSheaf_iff_colimit (S : Sieve X) : (∀ W : C, Presieve.IsSheafFor (yoneda.obj W) (S : Presieve X)) ↔ Nonempty (IsColimit S.arrows.cocone)

views.nl_informal: If the identity arrow is in a sieve, the sieve is maximal.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Sieve.id_mem_iff_eq_top : S (𝟙 X) ↔ S = ⊤

views.nl_informal: If an arrow set contains a split epi, it generates the maximal sieve.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Sieve.generate_of_contains_isSplitEpi {R : Presieve X} (f : Y ⟶ X) [IsSplitEpi f] (hf : R f) : generate R = ⊤

views.nl_informal:
The pretopology associated to a space is the largest pretopology that
generates the Grothendieck topology associated to the space.
views.lean_signature: theorem Opens.pretopology_ofGrothendieck : Pretopology.ofGrothendieck _ (Opens.grothendieckTopology T) = Opens.pretopology T

views.nl_informal: The pretopology associated to a space induces the Grothendieck topology associated to the space.
views.lean_signature: theorem Opens.pretopology_toGrothendieck : Pretopology.toGrothendieck _ (Opens.pretopology T) = Opens.grothendieckTopology T

views.nl_informal:
Two morphisms of sheaves of types `P ⟶ Q` coincide if the precompositions with morphisms
`yoneda.obj X ⟶ P` agree.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.hom_ext_yoneda {P Q : Sheaf J (Type v)} {f g : P ⟶ Q} (h : ∀ (X : C) (p : J.yoneda.obj X ⟶ P), p ≫ f = p ≫ g) : f = g

views.nl_informal:
Two morphisms of sheaves of types `P ⟶ Q` coincide if the precompositions
with morphisms `yoneda.obj X ⟶ P` agree.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.hom_ext_yonedaULift {P Q : Sheaf J (Type (max v v'))} {f g : P ⟶ Q} (h : ∀ (X : C) (p : J.yonedaULift.obj X ⟶ P), p ≫ f = p ≫ g) : f = g

views.nl_informal: The sheaf condition for `yoneda'`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presieve.isSheaf_yoneda' {α : Type u} : Presieve.IsSheaf typesGrothendieckTopology (yoneda.obj α)

views.nl_informal: The sheaf condition for `yoneda'`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presheaf.isSheaf_yoneda' {α : Type u} : Presheaf.IsSheaf typesGrothendieckTopology (yoneda.obj α)

views.nl_informal: Every Yoneda-presheaf is a sheaf for the coherent topology.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.coherentTopology.isSheaf_yoneda_obj (W : C) : Presieve.IsSheaf (coherentTopology C) (yoneda.obj W)

views.nl_informal:
For a precoherent category, any sieve that contains an `EffectiveEpiFamily` is a sieve of the
coherent topology.
Note: This is one direction of `mem_sieves_iff_hasEffectiveEpiFamily`, but is needed for the proof.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.coherentTopology.mem_sieves_of_hasEffectiveEpiFamily (S : Sieve X) : (∃ (α : Type) (_ : Finite α) (Y : α → C) (π : (a : α) → (Y a ⟶ X)), EffectiveEpiFamily Y π ∧ (∀ a : α, (S.arrows) (π a)) ) → (S ∈ (coherentTopology C) X)

views.nl_informal:
Effective epi families in a precoherent category are transitive, in the sense that an
`EffectiveEpiFamily` and an `EffectiveEpiFamily` over each member, the composition is an
`EffectiveEpiFamily`.
Note: The finiteness condition is an artifact of the proof and is probably unnecessary.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.EffectiveEpiFamily.transitive_of_finite {α : Type} [Finite α] {Y : α → C} (π : (a : α) → (Y a ⟶ X)) (h : EffectiveEpiFamily Y π) {β : α → Type} [∀ (a : α), Finite (β a)] {Y_n : (a : α) → β a → C} (π_n : (a : α) → (b : β a) → (Y_n a b ⟶ Y a)) (H : ∀ a, EffectiveEpiFamily (Y_n a) (π_n a)) : EffectiveEpiFamily (fun (c : Σ a, β a) => Y_n c.fst c.snd) (fun c => π_n c.fst c.snd ≫ π c.fst)

views.nl_informal:
A sieve belongs to the coherent topology if and only if it contains a finite
`EffectiveEpiFamily`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.coherentTopology.mem_sieves_iff_hasEffectiveEpiFamily (S : Sieve X) : (S ∈ (coherentTopology C) X) ↔ (∃ (α : Type) (_ : Finite α) (Y : α → C) (π : (a : α) → (Y a ⟶ X)), EffectiveEpiFamily Y π ∧ (∀ a : α, (S.arrows) (π a)) )

views.nl_informal: The union of the extensive and regular coverages generates the coherent topology on `C`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.extensive_regular_generate_coherent [Preregular C] [FinitaryPreExtensive C] : ((extensiveCoverage C) ⊔ (regularCoverage C)).toGrothendieck = (coherentTopology C)

views.nl_informal: `Precoherent` is preserved by equivalence of categories.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Equivalence.precoherent (e : C ≌ D) : Precoherent D

views.nl_informal: The coherent sheaf condition can be checked after precomposing with the equivalence.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Equivalence.precoherent_isSheaf_iff (e : C ≌ D) (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A) : haveI

views.nl_informal:

views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Equivalence.precoherent_isSheaf_iff_of_essentiallySmall [EssentiallySmall C] (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A) : IsSheaf (coherentTopology C) F ↔ IsSheaf (coherentTopology (SmallModel C)) ((equivSmallModel C).inverse.op ⋙ F)

views.nl_informal: `Preregular` is preserved by equivalence of categories.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Equivalence.preregular (e : C ≌ D) : Preregular D

views.nl_informal: The regular sheaf condition can be checked after precomposing with the equivalence.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Equivalence.preregular_isSheaf_iff (e : C ≌ D) (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A) : haveI

views.nl_informal:
The regular sheaf condition on an essentially small site can be checked after precomposing with
the equivalence with a small category.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Equivalence.preregular_isSheaf_iff_of_essentiallySmall [EssentiallySmall C] (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A) : IsSheaf (regularTopology C) F ↔ IsSheaf (regularTopology (SmallModel C)) ((equivSmallModel C).inverse.op ⋙ F)

views.nl_informal:
A finite product preserving presheaf is a sheaf for the extensive topology on a category which is
`FinitaryPreExtensive`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.isSheafFor_extensive_of_preservesFiniteProducts {X : C} (S : Presieve X) [S.Extensive] (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w) [PreservesFiniteProducts F] : S.IsSheafFor F

views.nl_informal: Every Yoneda-presheaf is a sheaf for the extensive topology.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.extensiveTopology.isSheaf_yoneda_obj (W : C) : Presieve.IsSheaf (extensiveTopology C) (yoneda.obj W)

views.nl_informal:
A presheaf of sets on a category which is `FinitaryExtensive` is a sheaf iff it preserves finite
products.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presieve.isSheaf_iff_preservesFiniteProducts (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w) : Presieve.IsSheaf (extensiveTopology C) F ↔ PreservesFiniteProducts F

views.nl_informal: A presheaf on a category which is `FinitaryExtensive` is a sheaf iff it preserves finite products.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_preservesFiniteProducts (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D) : IsSheaf (extensiveTopology C) F ↔ PreservesFiniteProducts F

views.nl_informal: The equalizer condition is preserved by natural isomorphism.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.regularTopology.equalizerCondition_of_natIso {P P' : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D} (i : P ≅ P') (hP : EqualizerCondition P) : EqualizerCondition P'

views.nl_informal: Precomposing with a pullback-preserving functor preserves the equalizer condition.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.regularTopology.equalizerCondition_precomp_of_preservesPullback (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D) (F : E ⥤ C) [∀ {X B} (π : X ⟶ B) [EffectiveEpi π], PreservesLimit (cospan π π) F] [F.PreservesEffectiveEpis] (hP : EqualizerCondition P) : EqualizerCondition (F.op ⋙ P)

views.nl_informal: An alternative phrasing of the explicit equalizer condition, using more categorical language.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.regularTopology.equalizerCondition_iff_isIso_lift (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type*) : EqualizerCondition P ↔ ∀ (X B : C) (π : X ⟶ B) [EffectiveEpi π] [HasPullback π π], IsIso (equalizer.lift (P.map π.op) (equalizerCondition_w' P π))

views.nl_informal: `P` satisfies the equalizer condition iff its precomposition by an equivalence does.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.regularTopology.equalizerCondition_iff_of_equivalence (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D) (e : C ≌ E) : EqualizerCondition P ↔ EqualizerCondition (e.op.inverse ⋙ P)

views.nl_informal: Every presheaf is a sheaf for the regular topology if every object of `C` is projective.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.regularTopology.isSheaf_of_projective (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D) [Preregular C] [∀ (X : C), Projective X] : Presheaf.IsSheaf (regularTopology C) F

views.nl_informal: Every Yoneda-presheaf is a sheaf for the regular topology.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.regularTopology.isSheaf_yoneda_obj [Preregular C] (W : C) : Presieve.IsSheaf (regularTopology C) (yoneda.obj W)

views.nl_informal:
For a preregular category, any sieve that contains an `EffectiveEpi` is a covering sieve of the
regular topology.
Note: This is one direction of `mem_sieves_iff_hasEffectiveEpi`, but is needed for the proof.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.regularTopology.mem_sieves_of_hasEffectiveEpi (S : Sieve X) : (∃ (Y : C) (π : Y ⟶ X), EffectiveEpi π ∧ S.arrows π) → (S ∈ (regularTopology C) X)

views.nl_informal: A sieve is a cover for the regular topology if and only if it contains an `EffectiveEpi`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.regularTopology.mem_sieves_iff_hasEffectiveEpi (S : Sieve X) : (S ∈ (regularTopology C) X) ↔ ∃ (Y : C) (π : Y ⟶ X), EffectiveEpi π ∧ (S.arrows π)

views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Functor.IsCoverDense.sheafHom_eq (α : ℱ ⟶ ℱ'.val) : sheafHom (whiskerLeft G.op α) = α

views.nl_informal:

views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Functor.whiskerLeft_obj_map_bijective_of_isCoverDense (G : C ⥤ D) [G.IsCoverDense K] [G.IsLocallyFull K] {A : Type*} [Category A] (P Q : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ A) (hQ : Presheaf.IsSheaf K Q) : Function.Bijective (((whiskeringLeft Cᵒᵖ Dᵒᵖ A).obj G.op).map : (P ⟶ Q) → _)

views.nl_informal:

then the class of morphism that have the left lifting property with respect to
the maps that have the right lifting property with respect to `I` are

views.nl_informal:
If `I : MorphismProperty C` permits the small object argument,

the maps that have the right lifting property with respect to `I` are
exactly the retracts of transfinite compositions
of pushouts of coproducts of morphisms in `C`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.llp_rlp_of_hasSmallObjectArgument : I.rlp.llp = (transfiniteCompositions.{w} (coproducts.{w} I).pushouts).retracts

views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.SmallObject.llp_rlp_of_isCardinalForSmallObjectArgument' : I.rlp.llp = (transfiniteCompositionsOfShape (coproducts.{w} I).pushouts κ.ord.toType).retracts

If `κ` is a suitable cardinal for the small object argument for `I : MorphismProperty C`,

views.nl_informal:
Given `sq' : SqStruct c p f g j`, this is the commutative square
```
               sq'.f'
F.obj j --------------------> X
   |                          |
   |                          |p
   v                      g   v
F.obj (succ j) ---> c.pt ---> Y
```

(Using the lifting property for this square is the key ingredient
in the proof that the left lifting property with respect to `p`
is stable under transfinite composition.)
views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.transfiniteComposition.SqStruct.sq [SuccOrder J] : CommSq sq'.f' (F.map (homOfLE (Order.le_succ j))) p (c.ι.app _ ≫ g)

Two morphisms into a subobject are equal exactly if
the morphisms into the ambient object are equal

views.nl_informal:
To show that two subobjects are equal, it suffices to exhibit an isomorphism commuting with

views.nl_informal:
To show that two subobjects are equal, it suffices to exhibit an isomorphism commuting with

views.nl_informal:
To show that two subobjects are equal, it suffices to exhibit an isomorphism commuting with

views.lean_signature: theorem CategoryTheory.Subobject.mk_eq_of_comm {B A : C} {X : Subobject B} (f : A ⟶ B) [Mono f] (i : A ≅ (X : C)) (w : i.hom ≫ X.arrow = f) : mk f = X

views.nl_informal:
To show that two subobjects are equal, it suffices to exhibit an isomorphism commuting with

views.nl_informal:
The **Combinatorial Nullstellensatz**.

If `f` vanishes at every point `x : σ → R` such that `x s ∈ S s` for all `s`,
then it can be written as a linear combination
`f = linearCombination (MvPolynomial σ R) (fun i ↦ (∏ r ∈ S i, (X i - C r))) h`,
for some `h : σ →₀ MvPolynomial σ R` such that
`((∏ r ∈ S s, (X i - C r)) * h i).totalDegree ≤ f.totalDegree` for all `s`.

[Alon_1999], theorem 1.
views.lean_signature: theorem MvPolynomial.combinatorial_nullstellensatz_exists_linearCombination [IsDomain R] (S : σ → Finset R) (Sne : ∀ i, (S i).Nonempty) (f : MvPolynomial σ R) (Heval : ∀ (x : σ → R), (∀ i, x i ∈ S i) → eval x f = 0) : ∃ (h : σ →₀ MvPolynomial σ R), (∀ i, ((∏ s ∈ S i, (X i - C s)) * h i).totalDegree ≤ f.totalDegree) ∧ f = linearCombination (MvPolynomial σ R) (fun i ↦ ∏ r ∈ S i, (X i - C r)) h

views.nl_informal:
The **Combinatorial Nullstellensatz**.

Given a multi-index `t : σ →₀ ℕ` such that `t s < (S s).card` for all `s`,
`f.totalDegree = t.degree` and `f.coeff t ≠ 0`,
there exists a point `x : σ → R` such that `x s ∈ S s` for all `s` and `f.eval s ≠ 0`.

[Alon_1999], theorem 2
views.lean_signature: theorem MvPolynomial.combinatorial_nullstellensatz_exists_eval_nonzero [IsDomain R] (f : MvPolynomial σ R) (t : σ →₀ ℕ) (ht : f.coeff t ≠ 0) (ht' : f.totalDegree = t.degree) (S : σ → Finset R) (htS : ∀ i, t i < #(S i)) : ∃ s : σ → R, (∀ i, s i ∈ S i) ∧ eval s f ≠ 0

views.nl_informal:
For any natural `n`, the Schnirelmann density multiplied by `n` is bounded by `|A ∩ {1, ..., n}|`.
Note this property fails for the natural density.
views.lean_signature: theorem schnirelmannDensity_mul_le_card_filter {n : ℕ} : schnirelmannDensity A * n ≤ #{a ∈ Ioc 0 n | a ∈ A}

views.nl_informal:
To show the Schnirelmann density is upper bounded by `x`, it suffices to show
`|A ∩ {1, ..., n}| / n ≤ x`, for any chosen positive value of `n`.

We provide `n` explicitly here to make this lemma more easily usable in `apply` or `refine`.
This lemma is analogous to `ciInf_le_of_le`.
views.lean_signature: theorem schnirelmannDensity_le_of_le {x : ℝ} (n : ℕ) (hn : n ≠ 0) (hx : #{a ∈ Ioc 0 n | a ∈ A} / n ≤ x) : schnirelmannDensity A ≤ x

views.nl_informal: If `k` is omitted from the set, its Schnirelmann density is upper bounded by `1 - k⁻¹`.
views.lean_signature: theorem schnirelmannDensity_le_of_not_mem {k : ℕ} (hk : k ∉ A) : schnirelmannDensity A ≤ 1 - (k⁻¹ : ℝ)

views.nl_informal: The Schnirelmann density of a set not containing `1` is `0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem schnirelmannDensity_eq_zero_of_one_not_mem (h : 1 ∉ A) : schnirelmannDensity A = 0

views.nl_informal: The Schnirelmann density is increasing with the set.
views.lean_signature: theorem schnirelmannDensity_le_of_subset {B : Set ℕ} [DecidablePred (· ∈ B)] (h : A ⊆ B) : schnirelmannDensity A ≤ schnirelmannDensity B

views.nl_informal: The Schnirelmann density of `A` is `1` if and only if `A` contains all the positive naturals.
views.lean_signature: theorem schnirelmannDensity_eq_one_iff : schnirelmannDensity A = 1 ↔ {0}ᶜ ⊆ A

views.nl_informal: The Schnirelmann density of `A` containing `0` is `1` if and only if `A` is the naturals.
views.lean_signature: theorem schnirelmannDensity_eq_one_iff_of_zero_mem (hA : 0 ∈ A) : schnirelmannDensity A = 1 ↔ A = Set.univ

views.nl_informal: The Schnirelmann density is unaffected by adding `0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem schnirelmannDensity_insert_zero [DecidablePred (· ∈ insert 0 A)] : schnirelmannDensity (insert 0 A) = schnirelmannDensity A

views.nl_informal: The Schnirelmann density is unaffected by removing `0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem schnirelmannDensity_diff_singleton_zero [DecidablePred (· ∈ A \ {0})] : schnirelmannDensity (A \ {0}) = schnirelmannDensity A

views.nl_informal:
If the Schnirelmann density is `0`, there is a positive natural for which
`|A ∩ {1, ..., n}| / n < ε`, for any positive `ε`.
Note this cannot be improved to `∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop`, as can be seen by `A = {1}ᶜ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem exists_of_schnirelmannDensity_eq_zero {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (hA : schnirelmannDensity A = 0) : ∃ n, 0 < n ∧ #{a ∈ Ioc 0 n | a ∈ A} / n < ε

views.nl_informal: The Schnirelmann density of any finset is `0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem schnirelmannDensity_finset (A : Finset ℕ) : schnirelmannDensity A = 0

views.nl_informal: The Schnirelmann density of any finite set is `0`.

views.nl_informal:
The Schnirelmann density of the set of naturals which are `1 mod m` is `m⁻¹`, for any `m ≠ 1`.

sum is divisible by `n`.

whose sum is zero.

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:

If `A` has small tripling, say with constant `K`, then `A` has small alternating powers, in the
sense that `|A^±1 * ... * A^±1|` is at most `|A|` times a constant exponential in the number of
terms in the product.

When `A` is symmetric (`A⁻¹ = A`), the base of the exponential can be lowered from `K ^ 3` to `K`,
where `K` is the tripling constant. See `Finset.small_pow_of_small_tripling`.

views.nl_informal:
If `A` is symmetric (`A⁻¹ = A`) and has small tripling, then `A` has small powers,
in the sense that `|A ^ m|` is at most `|A|` times a constant exponential in `m`.

which encompasses non-symmetric sets.

views.nl_informal:
If `A` has doubling strictly less than `3 / 2`, then there exists a subgroup `H` of the
normaliser of `A` of size strictly less than `3 / 2 * #A` such that `A` is a subset of a coset of
`H` (in fact a subset of `a • H` for every `a ∈ A`).

Note that this is sharp: `A = {0, 1}` in `ℤ` has doubling `3 / 2` and can't be covered by a subgroup
of size at most `2`.

This is Theorem 2.2.1 in [tointon2020].

views.nl_informal:
This is the version of **Hall's Marriage Theorem** in terms of indexed
families of finite sets `t : ι → Finset α`.  It states that there is a
set of distinct representatives if and only if every union of `k` of the
sets has at least `k` elements.

Recall that `s.biUnion t` is the union of all the sets `t i` for `i ∈ s`.

This theorem is bootstrapped from `Finset.all_card_le_biUnion_card_iff_exists_injective'`,
which has the additional constraint that `ι` is a `Fintype`.

views.nl_informal:
This is a version of **Hall's Marriage Theorem** in terms of a relation
between types `α` and `β` such that `α` is finite and the image of
each `x : α` is finite (it suffices for `β` to be finite; see
`Fintype.all_card_le_filter_rel_iff_exists_injective`).  There is
a transversal of the relation (an injective function `α → β` whose graph is
a subrelation of the relation) iff every subset of
`k` terms of `α` is related to at least `k` terms of `β`.

Note: if `[Fintype β]`, then there exist instances for `[∀ (a : α), Fintype (Rel.image r {a})]`.

views.nl_informal:

of the relation) iff every subset of `k` terms of `α` is related to at least `k` terms of `β`.

This is important for iterating Kruskal-Katona: the shadow of an initial segment is also an

Applying the compression makes the set smaller in colex. This is intuitive since a portion of

difference.

If we're compressed by all useful compressions, then we're an initial segment. This is the other
key Kruskal-Katona part.

Applying a compression strictly decreases the measure. This helps show that "compress until we
can't any more" is a terminating process.

views.nl_informal:
The main Kruskal-Katona helper: use induction with our measure to keep compressing until
we can't any more, which gives a set family which is fully compressed and has the nice properties we
want.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.UV.kruskal_katona_helper {r : ℕ} (𝒜 : Finset (Finset (Fin n))) (h : (𝒜 : Set (Finset (Fin n))).Sized r) : ∃ ℬ : Finset (Finset (Fin n)), #(∂ ℬ) ≤ #(∂ 𝒜) ∧ #𝒜 = #ℬ ∧ (ℬ : Set (Finset (Fin n))).Sized r ∧ ∀ U V, UsefulCompression U V → IsCompressed U V ℬ

views.nl_informal:
The **Kruskal-Katona theorem**.

Given a set family `𝒜` consisting of `r`-sets, and `𝒞` an initial segment of the colex order of the
same size, the shadow of `𝒞` is smaller than the shadow of `𝒜`. In particular, this gives that the
minimum shadow size is achieved by initial segments of colex.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.kruskal_katona (h𝒜r : (𝒜 : Set (Finset (Fin n))).Sized r) (h𝒞𝒜 : #𝒞 ≤ #𝒜) (h𝒞 : IsInitSeg 𝒞 r) : #(∂ 𝒞) ≤ #(∂ 𝒜)

views.nl_informal:
An iterated form of the Kruskal-Katona theorem. In particular, the minimum possible iterated
shadow size is attained by initial segments.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.iterated_kk (h₁ : (𝒜 : Set (Finset (Fin n))).Sized r) (h₂ : #𝒞 ≤ #𝒜) (h₃ : IsInitSeg 𝒞 r) : #(∂^[k] 𝒞) ≤ #(∂^[k] 𝒜)

views.nl_informal:
The **Lovasz formulation of the Kruskal-Katona theorem**.

If `|𝒜| ≥ k choose r`, (and everything in `𝒜` has size `r`) then the initial segment we compare to
is just all the subsets of `{0, ..., k - 1}` of size `r`. The `i`-th iterated shadow of this is all
the subsets of `{0, ..., k - 1}` of size `r - i`, so the `i`-th iterated shadow of `𝒜` has at least
`k.choose (r - i)` elements.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.kruskal_katona_lovasz_form (hir : i ≤ r) (hrk : r ≤ k) (hkn : k ≤ n) (h₁ : (𝒜 : Set (Finset (Fin n))).Sized r) (h₂ : k.choose r ≤ #𝒜) : k.choose (r - i) ≤ #(∂^[i] 𝒜)

views.nl_informal:
The **Erdős–Ko–Rado theorem**.

The maximum size of an intersecting family in `α` where all sets have size `r` is bounded by
`(card α - 1).choose (r - 1)`. This bound is sharp.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.erdos_ko_rado {𝒜 : Finset (Finset (Fin n))} {r : ℕ} (h𝒜 : (𝒜 : Set (Finset (Fin n))).Intersecting) (h₂ : (𝒜 : Set (Finset (Fin n))).Sized r) (h₃ : r ≤ n / 2) : #𝒜 ≤ (n - 1).choose (r - 1)

views.nl_informal:
The downward **local LYM inequality**, with cancelled denominators. `𝒜` takes up less of `α^(r)`
(the finsets of card `r`) than `∂𝒜` takes up of `α^(r - 1)`.

views.nl_informal:
The downward **local LYM inequality**. `𝒜` takes up less of `α^(r)` (the finsets of card `r`)
than `∂𝒜` takes up of `α^(r - 1)`.

views.nl_informal:
The **Lubell-Yamamoto-Meshalkin inequality**, also known as the **LYM inequality**.

If `𝒜` is an antichain, then the sum of the proportion of elements it takes from each layer is less
than `1`.

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:
Induction principle for finset families. To prove a statement for every finset family,
it suffices to prove it for
* the empty finset family.
* the finset family which only contains the empty finset.
* `ℬ ∪ {s ∪ {a} | s ∈ 𝒞}` assuming the property for `ℬ` and `𝒞`, where `a` is an element of the
  ground type and `𝒜` and `ℬ` are families of finsets not containing `a`.
  Note that instead of giving `ℬ` and `𝒞`, the `subfamily` case gives you
  `𝒜 = ℬ ∪ {s ∪ {a} | s ∈ 𝒞}`, so that `ℬ = 𝒜.nonMemberSubfamily` and `𝒞 = 𝒜.memberSubfamily`.

This is a way of formalising induction on `n` where `𝒜` is a finset family on `n` elements.

See also `Finset.family_induction_on.`

views.nl_informal:
Induction principle for finset families. To prove a statement for every finset family,
it suffices to prove it for
* the empty finset family.
* the finset family which only contains the empty finset.
* `{s ∪ {a} | s ∈ 𝒜}` assuming the property for `𝒜` a family of finsets not containing `a`.
* `ℬ ∪ 𝒞` assuming the property for `ℬ` and `𝒞`, where `a` is an element of the ground type and
  `ℬ`is a family of finsets not containing `a` and `𝒞` a family of finsets containing `a`.
  Note that instead of giving `ℬ` and `𝒞`, the `subfamily` case gives you `𝒜 = ℬ ∪ 𝒞`, so that
  `ℬ = {s ∈ 𝒜 | a ∉ s}` and `𝒞 = {s ∈ 𝒜 | a ∈ s}`.

This is a way of formalising induction on `n` where `𝒜` is a finset family on `n` elements.

See also `Finset.memberFamily_induction_on.`

views.nl_informal:
UV-compression reduces the size of the shadow of `𝒜` if, for all `x ∈ u` there is `y ∈ v` such
that `𝒜` is `(u.erase x, v.erase y)`-compressed. This is the key fact about compression for
Kruskal-Katona.
views.lean_signature: theorem UV.shadow_compression_subset_compression_shadow (u v : Finset α) (huv : ∀ x ∈ u, ∃ y ∈ v, IsCompressed (u.erase x) (v.erase y) 𝒜) : ∂ (𝓒 u v 𝒜) ⊆ 𝓒 u v (∂ 𝒜)

views.nl_informal:
UV-compression reduces the size of the shadow of `𝒜` if, for all `x ∈ u` there is `y ∈ v`
such that `𝒜` is `(u.erase x, v.erase y)`-compressed. This is the key UV-compression fact needed for
Kruskal-Katona.
views.lean_signature: theorem UV.card_shadow_compression_le (u v : Finset α) (huv : ∀ x ∈ u, ∃ y ∈ v, IsCompressed (u.erase x) (v.erase y) 𝒜) : #(∂ (𝓒 u v 𝒜)) ≤ #(∂ 𝒜)

views.nl_informal: A minimally connected graph is a tree.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.isTree_of_minimal_connected (h : Minimal Connected G) : IsTree G

views.nl_informal: Every connected graph has a spanning tree.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.Connected.exists_isTree_le [Finite V] (h : G.Connected) : ∃ T ≤ G, IsTree T

views.nl_informal: Every connected graph on `n` vertices has at least `n-1` edges.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.Connected.card_vert_le_card_edgeSet_add_one (h : G.Connected) : Nat.card V ≤ Nat.card G.edgeSet + 1

views.nl_informal: The adjacency matrix of `G` is an adjacency matrix.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.isAdjMatrix_adjMatrix [Zero α] [One α] : (G.adjMatrix α).IsAdjMatrix

views.nl_informal: The graph induced by the adjacency matrix of `G` is `G` itself.

views.nl_informal:
If `A` is qualified as an adjacency matrix,
