views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.IsAdjMatrix.adjMatrix_toGraph_eq [DecidableEq α] : h.toGraph.adjMatrix α = A

views.nl_informal:
Two vertices are adjacent iff there is an edge between them. The
condition `v ≠ w` ensures they are different endpoints of the edge,
which is necessary since when `v = w` the existential
`∃ (e ∈ G.edgeSet), v ∈ e ∧ w ∈ e` is satisfied by every edge
incident to `v`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.adj_iff_exists_edge {v w : V} : G.Adj v w ↔ v ≠ w ∧ ∃ e ∈ G.edgeSet, v ∈ e ∧ w ∈ e

views.nl_informal: If `G.IsBipartiteWith s t` and `v ∈ s`, then if `v` is adjacent to `w` in `G` then `w ∈ t`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.IsBipartiteWith.mem_of_mem_adj (h : G.IsBipartiteWith s t) (hv : v ∈ s) (hadj : G.Adj v w) : w ∈ t

views.nl_informal:
If `G.IsBipartiteWith s t` and `v ∈ s`, then the neighbor set of `v` is the set of vertices in
`t` adjacent to `v` in `G`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.isBipartiteWith_neighborSet (h : G.IsBipartiteWith s t) (hv : v ∈ s) : G.neighborSet v = { w ∈ t | G.Adj v w }

views.nl_informal: If `G.IsBipartiteWith s t` and `v ∈ s`, then the neighbor set of `v` is a subset of `t`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.isBipartiteWith_neighborSet_subset (h : G.IsBipartiteWith s t) (hv : v ∈ s) : G.neighborSet v ⊆ t

views.nl_informal: If `G.IsBipartiteWith s t` and `v ∈ s`, then the neighbor set of `v` is disjoint to `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.isBipartiteWith_neighborSet_disjoint (h : G.IsBipartiteWith s t) (hv : v ∈ s) : Disjoint (G.neighborSet v) s

views.nl_informal: If `G.IsBipartiteWith s t` and `w ∈ t`, then if `v` is adjacent to `w` in `G` then `v ∈ s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.IsBipartiteWith.mem_of_mem_adj' (h : G.IsBipartiteWith s t) (hw : w ∈ t) (hadj : G.Adj v w) : v ∈ s

views.nl_informal:
If `G.IsBipartiteWith s t` and `w ∈ t`, then the neighbor set of `w` is the set of vertices in
`s` adjacent to `w` in `G`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.isBipartiteWith_neighborSet' (h : G.IsBipartiteWith s t) (hw : w ∈ t) : G.neighborSet w = { v ∈ s | G.Adj v w }

views.nl_informal: If `G.IsBipartiteWith s t` and `w ∈ t`, then the neighbor set of `w` is a subset of `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.isBipartiteWith_neighborSet_subset' (h : G.IsBipartiteWith s t) (hw : w ∈ t) : G.neighborSet w ⊆ s

views.nl_informal: If `G.IsBipartiteWith s t`, then the support of `G` is a subset of `s ∪ t`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.isBipartiteWith_support_subset (h : G.IsBipartiteWith s t) : G.support ⊆ s ∪ t

views.nl_informal: If `G.IsBipartiteWith s t` and `w ∈ t`, then the neighbor set of `w` is disjoint to `t`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.isBipartiteWith_neighborSet_disjoint' (h : G.IsBipartiteWith s t) (hw : w ∈ t) : Disjoint (G.neighborSet w) t

views.nl_informal:
If `G.IsBipartiteWith s t` and `v ∈ s`, then the neighbor finset of `v` is the set of vertices
in `s` adjacent to `v` in `G`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.isBipartiteWith_neighborFinset (h : G.IsBipartiteWith s t) (hv : v ∈ s) : G.neighborFinset v = { w ∈ t | G.Adj v w }

views.nl_informal:
If `G.IsBipartiteWith s t` and `v ∈ s`, then the neighbor finset of `v` is the set of vertices
"above" `v` according to the adjacency relation of `G`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.isBipartiteWith_bipartiteAbove (h : G.IsBipartiteWith s t) (hv : v ∈ s) : G.neighborFinset v = bipartiteAbove G.Adj t v

views.nl_informal: If `G.IsBipartiteWith s t` and `v ∈ s`, then the neighbor finset of `v` is a subset of `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.isBipartiteWith_neighborFinset_subset (h : G.IsBipartiteWith s t) (hv : v ∈ s) : G.neighborFinset v ⊆ t

views.nl_informal: If `G.IsBipartiteWith s t` and `v ∈ s`, then the neighbor finset of `v` is disjoint to `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.isBipartiteWith_neighborFinset_disjoint (h : G.IsBipartiteWith s t) (hv : v ∈ s) : Disjoint (G.neighborFinset v) s

views.nl_informal:
If `G.IsBipartiteWith s t` and `v ∈ s`, then the degree of `v` in `G` is at most the size of
`t`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.isBipartiteWith_degree_le (h : G.IsBipartiteWith s t) (hv : v ∈ s) : G.degree v ≤ #t

views.nl_informal:
If `G.IsBipartiteWith s t` and `w ∈ t`, then the neighbor finset of `w` is the set of vertices
in `s` adjacent to `w` in `G`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.isBipartiteWith_neighborFinset' (h : G.IsBipartiteWith s t) (hw : w ∈ t) : G.neighborFinset w = { v ∈ s | G.Adj v w }

views.nl_informal:
If `G.IsBipartiteWith s t` and `w ∈ t`, then the neighbor finset of `w` is the set of vertices
"below" `w` according to the adjacency relation of `G`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.isBipartiteWith_bipartiteBelow (h : G.IsBipartiteWith s t) (hw : w ∈ t) : G.neighborFinset w = bipartiteBelow G.Adj s w

views.nl_informal: If `G.IsBipartiteWith s t` and `w ∈ t`, then the neighbor finset of `w` is a subset of `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.isBipartiteWith_neighborFinset_subset' (h : G.IsBipartiteWith s t) (hw : w ∈ t) : G.neighborFinset w ⊆ s

views.nl_informal: If `G.IsBipartiteWith s t` and `w ∈ t`, then the neighbor finset of `w` is disjoint to `t`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.isBipartiteWith_neighborFinset_disjoint' (h : G.IsBipartiteWith s t) (hw : w ∈ t) : Disjoint (G.neighborFinset w) t

views.nl_informal:
If `G.IsBipartiteWith s t` and `w ∈ t`, then the degree of `w` in `G` is at most the size of
`s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.isBipartiteWith_degree_le' (h : G.IsBipartiteWith s t) (hw : w ∈ t) : G.degree w ≤ #s

views.nl_informal:
If `G.IsBipartiteWith s t`, then the sum of the degrees of vertices in `s` is equal to the sum
of the degrees of vertices in `t`.

See `Finset.sum_card_bipartiteAbove_eq_sum_card_bipartiteBelow`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.isBipartiteWith_sum_degrees_eq (h : G.IsBipartiteWith s t) : ∑ v ∈ s, G.degree v = ∑ w ∈ t, G.degree w

views.nl_informal:
The degree-sum formula for bipartite graphs, summing over the "left" part.

See `SimpleGraph.sum_degrees_eq_twice_card_edges` for the general version, and
`SimpleGraph.isBipartiteWith_sum_degrees_eq_card_edges'` for the version from the "right".
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.isBipartiteWith_sum_degrees_eq_card_edges (h : G.IsBipartiteWith s t) : ∑ v ∈ s, G.degree v = #G.edgeFinset

views.nl_informal:
The degree-sum formula for bipartite graphs, summing over the "right" part.

See `SimpleGraph.sum_degrees_eq_twice_card_edges` for the general version, and
`SimpleGraph.isBipartiteWith_sum_degrees_eq_card_edges` for the version from the "left".
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.isBipartiteWith_sum_degrees_eq_card_edges' (h : G.IsBipartiteWith s t) : ∑ v ∈ t, G.degree v = #G.edgeFinset

views.nl_informal: A clique is a set of vertices whose induced graph is complete.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.isClique_iff_induce_eq : G.IsClique s ↔ G.induce s = ⊤

views.nl_informal:
If a set of vertices `A` is a clique in subgraph of `G` induced by a superset of `A`,
its embedding is a clique in `G`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.IsClique.of_induce {S : Subgraph G} {F : Set α} {A : Set F} (c : (S.induce F).coe.IsClique A) : G.IsClique (Subtype.val '' A)

views.nl_informal:
If a set of vertices `A` is an `n`-clique in subgraph of `G` induced by a superset of `A`,
its embedding is an `n`-clique in `G`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.IsNClique.of_induce {S : Subgraph G} {F : Set α} {s : Finset { x // x ∈ F }} {n : ℕ} (cc : (S.induce F).coe.IsNClique n s) : G.IsNClique n (Finset.map ⟨Subtype.val, Subtype.val_injective⟩ s)

views.nl_informal: If a graph is cliquefree, any graph that embeds into it is also cliquefree.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.CliqueFree.comap {H : SimpleGraph β} (f : H ↪g G) : G.CliqueFree n → H.CliqueFree n

views.nl_informal: A complete `r`-partite graph has no `n`-cliques for `r < n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.cliqueFree_completeMultipartiteGraph {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (V : ι → Type*) (hc : card ι < n) : (completeMultipartiteGraph V).CliqueFree n

views.nl_informal: Clique-freeness is preserved by `replaceVertex`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.CliqueFree.replaceVertex [DecidableEq α] (h : G.CliqueFree n) (s t : α) : (G.replaceVertex s t).CliqueFree n

views.nl_informal: Adding an edge increases the clique number by at most one.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.CliqueFree.sup_edge (h : G.CliqueFree n) (v w : α) : (G ⊔ edge v w).CliqueFree (n + 1)

views.nl_informal: A maximal clique in a graph `G` is a clique that cannot be extended by adding more vertices.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.isMaximalClique_iff {s : Set α} : Maximal G.IsClique s ↔ G.IsClique s ∧ ∀ t : Set α, G.IsClique t → s ⊆ t → t ⊆ s

views.nl_informal: An independent set is a clique in the complement graph and vice versa.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.isClique_compl : Gᶜ.IsClique s ↔ G.IsIndepSet s

views.nl_informal: An independent set in the complement graph is a clique and vice versa.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.isIndepSet_compl : Gᶜ.IsIndepSet s ↔ G.IsClique s

views.nl_informal: If `s` is an independent set, its complement meets every edge of `G`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.IsIndepSet.nonempty_mem_compl_mem_edge [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {s : Finset α} (indA : G.IsIndepSet s) {e} (he : e ∈ G.edgeSet) : { b ∈ sᶜ | b ∈ e }.Nonempty

views.nl_informal: The neighbors of a vertex `v` form an independent set in a triangle free graph `G`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.isIndepSet_neighborSet_of_triangleFree (h : G.CliqueFree 3) (v : α) : G.IsIndepSet (G.neighborSet v)

views.nl_informal:
The embedding of an independent set of an induced subgraph of the subgraph `G` is an independent
set in `G` and vice versa.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.isIndepSet_induce {F : Set α} {s : Set F} : ((⊤ : Subgraph G).induce F).coe.IsIndepSet s ↔ G.IsIndepSet (Subtype.val '' s)

views.nl_informal: An `n`-independent set is an `n`-clique in the complement graph and vice versa.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.isNClique_compl : Gᶜ.IsNClique n s ↔ G.IsNIndepSet n s

views.nl_informal: An `n`-independent set in the complement graph is an `n`-clique and vice versa.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.isNIndepSet_compl : Gᶜ.IsNIndepSet n s ↔ G.IsNClique n s

views.nl_informal:
The embedding of an `n`-independent set of an induced subgraph of the subgraph `G` is an
`n`-independent set in `G` and vice versa.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.isNIndepSet_induce {F : Set α} {s : Finset { x // x ∈ F }} {n : ℕ} : ((⊤ : Subgraph G).induce F).coe.IsNIndepSet n ↑s ↔ G.IsNIndepSet n (Finset.map ⟨Subtype.val, Subtype.val_injective⟩ s)

views.nl_informal: An graph is `n`-independent set free iff its complement is `n`-clique free.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.cliqueFree_compl : Gᶜ.CliqueFree n ↔ G.IndepSetFree n

views.nl_informal: An graph's complement is `n`-independent set free iff it is `n`-clique free.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.indepSetFree_compl : Gᶜ.IndepSetFree n ↔ G.CliqueFree n

views.nl_informal: An independent set in a graph `G` that cannot be extended by adding more vertices.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.isMaximalIndepSet_iff {s : Set α} : Maximal G.IsIndepSet s ↔ G.IsIndepSet s ∧ ∀ t : Set α, G.IsIndepSet t → s ⊆ t → t ⊆ s

views.nl_informal: A simple graph contains itself.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.IsContained.refl (G : SimpleGraph V) : G ⊑ G

views.nl_informal: A simple graph contains its subgraphs.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.IsContained.of_le (h : G₁ ≤ G₂) : G₁ ⊑ G₂

views.nl_informal: If `A` contains `B` and `B` contains `C`, then `A` contains `C`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.IsContained.trans : A ⊑ B → B ⊑ C → A ⊑ C

views.nl_informal: If `B` contains `C` and `A` contains `B`, then `A` contains `C`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.IsContained.trans' : B ⊑ C → A ⊑ B → A ⊑ C

views.nl_informal:
If `A ≃g H` and `B ≃g G` then `A` is contained in `B` if and only if `H` is contained
in `G`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.isContained_congr (e₁ : A ≃g H) (e₂ : B ≃g G) : A ⊑ B ↔ H ⊑ G

views.nl_informal: A simple graph having no vertices is contained in any simple graph.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.IsContained.of_isEmpty [IsEmpty α] : A ⊑ B

views.nl_informal: `⊥` is contained in any simple graph having sufficiently many vertices.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.bot_isContained_iff_card_le [Fintype α] [Fintype β] : (⊥ : SimpleGraph α) ⊑ B ↔ Fintype.card α ≤ Fintype.card β

views.nl_informal: A simple graph `G` contains all `Subgraph G` coercions.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.Subgraph.coe_isContained (G' : G.Subgraph) : G'.coe ⊑ G

views.nl_informal: `B` contains `A` if and only if `B` has a subgraph `B'` and `B'` is isomorphic to `A`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.isContained_iff_exists_iso_subgraph : A ⊑ B ↔ ∃ B' : B.Subgraph, Nonempty (A ≃g B'.coe)

views.nl_informal: If `A ≃g H` and `B ≃g G` then `B` is `A`-free if and only if `G` is `H`-free.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.free_congr (e₁ : A ≃g H) (e₂ : B ≃g G) : A.Free B ↔ H.Free G

views.nl_informal: If `G` is isomorphic to `H`, then `G` is inducingly contained in `H`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.Iso.isIndContained (e : G ≃g H) : G ⊴ H

views.nl_informal: If `G` is isomorphic to `H`, then `H` is inducingly contained in `G`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.Iso.isIndContained' (e : G ≃g H) : H ⊴ G

views.nl_informal: There's at least as many labelled copies of `H` in `G` than unlabelled ones.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.copyCount_le_labelledCopyCount [Fintype W] : G.copyCount H ≤ G.labelledCopyCount H

views.nl_informal: Removing an edge from `G` for each subgraph isomorphic to `H` results in a subgraph of `G`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.killCopies_le_left : G.killCopies H ≤ G

views.nl_informal:
`G.killCopies H` has no effect on `G` if and only if `G` already contained no copies of `H`. See
`Free.killCopies_eq_left` for the reverse implication with no assumption on `H`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.killCopies_eq_left (hH : H ≠ ⊥) : G.killCopies H = G ↔ H.Free G

views.nl_informal:
Removing an edge from `G` for each subgraph isomorphic to `H` results in a graph that doesn't
contain `H`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.free_killCopies (hH : H ≠ ⊥) : H.Free (G.killCopies H)

views.nl_informal:
Removing an edge from `H` for each subgraph isomorphic to `G` means that the number of edges
we've removed is at most the number of copies of `G` in `H`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.le_card_edgeFinset_killCopies [Fintype V] : #G.edgeFinset - G.copyCount H ≤ #(G.killCopies H).edgeFinset

views.nl_informal:
Removing an edge from `H` for each subgraph isomorphic to `G` means that the number of edges
we've removed is at most the number of copies of `G` in `H`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.le_card_edgeFinset_killCopies_add_copyCount [Fintype V] : #G.edgeFinset ≤ #(G.killCopies H).edgeFinset + G.copyCount H

views.nl_informal:
The degree-sum formula.  This is also known as the handshaking lemma, which might
more specifically refer to `SimpleGraph.even_card_odd_degree_vertices`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.sum_degrees_eq_twice_card_edges : ∑ v, G.degree v = 2 * #G.edgeFinset

views.nl_informal:
The degree-sum formula only counting over the vertices that form edges.

See `SimpleGraph.sum_degrees_eq_twice_card_edges` for the general version.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.sum_degrees_support_eq_twice_card_edges : ∑ v ∈ G.support, G.degree v = 2 * #G.edgeFinset

views.nl_informal: The handshaking lemma.  See also `SimpleGraph.sum_degrees_eq_twice_card_edges`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.even_card_odd_degree_vertices [Fintype V] [DecidableRel G.Adj] : Even #{v | Odd (G.degree v)}

views.nl_informal:
If `s₂ ⊆ s₁`, `t₂ ⊆ t₁` and they take up all but a `δ`-proportion, then the difference in edge
densities is at most `2 * δ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Rel.abs_edgeDensity_sub_edgeDensity_le_two_mul (hs : s₂ ⊆ s₁) (ht : t₂ ⊆ t₁) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ) (hscard : (1 - δ) * #s₁ ≤ #s₂) (htcard : (1 - δ) * #t₁ ≤ #t₂) : |(edgeDensity r s₂ t₂ : 𝕜) - edgeDensity r s₁ t₁| ≤ 2 * δ

views.nl_informal:
In a finite graph with nontrivial vertex set, the graph is connected
if and only if the extended diameter is not `⊤`.
See `connected_of_ediam_ne_top` for one of the implications without
the finiteness assumptions
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.connected_iff_ediam_ne_top [Nonempty α] [Finite α] : G.Connected ↔ G.ediam ≠ ⊤

views.nl_informal:
A finite and nontrivial graph is connected if and only if its diameter is not zero.
See also `connected_iff_ediam_ne_top` for the extended diameter version.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.connected_iff_diam_ne_zero [Finite α] [Nontrivial α] : G.Connected ↔ G.diam ≠ 0

views.nl_informal: The complete graph on `n` vertices has `n.choose 2` edges.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.card_edgeFinset_top_eq_card_choose_two [DecidableEq V] : #(⊤ : SimpleGraph V).edgeFinset = (Fintype.card V).choose 2

views.nl_informal: Any graph on `n` vertices has at most `n.choose 2` edges.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.card_edgeFinset_le_card_choose_two : #G.edgeFinset ≤ (Fintype.card V).choose 2

views.nl_informal: If `G ≤ H` then `G.degree v ≤ H.degree v` for any vertex `v`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.degree_le_of_le {H : SimpleGraph V} [Fintype (H.neighborSet v)] (hle : G ≤ H) : G.degree v ≤ H.degree v

views.nl_informal:
There exists a vertex of minimal degree. Note the assumption of being nonempty is necessary, as
the lemma implies there exists a vertex.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.exists_minimal_degree_vertex [DecidableRel G.Adj] [Nonempty V] : ∃ v, G.minDegree = G.degree v

views.nl_informal: The minimum degree in the graph is at most the degree of any particular vertex.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.minDegree_le_degree [DecidableRel G.Adj] (v : V) : G.minDegree ≤ G.degree v

views.nl_informal:
In a nonempty graph, if `k` is at most the degree of every vertex, it is at most the minimum
degree. Note the assumption that the graph is nonempty is necessary as long as `G.minDegree` is
defined to be a natural.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.le_minDegree_of_forall_le_degree [DecidableRel G.Adj] [Nonempty V] (k : ℕ) (h : ∀ v, k ≤ G.degree v) : k ≤ G.minDegree

views.nl_informal: If there are no vertices then the `minDegree` is zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.minDegree_of_isEmpty [DecidableRel G.Adj] [IsEmpty V] : G.minDegree = 0

views.nl_informal: If `G` is a subgraph of `H` then `G.minDegree ≤ H.minDegree`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.minDegree_le_minDegree {H : SimpleGraph V} [DecidableRel G.Adj] [DecidableRel H.Adj] (hle : G ≤ H) : G.minDegree ≤ H.minDegree

views.nl_informal:
There exists a vertex of maximal degree. Note the assumption of being nonempty is necessary, as
the lemma implies there exists a vertex.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.exists_maximal_degree_vertex [DecidableRel G.Adj] [Nonempty V] : ∃ v, G.maxDegree = G.degree v

views.nl_informal: The maximum degree in the graph is at least the degree of any particular vertex.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.degree_le_maxDegree [DecidableRel G.Adj] (v : V) : G.degree v ≤ G.maxDegree

views.nl_informal:
In a graph, if `k` is at least the degree of every vertex, then it is at least the maximum
degree.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.maxDegree_le_of_forall_degree_le [DecidableRel G.Adj] (k : ℕ) (h : ∀ v, G.degree v ≤ k) : G.maxDegree ≤ k

views.nl_informal:
The maximum degree of a nonempty graph is less than the number of vertices. Note that the assumption
that `V` is nonempty is necessary, as otherwise this would assert the existence of a
natural number less than zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.maxDegree_lt_card_verts [DecidableRel G.Adj] [Nonempty V] : G.maxDegree < Fintype.card V

views.nl_informal:
If the support of the simple graph `G` is a subset of the set `s`, then the induced subgraph of
`s` has the same number of edges as `G`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.card_edgeFinset_induce_of_support_subset (h : G.support ⊆ s) : #(G.induce s).edgeFinset = #G.edgeFinset

views.nl_informal:
If the neighbor set of a vertex `v` is a subset of `s`, then the degree of the vertex in the
induced subgraph of `s` is the same as in `G`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.degree_induce_of_neighborSet_subset {v : s} (h : G.neighborSet v ⊆ s) : (G.induce s).degree v = G.degree v

views.nl_informal:
If the support of the simple graph `G` is a subset of the set `s`, then the degree of vertices
in the induced subgraph of `s` are the same as in `G`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.degree_induce_of_support_subset (h : G.support ⊆ s) (v : s) : (G.induce s).degree v = G.degree v

views.nl_informal:
If every finite subgraph of a graph `G` has a homomorphism to a finite graph `F`, then there is
a homomorphism from the whole of `G` to `F`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.nonempty_hom_of_forall_finite_subgraph_hom [Finite W] (h : ∀ G' : G.Subgraph, G'.verts.Finite → G'.coe →g F) : Nonempty (G →g F)

views.nl_informal: A hamiltonian path visits every vertex.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.Walk.IsHamiltonian.mem_support (hp : p.IsHamiltonian) (c : α) : c ∈ p.support

views.nl_informal: Hamiltonian paths are paths.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.Walk.IsHamiltonian.isPath (hp : p.IsHamiltonian) : p.IsPath

views.nl_informal: A path whose support contains every vertex is hamiltonian.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.Walk.IsPath.isHamiltonian_of_mem (hp : p.IsPath) (hp' : ∀ w, w ∈ p.support) : p.IsHamiltonian

views.nl_informal: The support of a hamiltonian walk is the entire vertex set.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.Walk.IsHamiltonian.support_toFinset (hp : p.IsHamiltonian) : p.support.toFinset = Finset.univ

views.nl_informal: The length of a hamiltonian path is one less than the number of vertices of the graph.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.Walk.IsHamiltonian.length_eq (hp : p.IsHamiltonian) : p.length = Fintype.card α - 1

views.nl_informal: A hamiltonian cycle visits every vertex.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.Walk.IsHamiltonianCycle.mem_support (hp : p.IsHamiltonianCycle) (b : α) : b ∈ p.support

views.nl_informal: The length of a hamiltonian cycle is the number of vertices.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.Walk.IsHamiltonianCycle.length_eq [Fintype α] (hp : p.IsHamiltonianCycle) : p.length = Fintype.card α

views.nl_informal: Entries of the incidence matrix can be computed given additional decidable instances.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.incMatrix_apply' [Zero R] [One R] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableRel G.Adj] {a : α} {e : Sym2 α} : G.incMatrix R a e = if e ∈ G.incidenceSet a then 1 else 0

views.nl_informal:
Let $L$ be the graph Laplacian and let $x \in \mathbb{R}$, then
$$x^{\top} L x = \sum_{i \sim j} (x_{i}-x_{j})^{2}$$,
where $\sim$ denotes the adjacency relation
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.lapMatrix_toLinearMap₂' [Field R] [CharZero R] (x : V → R) : toLinearMap₂' R (G.lapMatrix R) x x = (∑ i : V, ∑ j : V, if G.Adj i j then (x i - x j)^2 else 0) / 2

views.nl_informal: The Laplacian matrix is positive semidefinite
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.posSemidef_lapMatrix [Field R] [LinearOrder R] [IsStrictOrderedRing R] [StarRing R] [TrivialStar R] : PosSemidef (G.lapMatrix R)

views.nl_informal: The number of connected components in `G` is the dimension of the nullspace of its Laplacian.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.card_connectedComponent_eq_finrank_ker_toLin'_lapMatrix : Fintype.card G.ConnectedComponent = Module.finrank ℝ (LinearMap.ker (Matrix.toLin' (G.lapMatrix ℝ)))

views.nl_informal: Every graph homomorphism from a complete graph is injective.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.Hom.injective_of_top_hom (f : (⊤ : SimpleGraph V) →g G') : Function.Injective f

views.nl_informal:
Given a vertex with one edge in a graph of cycles this gives the other edge incident
to the same vertex.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.IsCycles.other_adj_of_adj (h : G.IsCycles) (hadj : G.Adj v w) : ∃ w', w ≠ w' ∧ G.Adj v w'

views.nl_informal: The extended distance between vertices is equal to `1` if and only if these vertices are adjacent.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.edist_eq_one_iff_adj : G.edist u v = 1 ↔ G.Adj u v

views.nl_informal: Supergraphs have smaller or equal extended distances to their subgraphs.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.edist_anti {G' : SimpleGraph V} (h : G ≤ G') : G'.edist u v ≤ G.edist u v

views.nl_informal: The distance between vertices is equal to `1` if and only if these vertices are adjacent.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.dist_eq_one_iff_adj : G.dist u v = 1 ↔ G.Adj u v

views.nl_informal: Supergraphs have smaller or equal distances to their subgraphs.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.Reachable.dist_anti {G' : SimpleGraph V} (h : G ≤ G') (hr : G.Reachable u v) : G'.dist u v ≤ G.dist u v

views.nl_informal:
This bundles and abstracts some facts about the first three vertices of a shortest walk
of length at least two: the first and third nodes are different and not connected.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.Walk.exists_adj_adj_not_adj_ne {p : G.Walk v w} (hp : p.length = G.dist v w) (hl : 1 < G.dist v w) : ∃ (x a b : V), G.Adj x a ∧ G.Adj a b ∧ ¬ G.Adj x b ∧ x ≠ b

views.nl_informal: There is never an `s-t` edge in `G.replaceVertex s t`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.not_adj_replaceVertex_same : ¬(G.replaceVertex s t).Adj s t

views.nl_informal:
Except possibly for `t`, the neighbours of `s` in `G.replaceVertex s t` are its neighbours in
`G`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.adj_replaceVertex_iff_of_ne_left {w : V} (hw : w ≠ t) : (G.replaceVertex s t).Adj s w ↔ G.Adj s w

views.nl_informal:
Except possibly for itself, the neighbours of `t` in `G.replaceVertex s t` are the neighbours of
`s` in `G`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.adj_replaceVertex_iff_of_ne_right {w : V} (hw : w ≠ t) : (G.replaceVertex s t).Adj t w ↔ G.Adj s w

views.nl_informal: Adjacency in `G.replaceVertex s t` which does not involve `t` is the same as that of `G`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.adj_replaceVertex_iff_of_ne {v w : V} (hv : v ≠ t) (hw : w ≠ t) : (G.replaceVertex s t).Adj v w ↔ G.Adj v w

views.nl_informal: Taking a strict initial segment of a path removes the end vertex from the support.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.Walk.endpoint_not_mem_support_takeUntil {p : G.Walk u v} (hp : p.IsPath) (hw : w ∈ p.support) (h : v ≠ w) : v ∉ (p.takeUntil w hw).support

views.nl_informal: Distinct vertices are not reachable in the empty graph.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.reachable_bot {u v : V} : (⊥ : SimpleGraph V).Reachable u v ↔ u = v

views.nl_informal: Deleting a non-bridge edge from a connected graph preserves connectedness.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.Connected.connected_delete_edge_of_not_isBridge (hG : G.Connected) {x y : V} (h : ¬ G.IsBridge s(x, y)) : (G.deleteEdges {s(x, y)}).Connected

views.nl_informal:
Empty graphs are strongly regular. Note that `ℓ` can take any value
for empty graphs, since there are no pairs of adjacent vertices.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.bot_strongly_regular : (⊥ : SimpleGraph V).IsSRGWith (Fintype.card V) 0 ℓ 0

views.nl_informal:
Complete graphs are strongly regular. Note that `μ` can take any value
for complete graphs, since there are no distinct pairs of non-adjacent vertices.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.IsSRGWith.top : (⊤ : SimpleGraph V).IsSRGWith (Fintype.card V) (Fintype.card V - 1) (Fintype.card V - 2) μ

views.nl_informal:
Assuming `G` is strongly regular, `2*(k + 1) - m` in `G` is the number of vertices that are
adjacent to either `v` or `w` when `¬G.Adj v w`. So it's the cardinality of
`G.neighborSet v ∪ G.neighborSet w`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.IsSRGWith.card_neighborFinset_union_of_not_adj {v w : V} (h : G.IsSRGWith n k ℓ μ) (hne : v ≠ w) (ha : ¬G.Adj v w) : #(G.neighborFinset v ∪ G.neighborFinset w) = 2 * k - μ

views.nl_informal: The complement of a strongly regular graph is strongly regular.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.IsSRGWith.compl (h : G.IsSRGWith n k ℓ μ) : Gᶜ.IsSRGWith n (n - k - 1) (n - (2 * k - μ) - 2) (n - (2 * k - ℓ))

views.nl_informal:
The parameters of a strongly regular graph with at least one vertex satisfy
`k * (k - ℓ - 1) = (n - k - 1) * μ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.IsSRGWith.param_eq {V : Type u} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (h : G.IsSRGWith n k ℓ μ) (hn : 0 < n) : k * (k - ℓ - 1) = (n - k - 1) * μ

views.nl_informal:
Let `A` and `C` be the adjacency matrices of a strongly regular graph with parameters `n k ℓ μ`
and its complement respectively and `I` be the identity matrix,
then `A ^ 2 = k • I + ℓ • A + μ • C`. `C` is equivalent to the expression `J - I - A`
more often found in the literature, where `J` is the all-ones matrix.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.IsSRGWith.matrix_eq {α : Type*} [Semiring α] (h : G.IsSRGWith n k ℓ μ) : G.adjMatrix α ^ 2 = k • (1 : Matrix V V α) + ℓ • G.adjMatrix α + μ • Gᶜ.adjMatrix α

views.nl_informal:
An `r + 1`-cliquefree Turán-maximal graph is _not_ `r`-cliquefree
if it can accommodate such a clique.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.not_cliqueFree_of_isTuranMaximal (hn : r ≤ Fintype.card V) (hG : G.IsTuranMaximal r) : ¬G.CliqueFree r

views.nl_informal: In a Turán-maximal graph, non-adjacent vertices have the same degree.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.IsTuranMaximal.degree_eq_of_not_adj (h : G.IsTuranMaximal r) (hn : ¬G.Adj s t) : G.degree s = G.degree t

views.nl_informal: In a Turán-maximal graph, non-adjacency is transitive.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.IsTuranMaximal.not_adj_trans (h : G.IsTuranMaximal r) (hts : ¬G.Adj t s) (hsu : ¬G.Adj s u) : ¬G.Adj t u

views.nl_informal: In a Turán-maximal graph, non-adjacency is an equivalence relation.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.IsTuranMaximal.equivalence_not_adj : Equivalence (¬G.Adj · ·)

views.nl_informal: The parts of a Turán-maximal graph form an equipartition.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.IsTuranMaximal.isEquipartition [DecidableEq V] : h.finpartition.IsEquipartition

views.nl_informal:
There are `min n r` parts in a graph on `n` vertices satisfying `G.IsTuranMaximal r`.
`min` handles the `n < r` case, when `G` is complete but still `r + 1`-cliquefree
for having insufficiently many vertices.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.IsTuranMaximal.card_parts [DecidableEq V] : #h.finpartition.parts = min (Fintype.card V) r

views.nl_informal:
**Turán's theorem**, forward direction.

Any `r + 1`-cliquefree Turán-maximal graph on `n` vertices is isomorphic to `turanGraph n r`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.IsTuranMaximal.nonempty_iso_turanGraph : Nonempty (G ≃g turanGraph (Fintype.card V) r)

views.nl_informal:
**Turán's theorem**, reverse direction.

Any graph isomorphic to `turanGraph n r` is itself Turán-maximal if `0 < r`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.isTuranMaximal_of_iso (f : G ≃g turanGraph n r) (hr : 0 < r) : G.IsTuranMaximal r

views.nl_informal: Turán-maximality with `0 < r` transfers across graph isomorphisms.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.IsTuranMaximal.iso {W : Type*} [Fintype W] {H : SimpleGraph W} [DecidableRel H.Adj] (h : G.IsTuranMaximal r) (f : G ≃g H) (hr : 0 < r) : H.IsTuranMaximal r

views.nl_informal: For `0 < r`, `turanGraph n r` is Turán-maximal.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.isTuranMaximal_turanGraph (hr : 0 < r) : (turanGraph n r).IsTuranMaximal r

views.nl_informal:
**Turán's theorem**. `turanGraph n r` is, up to isomorphism, the unique
`r + 1`-cliquefree Turán-maximal graph on `n` vertices.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.isTuranMaximal_iff_nonempty_iso_turanGraph (hr : 0 < r) : G.IsTuranMaximal r ↔ Nonempty (G ≃g turanGraph (Fintype.card V) r)

views.nl_informal:
Given a graph in which the universal vertices do not violate Tutte's condition,
if the graph decomposes into cliques, there exists a matching that covers
everything except some universal vertices.

This lemma is marked private, because
it is strictly weaker than `IsPerfectMatching.exists_of_isClique_supp`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.Subgraph.IsMatching.exists_verts_compl_subset_universalVerts (h : ¬IsTutteViolator G G.universalVerts) (h' : ∀ (K : G.deleteUniversalVerts.coe.ConnectedComponent), G.deleteUniversalVerts.coe.IsClique K.supp) : ∃ M : Subgraph G, M.IsMatching ∧ M.vertsᶜ ⊆ G.universalVerts

views.nl_informal:
Given a graph in which the universal vertices do not violate Tutte's condition,
if the graph decomposes into cliques, it has a perfect matching.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.Subgraph.IsPerfectMatching.exists_of_isClique_supp (hveven : Even (Nat.card V)) (h : ¬G.IsTutteViolator G.universalVerts) (h' : ∀ (K : G.deleteUniversalVerts.coe.ConnectedComponent), G.deleteUniversalVerts.coe.IsClique K.supp) : ∃ (M : Subgraph G), M.IsPerfectMatching

views.nl_informal: Proves the necessity part of Tutte's theorem
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.not_isTutteViolator_of_isPerfectMatching {M : Subgraph G} (hM : M.IsPerfectMatching) (u : Set V) : ¬G.IsTutteViolator u

views.nl_informal:
A component of the graph with universal vertices is even if we remove a set of representatives
of odd components and a subset of universal vertices.

This is because the number of vertices in the even components is not affected, and from odd
components exactly one vertex is removed.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.even_ncard_image_val_supp_sdiff_image_val_rep_union {t : Set V} {s : Set G.deleteUniversalVerts.verts} (K : G.deleteUniversalVerts.coe.ConnectedComponent) (h : t ⊆ G.universalVerts) (hrep : ConnectedComponent.Represents s G.deleteUniversalVerts.coe.oddComponents) : Even (Subtype.val '' K.supp \ (Subtype.val '' s ∪ t)).ncard

views.nl_informal: A non-trivial `cons` walk is representable as a `concat` walk.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.Walk.exists_cons_eq_concat {u v w : V} (h : G.Adj u v) (p : G.Walk v w) : ∃ (x : V) (q : G.Walk u x) (h' : G.Adj x w), cons h p = q.concat h'

views.nl_informal: A non-trivial `concat` walk is representable as a `cons` walk.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.Walk.exists_concat_eq_cons {u v w : V} : ∀ (p : G.Walk u v) (h : G.Adj v w), ∃ (x : V) (h' : G.Adj u x) (q : G.Walk x w), p.concat h = cons h' q

views.nl_informal:
Every edge in a walk's edge list is an edge of the graph.
It is written in this form (rather than using `⊆`) to avoid unsightly coercions.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.Walk.edges_subset_edgeSet {u v : V} : ∀ (p : G.Walk u v) ⦃e : Sym2 V⦄, e ∈ p.edges → e ∈ G.edgeSet

views.nl_informal: A walk with its endpoints defeq is `Nil` if and only if it is equal to `nil`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.Walk.nil_iff_eq_nil : ∀ {p : G.Walk v v}, p.Nil ↔ p = nil

views.nl_informal:
Given a set `S` and a walk `w` from `u` to `v` such that `u ∈ S` but `v ∉ S`,
there exists a dart in the walk whose start is in `S` but whose end is not.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.Walk.exists_boundary_dart {u v : V} (p : G.Walk u v) (S : Set V) (uS : u ∈ S) (vS : v ∉ S) : ∃ d : G.Dart, d ∈ p.darts ∧ d.fst ∈ S ∧ d.snd ∉ S

views.nl_informal:
This lemma establishes a condition under which a subgraph is the same as a connected component.
Note the asymmetry in the hypothesis `h`: `v` is in `H.verts`, but `w` is not required to be.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.Subgraph.Connected.exists_verts_eq_connectedComponentSupp {H : Subgraph G} (hc : H.Connected) (h : ∀ v ∈ H.verts, ∀ w, G.Adj v w → H.Adj v w) : ∃ c : G.ConnectedComponent, H.verts = c.supp

views.nl_informal:
This lemma states that given some finite set of vertices, of which at least one is in the
support of a given walk, one of them is the first to be encountered. This consequence is encoded
as the set of vertices, restricted to those in the support, execept for the first, being empty.
You could interpret this as being `takeUntilSet`, but defining this is slightly involved due to
not knowing what the final vertex is. This could be done by defining a function to obtain the
first encountered vertex and then use that to define `takeUntilSet`. That direction could be
worthwhile if this concept is used more widely.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.Walk.exists_mem_support_mem_erase_mem_support_takeUntil_eq_empty (s : Finset V) (h : {x ∈ s | x ∈ p.support}.Nonempty) : ∃ x ∈ s, ∃ hx : x ∈ p.support, {t ∈ s.erase x | t ∈ (p.takeUntil x hx).support} = ∅

views.nl_informal:
The `takeUntil` and `dropUntil` functions split a walk into two pieces.
The lemma `SimpleGraph.Walk.count_support_takeUntil_eq_one` specifies where this split occurs.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.Walk.take_spec {u v w : V} (p : G.Walk v w) (h : u ∈ p.support) : (p.takeUntil u h).append (p.dropUntil u h) = p

views.nl_informal:
Given a walk `w` and a node in the support, there exists a natural `n`, such that given node
is the `n`-th node (zero-indexed) in the walk. In addition, `n` is at most the length of the path.
Due to the definition of `getVert` it would otherwise be legal to return a larger `n` for the last
node.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.Walk.mem_support_iff_exists_getVert {u v w : V} {p : G.Walk v w} : u ∈ p.support ↔ ∃ n, p.getVert n = u ∧ n ≤ p.length

views.nl_informal: Any vertex adjacent to a vertex of `C` and not lying in `K` must lie in `C`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.ComponentCompl.mem_of_adj : ∀ {C : G.ComponentCompl K} (c d : V), c ∈ C → d ∉ K → G.Adj c d → d ∈ C

views.nl_informal:
Assuming `G` is preconnected and `K` not empty, given any connected component `C` outside of `K`,
there exists a vertex `k ∈ K` adjacent to a vertex `v ∈ C`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.ComponentCompl.exists_adj_boundary_pair (Gc : G.Preconnected) (hK : K.Nonempty) : ∀ C : G.ComponentCompl K, ∃ ck : V × V, ck.1 ∈ C ∧ ck.2 ∈ K ∧ G.Adj ck.1 ck.2

views.nl_informal: The `componentCompl`s chosen by an end are all infinite.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.end_componentCompl_infinite (e : G.end) (K : (Finset V)ᵒᵖ) : ((e : (j : (Finset V)ᵒᵖ) → G.componentComplFunctor.obj j) K).supp.Infinite

views.nl_informal: A locally finite preconnected infinite graph has at least one end.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.nonempty_ends_of_infinite [LocallyFinite G] [Fact G.Preconnected] [Infinite V] : G.end.Nonempty

views.nl_informal: If one simple graph satisfies `p`, then there exists an extremal graph satisfying `p`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.exists_isExtremal_iff_exists (p : SimpleGraph V → Prop) : (∃ G : SimpleGraph V, ∃ _ : DecidableRel G.Adj, G.IsExtremal p) ↔ ∃ G, p G

views.nl_informal: If `H` has at least one edge, then there exists an extremal `H.Free` graph.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.exists_isExtremal_free {W : Type*} {H : SimpleGraph W} (h : H ≠ ⊥) : ∃ G : SimpleGraph V, ∃ _ : DecidableRel G.Adj, G.IsExtremal H.Free

views.nl_informal: If `G` is `H`-free, then `G` has at most `extremalNumber (card V) H` edges.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.card_edgeFinset_le_extremalNumber (h : H.Free G) : #G.edgeFinset ≤ extremalNumber (card V) H

views.nl_informal: If `G` has more than `extremalNumber (card V) H` edges, then `G` contains a copy of `H`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.IsContained.of_extremalNumber_lt_card_edgeFinset (h : extremalNumber (card V) H < #G.edgeFinset) : H ⊑ G

views.nl_informal:
`extremalNumber (card V) H` is at most `x` if and only if every `H`-free simple graph `G` has
at most `x` edges.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.extremalNumber_le_iff (H : SimpleGraph W) (m : ℕ) : extremalNumber (card V) H ≤ m ↔ ∀ ⦃G : SimpleGraph V⦄ [DecidableRel G.Adj], H.Free G → #G.edgeFinset ≤ m

views.nl_informal:
`extremalNumber (card V) H` is greater than `x` if and only if there exists a `H`-free simple
graph `G` with more than `x` edges.
views.lean_signature: theorem SimpleGraph.lt_extremalNumber_iff (H : SimpleGraph W) (m : ℕ) : m < extremalNumber (card V) H ↔ ∃ G : SimpleGraph V, ∃ _ : DecidableRel G.Adj, H.Free G ∧ m < #G.edgeFinset

views.nl_informal: If `H` contains a copy of `H'`, then `extremalNumber n H` is at most `extremalNumber n H`.

views.nl_informal:
Assume `k = l`. If two functions defined on `Fin k` and `Fin l` are equal on each element,
then they coincide (in the heq sense).
views.lean_signature: theorem Fin.heq_fun_iff {α : Sort*} {k l : ℕ} (h : k = l) {f : Fin k → α} {g : Fin l → α} : HEq f g ↔ ∀ i : Fin k, f i = g ⟨(i : ℕ), h ▸ i.2⟩

views.nl_informal:
Assume `k = l` and `k' = l'`.
If two functions `Fin k → Fin k' → α` and `Fin l → Fin l' → α` are equal on each pair,
then they coincide (in the heq sense).
views.lean_signature: theorem Fin.heq_fun₂_iff {α : Sort*} {k l k' l' : ℕ} (h : k = l) (h' : k' = l') {f : Fin k → Fin k' → α} {g : Fin l → Fin l' → α} : HEq f g ↔ ∀ (i : Fin k) (j : Fin k'), f i j = g ⟨(i : ℕ), h ▸ i.2⟩ ⟨(j : ℕ), h' ▸ j.2⟩

views.nl_informal:

views.lean_signature: theorem Fin.heq_ext_iff {k l : ℕ} (h : k = l) {i : Fin k} {j : Fin l} : HEq i j ↔ (i : ℕ) = (j : ℕ)

views.nl_informal: `a < b` as natural numbers if and only if `a < b` in `Fin n`.

views.nl_informal: `a ≤ b` as natural numbers if and only if `a ≤ b` in `Fin n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Fin.val_fin_le {n : ℕ} {a b : Fin n} : (a : ℕ) ≤ (b : ℕ) ↔ a ≤ b

in the same value.

views.nl_informal:
Embedding `i : Fin n` into `Fin (n + 1)` with a hole around `p : Fin (n + 1)`
embeds `i` by `castSucc` when the resulting `i.castSucc < p`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Fin.succAbove_of_castSucc_lt (p : Fin (n + 1)) (i : Fin n) (h : castSucc i < p) : p.succAbove i = castSucc i

views.nl_informal:
Embedding `i : Fin n` into `Fin (n + 1)` with a hole around `p : Fin (n + 1)`
embeds `i` by `succ` when the resulting `p < i.succ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Fin.succAbove_of_le_castSucc (p : Fin (n + 1)) (i : Fin n) (h : p ≤ castSucc i) : p.succAbove i = i.succ

views.nl_informal:
Embedding `i : Fin n` into `Fin (n + 1)` with a hole around `p : Fin (n + 1)`
never results in `p` itself
views.lean_signature: theorem Fin.succAbove_ne (p : Fin (n + 1)) (i : Fin n) : p.succAbove i ≠ p

views.nl_informal: Given a fixed pivot `p : Fin (n + 1)`, `p.succAbove` is injective.
views.lean_signature: theorem Fin.succAbove_right_injective : Injective p.succAbove

views.nl_informal: Given a fixed pivot `p : Fin (n + 1)`, `p.succAbove` is injective.
views.lean_signature: theorem Fin.succAbove_right_inj : p.succAbove i = p.succAbove j ↔ i = j

views.nl_informal: Embedding `Fin n` into `Fin (n + 1)` with a hole around zero embeds by `succ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Fin.succAbove_zero : succAbove (0 : Fin (n + 1)) = Fin.succ

views.nl_informal: Embedding `Fin n` into `Fin (n + 1)` with a hole around `last n` embeds by `castSucc`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Fin.succAbove_last : succAbove (last n) = castSucc

views.nl_informal:
Embedding `i : Fin n` into `Fin (n + 1)` using a pivot `p` that is greater
results in a value that is less than `p`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Fin.succAbove_lt_iff_castSucc_lt (p : Fin (n + 1)) (i : Fin n) : p.succAbove i < p ↔ castSucc i < p

views.nl_informal:
Embedding `i : Fin n` into `Fin (n + 1)` using a pivot `p` that is lesser
results in a value that is greater than `p`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Fin.lt_succAbove_iff_le_castSucc (p : Fin (n + 1)) (i : Fin n) : p < p.succAbove i ↔ p ≤ castSucc i

views.nl_informal: Embedding a positive `Fin n` results in a positive `Fin (n + 1)`
views.lean_signature: theorem Fin.succAbove_pos [NeZero n] (p : Fin (n + 1)) (i : Fin n) (h : 0 < i) : 0 < p.succAbove i

views.nl_informal: The range of `p.succAbove` is everything except `p`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Fin.range_succAbove (p : Fin (n + 1)) : Set.range p.succAbove = {p}ᶜ

views.nl_informal: `succAbove` is injective at the pivot
views.lean_signature: theorem Fin.succAbove_left_injective : Injective (@succAbove n)

views.nl_informal: `succAbove` is injective at the pivot
views.lean_signature: theorem Fin.succAbove_left_inj {x y : Fin (n + 1)} : x.succAbove = y.succAbove ↔ x = y

views.nl_informal: `succ` commutes with `succAbove`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Fin.succ_succAbove_succ {n : ℕ} (i : Fin (n + 1)) (j : Fin n) : i.succ.succAbove j.succ = (i.succAbove j).succ

views.nl_informal: `castSucc` commutes with `succAbove`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Fin.castSucc_succAbove_castSucc {n : ℕ} {i : Fin (n + 1)} {j : Fin n} : i.castSucc.succAbove j.castSucc = (i.succAbove j).castSucc

views.nl_informal:
Sending `Fin (n+1)` to `Fin n` by subtracting one from anything above `p`
then back to `Fin (n+1)` with a gap around `p` is the identity away from `p`.

views.nl_informal:

then back to `Fin (n+1)` with a gap around `p.succ` is the identity away from `p.succ`.

views.nl_informal:
Sending `Fin n` into `Fin (n + 1)` with a gap at `p`
then back to `Fin n` by subtracting one from anything above `p` is the identity.

views.nl_informal: `succ` commutes with `predAbove`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Fin.succ_predAbove_succ (a : Fin n) (b : Fin (n + 1)) : a.succ.predAbove b.succ = (a.predAbove b).succ

views.nl_informal: `castSucc` commutes with `predAbove`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Fin.castSucc_predAbove_castSucc {n : ℕ} (a : Fin n) (b : Fin (n + 1)) : a.castSucc.predAbove b.castSucc = (a.predAbove b).castSucc

views.nl_informal:

otherwise an element is odd iff its `Fin.val` value is odd.

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal: Updating a tuple and adding an element at the beginning commute.

views.nl_informal: As a binary function, `Fin.cons` is injective.
views.lean_signature: theorem Fin.cons_injective2 : Function.Injective2 (@cons n α)

views.nl_informal:

directly.

views.nl_informal: As a binary function, `Fin.snoc` is injective.

views.nl_informal: Updating the last element of a tuple does not change the beginning.

views.nl_informal: Updating an element and taking the beginning commute.

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:
`cons` and `snoc` commute. We state this lemma in a non-dependent setting, as otherwise it
would involve a cast to convince Lean that the two types are equal, making it harder to use.
views.lean_signature: theorem Fin.cons_snoc_eq_snoc_cons {β : Sort*} (a : β) (q : Fin n → β) (b : β) : @cons n.succ (fun _ ↦ β) a (snoc q b) = snoc (cons a q) b

views.nl_informal: Appending a one-tuple to the right is the same as `Fin.snoc`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Fin.append_right_eq_snoc {α : Sort*} {n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → α) (x₀ : Fin 1 → α) : Fin.append x x₀ = Fin.snoc x (x₀ 0)

views.nl_informal: `Fin.snoc` is the same as appending a one-tuple
views.lean_signature: theorem Fin.snoc_eq_append {α : Sort*} (xs : Fin n → α) (x : α) : snoc xs x = append xs (cons x Fin.elim0)

views.nl_informal: As a binary function, `Fin.insertNth` is injective.
views.lean_signature: theorem Fin.insertNth_injective2 {p : Fin (n + 1)} : Function.Injective2 (@insertNth n α p)

views.nl_informal: If `find p = some i`, then `p i` holds
views.lean_signature: theorem Fin.find_spec : ∀ {n : ℕ} (p : Fin n → Prop) [DecidablePred p] {i : Fin n} (_ : i ∈ Fin.find p), p i

views.nl_informal: `find p` does not return `none` if and only if `p i` holds at some index `i`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Fin.isSome_find_iff : ∀ {n : ℕ} {p : Fin n → Prop} [DecidablePred p], (find p).isSome ↔ ∃ i, p i

views.nl_informal: `find p` returns `none` if and only if `p i` never holds.
views.lean_signature: theorem Fin.find_eq_none_iff {n : ℕ} {p : Fin n → Prop} [DecidablePred p] : find p = none ↔ ∀ i, ¬p i

views.nl_informal:
If `find p` returns `some i`, then `p j` does not hold for `j < i`, i.e., `i` is minimal among
the indices where `p` holds.
views.lean_signature: theorem Fin.find_min : ∀ {n : ℕ} {p : Fin n → Prop} [DecidablePred p] {i : Fin n} (_ : i ∈ Fin.find p) {j : Fin n} (_ : j < i), ¬p j

views.nl_informal:
To show two sigma pairs of tuples agree, it to show the second elements are related via
`Fin.cast`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Fin.sigma_eq_of_eq_comp_cast {α : Type*} : ∀ {a b : Σ ii, Fin ii → α} (h : a.fst = b.fst), a.snd = b.snd ∘ Fin.cast h → a = b

views.nl_informal:
*Bubble sort induction*: Prove that the sorted version of `f` has some property `P`
if `f` satisfies `P` and `P` is preserved on permutations of `f` when swapping two
antitone values.
views.lean_signature: theorem Tuple.bubble_sort_induction' {n : ℕ} {α : Type*} [LinearOrder α] {f : Fin n → α} {P : (Fin n → α) → Prop} (hf : P f) (h : ∀ (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (i j : Fin n), i < j → (f ∘ σ) j < (f ∘ σ) i → P (f ∘ σ) → P (f ∘ σ ∘ Equiv.swap i j)) : P (f ∘ sort f)

views.nl_informal:
*Bubble sort induction*: Prove that the sorted version of `f` has some property `P`
if `f` satisfies `P` and `P` is preserved when swapping two antitone values.
views.lean_signature: theorem Tuple.bubble_sort_induction {n : ℕ} {α : Type*} [LinearOrder α] {f : Fin n → α} {P : (Fin n → α) → Prop} (hf : P f) (h : ∀ (g : Fin n → α) (i j : Fin n), i < j → g j < g i → P g → P (g ∘ Equiv.swap i j)) : P (f ∘ sort f)

views.nl_informal: The antidiagonal of `n` does not contain duplicate entries.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Nat.nodup_antidiagonalTuple (k n : ℕ) : List.Nodup (antidiagonalTuple k n)

views.nl_informal:
If `f₀ ≤ f₁ ≤ f₂ ≤ ⋯` is a sorted `m`-tuple of elements of `α`, then for any `j : Fin m` and
`a : α` we have `j < #{i | fᵢ ≤ a}` iff `fⱼ ≤ a`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Tuple.lt_card_le_iff_apply_le_of_monotone [Preorder α] [DecidableLE α] {m : ℕ} (f : Fin m → α) (a : α) (h_sorted : Monotone f) (j : Fin m) : j < Fintype.card {i // f i ≤ a} ↔ f j ≤ a

views.nl_informal: If two permutations of a tuple `f` are both monotone, then they are equal.
views.lean_signature: theorem Tuple.unique_monotone [PartialOrder α] {f : Fin n → α} {σ τ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)} (hfσ : Monotone (f ∘ σ)) (hfτ : Monotone (f ∘ τ)) : f ∘ σ = f ∘ τ

views.nl_informal: If two permutations of a tuple `f` are both antitone, then they are equal.
views.lean_signature: theorem Tuple.unique_antitone [PartialOrder α] {f : Fin n → α} {σ τ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)} (hfσ : Antitone (f ∘ σ)) (hfτ : Antitone (f ∘ τ)) : f ∘ σ = f ∘ τ

views.nl_informal:
A permutation `σ` equals `sort f` if and only if the map `i ↦ (f (σ i), σ i)` is
strictly monotone (w.r.t. the lexicographic ordering on the target).
views.lean_signature: theorem Tuple.eq_sort_iff' : σ = sort f ↔ StrictMono (σ.trans <| graphEquiv₁ f)

views.nl_informal:
A permutation `σ` equals `sort f` if and only if `f ∘ σ` is monotone and whenever `i < j`
and `f (σ i) = f (σ j)`, then `σ i < σ j`. This means that `sort f` is the lexicographically
smallest permutation `σ` such that `f ∘ σ` is monotone.
views.lean_signature: theorem Tuple.eq_sort_iff : σ = sort f ↔ Monotone (f ∘ σ) ∧ ∀ i j, i < j → f (σ i) = f (σ j) → σ i < σ j

views.nl_informal: The permutation that sorts `f` is the identity if and only if `f` is monotone.
views.lean_signature: theorem Tuple.sort_eq_refl_iff_monotone : sort f = Equiv.refl _ ↔ Monotone f

views.nl_informal: A permutation of a tuple `f` is `f` sorted if and only if it is monotone.
views.lean_signature: theorem Tuple.comp_sort_eq_comp_iff_monotone : f ∘ σ = f ∘ sort f ↔ Monotone (f ∘ σ)

views.nl_informal: The sorted versions of a tuple `f` and of any permutation of `f` agree.
views.lean_signature: theorem Tuple.comp_perm_comp_sort_eq_comp_sort : (f ∘ σ) ∘ sort (f ∘ σ) = f ∘ sort f

views.nl_informal:
If a permutation `f ∘ σ` of the tuple `f` is not the same as `f ∘ sort f`, then `f ∘ σ`
has a pair of strictly decreasing entries.
views.lean_signature: theorem Tuple.antitone_pair_of_not_sorted' (h : f ∘ σ ≠ f ∘ sort f) : ∃ i j, i < j ∧ (f ∘ σ) j < (f ∘ σ) i

views.nl_informal:
If the tuple `f` is not the same as `f ∘ sort f`, then `f` has a pair of strictly decreasing
entries.
views.lean_signature: theorem Tuple.antitone_pair_of_not_sorted (h : f ≠ f ∘ sort f) : ∃ i j, i < j ∧ f j < f i

views.nl_informal: Taking `m + 1` elements is equal to taking `m` elements and adding the `(m + 1)`th one.
views.lean_signature: theorem Fin.take_succ_eq_snoc (m : ℕ) (h : m < n) (v : (i : Fin n) → α i) : take m.succ h v = snoc (take m h.le v) (v ⟨m, h⟩)

views.nl_informal: `take` commutes with `update` for indices in the range of `take`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Fin.take_update_of_lt (m : ℕ) (h : m ≤ n) (v : (i : Fin n) → α i) (i : Fin m) (x : α (castLE h i)) : take m h (update v (castLE h i) x) = update (take m h v) i x

views.nl_informal: `take` is the same after `update` for indices outside the range of `take`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Fin.take_update_of_ge (m : ℕ) (h : m ≤ n) (v : (i : Fin n) → α i) (i : Fin n) (hi : i ≥ m) (x : α i) : take m h (update v i x) = take m h v

views.nl_informal:
Taking the first `m ≤ n` elements of an `addCases u v`, where `u` is a `n`-tuple, is the same as
taking the first `m` elements of `u`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Fin.take_addCases_left {n' : ℕ} {motive : Fin (n + n') → Sort*} (m : ℕ) (h : m ≤ n) (u : (i : Fin n) → motive (castAdd n' i)) (v : (i : Fin n') → motive (natAdd n i)) : take m (Nat.le_add_right_of_le h) (addCases u v) = take m h u

views.nl_informal:
Taking the first `n + m` elements of an `addCases u v`, where `v` is a `n'`-tuple and `m ≤ n'`,
is the same as appending `u` with the first `m` elements of `v`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Fin.take_addCases_right {n' : ℕ} {motive : Fin (n + n') → Sort*} (m : ℕ) (h : m ≤ n') (u : (i : Fin n) → motive (castAdd n' i)) (v : (i : Fin n') → motive (natAdd n i)) : take (n + m) (Nat.add_le_add_left h n) (addCases u v) = addCases u (take m h v)

views.nl_informal: `Fin.take` intertwines with `List.take` via `List.ofFn`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Fin.ofFn_take_eq_take_ofFn {α : Type*} {m : ℕ} (h : m ≤ n) (v : Fin n → α) : List.ofFn (take m h v) = (List.ofFn v).take m

views.nl_informal: `Fin.take` intertwines with `List.take` via `List.get`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Fin.get_take_eq_take_get_comp_cast {α : Type*} {m : ℕ} (l : List α) (h : m ≤ l.length) : (l.take m).get = take m h l.get ∘ Fin.cast (List.length_take_of_le h)

views.nl_informal:
For an empty type, the recursion principle evaluates to whatever `congr`
makes of the base case.
views.lean_signature: theorem FinEnum.recEmptyOption_of_card_eq_zero {P : Type u → Sort v} (finChoice : (n : ℕ) → Fin (n + 1)) (congr : {α β : Type u} → (_ : FinEnum α) → (_ : FinEnum β) → card β = card α → P α → P β) (empty : P PEmpty.{u + 1}) (option : {α : Type u} → FinEnum α → P α → P (Option α)) (α : Type u) [FinEnum α] (h : card α = 0) (_ : FinEnum PEmpty.{u + 1}) : recEmptyOption finChoice congr empty option α = congr _ _ (h.trans card_eq_zero.symm) empty

views.nl_informal:
For a type with positive `card`, the recursion principle evaluates to whatever
`congr` makes of the step result, where `Option.none` has been inserted into the
`(finChoice (card α - 1))`th rank of the enumeration.
views.lean_signature: theorem FinEnum.recEmptyOption_of_card_pos {P : Type u → Sort v} (finChoice : (n : ℕ) → Fin (n + 1)) (congr : {α β : Type u} → (_ : FinEnum α) → (_ : FinEnum β) → card β = card α → P α → P β) (empty : P PEmpty.{u + 1}) (option : {α : Type u} → FinEnum α → P α → P (Option α)) (α : Type u) [FinEnum α] (h : 0 < card α) : recEmptyOption finChoice congr empty option α = congr (insertNone _ <| finChoice (card α - 1)) ‹_› (congrArg (· + 1) card_fin |>.trans <| (card α).succ_pred_eq_of_pos h).symm (option ULift.instFinEnum <| recEmptyOption finChoice congr empty option (ULift.{u} <| Fin (card α - 1)))

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is injective, then `Nat.card α ≤ Nat.card β`. We must also assume
`Nat.card β = 0 → Nat.card α = 0` since `Nat.card` is defined to be `0` for infinite types.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finite.card_le_of_injective' {f : α → β} (hf : Function.Injective f) (h : Nat.card β = 0 → Nat.card α = 0) : Nat.card α ≤ Nat.card β

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is an embedding, then `Nat.card α ≤ Nat.card β`. We must also assume
`Nat.card β = 0 → Nat.card α = 0` since `Nat.card` is defined to be `0` for infinite types.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finite.card_le_of_embedding' (f : α ↪ β) (h : Nat.card β = 0 → Nat.card α = 0) : Nat.card α ≤ Nat.card β

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is surjective, then `Nat.card β ≤ Nat.card α`. We must also assume
`Nat.card α = 0 → Nat.card β = 0` since `Nat.card` is defined to be `0` for infinite types.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finite.card_le_of_surjective' {f : α → β} (hf : Function.Surjective f) (h : Nat.card α = 0 → Nat.card β = 0) : Nat.card β ≤ Nat.card α

views.nl_informal: `Infinite α` is not `Finite`
views.lean_signature: theorem not_finite (α : Sort*) [Infinite α] [Finite α] : False

views.nl_informal: Constructor for `Set.Finite` using a `Finite` instance.

views.nl_informal:
Projection of `Set.Finite` to its `Finite` instance.
This is intended to be used with dot notation.

views.lean_signature: theorem Set.Finite.to_subtype {s : Set α} (h : s.Finite) : Finite s

views.nl_informal:
After filtering out everything that does not equal a given value, at most that value remains.

This is equivalent to `filter_eq'` with the equality the other way.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.filter_eq [DecidableEq β] (s : Finset β) (b : β) : s.filter (Eq b) = ite (b ∈ s) {b} ∅

views.nl_informal:
After filtering out everything that does not equal a given value, at most that value remains.

This is equivalent to `filter_eq` with the equality the other way.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.filter_eq' [DecidableEq β] (s : Finset β) (b : β) : (s.filter fun a => a = b) = ite (b ∈ s) {b} ∅

views.nl_informal: $\#(s \setminus \{a\}) = \#s - 1$ if $a \in s$.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.card_erase_of_mem : a ∈ s → #(s.erase a) = #s - 1

views.nl_informal:
Reorder a finset.

The difference with `Finset.card_bij'` is that the bijection is specified as a surjective injection,
rather than by an inverse function.

The difference with `Finset.card_nbij` is that the bijection is allowed to use membership of the
domain, rather than being a non-dependent function.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.card_bij (i : ∀ a ∈ s, β) (hi : ∀ a ha, i a ha ∈ t) (i_inj : ∀ a₁ ha₁ a₂ ha₂, i a₁ ha₁ = i a₂ ha₂ → a₁ = a₂) (i_surj : ∀ b ∈ t, ∃ a ha, i a ha = b) : #s = #t

views.nl_informal:
Reorder a finset.

The difference with `Finset.card_bij` is that the bijection is specified with an inverse, rather
than as a surjective injection.

The difference with `Finset.card_nbij'` is that the bijection and its inverse are allowed to use
membership of the domains, rather than being non-dependent functions.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.card_bij' (i : ∀ a ∈ s, β) (j : ∀ a ∈ t, α) (hi : ∀ a ha, i a ha ∈ t) (hj : ∀ a ha, j a ha ∈ s) (left_inv : ∀ a ha, j (i a ha) (hi a ha) = a) (right_inv : ∀ a ha, i (j a ha) (hj a ha) = a) : #s = #t

views.nl_informal:
Reorder a finset.

The difference with `Finset.card_nbij'` is that the bijection is specified as a surjective
injection, rather than by an inverse function.

The difference with `Finset.card_bij` is that the bijection is a non-dependent function, rather than
being allowed to use membership of the domain.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.card_nbij (i : α → β) (hi : ∀ a ∈ s, i a ∈ t) (i_inj : (s : Set α).InjOn i) (i_surj : (s : Set α).SurjOn i t) : #s = #t

views.nl_informal:
Reorder a finset.

The difference with `Finset.card_nbij` is that the bijection is specified with an inverse, rather
than as a surjective injection.

The difference with `Finset.card_bij'` is that the bijection and its inverse are non-dependent
functions, rather than being allowed to use membership of the domains.

The difference with `Finset.card_equiv` is that bijectivity is only required to hold on the domains,
rather than on the entire types.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.card_nbij' (i : α → β) (j : β → α) (hi : ∀ a ∈ s, i a ∈ t) (hj : ∀ a ∈ t, j a ∈ s) (left_inv : ∀ a ∈ s, j (i a) = a) (right_inv : ∀ a ∈ t, i (j a) = a) : #s = #t

views.nl_informal: If there are more pigeons than pigeonholes, then there are two pigeons in the same pigeonhole.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.exists_ne_map_eq_of_card_lt_of_maps_to {t : Finset β} (hc : #t < #s) {f : α → β} (hf : ∀ a ∈ s, f a ∈ t) : ∃ x ∈ s, ∃ y ∈ s, x ≠ y ∧ f x = f y

views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.inter_nonempty_of_card_lt_card_add_card (hts : t ⊆ s) (hus : u ⊆ s) (hstu : #s < #t + #u) : (t ∩ u).Nonempty

views.nl_informal:
Given a subset `s` of a set `t`, of sizes at most and at least `n` respectively, there exists a
set `u` of size `n` which is both a superset of `s` and a subset of `t`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.exists_subsuperset_card_eq (hst : s ⊆ t) (hsn : #s ≤ n) (hnt : n ≤ #t) : ∃ u, s ⊆ u ∧ u ⊆ t ∧ #u = n

views.nl_informal: We can shrink a set to any smaller size.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.exists_subset_card_eq (hns : n ≤ #s) : ∃ t ⊆ s, #t = n

views.nl_informal: A `Finset` of a subsingleton type has cardinality at most one.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.card_le_one_of_subsingleton [Subsingleton α] (s : Finset α) : #s ≤ 1

views.nl_informal:
If a Finset in a Pi type is nontrivial (has at least two elements), then
its projection to some factor is nontrivial, and the fibers of the projection
are proper subsets.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.exists_of_one_lt_card_pi {ι : Type*} {α : ι → Type*} [∀ i, DecidableEq (α i)] {s : Finset (∀ i, α i)} (h : 1 < #s) : ∃ i, 1 < #(s.image (· i)) ∧ ∀ ai, s.filter (· i = ai) ⊂ s

Suppose that, given objects defined on all nonempty strict subsets of any nontrivial finset `s`,
one knows how to define an object on `s`. Then one can inductively define an object on all finsets,
starting from singletons and iterating.

views.nl_informal:
$\#(s \setminus \{a\}) = \#s - 1$ if $a \in s$.

views.nl_informal: A `Finset` for an empty type is empty.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.eq_empty_of_isEmpty [IsEmpty α] (s : Finset α) : s = ∅

views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.eq_of_mem_of_not_mem_erase (hs : b ∈ s) (hsa : b ∉ s.erase a) : b = a

views.nl_informal: If all elements of a `Finset` satisfy the predicate `p`, `s.filter p` is `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.Finset.filter_true_of_mem (h : ∀ x ∈ s, p x) : s.filter p = s

views.nl_informal: If all elements of a `Finset` fail to satisfy the predicate `p`, `s.filter p` is `∅`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.Finset.filter_false_of_mem (h : ∀ x ∈ s, ¬p x) : s.filter p = ∅

views.nl_informal: Finsets form an order-connected suborder of multisets.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.ordConnected_range_val : Set.OrdConnected (Set.range val : Set <| Multiset α)

views.nl_informal: Finsets form an order-connected suborder of sets.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.ordConnected_range_coe : Set.OrdConnected (Set.range ((↑) : Finset α → Set α))

views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.map_perm {σ : Equiv.Perm α} (hs : { a | σ a ≠ a } ⊆ s) : s.map (σ : α ↪ α) = s

views.nl_informal:
If all elements of a `Finset` satisfy the predicate `p`,
`s.subtype p` converts back to `s` with `Embedding.subtype`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.subtype_map_of_mem {p : α → Prop} [DecidablePred p] {s : Finset α} (h : ∀ x ∈ s, p x) : (s.subtype p).map (Embedding.subtype _) = s

views.nl_informal:
If a `Finset` of a subtype is converted to the main type with
`Embedding.subtype`, all elements of the result have the property of
the subtype.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.property_of_mem_map_subtype {p : α → Prop} (s : Finset { x // p x }) {a : α} (h : a ∈ s.map (Embedding.subtype _)) : p a

views.nl_informal:
If a `Finset` of a subtype is converted to the main type with
`Embedding.subtype`, the result does not contain any value that does
not satisfy the property of the subtype.

views.nl_informal:
If a `Finset` of a subtype is converted to the main type with
`Embedding.subtype`, the result is a subset of the set giving the
subtype.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.map_subtype_subset {t : Set α} (s : Finset t) : ↑(s.map (Embedding.subtype _)) ⊆ t

views.nl_informal:
If a `Finset` is a subset of the image of a `Set` under `f`,
then it is equal to the `Finset.image` of a `Finset` subset of that `Set`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.subset_set_image_iff [DecidableEq β] {s : Set α} {t : Finset β} {f : α → β} : ↑t ⊆ f '' s ↔ ∃ s' : Finset α, ↑s' ⊆ s ∧ s'.image f = t

views.nl_informal:
If a finset `t` is a subset of the image of another finset `s` under `f`, then it is equal to the
image of a subset of `s`.

views.nl_informal:
Induction principle to build a sequence, by adding one point at a time satisfying a given
relation with respect to all the previously chosen points.

More precisely, Assume that, for any finite set `s`, one can find another point satisfying
some relation `r` with respect to all the points in `s`. Then one may construct a
function `f : ℕ → α` such that `r (f m) (f n)` holds whenever `m < n`.
We also ensure that all constructed points satisfy a given predicate `P`.

views.nl_informal:
Induction principle to build a sequence, by adding one point at a time satisfying a given
symmetric relation with respect to all the previously chosen points.

More precisely, Assume that, for any finite set `s`, one can find another point satisfying
some relation `r` with respect to all the points in `s`. Then one may construct a
function `f : ℕ → α` such that `r (f m) (f n)` holds whenever `m ≠ n`.
We also ensure that all constructed points satisfy a given predicate `P`.

at two distinct indices `n m : ℕ` inside the list `l`.

views.nl_informal: This breaks a list of `m*n` items into `m` groups each containing `n` elements.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.ofFn_mul {m n} (f : Fin (m * n) → α) : List.ofFn f = List.flatten (List.ofFn fun i : Fin m => List.ofFn fun j : Fin n => f ⟨i * n + j, calc ↑i * n + j < (i + 1) * n := (Nat.add_lt_add_left j.prop _).trans_eq (by rw [Nat.add_mul, Nat.one_mul]) _ ≤ _ := Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ i.prop⟩)

views.nl_informal: This breaks a list of `m*n` items into `n` groups each containing `m` elements.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.ofFn_mul' {m n} (f : Fin (m * n) → α) : List.ofFn f = List.flatten (List.ofFn fun i : Fin n => List.ofFn fun j : Fin m => f ⟨m * i + j, calc m * i + j < m * (i + 1) := (Nat.add_lt_add_left j.prop _).trans_eq (by rw [Nat.mul_add, Nat.mul_one]) _ ≤ _ := Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ i.prop⟩)

views.nl_informal: The `r` argument to `permutationsAux2` is the same as appending.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.permutationsAux2_append (t : α) (ts : List α) (r : List β) (ys : List α) (f : List α → β) : (permutationsAux2 t ts nil ys f).2 ++ r = (permutationsAux2 t ts r ys f).2

views.nl_informal: The `ts` argument to `permutationsAux2` can be folded into the `f` argument.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.permutationsAux2_comp_append {t : α} {ts ys : List α} {r : List β} (f : List α → β) : ((permutationsAux2 t [] r ys) fun x => f (x ++ ts)).2 = (permutationsAux2 t ts r ys f).2

views.nl_informal: The `f` argument to `permutationsAux2` when `r = []` can be eliminated.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.map_permutationsAux2 (t : α) (ts : List α) (ys : List α) (f : List α → β) : (permutationsAux2 t ts [] ys id).2.map f = (permutationsAux2 t ts [] ys f).2

views.nl_informal:
An expository lemma to show how all of `ts`, `r`, and `f` can be eliminated from
`permutationsAux2`.

`(permutationsAux2 t [] [] ys id).2`, which appears on the RHS, is a list whose elements are
produced by inserting `t` into every non-terminal position of `ys` in order. As an example:
```lean
#eval permutationsAux2 1 [] [] [2, 3, 4] id
-- [[1, 2, 3, 4], [2, 1, 3, 4], [2, 3, 1, 4]]
```
views.lean_signature: theorem List.permutationsAux2_snd_eq (t : α) (ts : List α) (r : List β) (ys : List α) (f : List α → β) : (permutationsAux2 t ts r ys f).2 = ((permutationsAux2 t [] [] ys id).2.map fun x => f (x ++ ts)) ++ r

views.nl_informal: Prime `p` divides the product of a list `L` iff it divides some `a ∈ L`
views.lean_signature: theorem Prime.dvd_prod_iff {p : M} {L : List M} (pp : Prime p) : p ∣ L.prod ↔ ∃ a ∈ L, p ∣ a

views.nl_informal: The members of `l.ranges` are pairwise disjoint
views.lean_signature: theorem List.ranges_disjoint (l : List ℕ) : Pairwise Disjoint (ranges l)

views.nl_informal: The lengths of the members of `l.ranges` are those given by `l`
views.lean_signature: theorem List.ranges_length (l : List ℕ) : l.ranges.map length = l

views.nl_informal: If a `l : List α` is `Nodup l`, then all of its cyclic permutants are distinct.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Nodup.cyclicPermutations {l : List α} (hn : Nodup l) : Nodup (cyclicPermutations l)

views.nl_informal:
If a list `s` is shorter than a list `t`, then `s` is smaller than `t` under any shortlex
order.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Shortlex.of_length_lt {s t : List α} (h : s.length < t.length) : Shortlex r s t

views.nl_informal:
If two lists `s` and `t` have the same length, `s` is smaller than `t` under the shortlex order
over a relation `r`  when `s` is smaller than `t` under the lexicographic order over `r`
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Shortlex.of_lex {s t : List α} (len_eq : s.length = t.length) (h_lex : List.Lex r s t) : Shortlex r s t

views.nl_informal:
If two lists `s` and `t` have the same length, `s` is smaller than `t` under the shortlex order
over a relation `r` exactly when `s` is smaller than `t` under the lexicographic order over `r`.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.shortlex_iff_lex {s t : List α} (h : s.length = t.length) : Shortlex r s t ↔ List.Lex r s t

views.nl_informal:
If a list is sorted with respect to a decidable relation,
then it is sorted with respect to the corresponding Bool-valued relation.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Sorted.decide [DecidableRel r] (l : List α) (h : Sorted r l) : Sorted (fun a b => decide (r a b) = true) l

views.nl_informal:
The list `List.ofFn f` is strictly sorted with respect to `(· ≤ ·)` if and only if `f` is
strictly monotone.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.sorted_lt_ofFn_iff : (ofFn f).Sorted (· < ·) ↔ StrictMono f

views.nl_informal:
The list `List.ofFn f` is strictly sorted with respect to `(· ≥ ·)` if and only if `f` is
strictly antitone.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.sorted_gt_ofFn_iff : (ofFn f).Sorted (· > ·) ↔ StrictAnti f

views.nl_informal: The list `List.ofFn f` is sorted with respect to `(· ≤ ·)` if and only if `f` is monotone.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.sorted_le_ofFn_iff : (ofFn f).Sorted (· ≤ ·) ↔ Monotone f

views.nl_informal: The list `List.ofFn f` is sorted with respect to `(· ≥ ·)` if and only if `f` is antitone.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.sorted_ge_ofFn_iff : (ofFn f).Sorted (· ≥ ·) ↔ Antitone f

views.nl_informal: An alternative definition of `orderedInsert` using `takeWhile` and `dropWhile`.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.orderedInsert_eq_take_drop (a : α) : ∀ l : List α, l.orderedInsert r a = (l.takeWhile fun b => ¬a ≼ b) ++ a :: l.dropWhile fun b => ¬a ≼ b

views.nl_informal:
If `l` is already `List.Sorted` with respect to `r`, then `insertionSort` does not change
it.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Sorted.insertionSort_eq : ∀ {l : List α}, Sorted r l → insertionSort r l = l

views.nl_informal: For a reflexive relation, insert then erasing is the identity.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.erase_orderedInsert [DecidableEq α] [IsRefl α r] (x : α) (xs : List α) : (xs.orderedInsert r x).erase x = xs

views.nl_informal: Inserting then erasing an element that is absent is the identity.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.erase_orderedInsert_of_not_mem [DecidableEq α] {x : α} {xs : List α} (hx : x ∉ xs) : (xs.orderedInsert r x).erase x = xs

views.nl_informal: For an antisymmetric relation, erasing then inserting is the identity.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.orderedInsert_erase [DecidableEq α] [IsAntisymm α r] (x : α) (xs : List α) (hx : x ∈ xs) (hxs : Sorted r xs) : (xs.erase x).orderedInsert r x = xs

views.nl_informal: The list `List.insertionSort r l` is `List.Sorted` with respect to `r`.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.sorted_insertionSort : ∀ l, Sorted r (insertionSort r l)

views.nl_informal: If `c` is a sorted sublist of `l`, then `c` is still a sublist of `insertionSort r l`.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.sublist_insertionSort {l c : List α} (hr : c.Pairwise r) (hc : c <+ l) : c <+ insertionSort r l

views.nl_informal:
Another statement of stability of insertion sort.
If a pair `[a, b]` is a sublist of `l` and `r a b`,
then `[a, b]` is still a sublist of `insertionSort r l`.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.pair_sublist_insertionSort {a b : α} {l : List α} (hab : r a b) (h : [a, b] <+ l) : [a, b] <+ insertionSort r l

views.nl_informal:
Another statement of stability of insertion sort.
If a pair `[a, b]` is a sublist of a permutation of `l` and `a ≼ b`,
then `[a, b]` is still a sublist of `insertionSort r l`.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.pair_sublist_insertionSort' {a b : α} {l : List α} (hab : a ≼ b) (h : [a, b] <+~ l) : [a, b] <+ insertionSort r l

views.nl_informal:
The original list `L` can be recovered by flattening the lists produced by `splitOnP p L`,
interspersed with the elements `L.filter p`.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.splitOnP_spec (as : List α) : flatten (zipWith (· ++ ·) (splitOnP p as) (((as.filter p).map fun x => [x]) ++ [[]])) = as

views.nl_informal: If no element satisfies `p` in the list `xs`, then `xs.splitOnP p = [xs]`
views.lean_signature: theorem List.splitOnP_eq_single (h : ∀ x ∈ xs, ¬p x) : xs.splitOnP p = [xs]

views.nl_informal:
When a list of the form `[...xs, sep, ...as]` is split on `p`, the first element is `xs`,
assuming no element in `xs` satisfies `p` but `sep` does satisfy `p`
views.lean_signature: theorem List.splitOnP_first (h : ∀ x ∈ xs, ¬p x) (sep : α) (hsep : p sep) (as : List α) : (xs ++ sep :: as).splitOnP p = xs :: as.splitOnP p

views.nl_informal: `intercalate [x]` is the left inverse of `splitOn x`
views.lean_signature: theorem List.intercalate_splitOn (x : α) [DecidableEq α] : [x].intercalate (xs.splitOn x) = xs

views.nl_informal:
`splitOn x` is the left inverse of `intercalate [x]`, on the domain
consisting of each nonempty list of lists `ls` whose elements do not contain `x`
views.lean_signature: theorem List.splitOn_intercalate [DecidableEq α] (x : α) (hx : ∀ l ∈ ls, x ∉ l) (hls : ls ≠ []) : ([x].intercalate ls).splitOn x = ls

views.nl_informal:
If `P₁ x ↔ ... ↔ Pₙ x` for all `x`, then `(∀ x, P₁ x) ↔ ... ↔ (∀ x, Pₙ x)`.
Note: in concrete cases, Lean has trouble finding the list `[P₁, ..., Pₙ]` from the list
`[(∀ x, P₁ x), ..., (∀ x, Pₙ x)]`, but simply providing a list of underscores with the right
length makes it happier.

Example:
```lean
example (P₁ P₂ P₃ : ℕ → Prop) (H : ∀ n, [P₁ n, P₂ n, P₃ n].TFAE) :
    [∀ n, P₁ n, ∀ n, P₂ n, ∀ n, P₃ n].TFAE :=
  forall_tfae [_, _, _] H
```
views.lean_signature: theorem List.forall_tfae {α : Type*} (l : List (α → Prop)) (H : ∀ a : α, (l.map (fun p ↦ p a)).TFAE) : (l.map (fun p ↦ ∀ a, p a)).TFAE

views.nl_informal:
If `P₁ x ↔ ... ↔ Pₙ x` for all `x`, then `(∃ x, P₁ x) ↔ ... ↔ (∃ x, Pₙ x)`.
Note: in concrete cases, Lean has trouble finding the list `[P₁, ..., Pₙ]` from the list
`[(∃ x, P₁ x), ..., (∃ x, Pₙ x)]`, but simply providing a list of underscores with the right
length makes it happier.

Example:
```lean
example (P₁ P₂ P₃ : ℕ → Prop) (H : ∀ n, [P₁ n, P₂ n, P₃ n].TFAE) :
    [∃ n, P₁ n, ∃ n, P₂ n, ∃ n, P₃ n].TFAE :=
  exists_tfae [_, _, _] H
```
views.lean_signature: theorem List.exists_tfae {α : Type*} (l : List (α → Prop)) (H : ∀ a : α, (l.map (fun p ↦ p a)).TFAE) : (l.map (fun p ↦ ∃ a, p a)).TFAE

views.nl_informal:
Additive maps from finite matrices are equal if they agree on the standard basis.

See note [partially-applied ext lemmas].
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.ext_addMonoidHom [Finite m] [Finite n] [AddCommMonoid α] [AddCommMonoid β] ⦃f g : Matrix m n α →+ β⦄ (h : ∀ i j, f.comp (stdBasisMatrixAddMonoidHom i j) = g.comp (stdBasisMatrixAddMonoidHom i j)) : f = g

views.nl_informal:
Linear maps from finite matrices are equal if they agree on the standard basis.

See note [partially-applied ext lemmas].
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.ext_linearMap [Finite m] [Finite n] [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid α] [AddCommMonoid β] [Module R α] [Module R β] ⦃f g : Matrix m n α →ₗ[R] β⦄ (h : ∀ i j, f ∘ₗ stdBasisMatrixLinearMap R i j = g ∘ₗ stdBasisMatrixLinearMap R i j) : f = g

views.nl_informal: `M` is a scalar matrix if it commutes with every non-diagonal `stdBasisMatrix`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.mem_range_scalar_of_commute_stdBasisMatrix {M : Matrix n n α} (hM : Pairwise fun i j => Commute (stdBasisMatrix i j 1) M) : M ∈ Set.range (Matrix.scalar n)

views.nl_informal: `M` is a scalar matrix if and only if it commutes with every `stdBasisMatrix`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.mem_range_scalar_iff_commute_stdBasisMatrix' {M : Matrix n n α} : M ∈ Set.range (Matrix.scalar n) ↔ ∀ (i j : n), Commute (stdBasisMatrix i j 1) M

views.nl_informal: On square matrices, `Matrix.mulLeftLinearMap` and `LinearMap.mulLeft` coincide.
views.lean_signature: theorem mulLeftLinearMap_eq_mulLeft : mulLeftLinearMap m R = LinearMap.mulLeft R (A := Matrix m m A)

views.nl_informal: On square matrices, `Matrix.mulRightLinearMap` and `LinearMap.mulRight` coincide.
views.lean_signature: theorem mulRightLinearMap_eq_mulRight : mulRightLinearMap m R = LinearMap.mulRight R (A := Matrix m m A)

views.nl_informal: On square matrices, `Matrix.mulLinearMap` and `LinearMap.mul` coincide.
views.lean_signature: theorem mulLinearMap_eq_mul : mulLinearMap R = LinearMap.mul R (A := Matrix m m A)

views.nl_informal: Two block matrices are equal if their blocks are equal.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.ext_iff_blocks {A B : Matrix (n ⊕ o) (l ⊕ m) α} : A = B ↔ A.toBlocks₁₁ = B.toBlocks₁₁ ∧ A.toBlocks₁₂ = B.toBlocks₁₂ ∧ A.toBlocks₂₁ = B.toBlocks₂₁ ∧ A.toBlocks₂₂ = B.toBlocks₂₂

views.nl_informal:
A column partitioned matrix when transposed gives a row partitioned matrix with columns of the
initial matrix transposed to become rows.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.transpose_fromCols (A₁ : Matrix m n₁ R) (A₂ : Matrix m n₂ R) : transpose (fromCols A₁ A₂) = fromRows (transpose A₁) (transpose A₂)

views.nl_informal:
A row partitioned matrix when transposed gives a column partitioned matrix with rows of the
initial matrix transposed to become columns.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.transpose_fromRows (A₁ : Matrix m₁ n R) (A₂ : Matrix m₂ n R) : transpose (fromRows A₁ A₂) = fromCols (transpose A₁) (transpose A₂)

views.nl_informal: Negating a matrix partitioned by rows is equivalent to negating each of the rows.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.fromRows_neg (A₁ : Matrix m₁ n R) (A₂ : Matrix m₂ n R) : -fromRows A₁ A₂ = fromRows (-A₁) (-A₂)

views.nl_informal: Negating a matrix partitioned by columns is equivalent to negating each of the columns.
