views.lean_signature: theorem Setoid.classes_eqv_classes {r : Setoid α} (a) : ∃! b ∈ r.classes, a ∈ b

views.nl_informal: If x ∈ α is in 2 equivalence classes, the equivalence classes are equal.
views.lean_signature: theorem Setoid.eq_of_mem_classes {r : Setoid α} {x b} (hc : b ∈ r.classes) (hb : x ∈ b) {b'} (hc' : b' ∈ r.classes) (hb' : x ∈ b') : b = b'

views.nl_informal:
The elements of a set of sets partitioning α are the equivalence classes of the
equivalence relation defined by the set of sets.
views.lean_signature: theorem Setoid.eq_eqv_class_of_mem {c : Set (Set α)} (H : ∀ a, ∃! b ∈ c, a ∈ b) {s y} (hs : s ∈ c) (hy : y ∈ s) : s = { x | mkClasses c H x y }

views.nl_informal:
The equivalence classes of the equivalence relation defined by a set of sets
partitioning α are elements of the set of sets.
views.lean_signature: theorem Setoid.eqv_class_mem {c : Set (Set α)} (H : ∀ a, ∃! b ∈ c, a ∈ b) {y} : { x | mkClasses c H x y } ∈ c

views.nl_informal: Distinct elements of a set of sets partitioning α are disjoint.
views.lean_signature: theorem Setoid.eqv_classes_disjoint {c : Set (Set α)} (H : ∀ a, ∃! b ∈ c, a ∈ b) : c.PairwiseDisjoint id

views.nl_informal: A set of disjoint sets covering α partition α (classical).
views.lean_signature: theorem Setoid.eqv_classes_of_disjoint_union {c : Set (Set α)} (hu : Set.sUnion c = @Set.univ α) (H : c.PairwiseDisjoint id) (a) : ∃! b ∈ c, a ∈ b

views.nl_informal:
The equivalence relation made from the equivalence classes of an equivalence
relation r equals r.
views.lean_signature: theorem Setoid.mkClasses_classes (r : Setoid α) : mkClasses r.classes classes_eqv_classes = r

views.nl_informal: A partition of `α` does not contain the empty set.
views.lean_signature: theorem Setoid.nonempty_of_mem_partition {c : Set (Set α)} (hc : IsPartition c) {s} (h : s ∈ c) : s.Nonempty

views.nl_informal: All elements of a partition of α are the equivalence class of some y ∈ α.
views.lean_signature: theorem Setoid.exists_of_mem_partition {c : Set (Set α)} (hc : IsPartition c) {s} (hs : s ∈ c) : ∃ y, s = { x | mkClasses c hc.2 x y }

views.nl_informal:
The equivalence classes of the equivalence relation defined by a partition of α equal
the original partition.
views.lean_signature: theorem Setoid.classes_mkClasses (c : Set (Set α)) (hc : IsPartition c) : (mkClasses c hc.2).classes = c

views.nl_informal: A finpartition gives rise to a setoid partition
views.lean_signature: theorem Finpartition.isPartition_parts {α} (f : Finpartition (Set.univ : Set α)) : Setoid.IsPartition (f.parts : Set (Set α))

views.nl_informal: The indices of `Quotient.out` and `IndexedPartition.out` are equal.
views.lean_signature: theorem IndexedPartition.index_out (x : hs.Quotient) : hs.index x.out = hs.index (hs.out x)

views.nl_informal:
A family of injective functions with pairwise disjoint
domains and pairwise disjoint ranges can be glued together
to form an injective function.
views.lean_signature: theorem IndexedPartition.piecewise_inj {β : Type*} {f : ι → α → β} (h_injOn : ∀ i, InjOn (f i) (s i)) (h_disjoint : PairwiseDisjoint (univ : Set ι) fun i => (f i) '' (s i)) : Injective (piecewise hs f)

views.nl_informal:
A family of bijective functions with pairwise disjoint
domains and pairwise disjoint ranges can be glued together
to form a bijective function.
views.lean_signature: theorem IndexedPartition.piecewise_bij {β : Type*} {f : ι → α → β} {t : ι → Set β} (ht : IndexedPartition t) (hf : ∀ i, BijOn (f i) (s i) (t i)) : Bijective (piecewise hs f)

views.nl_informal:
Given a partition of the ambient type, the cardinal of a finite set
is the `finsum` of the cardinalities of its traces on the parts of the partition
views.lean_signature: theorem Setoid.IsPartition.ncard_eq_finsum {α : Type*} {P : Set (Set α)} (hP : Setoid.IsPartition P) (s : Set α) (hs : s.Finite := by toFinite_tac) : s.ncard = finsum fun t : P => (s ∩ t).ncard

views.nl_informal: A specialized ext lemma for equality of sigma types over an indexed subtype.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sigma.subtype_ext {β : Type*} {p : α → β → Prop} : ∀ {x₀ x₁ : Σa, Subtype (p a)}, x₀.fst = x₁.fst → (x₀.snd : β) = x₁.snd → x₀ = x₁

views.nl_informal: A specialized ext lemma for equality of `PSigma` types over an indexed subtype.
views.lean_signature: theorem PSigma.subtype_ext {β : Sort*} {p : α → β → Prop} : ∀ {x₀ x₁ : Σ'a, Subtype (p a)}, x₀.fst = x₁.fst → (x₀.snd : β) = x₁.snd → x₀ = x₁

views.nl_informal:
The length of the String returned by `String.leftpad n a c` is equal
to the larger of `n` and `s.length`
views.lean_signature: theorem String.length_leftpad (n : ℕ) (c : Char) : ∀ (s : String), (leftpad n c s).length = max n s.length

views.nl_informal: For any fintype `α` of cardinality `n`, `card (Sym α k) = multichoose (card α) k`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sym.card_sym_eq_multichoose (α : Type*) (k : ℕ) [Fintype α] [Fintype (Sym α k)] : card (Sym α k) = multichoose (card α) k

views.nl_informal:
The *stars and bars* lemma: the cardinality of `Sym α k` is equal to
`Nat.choose (card α + k - 1) k`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sym.card_sym_eq_choose {α : Type*} [Fintype α] (k : ℕ) [Fintype (Sym α k)] : card (Sym α k) = (card α + k - 1).choose k

views.nl_informal: The `diag` of `s : Finset α` is sent on a finset of `Sym2 α` of card `#s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sym2.card_image_diag (s : Finset α) : #(s.diag.image Sym2.mk) = #s

views.nl_informal:
The `offDiag` of `s : Finset α` is sent on a finset of `Sym2 α` of card `#s.offDiag / 2`.
This is because every element `s(x, y)` of `Sym2 α` not on the diagonal comes from exactly two
pairs: `(x, y)` and `(y, x)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sym2.card_image_offDiag (s : Finset α) : #(s.offDiag.image Sym2.mk) = (#s).choose 2

views.nl_informal: Type **stars and bars** for the case `n = 2`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sym2.card {α} [Fintype α] : card (Sym2 α) = Nat.choose (card α + 1) 2

views.nl_informal:
In a linear order, two symmetric squares are equal if and only if
they have the same infimum and supremum.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sym2.inf_eq_inf_and_sup_eq_sup [LinearOrder α] {s t : Sym2 α} : s.inf = t.inf ∧ s.sup = t.sup ↔ s = t

views.nl_informal: Two `v w : Vector α n` are equal iff they are equal at every single index.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.ext : ∀ {v w : Vector α n} (_ : ∀ m : Fin n, Vector.get v m = Vector.get w m), v = w

views.nl_informal: The `tail` of a `nil` vector is `nil`.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.tail_nil : (@nil α).tail = nil

views.nl_informal: The `tail` of a vector made up of one element is `nil`.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.singleton_tail : ∀ (v : Vector α 1), v.tail = Vector.nil

views.nl_informal:
The list that makes up a `Vector` made up of a single element,
retrieved via `toList`, is equal to the list of that single element.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.toList_singleton (v : Vector α 1) : v.toList = [v.head]

views.nl_informal: Mapping under `id` does not change a vector.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.map_id {n : ℕ} (v : Vector α n) : Vector.map id v = v

views.nl_informal:
The `List` of a vector after a `reverse`, retrieved by `toList` is equal
to the `List.reverse` after retrieving a vector's `toList`.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.toList_reverse {v : Vector α n} : v.reverse.toList = v.toList.reverse

views.nl_informal:
Accessing the nth element of a vector made up
of one element `x : α` is `x` itself.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.get_cons_nil : ∀ {ix : Fin 1} (x : α), get (x ::ᵥ nil) ix = x

views.nl_informal: The last element of a `Vector`, given that the vector is at least one element.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.last_def {v : Vector α (n + 1)} : v.last = v.get (Fin.last n)

views.nl_informal: The `last` element of a vector is the `head` of the `reverse` vector.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.reverse_get_zero {v : Vector α (n + 1)} : v.reverse.head = v.last

views.nl_informal: Providing an empty vector to `scanl` gives the starting value `b : β`.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.scanl_nil : scanl f b nil = b ::ᵥ nil

views.nl_informal:
The recursive step of `scanl` splits a vector `x ::ᵥ v : Vector α (n + 1)`
into the provided starting value `b : β` and the recursed `scanl`
`f b x : β` as the starting value.

This lemma is the `cons` version of `scanl_get`.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.scanl_cons (x : α) : scanl f b (x ::ᵥ v) = b ::ᵥ scanl f (f b x) v

views.nl_informal:
The underlying `List` of a `Vector` after a `scanl` is the `List.scanl`
of the underlying `List` of the original `Vector`.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.scanl_val : ∀ {v : Vector α n}, (scanl f b v).val = List.scanl f b v.val

views.nl_informal:
The `toList` of a `Vector` after a `scanl` is the `List.scanl`
of the `toList` of the original `Vector`.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.toList_scanl : (scanl f b v).toList = List.scanl f b v.toList

views.nl_informal:
The recursive step of `scanl` splits a vector made up of a single element
`x ::ᵥ nil : Vector α 1` into a `Vector` of the provided starting value `b : β`
and the mapped `f b x : β` as the last value.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.scanl_singleton (v : Vector α 1) : scanl f b v = b ::ᵥ f b v.head ::ᵥ nil

views.nl_informal:
The first element of `scanl` of a vector `v : Vector α n`,
retrieved via `head`, is the starting value `b : β`.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.scanl_head : (scanl f b v).head = b

views.nl_informal:
For an index `i : Fin n`, the nth element of `scanl` of a
vector `v : Vector α n` at `i.succ`, is equal to the application
function `f : β → α → β` of the `castSucc i` element of
`scanl f b v` and `get v i`.

This lemma is the `get` version of `scanl_cons`.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.scanl_get (i : Fin n) : (scanl f b v).get i.succ = f ((scanl f b v).get (Fin.castSucc i)) (v.get i)

views.nl_informal: Erasing an element after inserting an element, at different indices.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.eraseIdx_insertIdx' {v : Vector α (n + 1)} : ∀ {i : Fin (n + 1)} {j : Fin (n + 2)}, eraseIdx (j.succAbove i) (insertIdx a j v) = insertIdx a (i.predAbove j) (eraseIdx i v)

views.nl_informal: The head of a vector obtained by prepending is the element prepended.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.head_cons (a : α) : ∀ v : Vector α n, head (cons a v) = a

views.nl_informal: The tail of a vector obtained by prepending is the vector prepended. to
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.tail_cons (a : α) : ∀ v : Vector α n, tail (cons a v) = v

views.nl_informal: Prepending the head of a vector to its tail gives the vector.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.cons_head_tail : ∀ v : Vector α (succ n), cons (head v) (tail v) = v

views.nl_informal: A `nil` vector maps to a `nil` vector.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.map_nil (f : α → β) : map f nil = nil

views.nl_informal: `map` is natural with respect to `cons`.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.map_cons (f : α → β) (a : α) : ∀ v : Vector α n, map f (cons a v) = cons (f a) (map f v)

views.nl_informal: Vector is determined by the underlying list.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.eq {n : ℕ} : ∀ a1 a2 : Vector α n, toList a1 = toList a2 → a1 = a2

views.nl_informal: A vector of length `0` is a `nil` vector.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.eq_nil (v : Vector α 0) : v = nil

views.nl_informal:
Vector of length from a list `v`
with witness that `v` has length `n` maps to `v` under `toList`.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.toList_mk (v : List α) (P : List.length v = n) : toList (Subtype.mk v P) = v

views.nl_informal: A nil vector maps to a nil list.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.toList_nil : toList nil = @List.nil α

views.nl_informal: The length of the list to which a vector of length `n` maps is `n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.toList_length (v : Vector α n) : (toList v).length = n

views.nl_informal:
`toList` of `cons` of a vector and an element is
the `cons` of the list obtained by `toList` and the element
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.toList_cons (a : α) (v : Vector α n) : toList (cons a v) = a :: toList v

views.nl_informal: Appending of vectors corresponds under `toList` to appending of lists.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.toList_append {n m : ℕ} (v : Vector α n) (w : Vector α m) : toList (append v w) = toList v ++ toList w

views.nl_informal: `drop` of vectors corresponds under `toList` to `drop` of lists.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.toList_drop {n m : ℕ} (v : Vector α m) : toList (drop n v) = List.drop n (toList v)

views.nl_informal: `take` of vectors corresponds under `toList` to `take` of lists.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.toList_take {n m : ℕ} (v : Vector α m) : toList (take n v) = List.take n (toList v)

views.nl_informal:
If there is a set of states that is closed under `f`, and such that `f` produces that same output
for all states in this set, then the state is not actually needed.
Hence, then we can rewrite `mapAccumr` into just `map`.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.mapAccumr_eq_map {f : α → σ → σ × β} {s₀ : σ} (S : Set σ) (h₀ : s₀ ∈ S) (closure : ∀ a s, s ∈ S → (f a s).1 ∈ S) (out : ∀ a s s', s ∈ S → s' ∈ S → (f a s).2 = (f a s').2) : (mapAccumr f xs s₀).snd = map (f · s₀ |>.snd) xs

views.nl_informal:
If there is a set of states that is closed under `f`, and such that `f` produces that same output
for all states in this set, then the state is not actually needed.
Hence, then we can rewrite `mapAccumr₂` into just `map₂`.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.mapAccumr₂_eq_map₂ {f : α → β → σ → σ × γ} {s₀ : σ} (S : Set σ) (h₀ : s₀ ∈ S) (closure : ∀ a b s, s ∈ S → (f a b s).1 ∈ S) (out : ∀ a b s s', s ∈ S → s' ∈ S → (f a b s).2 = (f a b s').2) : (mapAccumr₂ f xs ys s₀).snd = map₂ (f · · s₀ |>.snd) xs ys

views.nl_informal:
If an accumulation function `f`, given an initial state `s`, produces `s` as its output state
for all possible input bits, then the state is redundant and can be optimized out.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.mapAccumr_eq_map_of_constant_state (f : α → σ → σ × β) (s : σ) (h : ∀ a, (f a s).fst = s) : mapAccumr f xs s = (s, (map (fun x => (f x s).snd) xs))

views.nl_informal:
If an accumulation function `f`, given an initial state `s`, produces `s` as its output state
for all possible input bits, then the state is redundant and can be optimized out.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.mapAccumr₂_eq_map₂_of_constant_state (f : α → β → σ → σ × γ) (s : σ) (h : ∀ a b, (f a b s).fst = s) : mapAccumr₂ f xs ys s = (s, (map₂ (fun x y => (f x y s).snd) xs ys))

views.nl_informal:
If an accumulation function `f`, produces the same output bits regardless of accumulation state,
then the state is redundant and can be optimized out.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.mapAccumr_eq_map_of_unused_state (f : α → σ → σ × β) (s : σ) (h : ∀ a s s', (f a s).snd = (f a s').snd) : (mapAccumr f xs s).snd = (map (fun x => (f x s).snd) xs)

views.nl_informal:
If an accumulation function `f`, produces the same output bits regardless of accumulation state,
then the state is redundant and can be optimized out.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.mapAccumr₂_eq_map₂_of_unused_state (f : α → β → σ → σ × γ) (s : σ) (h : ∀ a b s s', (f a b s).snd = (f a b s').snd) : (mapAccumr₂ f xs ys s).snd = (map₂ (fun x y => (f x y s).snd) xs ys)

views.nl_informal:
If `f` takes a pair of states, but always returns the same value for both elements of the
pair, then we can simplify to just a single element of state.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.mapAccumr_redundant_pair (f : α → (σ × σ) → (σ × σ) × β) (h : ∀ x s, (f x (s, s)).fst.fst = (f x (s, s)).fst.snd) : (mapAccumr f xs (s, s)).snd = (mapAccumr (fun x (s : σ) => (f x (s, s) |>.fst.fst, f x (s, s) |>.snd) ) xs s).snd

views.nl_informal:
If `f` takes a pair of states, but always returns the same value for both elements of the
pair, then we can simplify to just a single element of state.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.mapAccumr₂_redundant_pair (f : α → β → (σ × σ) → (σ × σ) × γ) (h : ∀ x y s, let s' := (f x y (s, s)).fst; s'.fst = s'.snd) : (mapAccumr₂ f xs ys (s, s)).snd = (mapAccumr₂ (fun x y (s : σ) => (f x y (s, s) |>.fst.fst, f x y (s, s) |>.snd) ) xs ys s).snd

views.nl_informal:
If `f` returns the same output and next state for every value of it's first argument, then
`xs : Vector` is ignored, and we can rewrite `mapAccumr₂` into `map`.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.mapAccumr₂_unused_input_left [Inhabited α] (f : α → β → σ → σ × γ) (h : ∀ a b s, f default b s = f a b s) : mapAccumr₂ f xs ys s = mapAccumr (fun b s => f default b s) ys s

views.nl_informal:
If `f` returns the same output and next state for every value of it's second argument, then
`ys : Vector` is ignored, and we can rewrite `mapAccumr₂` into `map`.
views.lean_signature: theorem List.Vector.mapAccumr₂_unused_input_right [Inhabited β] (f : α → β → σ → σ × γ) (h : ∀ a b s, f a default s = f a b s) : mapAccumr₂ f xs ys s = mapAccumr (fun a s => f a default s) xs s

views.nl_informal: `#(WType β)` is the least cardinal `κ` such that `sum (fun a : α ↦ κ ^ #(β a)) ≤ κ`
views.lean_signature: theorem WType.cardinalMk_le_of_le' {κ : Cardinal.{max u v}} (hκ : (sum fun a : α => κ ^ lift.{u} #(β a)) ≤ κ) : #(WType β) ≤ κ

views.nl_informal:
If, for any `a : α`, `β a` is finite, then the cardinality of `WType β`
is at most the maximum of the cardinality of `α` and `ℵ₀`
views.lean_signature: theorem WType.cardinalMk_le_max_aleph0_of_finite' [∀ a, Finite (β a)] : #(WType β) ≤ max (lift.{v} #α) ℵ₀

views.nl_informal: `#(WType β)` is the least cardinal `κ` such that `sum (fun a : α ↦ κ ^ #(β a)) ≤ κ`
views.lean_signature: theorem WType.cardinalMk_le_of_le {κ : Cardinal.{u}} (hκ : (sum fun a : α => κ ^ #(β a)) ≤ κ) : #(WType β) ≤ κ

views.nl_informal:
If, for any `a : α`, `β a` is finite, then the cardinality of `WType β`
is at most the maximum of the cardinality of `α` and `ℵ₀`
views.lean_signature: theorem WType.cardinalMk_le_max_aleph0_of_finite [∀ a, Finite (β a)] : #(WType β) ≤ max #α ℵ₀

views.nl_informal: We have that `ringChar (ZMod n) = n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.ringChar_zmod_n (n : ℕ) : ringChar (ZMod n) = n

views.nl_informal: `-1 : ZMod n` lifts to `n - 1 : R`. This avoids the characteristic assumption in `cast_neg`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.cast_neg_one {R : Type*} [Ring R] (n : ℕ) : cast (-1 : ZMod n) = (n - 1 : R)

views.nl_informal: Any ring homomorphism into `ZMod n` has a right inverse.
views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.ringHom_rightInverse [NonAssocRing R] (f : R →+* ZMod n) : Function.RightInverse (cast : ZMod n → R) f

views.nl_informal: Any ring homomorphism into `ZMod n` is surjective.
views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.ringHom_surjective [NonAssocRing R] (f : R →+* ZMod n) : Function.Surjective f

views.nl_informal:
The range of `(m * · + k)` on natural numbers is the set of elements `≥ k` in the
residue class of `k` mod `m`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.range_mul_add (m k : ℕ) : Set.range (fun n : ℕ ↦ m * n + k) = {n : ℕ | (n : ZMod m) = k ∧ k ≤ n}

views.nl_informal:
If `p` is a prime and `a` is an integer, then `a : ZMod p` is zero if and only if
`gcd a p ≠ 1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.eq_zero_iff_gcd_ne_one {a : ℤ} {p : ℕ} [pp : Fact p.Prime] : (a : ZMod p) = 0 ↔ a.gcd p ≠ 1

views.nl_informal: If an integer `a` and a prime `p` satisfy `gcd a p = 1`, then `a : ZMod p` is nonzero.
views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.ne_zero_of_gcd_eq_one {a : ℤ} {p : ℕ} (pp : p.Prime) (h : a.gcd p = 1) : (a : ZMod p) ≠ 0

views.nl_informal: If an integer `a` and a prime `p` satisfy `gcd a p ≠ 1`, then `a : ZMod p` is zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.eq_zero_of_gcd_ne_one {a : ℤ} {p : ℕ} (pp : p.Prime) (h : a.gcd p ≠ 1) : (a : ZMod p) = 0

views.nl_informal:
`unitsMap_val` shows that coercing from `(ZMod m)ˣ` to `ZMod n` gives the same result
when going via `(ZMod n)ˣ` and `ZMod m`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.unitsMap_val (h : n ∣ m) (a : (ZMod m)ˣ) : ↑(unitsMap h a) = ((a : ZMod m).cast : ZMod n)

views.nl_informal: Any element of `ZMod N` has the form `u * d` where `u` is a unit and `d` is a divisor of `N`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.eq_unit_mul_divisor {N : ℕ} (a : ZMod N) : ∃ d : ℕ, d ∣ N ∧ ∃ (u : ZMod N), IsUnit u ∧ a = u * d

views.nl_informal: An identity partial homeomorphism belongs to the analytic groupoid.
views.lean_signature: theorem ofSet_mem_analyticGroupoid {s : Set H} (hs : IsOpen s) : PartialHomeomorph.ofSet s hs ∈ analyticGroupoid I

views.nl_informal:
The composition of a partial homeomorphism from `H` to `M` and its inverse belongs to
the analytic groupoid.
views.lean_signature: theorem symm_trans_mem_analyticGroupoid (e : PartialHomeomorph M H) : e.symm.trans e ∈ analyticGroupoid I

views.nl_informal: `f ∈ analyticGroupoid` iff it and its inverse are analytic within `range I`.
views.lean_signature: theorem mem_analyticGroupoid {I : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 E H} {f : PartialHomeomorph H H} : f ∈ analyticGroupoid I ↔ AnalyticOn 𝕜 (I ∘ f ∘ I.symm) (I.symm ⁻¹' f.source ∩ range I) ∧ AnalyticOn 𝕜 (I ∘ f.symm ∘ I.symm) (I.symm ⁻¹' f.target ∩ range I)

views.nl_informal:
The analytic groupoid on a boundaryless charted space modeled on a complete vector space
consists of the partial homeomorphisms which are analytic and have analytic inverse.

views.nl_informal:
If `x` is almost a root of `P` in the sense that `P(x)` is nilpotent (and `P'(x)` is a
unit) then we may write `x` as a sum `x = n + r` where `n` is nilpotent and `r` is a root of `P`.
Moreover, `n` and `r` are unique.

This can be used to prove the Jordan-Chevalley decomposition of linear endomorphims.
views.lean_signature: theorem Polynomial.existsUnique_nilpotent_sub_and_aeval_eq_zero (h : IsNilpotent (aeval x P)) (h' : IsUnit (aeval x <| derivative P)) : ∃! r, IsNilpotent (x - r) ∧ aeval r P = 0

views.nl_informal:
An element `y` is in the ω-limit set of `s` w.r.t. `f` if the
preimages of an arbitrary neighbourhood of `y` frequently
(w.r.t. `f`) intersects of `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem mem_omegaLimit_iff_frequently (y : β) : y ∈ ω f ϕ s ↔ ∀ n ∈ 𝓝 y, ∃ᶠ t in f, (s ∩ ϕ t ⁻¹' n).Nonempty

views.nl_informal:
An element `y` is in the ω-limit set of `s` w.r.t. `f` if the
forward images of `s` frequently (w.r.t. `f`) intersect arbitrary
neighbourhoods of `y`.
views.lean_signature: theorem mem_omegaLimit_iff_frequently₂ (y : β) : y ∈ ω f ϕ s ↔ ∀ n ∈ 𝓝 y, ∃ᶠ t in f, (ϕ t '' s ∩ n).Nonempty

views.nl_informal:
An element `y` is in the ω-limit of `x` w.r.t. `f` if the forward
images of `x` frequently (w.r.t. `f`) falls within an arbitrary
neighbourhood of `y`.
views.lean_signature: theorem mem_omegaLimit_singleton_iff_map_cluster_point (x : α) (y : β) : y ∈ ω f ϕ {x} ↔ MapClusterPt y f fun t ↦ ϕ t x

views.nl_informal:
A set is eventually carried into any open neighbourhood of its ω-limit:
if `c` is a compact set such that `closure {ϕ t x | t ∈ v, x ∈ s} ⊆ c` for some `v ∈ f`
and `n` is an open neighbourhood of `ω f ϕ s`, then for some `u ∈ f` we have
`closure {ϕ t x | t ∈ u, x ∈ s} ⊆ n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem eventually_closure_subset_of_isCompact_absorbing_of_isOpen_of_omegaLimit_subset' {c : Set β} (hc₁ : IsCompact c) (hc₂ : ∃ v ∈ f, closure (image2 ϕ v s) ⊆ c) {n : Set β} (hn₁ : IsOpen n) (hn₂ : ω f ϕ s ⊆ n) : ∃ u ∈ f, closure (image2 ϕ u s) ⊆ n

views.nl_informal:
A set is eventually carried into any open neighbourhood of its ω-limit:
if `c` is a compact set such that `closure {ϕ t x | t ∈ v, x ∈ s} ⊆ c` for some `v ∈ f`
and `n` is an open neighbourhood of `ω f ϕ s`, then for some `u ∈ f` we have
`closure {ϕ t x | t ∈ u, x ∈ s} ⊆ n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem eventually_closure_subset_of_isCompact_absorbing_of_isOpen_of_omegaLimit_subset [T2Space β] {c : Set β} (hc₁ : IsCompact c) (hc₂ : ∀ᶠ t in f, MapsTo (ϕ t) s c) {n : Set β} (hn₁ : IsOpen n) (hn₂ : ω f ϕ s ⊆ n) : ∃ u ∈ f, closure (image2 ϕ u s) ⊆ n

views.lean_signature: theorem nonempty_omegaLimit_of_isCompact_absorbing [NeBot f] {c : Set β} (hc₁ : IsCompact c) (hc₂ : ∃ v ∈ f, closure (image2 ϕ v s) ⊆ c) (hs : s.Nonempty) : (ω f ϕ s).Nonempty

views.nl_informal: the ω-limit of a forward image of `s` is the same as the ω-limit of `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Flow.omegaLimit_image_eq (hf : ∀ t, Tendsto (· + t) f f) (t : τ) : ω f ϕ (ϕ t '' s) = ω f ϕ s

views.nl_informal:
Birkhoff average is "almost invariant" under `f`:
the difference between `birkhoffAverage R f g n (f x)` and `birkhoffAverage R f g n x`
is equal to `(n : R)⁻¹ • (g (f^[n] x) - g x)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem birkhoffAverage_apply_sub_birkhoffAverage {α M : Type*} (R : Type*) [DivisionRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (f : α → α) (g : α → M) (n : ℕ) (x : α) : birkhoffAverage R f g n (f x) - birkhoffAverage R f g n x = (n : R)⁻¹ • (g (f^[n] x) - g x)

views.nl_informal:
Birkhoff sum is "almost invariant" under `f`:
the difference between `birkhoffSum f g n (f x)` and `birkhoffSum f g n x`
is equal to `g (f^[n] x) - g x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem birkhoffSum_apply_sub_birkhoffSum (f : α → α) (g : α → G) (n : ℕ) (x : α) : birkhoffSum f g n (f x) - birkhoffSum f g n x = g (f^[n] x) - g x

views.nl_informal:
The Birkhoff averages of a function `g` over the orbit of a fixed point `x` of `f`
tend to `g x` as `N → ∞`. In fact, they are equal to `g x` for all `N ≠ 0`,
see `Function.IsFixedPt.birkhoffAverage_eq`.

TODO: add a version for a periodic orbit.

views.nl_informal:
If a function `g` is bounded along the positive orbit of `x` under `f`,
then the difference between Birkhoff averages of `g`
along the orbit of `f x` and along the orbit of `x`
tends to zero.

See also `tendsto_birkhoffAverage_apply_sub_birkhoffAverage'`.
views.lean_signature: theorem tendsto_birkhoffAverage_apply_sub_birkhoffAverage {f : α → α} {g : α → E} {x : α} (h : Bornology.IsBounded (range (g <| f^[·] x))) : Tendsto (fun n ↦ birkhoffAverage 𝕜 f g n (f x) - birkhoffAverage 𝕜 f g n x) atTop (𝓝 0)

views.nl_informal:
If a function `g` is bounded,
then the difference between Birkhoff averages of `g`
along the orbit of `f x` and along the orbit of `x`
tends to zero.

See also `tendsto_birkhoffAverage_apply_sub_birkhoffAverage`.
views.lean_signature: theorem tendsto_birkhoffAverage_apply_sub_birkhoffAverage' {g : α → E} (h : Bornology.IsBounded (range g)) (f : α → α) (x : α) : Tendsto (fun n ↦ birkhoffAverage 𝕜 f g n (f x) - birkhoffAverage 𝕜 f g n x) atTop (𝓝 0)

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is a non-strictly contracting map (i.e., it is Lipschitz with constant `1`)
and `g` is a uniformly continuous, then the Birkhoff averages of `g` along orbits of `f`
is a uniformly equicontinuous family of functions.
views.lean_signature: theorem uniformEquicontinuous_birkhoffAverage (hf : LipschitzWith 1 f) (hg : UniformContinuous g) : UniformEquicontinuous (birkhoffAverage 𝕜 f g)

views.nl_informal:
If `f : X → X` is a non-strictly contracting map (i.e., it is Lipschitz with constant `1`),
`g : X → E` is a uniformly continuous, and `l : X → E` is a continuous function,
then the set of points `x`
such that the Birkhoff average of `g` along the orbit of `x` tends to `l x`
is a closed set.
views.lean_signature: theorem isClosed_setOf_tendsto_birkhoffAverage (hf : LipschitzWith 1 f) (hg : UniformContinuous g) (hl : Continuous l) : IsClosed {x | Tendsto (birkhoffAverage 𝕜 f g · x) atTop (𝓝 (l x))}

views.nl_informal:
For any `x : ℝ` the sequence $\frac{f^n(x)-x}{n}$ tends to the translation number of `f`.
In particular, this limit does not depend on `x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CircleDeg1Lift.tendsto_translationNumber (x : ℝ) : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => ((f ^ n) x - x) / n) atTop (𝓝 <| τ f)

views.nl_informal:
If `f x - x` is an integer number `m` for some point `x`, then `τ f = m`.
On the circle this means that a map with a fixed point has rotation number zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem CircleDeg1Lift.translationNumber_of_eq_add_int {x : ℝ} {m : ℤ} (h : f x = x + m) : τ f = m

views.nl_informal:
If `f^n x - x`, `n > 0`, is an integer number `m` for some point `x`, then
`τ f = m / n`. On the circle this means that a map with a periodic orbit has
a rational rotation number.
views.lean_signature: theorem CircleDeg1Lift.translationNumber_of_map_pow_eq_add_int {x : ℝ} {n : ℕ} {m : ℤ} (h : (f ^ n) x = x + m) (hn : 0 < n) : τ f = m / n

views.nl_informal:
If a predicate depends only on `f x - x` and holds for all `0 ≤ x ≤ 1`,
then it holds for all `x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CircleDeg1Lift.forall_map_sub_of_Icc (P : ℝ → Prop) (h : ∀ x ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, P (f x - x)) (x : ℝ) : P (f x - x)

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is a continuous monotone map `ℝ → ℝ`, `f (x + 1) = f x + 1`, then there exists `x`
such that `f x = x + τ f`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CircleDeg1Lift.exists_eq_add_translationNumber (hf : Continuous f) : ∃ x, f x = x + τ f

views.nl_informal:
Consider two actions `f₁ f₂ : G →* CircleDeg1Lift` of a group on the real line by lifts of
orientation preserving circle homeomorphisms. Suppose that for each `g : G` the homeomorphisms
`f₁ g` and `f₂ g` have equal rotation numbers. Then there exists `F : CircleDeg1Lift` such that
`F * f₁ g = f₂ g * F` for all `g : G`.

This is a version of Proposition 5.4 from [Étienne Ghys, Groupes d'homeomorphismes du cercle et
cohomologie bornee][ghys87:groupes].
views.lean_signature: theorem CircleDeg1Lift.semiconj_of_group_action_of_forall_translationNumber_eq {G : Type*} [Group G] (f₁ f₂ : G →* CircleDeg1Lift) (h : ∀ g, τ (f₁ g) = τ (f₂ g)) : ∃ F : CircleDeg1Lift, ∀ g, Semiconj F (f₁ g) (f₂ g)

views.nl_informal:
If two lifts of circle homeomorphisms have the same translation number, then they are

to assume that `f₁` and `f₂` are homeomorphisms.
views.lean_signature: theorem CircleDeg1Lift.units_semiconj_of_translationNumber_eq {f₁ f₂ : CircleDeg1Liftˣ} (h : τ f₁ = τ f₂) : ∃ F : CircleDeg1Lift, Semiconj F f₁ f₂

views.nl_informal:
If two lifts of circle homeomorphisms have the same translation number, then they are
semiconjugate by a `CircleDeg1Lift`. This version uses assumptions `IsUnit f₁` and `IsUnit f₂`
to assume that `f₁` and `f₂` are homeomorphisms.
views.lean_signature: theorem CircleDeg1Lift.semiconj_of_isUnit_of_translationNumber_eq {f₁ f₂ : CircleDeg1Lift} (h₁ : IsUnit f₁) (h₂ : IsUnit f₂) (h : τ f₁ = τ f₂) : ∃ F : CircleDeg1Lift, Semiconj F f₁ f₂

views.nl_informal:
If two lifts of circle homeomorphisms have the same translation number, then they are

views.nl_informal: A self-map preserving a finite measure is conservative.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.MeasurePreserving.conservative [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (h : MeasurePreserving f μ μ) : Conservative f μ

views.nl_informal: The identity map is conservative w.r.t. any measure.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.Conservative.id (μ : Measure α) : Conservative id μ

views.nl_informal:
Restriction of a conservative system to an invariant set is a conservative system,
formulated in terms of the restriction of the measure.

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is a conservative self-map and `s` is a null measurable set of nonzero measure,
then there exists a point `x ∈ s` that returns to `s` under a non-zero iteration of `f`.

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is a conservative map and `s` is a measurable set of nonzero measure, then
for infinitely many values of `m` a positive measure of points `x ∈ s` returns back to `s`
after `m` iterations of `f`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.Conservative.frequently_measure_inter_ne_zero (hf : Conservative f μ) (hs : NullMeasurableSet s μ) (h0 : μ s ≠ 0) : ∃ᶠ m in atTop, μ (s ∩ f^[m] ⁻¹' s) ≠ 0

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is a conservative map and `s` is a measurable set of nonzero measure, then
for an arbitrarily large `m` a positive measure of points `x ∈ s` returns back to `s`
after `m` iterations of `f`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.Conservative.exists_gt_measure_inter_ne_zero (hf : Conservative f μ) (hs : NullMeasurableSet s μ) (h0 : μ s ≠ 0) (N : ℕ) : ∃ m > N, μ (s ∩ f^[m] ⁻¹' s) ≠ 0

views.nl_informal:
Poincaré recurrence theorem: given a conservative map `f` and a measurable set `s`, the set
of points `x ∈ s` such that `x` does not return to `s` after `≥ n` iterations has measure zero.

views.nl_informal:
Poincaré recurrence theorem: given a conservative map `f` and a measurable set `s`,
almost every point `x ∈ s` returns back to `s` infinitely many times.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.Conservative.ae_mem_imp_frequently_image_mem (hf : Conservative f μ) (hs : NullMeasurableSet s μ) : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, x ∈ s → ∃ᶠ n in atTop, f^[n] x ∈ s

views.nl_informal:
Poincaré recurrence theorem: if `f` is a conservative dynamical system and `s` is a measurable
set, then for `μ`-a.e. `x`, if the orbit of `x` visits `s` at least once, then it visits `s`
infinitely many times.

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is a conservative self-map and `s` is a measurable set of positive measure, then
`ae μ`-frequently we have `x ∈ s` and `s` returns to `s` under infinitely many iterations of `f`.

views.nl_informal:
Poincaré recurrence theorem. Let `f : α → α` be a conservative dynamical system on a topological
space with second countable topology and measurable open sets. Then almost every point `x : α`
is recurrent: it visits every neighborhood `s ∈ 𝓝 x` infinitely many times.

Let `f : α → α` be a (quasi)ergodic map. Let `g : α → X` is a null-measurable function

Let `f : α → α` be a quasi ergodic map.
Let `g : α → X` be a null-measurable function from `α` to a nonempty measurable space

If `g` is a.e.-invariant under `f`, then `g` is a.e. constant.

views.nl_informal:
Let `f : α → α` be an ergodic map.
Let `g : α → X` be a null-measurable function from `α` to a nonempty measurable space
with a countable family of measurable sets separating the points of `X`.
If `g` is a.e.-invariant under `f`, then `g` is a.e. constant.

views.nl_informal:
Let `f : α → α` be a quasi ergodic map.

views.nl_informal:

`U ○ U` and any multiple `m * n` of `m` with controlled cardinality. This lemma is the first step
in a submultiplicative-like property of `coverMincard`, with consequences such as explicit bounds
for the topological entropy (`coverEntropyInfEntourage_le_card_div`) and an equality between
two notions of topological entropy (`coverEntropyInf_eq_coverEntropySup_of_inv`).

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:

it is an algebraic element.
views.lean_signature: theorem mem_algebraicClosure_iff {x : E} : x ∈ algebraicClosure F E ↔ IsAlgebraic F x

views.lean_signature: theorem algebraicClosure.comap_eq_of_algHom (i : E →ₐ[F] K) : (algebraicClosure F K).comap i = algebraicClosure F E

views.nl_informal:
If `i` is an `F`-algebra homomorphism from `E` to `K`, then the image of `algebraicClosure F E`
under the map `i` is contained in `algebraicClosure F K`.
views.lean_signature: theorem algebraicClosure.map_le_of_algHom (i : E →ₐ[F] K) : (algebraicClosure F E).map i ≤ algebraicClosure F K

If `K / E / F` is a field extension tower, such that `K / E` has no non-trivial algebraic
subextensions (this means that it is purely transcendental),
then the image of `algebraicClosure F E` in `K` is equal to `algebraicClosure F K`.
views.lean_signature: theorem algebraicClosure.map_eq_of_algebraicClosure_eq_bot [Algebra E K] [IsScalarTower F E K] (h : algebraicClosure E K = ⊥) : (algebraicClosure F E).map (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom F E K) = algebraicClosure F K

views.nl_informal:
If `i` is an `F`-algebra isomorphism of `E` and `K`, then the image of `algebraicClosure F E`
under the map `i` is equal to `algebraicClosure F K`.
views.lean_signature: theorem algebraicClosure.map_eq_of_algEquiv (i : E ≃ₐ[F] K) : (algebraicClosure F E).map i = algebraicClosure F K

views.nl_informal:

if all of its elements are algebraic over `F`.

views.nl_informal:
An intermediate field of `E / F` is contained in the algebraic closure of `F` in `E`
if it is algebraic over `F`.
views.lean_signature: theorem le_algebraicClosure (L : IntermediateField F E) [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F L] : L ≤ algebraicClosure F E

views.nl_informal:
An intermediate field of `E / F` is contained in the algebraic closure of `F` in `E`
if and only if it is algebraic over `F`.

`F(S) / F` is a algebraic extension if and only if all elements of `S` are
algebraic elements.
views.lean_signature: theorem IntermediateField.isAlgebraic_adjoin_iff_isAlgebraic {S : Set E} : Algebra.IsAlgebraic F (adjoin F S) ↔ ∀ x ∈ S, IsAlgebraic F x

views.nl_informal:
The algebraic closure of `F` in `E` is equal to `E` if and only if `E / F` is
algebraic.
views.lean_signature: theorem algebraicClosure.eq_top_iff : algebraicClosure F E = ⊤ ↔ Algebra.IsAlgebraic F E

views.nl_informal:
If `K / E / F` is a field extension tower, then `algebraicClosure F K` is contained in
`algebraicClosure E K`.
views.lean_signature: theorem algebraicClosure.le_restrictScalars [Algebra E K] [IsScalarTower F E K] : algebraicClosure F K ≤ (algebraicClosure E K).restrictScalars F

views.nl_informal:
If `K / E / F` is a field extension tower, such that `E / F` is algebraic, then
`algebraicClosure F K` is equal to `algebraicClosure E K`.
views.lean_signature: theorem algebraicClosure.eq_restrictScalars_of_isAlgebraic [Algebra E K] [IsScalarTower F E K] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F E] : algebraicClosure F K = (algebraicClosure E K).restrictScalars F

views.nl_informal:
If `K / E / F` is a field extension tower, then `E` adjoin `algebraicClosure F K` is contained
in `algebraicClosure E K`.
views.lean_signature: theorem algebraicClosure.adjoin_le [Algebra E K] [IsScalarTower F E K] : adjoin E (algebraicClosure F K) ≤ algebraicClosure E K

views.nl_informal:
Let `E / F` be a field extension. If a polynomial `p`
splits in `E`, then it splits in the relative algebraic closure of `F` in `E` already.
views.lean_signature: theorem Splits.algebraicClosure {p : F[X]} (h : p.Splits (algebraMap F E)) : p.Splits (algebraMap F (algebraicClosure F E))

views.nl_informal: Any injective polynomial map over an algebraic extension of a finite field is surjective.
views.lean_signature: theorem ax_grothendieck_of_locally_finite {ι K R : Type*} [Field K] [Finite K] [CommRing R] [Finite ι] [Algebra K R] [alg : Algebra.IsAlgebraic K R] (ps : ι → MvPolynomial ι R) (S : Set (ι → R)) (hm : S.MapsTo (fun v i => eval v (ps i)) S) (hinj : S.InjOn (fun v i => eval v (ps i))) : S.SurjOn (fun v i => eval v (ps i)) S

views.nl_informal:
A slight generalization of the **Ax-Grothendieck** theorem

If `K` is an algebraically closed field, `ι` is a finite type, and `S` is a definable subset of
`ι → K`, then any injective polynomial map `S → S`  is also surjective on `S`.

views.nl_informal:
The **Ax-Grothendieck** theorem

If `K` is an algebraically closed field, and `S : Set (ι → K)` is the `zeroLocus` of an ideal
of the multivariable polynomial ring, then any injective polynomial map `S → S`  is also
surjective on `S`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ax_grothendieck_zeroLocus (I : Ideal (MvPolynomial ι K)) (p : ι → MvPolynomial ι K) : let S

views.nl_informal:
A special case of the **Ax-Grothendieck** theorem

Any injective polynomial map `K^n → K^n` is also surjective if `K` is an
algberaically closed field.
views.lean_signature: theorem ax_grothendieck_univ (p : ι → MvPolynomial ι K) : (fun v i => eval v (p i)).Injective → (fun v i => eval v (p i)).Surjective

views.nl_informal: A finite field has prime power cardinality.
views.lean_signature: theorem Fintype.isPrimePow_card_of_field {α} [Fintype α] [Field α] : IsPrimePow ‖α‖

views.nl_informal: A `Fintype` can be given a field structure iff its cardinality is a prime power.
views.lean_signature: theorem Fintype.nonempty_field_iff {α} [Fintype α] : Nonempty (Field α) ↔ IsPrimePow ‖α‖

views.nl_informal: Any infinite type can be endowed a field structure.
views.lean_signature: theorem Infinite.nonempty_field {α : Type u} [Infinite α] : Nonempty (Field α)

views.lean_signature: theorem Field.nonempty_iff {α : Type u} : Nonempty (Field α) ↔ IsPrimePow #α

views.nl_informal:
The **Chevalley–Warning theorem**, finitary version.
Let `(f i)` be a finite family of multivariate polynomials
in finitely many variables (`X s`, `s : σ`) over a finite field of characteristic `p`.
Assume that the sum of the total degrees of the `f i` is less than the cardinality of `σ`.
Then the number of common solutions of the `f i` is divisible by `p`.
views.lean_signature: theorem char_dvd_card_solutions_of_sum_lt {s : Finset ι} {f : ι → MvPolynomial σ K} (h : (∑ i ∈ s, (f i).totalDegree) < Fintype.card σ) : p ∣ Fintype.card { x : σ → K // ∀ i ∈ s, eval x (f i) = 0 }

views.nl_informal:
The **Chevalley–Warning theorem**, `Fintype` version.
Let `(f i)` be a finite family of multivariate polynomials
in finitely many variables (`X s`, `s : σ`) over a finite field of characteristic `p`.
Assume that the sum of the total degrees of the `f i` is less than the cardinality of `σ`.
Then the number of common solutions of the `f i` is divisible by `p`.
views.lean_signature: theorem char_dvd_card_solutions_of_fintype_sum_lt [Fintype ι] {f : ι → MvPolynomial σ K} (h : (∑ i, (f i).totalDegree) < Fintype.card σ) : p ∣ Fintype.card { x : σ → K // ∀ i, eval x (f i) = 0 }

views.nl_informal:
The **Chevalley–Warning theorem**, unary version.
Let `f` be a multivariate polynomial in finitely many variables (`X s`, `s : σ`)
over a finite field of characteristic `p`.
Assume that the total degree of `f` is less than the cardinality of `σ`.
Then the number of solutions of `f` is divisible by `p`.
See `char_dvd_card_solutions_of_sum_lt` for a version that takes a family of polynomials `f i`.
views.lean_signature: theorem char_dvd_card_solutions {f : MvPolynomial σ K} (h : f.totalDegree < Fintype.card σ) : p ∣ Fintype.card { x : σ → K // eval x f = 0 }

views.nl_informal:
The **Chevalley–Warning theorem**, binary version.
Let `f₁`, `f₂` be two multivariate polynomials in finitely many variables (`X s`, `s : σ`) over a
finite field of characteristic `p`.
Assume that the sum of the total degrees of `f₁` and `f₂` is less than the cardinality of `σ`.
Then the number of common solutions of the `f₁` and `f₂` is divisible by `p`.
views.lean_signature: theorem char_dvd_card_solutions_of_add_lt {f₁ f₂ : MvPolynomial σ K} (h : f₁.totalDegree + f₂.totalDegree < Fintype.card σ) : p ∣ Fintype.card { x : σ → K // eval x f₁ = 0 ∧ eval x f₂ = 0 }

views.nl_informal: A chain of lifts has an upper bound.

views.nl_informal:
Given a lift `x` and an integral element `s : E` over `x.carrier` whose conjugates over

views.lean_signature: theorem IntermediateField.Lifts.exists_lift_of_splits' (x : Lifts F E K) {s : E} (h1 : IsIntegral x.carrier s) (h2 : (minpoly x.carrier s).Splits x.emb.toRingHom) : ∃ y, x ≤ y ∧ s ∈ y.carrier

views.nl_informal:
Given an integral element `s : E` over `F` whose `F`-conjugates are all in `K`,
any lift can be extended to one whose carrier contains `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem IntermediateField.Lifts.exists_lift_of_splits (x : Lifts F E K) {s : E} (h1 : IsIntegral F s) (h2 : (minpoly F s).Splits (algebraMap F K)) : ∃ y, x ≤ y ∧ s ∈ y.carrier

views.nl_informal:
Let `K/F` be an algebraic extension of fields and `L` a field in which all the minimal
polynomial over `F` of elements of `K` splits. Then, for `x ∈ K`, the images of `x` by the
`F`-algebra morphisms from `K` to `L` are exactly the roots in `L` of the minimal polynomial
of `x` over `F`.

views.nl_informal:
A module over a division ring is noetherian if and only if
its dimension (as a cardinal) is strictly less than the first infinite cardinal `ℵ₀`.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsNoetherian.iff_rank_lt_aleph0 : IsNoetherian K V ↔ Module.rank K V < ℵ₀

views.nl_informal:
In a noetherian module over a division ring,
if a basis is indexed by a set, that set is finite.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsNoetherian.finite_basis_index {ι : Type*} {s : Set ι} [IsNoetherian K V] (b : Basis s K V) : s.Finite

views.nl_informal: A module over a division ring is noetherian if and only if it is finitely generated.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsNoetherian.iff_fg : IsNoetherian K V ↔ Module.Finite K V

views.nl_informal:
Let $F$ be a field. Let $G$ be a finite group acting faithfully on $F$.
Then $[F : F^G] = |G|$.
views.lean_signature: theorem FixedPoints.finrank_eq_card [Fintype G] [FaithfulSMul G F] : finrank (FixedPoints.subfield G F) F = Fintype.card G

views.lean_signature: theorem FixedPoints.toAlgAut_bijective [Finite G] [FaithfulSMul G F] : Function.Bijective (MulSemiringAction.toAlgAut G (FixedPoints.subfield G F) F)

views.lean_signature: theorem FixedPoints.toAlgAut_surjective [Finite G] : Function.Surjective (MulSemiringAction.toAlgAut G (FixedPoints.subfield G F) F)

views.nl_informal: Composition of `p`-radical ring homomorphisms is also `p`-radical.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsPRadical.trans [IsPRadical i p] [IsPRadical f p] : IsPRadical (f.comp i) p

views.nl_informal:
If `i : K →+* L` is a ring homomorphism of exponential characteristic `p` rings, such that `L`
is perfect, then the `p`-nilradical of `K` is contained in the kernel of `i`.
views.lean_signature: theorem RingHom.pNilradical_le_ker_of_perfectRing [ExpChar L p] [PerfectRing L p] : pNilradical K p ≤ RingHom.ker i

views.nl_informal:
If `i : K →+* L` is `p`-radical, then for any ring `M` of exponential charactistic `p` whose
`p`-nilradical is zero, the map `(L →+* M) → (K →+* M)` induced by `i` is injective.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsPRadical.injective_comp_of_pNilradical_eq_bot [IsPRadical i p] (h : pNilradical M p = ⊥) : Function.Injective fun f : L →+* M ↦ f.comp i

views.nl_informal:
If `i : K →+* L` is `p`-radical, then for any reduced ring `M` of exponential charactistic `p`,
the map `(L →+* M) → (K →+* M)` induced by `i` is injective.
A special case of `IsPRadical.injective_comp_of_pNilradical_eq_bot`
and a generalization of `IsPurelyInseparable.injective_comp_algebraMap`.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsPRadical.injective_comp [IsPRadical i p] [IsReduced M] : Function.Injective fun f : L →+* M ↦ f.comp i

views.nl_informal:
If `i : K →+* L` is `p`-radical, then for any perfect ring `M` of exponential charactistic `p`,
the map `(L →+* M) → (K →+* M)` induced by `i` is injective.
A special case of `IsPRadical.injective_comp_of_pNilradical_eq_bot`.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsPRadical.injective_comp_of_perfect [IsPRadical i p] [PerfectRing M p] : Function.Injective fun f : L →+* M ↦ f.comp i

views.nl_informal:
If `i : K →+* L` and `j : K →+* M` are ring homomorphisms of characteristic `p` rings, such that

views.lean_signature: theorem PerfectRing.liftAux_apply (x : L) (n : ℕ) (y : K) (h : i y = x ^ p ^ n) : liftAux i j p x = (iterateFrobeniusEquiv M p n).symm (j y)

views.nl_informal: If `L / K` is a `p`-radical field extension, then it is purely inseparable.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsPRadical.isPurelyInseparable [IsPRadical (algebraMap K L) p] : IsPurelyInseparable K L

views.nl_informal:
Every separable polynomial splits in the field extension `f : k →+* K` if `K` is
separably closed.

views.lean_signature: theorem IsSepClosed.splits_codomain [IsSepClosed K] {f : k →+* K} (p : k[X]) (h : p.Separable) : p.Splits f

views.nl_informal:
Every separable polynomial splits in the field extension `f : k →+* K` if `k` is
separably closed.

See also `IsSepClosed.splits_codomain` for the case where `k` is separably closed.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsSepClosed.splits_domain [IsSepClosed k] {f : k →+* K} (p : k[X]) (h : p.Separable) : p.Splits f

views.nl_informal:
If `n ≥ 2` equals zero in a separably closed field `k`, `b ≠ 0`,
then there exists `x` in `k` such that `a * x ^ n + b * x + c = 0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsSepClosed.exists_root_C_mul_X_pow_add_C_mul_X_add_C [IsSepClosed k] {n : ℕ} (a b c : k) (hn : (n : k) = 0) (hn' : 2 ≤ n) (hb : b ≠ 0) : ∃ x, a * x ^ n + b * x + c = 0

views.nl_informal:
If a separably closed field `k` is of characteristic `p`, `n ≥ 2` is such that `p ∣ n`, `b ≠ 0`,
then there exists `x` in `k` such that `a * x ^ n + b * x + c = 0`.

views.nl_informal:
If `k` is separably closed, `K / k` is a field extension, `L / k` is an intermediate field
which is separable, then `L` is equal to `k`. A corollary of `IsSepClosed.algebraMap_surjective`.
views.lean_signature: theorem IntermediateField.eq_bot_of_isSepClosed_of_isSeparable [IsSepClosed k] [Algebra k K] (L : IntermediateField k K) [Algebra.IsSeparable k L] : L = ⊥

views.nl_informal:
If `D` is a purely inseparable extension of `k` with characteristic `p`,
then for every element `a` of `D`, there exists a natural number `n`
such that `a ^ (p ^ n)` is contained in `k`.
views.lean_signature: theorem JacobsonNoether.exists_pow_mem_center_of_inseparable (p : ℕ) [hchar : ExpChar D p] (a : D) (hinsep : ∀ x : D, IsSeparable k x → x ∈ k) : ∃ n, a ^ (p ^ n) ∈ k

views.nl_informal:
If `D` is a purely inseparable extension of `k` with characteristic `p`,
then for every element `a` of `D \ k`, there exists a natural number `n`
**greater than 0** such that `a ^ (p ^ n)` is contained in `k`.
views.lean_signature: theorem JacobsonNoether.exists_pow_mem_center_of_inseparable' (p : ℕ) [ExpChar D p] {a : D} (ha : a ∉ k) (hinsep : ∀ x : D, IsSeparable k x → x ∈ k) : ∃ n, 1 ≤ n ∧ a ^ (p ^ n) ∈ k

views.nl_informal:
If `D` is a purely inseparable extension of `k` of characteristic `p`,
then for every element `a` of `D \ k`, there exists a natural number `m`
greater than 0 such that `(a * x - x * a) ^ n = 0` (as linear maps) for
every `n` greater than `(p ^ m)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem JacobsonNoether.exist_pow_eq_zero_of_le (p : ℕ) [hchar : ExpChar D p] {a : D} (ha : a ∉ k) (hinsep : ∀ x : D, IsSeparable k x → x ∈ k): ∃ m, 1 ≤ m ∧ ∀ n, p ^ m ≤ n → (ad k D a)^[n] = 0

views.nl_informal:
Jacobson-Noether theorem: For a non-commutative division algebra
`D` that is algebraic over its center `k`, there exists an element
`x` of `D \ k` that is separable over `k`.
views.lean_signature: theorem JacobsonNoether.exists_separable_and_not_isCentral (H : k ≠ (⊤ : Subring D)) : ∃ x : D, x ∉ k ∧ IsSeparable k x

views.nl_informal:
Jacobson-Noether theorem: For a non-commutative division algebra `D`
that is algebraic over a field `L`, if the center of

that is separable over `L`.

views.nl_informal: Mapping intermediate fields along the identity does not change them
views.lean_signature: theorem IntermediateField.map_id {K L : Type*} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L] (E : IntermediateField K L) : E.map (AlgHom.id K L) = E

views.nl_informal: For a field extension `L/K`, the intermediate field `K` is finite-dimensional over `K`
views.lean_signature: theorem IntermediateField.finiteDimensional_bot (K L : Type*) [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L] : FiniteDimensional K (⊥ : IntermediateField K L)

views.nl_informal: This lemma says that `Gal(L/K) = L ≃ₐ[K] L`

views.nl_informal: If `L/K` is a field extension, then we have `Gal(L/K) ∈ fixedByFinite K L`
views.lean_signature: theorem top_fixedByFinite {K L : Type*} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L] : ⊤ ∈ fixedByFinite K L

views.nl_informal:
If `E1` and `E2` are finite-dimensional intermediate fields, then so is their compositum.
This rephrases a result already in mathlib so that it is compatible with our type classes
views.lean_signature: theorem finiteDimensional_sup {K L : Type*} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L] (E1 E2 : IntermediateField K L) (_ : FiniteDimensional K E1) (_ : FiniteDimensional K E2) : FiniteDimensional K (↥(E1 ⊔ E2))

views.nl_informal: An element of `L ≃ₐ[K] L` is in `Gal(L/E)` if and only if it fixes every element of `E`.
views.lean_signature: theorem IntermediateField.mem_fixingSubgroup_iff {K L : Type*} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L] (E : IntermediateField K L) (σ : L ≃ₐ[K] L) : σ ∈ E.fixingSubgroup ↔ ∀ x : L, x ∈ E → σ x = x

views.nl_informal: The map `E ↦ Gal(L/E)` is inclusion-reversing
views.lean_signature: theorem IntermediateField.fixingSubgroup.antimono {K L : Type*} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L] {E1 E2 : IntermediateField K L} (h12 : E1 ≤ E2) : E2.fixingSubgroup ≤ E1.fixingSubgroup

views.nl_informal:
A subset of `L ≃ₐ[K] L` is a member of `galBasis K L` if and only if it is the underlying set
of `Gal(L/E)` for some finite subextension `E/K`.
views.lean_signature: theorem mem_galBasis_iff (K L : Type*) [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L] (U : Set (L ≃ₐ[K] L)) : U ∈ galBasis K L ↔ U ∈ (fun g => g.carrier) '' fixedByFinite K L

views.nl_informal:
Let `L/E/K` be a tower of fields with `E/K` finite. Then `Gal(L/E)` is an open subgroup of
`L ≃ₐ[K] L`.
views.lean_signature: theorem IntermediateField.fixingSubgroup_isOpen {K L : Type*} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L] (E : IntermediateField K L) [FiniteDimensional K E] : IsOpen (E.fixingSubgroup : Set (L ≃ₐ[K] L))

views.nl_informal:
Given a tower of fields `L/E/K`, with `E/K` finite, the subgroup `Gal(L/E) ≤ L ≃ₐ[K] L` is
closed.
views.lean_signature: theorem IntermediateField.fixingSubgroup_isClosed {K L : Type*} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L] (E : IntermediateField K L) [FiniteDimensional K E] : IsClosed (E.fixingSubgroup : Set (L ≃ₐ[K] L))

views.nl_informal: If `L/K` is an algebraic extension, then the Krull topology on `L ≃ₐ[K] L` is Hausdorff.
views.lean_signature: theorem krullTopology_t2 {K L : Type*} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L] [Algebra.IsIntegral K L] : T2Space (L ≃ₐ[K] L)

views.nl_informal:
If `L/K` is an algebraic field extension, then the Krull topology on `L ≃ₐ[K] L` is
totally disconnected.
views.lean_signature: theorem krullTopology_isTotallySeparated {K L : Type*} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L] [Algebra.IsIntegral K L] : IsTotallySeparated (Set.univ : Set (L ≃ₐ[K] L))

views.nl_informal:
If `K / E / k` is a field extension tower with `E / k` normal,
`L` is an intermediate field of `E / k`, then the fixing subgroup of `L` viewed as an
intermediate field of `K / k` is equal to the preimage of the fixing subgroup of `L` viewed as an
intermediate field of `E / k` under the natural map `Aut(K / k) → Aut(E / k)`
(`AlgEquiv.restrictNormalHom`).

views.nl_informal:
If `K / E / k` is a field extension tower with `E / k` and `K / k` normal,
`L` is an intermediate field of `E / k`, then the index of the fixing subgroup of `L` viewed as an
intermediate field of `K / k` is equal to the index of the fixing subgroup of `L` viewed as an
intermediate field of `E / k`.
views.lean_signature: theorem IntermediateField.map_fixingSubgroup_index [Normal k E] [Normal k K] : (L.map (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k E K)).fixingSubgroup.index = L.fixingSubgroup.index

views.nl_informal:
If `K / k` is a Galois extension, `L` is an intermediate field of `K / k`, then `[L : k]`
as a natural number is equal to the index of the fixing subgroup of `L`.
views.lean_signature: theorem IntermediateField.finrank_eq_fixingSubgroup_index (L : IntermediateField k K) [IsGalois k K] : Module.finrank k L = L.fixingSubgroup.index

views.nl_informal:
If `L/K` is a cyclic extension of degree `n`, and `K` contains all `n`-th roots of unity,
then `L = K[α]` for some `α ^ n ∈ K`.
views.lean_signature: theorem exists_root_adjoin_eq_top_of_isCyclic [IsGalois K L] [IsCyclic (L ≃ₐ[K] L)] : ∃ (α : L), α ^ (finrank K L) ∈ Set.range (algebraMap K L) ∧ K⟮α⟯ = ⊤

views.nl_informal:
Suppose `L/K` is a finite extension of dimension `n`, and `K` contains all `n`-th roots of unity.

`L` is a splitting field of some irreducible polynomial of the form `Xⁿ - a : K[X]` iff

If a non-zero polynomial over `F` splits in `K`, then it has no repeated roots on `K`
if and only if it is separable.
views.lean_signature: theorem Polynomial.nodup_aroots_iff_of_splits [Algebra F K] {f : F[X]} (hf : f ≠ 0) (h : f.Splits (algebraMap F K)) : (f.aroots K).Nodup ↔ f.Separable

views.nl_informal:
If the minimal polynomial of `x : K` over `F` is separable, then `x` is integral over `F`,
because the minimal polynomial of a non-integral element is `0`, which is not separable.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsSeparable.isIntegral {x : K} (h : IsSeparable F x) : IsIntegral F x

views.nl_informal: Transfer `IsSeparable` across an `AlgEquiv`.
views.lean_signature: theorem AlgEquiv.isSeparable_iff {x : K} : IsSeparable F (e x) ↔ IsSeparable F x

views.nl_informal: Transfer `Algebra.IsSeparable` across an `AlgEquiv`.
views.lean_signature: theorem AlgEquiv.Algebra.isSeparable [Algebra.IsSeparable F K] : Algebra.IsSeparable F E

views.nl_informal:
If `E / L / F` is a scalar tower and `x : E` is separable over `F`, then it's also separable
over `L`.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsSeparable.tower_top {x : E} (h : IsSeparable F x) : IsSeparable L x

views.nl_informal:
If `E / K / F` is an extension tower, `E` is separable over `F`, then it's also separable
over `K`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Algebra.isSeparable_tower_top_of_isSeparable [Algebra.IsSeparable F E] : Algebra.IsSeparable L E

views.nl_informal:
If `E / K / F` is a scalar tower and `algebraMap K E x` is separable over `F`, then `x` is
also separable over `F`.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsSeparable.tower_bot {x : K} (h : IsSeparable F (algebraMap K E x)) : IsSeparable F x

views.nl_informal:
An element is contained in the separable closure of `F` in `E` if and only if
it is a separable element.
views.lean_signature: theorem mem_separableClosure_iff {x : E} : x ∈ separableClosure F E ↔ IsSeparable F x

views.nl_informal:
If `i` is an `F`-algebra homomorphism from `E` to `K`, then `i x` is contained in
`separableClosure F K` if and only if `x` is contained in `separableClosure F E`.
views.lean_signature: theorem map_mem_separableClosure_iff (i : E →ₐ[F] K) {x : E} : i x ∈ separableClosure F K ↔ x ∈ separableClosure F E

views.nl_informal:
If `i` is an `F`-algebra homomorphism from `E` to `K`, then the preimage of
`separableClosure F K` under the map `i` is equal to `separableClosure F E`.
views.lean_signature: theorem separableClosure.comap_eq_of_algHom (i : E →ₐ[F] K) : (separableClosure F K).comap i = separableClosure F E

views.nl_informal:
If `i` is an `F`-algebra homomorphism from `E` to `K`, then the image of `separableClosure F E`
under the map `i` is contained in `separableClosure F K`.
views.lean_signature: theorem separableClosure.map_le_of_algHom (i : E →ₐ[F] K) : (separableClosure F E).map i ≤ separableClosure F K

views.nl_informal:
If `K / E / F` is a field extension tower, such that `K / E` has no non-trivial separable
subextensions (when `K / E` is algebraic, this means that it is purely inseparable),
then the image of `separableClosure F E` in `K` is equal to `separableClosure F K`.
views.lean_signature: theorem separableClosure.map_eq_of_separableClosure_eq_bot [Algebra E K] [IsScalarTower F E K] (h : separableClosure E K = ⊥) : (separableClosure F E).map (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom F E K) = separableClosure F K

views.nl_informal:
If `i` is an `F`-algebra isomorphism of `E` and `K`, then the image of `separableClosure F E`
under the map `i` is equal to `separableClosure F K`.
views.lean_signature: theorem separableClosure.map_eq_of_algEquiv (i : E ≃ₐ[F] K) : (separableClosure F E).map i = separableClosure F K

views.nl_informal:
An intermediate field of `E / F` is contained in the separable closure of `F` in `E`
if all of its elements are separable over `F`.
views.lean_signature: theorem le_separableClosure' {L : IntermediateField F E} (hs : ∀ x : L, IsSeparable F x) : L ≤ separableClosure F E

views.nl_informal:
An intermediate field of `E / F` is contained in the separable closure of `F` in `E`
if it is separable over `F`.
views.lean_signature: theorem le_separableClosure (L : IntermediateField F E) [Algebra.IsSeparable F L] : L ≤ separableClosure F E

views.nl_informal:
An intermediate field of `E / F` is contained in the separable closure of `F` in `E`
if and only if it is separable over `F`.
views.lean_signature: theorem le_separableClosure_iff (L : IntermediateField F E) : L ≤ separableClosure F E ↔ Algebra.IsSeparable F L

views.nl_informal: The separable closure in `E` of the separable closure of `F` in `E` is equal to itself.
views.lean_signature: theorem separableClosure.separableClosure_eq_bot : separableClosure (separableClosure F E) E = ⊥

views.nl_informal: The normal closure in `E/F` of the separable closure of `F` in `E` is equal to itself.
views.lean_signature: theorem separableClosure.normalClosure_eq_self : normalClosure F (separableClosure F E) E = separableClosure F E

views.nl_informal:
If `E / F` is a field extension and `E` is separably closed, then the separable closure
of `F` in `E` is equal to `F` if and only if `F` is separably closed.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsSepClosed.separableClosure_eq_bot_iff [IsSepClosed E] : separableClosure F E = ⊥ ↔ IsSepClosed F

views.nl_informal:
`F(S) / F` is a separable extension if and only if all elements of `S` are
separable elements.
views.lean_signature: theorem IntermediateField.isSeparable_adjoin_iff_isSeparable {S : Set E} : Algebra.IsSeparable F (adjoin F S) ↔ ∀ x ∈ S, IsSeparable F x

views.nl_informal:
The separable closure of `F` in `E` is equal to `E` if and only if `E / F` is
separable.
views.lean_signature: theorem separableClosure.eq_top_iff : separableClosure F E = ⊤ ↔ Algebra.IsSeparable F E

views.nl_informal:
If `K / E / F` is a field extension tower, then `separableClosure F K` is contained in
`separableClosure E K`.
views.lean_signature: theorem separableClosure.le_restrictScalars [Algebra E K] [IsScalarTower F E K] : separableClosure F K ≤ (separableClosure E K).restrictScalars F

views.nl_informal:
If `K / E / F` is a field extension tower, such that `E / F` is separable, then
`separableClosure F K` is equal to `separableClosure E K`.
views.lean_signature: theorem separableClosure.eq_restrictScalars_of_isSeparable [Algebra E K] [IsScalarTower F E K] [Algebra.IsSeparable F E] : separableClosure F K = (separableClosure E K).restrictScalars F

views.nl_informal:
If `K / E / F` is a field extension tower, then `E` adjoin `separableClosure F K` is contained
in `separableClosure E K`.
views.lean_signature: theorem separableClosure.adjoin_le [Algebra E K] [IsScalarTower F E K] : adjoin E (separableClosure F K) ≤ separableClosure E K

views.nl_informal:
If `E` and `K` are isomorphic as `F`-algebras, then they have the same
separable degree over `F`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Field.lift_sepDegree_eq_of_equiv (i : E ≃ₐ[F] K) : Cardinal.lift.{w} (sepDegree F E) = Cardinal.lift.{v} (sepDegree F K)

views.nl_informal:
The separable degree multiplied by the inseparable degree is equal
to the (infinite) field extension degree.
views.lean_signature: theorem Field.sepDegree_mul_insepDegree : sepDegree F E * insepDegree F E = Module.rank F E

views.nl_informal:
If `E` and `K` are isomorphic as `F`-algebras, then they have the same
inseparable degree over `F`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Field.lift_insepDegree_eq_of_equiv (i : E ≃ₐ[F] K) : Cardinal.lift.{w} (insepDegree F E) = Cardinal.lift.{v} (insepDegree F K)

views.nl_informal:
If `E` and `K` are isomorphic as `F`-algebras, then they have the same finite
inseparable degree over `F`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Field.finInsepDegree_eq_of_equiv (i : E ≃ₐ[F] K) : finInsepDegree F E = finInsepDegree F K

views.nl_informal: A separable extension has separable degree equal to degree.
views.lean_signature: theorem Algebra.IsSeparable.sepDegree_eq [Algebra.IsSeparable F E] : sepDegree F E = Module.rank F E

views.nl_informal: A separable extension has inseparable degree one.
views.lean_signature: theorem Algebra.IsSeparable.insepDegree_eq [Algebra.IsSeparable F E] : insepDegree F E = 1

views.nl_informal: A separable extension has finite inseparable degree one.
views.lean_signature: theorem Algebra.IsSeparable.finInsepDegree_eq [Algebra.IsSeparable F E] : finInsepDegree F E = 1

views.nl_informal:
If `E` and `K` are isomorphic as `F`-algebras, then they have the same `Field.finSepDegree`
over `F`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Field.finSepDegree_eq_of_equiv (i : E ≃ₐ[F] K) : finSepDegree F E = finSepDegree F K

views.nl_informal:
The `Field.finSepDegree F E` is equal to the cardinality of `E →ₐ[F] K`
if `E = F(S)` such that every element
`s` of `S` is integral (= algebraic) over `F` and whose minimal polynomial splits in `K`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Field.finSepDegree_eq_of_adjoin_splits {S : Set E} (hS : adjoin F S = ⊤) (hK : ∀ s ∈ S, IsIntegral F s ∧ Splits (algebraMap F K) (minpoly F s)) : finSepDegree F E = Nat.card (E →ₐ[F] K)

views.nl_informal:
The `Field.finSepDegree F E` is equal to the cardinality of `E →ₐ[F] K` as a natural number,
when `E / F` is algebraic and `K / F` is algebraically closed.
views.lean_signature: theorem Field.finSepDegree_eq_of_isAlgClosed [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F E] [IsAlgClosed K] : finSepDegree F E = Nat.card (E →ₐ[F] K)

views.nl_informal:
If the field extension `E / F` is transcendental, then `Field.finSepDegree F E = 0`, which
actually means that `Field.Emb F E` is infinite (see `Field.infinite_emb_of_transcendental`).
views.lean_signature: theorem Field.finSepDegree_eq_zero_of_transcendental [Algebra.Transcendental F E] : finSepDegree F E = 0

views.nl_informal:
If `K / E / F` is a field extension tower, such that `K / E` is algebraic, then their
separable degrees satisfy the tower law
$[E:F]_s [K:E]_s = [K:F]_s$. See also `Module.finrank_mul_finrank`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Field.finSepDegree_mul_finSepDegree_of_isAlgebraic [Algebra E K] [IsScalarTower F E K] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic E K] : finSepDegree F E * finSepDegree E K = finSepDegree F K

views.nl_informal: The separable degree of a polynomial is smaller than its degree.
views.lean_signature: theorem Polynomial.natSepDegree_le_natDegree : f.natSepDegree ≤ f.natDegree

views.nl_informal: A constant polynomial has zero separable degree.
views.lean_signature: theorem Polynomial.natSepDegree_eq_zero (h : f.natDegree = 0) : f.natSepDegree = 0

views.nl_informal: A non-constant polynomial has non-zero separable degree.
views.lean_signature: theorem Polynomial.natSepDegree_ne_zero (h : f.natDegree ≠ 0) : f.natSepDegree ≠ 0

views.nl_informal: A polynomial has zero separable degree if and only if it is constant.
views.lean_signature: theorem Polynomial.natSepDegree_eq_zero_iff : f.natSepDegree = 0 ↔ f.natDegree = 0

views.nl_informal: A polynomial has non-zero separable degree if and only if it is non-constant.
views.lean_signature: theorem Polynomial.natSepDegree_ne_zero_iff : f.natSepDegree ≠ 0 ↔ f.natDegree ≠ 0

views.nl_informal:
The separable degree of a non-zero polynomial is equal to its degree if and only if
it is separable.
views.lean_signature: theorem Polynomial.natSepDegree_eq_natDegree_iff (hf : f ≠ 0) : f.natSepDegree = f.natDegree ↔ f.Separable

views.nl_informal: If a polynomial is separable, then its separable degree is equal to its degree.
views.lean_signature: theorem Polynomial.natSepDegree_eq_natDegree_of_separable (h : f.Separable) : f.natSepDegree = f.natDegree

views.nl_informal:
If a polynomial splits over `E`, then its separable degree is equal to
the number of distinct roots of it over `E`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Polynomial.natSepDegree_eq_of_splits [DecidableEq E] (h : f.Splits (algebraMap F E)) : f.natSepDegree = (f.aroots E).toFinset.card

views.nl_informal:
The separable degree of a polynomial is equal to
the number of distinct roots of it over any algebraically closed field.
views.lean_signature: theorem Polynomial.natSepDegree_eq_of_isAlgClosed [DecidableEq E] [IsAlgClosed E] : f.natSepDegree = (f.aroots E).toFinset.card

views.nl_informal:
If a field `F` is of exponential characteristic `q`, then `Polynomial.expand F (q ^ n) f`
and `f` have the same separable degree.
views.lean_signature: theorem Polynomial.natSepDegree_expand (q : ℕ) [hF : ExpChar F q] {n : ℕ} : (expand F (q ^ n) f).natSepDegree = f.natSepDegree

views.nl_informal:
If `g` is a separable contraction of `f`, then the separable degree of `f` is equal to
the degree of `g`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Polynomial.IsSeparableContraction.natSepDegree_eq {g : Polynomial F} {q : ℕ} [ExpChar F q] (h : IsSeparableContraction q f g) : f.natSepDegree = g.natDegree

views.nl_informal:
If a polynomial has separable contraction, then its separable degree is equal to the degree of
the given separable contraction.
views.lean_signature: theorem Polynomial.HasSeparableContraction.natSepDegree_eq {q : ℕ} [ExpChar F q] (hf : f.HasSeparableContraction q) : f.natSepDegree = hf.degree

views.nl_informal: The separable degree of an irreducible polynomial divides its degree.
views.lean_signature: theorem Irreducible.natSepDegree_dvd_natDegree (h : Irreducible f) : f.natSepDegree ∣ f.natDegree

views.nl_informal:
A monic irreducible polynomial over a field `F` of exponential characteristic `q` has
separable degree one if and only if it is of the form `Polynomial.expand F (q ^ n) (X - C y)`
for some `n : ℕ` and `y : F`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Irreducible.natSepDegree_eq_one_iff_of_monic' (q : ℕ) [ExpChar F q] (hm : f.Monic) (hi : Irreducible f) : f.natSepDegree = 1 ↔ ∃ (n : ℕ) (y : F), f = expand F (q ^ n) (X - C y)

views.nl_informal:
A monic irreducible polynomial over a field `F` of exponential characteristic `q` has
separable degree one if and only if it is of the form `X ^ (q ^ n) - C y`
for some `n : ℕ` and `y : F`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Irreducible.natSepDegree_eq_one_iff_of_monic (q : ℕ) [ExpChar F q] (hm : f.Monic) (hi : Irreducible f) : f.natSepDegree = 1 ↔ ∃ (n : ℕ) (y : F), f = X ^ q ^ n - C y

views.nl_informal:
If a monic polynomial of separable degree one splits, then it is of form `(X - C y) ^ m` for
some non-zero natural number `m` and some element `y` of `F`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Polynomial.Monic.eq_X_sub_C_pow_of_natSepDegree_eq_one_of_splits (hm : f.Monic) (hs : f.Splits (RingHom.id F)) (h : f.natSepDegree = 1) : ∃ (m : ℕ) (y : F), m ≠ 0 ∧ f = (X - C y) ^ m

views.nl_informal:
If a monic irreducible polynomial over a field `F` of exponential characteristic `q` has
separable degree one, then it is of the form `X ^ (q ^ n) - C y` for some natural number `n`,
and some element `y` of `F`, such that either `n = 0` or `y` has no `q`-th root in `F`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Polynomial.Monic.eq_X_pow_char_pow_sub_C_of_natSepDegree_eq_one_of_irreducible (q : ℕ) [ExpChar F q] (hm : f.Monic) (hi : Irreducible f) (h : f.natSepDegree = 1) : ∃ (n : ℕ) (y : F), (n = 0 ∨ y ∉ (frobenius F q).range) ∧ f = X ^ q ^ n - C y

views.nl_informal:
If a monic polynomial over a field `F` of exponential characteristic `q` has separable degree
one, then it is of the form `(X ^ (q ^ n) - C y) ^ m` for some non-zero natural number `m`,
some natural number `n`, and some element `y` of `F`, such that either `n = 0` or `y` has no
`q`-th root in `F`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Polynomial.Monic.eq_X_pow_char_pow_sub_C_pow_of_natSepDegree_eq_one (q : ℕ) [ExpChar F q] (hm : f.Monic) (h : f.natSepDegree = 1) : ∃ (m n : ℕ) (y : F), m ≠ 0 ∧ (n = 0 ∨ y ∉ (frobenius F q).range) ∧ f = (X ^ q ^ n - C y) ^ m
theorem Polynomial.Monic.natSepDegree_eq_one_iff (q : ℕ) [ExpChar F q] (hm : f.Monic) : f.natSepDegree = 1 ↔ ∃ (m n : ℕ) (y : F), m ≠ 0 ∧ f = (X ^ q ^ n - C y) ^ m

views.nl_informal:
The minimal polynomial of an element of `E / F` of exponential characteristic `q` has
separable degree one if and only if the minimal polynomial is of the form
`Polynomial.expand F (q ^ n) (X - C y)` for some `n : ℕ` and `y : F`.
views.lean_signature: theorem minpoly.natSepDegree_eq_one_iff_eq_expand_X_sub_C : (minpoly F x).natSepDegree = 1 ↔ ∃ (n : ℕ) (y : F), minpoly F x = expand F (q ^ n) (X - C y)

views.nl_informal:
The minimal polynomial of an element of `E / F` of exponential characteristic `q` has
separable degree one if and only if the minimal polynomial is of the form
`X ^ (q ^ n) - C y` for some `n : ℕ` and `y : F`.
views.lean_signature: theorem minpoly.natSepDegree_eq_one_iff_eq_X_pow_sub_C : (minpoly F x).natSepDegree = 1 ↔ ∃ (n : ℕ) (y : F), minpoly F x = X ^ q ^ n - C y

views.nl_informal:
The minimal polynomial of an element `x` of `E / F` of exponential characteristic `q` has
separable degree one if and only if `x ^ (q ^ n) ∈ F` for some `n : ℕ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem minpoly.natSepDegree_eq_one_iff_pow_mem : (minpoly F x).natSepDegree = 1 ↔ ∃ n : ℕ, x ^ q ^ n ∈ (algebraMap F E).range

views.nl_informal:
The minimal polynomial of an element `x` of `E / F` of exponential characteristic `q` has
separable degree one if and only if the minimal polynomial is of the form
`(X - x) ^ (q ^ n)` for some `n : ℕ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem minpoly.natSepDegree_eq_one_iff_eq_X_sub_C_pow : (minpoly F x).natSepDegree = 1 ↔ ∃ n : ℕ, (minpoly F x).map (algebraMap F E) = (X - C x) ^ q ^ n

views.nl_informal:
The separable degree of `F⟮α⟯ / F` is equal to the separable degree of the
minimal polynomial of `α` over `F`.
views.lean_signature: theorem IntermediateField.finSepDegree_adjoin_simple_eq_natSepDegree {α : E} (halg : IsAlgebraic F α) : finSepDegree F F⟮α⟯ = (minpoly F α).natSepDegree

views.nl_informal:
The separable degree of `F⟮α⟯ / F` is smaller than the degree of `F⟮α⟯ / F` if `α` is
algebraic over `F`.
views.lean_signature: theorem IntermediateField.finSepDegree_adjoin_simple_le_finrank (α : E) (halg : IsAlgebraic F α) : finSepDegree F F⟮α⟯ ≤ finrank F F⟮α⟯

views.nl_informal:
If `α` is algebraic over `F`, then the separable degree of `F⟮α⟯ / F` is equal to the degree
of `F⟮α⟯ / F` if and only if `α` is a separable element.
views.lean_signature: theorem IntermediateField.finSepDegree_adjoin_simple_eq_finrank_iff (α : E) (halg : IsAlgebraic F α) : finSepDegree F F⟮α⟯ = finrank F F⟮α⟯ ↔ IsSeparable F α

views.nl_informal: The separable degree of any field extension `E / F` divides the degree of `E / F`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Field.finSepDegree_dvd_finrank : finSepDegree F E ∣ finrank F E

views.nl_informal: The separable degree of a finite extension `E / F` is smaller than the degree of `E / F`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Field.finSepDegree_le_finrank [FiniteDimensional F E] : finSepDegree F E ≤ finrank F E

views.nl_informal:
If `E / F` is a separable extension, then its separable degree is equal to its degree.
When `E / F` is infinite, it means that `Field.Emb F E` has infinitely many elements.
(But the cardinality of `Field.Emb F E` is not equal to `Module.rank F E` in general!)
views.lean_signature: theorem Field.finSepDegree_eq_finrank_of_isSeparable [Algebra.IsSeparable F E] : finSepDegree F E = finrank F E

views.nl_informal:
If `E / F` is a finite extension, then its separable degree is equal to its degree if and
only if it is a separable extension.
views.lean_signature: theorem Field.finSepDegree_eq_finrank_iff [FiniteDimensional F E] : finSepDegree F E = finrank F E ↔ Algebra.IsSeparable F E

views.nl_informal:
`F⟮x⟯ / F` is a separable extension if and only if `x` is a separable element.
As a consequence, any rational function of `x` is also a separable element.
views.lean_signature: theorem IntermediateField.isSeparable_adjoin_simple_iff_isSeparable {x : E} : Algebra.IsSeparable F F⟮x⟯ ↔ IsSeparable F x

views.nl_informal:
If `K / E / F` is an extension tower such that `E / F` is separable,
`x : K` is separable over `E`, then it's also separable over `F`.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsSeparable.of_algebra_isSeparable_of_isSeparable [Algebra E K] [IsScalarTower F E K] [Algebra.IsSeparable F E] {x : K} (hsep : IsSeparable E x) : IsSeparable F x

views.nl_informal: If `E / F` and `K / E` are both separable extensions, then `K / F` is also separable.
views.lean_signature: theorem Algebra.IsSeparable.trans [Algebra E K] [IsScalarTower F E K] [Algebra.IsSeparable F E] [Algebra.IsSeparable E K] : Algebra.IsSeparable F K

views.nl_informal:
If `x` and `y` are both separable elements, then `F⟮x, y⟯ / F` is a separable extension.
As a consequence, any rational function of `x` and `y` is also a separable element.
views.lean_signature: theorem IntermediateField.isSeparable_adjoin_pair_of_isSeparable {x y : E} (hx : IsSeparable F x) (hy : IsSeparable F y) : Algebra.IsSeparable F F⟮x, y⟯

views.nl_informal: Any element `x` of `F` is a separable element of `E / F` when embedded into `E`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Field.isSeparable_algebraMap (x : F) : IsSeparable F ((algebraMap F E) x)

views.nl_informal: If `x` and `y` are both separable elements, then `x * y` is also a separable element.
views.lean_signature: theorem Field.isSeparable_mul {x y : E} (hx : IsSeparable F x) (hy : IsSeparable F y) : IsSeparable F (x * y)

views.nl_informal: If `x` and `y` are both separable elements, then `x + y` is also a separable element.
views.lean_signature: theorem Field.isSeparable_add {x y : E} (hx : IsSeparable F x) (hy : IsSeparable F y) : IsSeparable F (x + y)

views.nl_informal: If `x` is a separable elements, then `-x` is also a separable element.
views.lean_signature: theorem Field.isSeparable_neg {x : E} (hx : IsSeparable F x) : IsSeparable F (-x)

views.nl_informal: If `x` and `y` are both separable elements, then `x - y` is also a separable element.
views.lean_signature: theorem Field.isSeparable_sub {x y : E} (hx : IsSeparable F x) (hy : IsSeparable F y) : IsSeparable F (x - y)

views.nl_informal: If `x` is a separable element, then `x⁻¹` is also a separable element.
views.lean_signature: theorem Field.isSeparable_inv {x : E} (hx : IsSeparable F x) : IsSeparable F x⁻¹

views.nl_informal:
A field is a perfect field (which means that any irreducible polynomial is separable)
if and only if every separable degree one polynomial splits.
views.lean_signature: theorem perfectField_iff_splits_of_natSepDegree_eq_one (F : Type*) [Field F] : PerfectField F ↔ ∀ f : F[X], f.natSepDegree = 1 → f.Splits (RingHom.id F)

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:
