The Monge point of an (n+2)-simplex, minus the centroid of an
n-dimensional face, in terms of `pointsWithCircumcenter`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Affine.Simplex.mongePoint_vsub_face_centroid_eq_weightedVSub_of_pointsWithCircumcenter {n : ℕ} (s : Simplex ℝ P (n + 2)) {i₁ i₂ : Fin (n + 3)} (h : i₁ ≠ i₂) : s.mongePoint -ᵥ ({i₁, i₂}ᶜ : Finset (Fin (n + 3))).centroid ℝ s.points = (univ : Finset (PointsWithCircumcenterIndex (n + 2))).weightedVSub s.pointsWithCircumcenter (mongePointVSubFaceCentroidWeightsWithCircumcenter i₁ i₂)

views.nl_informal:
The Monge point of an (n+2)-simplex, minus the centroid of an
n-dimensional face, is orthogonal to the difference of the two
vertices not in that face.
views.lean_signature: theorem Affine.Simplex.inner_mongePoint_vsub_face_centroid_vsub {n : ℕ} (s : Simplex ℝ P (n + 2)) {i₁ i₂ : Fin (n + 3)} : ⟪s.mongePoint -ᵥ ({i₁, i₂}ᶜ : Finset (Fin (n + 3))).centroid ℝ s.points, s.points i₁ -ᵥ s.points i₂⟫ = 0

views.nl_informal: The definition of a Monge plane.
views.lean_signature: theorem Affine.Simplex.mongePlane_def {n : ℕ} (s : Simplex ℝ P (n + 2)) (i₁ i₂ : Fin (n + 3)) : s.mongePlane i₁ i₂ = mk' (({i₁, i₂}ᶜ : Finset (Fin (n + 3))).centroid ℝ s.points) (ℝ ∙ s.points i₁ -ᵥ s.points i₂)ᗮ ⊓ affineSpan ℝ (Set.range s.points)

views.nl_informal:
The Monge plane associated with vertices `i₁` and `i₂` equals that
associated with `i₂` and `i₁`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Affine.Simplex.mongePlane_comm {n : ℕ} (s : Simplex ℝ P (n + 2)) (i₁ i₂ : Fin (n + 3)) : s.mongePlane i₁ i₂ = s.mongePlane i₂ i₁

views.nl_informal: The Monge point lies in the Monge planes.
views.lean_signature: theorem Affine.Simplex.mongePoint_mem_mongePlane {n : ℕ} (s : Simplex ℝ P (n + 2)) {i₁ i₂ : Fin (n + 3)} : s.mongePoint ∈ s.mongePlane i₁ i₂

views.nl_informal: The direction of a Monge plane.
views.lean_signature: theorem Affine.Simplex.direction_mongePlane {n : ℕ} (s : Simplex ℝ P (n + 2)) {i₁ i₂ : Fin (n + 3)} : (s.mongePlane i₁ i₂).direction = (ℝ ∙ s.points i₁ -ᵥ s.points i₂)ᗮ ⊓ vectorSpan ℝ (Set.range s.points)

views.nl_informal:
The Monge point is the only point in all the Monge planes from any
one vertex.
views.lean_signature: theorem Affine.Simplex.eq_mongePoint_of_forall_mem_mongePlane {n : ℕ} {s : Simplex ℝ P (n + 2)} {i₁ : Fin (n + 3)} {p : P} (h : ∀ i₂, i₁ ≠ i₂ → p ∈ s.mongePlane i₁ i₂) : p = s.mongePoint

views.nl_informal: The orthocenter equals the Monge point.
views.lean_signature: theorem Affine.Triangle.orthocenter_eq_mongePoint (t : Triangle ℝ P) : t.orthocenter = t.mongePoint

views.nl_informal:
The position of the orthocenter in relation to the circumcenter
and centroid.
views.lean_signature: theorem Affine.Triangle.orthocenter_eq_smul_vsub_vadd_circumcenter (t : Triangle ℝ P) : t.orthocenter = (3 : ℝ) • ((univ : Finset (Fin 3)).centroid ℝ t.points -ᵥ t.circumcenter : V) +ᵥ t.circumcenter

views.nl_informal: The orthocenter lies in the affine span.
views.lean_signature: theorem Affine.Triangle.orthocenter_mem_affineSpan (t : Triangle ℝ P) : t.orthocenter ∈ affineSpan ℝ (Set.range t.points)

views.nl_informal: Two triangles with the same points have the same orthocenter.
views.lean_signature: theorem Affine.Triangle.orthocenter_eq_of_range_eq {t₁ t₂ : Triangle ℝ P} (h : Set.range t₁.points = Set.range t₂.points) : t₁.orthocenter = t₂.orthocenter

views.nl_informal:
In the case of a triangle, altitudes are the same thing as Monge
planes.
views.lean_signature: theorem Affine.Triangle.altitude_eq_mongePlane (t : Triangle ℝ P) {i₁ i₂ i₃ : Fin 3} (h₁₂ : i₁ ≠ i₂) (h₁₃ : i₁ ≠ i₃) (h₂₃ : i₂ ≠ i₃) : t.altitude i₁ = t.mongePlane i₂ i₃

views.nl_informal: The orthocenter lies in the altitudes.
views.lean_signature: theorem Affine.Triangle.orthocenter_mem_altitude (t : Triangle ℝ P) {i₁ : Fin 3} : t.orthocenter ∈ t.altitude i₁

views.nl_informal:
The orthocenter is the only point lying in any two of the
altitudes.
views.lean_signature: theorem Affine.Triangle.eq_orthocenter_of_forall_mem_altitude {t : Triangle ℝ P} {i₁ i₂ : Fin 3} {p : P} (h₁₂ : i₁ ≠ i₂) (h₁ : p ∈ t.altitude i₁) (h₂ : p ∈ t.altitude i₂) : p = t.orthocenter

views.nl_informal:
The distance from the orthocenter to the reflection of the
circumcenter in a side equals the circumradius.
views.lean_signature: theorem Affine.Triangle.dist_orthocenter_reflection_circumcenter (t : Triangle ℝ P) {i₁ i₂ : Fin 3} (h : i₁ ≠ i₂) : dist t.orthocenter (reflection (affineSpan ℝ (t.points '' {i₁, i₂})) t.circumcenter) = t.circumradius

views.nl_informal:
The distance from the orthocenter to the reflection of the
circumcenter in a side equals the circumradius, variant using a
`Finset`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Affine.Triangle.dist_orthocenter_reflection_circumcenter_finset (t : Triangle ℝ P) {i₁ i₂ : Fin 3} (h : i₁ ≠ i₂) : dist t.orthocenter (reflection (affineSpan ℝ (t.points '' ↑({i₁, i₂} : Finset (Fin 3)))) t.circumcenter) = t.circumradius

views.nl_informal:
The affine span of the orthocenter and a vertex is contained in
the altitude.
views.lean_signature: theorem Affine.Triangle.affineSpan_orthocenter_point_le_altitude (t : Triangle ℝ P) (i : Fin 3) : line[ℝ, t.orthocenter, t.points i] ≤ t.altitude i

views.nl_informal:
Suppose we are given a triangle `t₁`, and replace one of its
vertices by its orthocenter, yielding triangle `t₂` (with vertices not
necessarily listed in the same order).  Then an altitude of `t₂` from
a vertex that was not replaced is the corresponding side of `t₁`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Affine.Triangle.altitude_replace_orthocenter_eq_affineSpan {t₁ t₂ : Triangle ℝ P} {i₁ i₂ i₃ j₁ j₂ j₃ : Fin 3} (hi₁₂ : i₁ ≠ i₂) (hi₁₃ : i₁ ≠ i₃) (hi₂₃ : i₂ ≠ i₃) (hj₁₂ : j₁ ≠ j₂) (hj₁₃ : j₁ ≠ j₃) (hj₂₃ : j₂ ≠ j₃) (h₁ : t₂.points j₁ = t₁.orthocenter) (h₂ : t₂.points j₂ = t₁.points i₂) (h₃ : t₂.points j₃ = t₁.points i₃) : t₂.altitude j₂ = line[ℝ, t₁.points i₁, t₁.points i₂]

views.nl_informal:
Suppose we are given a triangle `t₁`, and replace one of its
vertices by its orthocenter, yielding triangle `t₂` (with vertices not
necessarily listed in the same order).  Then the orthocenter of `t₂`
is the vertex of `t₁` that was replaced.
views.lean_signature: theorem Affine.Triangle.orthocenter_replace_orthocenter_eq_point {t₁ t₂ : Triangle ℝ P} {i₁ i₂ i₃ j₁ j₂ j₃ : Fin 3} (hi₁₂ : i₁ ≠ i₂) (hi₁₃ : i₁ ≠ i₃) (hi₂₃ : i₂ ≠ i₃) (hj₁₂ : j₁ ≠ j₂) (hj₁₃ : j₁ ≠ j₃) (hj₂₃ : j₂ ≠ j₃) (h₁ : t₂.points j₁ = t₁.orthocenter) (h₂ : t₂.points j₂ = t₁.points i₂) (h₃ : t₂.points j₃ = t₁.points i₃) : t₂.orthocenter = t₁.points i₁

views.nl_informal:
This is an auxiliary lemma giving information about the relation
of two triangles in an orthocentric system; it abstracts some
reasoning, with no geometric content, that is common to some other
lemmas.  Suppose the orthocentric system is generated by triangle `t`,
and we are given three points `p` in the orthocentric system.  Then
either we can find indices `i₁`, `i₂` and `i₃` for `p` such that `p
i₁` is the orthocenter of `t` and `p i₂` and `p i₃` are points `j₂`
and `j₃` of `t`, or `p` has the same points as `t`.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.exists_of_range_subset_orthocentricSystem {t : Triangle ℝ P} (ho : t.orthocenter ∉ Set.range t.points) {p : Fin 3 → P} (hps : Set.range p ⊆ insert t.orthocenter (Set.range t.points)) (hpi : Function.Injective p) : (∃ i₁ i₂ i₃ j₂ j₃ : Fin 3, i₁ ≠ i₂ ∧ i₁ ≠ i₃ ∧ i₂ ≠ i₃ ∧ (∀ i : Fin 3, i = i₁ ∨ i = i₂ ∨ i = i₃) ∧ p i₁ = t.orthocenter ∧ j₂ ≠ j₃ ∧ t.points j₂ = p i₂ ∧ t.points j₃ = p i₃) ∨ Set.range p = Set.range t.points

views.nl_informal:
For any three points in an orthocentric system generated by
triangle `t`, there is a point in the subspace spanned by the triangle
from which the distance of all those three points equals the circumradius.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.exists_dist_eq_circumradius_of_subset_insert_orthocenter {t : Triangle ℝ P} (ho : t.orthocenter ∉ Set.range t.points) {p : Fin 3 → P} (hps : Set.range p ⊆ insert t.orthocenter (Set.range t.points)) (hpi : Function.Injective p) : ∃ c ∈ affineSpan ℝ (Set.range t.points), ∀ p₁ ∈ Set.range p, dist p₁ c = t.circumradius

views.nl_informal: Any three points in an orthocentric system are affinely independent.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.OrthocentricSystem.affineIndependent {s : Set P} (ho : OrthocentricSystem s) {p : Fin 3 → P} (hps : Set.range p ⊆ s) (hpi : Function.Injective p) : AffineIndependent ℝ p

views.nl_informal:
Any three points in an orthocentric system span the same subspace
as the whole orthocentric system.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.affineSpan_of_orthocentricSystem {s : Set P} (ho : OrthocentricSystem s) {p : Fin 3 → P} (hps : Set.range p ⊆ s) (hpi : Function.Injective p) : affineSpan ℝ (Set.range p) = affineSpan ℝ s

views.nl_informal: All triangles in an orthocentric system have the same circumradius.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.OrthocentricSystem.exists_circumradius_eq {s : Set P} (ho : OrthocentricSystem s) : ∃ r : ℝ, ∀ t : Triangle ℝ P, Set.range t.points ⊆ s → t.circumradius = r

views.nl_informal:
Given any triangle in an orthocentric system, the fourth point is
its orthocenter.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.OrthocentricSystem.eq_insert_orthocenter {s : Set P} (ho : OrthocentricSystem s) {t : Triangle ℝ P} (ht : Set.range t.points ⊆ s) : s = insert t.orthocenter (Set.range t.points)

views.nl_informal:
A point `c` belongs the perpendicular bisector of `[p₁, p₂] iff `p₂ -ᵥ p₁` is orthogonal to
`c -ᵥ midpoint ℝ p₁ p₂`.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineSubspace.mem_perpBisector_iff_inner_eq_zero' : c ∈ perpBisector p₁ p₂ ↔ ⟪p₂ -ᵥ p₁, c -ᵥ midpoint ℝ p₁ p₂⟫ = 0

views.nl_informal:
A point `c` belongs the perpendicular bisector of `[p₁, p₂] iff `c -ᵥ midpoint ℝ p₁ p₂` is
orthogonal to `p₂ -ᵥ p₁`.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineSubspace.mem_perpBisector_iff_inner_eq_zero : c ∈ perpBisector p₁ p₂ ↔ ⟪c -ᵥ midpoint ℝ p₁ p₂, p₂ -ᵥ p₁⟫ = 0

views.nl_informal:
Suppose that `c₁` is equidistant from `p₁` and `p₂`, and the same applies to `c₂`. Then the
vector between `c₁` and `c₂` is orthogonal to that between `p₁` and `p₂`. (In two dimensions, this
says that the diagonals of a kite are orthogonal.)
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.inner_vsub_vsub_of_dist_eq_of_dist_eq {c₁ c₂ p₁ p₂ : P} (hc₁ : dist p₁ c₁ = dist p₂ c₁) (hc₂ : dist p₁ c₂ = dist p₂ c₂) : ⟪c₂ -ᵥ c₁, p₂ -ᵥ p₁⟫ = 0

views.nl_informal:
The intersection of the subspace and the orthogonal subspace
through the given point is the `orthogonalProjectionFn` of that
point onto the subspace. This lemma is only intended for use in
setting up the bundled version and should not be used once that is
defined.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.inter_eq_singleton_orthogonalProjectionFn {s : AffineSubspace ℝ P} [Nonempty s] [s.direction.HasOrthogonalProjection] (p : P) : (s : Set P) ∩ mk' p s.directionᗮ = {orthogonalProjectionFn s p}

views.nl_informal:
The `orthogonalProjectionFn` lies in the given subspace. This
lemma is only intended for use in setting up the bundled version and
should not be used once that is defined.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.orthogonalProjectionFn_mem {s : AffineSubspace ℝ P} [Nonempty s] [s.direction.HasOrthogonalProjection] (p : P) : orthogonalProjectionFn s p ∈ s

views.nl_informal:
The `orthogonalProjectionFn` lies in the orthogonal
subspace. This lemma is only intended for use in setting up the
bundled version and should not be used once that is defined.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.orthogonalProjectionFn_mem_orthogonal {s : AffineSubspace ℝ P} [Nonempty s] [s.direction.HasOrthogonalProjection] (p : P) : orthogonalProjectionFn s p ∈ mk' p s.directionᗮ

views.nl_informal:
Subtracting `p` from its `orthogonalProjectionFn` produces a
result in the orthogonal direction. This lemma is only intended for
use in setting up the bundled version and should not be used once that
is defined.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.orthogonalProjectionFn_vsub_mem_direction_orthogonal {s : AffineSubspace ℝ P} [Nonempty s] [s.direction.HasOrthogonalProjection] (p : P) : orthogonalProjectionFn s p -ᵥ p ∈ s.directionᗮ

views.nl_informal: The linear map corresponding to `orthogonalProjection`.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.orthogonalProjection_linear {s : AffineSubspace ℝ P} [Nonempty s] [s.direction.HasOrthogonalProjection] : (orthogonalProjection s).linear = s.direction.orthogonalProjection

views.nl_informal:
The intersection of the subspace and the orthogonal subspace
through the given point is the `orthogonalProjection` of that point
onto the subspace.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.inter_eq_singleton_orthogonalProjection {s : AffineSubspace ℝ P} [Nonempty s] [s.direction.HasOrthogonalProjection] (p : P) : (s : Set P) ∩ mk' p s.directionᗮ = {↑(orthogonalProjection s p)}

views.nl_informal: The `orthogonalProjection` lies in the given subspace.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.orthogonalProjection_mem {s : AffineSubspace ℝ P} [Nonempty s] [s.direction.HasOrthogonalProjection] (p : P) : ↑(orthogonalProjection s p) ∈ s

views.nl_informal: The `orthogonalProjection` lies in the orthogonal subspace.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.orthogonalProjection_mem_orthogonal (s : AffineSubspace ℝ P) [Nonempty s] [s.direction.HasOrthogonalProjection] (p : P) : ↑(orthogonalProjection s p) ∈ mk' p s.directionᗮ

views.nl_informal:
Subtracting a point in the given subspace from the
`orthogonalProjection` produces a result in the direction of the
given subspace.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.orthogonalProjection_vsub_mem_direction {s : AffineSubspace ℝ P} [Nonempty s] [s.direction.HasOrthogonalProjection] {p₁ : P} (p₂ : P) (hp₁ : p₁ ∈ s) : ↑(orthogonalProjection s p₂ -ᵥ ⟨p₁, hp₁⟩ : s.direction) ∈ s.direction

views.nl_informal:
Subtracting the `orthogonalProjection` from a point in the given
subspace produces a result in the direction of the given subspace.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.vsub_orthogonalProjection_mem_direction {s : AffineSubspace ℝ P} [Nonempty s] [s.direction.HasOrthogonalProjection] {p₁ : P} (p₂ : P) (hp₁ : p₁ ∈ s) : ↑((⟨p₁, hp₁⟩ : s) -ᵥ orthogonalProjection s p₂ : s.direction) ∈ s.direction

views.nl_informal:
A point equals its orthogonal projection if and only if it lies in
the subspace.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.orthogonalProjection_eq_self_iff {s : AffineSubspace ℝ P} [Nonempty s] [s.direction.HasOrthogonalProjection] {p : P} : ↑(orthogonalProjection s p) = p ↔ p ∈ s

views.nl_informal: Orthogonal projection is idempotent.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.orthogonalProjection_orthogonalProjection (s : AffineSubspace ℝ P) [Nonempty s] [s.direction.HasOrthogonalProjection] (p : P) : orthogonalProjection s (orthogonalProjection s p) = orthogonalProjection s p

views.nl_informal: The distance to a point's orthogonal projection is 0 iff it lies in the subspace.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.dist_orthogonalProjection_eq_zero_iff {s : AffineSubspace ℝ P} [Nonempty s] [s.direction.HasOrthogonalProjection] {p : P} : dist p (orthogonalProjection s p) = 0 ↔ p ∈ s

views.nl_informal:
The distance between a point and its orthogonal projection is
nonzero if it does not lie in the subspace.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.dist_orthogonalProjection_ne_zero_of_not_mem {s : AffineSubspace ℝ P} [Nonempty s] [s.direction.HasOrthogonalProjection] {p : P} (hp : p ∉ s) : dist p (orthogonalProjection s p) ≠ 0

views.nl_informal:
Subtracting `p` from its `orthogonalProjection` produces a result
in the orthogonal direction.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.orthogonalProjection_vsub_mem_direction_orthogonal (s : AffineSubspace ℝ P) [Nonempty s] [s.direction.HasOrthogonalProjection] (p : P) : (orthogonalProjection s p : P) -ᵥ p ∈ s.directionᗮ

views.nl_informal:
Subtracting the `orthogonalProjection` from `p` produces a result
in the orthogonal direction.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.vsub_orthogonalProjection_mem_direction_orthogonal (s : AffineSubspace ℝ P) [Nonempty s] [s.direction.HasOrthogonalProjection] (p : P) : p -ᵥ orthogonalProjection s p ∈ s.directionᗮ

views.nl_informal:
Subtracting the `orthogonalProjection` from `p` produces a result in the kernel of the linear
part of the orthogonal projection.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.orthogonalProjection_vsub_orthogonalProjection (s : AffineSubspace ℝ P) [Nonempty s] [s.direction.HasOrthogonalProjection] (p : P) : s.direction.orthogonalProjection (p -ᵥ orthogonalProjection s p) = 0

views.nl_informal:
Adding a vector to a point in the given subspace, then taking the
orthogonal projection, produces the original point if the vector was
in the orthogonal direction.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.orthogonalProjection_vadd_eq_self {s : AffineSubspace ℝ P} [Nonempty s] [s.direction.HasOrthogonalProjection] {p : P} (hp : p ∈ s) {v : V} (hv : v ∈ s.directionᗮ) : orthogonalProjection s (v +ᵥ p) = ⟨p, hp⟩

views.nl_informal:
Adding a vector to a point in the given subspace, then taking the
orthogonal projection, produces the original point if the vector is a
multiple of the result of subtracting a point's orthogonal projection
from that point.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.orthogonalProjection_vadd_smul_vsub_orthogonalProjection {s : AffineSubspace ℝ P} [Nonempty s] [s.direction.HasOrthogonalProjection] {p₁ : P} (p₂ : P) (r : ℝ) (hp : p₁ ∈ s) : orthogonalProjection s (r • (p₂ -ᵥ orthogonalProjection s p₂ : V) +ᵥ p₁) = ⟨p₁, hp⟩

views.nl_informal:
The square of the distance from a point in `s` to `p₂` equals the
sum of the squares of the distances of the two points to the
`orthogonalProjection`.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.dist_sq_eq_dist_orthogonalProjection_sq_add_dist_orthogonalProjection_sq {s : AffineSubspace ℝ P} [Nonempty s] [s.direction.HasOrthogonalProjection] {p₁ : P} (p₂ : P) (hp₁ : p₁ ∈ s) : dist p₁ p₂ * dist p₁ p₂ = dist p₁ (orthogonalProjection s p₂) * dist p₁ (orthogonalProjection s p₂) + dist p₂ (orthogonalProjection s p₂) * dist p₂ (orthogonalProjection s p₂)

views.nl_informal:
The distance between a point and its orthogonal projection to a subspace equals the distance
to that subspace as given by `Metric.infDist`. This is not a `simp` lemma since the simplest form
depends on the context (if any calculations are to be done with the distance, the version with
the orthogonal projection gives access to more lemmas about orthogonal projections that may be
useful).
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.dist_orthogonalProjection_eq_infDist (s : AffineSubspace ℝ P) [Nonempty s] [s.direction.HasOrthogonalProjection] (p : P) : dist p (orthogonalProjection s p) = Metric.infDist p s

views.nl_informal:
The nonnegative distance between a point and its orthogonal projection to a subspace equals
the distance to that subspace as given by `Metric.infNndist`. This is not a `simp` lemma since
the simplest form depends on the context (if any calculations are to be done with the distance,
the version with the orthogonal projection gives access to more lemmas about orthogonal
projections that may be useful).
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.dist_orthogonalProjection_eq_infNndist (s : AffineSubspace ℝ P) [Nonempty s] [s.direction.HasOrthogonalProjection] (p : P) : nndist p (orthogonalProjection s p) = Metric.infNndist p s

views.nl_informal:
The square of the distance between two points constructed by
adding multiples of the same orthogonal vector to points in the same
subspace.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.dist_sq_smul_orthogonal_vadd_smul_orthogonal_vadd {s : AffineSubspace ℝ P} {p₁ p₂ : P} (hp₁ : p₁ ∈ s) (hp₂ : p₂ ∈ s) (r₁ r₂ : ℝ) {v : V} (hv : v ∈ s.directionᗮ) : dist (r₁ • v +ᵥ p₁) (r₂ • v +ᵥ p₂) * dist (r₁ • v +ᵥ p₁) (r₂ • v +ᵥ p₂) = dist p₁ p₂ * dist p₁ p₂ + (r₁ - r₂) * (r₁ - r₂) * (‖v‖ * ‖v‖)

views.nl_informal:
`p` is equidistant from two points in `s` if and only if its
`orthogonalProjection` is.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.dist_eq_iff_dist_orthogonalProjection_eq {s : AffineSubspace ℝ P} [Nonempty s] [s.direction.HasOrthogonalProjection] {p₁ p₂ : P} (p₃ : P) (hp₁ : p₁ ∈ s) (hp₂ : p₂ ∈ s) : dist p₁ p₃ = dist p₂ p₃ ↔ dist p₁ (orthogonalProjection s p₃) = dist p₂ (orthogonalProjection s p₃)

views.nl_informal:
`p` is equidistant from a set of points in `s` if and only if its
`orthogonalProjection` is.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.dist_set_eq_iff_dist_orthogonalProjection_eq {s : AffineSubspace ℝ P} [Nonempty s] [s.direction.HasOrthogonalProjection] {ps : Set P} (hps : ps ⊆ s) (p : P) : (Set.Pairwise ps fun p₁ p₂ => dist p₁ p = dist p₂ p) ↔ Set.Pairwise ps fun p₁ p₂ => dist p₁ (orthogonalProjection s p) = dist p₂ (orthogonalProjection s p)

views.nl_informal:
There exists `r` such that `p` has distance `r` from all the
points of a set of points in `s` if and only if there exists (possibly
different) `r` such that its `orthogonalProjection` has that distance
from all the points in that set.

views.nl_informal: A point is its own reflection if and only if it is in the subspace.

views.nl_informal:

and only if the point has the same orthogonal projection in each of

between the reflection of `p₁` and `p₂`.

views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.oangle_eq_pi_iff_angle_eq_pi {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} : ∡ p₁ p₂ p₃ = π ↔ ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = π

views.nl_informal: If the oriented angle between three points is `π / 2`, so is the unoriented angle.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.angle_eq_pi_div_two_of_oangle_eq_pi_div_two {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : ∡ p₁ p₂ p₃ = ↑(π / 2)) : ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = π / 2

views.nl_informal:
If the oriented angle between three points is `π / 2`, so is the unoriented angle
(reversed).
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.angle_rev_eq_pi_div_two_of_oangle_eq_pi_div_two {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : ∡ p₁ p₂ p₃ = ↑(π / 2)) : ∠ p₃ p₂ p₁ = π / 2

views.nl_informal: If the oriented angle between three points is `-π / 2`, the unoriented angle is `π / 2`.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.angle_eq_pi_div_two_of_oangle_eq_neg_pi_div_two {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : ∡ p₁ p₂ p₃ = ↑(-π / 2)) : ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = π / 2

views.nl_informal:
If the oriented angle between three points is `-π / 2`, the unoriented angle (reversed) is
`π / 2`.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.angle_rev_eq_pi_div_two_of_oangle_eq_neg_pi_div_two {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : ∡ p₁ p₂ p₃ = ↑(-π / 2)) : ∠ p₃ p₂ p₁ = π / 2

views.nl_informal: Swapping the first and second points in an oriented angle negates the sign of that angle.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.oangle_swap₁₂_sign (p₁ p₂ p₃ : P) : -(∡ p₁ p₂ p₃).sign = (∡ p₂ p₁ p₃).sign

views.nl_informal: Swapping the first and third points in an oriented angle negates the sign of that angle.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.oangle_swap₁₃_sign (p₁ p₂ p₃ : P) : -(∡ p₁ p₂ p₃).sign = (∡ p₃ p₂ p₁).sign

views.nl_informal: Swapping the second and third points in an oriented angle negates the sign of that angle.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.oangle_swap₂₃_sign (p₁ p₂ p₃ : P) : -(∡ p₁ p₂ p₃).sign = (∡ p₁ p₃ p₂).sign

views.nl_informal: Rotating the points in an oriented angle does not change the sign of that angle.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.oangle_rotate_sign (p₁ p₂ p₃ : P) : (∡ p₂ p₃ p₁).sign = (∡ p₁ p₂ p₃).sign

views.nl_informal:
The oriented angle between three points is π if and only if the second point is strictly
between the other two.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.oangle_eq_pi_iff_sbtw {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} : ∡ p₁ p₂ p₃ = π ↔ Sbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₃

views.nl_informal:
If the second of three points is strictly between the other two, the oriented angle at that
point is π.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sbtw.oangle₁₂₃_eq_pi {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : Sbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₃) : ∡ p₁ p₂ p₃ = π

views.nl_informal:
If the second of three points is strictly between the other two, the oriented angle at that
point (reversed) is π.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sbtw.oangle₃₂₁_eq_pi {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : Sbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₃) : ∡ p₃ p₂ p₁ = π

views.nl_informal:
If the second of three points is weakly between the other two, the oriented angle at the
first point is zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Wbtw.oangle₂₁₃_eq_zero {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : Wbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₃) : ∡ p₂ p₁ p₃ = 0

views.nl_informal:
If the second of three points is strictly between the other two, the oriented angle at the
first point is zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sbtw.oangle₂₁₃_eq_zero {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : Sbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₃) : ∡ p₂ p₁ p₃ = 0

views.nl_informal:
If the second of three points is weakly between the other two, the oriented angle at the
first point (reversed) is zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Wbtw.oangle₃₁₂_eq_zero {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : Wbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₃) : ∡ p₃ p₁ p₂ = 0

views.nl_informal:
If the second of three points is strictly between the other two, the oriented angle at the
first point (reversed) is zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sbtw.oangle₃₁₂_eq_zero {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : Sbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₃) : ∡ p₃ p₁ p₂ = 0

views.nl_informal:
If the second of three points is weakly between the other two, the oriented angle at the
third point is zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Wbtw.oangle₂₃₁_eq_zero {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : Wbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₃) : ∡ p₂ p₃ p₁ = 0

views.nl_informal:
If the second of three points is strictly between the other two, the oriented angle at the
third point is zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sbtw.oangle₂₃₁_eq_zero {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : Sbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₃) : ∡ p₂ p₃ p₁ = 0

views.nl_informal:
If the second of three points is weakly between the other two, the oriented angle at the
third point (reversed) is zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Wbtw.oangle₁₃₂_eq_zero {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : Wbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₃) : ∡ p₁ p₃ p₂ = 0

views.nl_informal:
If the second of three points is strictly between the other two, the oriented angle at the
third point (reversed) is zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sbtw.oangle₁₃₂_eq_zero {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : Sbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₃) : ∡ p₁ p₃ p₂ = 0

views.nl_informal:
The oriented angle between three points is zero if and only if one of the first and third
points is weakly between the other two.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.oangle_eq_zero_iff_wbtw {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} : ∡ p₁ p₂ p₃ = 0 ↔ Wbtw ℝ p₂ p₁ p₃ ∨ Wbtw ℝ p₂ p₃ p₁

views.nl_informal:
An oriented angle is unchanged by replacing the first point by one weakly further away on the
same ray.
views.lean_signature: theorem Wbtw.oangle_eq_left {p₁ p₁' p₂ p₃ : P} (h : Wbtw ℝ p₂ p₁ p₁') (hp₁p₂ : p₁ ≠ p₂) : ∡ p₁ p₂ p₃ = ∡ p₁' p₂ p₃

views.nl_informal:
An oriented angle is unchanged by replacing the first point by one strictly further away on
the same ray.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sbtw.oangle_eq_left {p₁ p₁' p₂ p₃ : P} (h : Sbtw ℝ p₂ p₁ p₁') : ∡ p₁ p₂ p₃ = ∡ p₁' p₂ p₃

views.nl_informal:
An oriented angle is unchanged by replacing the third point by one weakly further away on the
same ray.
views.lean_signature: theorem Wbtw.oangle_eq_right {p₁ p₂ p₃ p₃' : P} (h : Wbtw ℝ p₂ p₃ p₃') (hp₃p₂ : p₃ ≠ p₂) : ∡ p₁ p₂ p₃ = ∡ p₁ p₂ p₃'

views.nl_informal:
An oriented angle is unchanged by replacing the third point by one strictly further away on
the same ray.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sbtw.oangle_eq_right {p₁ p₂ p₃ p₃' : P} (h : Sbtw ℝ p₂ p₃ p₃') : ∡ p₁ p₂ p₃ = ∡ p₁ p₂ p₃'

views.nl_informal:
An oriented angle is unchanged by replacing the first point with the midpoint of the segment
between it and the second point.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.oangle_midpoint_left (p₁ p₂ p₃ : P) : ∡ (midpoint ℝ p₁ p₂) p₂ p₃ = ∡ p₁ p₂ p₃

views.nl_informal:
An oriented angle is unchanged by replacing the first point with the midpoint of the segment
between the second point and that point.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.oangle_midpoint_rev_left (p₁ p₂ p₃ : P) : ∡ (midpoint ℝ p₂ p₁) p₂ p₃ = ∡ p₁ p₂ p₃

views.nl_informal:
An oriented angle is unchanged by replacing the third point with the midpoint of the segment
between it and the second point.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.oangle_midpoint_right (p₁ p₂ p₃ : P) : ∡ p₁ p₂ (midpoint ℝ p₃ p₂) = ∡ p₁ p₂ p₃

views.nl_informal:
An oriented angle is unchanged by replacing the third point with the midpoint of the segment
between the second point and that point.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.oangle_midpoint_rev_right (p₁ p₂ p₃ : P) : ∡ p₁ p₂ (midpoint ℝ p₂ p₃) = ∡ p₁ p₂ p₃

views.nl_informal:
Replacing the first point by one on the same line but the opposite ray adds π to the oriented
angle.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sbtw.oangle_eq_add_pi_left {p₁ p₁' p₂ p₃ : P} (h : Sbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₁') (hp₃p₂ : p₃ ≠ p₂) : ∡ p₁ p₂ p₃ = ∡ p₁' p₂ p₃ + π

views.nl_informal:
Replacing the third point by one on the same line but the opposite ray adds π to the oriented
angle.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sbtw.oangle_eq_add_pi_right {p₁ p₂ p₃ p₃' : P} (h : Sbtw ℝ p₃ p₂ p₃') (hp₁p₂ : p₁ ≠ p₂) : ∡ p₁ p₂ p₃ = ∡ p₁ p₂ p₃' + π

views.nl_informal:
Replacing both the first and third points by ones on the same lines but the opposite rays
does not change the oriented angle (vertically opposite angles).
views.lean_signature: theorem Sbtw.oangle_eq_left_right {p₁ p₁' p₂ p₃ p₃' : P} (h₁ : Sbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₁') (h₃ : Sbtw ℝ p₃ p₂ p₃') : ∡ p₁ p₂ p₃ = ∡ p₁' p₂ p₃'

views.nl_informal: Replacing the first point by one on the same line does not change twice the oriented angle.
views.lean_signature: theorem Collinear.two_zsmul_oangle_eq_left {p₁ p₁' p₂ p₃ : P} (h : Collinear ℝ ({p₁, p₂, p₁'} : Set P)) (hp₁p₂ : p₁ ≠ p₂) (hp₁'p₂ : p₁' ≠ p₂) : (2 : ℤ) • ∡ p₁ p₂ p₃ = (2 : ℤ) • ∡ p₁' p₂ p₃

views.nl_informal: Replacing the third point by one on the same line does not change twice the oriented angle.
views.lean_signature: theorem Collinear.two_zsmul_oangle_eq_right {p₁ p₂ p₃ p₃' : P} (h : Collinear ℝ ({p₃, p₂, p₃'} : Set P)) (hp₃p₂ : p₃ ≠ p₂) (hp₃'p₂ : p₃' ≠ p₂) : (2 : ℤ) • ∡ p₁ p₂ p₃ = (2 : ℤ) • ∡ p₁ p₂ p₃'

views.nl_informal:
Two different points are equidistant from a third point if and only if that third point
equals some multiple of a `π / 2` rotation of the vector between those points, plus the midpoint
of those points.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.dist_eq_iff_eq_smul_rotation_pi_div_two_vadd_midpoint {p₁ p₂ p : P} (h : p₁ ≠ p₂) : dist p₁ p = dist p₂ p ↔ ∃ r : ℝ, r • o.rotation (π / 2 : ℝ) (p₂ -ᵥ p₁) +ᵥ midpoint ℝ p₁ p₂ = p

views.nl_informal:
Given two pairs of distinct points on the same line, such that the vectors between those
pairs of points are on the same ray (oriented in the same direction on that line), and a fifth
point, the angles at the fifth point between each of those two pairs of points have the same
sign.
views.lean_signature: theorem Collinear.oangle_sign_of_sameRay_vsub {p₁ p₂ p₃ p₄ : P} (p₅ : P) (hp₁p₂ : p₁ ≠ p₂) (hp₃p₄ : p₃ ≠ p₄) (hc : Collinear ℝ ({p₁, p₂, p₃, p₄} : Set P)) (hr : SameRay ℝ (p₂ -ᵥ p₁) (p₄ -ᵥ p₃)) : (∡ p₁ p₅ p₂).sign = (∡ p₃ p₅ p₄).sign

views.nl_informal:
Given three points in strict order on the same line, and a fourth point, the angles at the
fourth point between the first and second or second and third points have the same sign.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sbtw.oangle_sign_eq {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (p₄ : P) (h : Sbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₃) : (∡ p₁ p₄ p₂).sign = (∡ p₂ p₄ p₃).sign

views.nl_informal:
Given three points in weak order on the same line, with the first not equal to the second,
and a fourth point, the angles at the fourth point between the first and second or first and
third points have the same sign.
views.lean_signature: theorem Wbtw.oangle_sign_eq_of_ne_left {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (p₄ : P) (h : Wbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₃) (hne : p₁ ≠ p₂) : (∡ p₁ p₄ p₂).sign = (∡ p₁ p₄ p₃).sign

views.nl_informal:
Given three points in strict order on the same line, and a fourth point, the angles at the
fourth point between the first and second or first and third points have the same sign.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sbtw.oangle_sign_eq_left {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (p₄ : P) (h : Sbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₃) : (∡ p₁ p₄ p₂).sign = (∡ p₁ p₄ p₃).sign

views.nl_informal:
Given three points in weak order on the same line, with the second not equal to the third,
and a fourth point, the angles at the fourth point between the second and third or first and
third points have the same sign.
views.lean_signature: theorem Wbtw.oangle_sign_eq_of_ne_right {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (p₄ : P) (h : Wbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₃) (hne : p₂ ≠ p₃) : (∡ p₂ p₄ p₃).sign = (∡ p₁ p₄ p₃).sign

views.nl_informal:
Given three points in strict order on the same line, and a fourth point, the angles at the
fourth point between the second and third or first and third points have the same sign.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sbtw.oangle_sign_eq_right {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (p₄ : P) (h : Sbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₃) : (∡ p₂ p₄ p₃).sign = (∡ p₁ p₄ p₃).sign

views.nl_informal:
Given two points in an affine subspace, the angles between those two points at two other
points on the same side of that subspace have the same sign.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineSubspace.SSameSide.oangle_sign_eq {s : AffineSubspace ℝ P} {p₁ p₂ p₃ p₄ : P} (hp₁ : p₁ ∈ s) (hp₂ : p₂ ∈ s) (hp₃p₄ : s.SSameSide p₃ p₄) : (∡ p₁ p₄ p₂).sign = (∡ p₁ p₃ p₂).sign

views.nl_informal:
Given two points in an affine subspace, the angles between those two points at two other
points on opposite sides of that subspace have opposite signs.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineSubspace.SOppSide.oangle_sign_eq_neg {s : AffineSubspace ℝ P} {p₁ p₂ p₃ p₄ : P} (hp₁ : p₁ ∈ s) (hp₂ : p₂ ∈ s) (hp₃p₄ : s.SOppSide p₃ p₄) : (∡ p₁ p₄ p₂).sign = -(∡ p₁ p₃ p₂).sign

views.nl_informal: Oriented angles are continuous when the vectors involved are nonzero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.continuousAt_oangle {x : V × V} (hx1 : x.1 ≠ 0) (hx2 : x.2 ≠ 0) : ContinuousAt (fun y : V × V => o.oangle y.1 y.2) x

views.nl_informal: If the first vector passed to `oangle` is 0, the result is 0.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_zero_left (x : V) : o.oangle 0 x = 0

views.nl_informal: If the second vector passed to `oangle` is 0, the result is 0.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_zero_right (x : V) : o.oangle x 0 = 0

views.nl_informal: If the two vectors passed to `oangle` are the same, the result is 0.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_self (x : V) : o.oangle x x = 0

views.nl_informal: If the angle between two vectors is nonzero, the first vector is nonzero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.left_ne_zero_of_oangle_ne_zero {x y : V} (h : o.oangle x y ≠ 0) : x ≠ 0

views.nl_informal: If the angle between two vectors is nonzero, the second vector is nonzero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.right_ne_zero_of_oangle_ne_zero {x y : V} (h : o.oangle x y ≠ 0) : y ≠ 0

views.nl_informal: If the angle between two vectors is nonzero, the vectors are not equal.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.ne_of_oangle_ne_zero {x y : V} (h : o.oangle x y ≠ 0) : x ≠ y

views.nl_informal: If the angle between two vectors is `π`, the first vector is nonzero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.left_ne_zero_of_oangle_eq_pi {x y : V} (h : o.oangle x y = π) : x ≠ 0

views.nl_informal: If the angle between two vectors is `π`, the second vector is nonzero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.right_ne_zero_of_oangle_eq_pi {x y : V} (h : o.oangle x y = π) : y ≠ 0

views.nl_informal: If the angle between two vectors is `π`, the vectors are not equal.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.ne_of_oangle_eq_pi {x y : V} (h : o.oangle x y = π) : x ≠ y

views.nl_informal: If the angle between two vectors is `π / 2`, the first vector is nonzero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.left_ne_zero_of_oangle_eq_pi_div_two {x y : V} (h : o.oangle x y = (π / 2 : ℝ)) : x ≠ 0

views.nl_informal: If the angle between two vectors is `π / 2`, the second vector is nonzero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.right_ne_zero_of_oangle_eq_pi_div_two {x y : V} (h : o.oangle x y = (π / 2 : ℝ)) : y ≠ 0

views.nl_informal: If the angle between two vectors is `π / 2`, the vectors are not equal.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.ne_of_oangle_eq_pi_div_two {x y : V} (h : o.oangle x y = (π / 2 : ℝ)) : x ≠ y

views.nl_informal: If the angle between two vectors is `-π / 2`, the first vector is nonzero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.left_ne_zero_of_oangle_eq_neg_pi_div_two {x y : V} (h : o.oangle x y = (-π / 2 : ℝ)) : x ≠ 0

views.nl_informal: If the angle between two vectors is `-π / 2`, the second vector is nonzero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.right_ne_zero_of_oangle_eq_neg_pi_div_two {x y : V} (h : o.oangle x y = (-π / 2 : ℝ)) : y ≠ 0

views.nl_informal: If the angle between two vectors is `-π / 2`, the vectors are not equal.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.ne_of_oangle_eq_neg_pi_div_two {x y : V} (h : o.oangle x y = (-π / 2 : ℝ)) : x ≠ y

views.nl_informal: If the sign of the angle between two vectors is nonzero, the first vector is nonzero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.left_ne_zero_of_oangle_sign_ne_zero {x y : V} (h : (o.oangle x y).sign ≠ 0) : x ≠ 0

views.nl_informal: If the sign of the angle between two vectors is nonzero, the second vector is nonzero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.right_ne_zero_of_oangle_sign_ne_zero {x y : V} (h : (o.oangle x y).sign ≠ 0) : y ≠ 0

views.nl_informal: If the sign of the angle between two vectors is nonzero, the vectors are not equal.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.ne_of_oangle_sign_ne_zero {x y : V} (h : (o.oangle x y).sign ≠ 0) : x ≠ y

views.nl_informal: If the sign of the angle between two vectors is positive, the first vector is nonzero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.left_ne_zero_of_oangle_sign_eq_one {x y : V} (h : (o.oangle x y).sign = 1) : x ≠ 0

views.nl_informal: If the sign of the angle between two vectors is positive, the second vector is nonzero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.right_ne_zero_of_oangle_sign_eq_one {x y : V} (h : (o.oangle x y).sign = 1) : y ≠ 0

views.nl_informal: If the sign of the angle between two vectors is positive, the vectors are not equal.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.ne_of_oangle_sign_eq_one {x y : V} (h : (o.oangle x y).sign = 1) : x ≠ y

views.nl_informal: If the sign of the angle between two vectors is negative, the first vector is nonzero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.left_ne_zero_of_oangle_sign_eq_neg_one {x y : V} (h : (o.oangle x y).sign = -1) : x ≠ 0

views.nl_informal: If the sign of the angle between two vectors is negative, the second vector is nonzero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.right_ne_zero_of_oangle_sign_eq_neg_one {x y : V} (h : (o.oangle x y).sign = -1) : y ≠ 0

views.nl_informal: If the sign of the angle between two vectors is negative, the vectors are not equal.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.ne_of_oangle_sign_eq_neg_one {x y : V} (h : (o.oangle x y).sign = -1) : x ≠ y

views.nl_informal: Swapping the two vectors passed to `oangle` negates the angle.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_rev (x y : V) : o.oangle y x = -o.oangle x y

views.nl_informal: Adding the angles between two vectors in each order results in 0.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_add_oangle_rev (x y : V) : o.oangle x y + o.oangle y x = 0

views.nl_informal: Negating the first vector passed to `oangle` adds `π` to the angle.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_neg_left {x y : V} (hx : x ≠ 0) (hy : y ≠ 0) : o.oangle (-x) y = o.oangle x y + π

views.nl_informal: Negating the second vector passed to `oangle` adds `π` to the angle.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_neg_right {x y : V} (hx : x ≠ 0) (hy : y ≠ 0) : o.oangle x (-y) = o.oangle x y + π

views.nl_informal: Negating the first vector passed to `oangle` does not change twice the angle.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.two_zsmul_oangle_neg_left (x y : V) : (2 : ℤ) • o.oangle (-x) y = (2 : ℤ) • o.oangle x y

views.nl_informal: Negating the second vector passed to `oangle` does not change twice the angle.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.two_zsmul_oangle_neg_right (x y : V) : (2 : ℤ) • o.oangle x (-y) = (2 : ℤ) • o.oangle x y

views.nl_informal: Negating both vectors passed to `oangle` does not change the angle.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_neg_neg (x y : V) : o.oangle (-x) (-y) = o.oangle x y

views.nl_informal: Negating the first vector produces the same angle as negating the second vector.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_neg_left_eq_neg_right (x y : V) : o.oangle (-x) y = o.oangle x (-y)

views.nl_informal: The angle between the negation of a nonzero vector and that vector is `π`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_neg_self_left {x : V} (hx : x ≠ 0) : o.oangle (-x) x = π

views.nl_informal: The angle between a nonzero vector and its negation is `π`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_neg_self_right {x : V} (hx : x ≠ 0) : o.oangle x (-x) = π

views.nl_informal: Twice the angle between the negation of a vector and that vector is 0.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.two_zsmul_oangle_neg_self_left (x : V) : (2 : ℤ) • o.oangle (-x) x = 0

views.nl_informal: Twice the angle between a vector and its negation is 0.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.two_zsmul_oangle_neg_self_right (x : V) : (2 : ℤ) • o.oangle x (-x) = 0

views.nl_informal:
Adding the angles between two vectors in each order, with the first vector in each angle
negated, results in 0.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_add_oangle_rev_neg_left (x y : V) : o.oangle (-x) y + o.oangle (-y) x = 0

views.nl_informal:
Adding the angles between two vectors in each order, with the second vector in each angle
negated, results in 0.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_add_oangle_rev_neg_right (x y : V) : o.oangle x (-y) + o.oangle y (-x) = 0

views.nl_informal:
Multiplying the first vector passed to `oangle` by a positive real does not change the
angle.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_smul_left_of_pos (x y : V) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) : o.oangle (r • x) y = o.oangle x y

views.nl_informal:
Multiplying the second vector passed to `oangle` by a positive real does not change the
angle.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_smul_right_of_pos (x y : V) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) : o.oangle x (r • y) = o.oangle x y

views.nl_informal:
Multiplying the first vector passed to `oangle` by a negative real produces the same angle
as negating that vector.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_smul_left_of_neg (x y : V) {r : ℝ} (hr : r < 0) : o.oangle (r • x) y = o.oangle (-x) y

views.nl_informal:
Multiplying the second vector passed to `oangle` by a negative real produces the same angle
as negating that vector.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_smul_right_of_neg (x y : V) {r : ℝ} (hr : r < 0) : o.oangle x (r • y) = o.oangle x (-y)

views.nl_informal: The angle between a nonnegative multiple of a vector and that vector is 0.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_smul_left_self_of_nonneg (x : V) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 ≤ r) : o.oangle (r • x) x = 0

views.nl_informal: The angle between a vector and a nonnegative multiple of that vector is 0.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_smul_right_self_of_nonneg (x : V) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 ≤ r) : o.oangle x (r • x) = 0

views.nl_informal: The angle between two nonnegative multiples of the same vector is 0.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_smul_smul_self_of_nonneg (x : V) {r₁ r₂ : ℝ} (hr₁ : 0 ≤ r₁) (hr₂ : 0 ≤ r₂) : o.oangle (r₁ • x) (r₂ • x) = 0

views.nl_informal:
Multiplying the first vector passed to `oangle` by a nonzero real does not change twice the
angle.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.two_zsmul_oangle_smul_left_of_ne_zero (x y : V) {r : ℝ} (hr : r ≠ 0) : (2 : ℤ) • o.oangle (r • x) y = (2 : ℤ) • o.oangle x y

views.nl_informal:
Multiplying the second vector passed to `oangle` by a nonzero real does not change twice the
angle.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.two_zsmul_oangle_smul_right_of_ne_zero (x y : V) {r : ℝ} (hr : r ≠ 0) : (2 : ℤ) • o.oangle x (r • y) = (2 : ℤ) • o.oangle x y

views.nl_informal: Twice the angle between a multiple of a vector and that vector is 0.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.two_zsmul_oangle_smul_left_self (x : V) {r : ℝ} : (2 : ℤ) • o.oangle (r • x) x = 0

views.nl_informal: Twice the angle between a vector and a multiple of that vector is 0.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.two_zsmul_oangle_smul_right_self (x : V) {r : ℝ} : (2 : ℤ) • o.oangle x (r • x) = 0

views.nl_informal: Twice the angle between two multiples of a vector is 0.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.two_zsmul_oangle_smul_smul_self (x : V) {r₁ r₂ : ℝ} : (2 : ℤ) • o.oangle (r₁ • x) (r₂ • x) = 0

views.nl_informal:
If the spans of two vectors are equal, twice angles with those vectors on the left are
equal.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.two_zsmul_oangle_left_of_span_eq {x y : V} (z : V) (h : (ℝ ∙ x) = ℝ ∙ y) : (2 : ℤ) • o.oangle x z = (2 : ℤ) • o.oangle y z

views.nl_informal:
If the spans of two vectors are equal, twice angles with those vectors on the right are
equal.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.two_zsmul_oangle_right_of_span_eq (x : V) {y z : V} (h : (ℝ ∙ y) = ℝ ∙ z) : (2 : ℤ) • o.oangle x y = (2 : ℤ) • o.oangle x z

views.nl_informal:
If the spans of two pairs of vectors are equal, twice angles between those vectors are
equal.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.two_zsmul_oangle_of_span_eq_of_span_eq {w x y z : V} (hwx : (ℝ ∙ w) = ℝ ∙ x) (hyz : (ℝ ∙ y) = ℝ ∙ z) : (2 : ℤ) • o.oangle w y = (2 : ℤ) • o.oangle x z

views.nl_informal:
The oriented angle between two vectors is zero if and only if the angle with the vectors
swapped is zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_eq_zero_iff_oangle_rev_eq_zero {x y : V} : o.oangle x y = 0 ↔ o.oangle y x = 0

views.nl_informal: The oriented angle between two vectors is zero if and only if they are on the same ray.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_eq_zero_iff_sameRay {x y : V} : o.oangle x y = 0 ↔ SameRay ℝ x y

views.nl_informal:
The oriented angle between two vectors is `π` if and only if the angle with the vectors
swapped is `π`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_eq_pi_iff_oangle_rev_eq_pi {x y : V} : o.oangle x y = π ↔ o.oangle y x = π

views.nl_informal:
The oriented angle between two vectors is `π` if and only they are nonzero and the first is
on the same ray as the negation of the second.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_eq_pi_iff_sameRay_neg {x y : V} : o.oangle x y = π ↔ x ≠ 0 ∧ y ≠ 0 ∧ SameRay ℝ x (-y)

views.nl_informal:
The oriented angle between two vectors is zero or `π` if and only if those two vectors are
not linearly independent.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_eq_zero_or_eq_pi_iff_not_linearIndependent {x y : V} : o.oangle x y = 0 ∨ o.oangle x y = π ↔ ¬LinearIndependent ℝ ![x, y]

views.nl_informal:
The oriented angle between two vectors is zero or `π` if and only if the first vector is zero
or the second is a multiple of the first.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_eq_zero_or_eq_pi_iff_right_eq_smul {x y : V} : o.oangle x y = 0 ∨ o.oangle x y = π ↔ x = 0 ∨ ∃ r : ℝ, y = r • x

views.nl_informal:
The oriented angle between two vectors is not zero or `π` if and only if those two vectors
are linearly independent.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_ne_zero_and_ne_pi_iff_linearIndependent {x y : V} : o.oangle x y ≠ 0 ∧ o.oangle x y ≠ π ↔ LinearIndependent ℝ ![x, y]

views.nl_informal: Two vectors are equal if and only if they have equal norms and zero angle between them.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.eq_iff_norm_eq_and_oangle_eq_zero (x y : V) : x = y ↔ ‖x‖ = ‖y‖ ∧ o.oangle x y = 0

views.nl_informal: Two vectors with equal norms are equal if and only if they have zero angle between them.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.eq_iff_oangle_eq_zero_of_norm_eq {x y : V} (h : ‖x‖ = ‖y‖) : x = y ↔ o.oangle x y = 0

views.nl_informal: Two vectors with zero angle between them are equal if and only if they have equal norms.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.eq_iff_norm_eq_of_oangle_eq_zero {x y : V} (h : o.oangle x y = 0) : x = y ↔ ‖x‖ = ‖y‖

views.nl_informal:
Given three nonzero vectors, the angle between the first and the second plus the angle
between the second and the third equals the angle between the first and the third.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_add {x y z : V} (hx : x ≠ 0) (hy : y ≠ 0) (hz : z ≠ 0) : o.oangle x y + o.oangle y z = o.oangle x z

views.nl_informal:
Given three nonzero vectors, the angle between the second and the third plus the angle
between the first and the second equals the angle between the first and the third.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_add_swap {x y z : V} (hx : x ≠ 0) (hy : y ≠ 0) (hz : z ≠ 0) : o.oangle y z + o.oangle x y = o.oangle x z

views.nl_informal:
Given three nonzero vectors, the angle between the first and the third minus the angle
between the first and the second equals the angle between the second and the third.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_sub_left {x y z : V} (hx : x ≠ 0) (hy : y ≠ 0) (hz : z ≠ 0) : o.oangle x z - o.oangle x y = o.oangle y z

views.nl_informal:
Given three nonzero vectors, the angle between the first and the third minus the angle
between the second and the third equals the angle between the first and the second.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_sub_right {x y z : V} (hx : x ≠ 0) (hy : y ≠ 0) (hz : z ≠ 0) : o.oangle x z - o.oangle y z = o.oangle x y

views.nl_informal: Given three nonzero vectors, adding the angles between them in cyclic order results in 0.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_add_cyc3 {x y z : V} (hx : x ≠ 0) (hy : y ≠ 0) (hz : z ≠ 0) : o.oangle x y + o.oangle y z + o.oangle z x = 0

views.nl_informal:
Given three nonzero vectors, adding the angles between them in cyclic order, with the first
vector in each angle negated, results in π. If the vectors add to 0, this is a version of the
sum of the angles of a triangle.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_add_cyc3_neg_left {x y z : V} (hx : x ≠ 0) (hy : y ≠ 0) (hz : z ≠ 0) : o.oangle (-x) y + o.oangle (-y) z + o.oangle (-z) x = π

views.nl_informal:
Given three nonzero vectors, adding the angles between them in cyclic order, with the second
vector in each angle negated, results in π. If the vectors add to 0, this is a version of the
sum of the angles of a triangle.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_add_cyc3_neg_right {x y z : V} (hx : x ≠ 0) (hy : y ≠ 0) (hz : z ≠ 0) : o.oangle x (-y) + o.oangle y (-z) + o.oangle z (-x) = π

views.nl_informal: Pons asinorum, oriented vector angle form.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_sub_eq_oangle_sub_rev_of_norm_eq {x y : V} (h : ‖x‖ = ‖y‖) : o.oangle x (x - y) = o.oangle (y - x) y

views.nl_informal:
The angle at the apex of an isosceles triangle is `π` minus twice a base angle, oriented
vector angle form.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_eq_pi_sub_two_zsmul_oangle_sub_of_norm_eq {x y : V} (hn : x ≠ y) (h : ‖x‖ = ‖y‖) : o.oangle y x = π - (2 : ℤ) • o.oangle (y - x) y

views.nl_informal:
The angle between two vectors, with respect to an orientation given by `Orientation.map`
with a linear isometric equivalence, equals the angle between those two vectors, transformed by
the inverse of that equivalence, with respect to the original orientation.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_map (x y : V') (f : V ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] V') : (Orientation.map (Fin 2) f.toLinearEquiv o).oangle x y = o.oangle (f.symm x) (f.symm y)

views.nl_informal:
The oriented angle on an oriented real inner product space of dimension 2 can be evaluated in
terms of a complex-number representation of the space.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_map_complex (f : V ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] ℂ) (hf : Orientation.map (Fin 2) f.toLinearEquiv o = Complex.orientation) (x y : V) : o.oangle x y = Complex.arg (conj (f x) * f y)

views.nl_informal: Negating the orientation negates the value of `oangle`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_neg_orientation_eq_neg (x y : V) : (-o).oangle x y = -o.oangle x y

views.nl_informal:
The inner product of two vectors is the product of the norms and the cosine of the oriented
angle between the vectors.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.inner_eq_norm_mul_norm_mul_cos_oangle (x y : V) : ⟪x, y⟫ = ‖x‖ * ‖y‖ * Real.Angle.cos (o.oangle x y)

views.nl_informal:
The cosine of the oriented angle between two nonzero vectors is the inner product divided by
the product of the norms.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.cos_oangle_eq_inner_div_norm_mul_norm {x y : V} (hx : x ≠ 0) (hy : y ≠ 0) : Real.Angle.cos (o.oangle x y) = ⟪x, y⟫ / (‖x‖ * ‖y‖)

views.nl_informal:
The cosine of the oriented angle between two nonzero vectors equals that of the unoriented
angle.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.cos_oangle_eq_cos_angle {x y : V} (hx : x ≠ 0) (hy : y ≠ 0) : Real.Angle.cos (o.oangle x y) = Real.cos (InnerProductGeometry.angle x y)

views.nl_informal: The oriented angle between two nonzero vectors is plus or minus the unoriented angle.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_eq_angle_or_eq_neg_angle {x y : V} (hx : x ≠ 0) (hy : y ≠ 0) : o.oangle x y = InnerProductGeometry.angle x y ∨ o.oangle x y = -InnerProductGeometry.angle x y

views.nl_informal:
The unoriented angle between two nonzero vectors is the absolute value of the oriented angle,
converted to a real.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.angle_eq_abs_oangle_toReal {x y : V} (hx : x ≠ 0) (hy : y ≠ 0) : InnerProductGeometry.angle x y = |(o.oangle x y).toReal|

views.nl_informal:
If the sign of the oriented angle between two vectors is zero, either one of the vectors is
zero or the unoriented angle is 0 or π.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.eq_zero_or_angle_eq_zero_or_pi_of_sign_oangle_eq_zero {x y : V} (h : (o.oangle x y).sign = 0) : x = 0 ∨ y = 0 ∨ InnerProductGeometry.angle x y = 0 ∨ InnerProductGeometry.angle x y = π

views.nl_informal:
If two unoriented angles are equal, and the signs of the corresponding oriented angles are
equal, then the oriented angles are equal (even in degenerate cases).
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_eq_of_angle_eq_of_sign_eq {w x y z : V} (h : InnerProductGeometry.angle w x = InnerProductGeometry.angle y z) (hs : (o.oangle w x).sign = (o.oangle y z).sign) : o.oangle w x = o.oangle y z

views.nl_informal:
If the signs of two oriented angles between nonzero vectors are equal, the oriented angles are
equal if and only if the unoriented angles are equal.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.angle_eq_iff_oangle_eq_of_sign_eq {w x y z : V} (hw : w ≠ 0) (hx : x ≠ 0) (hy : y ≠ 0) (hz : z ≠ 0) (hs : (o.oangle w x).sign = (o.oangle y z).sign) : InnerProductGeometry.angle w x = InnerProductGeometry.angle y z ↔ o.oangle w x = o.oangle y z

views.nl_informal: The oriented angle between two vectors equals the unoriented angle if the sign is positive.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_eq_angle_of_sign_eq_one {x y : V} (h : (o.oangle x y).sign = 1) : o.oangle x y = InnerProductGeometry.angle x y

views.nl_informal:
The oriented angle between two vectors equals minus the unoriented angle if the sign is
negative.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_eq_neg_angle_of_sign_eq_neg_one {x y : V} (h : (o.oangle x y).sign = -1) : o.oangle x y = -InnerProductGeometry.angle x y

views.nl_informal:
The oriented angle between two nonzero vectors is zero if and only if the unoriented angle
is zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_eq_zero_iff_angle_eq_zero {x y : V} (hx : x ≠ 0) (hy : y ≠ 0) : o.oangle x y = 0 ↔ InnerProductGeometry.angle x y = 0

views.nl_informal: The oriented angle between two vectors is `π` if and only if the unoriented angle is `π`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_eq_pi_iff_angle_eq_pi {x y : V} : o.oangle x y = π ↔ InnerProductGeometry.angle x y = π

views.nl_informal:
One of two vectors is zero or the oriented angle between them is plus or minus `π / 2` if
and only if the inner product of those vectors is zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.eq_zero_or_oangle_eq_iff_inner_eq_zero {x y : V} : x = 0 ∨ y = 0 ∨ o.oangle x y = (π / 2 : ℝ) ∨ o.oangle x y = (-π / 2 : ℝ) ↔ ⟪x, y⟫ = 0

views.nl_informal:
If the oriented angle between two vectors is `π / 2`, the inner product of those vectors
is zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.inner_eq_zero_of_oangle_eq_pi_div_two {x y : V} (h : o.oangle x y = (π / 2 : ℝ)) : ⟪x, y⟫ = 0

views.nl_informal:
If the oriented angle between two vectors is `π / 2`, the inner product of those vectors
(reversed) is zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.inner_rev_eq_zero_of_oangle_eq_pi_div_two {x y : V} (h : o.oangle x y = (π / 2 : ℝ)) : ⟪y, x⟫ = 0

views.nl_informal:
If the oriented angle between two vectors is `-π / 2`, the inner product of those vectors
is zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.inner_eq_zero_of_oangle_eq_neg_pi_div_two {x y : V} (h : o.oangle x y = (-π / 2 : ℝ)) : ⟪x, y⟫ = 0

views.nl_informal:
If the oriented angle between two vectors is `-π / 2`, the inner product of those vectors
(reversed) is zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.inner_rev_eq_zero_of_oangle_eq_neg_pi_div_two {x y : V} (h : o.oangle x y = (-π / 2 : ℝ)) : ⟪y, x⟫ = 0

views.nl_informal: Negating the first vector passed to `oangle` negates the sign of the angle.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_sign_neg_left (x y : V) : (o.oangle (-x) y).sign = -(o.oangle x y).sign

views.nl_informal: Negating the second vector passed to `oangle` negates the sign of the angle.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_sign_neg_right (x y : V) : (o.oangle x (-y)).sign = -(o.oangle x y).sign

views.nl_informal:
Multiplying the first vector passed to `oangle` by a real multiplies the sign of the angle by
the sign of the real.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_sign_smul_left (x y : V) (r : ℝ) : (o.oangle (r • x) y).sign = SignType.sign r * (o.oangle x y).sign

views.nl_informal:
Multiplying the second vector passed to `oangle` by a real multiplies the sign of the angle by
the sign of the real.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_sign_smul_right (x y : V) (r : ℝ) : (o.oangle x (r • y)).sign = SignType.sign r * (o.oangle x y).sign

views.nl_informal:
Adding a multiple of the first vector passed to `oangle` to the second vector does not change
the sign of the angle.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_sign_smul_add_right (x y : V) (r : ℝ) : (o.oangle x (r • x + y)).sign = (o.oangle x y).sign

views.nl_informal:
Adding a multiple of the second vector passed to `oangle` to the first vector does not change
the sign of the angle.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_sign_add_smul_left (x y : V) (r : ℝ) : (o.oangle (x + r • y) y).sign = (o.oangle x y).sign

views.nl_informal:
Subtracting a multiple of the first vector passed to `oangle` from the second vector does
not change the sign of the angle.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_sign_sub_smul_right (x y : V) (r : ℝ) : (o.oangle x (y - r • x)).sign = (o.oangle x y).sign

views.nl_informal:
Subtracting a multiple of the second vector passed to `oangle` from the first vector does
not change the sign of the angle.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_sign_sub_smul_left (x y : V) (r : ℝ) : (o.oangle (x - r • y) y).sign = (o.oangle x y).sign

views.nl_informal:
Adding the first vector passed to `oangle` to the second vector does not change the sign of
the angle.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_sign_add_right (x y : V) : (o.oangle x (x + y)).sign = (o.oangle x y).sign

views.nl_informal:
Adding the second vector passed to `oangle` to the first vector does not change the sign of
the angle.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_sign_add_left (x y : V) : (o.oangle (x + y) y).sign = (o.oangle x y).sign

views.nl_informal:
Subtracting the first vector passed to `oangle` from the second vector does not change the
sign of the angle.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_sign_sub_right (x y : V) : (o.oangle x (y - x)).sign = (o.oangle x y).sign

views.nl_informal:
Subtracting the second vector passed to `oangle` from the first vector does not change the
sign of the angle.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_sign_sub_left (x y : V) : (o.oangle (x - y) y).sign = (o.oangle x y).sign

views.nl_informal:
Subtracting the second vector passed to `oangle` from a multiple of the first vector negates
the sign of the angle.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_sign_smul_sub_right (x y : V) (r : ℝ) : (o.oangle x (r • x - y)).sign = -(o.oangle x y).sign

views.nl_informal:
Subtracting the first vector passed to `oangle` from a multiple of the second vector negates
the sign of the angle.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_sign_smul_sub_left (x y : V) (r : ℝ) : (o.oangle (r • y - x) y).sign = -(o.oangle x y).sign

views.nl_informal:
Subtracting the second vector passed to `oangle` from the first vector negates the sign of
the angle.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_sign_sub_right_eq_neg (x y : V) : (o.oangle x (x - y)).sign = -(o.oangle x y).sign

views.nl_informal:
Subtracting the first vector passed to `oangle` from the second vector negates the sign of
the angle.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_sign_sub_left_eq_neg (x y : V) : (o.oangle (y - x) y).sign = -(o.oangle x y).sign

views.nl_informal:
Subtracting the first vector passed to `oangle` from the second vector then swapping the
vectors does not change the sign of the angle.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_sign_sub_right_swap (x y : V) : (o.oangle y (y - x)).sign = (o.oangle x y).sign

views.nl_informal:
Subtracting the second vector passed to `oangle` from the first vector then swapping the
vectors does not change the sign of the angle.

views.nl_informal: The determinant of `rotation` (as a linear map) is equal to `1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.det_rotation (θ : Real.Angle) : LinearMap.det (o.rotation θ).toLinearMap = 1

views.nl_informal: The determinant of `rotation` (as a linear equiv) is equal to `1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.linearEquiv_det_rotation (θ : Real.Angle) : LinearEquiv.det (o.rotation θ).toLinearEquiv = 1

views.nl_informal: The inverse of `rotation` is rotation by the negation of the angle.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.rotation_symm (θ : Real.Angle) : (o.rotation θ).symm = o.rotation (-θ)

views.nl_informal: Rotation by 0 is the identity.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.rotation_zero : o.rotation 0 = LinearIsometryEquiv.refl ℝ V

views.nl_informal: Rotation by π is negation.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.rotation_pi : o.rotation π = LinearIsometryEquiv.neg ℝ

views.nl_informal: Rotation by π is negation.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.rotation_pi_apply (x : V) : o.rotation π x = -x

views.nl_informal: Rotation by π / 2 is the "right-angle-rotation" map `J`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.rotation_pi_div_two : o.rotation (π / 2 : ℝ) = J

views.nl_informal: Rotating twice is equivalent to rotating by the sum of the angles.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.rotation_rotation (θ₁ θ₂ : Real.Angle) (x : V) : o.rotation θ₁ (o.rotation θ₂ x) = o.rotation (θ₁ + θ₂) x

views.nl_informal: Rotating twice is equivalent to rotating by the sum of the angles.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.rotation_trans (θ₁ θ₂ : Real.Angle) : (o.rotation θ₁).trans (o.rotation θ₂) = o.rotation (θ₂ + θ₁)

views.nl_informal: Rotating the first of two vectors by `θ` scales their Kahler form by `cos θ - sin θ * I`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.kahler_rotation_left (x y : V) (θ : Real.Angle) : o.kahler (o.rotation θ x) y = conj (θ.toCircle : ℂ) * o.kahler x y

views.nl_informal: Negating a rotation is equivalent to rotation by π plus the angle.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.neg_rotation (θ : Real.Angle) (x : V) : -o.rotation θ x = o.rotation (π + θ) x

views.nl_informal: Negating a rotation by -π / 2 is equivalent to rotation by π / 2.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.neg_rotation_neg_pi_div_two (x : V) : -o.rotation (-π / 2 : ℝ) x = o.rotation (π / 2 : ℝ) x

views.nl_informal: Negating a rotation by π / 2 is equivalent to rotation by -π / 2.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.neg_rotation_pi_div_two (x : V) : -o.rotation (π / 2 : ℝ) x = o.rotation (-π / 2 : ℝ) x

views.nl_informal: Rotating the first of two vectors by `θ` scales their Kahler form by `cos (-θ) + sin (-θ) * I`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.kahler_rotation_left' (x y : V) (θ : Real.Angle) : o.kahler (o.rotation θ x) y = (-θ).toCircle * o.kahler x y

views.nl_informal: Rotating the second of two vectors by `θ` scales their Kahler form by `cos θ + sin θ * I`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.kahler_rotation_right (x y : V) (θ : Real.Angle) : o.kahler x (o.rotation θ y) = θ.toCircle * o.kahler x y

views.nl_informal: Rotating the first vector by `θ` subtracts `θ` from the angle between two vectors.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_rotation_left {x y : V} (hx : x ≠ 0) (hy : y ≠ 0) (θ : Real.Angle) : o.oangle (o.rotation θ x) y = o.oangle x y - θ

views.nl_informal: Rotating the second vector by `θ` adds `θ` to the angle between two vectors.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_rotation_right {x y : V} (hx : x ≠ 0) (hy : y ≠ 0) (θ : Real.Angle) : o.oangle x (o.rotation θ y) = o.oangle x y + θ

views.nl_informal: The rotation of a vector by `θ` has an angle of `-θ` from that vector.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_rotation_self_left {x : V} (hx : x ≠ 0) (θ : Real.Angle) : o.oangle (o.rotation θ x) x = -θ

views.nl_informal: A vector has an angle of `θ` from the rotation of that vector by `θ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_rotation_self_right {x : V} (hx : x ≠ 0) (θ : Real.Angle) : o.oangle x (o.rotation θ x) = θ

views.nl_informal: Rotating the first vector by the angle between the two vectors results in an angle of 0.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_rotation_oangle_left (x y : V) : o.oangle (o.rotation (o.oangle x y) x) y = 0

views.nl_informal:
Rotating the first vector by the angle between the two vectors and swapping the vectors
results in an angle of 0.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_rotation_oangle_right (x y : V) : o.oangle y (o.rotation (o.oangle x y) x) = 0

views.nl_informal: Rotating both vectors by the same angle does not change the angle between those vectors.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_rotation (x y : V) (θ : Real.Angle) : o.oangle (o.rotation θ x) (o.rotation θ y) = o.oangle x y

views.nl_informal: A rotation of a nonzero vector equals that vector if and only if the angle is zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.rotation_eq_self_iff_angle_eq_zero {x : V} (hx : x ≠ 0) (θ : Real.Angle) : o.rotation θ x = x ↔ θ = 0

views.nl_informal: A nonzero vector equals a rotation of that vector if and only if the angle is zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.eq_rotation_self_iff_angle_eq_zero {x : V} (hx : x ≠ 0) (θ : Real.Angle) : x = o.rotation θ x ↔ θ = 0

views.nl_informal: A rotation of a vector equals that vector if and only if the vector or the angle is zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.rotation_eq_self_iff (x : V) (θ : Real.Angle) : o.rotation θ x = x ↔ x = 0 ∨ θ = 0

views.nl_informal: A vector equals a rotation of that vector if and only if the vector or the angle is zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.eq_rotation_self_iff (x : V) (θ : Real.Angle) : x = o.rotation θ x ↔ x = 0 ∨ θ = 0

views.nl_informal:
Rotating a vector by the angle to another vector gives the second vector if and only if the
norms are equal.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.rotation_oangle_eq_iff_norm_eq (x y : V) : o.rotation (o.oangle x y) x = y ↔ ‖x‖ = ‖y‖

views.nl_informal:
The angle between two nonzero vectors is `θ` if and only if the second vector is the first
rotated by `θ` and scaled by the ratio of the norms.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_eq_iff_eq_norm_div_norm_smul_rotation_of_ne_zero {x y : V} (hx : x ≠ 0) (hy : y ≠ 0) (θ : Real.Angle) : o.oangle x y = θ ↔ y = (‖y‖ / ‖x‖) • o.rotation θ x

views.nl_informal:
The angle between two nonzero vectors is `θ` if and only if the second vector is the first
rotated by `θ` and scaled by a positive real.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_eq_iff_eq_pos_smul_rotation_of_ne_zero {x y : V} (hx : x ≠ 0) (hy : y ≠ 0) (θ : Real.Angle) : o.oangle x y = θ ↔ ∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ y = r • o.rotation θ x

views.nl_informal:
The angle between two vectors is `θ` if and only if they are nonzero and the second vector
is the first rotated by `θ` and scaled by the ratio of the norms, or `θ` and at least one of the
vectors are zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_eq_iff_eq_norm_div_norm_smul_rotation_or_eq_zero {x y : V} (θ : Real.Angle) : o.oangle x y = θ ↔ x ≠ 0 ∧ y ≠ 0 ∧ y = (‖y‖ / ‖x‖) • o.rotation θ x ∨ θ = 0 ∧ (x = 0 ∨ y = 0)

views.nl_informal:
The angle between two vectors is `θ` if and only if they are nonzero and the second vector
is the first rotated by `θ` and scaled by a positive real, or `θ` and at least one of the
vectors are zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.oangle_eq_iff_eq_pos_smul_rotation_or_eq_zero {x y : V} (θ : Real.Angle) : o.oangle x y = θ ↔ (x ≠ 0 ∧ y ≠ 0 ∧ ∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ y = r • o.rotation θ x) ∨ θ = 0 ∧ (x = 0 ∨ y = 0)

views.nl_informal: Any linear isometric equivalence in `V` with positive determinant is `rotation`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.exists_linearIsometryEquiv_eq_of_det_pos {f : V ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] V} (hd : 0 < LinearMap.det (f.toLinearEquiv : V →ₗ[ℝ] V)) : ∃ θ : Real.Angle, f = o.rotation θ

views.nl_informal:
Rotation in an oriented real inner product space of dimension 2 can be evaluated in terms of a
complex-number representation of the space.

views.nl_informal: Negating the orientation negates the angle in `rotation`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.rotation_neg_orientation_eq_neg (θ : Real.Angle) : (-o).rotation θ = o.rotation (-θ)

views.nl_informal: The inner product between a `π / 2` rotation of a vector and that vector is zero.

views.nl_informal: The inner product between a vector and a `π / 2` rotation of that vector is zero.

views.nl_informal:

views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.inner_smul_rotation_pi_div_two_right (x : V) (r : ℝ) : ⟪x, r • o.rotation (π / 2 : ℝ) x⟫ = 0

views.nl_informal:
The inner product between a `π / 2` rotation of a vector and a multiple of that vector is

views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.inner_rotation_pi_div_two_left_smul (x : V) (r : ℝ) : ⟪o.rotation (π / 2 : ℝ) x, r • x⟫ = 0

views.nl_informal:
The inner product between a multiple of a vector and a `π / 2` rotation of that vector is
zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.inner_rotation_pi_div_two_right_smul (x : V) (r : ℝ) : ⟪r • x, o.rotation (π / 2 : ℝ) x⟫ = 0

views.nl_informal:
The inner product between a multiple of a `π / 2` rotation of a vector and a multiple of
that vector is zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.inner_smul_rotation_pi_div_two_smul_left (x : V) (r₁ r₂ : ℝ) : ⟪r₁ • o.rotation (π / 2 : ℝ) x, r₂ • x⟫ = 0

views.nl_informal:
The inner product between a multiple of a vector and a multiple of a `π / 2` rotation of
that vector is zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Orientation.inner_smul_rotation_pi_div_two_smul_right (x : V) (r₁ r₂ : ℝ) : ⟪r₂ • x, r₁ • o.rotation (π / 2 : ℝ) x⟫ = 0

views.nl_informal:
The inner product between two vectors is zero if and only if the first vector is zero or

views.nl_informal: Angles are translation invariant
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.angle_const_vadd (v : V) (p₁ p₂ p₃ : P) : ∠ (v +ᵥ p₁) (v +ᵥ p₂) (v +ᵥ p₃) = ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃

views.nl_informal: Angles are translation invariant
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.angle_const_vsub (p p₁ p₂ p₃ : P) : ∠ (p -ᵥ p₁) (p -ᵥ p₂) (p -ᵥ p₃) = ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃

views.nl_informal: Angles are translation invariant
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.angle_vsub_const (p₁ p₂ p₃ p : P) : ∠ (p₁ -ᵥ p) (p₂ -ᵥ p) (p₃ -ᵥ p) = ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃

views.nl_informal: Angles in a vector space are translation invariant
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.angle_add_const (v₁ v₂ v₃ : V) (v : V) : ∠ (v₁ + v) (v₂ + v) (v₃ + v) = ∠ v₁ v₂ v₃

views.nl_informal: Angles in a vector space are translation invariant
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.angle_const_add (v : V) (v₁ v₂ v₃ : V) : ∠ (v + v₁) (v + v₂) (v + v₃) = ∠ v₁ v₂ v₃

views.nl_informal: Angles in a vector space are translation invariant
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.angle_sub_const (v₁ v₂ v₃ : V) (v : V) : ∠ (v₁ - v) (v₂ - v) (v₃ - v) = ∠ v₁ v₂ v₃

views.nl_informal: Angles in a vector space are invariant to inversion
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.angle_const_sub (v : V) (v₁ v₂ v₃ : V) : ∠ (v - v₁) (v - v₂) (v - v₃) = ∠ v₁ v₂ v₃

views.nl_informal: Angles in a vector space are invariant to inversion
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.angle_neg (v₁ v₂ v₃ : V) : ∠ (-v₁) (-v₂) (-v₃) = ∠ v₁ v₂ v₃

views.nl_informal:
The angle at a point does not depend on the order of the other two
points.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.angle_comm (p₁ p₂ p₃ : P) : ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = ∠ p₃ p₂ p₁

views.nl_informal: The angle at a point is nonnegative.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.angle_nonneg (p₁ p₂ p₃ : P) : 0 ≤ ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃

views.nl_informal: The angle at a point is at most π.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.angle_le_pi (p₁ p₂ p₃ : P) : ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ ≤ π

views.nl_informal: The angle ∠AAB at a point is always `π / 2`.

views.nl_informal: The angle ∠ABB at a point is always `π / 2`.

views.nl_informal: The angle ∠ABA at a point is `0`, unless `A = B`.

views.nl_informal: If the angle ∠ABC at a point is π, the angle ∠BAC is 0.
