views.nl_informal: If the angle ∠ABC at a point is π, the angle ∠BCA is 0.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.angle_eq_zero_of_angle_eq_pi_right {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = π) : ∠ p₂ p₃ p₁ = 0

views.nl_informal: If ∠BCD = π, then ∠ABC = ∠ABD.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.angle_eq_angle_of_angle_eq_pi (p₁ : P) {p₂ p₃ p₄ : P} (h : ∠ p₂ p₃ p₄ = π) : ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = ∠ p₁ p₂ p₄

views.nl_informal: If ∠BCD = π, then ∠ACB + ∠ACD = π.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.angle_add_angle_eq_pi_of_angle_eq_pi (p₁ : P) {p₂ p₃ p₄ : P} (h : ∠ p₂ p₃ p₄ = π) : ∠ p₁ p₃ p₂ + ∠ p₁ p₃ p₄ = π

views.nl_informal:
**Vertical Angles Theorem**: angles opposite each other, formed by two intersecting straight
lines, are equal.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.angle_eq_angle_of_angle_eq_pi_of_angle_eq_pi {p₁ p₂ p₃ p₄ p₅ : P} (hapc : ∠ p₁ p₅ p₃ = π) (hbpd : ∠ p₂ p₅ p₄ = π) : ∠ p₁ p₅ p₂ = ∠ p₃ p₅ p₄

views.nl_informal: If ∠ABC = π then dist A B ≠ 0.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.left_dist_ne_zero_of_angle_eq_pi {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = π) : dist p₁ p₂ ≠ 0

views.nl_informal: If ∠ABC = π then dist C B ≠ 0.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.right_dist_ne_zero_of_angle_eq_pi {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = π) : dist p₃ p₂ ≠ 0

views.nl_informal: If ∠ABC = π, then (dist A C) = (dist A B) + (dist B C).
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.dist_eq_add_dist_of_angle_eq_pi {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = π) : dist p₁ p₃ = dist p₁ p₂ + dist p₃ p₂

views.nl_informal: If A ≠ B and C ≠ B then ∠ABC = π if and only if (dist A C) = (dist A B) + (dist B C).
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.dist_eq_add_dist_iff_angle_eq_pi {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (hp₁p₂ : p₁ ≠ p₂) (hp₃p₂ : p₃ ≠ p₂) : dist p₁ p₃ = dist p₁ p₂ + dist p₃ p₂ ↔ ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = π

views.nl_informal: If ∠ABC = 0, then (dist A C) = abs ((dist A B) - (dist B C)).
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.dist_eq_abs_sub_dist_of_angle_eq_zero {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = 0) : dist p₁ p₃ = |dist p₁ p₂ - dist p₃ p₂|

views.nl_informal: If A ≠ B and C ≠ B then ∠ABC = 0 if and only if (dist A C) = abs ((dist A B) - (dist B C)).
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.dist_eq_abs_sub_dist_iff_angle_eq_zero {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (hp₁p₂ : p₁ ≠ p₂) (hp₃p₂ : p₃ ≠ p₂) : dist p₁ p₃ = |dist p₁ p₂ - dist p₃ p₂| ↔ ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = 0

views.nl_informal: If M is the midpoint of the segment AB, then ∠AMB = π.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.angle_midpoint_eq_pi (p₁ p₂ : P) (hp₁p₂ : p₁ ≠ p₂) : ∠ p₁ (midpoint ℝ p₁ p₂) p₂ = π

views.nl_informal:
If M is the midpoint of the segment AB and C is the same distance from A as it is from B
then ∠CMA = π / 2.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.angle_left_midpoint_eq_pi_div_two_of_dist_eq {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : dist p₃ p₁ = dist p₃ p₂) : ∠ p₃ (midpoint ℝ p₁ p₂) p₁ = π / 2

views.nl_informal:
If M is the midpoint of the segment AB and C is the same distance from A as it is from B
then ∠CMB = π / 2.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.angle_right_midpoint_eq_pi_div_two_of_dist_eq {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : dist p₃ p₁ = dist p₃ p₂) : ∠ p₃ (midpoint ℝ p₁ p₂) p₂ = π / 2

views.nl_informal:
If the second of three points is strictly between the other two, the angle at that point
is π.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sbtw.angle₁₂₃_eq_pi {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : Sbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₃) : ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = π

views.nl_informal:
If the second of three points is strictly between the other two, the angle at that point
(reversed) is π.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sbtw.angle₃₂₁_eq_pi {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : Sbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₃) : ∠ p₃ p₂ p₁ = π

views.nl_informal:
The angle between three points is π if and only if the second point is strictly between the
other two.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.angle_eq_pi_iff_sbtw {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} : ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = π ↔ Sbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₃

views.nl_informal:
If the second of three points is weakly between the other two, and not equal to the first,
the angle at the first point is zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Wbtw.angle₂₁₃_eq_zero_of_ne {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : Wbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₃) (hp₂p₁ : p₂ ≠ p₁) : ∠ p₂ p₁ p₃ = 0

views.nl_informal:
If the second of three points is strictly between the other two, the angle at the first point
is zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sbtw.angle₂₁₃_eq_zero {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : Sbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₃) : ∠ p₂ p₁ p₃ = 0

views.nl_informal:
If the second of three points is weakly between the other two, and not equal to the first,
the angle at the first point (reversed) is zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Wbtw.angle₃₁₂_eq_zero_of_ne {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : Wbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₃) (hp₂p₁ : p₂ ≠ p₁) : ∠ p₃ p₁ p₂ = 0

views.nl_informal:
If the second of three points is strictly between the other two, the angle at the first point
(reversed) is zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sbtw.angle₃₁₂_eq_zero {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : Sbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₃) : ∠ p₃ p₁ p₂ = 0

views.nl_informal:
If the second of three points is weakly between the other two, and not equal to the third,
the angle at the third point is zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Wbtw.angle₂₃₁_eq_zero_of_ne {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : Wbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₃) (hp₂p₃ : p₂ ≠ p₃) : ∠ p₂ p₃ p₁ = 0

views.nl_informal:
If the second of three points is strictly between the other two, the angle at the third point
is zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sbtw.angle₂₃₁_eq_zero {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : Sbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₃) : ∠ p₂ p₃ p₁ = 0

views.nl_informal:
If the second of three points is weakly between the other two, and not equal to the third,
the angle at the third point (reversed) is zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Wbtw.angle₁₃₂_eq_zero_of_ne {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : Wbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₃) (hp₂p₃ : p₂ ≠ p₃) : ∠ p₁ p₃ p₂ = 0

views.nl_informal:
If the second of three points is strictly between the other two, the angle at the third point
(reversed) is zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sbtw.angle₁₃₂_eq_zero {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : Sbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₃) : ∠ p₁ p₃ p₂ = 0

views.nl_informal:
The angle between three points is zero if and only if one of the first and third points is
weakly between the other two, and not equal to the second.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.angle_eq_zero_iff_ne_and_wbtw {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} : ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = 0 ↔ p₁ ≠ p₂ ∧ Wbtw ℝ p₂ p₁ p₃ ∨ p₃ ≠ p₂ ∧ Wbtw ℝ p₂ p₃ p₁

views.nl_informal:
The angle between three points is zero if and only if one of the first and third points is
strictly between the other two, or those two points are equal but not equal to the second.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.angle_eq_zero_iff_eq_and_ne_or_sbtw {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} : ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = 0 ↔ p₁ = p₃ ∧ p₁ ≠ p₂ ∨ Sbtw ℝ p₂ p₁ p₃ ∨ Sbtw ℝ p₂ p₃ p₁

views.nl_informal:
Three points are collinear if and only if the first or third point equals the second or the
angle between them is 0 or π.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.collinear_iff_eq_or_eq_or_angle_eq_zero_or_angle_eq_pi {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} : Collinear ℝ ({p₁, p₂, p₃} : Set P) ↔ p₁ = p₂ ∨ p₃ = p₂ ∨ ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = 0 ∨ ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = π

views.nl_informal: If the angle between three points is 0, they are collinear.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.collinear_of_angle_eq_zero {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = 0) : Collinear ℝ ({p₁, p₂, p₃} : Set P)

views.nl_informal: If the angle between three points is π, they are collinear.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.collinear_of_angle_eq_pi {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = π) : Collinear ℝ ({p₁, p₂, p₃} : Set P)

views.nl_informal: If three points are not collinear, the angle between them is nonzero.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.angle_ne_zero_of_not_collinear {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : ¬Collinear ℝ ({p₁, p₂, p₃} : Set P)) : ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ ≠ 0

views.nl_informal: If three points are not collinear, the angle between them is not π.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.angle_ne_pi_of_not_collinear {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : ¬Collinear ℝ ({p₁, p₂, p₃} : Set P)) : ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ ≠ π

views.nl_informal: If three points are not collinear, the angle between them is positive.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.angle_pos_of_not_collinear {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : ¬Collinear ℝ ({p₁, p₂, p₃} : Set P)) : 0 < ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃

views.nl_informal: If three points are not collinear, the angle between them is less than π.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.angle_lt_pi_of_not_collinear {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : ¬Collinear ℝ ({p₁, p₂, p₃} : Set P)) : ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ < π

views.nl_informal: The cosine of the angle between three points is 1 if and only if the angle is 0.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.cos_eq_one_iff_angle_eq_zero {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} : Real.cos (∠ p₁ p₂ p₃) = 1 ↔ ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = 0

views.nl_informal: The cosine of the angle between three points is 0 if and only if the angle is π / 2.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.cos_eq_zero_iff_angle_eq_pi_div_two {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} : Real.cos (∠ p₁ p₂ p₃) = 0 ↔ ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = π / 2

views.nl_informal: The cosine of the angle between three points is -1 if and only if the angle is π.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.cos_eq_neg_one_iff_angle_eq_pi {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} : Real.cos (∠ p₁ p₂ p₃) = -1 ↔ ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = π

views.nl_informal: The sine of the angle between three points is 0 if and only if the angle is 0 or π.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.sin_eq_zero_iff_angle_eq_zero_or_angle_eq_pi {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} : Real.sin (∠ p₁ p₂ p₃) = 0 ↔ ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = 0 ∨ ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = π

views.nl_informal: The sine of the angle between three points is 1 if and only if the angle is π / 2.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.sin_eq_one_iff_angle_eq_pi_div_two {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} : Real.sin (∠ p₁ p₂ p₃) = 1 ↔ ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = π / 2

views.nl_informal:
Three points are collinear if and only if the first or third point equals the second or
the sine of the angle between three points is zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.collinear_iff_eq_or_eq_or_sin_eq_zero {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} : Collinear ℝ ({p₁, p₂, p₃} : Set P) ↔ p₁ = p₂ ∨ p₃ = p₂ ∨ Real.sin (∠ p₁ p₂ p₃) = 0

views.nl_informal: If three points are not collinear, the sine of the angle between them is positive.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.sin_pos_of_not_collinear {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : ¬Collinear ℝ ({p₁, p₂, p₃} : Set P)) : 0 < Real.sin (∠ p₁ p₂ p₃)

views.nl_informal: If three points are not collinear, the sine of the angle between them is nonzero.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.sin_ne_zero_of_not_collinear {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : ¬Collinear ℝ ({p₁, p₂, p₃} : Set P)) : Real.sin (∠ p₁ p₂ p₃) ≠ 0

views.nl_informal: If the sine of the angle between three points is 0, they are collinear.
views.lean_signature: theorem EuclideanGeometry.collinear_of_sin_eq_zero {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : Real.sin (∠ p₁ p₂ p₃) = 0) : Collinear ℝ ({p₁, p₂, p₃} : Set P)

views.nl_informal: The cosine of the angle between two vectors.
views.lean_signature: theorem InnerProductGeometry.cos_angle (x y : V) : Real.cos (angle x y) = ⟪x, y⟫ / (‖x‖ * ‖y‖)

views.nl_informal: The angle between two vectors does not depend on their order.
views.lean_signature: theorem InnerProductGeometry.angle_comm (x y : V) : angle x y = angle y x

views.nl_informal: The angle between the negation of two vectors.
views.lean_signature: theorem InnerProductGeometry.angle_neg_neg (x y : V) : angle (-x) (-y) = angle x y

views.nl_informal: The angle between two vectors is nonnegative.
views.lean_signature: theorem InnerProductGeometry.angle_nonneg (x y : V) : 0 ≤ angle x y

views.nl_informal: The angle between two vectors is at most π.
views.lean_signature: theorem InnerProductGeometry.angle_le_pi (x y : V) : angle x y ≤ π

views.nl_informal: The sine of the angle between two vectors is nonnegative.
views.lean_signature: theorem InnerProductGeometry.sin_angle_nonneg (x y : V) : 0 ≤ sin (angle x y)

views.nl_informal: The angle between a vector and the negation of another vector.
views.lean_signature: theorem InnerProductGeometry.angle_neg_right (x y : V) : angle x (-y) = π - angle x y

views.nl_informal: The angle between the negation of a vector and another vector.
views.lean_signature: theorem InnerProductGeometry.angle_neg_left (x y : V) : angle (-x) y = π - angle x y

views.nl_informal: The angle between the zero vector and a vector.
views.lean_signature: theorem InnerProductGeometry.angle_zero_left (x : V) : angle 0 x = π / 2

views.nl_informal: The angle between a vector and the zero vector.
views.lean_signature: theorem InnerProductGeometry.angle_zero_right (x : V) : angle x 0 = π / 2

views.nl_informal: The angle between a nonzero vector and itself.
views.lean_signature: theorem InnerProductGeometry.angle_self {x : V} (hx : x ≠ 0) : angle x x = 0

views.nl_informal: The angle between a nonzero vector and its negation.
views.lean_signature: theorem InnerProductGeometry.angle_self_neg_of_nonzero {x : V} (hx : x ≠ 0) : angle x (-x) = π

views.nl_informal:
The angle between the negation of a nonzero vector and that
vector.
views.lean_signature: theorem InnerProductGeometry.angle_neg_self_of_nonzero {x : V} (hx : x ≠ 0) : angle (-x) x = π

views.nl_informal: The angle between a vector and a positive multiple of a vector.
views.lean_signature: theorem InnerProductGeometry.angle_smul_right_of_pos (x y : V) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) : angle x (r • y) = angle x y

views.nl_informal: The angle between a positive multiple of a vector and a vector.
views.lean_signature: theorem InnerProductGeometry.angle_smul_left_of_pos (x y : V) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) : angle (r • x) y = angle x y

views.nl_informal: The angle between a vector and a negative multiple of a vector.
views.lean_signature: theorem InnerProductGeometry.angle_smul_right_of_neg (x y : V) {r : ℝ} (hr : r < 0) : angle x (r • y) = angle x (-y)

views.nl_informal: The angle between a negative multiple of a vector and a vector.
views.lean_signature: theorem InnerProductGeometry.angle_smul_left_of_neg (x y : V) {r : ℝ} (hr : r < 0) : angle (r • x) y = angle (-x) y

views.nl_informal:
The cosine of the angle between two vectors, multiplied by the
product of their norms.
views.lean_signature: theorem InnerProductGeometry.cos_angle_mul_norm_mul_norm (x y : V) : Real.cos (angle x y) * (‖x‖ * ‖y‖) = ⟪x, y⟫

views.nl_informal:
The sine of the angle between two vectors, multiplied by the
product of their norms.
views.lean_signature: theorem InnerProductGeometry.sin_angle_mul_norm_mul_norm (x y : V) : Real.sin (angle x y) * (‖x‖ * ‖y‖) = √(⟪x, x⟫ * ⟪y, y⟫ - ⟪x, y⟫ * ⟪x, y⟫)

views.nl_informal:
The angle between two vectors is zero if and only if they are
nonzero and one is a positive multiple of the other.
views.lean_signature: theorem InnerProductGeometry.angle_eq_zero_iff {x y : V} : angle x y = 0 ↔ x ≠ 0 ∧ ∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ y = r • x

views.nl_informal:
The angle between two vectors is π if and only if they are nonzero
and one is a negative multiple of the other.
views.lean_signature: theorem InnerProductGeometry.angle_eq_pi_iff {x y : V} : angle x y = π ↔ x ≠ 0 ∧ ∃ r : ℝ, r < 0 ∧ y = r • x

views.nl_informal:
If the angle between two vectors is π, the angles between those
vectors and a third vector add to π.
views.lean_signature: theorem InnerProductGeometry.angle_add_angle_eq_pi_of_angle_eq_pi {x y : V} (z : V) (h : angle x y = π) : angle x z + angle y z = π

views.nl_informal:
Two vectors have inner product 0 if and only if the angle between
them is π/2.
views.lean_signature: theorem InnerProductGeometry.inner_eq_zero_iff_angle_eq_pi_div_two (x y : V) : ⟪x, y⟫ = 0 ↔ angle x y = π / 2

views.nl_informal:
If the angle between two vectors is π, the inner product equals the negative product
of the norms.
views.lean_signature: theorem InnerProductGeometry.inner_eq_neg_mul_norm_of_angle_eq_pi {x y : V} (h : angle x y = π) : ⟪x, y⟫ = -(‖x‖ * ‖y‖)

views.nl_informal: If the angle between two vectors is 0, the inner product equals the product of the norms.
views.lean_signature: theorem InnerProductGeometry.inner_eq_mul_norm_of_angle_eq_zero {x y : V} (h : angle x y = 0) : ⟪x, y⟫ = ‖x‖ * ‖y‖

views.nl_informal:
The inner product of two non-zero vectors equals the negative product of their norms
if and only if the angle between the two vectors is π.
views.lean_signature: theorem InnerProductGeometry.inner_eq_neg_mul_norm_iff_angle_eq_pi {x y : V} (hx : x ≠ 0) (hy : y ≠ 0) : ⟪x, y⟫ = -(‖x‖ * ‖y‖) ↔ angle x y = π

views.nl_informal:
The inner product of two non-zero vectors equals the product of their norms
if and only if the angle between the two vectors is 0.
views.lean_signature: theorem InnerProductGeometry.inner_eq_mul_norm_iff_angle_eq_zero {x y : V} (hx : x ≠ 0) (hy : y ≠ 0) : ⟪x, y⟫ = ‖x‖ * ‖y‖ ↔ angle x y = 0

views.nl_informal:
If the angle between two vectors is π, the norm of their difference equals
the sum of their norms.
views.lean_signature: theorem InnerProductGeometry.norm_sub_eq_add_norm_of_angle_eq_pi {x y : V} (h : angle x y = π) : ‖x - y‖ = ‖x‖ + ‖y‖

views.nl_informal:
If the angle between two vectors is 0, the norm of their sum equals
the sum of their norms.
views.lean_signature: theorem InnerProductGeometry.norm_add_eq_add_norm_of_angle_eq_zero {x y : V} (h : angle x y = 0) : ‖x + y‖ = ‖x‖ + ‖y‖

views.nl_informal:
If the angle between two vectors is 0, the norm of their difference equals
the absolute value of the difference of their norms.
views.lean_signature: theorem InnerProductGeometry.norm_sub_eq_abs_sub_norm_of_angle_eq_zero {x y : V} (h : angle x y = 0) : ‖x - y‖ = |‖x‖ - ‖y‖|

views.nl_informal:
The norm of the difference of two non-zero vectors equals the sum of their norms
if and only the angle between the two vectors is π.
views.lean_signature: theorem InnerProductGeometry.norm_sub_eq_add_norm_iff_angle_eq_pi {x y : V} (hx : x ≠ 0) (hy : y ≠ 0) : ‖x - y‖ = ‖x‖ + ‖y‖ ↔ angle x y = π

views.nl_informal:
The norm of the sum of two non-zero vectors equals the sum of their norms
if and only the angle between the two vectors is 0.
views.lean_signature: theorem InnerProductGeometry.norm_add_eq_add_norm_iff_angle_eq_zero {x y : V} (hx : x ≠ 0) (hy : y ≠ 0) : ‖x + y‖ = ‖x‖ + ‖y‖ ↔ angle x y = 0

views.nl_informal:
The norm of the difference of two non-zero vectors equals the absolute value
of the difference of their norms if and only the angle between the two vectors is 0.
views.lean_signature: theorem InnerProductGeometry.norm_sub_eq_abs_sub_norm_iff_angle_eq_zero {x y : V} (hx : x ≠ 0) (hy : y ≠ 0) : ‖x - y‖ = |‖x‖ - ‖y‖| ↔ angle x y = 0

views.nl_informal:
The norm of the sum of two vectors equals the norm of their difference if and only if
the angle between them is π/2.
views.lean_signature: theorem InnerProductGeometry.norm_add_eq_norm_sub_iff_angle_eq_pi_div_two (x y : V) : ‖x + y‖ = ‖x - y‖ ↔ angle x y = π / 2

views.nl_informal: The cosine of the angle between two vectors is 1 if and only if the angle is 0.
views.lean_signature: theorem InnerProductGeometry.cos_eq_one_iff_angle_eq_zero : cos (angle x y) = 1 ↔ angle x y = 0

views.nl_informal: The cosine of the angle between two vectors is 0 if and only if the angle is π / 2.
views.lean_signature: theorem InnerProductGeometry.cos_eq_zero_iff_angle_eq_pi_div_two : cos (angle x y) = 0 ↔ angle x y = π / 2

views.nl_informal: The cosine of the angle between two vectors is -1 if and only if the angle is π.
views.lean_signature: theorem InnerProductGeometry.cos_eq_neg_one_iff_angle_eq_pi : cos (angle x y) = -1 ↔ angle x y = π

views.nl_informal: The sine of the angle between two vectors is 0 if and only if the angle is 0 or π.

views.nl_informal:
Given a smooth bump function `f : SmoothBumpFunction I c`, the closed ball of radius `f.R` is
known to include the support of `f`. These closed balls (in the model normed space `E`) intersected
with `Set.range I` form a basis of `𝓝[range I] (extChartAt I c c)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SmoothBumpFunction.nhdsWithin_range_basis : (𝓝[range I] extChartAt I c c).HasBasis (fun _ : SmoothBumpFunction I c => True) fun f => closedBall (extChartAt I c c) f.rOut ∩ range I

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is a smooth bump function and `s` closed subset of the support of `f` (i.e., of the open
ball of radius `f.rOut`), then there exists `0 < r < f.rOut` such that `s` is a subset of the open
ball of radius `r`. Formally, `s ⊆ e.source ∩ e ⁻¹' (ball (e c) r)`, where `e = extChartAt I c`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SmoothBumpFunction.exists_r_pos_lt_subset_ball {s : Set M} (hsc : IsClosed s) (hs : s ⊆ support f) : ∃ r ∈ Ioo 0 f.rOut, s ⊆ (chartAt H c).source ∩ extChartAt I c ⁻¹' ball (extChartAt I c c) r

views.nl_informal:
The closures of supports of smooth bump functions centered at `c` form a basis of `𝓝 c`.
In other words, each of these closures is a neighborhood of `c` and each neighborhood of `c`
includes `tsupport f` for some `f : SmoothBumpFunction I c`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SmoothBumpFunction.nhds_basis_tsupport : (𝓝 c).HasBasis (fun _ : SmoothBumpFunction I c => True) fun f => tsupport f

views.nl_informal:
Given `s ∈ 𝓝 c`, the supports of smooth bump functions `f : SmoothBumpFunction I c` such that
`tsupport f ⊆ s` form a basis of `𝓝 c`.  In other words, each of these supports is a
neighborhood of `c` and each neighborhood of `c` includes `support f` for some
`f : SmoothBumpFunction I c` such that `tsupport f ⊆ s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SmoothBumpFunction.nhds_basis_support {s : Set M} (hs : s ∈ 𝓝 c) : (𝓝 c).HasBasis (fun f : SmoothBumpFunction I c => tsupport f ⊆ s) fun f => support f

where the derivative is taken as a continuous linear map.
We have to assume that `f` is `C^n` at `(x₀, g(x₀))` for `n ≥ m + 1` and `g` is `C^m` at `x₀`.
We have to insert a coordinate change from `x₀` to `x` to make the derivative sensible.

views.nl_informal:
The derivative of the zero section of the tangent bundle maps `⟨x, v⟩` to `⟨⟨x, 0⟩, ⟨v, 0⟩⟩`.

Note that, as currently framed, this is a statement in coordinates, thus reliant on the choice
of the coordinate system we use on the tangent bundle.

However, the result itself is coordinate-dependent only to the extent that the coordinates
determine a splitting of the tangent bundle.  Moreover, there is a canonical splitting at each
point of the zero section (since there is a canonical horizontal space there, the tangent space
to the zero section, in addition to the canonical vertical space which is the kernel of the
derivative of the projection), and this canonical splitting is also the one that comes from the
coordinates on the tangent bundle in our definitions. So this statement is not as crazy as it
may seem.

`U ∈ 𝓝 x` and a function `g : M → F` such that `g` is smooth on `U` and `g y ∈ t y` for all `y ∈ U`.

`exists_smooth_forall_mem_convex_of_local_const`.

a family of convex sets. Suppose that for each point `x : M` there exists a vector `c : F` such that
for all `y` in a neighborhood of `x` we have `c ∈ t y`. Then there exists a smooth function
`g : C^∞⟮I, M; 𝓘(ℝ, F), F⟯` such that `g x ∈ t x` for all `x`.  See also

finite family of closed sets, let `U : ι → Set M` be a family of open sets such that `K i ⊆ U i` for

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:

function with support equal to `s`.

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:

exactly on `t`. See also `exists_smooth_zero_one_of_isClosed` for a slightly weaker version.

views.nl_informal:
Let `M` and `M'` be manifolds with the same model-with-corners, `I`.  Then `f : M → M'`

point, and being `Cⁿ` in the corresponding extended chart. This form states regularity of `f`

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:
Consider the differential of the inclusion of the sphere in `E` at the point `v` as a continuous
linear map from `TangentSpace (𝓡 n) v` to `E`.  The range of this map is the orthogonal complement
of `v` in `E`.

Note that there is an abuse here of the defeq between `E` and the tangent space to `E` at `(v:E`).
In general this defeq is not canonical, but in this case (the tangent space of a vector space) it is
canonical.
views.lean_signature: theorem range_mfderiv_coe_sphere {n : ℕ} [Fact (finrank ℝ E = n + 1)] (v : sphere (0 : E) 1) : LinearMap.range (mfderiv (𝓡 n) 𝓘(ℝ, E) ((↑) : sphere (0 : E) 1 → E) v : TangentSpace (𝓡 n) v →L[ℝ] E) = (ℝ ∙ (v : E))ᗮ

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:
Local integral curves are unique.

If a $C^1$ vector field `v` admits two local integral curves `γ γ' : ℝ → M` at `t₀` with
`γ t₀ = γ' t₀`, then `γ` and `γ'` agree on some open interval containing `t₀`.
views.lean_signature: theorem isIntegralCurveAt_eventuallyEq_of_contMDiffAt (hγt₀ : I.IsInteriorPoint (γ t₀)) (hv : ContMDiffAt I I.tangent 1 (fun x ↦ (⟨x, v x⟩ : TangentBundle I M)) (γ t₀)) (hγ : IsIntegralCurveAt γ v t₀) (hγ' : IsIntegralCurveAt γ' v t₀) (h : γ t₀ = γ' t₀) : γ =ᶠ[𝓝 t₀] γ'

views.nl_informal:
Integral curves are unique on open intervals.

If a $C^1$ vector field `v` admits two integral curves `γ γ' : ℝ → M` on some open interval
`Ioo a b`, and `γ t₀ = γ' t₀` for some `t ∈ Ioo a b`, then `γ` and `γ'` agree on `Ioo a b`.
views.lean_signature: theorem isIntegralCurveOn_Ioo_eqOn_of_contMDiff (ht₀ : t₀ ∈ Ioo a b) (hγt : ∀ t ∈ Ioo a b, I.IsInteriorPoint (γ t)) (hv : ContMDiff I I.tangent 1 (fun x ↦ (⟨x, v x⟩ : TangentBundle I M))) (hγ : IsIntegralCurveOn γ v (Ioo a b)) (hγ' : IsIntegralCurveOn γ' v (Ioo a b)) (h : γ t₀ = γ' t₀) : EqOn γ γ' (Ioo a b)

views.nl_informal:
Global integral curves are unique.

If a continuously differentiable vector field `v` admits two global integral curves
`γ γ' : ℝ → M`, and `γ t₀ = γ' t₀` for some `t₀`, then `γ` and `γ'` are equal.
views.lean_signature: theorem isIntegralCurve_eq_of_contMDiff (hγt : ∀ t, I.IsInteriorPoint (γ t)) (hv : ContMDiff I I.tangent 1 (fun x ↦ (⟨x, v x⟩ : TangentBundle I M))) (hγ : IsIntegralCurve γ v) (hγ' : IsIntegralCurve γ' v) (h : γ t₀ = γ' t₀) : γ = γ'

views.nl_informal:
For a global integral curve `γ`, if it crosses itself at `a b : ℝ`, then it is periodic with
period `a - b`.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsIntegralCurve.periodic_of_eq [BoundarylessManifold I M] (hγ : IsIntegralCurve γ v) (hv : ContMDiff I I.tangent 1 (fun x ↦ (⟨x, v x⟩ : TangentBundle I M))) (heq : γ a = γ b) : Periodic γ (a - b)

views.nl_informal:
If the vector field `v` vanishes at `x₀`, then the constant curve at `x₀`

views.nl_informal:
This is the uniqueness theorem of integral curves applied to a real-indexed family of integral
curves with the same starting point.
views.lean_signature: theorem eqOn_of_isIntegralCurveOn_Ioo [BoundarylessManifold I M] (hv : ContMDiff I I.tangent 1 (fun x ↦ (⟨x, v x⟩ : TangentBundle I M))) {x : M} (γ : ℝ → ℝ → M) (hγx : ∀ a, γ a 0 = x) (hγ : ∀ a > 0, IsIntegralCurveOn (γ a) v (Ioo (-a) a)) {a a' : ℝ} (hpos : 0 < a') (hle : a' ≤ a) : EqOn (γ a') (γ a) (Ioo (-a') a')

For a family of integral curves `γ : ℝ → ℝ → M` with the same starting point `γ 0 = x` such that
each `γ a` is defined on `Ioo (-a) a`, the global curve `γ_ext := fun t ↦ γ (|t| + 1) t` agrees
with each `γ a` on `Ioo (-a) a`. This will help us show that `γ_ext` is a global integral curve.

views.nl_informal:
For a family of integral curves `γ : ℝ → ℝ → M` with the same starting point `γ 0 = x` such that

The existence of a global integral curve is equivalent to the existence of a family of local

views.nl_informal:
Let `γ` and `γ'` be integral curves defined on `Ioo a b` and `Ioo a' b'`, respectively. Then,
`piecewise (Ioo a b) γ γ'` is equal to `γ` and `γ'` in their respective domains.

for `γ'` by the uniqueness of integral curves.

views.nl_informal:
The extension of an integral curve by another integral curve is an integral curve.

If two integral curves are defined on overlapping open intervals, and they agree at a point in
their common domain, then they can be patched together to form a longer integral curve.

This is stated for manifolds without boundary for simplicity. We actually only need to assume that
the images of `γ` and `γ'` lie in the interior of the manifold.
TODO: Generalise to manifolds with boundary.

views.nl_informal:
If there exists `ε > 0` such that the local integral curve at each point `x : M` is defined at

passing through it.

views.nl_informal:
In the case of the manifold structure on a vector space, the extended charts are just the
identity.

views.nl_informal:
A finite-dimensional manifold modelled on a locally compact field
(such as ℝ, ℂ or the `p`-adic numbers) is locally compact.

views.nl_informal:
Riesz's theorem applied to manifolds: a locally compact manifolds must be modelled on a

views.nl_informal: Every point is either an interior or a boundary point.
views.lean_signature: theorem ModelWithCorners.isInteriorPoint_or_isBoundaryPoint (x : M) : I.IsInteriorPoint x ∨ I.IsBoundaryPoint x

views.nl_informal: A manifold decomposes into interior and boundary.
views.lean_signature: theorem ModelWithCorners.interior_union_boundary_eq_univ : (I.interior M) ∪ (I.boundary M) = (univ : Set M)

views.nl_informal: The interior and boundary of a manifold `M` are disjoint.
views.lean_signature: theorem ModelWithCorners.disjoint_interior_boundary : Disjoint (I.interior M) (I.boundary M)

views.nl_informal: The boundary is the complement of the interior.
views.lean_signature: theorem ModelWithCorners.compl_interior : (I.interior M)ᶜ = I.boundary M

views.nl_informal: The interior is the complement of the boundary.
views.lean_signature: theorem ModelWithCorners.compl_boundary : (I.boundary M)ᶜ = I.interior M

views.nl_informal: If `I` is boundaryless, `M` has full interior.
views.lean_signature: theorem ModelWithCorners.interior_eq_univ [BoundarylessManifold I M] : I.interior M = univ

views.nl_informal: Boundaryless manifolds have empty boundary.
views.lean_signature: theorem ModelWithCorners.Boundaryless.boundary_eq_empty [BoundarylessManifold I M] : I.boundary M = ∅

views.nl_informal: `M` is boundaryless iff its boundary is empty.

views.nl_informal: Manifolds with empty boundary are boundaryless.
views.lean_signature: theorem ModelWithCorners.Boundaryless.of_boundary_eq_empty (h : I.boundary M = ∅) : BoundarylessManifold I M

views.nl_informal: The interior of `M × N` is the product of the interiors of `M` and `N`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ModelWithCorners.interior_prod : (I.prod J).interior (M × N) = (I.interior M) ×ˢ (J.interior N)

views.nl_informal: The boundary of `M × N` is `∂M × N ∪ (M × ∂N)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ModelWithCorners.boundary_prod : (I.prod J).boundary (M × N) = Set.prod univ (J.boundary N) ∪ Set.prod (I.boundary M) univ

views.nl_informal: If `M` is boundaryless, `∂(M×N) = M × ∂N`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ModelWithCorners.boundary_of_boundaryless_left [BoundarylessManifold I M] : (I.prod J).boundary (M × N) = Set.prod (univ : Set M) (J.boundary N)

views.nl_informal: If `N` is boundaryless, `∂(M×N) = ∂M × N`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ModelWithCorners.boundary_of_boundaryless_right [BoundarylessManifold J N] : (I.prod J).boundary (M × N) = Set.prod (I.boundary M) (univ : Set N)

views.nl_informal:
The composition of the derivative of the inverse of `extChartAt` with the derivative of

views.nl_informal:
One can reformulate smoothness within a set at a point as continuity within this set at this
point, and smoothness in the corresponding extended chart.

views.nl_informal:
One can reformulate smoothness within a set at a point as continuity within this set at this
point, and smoothness in the corresponding extended chart. This form states smoothness of `f`
written in such a way that the set is restricted to lie within the domain/codomain of the
corresponding charts.
Even though this expression is more complicated than the one in `mdifferentiableWithinAt_iff`, it is
a smaller set, but their germs at `extChartAt I x x` are equal. It is sometimes useful to rewrite
using this in the goal.

views.nl_informal:
One can reformulate smoothness within a set at a point as continuity within this set at this
point, and smoothness in the corresponding extended chart in the target.

views.nl_informal:
One can reformulate smoothness within a set at a point as continuity within this set at this
point, and smoothness in any chart containing that point.
views.lean_signature: theorem mdifferentiableWithinAt_iff_of_mem_source {x' : M} {y : M'} (hx : x' ∈ (chartAt H x).source) (hy : f x' ∈ (chartAt H' y).source) : MDifferentiableWithinAt I I' f s x' ↔ ContinuousWithinAt f s x' ∧ DifferentiableWithinAt 𝕜 (extChartAt I' y ∘ f ∘ (extChartAt I x).symm) ((extChartAt I x).symm ⁻¹' s ∩ range I) (extChartAt I x x')

views.nl_informal:
One can reformulate smoothness within a set at a point as continuity within this set at this
point, and smoothness in any chart containing that point. Version requiring differentiability
in the target instead of `range I`.
views.lean_signature: theorem mdifferentiableWithinAt_iff_of_mem_source' {x' : M} {y : M'} (hx : x' ∈ (chartAt H x).source) (hy : f x' ∈ (chartAt H' y).source) : MDifferentiableWithinAt I I' f s x' ↔ ContinuousWithinAt f s x' ∧ DifferentiableWithinAt 𝕜 (extChartAt I' y ∘ f ∘ (extChartAt I x).symm) ((extChartAt I x).target ∩ (extChartAt I x).symm ⁻¹' (s ∩ f ⁻¹' (extChartAt I' y).source)) (extChartAt I x x')

views.nl_informal: Differentiability on a set is equivalent to differentiability in the extended charts.
views.lean_signature: theorem mdifferentiableOn_iff_of_mem_maximalAtlas' (he : e ∈ maximalAtlas I 1 M) (he' : e' ∈ maximalAtlas I' 1 M') (hs : s ⊆ e.source) (h2s : MapsTo f s e'.source) : MDifferentiableOn I I' f s ↔ DifferentiableOn 𝕜 (e'.extend I' ∘ f ∘ (e.extend I).symm) (e.extend I '' s)

views.nl_informal:
If the set where you want `f` to be smooth lies entirely in a single chart, and `f` maps it
into a single chart, the smoothness of `f` on that set can be expressed by purely looking in
these charts.
Note: this lemma uses `extChartAt I x '' s` instead of `(extChartAt I x).symm ⁻¹' s` to ensure
that this set lies in `(extChartAt I x).target`.
views.lean_signature: theorem mdifferentiableOn_iff_of_subset_source {x : M} {y : M'} (hs : s ⊆ (chartAt H x).source) (h2s : MapsTo f s (chartAt H' y).source) : MDifferentiableOn I I' f s ↔ ContinuousOn f s ∧ DifferentiableOn 𝕜 (extChartAt I' y ∘ f ∘ (extChartAt I x).symm) (extChartAt I x '' s)

views.nl_informal:
If the set where you want `f` to be smooth lies entirely in a single chart, and `f` maps it
into a single chart, the smoothness of `f` on that set can be expressed by purely looking in
these charts.
Note: this lemma uses `extChartAt I x '' s` instead of `(extChartAt I x).symm ⁻¹' s` to ensure
that this set lies in `(extChartAt I x).target`.
views.lean_signature: theorem mdifferentiableOn_iff_of_subset_source' {x : M} {y : M'} (hs : s ⊆ (extChartAt I x).source) (h2s : MapsTo f s (extChartAt I' y).source) : MDifferentiableOn I I' f s ↔ DifferentiableOn 𝕜 (extChartAt I' y ∘ f ∘ (extChartAt I x).symm) (extChartAt I x '' s)

views.nl_informal:
One can reformulate smoothness on a set as continuity on this set, and smoothness in any
extended chart.
views.lean_signature: theorem mdifferentiableOn_iff : MDifferentiableOn I I' f s ↔ ContinuousOn f s ∧ ∀ (x : M) (y : M'), DifferentiableOn 𝕜 (extChartAt I' y ∘ f ∘ (extChartAt I x).symm) ((extChartAt I x).target ∩ (extChartAt I x).symm ⁻¹' (s ∩ f ⁻¹' (extChartAt I' y).source))

views.nl_informal:
One can reformulate smoothness on a set as continuity on this set, and smoothness in any
extended chart in the target.
views.lean_signature: theorem mdifferentiableOn_iff_target : MDifferentiableOn I I' f s ↔ ContinuousOn f s ∧ ∀ y : M', MDifferentiableOn I 𝓘(𝕜, E') (extChartAt I' y ∘ f) (s ∩ f ⁻¹' (extChartAt I' y).source)

views.nl_informal: One can reformulate smoothness as continuity and smoothness in any extended chart.

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:
If two sets coincide locally, then derivatives within these sets

views.nl_informal:
If two sets coincide locally, except maybe at a point, then derivatives within these sets

views.nl_informal: If two sets coincide locally, then derivatives within these sets coincide locally.

views.nl_informal:
A congruence lemma for `mfderiv`, (ab)using the fact that `TangentSpace I' (f x)` is

views.nl_informal:
The total derivative of a function in two variables is the sum of the partial derivatives.
Note that to state this (without casts) we need to be able to see through the definition of
`TangentSpace`.
views.lean_signature: theorem mfderiv_prod_eq_add {f : M × M' → M''} {p : M × M'} (hf : MDifferentiableAt (I.prod I') I'' f p) : mfderiv (I.prod I') I'' f p = mfderiv (I.prod I') I'' (fun z : M × M' => f (z.1, p.2)) p + mfderiv (I.prod I') I'' (fun z : M × M' => f (p.1, z.2)) p

views.nl_informal:
The total derivative of a function in two variables is the sum of the partial derivatives.
Note that to state this (without casts) we need to be able to see through the definition of
`TangentSpace`. Version in terms of the one-variable derivatives.
views.lean_signature: theorem mfderiv_prod_eq_add_comp {f : M × M' → M''} {p : M × M'} (hf : MDifferentiableAt (I.prod I') I'' f p) : mfderiv (I.prod I') I'' f p = (mfderiv I I'' (fun z : M => f (z, p.2)) p.1) ∘L (id (ContinuousLinearMap.fst 𝕜 E E') : (TangentSpace (I.prod I') p) →L[𝕜] (TangentSpace I p.1)) + (mfderiv I' I'' (fun z : M' => f (p.1, z)) p.2) ∘L (id (ContinuousLinearMap.snd 𝕜 E E') : (TangentSpace (I.prod I') p) →L[𝕜] (TangentSpace I' p.2))

views.nl_informal:
The total derivative of a function in two variables is the sum of the partial derivatives.
Note that to state this (without casts) we need to be able to see through the definition of
`TangentSpace`. Version in terms of the one-variable derivatives.
views.lean_signature: theorem mfderiv_prod_eq_add_apply {f : M × M' → M''} {p : M × M'} {v : TangentSpace (I.prod I') p} (hf : MDifferentiableAt (I.prod I') I'' f p) : mfderiv (I.prod I') I'' f p v = mfderiv I I'' (fun z : M => f (z, p.2)) p.1 v.1 + mfderiv I' I'' (fun z : M' => f (p.1, z)) p.2 v.2

views.nl_informal:
The derivative of the chart at a base point is the chart of the tangent bundle, composed with
the identification between the tangent bundle of the model space and the product space.
views.lean_signature: theorem tangentMap_chart {p q : TangentBundle I M} (h : q.1 ∈ (chartAt H p.1).source) : tangentMap I I (chartAt H p.1) q = (TotalSpace.toProd _ _).symm ((chartAt (ModelProd H E) p : TangentBundle I M → ModelProd H E) q)

views.nl_informal:

tangent bundle, composed with the identification between the tangent bundle of the model space and
the product space.
views.lean_signature: theorem tangentMap_chart_symm {p : TangentBundle I M} {q : TangentBundle I H} (h : q.1 ∈ (chartAt H p.1).target) : tangentMap I I (chartAt H p.1).symm q = (chartAt (ModelProd H E) p).symm (TotalSpace.toProd H E q)

views.nl_informal:
The preimage under the projection from the tangent bundle of a set with unique differential in
the basis also has unique differential.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniqueMDiffOn.tangentBundle_proj_preimage {s : Set M} (hs : UniqueMDiffOn I s) : UniqueMDiffOn I.tangent (π E (TangentSpace I) ⁻¹' s)

views.nl_informal:
To write a linear map between tangent spaces in coordinates amounts to precomposing and
postcomposing it with derivatives of extended charts.
Concrete version of `inTangentCoordinates_eq`.
views.lean_signature: theorem inTangentCoordinates_eq_mfderiv_comp {N : Type*} {f : N → M} {g : N → M'} {ϕ : Π x : N, TangentSpace I (f x) →L[𝕜] TangentSpace I' (g x)} {x₀ : N} {x : N} (hx : f x ∈ (chartAt H (f x₀)).source) (hy : g x ∈ (chartAt H' (g x₀)).source) : inTangentCoordinates I I' f g ϕ x₀ x = (mfderiv I' 𝓘(𝕜, E') (extChartAt I' (g x₀)) (g x)) ∘L (ϕ x) ∘L (mfderivWithin 𝓘(𝕜, E) I (extChartAt I (f x₀)).symm (range I) (extChartAt I (f x₀) (f x)))

views.nl_informal:

Let `e` be a partial homeomorphism of `B × F`.  Suppose that at every point `p` in the source of
`e`, there is some neighbourhood `s` of `p` on which `e` is equal to a bi-`C^n` fiberwise linear
partial homeomorphism.

`U`, admits a neighbourhood `u` of `x` such that `e` is equal on `u ×ˢ univ` to some bi-`C^n`
fiberwise linear partial homeomorphism.

views.nl_informal:
Let `e` be a partial homeomorphism of `B × F` whose source is `U ×ˢ univ`, for some set `U` in
`B`, and which, at any point `x` in `U`, admits a neighbourhood `u` of `x` such that `e` is equal
on `u ×ˢ univ` to some bi-`C^n` fiberwise linear partial homeomorphism.  Then `e` itself
is equal to some bi-`C^n` fiberwise linear partial homeomorphism.

This is the key mathematical point of the `locality` condition in the construction of the
`StructureGroupoid` of bi-`C^n` fiberwise linear partial homeomorphisms.  The proof is by gluing
together the various bi-`C^n` fiberwise linear partial homeomorphism which exist locally.

is exactly what we need for `contMDiffFiberwiseLinear`.

using smoothness of `ϕ` read in coordinates.

views.nl_informal:
The **Ping-Pong-Lemma**.

Given a group action of `G` on `X` so that the `H i` acts in a specific way on disjoint subsets
`X i` we can prove that `lift f` is injective, and thus the image of `lift f` is isomorphic to the
free product of the `H i`.

Often the Ping-Pong-Lemma is stated with regard to subgroups `H i` that generate the whole group;
we generalize to arbitrary group homomorphisms `f i : H i →* G` and do not require the group to be
generated by the images.

Usually the Ping-Pong-Lemma requires that one group `H i` has at least three elements. This
condition is only needed if `# ι = 2`, and we accept `3 ≤ # ι` as an alternative.
views.lean_signature: theorem Monoid.CoprodI.lift_injective_of_ping_pong : Function.Injective (lift f)

views.nl_informal:

Given a group action of `G` on `X` so that the generators of the free groups act in specific
ways on disjoint subsets `X i` and `Y i` we can prove that `lift f` is injective, and thus the image
of `lift f` is isomorphic to the free group.

Often the Ping-Pong-Lemma is stated with regard to group elements that generate the whole group;
we generalize to arbitrary group homomorphisms from the free group to `G` and do not require the
group to be generated by the elements.

views.nl_informal: A group is finitely generated if and only if it is finitely generated as a monoid.
views.lean_signature: theorem Group.fg_iff_monoid_fg : Group.FG G ↔ Monoid.FG G

views.nl_informal:
The Frattini subgroup consists of "non-generating" elements in the following sense:

If a subgroup together with the Frattini subgroup generates the whole group,
then the subgroup is already the whole group.
views.lean_signature: theorem frattini_nongenerating [IsCoatomic (Subgroup G)] {K : Subgroup G} (h : K ⊔ frattini G = ⊤) : K = ⊤

views.nl_informal: When `G` is finite, the Frattini subgroup is nilpotent.
views.lean_signature: theorem frattini_nilpotent [Finite G] : Group.IsNilpotent (frattini G)

views.nl_informal:
**Goursat's lemma** for a subgroup of a product with surjective projections.

If `I` is a subgroup of `G × H` which projects fully on both factors, then there exist normal
subgroups `M ≤ G` and `N ≤ H` such that `G' × H' ≤ I` and the image of `I` in `G ⧸ M × H ⧸ N` is the
graph of an isomorphism `G ⧸ M ≃ H ⧸ N'`.

`G'` and `H'` can be explicitly constructed as `I.goursatFst` and `I.goursatSnd` respectively.
views.lean_signature: theorem Subgroup.goursat_surjective : have

views.nl_informal:
**Goursat's lemma** for an arbitrary subgroup.

If `I` is a subgroup of `G × H`, then there exist subgroups `G' ≤ G`, `H' ≤ H` and normal subgroups
`M ⊴ G'` and `N ⊴ H'` such that `M × N ≤ I` and the image of `I` in `G' ⧸ M × H' ⧸ N` is the graph
of an isomorphism `G' ⧸ M ≃ H' ⧸ N`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Subgroup.goursat : ∃ (G' : Subgroup G) (H' : Subgroup H) (M : Subgroup G') (N : Subgroup H') (_ : M.Normal) (_ : N.Normal) (e : G' ⧸ M ≃* H' ⧸ N), I = (e.toMonoidHom.graph.comap <| (QuotientGroup.mk' M).prodMap (QuotientGroup.mk' N)).map (G'.subtype.prodMap H'.subtype)

views.nl_informal:
Two reduced words representing the same element of the `HNNExtension G A B φ` have the same
length corresponding list, with the same pattern of occurrences of `t^1` and `t^(-1)`,
and also the `head` is in the same left coset of `toSubgroup A B (-u)`, where `u : ℤˣ`
is the exponent of the first occurrence of `t` in the word.
views.lean_signature: theorem HNNExtension.ReducedWord.map_fst_eq_and_of_prod_eq {w₁ w₂ : ReducedWord G A B} (hprod : w₁.prod φ = w₂.prod φ) : w₁.toList.map Prod.fst = w₂.toList.map Prod.fst ∧ ∀ u ∈ w₁.toList.head?.map Prod.fst, w₁.head⁻¹ * w₂.head ∈ toSubgroup A B (-u)

views.nl_informal:
**Britton's Lemma**. Any reduced word whose product is an element of `G`, has no
occurrences of `t`.
views.lean_signature: theorem HNNExtension.ReducedWord.toList_eq_nil_of_mem_of_range (w : ReducedWord G A B) (hw : w.prod φ ∈ (of.range : Subgroup (HNNExtension G A B φ))) : w.toList = []

views.nl_informal:
A subgroup has index two if and only if there exists `a` such that for all `b`, exactly one
of `b * a` and `b` belong to `H`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Subgroup.index_eq_two_iff : H.index = 2 ↔ ∃ a, ∀ b, Xor' (b * a ∈ H) (b ∈ H)

views.nl_informal: A subgroup of index 1 is normal (does not require finiteness of G)
views.lean_signature: theorem Subgroup.normal_of_index_eq_one (hH : H.index = 1) : H.Normal

views.nl_informal: A subgroup of index 2 is normal (does not require finiteness of G)
views.lean_signature: theorem Subgroup.normal_of_index_eq_two (hH : H.index = 2) : H.Normal

views.nl_informal:
A subgroup of a finite group whose index is the smallest prime factor is normal.

Note : if `G` is infinite, then `Nat.card G = 0` and `(Nat.card G).minFac = 2`
views.lean_signature: theorem Subgroup.normal_of_index_eq_minFac_card (hHp : H.index = (Nat.card G).minFac) : H.Normal

views.nl_informal:
The proof that `upperCentralSeriesStep H` is the preimage of the centre of `G/H` under
the canonical surjection.
views.lean_signature: theorem upperCentralSeriesStep_eq_comap_center : upperCentralSeriesStep H = Subgroup.comap (mk' H) (center (G ⧸ H))

views.nl_informal:
The `n+1`st term of the upper central series `H i` has underlying set equal to the `x` such
that `⁅x,G⁆ ⊆ H n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem mem_upperCentralSeries_succ_iff {n : ℕ} {x : G} : x ∈ upperCentralSeries G (n + 1) ↔ ∀ y : G, x * y * x⁻¹ * y⁻¹ ∈ upperCentralSeries G n

views.nl_informal: Any ascending central series for a group is bounded above by the upper central series.
views.lean_signature: theorem ascending_central_series_le_upper (H : ℕ → Subgroup G) (hH : IsAscendingCentralSeries H) : ∀ n : ℕ, H n ≤ upperCentralSeries G n

views.nl_informal: The upper central series of a group is an ascending central series.
views.lean_signature: theorem upperCentralSeries_isAscendingCentralSeries : IsAscendingCentralSeries (upperCentralSeries G)

views.nl_informal:
A group `G` is nilpotent iff there exists an ascending central series which reaches `G` in
finitely many steps.
views.lean_signature: theorem nilpotent_iff_finite_ascending_central_series : IsNilpotent G ↔ ∃ n : ℕ, ∃ H : ℕ → Subgroup G, IsAscendingCentralSeries H ∧ H n = ⊤

views.nl_informal:
A group `G` is nilpotent iff there exists a descending central series which reaches the
trivial group in a finite time.
views.lean_signature: theorem nilpotent_iff_finite_descending_central_series : IsNilpotent G ↔ ∃ n : ℕ, ∃ H : ℕ → Subgroup G, IsDescendingCentralSeries H ∧ H n = ⊥

views.nl_informal: The lower central series of a group is a descending central series.
views.lean_signature: theorem lowerCentralSeries_isDescendingCentralSeries : IsDescendingCentralSeries (lowerCentralSeries G)

views.nl_informal: Any descending central series for a group is bounded below by the lower central series.
views.lean_signature: theorem descending_central_series_ge_lower (H : ℕ → Subgroup G) (hH : IsDescendingCentralSeries H) : ∀ n : ℕ, lowerCentralSeries G n ≤ H n

views.nl_informal:
A group is nilpotent if and only if its lower central series eventually reaches
the trivial subgroup.
views.lean_signature: theorem nilpotent_iff_lowerCentralSeries : IsNilpotent G ↔ ∃ n, lowerCentralSeries G n = ⊥

views.nl_informal:
The nilpotency class of a nilpotent `G` is equal to the smallest `n` for which an ascending
central series reaches `G` in its `n`'th term.
views.lean_signature: theorem least_ascending_central_series_length_eq_nilpotencyClass : Nat.find ((nilpotent_iff_finite_ascending_central_series G).mp hG) = Group.nilpotencyClass G

views.nl_informal:
The nilpotency class of a nilpotent `G` is equal to the smallest `n` for which the descending
central series reaches `⊥` in its `n`'th term.
views.lean_signature: theorem least_descending_central_series_length_eq_nilpotencyClass : Nat.find ((nilpotent_iff_finite_descending_central_series G).mp hG) = Group.nilpotencyClass G

views.nl_informal: The nilpotency class of a nilpotent `G` is equal to the length of the lower central series.
views.lean_signature: theorem lowerCentralSeries_length_eq_nilpotencyClass : Nat.find (nilpotent_iff_lowerCentralSeries.mp hG) = Group.nilpotencyClass (G := G)

views.nl_informal: The nilpotency class of a subgroup is less or equal to the nilpotency class of the group
views.lean_signature: theorem Subgroup.nilpotencyClass_le (H : Subgroup G) [hG : IsNilpotent G] : Group.nilpotencyClass H ≤ Group.nilpotencyClass G

views.nl_informal:
The preimage of a nilpotent group is nilpotent if the kernel of the homomorphism is contained
in the center
views.lean_signature: theorem isNilpotent_of_ker_le_center {H : Type*} [Group H] (f : G →* H) (hf1 : f.ker ≤ center G) (hH : IsNilpotent H) : IsNilpotent G

views.nl_informal: The range of a surjective homomorphism from a nilpotent group is nilpotent
views.lean_signature: theorem nilpotent_of_surjective {G' : Type*} [Group G'] [h : IsNilpotent G] (f : G →* G') (hf : Function.Surjective f) : IsNilpotent G'

views.nl_informal:
The nilpotency class of the range of a surjective homomorphism from a
nilpotent group is less or equal the nilpotency class of the domain
views.lean_signature: theorem nilpotencyClass_le_of_surjective {G' : Type*} [Group G'] (f : G →* G') (hf : Function.Surjective f) [h : IsNilpotent G] : Group.nilpotencyClass (hG := nilpotent_of_surjective _ hf) ≤ Group.nilpotencyClass G

views.nl_informal: Nilpotency respects isomorphisms
views.lean_signature: theorem nilpotent_of_mulEquiv {G' : Type*} [Group G'] [_h : IsNilpotent G] (f : G ≃* G') : IsNilpotent G'

views.nl_informal: The nilpotency class of a quotient of `G` is less or equal the nilpotency class of `G`
views.lean_signature: theorem nilpotencyClass_quotient_le (H : Subgroup G) [H.Normal] [_h : IsNilpotent G] : Group.nilpotencyClass (G ⧸ H) ≤ Group.nilpotencyClass G

views.nl_informal: Quotienting the `center G` reduces the nilpotency class by 1
views.lean_signature: theorem nilpotencyClass_quotient_center [hH : IsNilpotent G] : Group.nilpotencyClass (G ⧸ center G) = Group.nilpotencyClass G - 1

views.nl_informal: The nilpotency class of a non-trivial group is one more than its quotient by the center
views.lean_signature: theorem nilpotencyClass_eq_quotient_center_plus_one [hH : IsNilpotent G] [Nontrivial G] : Group.nilpotencyClass G = Group.nilpotencyClass (G ⧸ center G) + 1

views.nl_informal: If the quotient by `center G` is nilpotent, then so is G.
views.lean_signature: theorem of_quotient_center_nilpotent (h : IsNilpotent (G ⧸ center G)) : IsNilpotent G

views.nl_informal:
A custom induction principle for nilpotent groups. The base case is a trivial group
(`subsingleton G`), and in the induction step, one can assume the hypothesis for
the group quotiented by its center.
views.lean_signature: theorem nilpotent_center_quotient_ind {P : ∀ (G) [Group G] [IsNilpotent G], Prop} (G : Type*) [Group G] [IsNilpotent G] (hbase : ∀ (G) [Group G] [Subsingleton G], P G) (hstep : ∀ (G) [Group G] [IsNilpotent G], P (G ⧸ center G) → P G) : P G

views.nl_informal: Abelian groups have nilpotency class at most one
views.lean_signature: theorem CommGroup.nilpotencyClass_le_one {G : Type*} [CommGroup G] : Group.nilpotencyClass G ≤ 1

views.nl_informal: The nilpotency class of a product is the max of the nilpotency classes of the factors
views.lean_signature: theorem nilpotencyClass_prod [IsNilpotent G₁] [IsNilpotent G₂] : Group.nilpotencyClass (G₁ × G₂) = max (Group.nilpotencyClass G₁) (Group.nilpotencyClass G₂)

views.nl_informal: products of nilpotent groups are nilpotent if their nilpotency class is bounded
views.lean_signature: theorem isNilpotent_pi_of_bounded_class [∀ i, IsNilpotent (Gs i)] (n : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, Group.nilpotencyClass (Gs i) ≤ n) : IsNilpotent (∀ i, Gs i)

views.nl_informal: The nilpotency class of an n-ary product is the sup of the nilpotency classes of the factors
views.lean_signature: theorem nilpotencyClass_pi [Fintype η] [∀ i, IsNilpotent (Gs i)] : Group.nilpotencyClass (∀ i, Gs i) = Finset.univ.sup fun i => Group.nilpotencyClass (Gs i)

views.nl_informal: A p-group is nilpotent
views.lean_signature: theorem IsPGroup.isNilpotent [Finite G] {p : ℕ} [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (h : IsPGroup p G) : IsNilpotent G

views.nl_informal: If a finite group is the direct product of its Sylow groups, it is nilpotent
views.lean_signature: theorem isNilpotent_of_product_of_sylow_group (e : (∀ p : (Nat.card G).primeFactors, ∀ P : Sylow p G, (↑P : Subgroup G)) ≃* G) : IsNilpotent G

views.nl_informal:
A finite group is nilpotent iff the normalizer condition holds, and iff all maximal groups are
normal and iff all Sylow groups are normal and iff the group is the direct product of its Sylow
groups.
views.lean_signature: theorem isNilpotent_of_finite_tfae : List.TFAE [IsNilpotent G, NormalizerCondition G, ∀ H : Subgroup G, IsCoatom H → H.Normal, ∀ (p : ℕ) (_hp : Fact p.Prime) (P : Sylow p G), (↑P : Subgroup G).Normal, Nonempty ((∀ p : (Nat.card G).primeFactors, ∀ P : Sylow p G, (↑P : Subgroup G)) ≃* G)]

views.nl_informal:
`Finset.noncommProd` is “injective” in `f` if `f` maps into independent subgroups.  This
generalizes (one direction of) `Subgroup.disjoint_iff_mul_eq_one`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Subgroup.eq_one_of_noncommProd_eq_one_of_iSupIndep {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (f : ι → G) (comm) (K : ι → Subgroup G) (hind : iSupIndep K) (hmem : ∀ x ∈ s, f x ∈ K x) (heq1 : s.noncommProd f comm = 1) : ∀ i ∈ s, f i = 1

views.nl_informal:
Given monoid morphisms `φᵢ : Nᵢ → M` and `f : M → P`, if we have sufficient commutativity, then
`f ∘ (∐ᵢ φᵢ) = ∐ᵢ (f ∘ φᵢ)`
views.lean_signature: theorem MonoidHom.comp_noncommPiCoprod {P : Type*} [Monoid P] {f : M →* P} (hcomm' : Pairwise fun i j => ∀ x y, Commute (f.comp (ϕ i) x) (f.comp (ϕ j) y) := Pairwise.mono hcomm (fun i j ↦ forall_imp (fun x h y ↦ by simp only [MonoidHom.coe_comp, Function.comp_apply, Commute.map (h y) f]))) : f.comp (MonoidHom.noncommPiCoprod ϕ hcomm) = MonoidHom.noncommPiCoprod (fun i ↦ f.comp (ϕ i)) hcomm'

views.nl_informal: 1 is of finite order in any monoid.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsOfFinOrder.one : IsOfFinOrder (1 : G)

views.nl_informal: Elements of finite order are of finite order in submonoids.
views.lean_signature: theorem Submonoid.isOfFinOrder_coe {H : Submonoid G} {x : H} : IsOfFinOrder (x : G) ↔ IsOfFinOrder x

views.nl_informal: The image of an element of finite order has finite order.
views.lean_signature: theorem MonoidHom.isOfFinOrder [Monoid H] (f : G →* H) {x : G} (h : IsOfFinOrder x) : IsOfFinOrder <| f x

views.nl_informal: If a direct product has finite order then so does each component.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsOfFinOrder.apply {η : Type*} {Gs : η → Type*} [∀ i, Monoid (Gs i)] {x : ∀ i, Gs i} (h : IsOfFinOrder x) : ∀ i, IsOfFinOrder (x i)

views.nl_informal: A group element has finite order iff its order is positive.
views.lean_signature: theorem orderOf_pos_iff : 0 < orderOf x ↔ IsOfFinOrder x

views.nl_informal:
If `x^n = 1`, but `x^(n/p) ≠ 1` for all prime factors `p` of `n`,
then `x` has order `n` in `G`.
views.lean_signature: theorem orderOf_eq_of_pow_and_pow_div_prime (hn : 0 < n) (hx : x ^ n = 1) (hd : ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → p ∣ n → x ^ (n / p) ≠ 1) : orderOf x = n

views.nl_informal: An injective homomorphism of monoids preserves orders of elements.
views.lean_signature: theorem orderOf_injective {H : Type*} [Monoid H] (f : G →* H) (hf : Function.Injective f) (x : G) : orderOf (f x) = orderOf x

views.nl_informal: A multiplicative equivalence preserves orders of elements.
views.lean_signature: theorem MulEquiv.orderOf_eq {H : Type*} [Monoid H] (e : G ≃* H) (x : G) : orderOf (e x) = orderOf x

views.nl_informal: Commuting elements of finite order are closed under multiplication.
views.lean_signature: theorem Commute.isOfFinOrder_mul (h : Commute x y) (hx : IsOfFinOrder x) (hy : IsOfFinOrder y) : IsOfFinOrder (x * y)

views.nl_informal:
If each prime factor of `orderOf x` has higher multiplicity in `orderOf y`, and `x` commutes
with `y`, then `x * y` has the same order as `y`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Commute.orderOf_mul_eq_right_of_forall_prime_mul_dvd (h : Commute x y) (hy : IsOfFinOrder y) (hdvd : ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → p ∣ orderOf x → p * orderOf x ∣ orderOf y) : orderOf (x * y) = orderOf y

views.nl_informal: Inverses of elements of finite order have finite order.
views.lean_signature: theorem isOfFinOrder_inv_iff {x : G} : IsOfFinOrder x⁻¹ ↔ IsOfFinOrder x

views.nl_informal: Elements of finite order are closed under multiplication.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsOfFinOrder.mul (hx : IsOfFinOrder x) (hy : IsOfFinOrder y) : IsOfFinOrder (x * y)

views.nl_informal:
If `G` is a `p`-group acting on a finite set `α`, then the number of fixed points
of the action is congruent mod `p` to the cardinality of `α`
views.lean_signature: theorem IsPGroup.card_modEq_card_fixedPoints : Nat.card α ≡ Nat.card (fixedPoints G α) [MOD p]

views.nl_informal:
If a p-group acts on `α` and the cardinality of `α` is not a multiple
of `p` then the action has a fixed point.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsPGroup.nonempty_fixed_point_of_prime_not_dvd_card (α) [MulAction G α] (hpα : ¬p ∣ Nat.card α) : (fixedPoints G α).Nonempty

views.nl_informal:
If a p-group acts on `α` and the cardinality of `α` is a multiple
of `p`, and the action has one fixed point, then it has another fixed point.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsPGroup.exists_fixed_point_of_prime_dvd_card_of_fixed_point (hpα : p ∣ Nat.card α) {a : α} (ha : a ∈ fixedPoints G α) : ∃ b, b ∈ fixedPoints G α ∧ a ≠ b

views.nl_informal: finite p-groups with different p have coprime orders
views.lean_signature: theorem IsPGroup.coprime_card_of_ne {G₂ : Type*} [Group G₂] (p₁ p₂ : ℕ) [hp₁ : Fact p₁.Prime] [hp₂ : Fact p₂.Prime] (hne : p₁ ≠ p₂) (H₁ : Subgroup G) (H₂ : Subgroup G₂) [Finite H₁] [Finite H₂] (hH₁ : IsPGroup p₁ H₁) (hH₂ : IsPGroup p₂ H₂) : Nat.Coprime (Nat.card H₁) (Nat.card H₂)

views.nl_informal: p-groups with different p are disjoint
views.lean_signature: theorem IsPGroup.disjoint_of_ne (p₁ p₂ : ℕ) [hp₁ : Fact p₁.Prime] [hp₂ : Fact p₂.Prime] (hne : p₁ ≠ p₂) (H₁ H₂ : Subgroup G) (hH₁ : IsPGroup p₁ H₁) (hH₂ : IsPGroup p₂ H₂) : Disjoint H₁ H₂

views.nl_informal: The cardinality of the `center` of a `p`-group is `p ^ k` where `k` is positive.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsPGroup.card_center_eq_prime_pow (hGpn : Nat.card G = p ^ n) (hn : 0 < n) : ∃ k > 0, Nat.card (center G) = p ^ k

views.nl_informal: The quotient by the center of a group of cardinality `p ^ 2` is cyclic.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsPGroup.cyclic_center_quotient_of_card_eq_prime_sq (hG : Nat.card G = p ^ 2) : IsCyclic (G ⧸ center G)

views.nl_informal:
A group of order `p ^ 2` is commutative. See also `IsPGroup.commGroupOfCardEqPrimeSq`
for the `CommGroup` instance.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsPGroup.commutative_of_card_eq_prime_sq (hG : Nat.card G = p ^ 2) : ∀ a b : G, a * b = b * a

views.nl_informal:
The generators of a presented group generate the presented group. That is, the subgroup closure
of the set of generators equals `⊤`.
views.lean_signature: theorem PresentedGroup.closure_range_of (rels : Set (FreeGroup α)) : Subgroup.closure (Set.range (PresentedGroup.of : α → PresentedGroup rels)) = ⊤

views.nl_informal:
Given a word in `CoprodI`, if every letter is in the transversal and when
we multiply by an element of the base group it still has this property,
then the element of the base group we multiplied by was one.
views.lean_signature: theorem Monoid.PushoutI.NormalWord.eq_one_of_smul_normalized (w : CoprodI.Word G) {i : ι} (h : H) (hw : ∀ i g, ⟨i, g⟩ ∈ w.toList → g ∈ d.set i) (hφw : ∀ j g, ⟨j, g⟩ ∈ (CoprodI.of (φ i h) • w).toList → g ∈ d.set j) : h = 1

views.nl_informal:
All maps into the `PushoutI`, or amalgamated product of groups are injective,
provided all maps in the diagram are injective.

See also `base_injective`
views.lean_signature: theorem Monoid.PushoutI.of_injective (hφ : ∀ i, Function.Injective (φ i)) (i : ι) : Function.Injective (of (φ := φ) i)

views.nl_informal:
For any word `w` in the coproduct,
if `w` is reduced (i.e none its letters are in the image of the base monoid), and nonempty, then
`w` itself is not in the image of the base group.
views.lean_signature: theorem Monoid.PushoutI.Reduced.eq_empty_of_mem_range (hφ : ∀ i, Injective (φ i)) {w : Word G} (hw : Reduced φ w) (h : ofCoprodI w.prod ∈ (base φ).range) : w = .empty

views.nl_informal:
The intersection of the images of the maps from any two distinct groups in the diagram
into the amalgamated product is the image of the map from the base group in the diagram.
views.lean_signature: theorem Monoid.PushoutI.inf_of_range_eq_base_range (hφ : ∀ i, Injective (φ i)) {i j : ι} (hij : i ≠ j) : (of i).range ⊓ (of j).range = (base φ).range

views.nl_informal:
**Schreier's Lemma**: If `R : Set G` is a `rightTransversal` of `H : Subgroup G`
with `1 ∈ R`, and if `G` is generated by `S : Set G`, then `H` is generated by the `Set`
`(R * S).image (fun g ↦ g * (hR.toRightFun g)⁻¹)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Subgroup.closure_mul_image_eq (hR : IsComplement H R) (hR1 : (1 : G) ∈ R) (hS : closure S = ⊤) : closure ((R * S).image fun g => g * (hR.toRightFun g : G)⁻¹) = H

views.nl_informal:
**Schreier's Lemma**: If `R : Set G` is a `rightTransversal` of `H : Subgroup G`
with `1 ∈ R`, and if `G` is generated by `S : Set G`, then `H` is generated by the `Set`
`(R * S).image (fun g ↦ g * (hR.toRightFun g)⁻¹)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Subgroup.closure_mul_image_eq_top (hR : IsComplement H R) (hR1 : (1 : G) ∈ R) (hS : closure S = ⊤) : closure ((R * S).image fun g => ⟨g * (hR.toRightFun g : G)⁻¹, hR.mul_inv_toRightFun_mem g⟩ : Set H) = ⊤

views.nl_informal:
**Schreier's Lemma**: If `R : Finset G` is a `rightTransversal` of `H : Subgroup G`
with `1 ∈ R`, and if `G` is generated by `S : Finset G`, then `H` is generated by the `Finset`
`(R * S).image (fun g ↦ g * (hR.toRightFun g)⁻¹)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Subgroup.closure_mul_image_eq_top' [DecidableEq G] {R S : Finset G} (hR : IsComplement (H : Set G) R) (hR1 : (1 : G) ∈ R) (hS : closure (S : Set G) = ⊤) : closure (((R * S).image fun g => ⟨_, hR.mul_inv_toRightFun_mem g⟩ : Finset H) : Set H) = ⊤

views.nl_informal:
If `G` has `n` commutators `[g₁, g₂]`, then `|G'| ∣ [G : Z(G)] ^ ([G : Z(G)] * n + 1)`,
where `G'` denotes the commutator of `G`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Subgroup.card_commutator_dvd_index_center_pow [Finite (commutatorSet G)] : Nat.card (_root_.commutator G) ∣ (center G).index ^ ((center G).index * Nat.card (commutatorSet G) + 1)

views.nl_informal:
A theorem of Schur: The size of the commutator subgroup is bounded in terms of the number of
commutators.
views.lean_signature: theorem Subgroup.card_commutator_le_of_finite_commutatorSet [Finite (commutatorSet G)] : Nat.card (_root_.commutator G) ≤ cardCommutatorBound (Nat.card (commutatorSet G))

views.nl_informal:
**Schur-Zassenhaus** for normal subgroups:
If `H : Subgroup G` is normal, and has order coprime to its index, then there exists a
subgroup `K` which is a (right) complement of `H`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Subgroup.exists_right_complement'_of_coprime {N : Subgroup G} [N.Normal] (hN : Nat.Coprime (Nat.card N) N.index) : ∃ H : Subgroup G, IsComplement' N H

views.nl_informal:
**Schur-Zassenhaus** for normal subgroups:
If `H : Subgroup G` is normal, and has order coprime to its index, then there exists a
subgroup `K` which is a (left) complement of `H`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Subgroup.exists_left_complement'_of_coprime {N : Subgroup G} [N.Normal] (hN : Nat.Coprime (Nat.card N) N.index) : ∃ H : Subgroup G, IsComplement' H N

views.nl_informal:
Two maps out of the semidirect product are equal if they're equal after composition
with both `inl` and `inr`
views.lean_signature: theorem SemidirectProduct.hom_ext {f g : N ⋊[φ] G →* H} (hl : f.comp inl = g.comp inl) (hr : f.comp inr = g.comp inr) : f = g

views.nl_informal:
A generalization of **Sylow's first theorem**.
Every `p`-subgroup is contained in a Sylow `p`-subgroup.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsPGroup.exists_le_sylow {P : Subgroup G} (hP : IsPGroup p P) : ∃ Q : Sylow p G, P ≤ Q

views.nl_informal:
If the kernel of `f : H →* G` is a `p`-group,
then `Finite (Sylow p G)` implies `Finite (Sylow p H)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sylow.finite_of_ker_is_pGroup {H : Type*} [Group H] {f : H →* G} (hf : IsPGroup p f.ker) [Finite (Sylow p G)] : Finite (Sylow p H)

views.nl_informal: If `f : H →* G` is injective, then `Finite (Sylow p G)` implies `Finite (Sylow p H)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sylow.finite_of_injective {H : Type*} [Group H] {f : H →* G} (hf : Function.Injective f) [Finite (Sylow p G)] : Finite (Sylow p H)

views.nl_informal:
A generalization of **Sylow's third theorem**.
If the number of Sylow `p`-subgroups is finite, then it is congruent to `1` modulo `p`.
views.lean_signature: theorem card_sylow_modEq_one [Fact p.Prime] [Finite (Sylow p G)] : Nat.card (Sylow p G) ≡ 1 [MOD p]

views.nl_informal: A Sylow p-subgroup has index indivisible by `p`, assuming [N(P) : P] < ∞.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sylow.not_dvd_index' [hp : Fact p.Prime] [Finite (Sylow p G)] (P : Sylow p G) (hP : P.relindex P.normalizer ≠ 0) : ¬ p ∣ P.index

views.nl_informal: A Sylow p-subgroup has index indivisible by `p`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sylow.not_dvd_index [Fact p.Prime] [Finite (Sylow p G)] (P : Sylow p G) [P.FiniteIndex] : ¬ p ∣ P.index

views.nl_informal:
**Frattini's Argument**: If `N` is a normal subgroup of `G`, and if `P` is a Sylow `p`-subgroup
of `N`, then `N_G(P) ⊔ N = G`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sylow.normalizer_sup_eq_top {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {N : Subgroup G} [N.Normal] [Finite (Sylow p N)] (P : Sylow p N) : (P.map N.subtype).normalizer ⊔ N = ⊤

views.nl_informal:
**Frattini's Argument**: If `N` is a normal subgroup of `G`, and if `P` is a Sylow `p`-subgroup
of `N`, then `N_G(P) ⊔ N = G`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sylow.normalizer_sup_eq_top' {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {N : Subgroup G} [N.Normal] [Finite (Sylow p N)] (P : Sylow p G) (hP : P ≤ N) : P.normalizer ⊔ N = ⊤

views.nl_informal:
If `H` is a `p`-subgroup of `G`, then the index of `H` inside its normalizer is congruent
mod `p` to the index of `H`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sylow.card_quotient_normalizer_modEq_card_quotient [Finite G] {p : ℕ} {n : ℕ} [hp : Fact p.Prime] {H : Subgroup G} (hH : Nat.card H = p ^ n) : Nat.card (normalizer H ⧸ Subgroup.comap ((normalizer H).subtype : normalizer H →* G) H) ≡ Nat.card (G ⧸ H) [MOD p]

views.nl_informal:
If `H` is a subgroup of `G` of cardinality `p ^ n`, then the cardinality of the
normalizer of `H` is congruent mod `p ^ (n + 1)` to the cardinality of `G`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sylow.card_normalizer_modEq_card [Finite G] {p : ℕ} {n : ℕ} [hp : Fact p.Prime] {H : Subgroup G} (hH : Nat.card H = p ^ n) : Nat.card (normalizer H) ≡ Nat.card G [MOD p ^ (n + 1)]

views.nl_informal:
If `H` is a `p`-subgroup but not a Sylow `p`-subgroup, then `p` divides the
index of `H` inside its normalizer.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sylow.prime_dvd_card_quotient_normalizer [Finite G] {p : ℕ} {n : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (hdvd : p ^ (n + 1) ∣ Nat.card G) {H : Subgroup G} (hH : Nat.card H = p ^ n) : p ∣ Nat.card (normalizer H ⧸ Subgroup.comap ((normalizer H).subtype : normalizer H →* G) H)

views.nl_informal:
If `H` is a `p`-subgroup but not a Sylow `p`-subgroup of cardinality `p ^ n`,
then `p ^ (n + 1)` divides the cardinality of the normalizer of `H`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sylow.prime_pow_dvd_card_normalizer [Finite G] {p : ℕ} {n : ℕ} [_hp : Fact p.Prime] (hdvd : p ^ (n + 1) ∣ Nat.card G) {H : Subgroup G} (hH : Nat.card H = p ^ n) : p ^ (n + 1) ∣ Nat.card (normalizer H)

views.nl_informal:
If `H` is a subgroup of `G` of cardinality `p ^ n`,
then `H` is contained in a subgroup of cardinality `p ^ (n + 1)`
if `p ^ (n + 1)` divides the cardinality of `G`
views.lean_signature: theorem Sylow.exists_subgroup_card_pow_succ [Finite G] {p : ℕ} {n : ℕ} [hp : Fact p.Prime] (hdvd : p ^ (n + 1) ∣ Nat.card G) {H : Subgroup G} (hH : Nat.card H = p ^ n) : ∃ K : Subgroup G, Nat.card K = p ^ (n + 1) ∧ H ≤ K

views.nl_informal:
If `H` is a subgroup of `G` of cardinality `p ^ n`,
then `H` is contained in a subgroup of cardinality `p ^ m`
if `n ≤ m` and `p ^ m` divides the cardinality of `G`
views.lean_signature: theorem Sylow.exists_subgroup_card_pow_prime_le [Finite G] (p : ℕ) : ∀ {n m : ℕ} [_hp : Fact p.Prime] (_hdvd : p ^ m ∣ Nat.card G) (H : Subgroup G) (_hH : Nat.card H = p ^ n) (_hnm : n ≤ m), ∃ K : Subgroup G, Nat.card K = p ^ m ∧ H ≤ K

views.nl_informal:
A generalisation of **Sylow's first theorem**. If `p ^ n` divides
the cardinality of `G`, then there is a subgroup of cardinality `p ^ n`
views.lean_signature: theorem Sylow.exists_subgroup_card_pow_prime [Finite G] (p : ℕ) {n : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (hdvd : p ^ n ∣ Nat.card G) : ∃ K : Subgroup G, Nat.card K = p ^ n

views.nl_informal:
A special case of **Sylow's first theorem**. If `G` is a `p`-group of size at least `p ^ n`
then there is a subgroup of cardinality `p ^ n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sylow.exists_subgroup_card_pow_prime_of_le_card {n p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (h : IsPGroup p G) (hn : p ^ n ≤ Nat.card G) : ∃ H : Subgroup G, Nat.card H = p ^ n

views.nl_informal:
A special case of **Sylow's first theorem**. If `G` is a `p`-group and `H` a subgroup of size at
least `p ^ n` then there is a subgroup of `H` of cardinality `p ^ n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sylow.exists_subgroup_le_card_pow_prime_of_le_card {n p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (h : IsPGroup p G) {H : Subgroup G} (hn : p ^ n ≤ Nat.card H) : ∃ H' ≤ H, Nat.card H' = p ^ n

views.nl_informal:
A special case of **Sylow's first theorem**. If `G` is a `p`-group and `H` a subgroup of size at
least `k` then there is a subgroup of `H` of cardinality between `k / p` and `k`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sylow.exists_subgroup_le_card_le {k p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (h : IsPGroup p G) {H : Subgroup G} (hk : k ≤ Nat.card H) (hk₀ : k ≠ 0) : ∃ H' ≤ H, Nat.card H' ≤ k ∧ k < p * Nat.card H'

views.nl_informal: Sylow subgroups are Hall subgroups.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sylow.card_coprime_index [Finite G] {p : ℕ} [hp : Fact p.Prime] (P : Sylow p G) : (Nat.card P).Coprime P.index

views.nl_informal:
The cardinality of a Sylow subgroup is `p ^ n`
where `n` is the multiplicity of `p` in the group order.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sylow.card_eq_multiplicity [Finite G] {p : ℕ} [hp : Fact p.Prime] (P : Sylow p G) : Nat.card P = p ^ Nat.factorization (Nat.card G) p

views.nl_informal: A monoid is not a torsion monoid if it has an element of infinite order.

views.nl_informal: Subgroups of torsion groups are torsion groups.

views.nl_informal: The image of a surjective torsion group homomorphism is torsion.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsTorsion.of_surjective {f : G →* H} (hf : Function.Surjective f) (tG : IsTorsion G) : IsTorsion H

views.nl_informal: Torsion groups are closed under extensions.

views.nl_informal: The group exponent exists for any bounded torsion group.

views.nl_informal: Finite groups are torsion groups.

views.nl_informal: A module whose scalars are additively torsion is additively torsion.
views.lean_signature: theorem AddMonoid.IsTorsion.module_of_torsion [Semiring R] [Module R M] (tR : IsTorsion R) : IsTorsion M

views.nl_informal: A module with a finite ring of scalars is additively torsion.
views.lean_signature: theorem AddMonoid.IsTorsion.module_of_finite [Ring R] [Finite R] [Module R M] : IsTorsion M

views.nl_informal: Torsion submonoids are torsion.
views.lean_signature: theorem CommMonoid.torsion.isTorsion : IsTorsion <| torsion G

views.nl_informal: Elements of the `p`-primary component have order `p^n` for some `n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CommMonoid.primaryComponent.exists_orderOf_eq_prime_pow (g : CommMonoid.primaryComponent G p) : ∃ n : ℕ, orderOf g = p ^ n

views.nl_informal: The `p`- and `q`-primary components are disjoint for `p ≠ q`.

views.nl_informal: The torsion submonoid of a torsion monoid is `⊤`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Monoid.IsTorsion.torsion_eq_top (tG : IsTorsion G) : torsion G = ⊤

views.nl_informal: The torsion submonoid of an abelian group equals the torsion subgroup as a submonoid.
views.lean_signature: theorem CommGroup.torsion_eq_torsion_submonoid : CommMonoid.torsion G = (torsion G).toSubmonoid

views.nl_informal: The `p`-primary component is a `p` group.

views.nl_informal: A nontrivial monoid is not torsion-free if any nontrivial element has finite order.
views.lean_signature: theorem Monoid.not_isTorsionFree_iff : ¬IsTorsionFree G ↔ ∃ g : G, g ≠ 1 ∧ IsOfFinOrder g

views.nl_informal: A nontrivial torsion group is not torsion-free.
views.lean_signature: theorem Monoid.IsTorsion.not_torsion_free [hN : Nontrivial G] : IsTorsion G → ¬IsTorsionFree G

views.nl_informal: A nontrivial torsion-free group is not torsion.
views.lean_signature: theorem Monoid.IsTorsionFree.not_torsion [hN : Nontrivial G] : IsTorsionFree G → ¬IsTorsion G

views.nl_informal: Subgroups of torsion-free groups are torsion-free.

views.lean_signature: theorem Monoid.IsTorsionFree.quotient_torsion : IsTorsionFree <| G ⧸ torsion G

views.nl_informal: Explicit computation of the transfer homomorphism.

views.lean_signature: theorem Subgroup.commutator_commutator_eq_bot_of_rotate (h1 : ⁅⁅H₂, H₃⁆, H₁⁆ = ⊥) (h2 : ⁅⁅H₃, H₁⁆, H₂⁆ = ⊥) : ⁅⁅H₁, H₂⁆, H₃⁆ = ⊥

views.nl_informal:
The commutator of direct product is contained in the direct product of the commutators.
