views.nl_informal:
Given a congruence relation `c` on a monoid and a homomorphism `f` constant on `c`'s
equivalence classes, `f` has the same image as the homomorphism that `f` induces on the
quotient.
views.lean_signature: theorem Con.lift_range (H : c ≤ ker f) : MonoidHom.mrange (c.lift f H) = MonoidHom.mrange f

views.nl_informal:
Given a monoid homomorphism `f`, the induced homomorphism on the quotient by `f`'s kernel has
the same image as `f`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Con.kerLift_range_eq : MonoidHom.mrange (kerLift f) = MonoidHom.mrange f

views.nl_informal: Multiplicative congruence relations preserve product indexed by a list.
views.lean_signature: theorem Con.list_prod {ι M : Type*} [MulOneClass M] (c : Con M) {l : List ι} {f g : ι → M} (h : ∀ x ∈ l, c (f x) (g x)) : c (l.map f).prod (l.map g).prod

views.nl_informal: Multiplicative congruence relations preserve product indexed by a multiset.
views.lean_signature: theorem Con.multiset_prod {ι M : Type*} [CommMonoid M] (c : Con M) {s : Multiset ι} {f g : ι → M} (h : ∀ x ∈ s, c (f x) (g x)) : c (s.map f).prod (s.map g).prod

views.nl_informal: Multiplicative congruence relations preserve finite product.
views.lean_signature: theorem Con.finset_prod {ι M : Type*} [CommMonoid M] (c : Con M) (s : Finset ι) {f g : ι → M} (h : ∀ i ∈ s, c (f i) (g i)) : c (s.prod f) (s.prod g)

views.nl_informal: Congruence relations are reflexive.
views.lean_signature: theorem Con.refl (x) : c x x

views.nl_informal: Congruence relations are symmetric.
views.lean_signature: theorem Con.symm {x y} : c x y → c y x

views.nl_informal: Congruence relations are transitive.
views.lean_signature: theorem Con.trans {x y z} : c x y → c y z → c x z

views.nl_informal: Multiplicative congruence relations preserve multiplication.
views.lean_signature: theorem Con.mul {w x y z} : c w x → c y z → c (w * y) (x * z)

views.nl_informal: The map sending a congruence relation to its underlying binary relation is injective.
views.lean_signature: theorem Con.ext' {c d : Con M} (H : ⇑c = ⇑d) : c = d

views.nl_informal: Extensionality rule for congruence relations.
views.lean_signature: theorem Con.ext {c d : Con M} (H : ∀ x y, c x y ↔ d x y) : c = d

views.nl_informal: The map sending a congruence relation to its underlying equivalence relation is injective.
views.lean_signature: theorem Con.toSetoid_inj {c d : Con M} (H : c.toSetoid = d.toSetoid) : c = d

views.nl_informal: Two congruence relations are equal iff their underlying binary relations are equal.
views.lean_signature: theorem Con.coe_inj {c d : Con M} : ⇑c = ⇑d ↔ c = d

views.nl_informal:
The inductive principle used to prove propositions about the elements of a quotient by a
congruence relation.
views.lean_signature: theorem Con.induction_on {C : c.Quotient → Prop} (q : c.Quotient) (H : ∀ x : M, C x) : C q

views.nl_informal:
Two elements are related by a congruence relation `c` iff they are represented by the same
element of the quotient by `c`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Con.eq {a b : M} : (a : c.Quotient) = (b : c.Quotient) ↔ c a b

views.nl_informal:
The coercion to the quotient of a congruence relation commutes with multiplication (by
definition).
views.lean_signature: theorem Con.coe_mul (x y : M) : (↑(x * y) : c.Quotient) = ↑x * ↑y

views.nl_informal:
Definition of the function on the quotient by a congruence relation `c` induced by a function
that is constant on `c`'s equivalence classes.
views.lean_signature: theorem Con.liftOn_coe {β} (c : Con M) (f : M → β) (h : ∀ a b, c a b → f a = f b) (x : M) : Con.liftOn (x : c.Quotient) f h = f x

views.nl_informal: Definition of `≤` for congruence relations.
views.lean_signature: theorem Con.le_def {c d : Con M} : c ≤ d ↔ ∀ {x y}, c x y → d x y

views.nl_informal:
The infimum of a set of congruence relations is the same as the infimum of the set's image
under the map to the underlying equivalence relation.
views.lean_signature: theorem Con.sInf_toSetoid (S : Set (Con M)) : (sInf S).toSetoid = sInf (toSetoid '' S)

views.nl_informal:
The infimum of a set of congruence relations is the same as the infimum of the set's image
under the map to the underlying binary relation.
views.lean_signature: theorem Con.coe_sInf (S : Set (Con M)) : ⇑(sInf S) = sInf ((⇑) '' S)

views.nl_informal:
The infimum of two congruence relations equals the infimum of the underlying binary
operations.
views.lean_signature: theorem Con.coe_inf {c d : Con M} : ⇑(c ⊓ d) = ⇑c ⊓ ⇑d

views.nl_informal: Definition of the infimum of two congruence relations.
views.lean_signature: theorem Con.inf_iff_and {c d : Con M} {x y} : (c ⊓ d) x y ↔ c x y ∧ d x y

views.nl_informal:
The inductively defined smallest congruence relation containing a binary relation `r` equals
the infimum of the set of congruence relations containing `r`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Con.conGen_eq (r : M → M → Prop) : conGen r = sInf { s : Con M | ∀ x y, r x y → s x y }

views.nl_informal:
The smallest congruence relation containing a binary relation `r` is contained in any
congruence relation containing `r`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Con.conGen_le {r : M → M → Prop} {c : Con M} (h : ∀ x y, r x y → c x y) : conGen r ≤ c

views.nl_informal:
Given binary relations `r, s` with `r` contained in `s`, the smallest congruence relation
containing `s` contains the smallest congruence relation containing `r`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Con.conGen_mono {r s : M → M → Prop} (h : ∀ x y, r x y → s x y) : conGen r ≤ conGen s

views.nl_informal: Congruence relations equal the smallest congruence relation in which they are contained.
views.lean_signature: theorem Con.conGen_of_con (c : Con M) : conGen c = c

views.nl_informal:
The map sending a binary relation to the smallest congruence relation in which it is
contained is idempotent.
views.lean_signature: theorem Con.conGen_idem (r : M → M → Prop) : conGen (conGen r) = conGen r

views.nl_informal:
The supremum of congruence relations `c, d` equals the smallest congruence relation containing
the binary relation '`x` is related to `y` by `c` or `d`'.
views.lean_signature: theorem Con.sup_eq_conGen (c d : Con M) : c ⊔ d = conGen fun x y => c x y ∨ d x y

views.nl_informal:
The supremum of two congruence relations equals the smallest congruence relation containing
the supremum of the underlying binary operations.
views.lean_signature: theorem Con.sup_def {c d : Con M} : c ⊔ d = conGen (⇑c ⊔ ⇑d)

views.nl_informal:
The supremum of a set of congruence relations `S` equals the smallest congruence relation
containing the binary relation 'there exists `c ∈ S` such that `x` is related to `y` by
`c`'.
views.lean_signature: theorem Con.sSup_eq_conGen (S : Set (Con M)) : sSup S = conGen fun x y => ∃ c : Con M, c ∈ S ∧ c x y

views.nl_informal:
The supremum of a set of congruence relations is the same as the smallest congruence relation
containing the supremum of the set's image under the map to the underlying binary relation.
views.lean_signature: theorem Con.sSup_def {S : Set (Con M)} : sSup S = conGen (sSup ((⇑) '' S))

views.nl_informal:
The 1 of the quotient of a monoid by a congruence relation is the equivalence class of the
monoid's 1.
views.lean_signature: theorem Con.coe_one : ((1 : M) : c.Quotient) = 1

views.nl_informal: Multiplicative congruence relations preserve natural powers.
views.lean_signature: theorem Con.pow {M : Type*} [Monoid M] (c : Con M) : ∀ (n : ℕ) {w x}, c w x → c (w ^ n) (x ^ n)

views.nl_informal:
Sometimes, a group is defined as a quotient of a monoid by a congruence relation.
Usually, the inverse operation is defined as `Setoid.map f _` for some `f`.
This lemma allows to avoid code duplication in the definition of the inverse operation:
instead of proving both `∀ x y, c x y → c (f x) (f y)` (to define the operation)
and `∀ x, c (f x * x) 1` (to prove the group laws), one can only prove the latter.

views.lean_signature: theorem Equiv.Perm.IsCycle.commute_iff' {g c : Perm α} (hc : c.IsCycle) : Commute g c ↔ ∃ hc' : ∀ x : α, x ∈ c.support ↔ g x ∈ c.support, subtypePerm g hc' ∈ Subgroup.zpowers c.subtypePermOfSupport

views.nl_informal:
A permutation `g` commutes with a cycle `c` if and only if
`c.support` is invariant under `g`, and `g` acts on it as a power of `c`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Equiv.Perm.IsCycle.commute_iff {g c : Perm α} (hc : c.IsCycle) : Commute g c ↔ ∃ hc' : ∀ x : α, x ∈ c.support ↔ g x ∈ c.support, ofSubtype (subtypePerm g hc') ∈ Subgroup.zpowers c

views.nl_informal: `x` is in the support of `f` iff `Equiv.Perm.cycle_of f x` is a cycle.
views.lean_signature: theorem Equiv.Perm.isCycle_cycleOf_iff (f : Perm α) [DecidableRel f.SameCycle] : IsCycle (cycleOf f x) ↔ f x ≠ x

views.nl_informal: Two cycles of a permutation commute.
views.lean_signature: theorem Equiv.Perm.cycleFactorsFinset_mem_commute : (cycleFactorsFinset f : Set (Perm α)).Pairwise Commute

views.nl_informal: Two cycles of a permutation commute.
views.lean_signature: theorem Equiv.Perm.cycleFactorsFinset_mem_commute' {g1 g2 : Perm α} (h1 : g1 ∈ f.cycleFactorsFinset) (h2 : g2 ∈ f.cycleFactorsFinset) : Commute g1 g2

views.nl_informal: The product of cycle factors is equal to the original `f : perm α`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Equiv.Perm.cycleFactorsFinset_noncommProd (comm : (cycleFactorsFinset f : Set (Perm α)).Pairwise Commute := cycleFactorsFinset_mem_commute f) : f.cycleFactorsFinset.noncommProd id comm = f

views.nl_informal: Two permutations `f g : Perm α` have the same cycle factors iff they are the same.
views.lean_signature: theorem Equiv.Perm.cycleFactorsFinset_injective : Function.Injective (@cycleFactorsFinset α _ _)

views.nl_informal: If c is a cycle, a ∈ c.support and c is a cycle of f, then `c = f.cycleOf a`
views.lean_signature: theorem Equiv.Perm.cycle_is_cycleOf {f c : Equiv.Perm α} {a : α} (ha : a ∈ c.support) (hc : c ∈ f.cycleFactorsFinset) : c = f.cycleOf a

views.nl_informal: A permutation `c` is a cycle of `g` iff `k * c * k⁻¹` is a cycle of `k * g * k⁻¹`
views.lean_signature: theorem Equiv.Perm.mem_cycleFactorsFinset_conj (g k c : Perm α) : k * c * k⁻¹ ∈ (k * g * k⁻¹).cycleFactorsFinset ↔ c ∈ g.cycleFactorsFinset

views.nl_informal:
If a permutation commutes with every cycle of `g`, then it commutes with `g`

NB. The converse is false. Commuting with every cycle of `g` means that we belong
to the kernel of the action of `Equiv.Perm α` on `g.cycleFactorsFinset`
views.lean_signature: theorem Equiv.Perm.commute_of_mem_cycleFactorsFinset_commute (k g : Perm α) (hk : ∀ c ∈ g.cycleFactorsFinset, Commute k c) : Commute k g

views.nl_informal: The cycles of a permutation commute with it
views.lean_signature: theorem Equiv.Perm.self_mem_cycle_factors_commute {g c : Perm α} (hc : c ∈ g.cycleFactorsFinset) : Commute c g

views.nl_informal: If `c` and `d` are cycles of `g`, then `d` stabilizes the support of `c`
views.lean_signature: theorem Equiv.Perm.mem_support_cycle_of_cycle {g d c : Perm α} (hc : c ∈ g.cycleFactorsFinset) (hd : d ∈ g.cycleFactorsFinset) : ∀ x : α, x ∈ c.support ↔ d x ∈ c.support

views.nl_informal: If a permutation is a cycle of `g`, then its support is invariant under `g`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Equiv.Perm.mem_cycleFactorsFinset_support {g c : Perm α} (hc : c ∈ g.cycleFactorsFinset) (a : α) : a ∈ c.support ↔ g a ∈ c.support

views.nl_informal: A permutation restricted to the support of a cycle factor is that cycle factor
views.lean_signature: theorem Equiv.Perm.subtypePerm_on_cycleFactorsFinset [DecidableEq α] [Fintype α] {g c : Perm α} (hc : c ∈ g.cycleFactorsFinset) : g.subtypePerm (mem_cycleFactorsFinset_support hc) = c.subtypePermOfSupport

views.nl_informal:
For any `c : List ℕ` whose sum is at most `Fintype.card α`,
we can find `o : List (List α)` whose members have no duplicate,
whose lengths given by `c`, and which are pairwise disjoint
views.lean_signature: theorem List.exists_pw_disjoint_with_card {α : Type*} [Fintype α] {c : List ℕ} (hc : c.sum ≤ Fintype.card α) : ∃ o : List (List α), o.map length = c ∧ (∀ s ∈ o, s.Nodup) ∧ Pairwise List.Disjoint o

views.nl_informal:
There are permutations with cycleType `m` if and only if
its sum is at most `Fintype.card α` and its members are at least 2.
views.lean_signature: theorem Equiv.Perm.exists_with_cycleType_iff {m : Multiset ℕ} : (∃ g : Equiv.Perm α, g.cycleType = m) ↔ (m.sum ≤ Fintype.card α ∧ ∀ a ∈ m, 2 ≤ a)

views.nl_informal:
The number of fixed points of a `p ^ n`-th root of the identity function over a finite set
and the set's cardinality have the same residue modulo `p`, where `p` is a prime.
views.lean_signature: theorem Equiv.Perm.card_fixedPoints_modEq [DecidableEq α] {f : Function.End α} {p n : ℕ} [hp : Fact p.Prime] (hf : f ^ p ^ n = 1) : Fintype.card α ≡ Fintype.card f.fixedPoints [MOD p]

views.nl_informal:
For every prime `p` dividing the order of a finite group `G` there exists an element of order
`p` in `G`. This is known as Cauchy's theorem.
views.lean_signature: theorem exists_prime_orderOf_dvd_card {G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G] (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact p.Prime] (hdvd : p ∣ Fintype.card G) : ∃ x : G, orderOf x = p

views.nl_informal:
For every prime `p` dividing the order of a finite additive group `G` there exists an element of
order `p` in `G`. This is the additive version of Cauchy's theorem.
views.lean_signature: theorem exists_prime_addOrderOf_dvd_card {G : Type*} [AddGroup G] [Fintype G] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hdvd : p ∣ Fintype.card G) : ∃ x : G, addOrderOf x = p

views.nl_informal:
For every prime `p` dividing the order of a finite group `G` there exists an element of order
`p` in `G`. This is known as Cauchy's theorem.
views.lean_signature: theorem exists_prime_orderOf_dvd_card' {G : Type*} [Group G] [Finite G] (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact p.Prime] (hdvd : p ∣ Nat.card G) : ∃ x : G, orderOf x = p

views.nl_informal: If the quotient by a subgroup gives a singleton then the subgroup is the whole group.
views.lean_signature: theorem QuotientGroup.subgroup_eq_top_of_subsingleton (H : Subgroup G) (h : Subsingleton (G ⧸ H)) : H = ⊤

views.nl_informal:
The congruence relation defined by the kernel of a group homomorphism is equal to its kernel
as a congruence relation.
views.lean_signature: theorem QuotientGroup.con_ker_eq_conKer (f : G →* M) : QuotientGroup.con f.ker = Con.ker f

views.nl_informal:
Two `MonoidHom`s from a quotient group are equal if their compositions with
`QuotientGroup.mk'` are equal.

See note [partially-applied ext lemmas].
views.lean_signature: theorem QuotientGroup.monoidHom_ext ⦃f g : G ⧸ N →* M⦄ (h : f.comp (mk' N) = g.comp (mk' N)) : f = g

views.nl_informal:
A key lemma to prove $A_5$ is simple. Shows that any normal subgroup of an alternating group on
at least 5 elements is the entire alternating group if it contains a 3-cycle.
views.lean_signature: theorem Equiv.Perm.IsThreeCycle.alternating_normalClosure (h5 : 5 ≤ Fintype.card α) {f : Perm α} (hf : IsThreeCycle f) : normalClosure ({⟨f, hf.mem_alternatingGroup⟩} : Set (alternatingGroup α)) = ⊤

views.nl_informal:
Part of proving $A_5$ is simple. Shows that the square of any element of $A_5$ with a 3-cycle in
its cycle decomposition is a 3-cycle, so the normal closure of the original element must be
$A_5$.
views.lean_signature: theorem Equiv.Perm.isThreeCycle_sq_of_three_mem_cycleType_five {g : Perm (Fin 5)} (h : 3 ∈ cycleType g) : IsThreeCycle (g * g)

views.nl_informal:
The normal closure of the 5-cycle `finRotate 5` within $A_5$ is the whole group. This will be
used to show that the normal closure of any 5-cycle within $A_5$ is the whole group.
views.lean_signature: theorem alternatingGroup.normalClosure_finRotate_five : normalClosure ({⟨finRotate 5, finRotate_bit1_mem_alternatingGroup (n := 2)⟩} : Set (alternatingGroup (Fin 5))) = ⊤

views.nl_informal:
The normal closure of $(04)(13)$ within $A_5$ is the whole group. This will be
used to show that the normal closure of any permutation of cycle type $(2,2)$ is the whole group.
views.lean_signature: theorem alternatingGroup.normalClosure_swap_mul_swap_five : normalClosure ({⟨swap 0 4 * swap 1 3, mem_alternatingGroup.2 (by decide)⟩} : Set (alternatingGroup (Fin 5))) = ⊤

views.nl_informal:
Shows that any non-identity element of $A_5$ whose cycle decomposition consists only of swaps
is conjugate to $(04)(13)$. This is used to show that the normal closure of such a permutation
in $A_5$ is $A_5$.
views.lean_signature: theorem alternatingGroup.isConj_swap_mul_swap_of_cycleType_two {g : Perm (Fin 5)} (ha : g ∈ alternatingGroup (Fin 5)) (h1 : g ≠ 1) (h2 : ∀ n, n ∈ cycleType (g : Perm (Fin 5)) → n = 2) : IsConj (swap 0 4 * swap 1 3) g

views.nl_informal: The alternating group is the only subgroup of index 2 of the permutation group.
views.lean_signature: theorem Equiv.Perm.eq_alternatingGroup_of_index_eq_two {G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm α)} (hG : G.index = 2) : G = alternatingGroup α

views.nl_informal: A subgroup of the permutation group of index ≤ 2 contains the alternating group.
views.lean_signature: theorem Equiv.Perm.alternatingGroup_le_of_index_le_two {G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm α)} (hG : G.index ≤ 2) : alternatingGroup α ≤ G

views.nl_informal: A non-cyclic multiplicative group is non-trivial.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nontrivial.of_not_isCyclic (nc : ¬IsCyclic α) : Nontrivial α

views.nl_informal: Any non-identity element of a finite group of prime order generates the group.
views.lean_signature: theorem zpowers_eq_top_of_prime_card {p : ℕ} [hp : Fact p.Prime] (h : Nat.card G = p) {g : G} (hg : g ≠ 1) : zpowers g = ⊤

views.nl_informal: A finite group of prime order is cyclic.
views.lean_signature: theorem isCyclic_of_prime_card {p : ℕ} [hp : Fact p.Prime] (h : Nat.card α = p) : IsCyclic α

views.nl_informal: A finite group of order dividing a prime is cyclic.
views.lean_signature: theorem isCyclic_of_card_dvd_prime {p : ℕ} [hp : Fact p.Prime] (h : Nat.card α ∣ p) : IsCyclic α

views.nl_informal: A finite group of prime order is simple.
views.lean_signature: theorem isSimpleGroup_of_prime_card {p : ℕ} [hp : Fact p.Prime] (h : Nat.card α = p) : IsSimpleGroup α

views.nl_informal:
A group is commutative if the quotient by the center is cyclic.
Also see `commGroupOfCyclicCenterQuotient` for the `CommGroup` instance.
views.lean_signature: theorem commutative_of_cyclic_center_quotient [IsCyclic G'] (f : G →* G') (hf : f.ker ≤ center G) (a b : G) : a * b = b * a

views.nl_informal: A group of order `p ^ 2` is not cyclic if and only if its exponent is `p`.
views.lean_signature: theorem not_isCyclic_iff_exponent_eq_prime [Group α] {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hα : Nat.card α = p ^ 2) : ¬ IsCyclic α ↔ Monoid.exponent α = p

views.nl_informal:
The kernel of `zmultiplesHom G g` is equal to the additive subgroup generated by
`addOrderOf g`.
views.lean_signature: theorem zmultiplesHom_ker_eq [AddGroup G] (g : G) : (zmultiplesHom G g).ker = zmultiples ↑(addOrderOf g)

views.nl_informal: The kernel of `zpowersHom G g` is equal to the subgroup generated by `orderOf g`.
views.lean_signature: theorem zpowersHom_ker_eq [Group G] (g : G) : (zpowersHom G g).ker = zpowers (Multiplicative.ofAdd ↑(orderOf g))

views.nl_informal: Two group homomorphisms `G →* G'` are equal if and only if they agree on a generator of `G`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MonoidHom.eq_iff_eq_on_generator (f₁ f₂ : G →* G') : f₁ = f₂ ↔ f₁ g = f₂ g

views.nl_informal: Two group isomorphisms `G ≃* G'` are equal if and only if they agree on a generator of `G`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MulEquiv.eq_iff_eq_on_generator (f₁ f₂ : G ≃* G') : f₁ = f₂ ↔ f₁ g = f₂ g

views.nl_informal: If `0 < n`, then `DihedralGroup n` has `2n` elements.
views.lean_signature: theorem DihedralGroup.card [NeZero n] : Fintype.card (DihedralGroup n) = 2 * n

views.nl_informal: If `0 < n`, then `sr i` has order 2.
views.lean_signature: theorem DihedralGroup.orderOf_sr (i : ZMod n) : orderOf (sr i) = 2

views.nl_informal: If `0 < n`, then `r 1` has order `n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem DihedralGroup.orderOf_r_one : orderOf (r 1 : DihedralGroup n) = n

views.nl_informal: If `0 < n`, then `i : ZMod n` has order `n / gcd n i`.
views.lean_signature: theorem DihedralGroup.orderOf_r [NeZero n] (i : ZMod n) : orderOf (r i) = n / Nat.gcd n i.val

views.lean_signature: theorem DihedralGroup.card_commute_odd (hn : Odd n) : Nat.card { p : DihedralGroup n × DihedralGroup n // Commute p.1 p.2 } = n * (n + 3)

views.nl_informal: Any two `IsKleinFour` groups are isomorphic.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsKleinFour.nonempty_mulEquiv [IsKleinFour G₂] : Nonempty (G₁ ≃* G₂)

views.nl_informal: If `0 < n`, then `QuaternionGroup n` has `4n` elements.
views.lean_signature: theorem QuaternionGroup.card [NeZero n] : Fintype.card (QuaternionGroup n) = 4 * n

views.nl_informal: If `0 < n`, then `xa i` has order 4.
views.lean_signature: theorem QuaternionGroup.orderOf_xa [NeZero n] (i : ZMod (2 * n)) : orderOf (xa i) = 4

views.nl_informal: In the special case `n = 1`, `Quaternion 1` is a cyclic group (of order `4`).
views.lean_signature: theorem QuaternionGroup.quaternionGroup_one_isCyclic : IsCyclic (QuaternionGroup 1)

views.nl_informal: If `0 < n`, then `a 1` has order `2 * n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem QuaternionGroup.orderOf_a_one : orderOf (a 1 : QuaternionGroup n) = 2 * n

views.nl_informal: If `0 < n`, then `a i` has order `(2 * n) / gcd (2 * n) i`.
views.lean_signature: theorem QuaternionGroup.orderOf_a [NeZero n] (i : ZMod (2 * n)) : orderOf (a i) = 2 * n / Nat.gcd (2 * n) i.val

views.nl_informal: A finite Z-group has cyclic commutator subgroup.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsZGroup.isCyclic_commutator [Finite G] [IsZGroup G] : IsCyclic (commutator G)

views.nl_informal:
If a cyclic `p`-group `G` acts on a group `K` of coprime order, then the map `K × G → G`
defined by `(k, g) ↦ k • g * g⁻¹` is either trivial or surjective.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsPGroup.smul_mul_inv_trivial_or_surjective [IsCyclic G] (hG : IsPGroup p G) {K : Type*} [Group K] [MulDistribMulAction K G] (hGK : (Nat.card G).Coprime (Nat.card K)) : (∀ g : G, ∀ k : K, k • g * g⁻¹ = 1) ∨ (∀ g : G, ∃ k : K, ∃ q : G, k • q * q⁻¹ = g)

views.nl_informal:
If a cyclic `p`-subgroup `P` acts by conjugation on a subgroup `K` of coprime order, then
either `⁅K, P⁆ = ⊥` or `⁅K, P⁆ = P`.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsPGroup.commutator_eq_bot_or_commutator_eq_self {P K : Subgroup G} [IsCyclic P] (hP : IsPGroup p P) (hKP : K ≤ P.normalizer) (hPK : (Nat.card P).Coprime (Nat.card K)) : ⁅K, P⁆ = ⊥ ∨ ⁅K, P⁆ = P

views.nl_informal:
If a normal cyclic Sylow `p`-subgroup `P` has a complement `K`, then either `⁅K, P⁆ = ⊥` or
`⁅K, P⁆ = P`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sylow.commutator_eq_bot_or_commutator_eq_self [P.Normal] {K : Subgroup G} (h : K.IsComplement' P) : ⁅K, P.1⁆ = ⊥ ∨ ⁅K, P.1⁆ = P

views.nl_informal: A normal cyclic Sylow subgroup is either central or contained in the commutator subgroup.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sylow.le_center_or_le_commutator [P.Normal] : P ≤ Subgroup.center G ∨ P ≤ commutator G

views.nl_informal:
A cyclic Sylow subgroup is either central in its normalizer or contained in the commutator
subgroup.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sylow.normalizer_le_centralizer_or_le_commutator : P.normalizer ≤ Subgroup.centralizer P ∨ P ≤ commutator G

views.nl_informal:
If `G` has a cyclic Sylow `p`-subgroup, then the cardinality and index of the commutator
subgroup of `G` cannot both be divisible by `p`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sylow.not_dvd_card_commutator_or_not_dvd_index_commutator : ¬ p ∣ Nat.card (commutator G) ∨ ¬ p ∣ (commutator G).index

views.nl_informal: If `G` is a finite Z-group, then `commutator G` is a Hall subgroup of `G`.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsZGroup.coprime_commutator_index [Finite G] [IsZGroup G] : (Nat.card (commutator G)).Coprime (commutator G).index

views.nl_informal: An extension of coprime Z-groups is a Z-group.
views.lean_signature: theorem isZGroup_of_coprime [Finite G] [IsZGroup G] [IsZGroup G''] (h_le : f'.ker ≤ f.range) (h_cop : (Nat.card G).Coprime (Nat.card G'')) : IsZGroup G'

views.nl_informal:
A finite group `G` is a Z-group if and only if `G` is isomorphic to a semidirect product of two
cyclic subgroups of coprime order.
views.lean_signature: theorem isZGroup_iff_exists_mulEquiv [Finite G] : IsZGroup G ↔ ∃ (N H : Subgroup G) (φ : H →* MulAut N) (_ : G ≃* N ⋊[φ] H), IsCyclic H ∧ IsCyclic N ∧ (Nat.card N).Coprime (Nat.card H)

views.nl_informal: The cardinality of even permutations of given `cycleType`
views.lean_signature: theorem AlternatingGroup.card_of_cycleType_mul_eq (m : Multiset ℕ) : #{g : alternatingGroup α | g.val.cycleType = m} * ((Fintype.card α - m.sum)! * m.prod * (∏ n ∈ m.toFinset, (m.count n)!)) = if ((m.sum ≤ Fintype.card α ∧ ∀ a ∈ m, 2 ≤ a) ∧ Even (m.sum + Multiset.card m)) then (Fintype.card α)! else 0

views.nl_informal: The cardinality of even permutations of given `cycleType`
views.lean_signature: theorem AlternatingGroup.card_of_cycleType (m : Multiset ℕ) : #{g : alternatingGroup α | (g : Equiv.Perm α).cycleType = m} = if (m.sum ≤ Fintype.card α ∧ ∀ a ∈ m, 2 ≤ a) ∧ Even (m.sum + Multiset.card m) then (Fintype.card α)! / ((Fintype.card α - m.sum)! * (m.prod * (∏ n ∈ m.toFinset, (m.count n)!))) else 0

views.nl_informal: The number of cycles of given length
views.lean_signature: theorem AlternatingGroup.card_of_cycleType_singleton {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hα : n ≤ card α) : #{g : alternatingGroup α | g.val.cycleType = {n}} = if Odd n then (n - 1)! * (choose (card α) n) else 0

views.nl_informal:
The centralizer of a permutation is contained in the alternating group if and only if
its cycles have odd length, with at most one of each, and there is at most one fixed point.
views.lean_signature: theorem Equiv.Perm.centralizer_le_alternating_iff : Subgroup.centralizer {g} ≤ alternatingGroup α ↔ (∀ c ∈ g.cycleType, Odd c) ∧ Fintype.card α ≤ g.cycleType.sum + 1 ∧ ∀ i, g.cycleType.count i ≤ 1

views.nl_informal:
**Gibbs' inequality**: the Kullback-Leibler divergence is nonnegative.
Note that since `klDiv` takes value in `ℝ≥0∞` (defined when it is finite as `ENNReal.ofReal (...)`),
it is nonnegative by definition. This lemma proves that the argument of `ENNReal.ofReal`
is also nonnegative.
views.lean_signature: theorem InformationTheory.integral_llr_add_sub_measure_univ_nonneg (hμν : μ ≪ ν) (h_int : Integrable (llr μ ν) μ) : 0 ≤ ∫ x, llr μ ν x ∂μ + ν.real univ - μ.real univ

views.nl_informal:
If `μ ≪ ν` and `μ univ = ν univ`, then `toReal` of the Kullback-Leibler divergence is equal to
an integral, without any integrability condition.
views.lean_signature: theorem InformationTheory.toReal_klDiv_of_measure_eq (h : μ ≪ ν) (h_eq : μ univ = ν univ) : (klDiv μ ν).toReal = ∫ a, llr μ ν a ∂μ

views.nl_informal:
**Converse Gibbs' inequality**: the Kullback-Leibler divergence between two finite measures is
zero if and only if the two measures are equal.
views.lean_signature: theorem InformationTheory.klDiv_eq_zero_iff [IsFiniteMeasure μ] [IsFiniteMeasure ν] : klDiv μ ν = 0 ↔ μ = ν

views.nl_informal: `klFun` is strictly convex on [0,∞).
views.lean_signature: theorem InformationTheory.strictConvexOn_klFun : StrictConvexOn ℝ (Ici 0) klFun

views.nl_informal: `klFun` is convex on [0,∞).
views.lean_signature: theorem InformationTheory.convexOn_klFun : ConvexOn ℝ (Ici 0) klFun

views.nl_informal:
`klFun` is convex on (0,∞).

views.lean_signature: theorem InformationTheory.convexOn_Ioi_klFun : ConvexOn ℝ (Ioi 0) klFun

views.nl_informal: `klFun` is continuous.
views.lean_signature: theorem InformationTheory.continuous_klFun : Continuous klFun

views.nl_informal: `klFun` is measurable.
views.lean_signature: theorem InformationTheory.measurable_klFun : Measurable klFun

views.nl_informal: `klFun` is strongly measurable.
views.lean_signature: theorem InformationTheory.stronglyMeasurable_klFun : StronglyMeasurable klFun

views.nl_informal: The derivative of `klFun` at `x ≠ 0` is `log x`.

views.lean_signature: theorem InformationTheory.deriv_klFun : deriv klFun = log

views.nl_informal:

differentiable there since the default value of `derivWithin` in that case is 0.
views.lean_signature: theorem InformationTheory.rightDeriv_klFun : derivWithin klFun (Ioi x) x = log x

views.nl_informal:
The left derivative of `klFun` is `log x`. This also holds at `x = 0` although `klFun` is not
differentiable there since the default value of `derivWithin` in that case is 0.
views.lean_signature: theorem InformationTheory.leftDeriv_klFun : derivWithin klFun (Iio x) x = log x

views.nl_informal: The function `klFun` is nonnegative on `[0,∞)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem InformationTheory.klFun_nonneg (hx : 0 ≤ x) : 0 ≤ klFun x

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:
**Goursat's lemma** for a submodule of a product with surjective projections.

If `L` is a submodule of `M × N` which projects fully on both factors, then there exist submodules
`M' ≤ M` and `N' ≤ N` such that `M' × N' ≤ L` and the image of `L` in `(M ⧸ M') × (N ⧸ N')` is the
graph of an isomorphism of `R`-modules `(M ⧸ M') ≃ (N ⧸ N')`.

`M` and `N` can be explicitly constructed as `L.goursatFst` and `L.goursatSnd` respectively.
views.lean_signature: theorem Submodule.goursat_surjective : ∃ e : (M ⧸ L.goursatFst) ≃ₗ[R] N ⧸ L.goursatSnd, LinearMap.range ((L.goursatFst.mkQ.prodMap L.goursatSnd.mkQ).comp L.subtype) = e.graph

views.nl_informal:
**Goursat's lemma** for an arbitrary submodule of a product.

If `L` is a submodule of `M × N`, then there exist submodules `M'' ≤ M' ≤ M` and `N'' ≤ N' ≤ N` such
that `L ≤ M' × N'`, and `L` is (the image in `M × N` of) the preimage of the graph of an `R`-linear
isomorphism `M' ⧸ M'' ≃ N' ⧸ N''`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Submodule.goursat : ∃ (M' : Submodule R M) (N' : Submodule R N) (M'' : Submodule R M') (N'' : Submodule R N') (e : (M' ⧸ M'') ≃ₗ[R] N' ⧸ N''), L = (e.graph.comap <| M''.mkQ.prodMap N''.mkQ).map (M'.subtype.prodMap N'.subtype)

To show a property `motive` of modules holds for arbitrary finite products of modules, it suffices
to show
1. `motive` is stable under isomorphism.
2. `motive` holds for the zero module.
3. `motive` holds for `M × N` if it holds for both `M` and `N`.

Since we need to apply `motive` to modules in `Type u` and in `Type (max u v)`, there is a second
`motive'` argument which is required to be equivalent to `motive` up to universe lifting by `equiv`.

See `Module.pi_induction'` for a version where `motive` assumes `AddCommGroup` instead.

views.nl_informal:
**Vertical line test** for linear maps.

Let `f : G → H × I` be a linear (or semilinear) map to a product. Assume that `f` is surjective on
the first factor and that the image of `f` intersects every "vertical line" `{(h, i) | i : I}` at
most once. Then the image of `f` is the graph of some linear map `f' : H → I`.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.exists_range_eq_graph {f : G →ₛₗ[σ] H × I} (hf₁ : Surjective (Prod.fst ∘ f)) (hf : ∀ g₁ g₂, (f g₁).1 = (f g₂).1 → (f g₁).2 = (f g₂).2) : ∃ f' : H →ₗ[S] I, LinearMap.range f = LinearMap.graph f'

views.nl_informal:
**Vertical line test** for linear maps.

Let `G ≤ H × I` be a submodule of a product of modules. Assume that `G` maps bijectively to the
first factor. Then `G` is the graph of some linear map `f : H →ₗ[R] I`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Submodule.exists_eq_graph {G : Submodule S (H × I)} (hf₁ : Bijective (Prod.fst ∘ G.subtype)) : ∃ f : H →ₗ[S] I, G = LinearMap.graph f

views.nl_informal:
**Line test** for module isomorphisms.

Let `f : G → H × I` be a linear (or semilinear) map to a product of modules. Assume that `f` is
surjective onto both factors and that the image of `f` intersects every "vertical line"
`{(h, i) | i : I}` and every "horizontal line" `{(h, i) | h : H}` at most once. Then the image of
`f` is the graph of some module isomorphism `f' : H ≃ I`.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.exists_linearEquiv_eq_graph {f : G →ₛₗ[σ] H × I} (hf₁ : Surjective (Prod.fst ∘ f)) (hf₂ : Surjective (Prod.snd ∘ f)) (hf : ∀ g₁ g₂, (f g₁).1 = (f g₂).1 ↔ (f g₁).2 = (f g₂).2) : ∃ e : H ≃ₗ[S] I, range f = e.toLinearMap.graph

views.nl_informal:
**Goursat's lemma** for module isomorphisms.

Let `G ≤ H × I` be a submodule of a product of modules. Assume that the natural maps from `G` to
both factors are bijective. Then `G` is the graph of some module isomorphism `f : H ≃ I`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Submodule.exists_equiv_eq_graph {G : Submodule S (H × I)} (hG₁ : Bijective (Prod.fst ∘ G.subtype)) (hG₂ : Bijective (Prod.snd ∘ G.subtype)) : ∃ e : H ≃ₗ[S] I, G = e.toLinearMap.graph

views.nl_informal: `SameRay` is reflexive.
views.lean_signature: theorem SameRay.refl (x : M) : SameRay R x x

views.nl_informal: `SameRay` is symmetric.
views.lean_signature: theorem SameRay.symm (h : SameRay R x y) : SameRay R y x

views.nl_informal:
If `x` and `y` are nonzero vectors on the same ray, then there exist positive numbers `r₁ r₂`
such that `r₁ • x = r₂ • y`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SameRay.exists_pos (h : SameRay R x y) (hx : x ≠ 0) (hy : y ≠ 0) : ∃ r₁ r₂ : R, 0 < r₁ ∧ 0 < r₂ ∧ r₁ • x = r₂ • y

views.nl_informal:
`SameRay` is transitive unless the vector in the middle is zero and both other vectors are
nonzero.
views.lean_signature: theorem SameRay.trans (hxy : SameRay R x y) (hyz : SameRay R y z) (hy : y = 0 → x = 0 ∨ z = 0) : SameRay R x z

views.nl_informal: A vector is in the same ray as a nonnegative multiple of itself.
views.lean_signature: theorem SameRay.sameRay_nonneg_smul_right (v : M) (h : 0 ≤ a) : SameRay R v (a • v)

views.nl_informal: A nonnegative multiple of a vector is in the same ray as that vector.
views.lean_signature: theorem SameRay.sameRay_nonneg_smul_left (v : M) (ha : 0 ≤ a) : SameRay R (a • v) v

views.nl_informal: A vector is in the same ray as a positive multiple of itself.
views.lean_signature: theorem SameRay.sameRay_pos_smul_right (v : M) (ha : 0 < a) : SameRay R v (a • v)

views.nl_informal: A positive multiple of a vector is in the same ray as that vector.
views.lean_signature: theorem SameRay.sameRay_pos_smul_left (v : M) (ha : 0 < a) : SameRay R (a • v) v

views.nl_informal: A vector is in the same ray as a nonnegative multiple of one it is in the same ray as.
views.lean_signature: theorem SameRay.nonneg_smul_right (h : SameRay R x y) (ha : 0 ≤ a) : SameRay R x (a • y)

views.nl_informal: A nonnegative multiple of a vector is in the same ray as one it is in the same ray as.
views.lean_signature: theorem SameRay.nonneg_smul_left (h : SameRay R x y) (ha : 0 ≤ a) : SameRay R (a • x) y

views.nl_informal: A vector is in the same ray as a positive multiple of one it is in the same ray as.
views.lean_signature: theorem SameRay.pos_smul_right (h : SameRay R x y) (ha : 0 < a) : SameRay R x (a • y)

views.nl_informal: A positive multiple of a vector is in the same ray as one it is in the same ray as.
views.lean_signature: theorem SameRay.pos_smul_left (h : SameRay R x y) (hr : 0 < a) : SameRay R (a • x) y

views.nl_informal: If two vectors are on the same ray then they remain so after applying a linear map.
views.lean_signature: theorem SameRay.map (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (h : SameRay R x y) : SameRay R (f x) (f y)

views.nl_informal:
The images of two vectors under an injective linear map are on the same ray if and only if the
original vectors are on the same ray.
views.lean_signature: theorem Function.Injective.sameRay_map_iff {F : Type*} [FunLike F M N] [LinearMapClass F R M N] {f : F} (hf : Function.Injective f) : SameRay R (f x) (f y) ↔ SameRay R x y

views.nl_informal:
The images of two vectors under a linear equivalence are on the same ray if and only if the
original vectors are on the same ray.
views.lean_signature: theorem SameRay.sameRay_map_iff (e : M ≃ₗ[R] N) : SameRay R (e x) (e y) ↔ SameRay R x y

views.nl_informal:
If two vectors are on the same ray then both scaled by the same action are also on the same
ray.
views.lean_signature: theorem SameRay.smul {S : Type*} [Monoid S] [DistribMulAction S M] [SMulCommClass R S M] (h : SameRay R x y) (s : S) : SameRay R (s • x) (s • y)

views.nl_informal: If `x` and `y` are on the same ray as `z`, then so is `x + y`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SameRay.add_left (hx : SameRay R x z) (hy : SameRay R y z) : SameRay R (x + y) z

views.nl_informal: If `y` and `z` are on the same ray as `x`, then so is `y + z`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SameRay.add_right (hy : SameRay R x y) (hz : SameRay R x z) : SameRay R x (y + z)

views.nl_informal: Equivalence of nonzero vectors, in terms of `SameRay`.
views.lean_signature: theorem equiv_iff_sameRay {v₁ v₂ : RayVector R M} : v₁ ≈ v₂ ↔ SameRay R (v₁ : M) v₂

views.nl_informal: An induction principle for `Module.Ray`, used as `induction x using Module.Ray.ind`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.Ray.ind {C : Module.Ray R M → Prop} (h : ∀ (v) (hv : v ≠ 0), C (rayOfNeZero R v hv)) (x : Module.Ray R M) : C x

views.nl_informal:
The rays given by two nonzero vectors are equal if and only if those vectors
satisfy `SameRay`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ray_eq_iff {v₁ v₂ : M} (hv₁ : v₁ ≠ 0) (hv₂ : v₂ ≠ 0) : rayOfNeZero R _ hv₁ = rayOfNeZero R _ hv₂ ↔ SameRay R v₁ v₂

views.nl_informal: The ray given by a positive multiple of a nonzero vector.
views.lean_signature: theorem ray_pos_smul {v : M} (h : v ≠ 0) {r : R} (hr : 0 < r) (hrv : r • v ≠ 0) : rayOfNeZero R (r • v) hrv = rayOfNeZero R v h

views.nl_informal: The action via `LinearEquiv.apply_distribMulAction` corresponds to `Module.Ray.map`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.Ray.linearEquiv_smul_eq_map (e : M ≃ₗ[R] M) (v : Module.Ray R M) : e • v = Module.Ray.map e v

views.nl_informal: Scaling by a positive unit is a no-op.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.Ray.units_smul_of_pos (u : Rˣ) (hu : 0 < (u : R)) (v : Module.Ray R M) : u • v = v

views.nl_informal: The ray of `someRayVector`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.Ray.someRayVector_ray (x : Module.Ray R M) : (⟦x.someRayVector⟧ : Module.Ray R M) = x

views.nl_informal: `someVector` is nonzero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.Ray.someVector_ne_zero (x : Module.Ray R M) : x.someVector ≠ 0

views.nl_informal: The ray of `someVector`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.Ray.someVector_ray (x : Module.Ray R M) : rayOfNeZero R _ x.someVector_ne_zero = x

views.nl_informal: If a vector is in the same ray as its negation, that vector is zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem eq_zero_of_sameRay_self_neg [NoZeroSMulDivisors R M] (h : SameRay R x (-x)) : x = 0

views.nl_informal: Negating a nonzero vector commutes with coercion to the underlying module.
views.lean_signature: theorem RayVector.coe_neg {R : Type*} (v : RayVector R M) : ↑(-v) = -(v : M)

views.nl_informal: If two nonzero vectors are equivalent, so are their negations.
views.lean_signature: theorem RayVector.equiv_neg_iff {v₁ v₂ : RayVector R M} : -v₁ ≈ -v₂ ↔ v₁ ≈ v₂

views.nl_informal: The ray given by the negation of a nonzero vector.
views.lean_signature: theorem neg_rayOfNeZero (v : M) (h : v ≠ 0) : -rayOfNeZero R _ h = rayOfNeZero R (-v) (neg_ne_zero.2 h)

views.nl_informal: A ray does not equal its own negation.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.Ray.ne_neg_self [NoZeroSMulDivisors R M] (x : Module.Ray R M) : x ≠ -x

views.nl_informal: Scaling by a negative unit is negation.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.Ray.units_smul_of_neg (u : Rˣ) (hu : (u : R) < 0) (v : Module.Ray R M) : u • v = -v

views.nl_informal: `SameRay` follows from membership of `MulAction.orbit` for the `Units.posSubgroup`.
views.lean_signature: theorem sameRay_of_mem_orbit {v₁ v₂ : M} (h : v₁ ∈ MulAction.orbit (Units.posSubgroup R) v₂) : SameRay R v₁ v₂

views.nl_informal: Scaling by an inverse unit is the same as scaling by itself.
views.lean_signature: theorem units_inv_smul (u : Rˣ) (v : Module.Ray R M) : u⁻¹ • v = u • v

views.nl_informal:
A nonzero vector is in the same ray as a multiple of itself if and only if that multiple
is positive.
views.lean_signature: theorem sameRay_smul_right_iff_of_ne {v : M} (hv : v ≠ 0) {r : R} (hr : r ≠ 0) : SameRay R v (r • v) ↔ 0 < r

views.nl_informal:
A multiple of a nonzero vector is in the same ray as that vector if and only if that multiple
is positive.
views.lean_signature: theorem sameRay_smul_left_iff_of_ne {v : M} (hv : v ≠ 0) {r : R} (hr : r ≠ 0) : SameRay R (r • v) v ↔ 0 < r

views.nl_informal:
Two vectors are in the same ray, or the first is in the same ray as the negation of the
second, if and only if they are not linearly independent.
views.lean_signature: theorem sameRay_or_sameRay_neg_iff_not_linearIndependent {x y : M} : SameRay R x y ∨ SameRay R x (-y) ↔ ¬LinearIndependent R ![x, y]

views.nl_informal:
Two vectors are in the same ray, or they are nonzero and the first is in the same ray as the
negation of the second, if and only if they are not linearly independent.
views.lean_signature: theorem sameRay_or_ne_zero_and_sameRay_neg_iff_not_linearIndependent {x y : M} : SameRay R x y ∨ x ≠ 0 ∧ y ≠ 0 ∧ SameRay R x (-y) ↔ ¬LinearIndependent R ![x, y]

views.nl_informal:
If a vector `v₂` is on the same ray as a nonzero vector `v₁`, then it is equal to `c • v₁` for
some nonnegative `c`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SameRay.exists_nonneg_left (h : SameRay R x y) (hx : x ≠ 0) : ∃ r : R, 0 ≤ r ∧ r • x = y

views.nl_informal:
If a vector `v₁` is on the same ray as a nonzero vector `v₂`, then it is equal to `c • v₂` for
some nonnegative `c`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SameRay.exists_nonneg_right (h : SameRay R x y) (hy : y ≠ 0) : ∃ r : R, 0 ≤ r ∧ x = r • y

views.nl_informal:
If vectors `v₁` and `v₂` are on the same ray, then for some nonnegative `a b`, `a + b = 1`, we
have `v₁ = a • (v₁ + v₂)` and `v₂ = b • (v₁ + v₂)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SameRay.exists_eq_smul_add (h : SameRay R v₁ v₂) : ∃ a b : R, 0 ≤ a ∧ 0 ≤ b ∧ a + b = 1 ∧ v₁ = a • (v₁ + v₂) ∧ v₂ = b • (v₁ + v₂)

views.nl_informal:
If vectors `v₁` and `v₂` are on the same ray, then they are nonnegative multiples of the same
vector. Actually, this vector can be assumed to be `v₁ + v₂`, see `SameRay.exists_eq_smul_add`.
views.lean_signature: theorem SameRay.exists_eq_smul (h : SameRay R v₁ v₂) : ∃ (u : M) (a b : R), 0 ≤ a ∧ 0 ≤ b ∧ a + b = 1 ∧ v₁ = a • u ∧ v₂ = b • u

views.nl_informal: A formula for $(r_1 r_2)^m z$, where $m$ is a natural number and $z \in M$.

views.nl_informal: A formula for $(r_1 r_2)^m$, where $m$ is an integer.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.reflection_mul_reflection_zpow (m : ℤ) (t : R := f y * g x - 2) (ht : t = f y * g x - 2 := by rfl) : ((reflection hf * reflection hg) ^ m).toLinearMap = LinearMap.id (R := R) (M := M) + ((S R ((m - 2) / 2)).eval t * ((S R ((m - 1) / 2)).eval t + (S R ((m - 3) / 2)).eval t)) • ((g x • f - g).smulRight y - f.smulRight x) + ((S R ((m - 1) / 2)).eval t * ((S R (m / 2)).eval t + (S R ((m - 2) / 2)).eval t)) • ((f y • g - f).smulRight x - g.smulRight y)

views.nl_informal:
A formula for $(r_1 r_2)^m x$, where $m$ is an integer. This is the special case of

views.nl_informal: Composite of reflections in "parallel" hyperplanes is a shear (special case).

views.nl_informal:
A linear endomorphism is semisimple if every invariant submodule has in invariant complement.

See also `Module.End.isSemisimple_iff`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.End.isSemisimple_iff' : f.IsSemisimple ↔ ∀ p : invtSubmodule f, ∃ q : invtSubmodule f, IsCompl p q

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:

if the basis has no elements which are self-orthogonal.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.IsOrthoᵢ.nondegenerate_of_not_isOrtho_basis_self [NoZeroSMulDivisors R M₁] {B : M →ₗ[R] M →ₗ[R] M₁} (v : Basis n R M) (hO : B.IsOrthoᵢ v) (h : ∀ i, ¬B.IsOrtho (v i) (v i)) : B.Nondegenerate

views.nl_informal: The **Cauchy-Schwarz inequality** for positive semidefinite symmetric forms.

views.nl_informal:
Strict **Cauchy-Schwarz** is equivalent to linear independence for positive definite symmetric

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:
An affine map on the result of adding a vector to a point produces

affine map applied to that point.

views.nl_informal: Two affine maps are equal if they coerce to the same function.

views.nl_informal: Two affine maps are equal if they have equal linear maps and are equal at some point.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineMap.ext_linear_iff {f g : P1 →ᵃ[k] P2} : f = g ↔ (f.linear = g.linear) ∧ (∃ p, f p = g p)

views.nl_informal: The identity affine map acts as the identity.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineMap.id_apply (p : P1) : id k P1 p = p

views.nl_informal: Composition of affine maps acts as applying the two functions.

views.nl_informal:

the images.

views.nl_informal: The value of `weightedVSubOfPoint`, where the given points are equal.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.weightedVSubOfPoint_apply_const (w : ι → k) (p : P) (b : P) : s.weightedVSubOfPoint (fun _ => p) b w = (∑ i ∈ s, w i) • (p -ᵥ b)

views.nl_informal:
`weightedVSubOfPoint` gives equal results for two families of weights and two families of
points that are equal on `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.weightedVSubOfPoint_congr {w₁ w₂ : ι → k} (hw : ∀ i ∈ s, w₁ i = w₂ i) {p₁ p₂ : ι → P} (hp : ∀ i ∈ s, p₁ i = p₂ i) (b : P) : s.weightedVSubOfPoint p₁ b w₁ = s.weightedVSubOfPoint p₂ b w₂

views.nl_informal:
Given a family of points, if we use a member of the family as a base point, the
`weightedVSubOfPoint` does not depend on the value of the weights at this point.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.weightedVSubOfPoint_eq_of_weights_eq (p : ι → P) (j : ι) (w₁ w₂ : ι → k) (hw : ∀ i, i ≠ j → w₁ i = w₂ i) : s.weightedVSubOfPoint p (p j) w₁ = s.weightedVSubOfPoint p (p j) w₂

views.nl_informal:
The weighted sum is independent of the base point when the sum of
the weights is 0.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.weightedVSubOfPoint_eq_of_sum_eq_zero (w : ι → k) (p : ι → P) (h : ∑ i ∈ s, w i = 0) (b₁ b₂ : P) : s.weightedVSubOfPoint p b₁ w = s.weightedVSubOfPoint p b₂ w

views.nl_informal:
The weighted sum, added to the base point, is independent of the
base point when the sum of the weights is 1.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.weightedVSubOfPoint_vadd_eq_of_sum_eq_one (w : ι → k) (p : ι → P) (h : ∑ i ∈ s, w i = 1) (b₁ b₂ : P) : s.weightedVSubOfPoint p b₁ w +ᵥ b₁ = s.weightedVSubOfPoint p b₂ w +ᵥ b₂

views.nl_informal:
The weighted sum is unaffected by removing the base point, if
present, from the set of points.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.weightedVSubOfPoint_erase [DecidableEq ι] (w : ι → k) (p : ι → P) (i : ι) : (s.erase i).weightedVSubOfPoint p (p i) w = s.weightedVSubOfPoint p (p i) w

views.nl_informal:
The weighted sum is unaffected by adding the base point, whether
or not present, to the set of points.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.weightedVSubOfPoint_insert [DecidableEq ι] (w : ι → k) (p : ι → P) (i : ι) : (insert i s).weightedVSubOfPoint p (p i) w = s.weightedVSubOfPoint p (p i) w

views.nl_informal:

corresponding indicator function and adding points to the set.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.weightedVSubOfPoint_indicator_subset (w : ι → k) (p : ι → P) (b : P) {s₁ s₂ : Finset ι} (h : s₁ ⊆ s₂) : s₁.weightedVSubOfPoint p b w = s₂.weightedVSubOfPoint p b (Set.indicator (↑s₁) w)

views.nl_informal:
A weighted sum, over the image of an embedding, equals a weighted
sum with the same points and weights over the original

views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.weightedVSubOfPoint_map (e : ι₂ ↪ ι) (w : ι → k) (p : ι → P) (b : P) : (s₂.map e).weightedVSubOfPoint p b w = s₂.weightedVSubOfPoint (p ∘ e) b (w ∘ e)

views.nl_informal:

views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.sum_smul_vsub_eq_weightedVSubOfPoint_sub (w : ι → k) (p₁ p₂ : ι → P) (b : P) : (∑ i ∈ s, w i • (p₁ i -ᵥ p₂ i)) = s.weightedVSubOfPoint p₁ b w - s.weightedVSubOfPoint p₂ b w

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:

expressed as a subtraction involving a `weightedVSubOfPoint` expression.

views.nl_informal:

views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.weightedVSub_indicator_subset (w : ι → k) (p : ι → P) {s₁ s₂ : Finset ι} (h : s₁ ⊆ s₂) : s₁.weightedVSub p w = s₂.weightedVSub p (Set.indicator (↑s₁) w)

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:
A weighted sum of pairwise subtractions, where the point on the left is constant and the

views.nl_informal: A weighted sum may be split into such sums over two subsets.

views.nl_informal: A weighted sum over `s.subtype pred` equals one over `{x ∈ s | pred x}`.
