views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.affineCombination_vsub (w₁ w₂ : ι → k) (p : ι → P) : s.affineCombination k p w₁ -ᵥ s.affineCombination k p w₂ = s.weightedVSub p (w₁ - w₂)

views.nl_informal:
Viewing a module as an affine space modelled on itself, a `weightedVSub` is just a linear
combination.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.weightedVSub_eq_linear_combination {ι} (s : Finset ι) {w : ι → k} {p : ι → V} (hw : s.sum w = 0) : s.weightedVSub p w = ∑ i ∈ s, w i • p i

views.nl_informal:
Viewing a module as an affine space modelled on itself, affine combinations are just linear
combinations.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.affineCombination_eq_linear_combination (s : Finset ι) (p : ι → V) (w : ι → k) (hw : ∑ i ∈ s, w i = 1) : s.affineCombination k p w = ∑ i ∈ s, w i • p i

views.nl_informal:
An `affineCombination` equals a point if that point is in the set
and has weight 1 and the other points in the set have weight 0.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.affineCombination_of_eq_one_of_eq_zero (w : ι → k) (p : ι → P) {i : ι} (his : i ∈ s) (hwi : w i = 1) (hw0 : ∀ i2 ∈ s, i2 ≠ i → w i2 = 0) : s.affineCombination k p w = p i

views.nl_informal:
An affine combination is unaffected by changing the weights to the
corresponding indicator function and adding points to the set.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.affineCombination_indicator_subset (w : ι → k) (p : ι → P) {s₁ s₂ : Finset ι} (h : s₁ ⊆ s₂) : s₁.affineCombination k p w = s₂.affineCombination k p (Set.indicator (↑s₁) w)

views.nl_informal:
An affine combination, over the image of an embedding, equals an
affine combination with the same points and weights over the original
`Finset`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.affineCombination_map (e : ι₂ ↪ ι) (w : ι → k) (p : ι → P) : (s₂.map e).affineCombination k p w = s₂.affineCombination k (p ∘ e) (w ∘ e)

views.nl_informal:
A weighted sum of pairwise subtractions, expressed as a subtraction of two `affineCombination`
expressions.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.sum_smul_vsub_eq_affineCombination_vsub (w : ι → k) (p₁ p₂ : ι → P) : (∑ i ∈ s, w i • (p₁ i -ᵥ p₂ i)) = s.affineCombination k p₁ w -ᵥ s.affineCombination k p₂ w

views.nl_informal:
A weighted sum of pairwise subtractions, where the point on the right is constant and the
sum of the weights is 1.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.sum_smul_vsub_const_eq_affineCombination_vsub (w : ι → k) (p₁ : ι → P) (p₂ : P) (h : ∑ i ∈ s, w i = 1) : (∑ i ∈ s, w i • (p₁ i -ᵥ p₂)) = s.affineCombination k p₁ w -ᵥ p₂

views.nl_informal:
A weighted sum of pairwise subtractions, where the point on the left is constant and the
sum of the weights is 1.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.sum_smul_const_vsub_eq_vsub_affineCombination (w : ι → k) (p₂ : ι → P) (p₁ : P) (h : ∑ i ∈ s, w i = 1) : (∑ i ∈ s, w i • (p₁ -ᵥ p₂ i)) = p₁ -ᵥ s.affineCombination k p₂ w

views.nl_informal: A weighted sum may be split into a subtraction of affine combinations over two subsets.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.affineCombination_sdiff_sub [DecidableEq ι] {s₂ : Finset ι} (h : s₂ ⊆ s) (w : ι → k) (p : ι → P) : (s \ s₂).affineCombination k p w -ᵥ s₂.affineCombination k p (-w) = s.weightedVSub p w

views.nl_informal:
If a weighted sum is zero and one of the weights is `-1`, the corresponding point is
the affine combination of the other points with the given weights.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.affineCombination_eq_of_weightedVSub_eq_zero_of_eq_neg_one {w : ι → k} {p : ι → P} (hw : s.weightedVSub p w = (0 : V)) {i : ι} [DecidablePred (· ≠ i)] (his : i ∈ s) (hwi : w i = -1) : {x ∈ s | x ≠ i}.affineCombination k p w = p i

views.nl_informal: An affine combination over `s.subtype pred` equals one over `{x ∈ s | pred x}`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.affineCombination_subtype_eq_filter (w : ι → k) (p : ι → P) (pred : ι → Prop) [DecidablePred pred] : ((s.subtype pred).affineCombination k (fun i => p i) fun i => w i) = {x ∈ s | pred x}.affineCombination k p w

views.nl_informal:
An affine combination over `{x ∈ s | pred x}` equals one over `s` if all the weights at indices
in `s` not satisfying `pred` are zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.affineCombination_filter_of_ne (w : ι → k) (p : ι → P) {pred : ι → Prop} [DecidablePred pred] (h : ∀ i ∈ s, w i ≠ 0 → pred i) : {x ∈ s | pred x}.affineCombination k p w = s.affineCombination k p w

views.nl_informal:
Suppose an indexed family of points is given, along with a subset
of the index type.  A vector can be expressed as
`weightedVSubOfPoint` using a `Finset` lying within that subset and
with a given sum of weights if and only if it can be expressed as
`weightedVSubOfPoint` with that sum of weights for the
corresponding indexed family whose index type is the subtype
corresponding to that subset.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.eq_weightedVSubOfPoint_subset_iff_eq_weightedVSubOfPoint_subtype {v : V} {x : k} {s : Set ι} {p : ι → P} {b : P} : (∃ fs : Finset ι, ↑fs ⊆ s ∧ ∃ w : ι → k, ∑ i ∈ fs, w i = x ∧ v = fs.weightedVSubOfPoint p b w) ↔ ∃ (fs : Finset s) (w : s → k), ∑ i ∈ fs, w i = x ∧ v = fs.weightedVSubOfPoint (fun i : s => p i) b w

views.nl_informal:
Suppose an indexed family of points is given, along with a subset
of the index type.  A vector can be expressed as `weightedVSub` using
a `Finset` lying within that subset and with sum of weights 0 if and
only if it can be expressed as `weightedVSub` with sum of weights 0
for the corresponding indexed family whose index type is the subtype
corresponding to that subset.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.eq_weightedVSub_subset_iff_eq_weightedVSub_subtype {v : V} {s : Set ι} {p : ι → P} : (∃ fs : Finset ι, ↑fs ⊆ s ∧ ∃ w : ι → k, ∑ i ∈ fs, w i = 0 ∧ v = fs.weightedVSub p w) ↔ ∃ (fs : Finset s) (w : s → k), ∑ i ∈ fs, w i = 0 ∧ v = fs.weightedVSub (fun i : s => p i) w

views.nl_informal:
Suppose an indexed family of points is given, along with a subset
of the index type.  A point can be expressed as an
`affineCombination` using a `Finset` lying within that subset and
with sum of weights 1 if and only if it can be expressed an
`affineCombination` with sum of weights 1 for the corresponding
indexed family whose index type is the subtype corresponding to that
subset.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.eq_affineCombination_subset_iff_eq_affineCombination_subtype {p0 : P} {s : Set ι} {p : ι → P} : (∃ fs : Finset ι, ↑fs ⊆ s ∧ ∃ w : ι → k, ∑ i ∈ fs, w i = 1 ∧ p0 = fs.affineCombination k p w) ↔ ∃ (fs : Finset s) (w : s → k), ∑ i ∈ fs, w i = 1 ∧ p0 = fs.affineCombination k (fun i : s => p i) w

views.nl_informal: Affine maps commute with affine combinations.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.map_affineCombination {V₂ P₂ : Type*} [AddCommGroup V₂] [Module k V₂] [AffineSpace V₂ P₂] (p : ι → P) (w : ι → k) (hw : s.sum w = 1) (f : P →ᵃ[k] P₂) : f (s.affineCombination k p w) = s.affineCombination k (f ∘ p) w

views.nl_informal: The value of `affineCombination`, where the given points take only two values.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.affineCombination_apply_eq_lineMap_sum [DecidableEq ι] (w : ι → k) (p : ι → P) (p₁ p₂ : P) (s' : Finset ι) (h : ∑ i ∈ s, w i = 1) (hp₂ : ∀ i ∈ s ∩ s', p i = p₂) (hp₁ : ∀ i ∈ s \ s', p i = p₁) : s.affineCombination k p w = AffineMap.lineMap p₁ p₂ (∑ i ∈ s ∩ s', w i)

views.nl_informal: An affine combination with `affineCombinationSingleWeights` gives the specified point.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.affineCombination_affineCombinationSingleWeights [DecidableEq ι] (p : ι → P) {i : ι} (hi : i ∈ s) : s.affineCombination k p (affineCombinationSingleWeights k i) = p i

views.nl_informal:
A weighted subtraction with `weightedVSubVSubWeights` gives the result of subtracting the
specified points.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.weightedVSub_weightedVSubVSubWeights [DecidableEq ι] (p : ι → P) {i j : ι} (hi : i ∈ s) (hj : j ∈ s) : s.weightedVSub p (weightedVSubVSubWeights k i j) = p i -ᵥ p j

views.nl_informal:
An affine combination with `affineCombinationLineMapWeights` gives the result of
`line_map`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.affineCombination_affineCombinationLineMapWeights [DecidableEq ι] (p : ι → P) {i j : ι} (hi : i ∈ s) (hj : j ∈ s) (c : k) : s.affineCombination k p (affineCombinationLineMapWeights i j c) = AffineMap.lineMap (p i) (p j) c

views.nl_informal: `centroidWeights` at any point.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.centroidWeights_apply (i : ι) : s.centroidWeights k i = (#s : k)⁻¹

views.nl_informal: `centroidWeights` equals a constant function.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.centroidWeights_eq_const : s.centroidWeights k = Function.const ι (#s : k)⁻¹

views.nl_informal:
The weights in the centroid sum to 1, if the number of points,
converted to `k`, is not zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.sum_centroidWeights_eq_one_of_cast_card_ne_zero (h : (#s : k) ≠ 0) : ∑ i ∈ s, s.centroidWeights k i = 1

views.nl_informal:
In the characteristic zero case, the weights in the centroid sum
to 1 if the number of points is not zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.sum_centroidWeights_eq_one_of_card_ne_zero [CharZero k] (h : #s ≠ 0) : ∑ i ∈ s, s.centroidWeights k i = 1

views.nl_informal:
In the characteristic zero case, the weights in the centroid sum
to 1 if the set is nonempty.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.sum_centroidWeights_eq_one_of_nonempty [CharZero k] (h : s.Nonempty) : ∑ i ∈ s, s.centroidWeights k i = 1

views.nl_informal:
In the characteristic zero case, the weights in the centroid sum
to 1 if the number of points is `n + 1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.sum_centroidWeights_eq_one_of_card_eq_add_one [CharZero k] {n : ℕ} (h : #s = n + 1) : ∑ i ∈ s, s.centroidWeights k i = 1

views.nl_informal: The definition of the centroid.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.centroid_def (p : ι → P) : s.centroid k p = s.affineCombination k p (s.centroidWeights k)

views.nl_informal: The centroid of a single point.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.centroid_singleton (p : ι → P) (i : ι) : ({i} : Finset ι).centroid k p = p i

views.nl_informal:
The centroid of two points, expressed directly as adding a vector
to a point.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.centroid_pair [DecidableEq ι] [Invertible (2 : k)] (p : ι → P) (i₁ i₂ : ι) : ({i₁, i₂} : Finset ι).centroid k p = (2⁻¹ : k) • (p i₂ -ᵥ p i₁) +ᵥ p i₁

views.nl_informal:
The centroid of two points indexed by `Fin 2`, expressed directly
as adding a vector to the first point.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.centroid_pair_fin [Invertible (2 : k)] (p : Fin 2 → P) : univ.centroid k p = (2⁻¹ : k) • (p 1 -ᵥ p 0) +ᵥ p 0

views.nl_informal:
A centroid, over the image of an embedding, equals a centroid with
the same points and weights over the original `Finset`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.centroid_map (e : ι₂ ↪ ι) (p : ι → P) : (s₂.map e).centroid k p = s₂.centroid k (p ∘ e)

views.nl_informal: The definition of `centroidWeightsIndicator`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.centroidWeightsIndicator_def : s.centroidWeightsIndicator k = Set.indicator (↑s) (s.centroidWeights k)

views.nl_informal: The sum of the weights for the centroid indexed by a `Fintype`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.sum_centroidWeightsIndicator [Fintype ι] : ∑ i, s.centroidWeightsIndicator k i = ∑ i ∈ s, s.centroidWeights k i

views.nl_informal:
In the characteristic zero case, the weights in the centroid
indexed by a `Fintype` sum to 1 if the number of points is not
zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.sum_centroidWeightsIndicator_eq_one_of_card_ne_zero [CharZero k] [Fintype ι] (h : #s ≠ 0) : ∑ i, s.centroidWeightsIndicator k i = 1

views.nl_informal:
In the characteristic zero case, the weights in the centroid
indexed by a `Fintype` sum to 1 if the set is nonempty.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.sum_centroidWeightsIndicator_eq_one_of_nonempty [CharZero k] [Fintype ι] (h : s.Nonempty) : ∑ i, s.centroidWeightsIndicator k i = 1

views.nl_informal:
In the characteristic zero case, the weights in the centroid
indexed by a `Fintype` sum to 1 if the number of points is `n + 1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.sum_centroidWeightsIndicator_eq_one_of_card_eq_add_one [CharZero k] [Fintype ι] {n : ℕ} (h : #s = n + 1) : ∑ i, s.centroidWeightsIndicator k i = 1

views.nl_informal: The centroid as an affine combination over a `Fintype`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.centroid_eq_affineCombination_fintype [Fintype ι] (p : ι → P) : s.centroid k p = univ.affineCombination k p (s.centroidWeightsIndicator k)

views.nl_informal:
An indexed family of points that is injective on the given
`Finset` has the same centroid as the image of that `Finset`.  This is
stated in terms of a set equal to the image to provide control of
definitional equality for the index type used for the centroid of the
image.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.centroid_eq_centroid_image_of_inj_on {p : ι → P} (hi : ∀ i ∈ s, ∀ j ∈ s, p i = p j → i = j) {ps : Set P} [Fintype ps] (hps : ps = p '' ↑s) : s.centroid k p = (univ : Finset ps).centroid k fun x => (x : P)

views.nl_informal:
Two indexed families of points that are injective on the given
`Finset`s and with the same points in the image of those `Finset`s
have the same centroid.
views.lean_signature: theorem Finset.centroid_eq_of_inj_on_of_image_eq {p : ι → P} (hi : ∀ i ∈ s, ∀ j ∈ s, p i = p j → i = j) {p₂ : ι₂ → P} (hi₂ : ∀ i ∈ s₂, ∀ j ∈ s₂, p₂ i = p₂ j → i = j) (he : p '' ↑s = p₂ '' ↑s₂) : s.centroid k p = s₂.centroid k p₂

views.nl_informal:
A `weightedVSub` with sum of weights 0 is in the `vectorSpan` of
an indexed family.
views.lean_signature: theorem weightedVSub_mem_vectorSpan {s : Finset ι} {w : ι → k} (h : ∑ i ∈ s, w i = 0) (p : ι → P) : s.weightedVSub p w ∈ vectorSpan k (Set.range p)

views.nl_informal:
An `affineCombination` with sum of weights 1 is in the
`affineSpan` of an indexed family, if the underlying ring is
nontrivial.
views.lean_signature: theorem affineCombination_mem_affineSpan [Nontrivial k] {s : Finset ι} {w : ι → k} (h : ∑ i ∈ s, w i = 1) (p : ι → P) : s.affineCombination k p w ∈ affineSpan k (Set.range p)

views.nl_informal:
A vector is in the `vectorSpan` of an indexed family if and only
if it is a `weightedVSub` with sum of weights 0.
views.lean_signature: theorem mem_vectorSpan_iff_eq_weightedVSub {v : V} {p : ι → P} : v ∈ vectorSpan k (Set.range p) ↔ ∃ (s : Finset ι) (w : ι → k), ∑ i ∈ s, w i = 0 ∧ v = s.weightedVSub p w

views.nl_informal:
A point in the `affineSpan` of an indexed family is an
`affineCombination` with sum of weights 1. See also
`eq_affineCombination_of_mem_affineSpan_of_fintype`.
views.lean_signature: theorem eq_affineCombination_of_mem_affineSpan {p1 : P} {p : ι → P} (h : p1 ∈ affineSpan k (Set.range p)) : ∃ (s : Finset ι) (w : ι → k), ∑ i ∈ s, w i = 1 ∧ p1 = s.affineCombination k p w

views.nl_informal:
A point is in the `affineSpan` of an indexed family if and only
if it is an `affineCombination` with sum of weights 1, provided the
underlying ring is nontrivial.
views.lean_signature: theorem mem_affineSpan_iff_eq_affineCombination [Nontrivial k] {p1 : P} {p : ι → P} : p1 ∈ affineSpan k (Set.range p) ↔ ∃ (s : Finset ι) (w : ι → k), ∑ i ∈ s, w i = 1 ∧ p1 = s.affineCombination k p w

views.nl_informal:
Given a family of points together with a chosen base point in that family, membership of the
affine span of this family corresponds to an identity in terms of `weightedVSubOfPoint`, with
weights that are not required to sum to 1.
views.lean_signature: theorem mem_affineSpan_iff_eq_weightedVSubOfPoint_vadd [Nontrivial k] (p : ι → P) (j : ι) (q : P) : q ∈ affineSpan k (Set.range p) ↔ ∃ (s : Finset ι) (w : ι → k), q = s.weightedVSubOfPoint p (p j) w +ᵥ p j

views.nl_informal:
Given a set of points, together with a chosen base point in this set, if we affinely transport
all other members of the set along the line joining them to this base point, the affine span is
unchanged.
views.lean_signature: theorem affineSpan_eq_affineSpan_lineMap_units [Nontrivial k] {s : Set P} {p : P} (hp : p ∈ s) (w : s → Units k) : affineSpan k (Set.range fun q : s => AffineMap.lineMap p ↑q (w q : k)) = affineSpan k s

views.nl_informal:
The centroid lies in the affine span if the number of points,
converted to `k`, is not zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem centroid_mem_affineSpan_of_cast_card_ne_zero {s : Finset ι} (p : ι → P) (h : (#s : k) ≠ 0) : s.centroid k p ∈ affineSpan k (range p)

views.nl_informal:
In the characteristic zero case, the centroid lies in the affine
span if the number of points is not zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem centroid_mem_affineSpan_of_card_ne_zero [CharZero k] {s : Finset ι} (p : ι → P) (h : #s ≠ 0) : s.centroid k p ∈ affineSpan k (range p)

views.nl_informal:
In the characteristic zero case, the centroid lies in the affine
span if the set is nonempty.
views.lean_signature: theorem centroid_mem_affineSpan_of_nonempty [CharZero k] {s : Finset ι} (p : ι → P) (h : s.Nonempty) : s.centroid k p ∈ affineSpan k (range p)

views.nl_informal:
In the characteristic zero case, the centroid lies in the affine
span if the number of points is `n + 1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem centroid_mem_affineSpan_of_card_eq_add_one [CharZero k] {s : Finset ι} (p : ι → P) {n : ℕ} (h : #s = n + 1) : s.centroid k p ∈ affineSpan k (range p)

views.nl_informal: The `vectorSpan` of a finite set is finite-dimensional.
views.lean_signature: theorem finiteDimensional_vectorSpan_of_finite {s : Set P} (h : Set.Finite s) : FiniteDimensional k (vectorSpan k s)

views.nl_informal:
The direction of the affine span of a finite set is
finite-dimensional.
views.lean_signature: theorem finiteDimensional_direction_affineSpan_of_finite {s : Set P} (h : Set.Finite s) : FiniteDimensional k (affineSpan k s).direction

views.nl_informal: An affine-independent family of points in a finite-dimensional affine space is finite.
views.lean_signature: theorem finite_of_fin_dim_affineIndependent [FiniteDimensional k V] {p : ι → P} (hi : AffineIndependent k p) : Finite ι

views.nl_informal: An affine-independent subset of a finite-dimensional affine space is finite.
views.lean_signature: theorem finite_set_of_fin_dim_affineIndependent [FiniteDimensional k V] {s : Set ι} {f : s → P} (hi : AffineIndependent k f) : s.Finite

views.nl_informal:
The `vectorSpan` of a finite subset of an affinely independent
family has dimension one less than its cardinality.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineIndependent.finrank_vectorSpan_image_finset [DecidableEq P] {p : ι → P} (hi : AffineIndependent k p) {s : Finset ι} {n : ℕ} (hc : #s = n + 1) : finrank k (vectorSpan k (s.image p : Set P)) = n

views.nl_informal:
The `vectorSpan` of a finite affinely independent family has
dimension one less than its cardinality.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineIndependent.finrank_vectorSpan [Fintype ι] {p : ι → P} (hi : AffineIndependent k p) {n : ℕ} (hc : Fintype.card ι = n + 1) : finrank k (vectorSpan k (Set.range p)) = n

views.nl_informal:
The `vectorSpan` of a finite affinely independent family has dimension one less than its
cardinality.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineIndependent.finrank_vectorSpan_add_one [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] {p : ι → P} (hi : AffineIndependent k p) : finrank k (vectorSpan k (Set.range p)) + 1 = Fintype.card ι

views.nl_informal:
The `vectorSpan` of a finite affinely independent family whose
cardinality is one more than that of the finite-dimensional space is
`⊤`.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineIndependent.vectorSpan_eq_top_of_card_eq_finrank_add_one [FiniteDimensional k V] [Fintype ι] {p : ι → P} (hi : AffineIndependent k p) (hc : Fintype.card ι = finrank k V + 1) : vectorSpan k (Set.range p) = ⊤

views.nl_informal:
The `vectorSpan` of `n + 1` points in an indexed family has
dimension at most `n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem finrank_vectorSpan_image_finset_le [DecidableEq P] (p : ι → P) (s : Finset ι) {n : ℕ} (hc : #s = n + 1) : finrank k (vectorSpan k (s.image p : Set P)) ≤ n

views.nl_informal:
The `vectorSpan` of an indexed family of `n + 1` points has
dimension at most `n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem finrank_vectorSpan_range_le [Fintype ι] (p : ι → P) {n : ℕ} (hc : Fintype.card ι = n + 1) : finrank k (vectorSpan k (Set.range p)) ≤ n

views.nl_informal: The `vectorSpan` of an indexed family of `n + 1` points has dimension at most `n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem finrank_vectorSpan_range_add_one_le [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] (p : ι → P) : finrank k (vectorSpan k (Set.range p)) + 1 ≤ Fintype.card ι

views.nl_informal:
`n + 1` points are affinely independent if and only if their
`vectorSpan` has dimension `n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem affineIndependent_iff_finrank_vectorSpan_eq [Fintype ι] (p : ι → P) {n : ℕ} (hc : Fintype.card ι = n + 1) : AffineIndependent k p ↔ finrank k (vectorSpan k (Set.range p)) = n

views.nl_informal:
`n + 1` points are affinely independent if and only if their
`vectorSpan` has dimension at least `n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem affineIndependent_iff_le_finrank_vectorSpan [Fintype ι] (p : ι → P) {n : ℕ} (hc : Fintype.card ι = n + 1) : AffineIndependent k p ↔ n ≤ finrank k (vectorSpan k (Set.range p))

views.nl_informal:
`n + 2` points are affinely independent if and only if their
`vectorSpan` does not have dimension at most `n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem affineIndependent_iff_not_finrank_vectorSpan_le [Fintype ι] (p : ι → P) {n : ℕ} (hc : Fintype.card ι = n + 2) : AffineIndependent k p ↔ ¬finrank k (vectorSpan k (Set.range p)) ≤ n

views.nl_informal:
`n + 2` points have a `vectorSpan` with dimension at most `n` if
and only if they are not affinely independent.
views.lean_signature: theorem finrank_vectorSpan_le_iff_not_affineIndependent [Fintype ι] (p : ι → P) {n : ℕ} (hc : Fintype.card ι = n + 2) : finrank k (vectorSpan k (Set.range p)) ≤ n ↔ ¬AffineIndependent k p

views.nl_informal:
If an affine independent finset is contained in the affine span of another finset, then its
cardinality is at most the cardinality of that finset.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineIndependent.card_le_card_of_subset_affineSpan {s t : Finset V} (hs : AffineIndependent k ((↑) : s → V)) (hst : (s : Set V) ⊆ affineSpan k (t : Set V)) : #s ≤ #t

views.nl_informal:
If the affine span of an affine independent finset is strictly contained in the affine span of
another finset, then its cardinality is strictly less than the cardinality of that finset.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineIndependent.card_lt_card_of_affineSpan_lt_affineSpan {s t : Finset V} (hs : AffineIndependent k ((↑) : s → V)) (hst : affineSpan k (s : Set V) < affineSpan k (t : Set V)) : #s < #t

views.nl_informal:
If the `vectorSpan` of a finite subset of an affinely independent
family lies in a submodule with dimension one less than its
cardinality, it equals that submodule.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineIndependent.vectorSpan_image_finset_eq_of_le_of_card_eq_finrank_add_one [DecidableEq P] {p : ι → P} (hi : AffineIndependent k p) {s : Finset ι} {sm : Submodule k V} [FiniteDimensional k sm] (hle : vectorSpan k (s.image p : Set P) ≤ sm) (hc : #s = finrank k sm + 1) : vectorSpan k (s.image p : Set P) = sm

views.nl_informal:
If the `vectorSpan` of a finite affinely independent
family lies in a submodule with dimension one less than its
cardinality, it equals that submodule.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineIndependent.vectorSpan_eq_of_le_of_card_eq_finrank_add_one [Fintype ι] {p : ι → P} (hi : AffineIndependent k p) {sm : Submodule k V} [FiniteDimensional k sm] (hle : vectorSpan k (Set.range p) ≤ sm) (hc : Fintype.card ι = finrank k sm + 1) : vectorSpan k (Set.range p) = sm

views.nl_informal:
If the `affineSpan` of a finite subset of an affinely independent
family lies in an affine subspace whose direction has dimension one
less than its cardinality, it equals that subspace.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineIndependent.affineSpan_image_finset_eq_of_le_of_card_eq_finrank_add_one [DecidableEq P] {p : ι → P} (hi : AffineIndependent k p) {s : Finset ι} {sp : AffineSubspace k P} [FiniteDimensional k sp.direction] (hle : affineSpan k (s.image p : Set P) ≤ sp) (hc : #s = finrank k sp.direction + 1) : affineSpan k (s.image p : Set P) = sp

views.nl_informal:
If the `affineSpan` of a finite affinely independent family lies
in an affine subspace whose direction has dimension one less than its
cardinality, it equals that subspace.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineIndependent.affineSpan_eq_of_le_of_card_eq_finrank_add_one [Fintype ι] {p : ι → P} (hi : AffineIndependent k p) {sp : AffineSubspace k P} [FiniteDimensional k sp.direction] (hle : affineSpan k (Set.range p) ≤ sp) (hc : Fintype.card ι = finrank k sp.direction + 1) : affineSpan k (Set.range p) = sp

views.nl_informal:
The `affineSpan` of a finite affinely independent family is `⊤` iff the
family's cardinality is one more than that of the finite-dimensional space.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineIndependent.affineSpan_eq_top_iff_card_eq_finrank_add_one [FiniteDimensional k V] [Fintype ι] {p : ι → P} (hi : AffineIndependent k p) : affineSpan k (Set.range p) = ⊤ ↔ Fintype.card ι = finrank k V + 1

views.nl_informal: The definition of `Collinear`.
views.lean_signature: theorem collinear_iff_rank_le_one (s : Set P) : Collinear k s ↔ Module.rank k (vectorSpan k s) ≤ 1

views.nl_informal:
A set of points, whose `vectorSpan` is finite-dimensional, is
collinear if and only if their `vectorSpan` has dimension at most
`1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem collinear_iff_finrank_le_one {s : Set P} [FiniteDimensional k (vectorSpan k s)] : Collinear k s ↔ finrank k (vectorSpan k s) ≤ 1

views.nl_informal: A subset of a collinear set is collinear.
views.lean_signature: theorem Collinear.subset {s₁ s₂ : Set P} (hs : s₁ ⊆ s₂) (h : Collinear k s₂) : Collinear k s₁

views.nl_informal: The `vectorSpan` of collinear points is finite-dimensional.
views.lean_signature: theorem Collinear.finiteDimensional_vectorSpan {s : Set P} (h : Collinear k s) : FiniteDimensional k (vectorSpan k s)

views.nl_informal: The direction of the affine span of collinear points is finite-dimensional.
views.lean_signature: theorem Collinear.finiteDimensional_direction_affineSpan {s : Set P} (h : Collinear k s) : FiniteDimensional k (affineSpan k s).direction

views.nl_informal: The empty set is collinear.
views.lean_signature: theorem collinear_empty : Collinear k (∅ : Set P)

views.nl_informal: A single point is collinear.
views.lean_signature: theorem collinear_singleton (p : P) : Collinear k ({p} : Set P)

views.nl_informal:
Given a point `p₀` in a set of points, that set is collinear if and
only if the points can all be expressed as multiples of the same
vector, added to `p₀`.
views.lean_signature: theorem collinear_iff_of_mem {s : Set P} {p₀ : P} (h : p₀ ∈ s) : Collinear k s ↔ ∃ v : V, ∀ p ∈ s, ∃ r : k, p = r • v +ᵥ p₀

views.nl_informal:
A set of points is collinear if and only if they can all be
expressed as multiples of the same vector, added to the same base
point.
views.lean_signature: theorem collinear_iff_exists_forall_eq_smul_vadd (s : Set P) : Collinear k s ↔ ∃ (p₀ : P) (v : V), ∀ p ∈ s, ∃ r : k, p = r • v +ᵥ p₀

views.nl_informal: Two points are collinear.
views.lean_signature: theorem collinear_pair (p₁ p₂ : P) : Collinear k ({p₁, p₂} : Set P)

views.nl_informal:
Three points are affinely independent if and only if they are not
collinear.
views.lean_signature: theorem affineIndependent_iff_not_collinear {p : Fin 3 → P} : AffineIndependent k p ↔ ¬Collinear k (Set.range p)

views.nl_informal:
Three points are collinear if and only if they are not affinely
independent.
views.lean_signature: theorem collinear_iff_not_affineIndependent {p : Fin 3 → P} : Collinear k (Set.range p) ↔ ¬AffineIndependent k p

views.nl_informal: Three points are affinely independent if and only if they are not collinear.
views.lean_signature: theorem affineIndependent_iff_not_collinear_set {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} : AffineIndependent k ![p₁, p₂, p₃] ↔ ¬Collinear k ({p₁, p₂, p₃} : Set P)

views.nl_informal: Three points are collinear if and only if they are not affinely independent.
views.lean_signature: theorem collinear_iff_not_affineIndependent_set {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} : Collinear k ({p₁, p₂, p₃} : Set P) ↔ ¬AffineIndependent k ![p₁, p₂, p₃]

views.nl_informal: Three points are affinely independent if and only if they are not collinear.
views.lean_signature: theorem affineIndependent_iff_not_collinear_of_ne {p : Fin 3 → P} {i₁ i₂ i₃ : Fin 3} (h₁₂ : i₁ ≠ i₂) (h₁₃ : i₁ ≠ i₃) (h₂₃ : i₂ ≠ i₃) : AffineIndependent k p ↔ ¬Collinear k ({p i₁, p i₂, p i₃} : Set P)

views.nl_informal: Three points are collinear if and only if they are not affinely independent.
views.lean_signature: theorem collinear_iff_not_affineIndependent_of_ne {p : Fin 3 → P} {i₁ i₂ i₃ : Fin 3} (h₁₂ : i₁ ≠ i₂) (h₁₃ : i₁ ≠ i₃) (h₂₃ : i₂ ≠ i₃) : Collinear k ({p i₁, p i₂, p i₃} : Set P) ↔ ¬AffineIndependent k p

views.nl_informal: If three points are not collinear, the first and second are different.
views.lean_signature: theorem ne₁₂_of_not_collinear {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : ¬Collinear k ({p₁, p₂, p₃} : Set P)) : p₁ ≠ p₂

views.nl_informal: If three points are not collinear, the first and third are different.
views.lean_signature: theorem ne₁₃_of_not_collinear {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : ¬Collinear k ({p₁, p₂, p₃} : Set P)) : p₁ ≠ p₃

views.nl_informal: If three points are not collinear, the second and third are different.
views.lean_signature: theorem ne₂₃_of_not_collinear {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : ¬Collinear k ({p₁, p₂, p₃} : Set P)) : p₂ ≠ p₃

views.nl_informal:
A point in a collinear set of points lies in the affine span of any two distinct points of
that set.
views.lean_signature: theorem Collinear.mem_affineSpan_of_mem_of_ne {s : Set P} (h : Collinear k s) {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (hp₁ : p₁ ∈ s) (hp₂ : p₂ ∈ s) (hp₃ : p₃ ∈ s) (hp₁p₂ : p₁ ≠ p₂) : p₃ ∈ line[k, p₁, p₂]

views.nl_informal:
The affine span of any two distinct points of a collinear set of points equals the affine
span of the whole set.
views.lean_signature: theorem Collinear.affineSpan_eq_of_ne {s : Set P} (h : Collinear k s) {p₁ p₂ : P} (hp₁ : p₁ ∈ s) (hp₂ : p₂ ∈ s) (hp₁p₂ : p₁ ≠ p₂) : line[k, p₁, p₂] = affineSpan k s

views.nl_informal:
Given a collinear set of points, and two distinct points `p₂` and `p₃` in it, a point `p₁` is
collinear with the set if and only if it is collinear with `p₂` and `p₃`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Collinear.collinear_insert_iff_of_ne {s : Set P} (h : Collinear k s) {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (hp₂ : p₂ ∈ s) (hp₃ : p₃ ∈ s) (hp₂p₃ : p₂ ≠ p₃) : Collinear k (insert p₁ s) ↔ Collinear k ({p₁, p₂, p₃} : Set P)

views.nl_informal: Adding a point in the affine span of a set does not change whether that set is collinear.
views.lean_signature: theorem collinear_insert_iff_of_mem_affineSpan {s : Set P} {p : P} (h : p ∈ affineSpan k s) : Collinear k (insert p s) ↔ Collinear k s

views.nl_informal: If a point lies in the affine span of two points, those three points are collinear.
views.lean_signature: theorem collinear_insert_of_mem_affineSpan_pair {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : p₁ ∈ line[k, p₂, p₃]) : Collinear k ({p₁, p₂, p₃} : Set P)

views.nl_informal: If two points lie in the affine span of two points, those four points are collinear.
views.lean_signature: theorem collinear_insert_insert_of_mem_affineSpan_pair {p₁ p₂ p₃ p₄ : P} (h₁ : p₁ ∈ line[k, p₃, p₄]) (h₂ : p₂ ∈ line[k, p₃, p₄]) : Collinear k ({p₁, p₂, p₃, p₄} : Set P)

views.nl_informal: If three points lie in the affine span of two points, those five points are collinear.
views.lean_signature: theorem collinear_insert_insert_insert_of_mem_affineSpan_pair {p₁ p₂ p₃ p₄ p₅ : P} (h₁ : p₁ ∈ line[k, p₄, p₅]) (h₂ : p₂ ∈ line[k, p₄, p₅]) (h₃ : p₃ ∈ line[k, p₄, p₅]) : Collinear k ({p₁, p₂, p₃, p₄, p₅} : Set P)

views.nl_informal: If three points lie in the affine span of two points, the first four points are collinear.
views.lean_signature: theorem collinear_insert_insert_insert_left_of_mem_affineSpan_pair {p₁ p₂ p₃ p₄ p₅ : P} (h₁ : p₁ ∈ line[k, p₄, p₅]) (h₂ : p₂ ∈ line[k, p₄, p₅]) (h₃ : p₃ ∈ line[k, p₄, p₅]) : Collinear k ({p₁, p₂, p₃, p₄} : Set P)

views.nl_informal: If three points lie in the affine span of two points, the first three points are collinear.
views.lean_signature: theorem collinear_triple_of_mem_affineSpan_pair {p₁ p₂ p₃ p₄ p₅ : P} (h₁ : p₁ ∈ line[k, p₄, p₅]) (h₂ : p₂ ∈ line[k, p₄, p₅]) (h₃ : p₃ ∈ line[k, p₄, p₅]) : Collinear k ({p₁, p₂, p₃} : Set P)

views.nl_informal: The `vectorSpan` of coplanar points is finite-dimensional.
views.lean_signature: theorem Coplanar.finiteDimensional_vectorSpan {s : Set P} (h : Coplanar k s) : FiniteDimensional k (vectorSpan k s)

views.nl_informal: The direction of the affine span of coplanar points is finite-dimensional.
views.lean_signature: theorem Coplanar.finiteDimensional_direction_affineSpan {s : Set P} (h : Coplanar k s) : FiniteDimensional k (affineSpan k s).direction

views.nl_informal:
A set of points, whose `vectorSpan` is finite-dimensional, is coplanar if and only if their
`vectorSpan` has dimension at most `2`.
views.lean_signature: theorem coplanar_iff_finrank_le_two {s : Set P} [FiniteDimensional k (vectorSpan k s)] : Coplanar k s ↔ finrank k (vectorSpan k s) ≤ 2

views.nl_informal: A subset of a coplanar set is coplanar.
views.lean_signature: theorem Coplanar.subset {s₁ s₂ : Set P} (hs : s₁ ⊆ s₂) (h : Coplanar k s₂) : Coplanar k s₁

views.nl_informal: Collinear points are coplanar.
views.lean_signature: theorem Collinear.coplanar {s : Set P} (h : Collinear k s) : Coplanar k s

views.nl_informal: The empty set is coplanar.
views.lean_signature: theorem coplanar_empty : Coplanar k (∅ : Set P)

views.nl_informal: A single point is coplanar.
views.lean_signature: theorem coplanar_singleton (p : P) : Coplanar k ({p} : Set P)

views.nl_informal: Two points are coplanar.
views.lean_signature: theorem coplanar_pair (p₁ p₂ : P) : Coplanar k ({p₁, p₂} : Set P)

views.nl_informal: Adding a point in the affine span of a set does not change whether that set is coplanar.
views.lean_signature: theorem coplanar_insert_iff_of_mem_affineSpan {s : Set P} {p : P} (h : p ∈ affineSpan k s) : Coplanar k (insert p s) ↔ Coplanar k s

views.nl_informal: Adding a point to a finite-dimensional subspace increases the dimension by at most one.
views.lean_signature: theorem finrank_vectorSpan_insert_le (s : AffineSubspace k P) (p : P) : finrank k (vectorSpan k (insert p (s : Set P))) ≤ finrank k s.direction + 1

views.nl_informal:
Adding a point to a set with a finite-dimensional span increases the dimension by at most
one.
views.lean_signature: theorem finrank_vectorSpan_insert_le_set (s : Set P) (p : P) : finrank k (vectorSpan k (insert p s)) ≤ finrank k (vectorSpan k s) + 1

views.nl_informal: Adding a point to a collinear set produces a coplanar set.
views.lean_signature: theorem Collinear.coplanar_insert {s : Set P} (h : Collinear k s) (p : P) : Coplanar k (insert p s)

views.nl_informal: A set of points in a two-dimensional space is coplanar.
views.lean_signature: theorem coplanar_of_finrank_eq_two (s : Set P) (h : finrank k V = 2) : Coplanar k s

views.nl_informal: A set of points in a two-dimensional space is coplanar.
views.lean_signature: theorem coplanar_of_fact_finrank_eq_two (s : Set P) [h : Fact (finrank k V = 2)] : Coplanar k s

views.nl_informal: Three points are coplanar.
views.lean_signature: theorem coplanar_triple (p₁ p₂ p₃ : P) : Coplanar k ({p₁, p₂, p₃} : Set P)

views.nl_informal: The definition of `AffineIndependent`.
views.lean_signature: theorem affineIndependent_def (p : ι → P) : AffineIndependent k p ↔ ∀ (s : Finset ι) (w : ι → k), ∑ i ∈ s, w i = 0 → s.weightedVSub p w = (0 : V) → ∀ i ∈ s, w i = 0

views.nl_informal: A family with at most one point is affinely independent.
views.lean_signature: theorem affineIndependent_of_subsingleton [Subsingleton ι] (p : ι → P) : AffineIndependent k p

views.nl_informal:
A family indexed by a `Fintype` is affinely independent if and
only if no nontrivial weighted subtractions over `Finset.univ` (where
the sum of the weights is 0) are 0.
views.lean_signature: theorem affineIndependent_iff_of_fintype [Fintype ι] (p : ι → P) : AffineIndependent k p ↔ ∀ w : ι → k, ∑ i, w i = 0 → Finset.univ.weightedVSub p w = (0 : V) → ∀ i, w i = 0

views.nl_informal:
A family is affinely independent if and only if the differences
from a base point in that family are linearly independent.
views.lean_signature: theorem affineIndependent_iff_linearIndependent_vsub (p : ι → P) (i1 : ι) : AffineIndependent k p ↔ LinearIndependent k fun i : { x // x ≠ i1 } => (p i -ᵥ p i1 : V)

views.nl_informal:
A set is affinely independent if and only if the differences from
a base point in that set are linearly independent.
views.lean_signature: theorem affineIndependent_set_iff_linearIndependent_vsub {s : Set P} {p₁ : P} (hp₁ : p₁ ∈ s) : AffineIndependent k (fun p => p : s → P) ↔ LinearIndependent k (fun v => v : (fun p => (p -ᵥ p₁ : V)) '' (s \ {p₁}) → V)

views.nl_informal:
A set of nonzero vectors is linearly independent if and only if,
given a point `p₁`, the vectors added to `p₁` and `p₁` itself are
affinely independent.
views.lean_signature: theorem linearIndependent_set_iff_affineIndependent_vadd_union_singleton {s : Set V} (hs : ∀ v ∈ s, v ≠ (0 : V)) (p₁ : P) : LinearIndependent k (fun v => v : s → V) ↔ AffineIndependent k (fun p => p : ({p₁} ∪ (fun v => v +ᵥ p₁) '' s : Set P) → P)

views.nl_informal:
A family is affinely independent if and only if any affine
combinations (with sum of weights 1) that evaluate to the same point
have equal `Set.indicator`.
views.lean_signature: theorem affineIndependent_iff_indicator_eq_of_affineCombination_eq (p : ι → P) : AffineIndependent k p ↔ ∀ (s1 s2 : Finset ι) (w1 w2 : ι → k), ∑ i ∈ s1, w1 i = 1 → ∑ i ∈ s2, w2 i = 1 → s1.affineCombination k p w1 = s2.affineCombination k p w2 → Set.indicator (↑s1) w1 = Set.indicator (↑s2) w2

views.nl_informal:
A finite family is affinely independent if and only if any affine
combinations (with sum of weights 1) that evaluate to the same point are equal.
views.lean_signature: theorem affineIndependent_iff_eq_of_fintype_affineCombination_eq [Fintype ι] (p : ι → P) : AffineIndependent k p ↔ ∀ w1 w2 : ι → k, ∑ i, w1 i = 1 → ∑ i, w2 i = 1 → Finset.univ.affineCombination k p w1 = Finset.univ.affineCombination k p w2 → w1 = w2

views.nl_informal:
If we single out one member of an affine-independent family of points and affinely transport
all others along the line joining them to this member, the resulting new family of points is affine-
independent.

This is the affine version of `LinearIndependent.units_smul`.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineIndependent.units_lineMap {p : ι → P} (hp : AffineIndependent k p) (j : ι) (w : ι → Units k) : AffineIndependent k fun i => AffineMap.lineMap (p j) (p i) (w i : k)

views.nl_informal:
An affinely independent family is injective, if the underlying
ring is nontrivial.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineIndependent.injective [Nontrivial k] {p : ι → P} (ha : AffineIndependent k p) : Function.Injective p

views.nl_informal:
If a family is affinely independent, so is any subfamily given by
composition of an embedding into index type with the original
family.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineIndependent.comp_embedding {ι2 : Type*} (f : ι2 ↪ ι) {p : ι → P} (ha : AffineIndependent k p) : AffineIndependent k (p ∘ f)

views.nl_informal:
If a family is affinely independent, so is any subfamily indexed
by a subtype of the index type.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineIndependent.subtype {p : ι → P} (ha : AffineIndependent k p) (s : Set ι) : AffineIndependent k fun i : s => p i

views.nl_informal:
If an indexed family of points is affinely independent, so is the
corresponding set of points.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineIndependent.range {p : ι → P} (ha : AffineIndependent k p) : AffineIndependent k (fun x => x : Set.range p → P)

views.nl_informal: If a set of points is affinely independent, so is any subset.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineIndependent.mono {s t : Set P} (ha : AffineIndependent k (fun x => x : t → P)) (hs : s ⊆ t) : AffineIndependent k (fun x => x : s → P)

views.nl_informal:
If the range of an injective indexed family of points is affinely
independent, so is that family.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineIndependent.of_set_of_injective {p : ι → P} (ha : AffineIndependent k (fun x => x : Set.range p → P)) (hi : Function.Injective p) : AffineIndependent k p

views.nl_informal:
If the image of a family of points in affine space under an affine transformation is affine-
independent, then the original family of points is also affine-independent.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineIndependent.of_comp {p : ι → P} (f : P →ᵃ[k] P₂) (hai : AffineIndependent k (f ∘ p)) : AffineIndependent k p

views.nl_informal:
The image of a family of points in affine space, under an injective affine transformation, is
affine-independent.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineIndependent.map' {p : ι → P} (hai : AffineIndependent k p) (f : P →ᵃ[k] P₂) (hf : Function.Injective f) : AffineIndependent k (f ∘ p)

views.nl_informal: Injective affine maps preserve affine independence.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineMap.affineIndependent_iff {p : ι → P} (f : P →ᵃ[k] P₂) (hf : Function.Injective f) : AffineIndependent k (f ∘ p) ↔ AffineIndependent k p

views.nl_informal: Affine equivalences preserve affine independence of families of points.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineEquiv.affineIndependent_iff {p : ι → P} (e : P ≃ᵃ[k] P₂) : AffineIndependent k (e ∘ p) ↔ AffineIndependent k p

views.nl_informal: Affine equivalences preserve affine independence of subsets.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineEquiv.affineIndependent_set_of_eq_iff {s : Set P} (e : P ≃ᵃ[k] P₂) : AffineIndependent k ((↑) : e '' s → P₂) ↔ AffineIndependent k ((↑) : s → P)

views.nl_informal:
If a family is affinely independent, and the spans of points
indexed by two subsets of the index type have a point in common, those
subsets of the index type have an element in common, if the underlying
ring is nontrivial.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineIndependent.exists_mem_inter_of_exists_mem_inter_affineSpan [Nontrivial k] {p : ι → P} (ha : AffineIndependent k p) {s1 s2 : Set ι} {p0 : P} (hp0s1 : p0 ∈ affineSpan k (p '' s1)) (hp0s2 : p0 ∈ affineSpan k (p '' s2)) : ∃ i : ι, i ∈ s1 ∩ s2

views.nl_informal:
If a family is affinely independent, the spans of points indexed
by disjoint subsets of the index type are disjoint, if the underlying
ring is nontrivial.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineIndependent.affineSpan_disjoint_of_disjoint [Nontrivial k] {p : ι → P} (ha : AffineIndependent k p) {s1 s2 : Set ι} (hd : Disjoint s1 s2) : Disjoint (affineSpan k (p '' s1) : Set P) (affineSpan k (p '' s2))

views.nl_informal:
If a family is affinely independent, a point in the family is in
the span of some of the points given by a subset of the index type if
and only if that point's index is in the subset, if the underlying
ring is nontrivial.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineIndependent.mem_affineSpan_iff [Nontrivial k] {p : ι → P} (ha : AffineIndependent k p) (i : ι) (s : Set ι) : p i ∈ affineSpan k (p '' s) ↔ i ∈ s

views.nl_informal:
If a family is affinely independent, a point in the family is not
in the affine span of the other points, if the underlying ring is
nontrivial.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineIndependent.not_mem_affineSpan_diff [Nontrivial k] {p : ι → P} (ha : AffineIndependent k p) (i : ι) (s : Set ι) : p i ∉ affineSpan k (p '' (s \ {i}))

views.nl_informal:
Viewing a module as an affine space modelled on itself, we can characterise affine independence
in terms of linear combinations.
views.lean_signature: theorem affineIndependent_iff {ι} {p : ι → V} : AffineIndependent k p ↔ ∀ (s : Finset ι) (w : ι → k), s.sum w = 0 → ∑ e ∈ s, w e • p e = 0 → ∀ e ∈ s, w e = 0

views.nl_informal:
Given an affinely independent family of points, a weighted subtraction lies in the
`vectorSpan` of two points given as affine combinations if and only if it is a weighted
subtraction with weights a multiple of the difference between the weights of the two points.
views.lean_signature: theorem weightedVSub_mem_vectorSpan_pair {p : ι → P} (h : AffineIndependent k p) {w w₁ w₂ : ι → k} {s : Finset ι} (hw : ∑ i ∈ s, w i = 0) (hw₁ : ∑ i ∈ s, w₁ i = 1) (hw₂ : ∑ i ∈ s, w₂ i = 1) : s.weightedVSub p w ∈ vectorSpan k ({s.affineCombination k p w₁, s.affineCombination k p w₂} : Set P) ↔ ∃ r : k, ∀ i ∈ s, w i = r * (w₁ i - w₂ i)

views.nl_informal:
Given an affinely independent family of points, an affine combination lies in the
span of two points given as affine combinations if and only if it is an affine combination
with weights those of one point plus a multiple of the difference between the weights of the
two points.
views.lean_signature: theorem affineCombination_mem_affineSpan_pair {p : ι → P} (h : AffineIndependent k p) {w w₁ w₂ : ι → k} {s : Finset ι} (_ : ∑ i ∈ s, w i = 1) (hw₁ : ∑ i ∈ s, w₁ i = 1) (hw₂ : ∑ i ∈ s, w₂ i = 1) : s.affineCombination k p w ∈ line[k, s.affineCombination k p w₁, s.affineCombination k p w₂] ↔ ∃ r : k, ∀ i ∈ s, w i = r * (w₂ i - w₁ i) + w₁ i

views.nl_informal:
An affinely independent set of points can be extended to such a
set that spans the whole space.
views.lean_signature: theorem exists_subset_affineIndependent_affineSpan_eq_top {s : Set P} (h : AffineIndependent k (fun p => p : s → P)) : ∃ t : Set P, s ⊆ t ∧ AffineIndependent k (fun p => p : t → P) ∧ affineSpan k t = ⊤

views.nl_informal: Two different points are affinely independent.
views.lean_signature: theorem affineIndependent_of_ne {p₁ p₂ : P} (h : p₁ ≠ p₂) : AffineIndependent k ![p₁, p₂]

views.nl_informal:
If all but one point of a family are affinely independent, and that point does not lie in
the affine span of that family, the family is affinely independent.

views.nl_informal:
If distinct points `p₁` and `p₂` lie in `s` but `p₃` does not, the three points are affinely
independent.

views.nl_informal:
If distinct points `p₁` and `p₃` lie in `s` but `p₂` does not, the three points are affinely
independent.

views.nl_informal:
If distinct points `p₂` and `p₃` lie in `s` but `p₁` does not, the three points are affinely
independent.
views.lean_signature: theorem affineIndependent_of_ne_of_not_mem_of_mem_of_mem {s : AffineSubspace k P} {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (hp₂p₃ : p₂ ≠ p₃) (hp₁ : p₁ ∉ s) (hp₂ : p₂ ∈ s) (hp₃ : p₃ ∈ s) : AffineIndependent k ![p₁, p₂, p₃]

views.nl_informal:
Given an affinely independent family of points, suppose that an affine combination lies in
the span of two points given as affine combinations, and suppose that, for two indices, the
coefficients in the first point in the span are zero and those in the second point in the span
have the same sign. Then the coefficients in the combination lying in the span have the same
sign.

views.nl_informal:
Given an affinely independent family of points, suppose that an affine combination lies in
the span of one point of that family and a combination of another two points of that family given
by `lineMap` with coefficient between 0 and 1. Then the coefficients of those two points in the
combination lying in the span have the same sign.
views.lean_signature: theorem sign_eq_of_affineCombination_mem_affineSpan_single_lineMap {p : ι → P} (h : AffineIndependent k p) {w : ι → k} {s : Finset ι} (hw : ∑ i ∈ s, w i = 1) {i₁ i₂ i₃ : ι} (h₁ : i₁ ∈ s) (h₂ : i₂ ∈ s) (h₃ : i₃ ∈ s) (h₁₂ : i₁ ≠ i₂) (h₁₃ : i₁ ≠ i₃) (h₂₃ : i₂ ≠ i₃) {c : k} (hc0 : 0 < c) (hc1 : c < 1) (hs : s.affineCombination k p w ∈ line[k, p i₁, AffineMap.lineMap (p i₂) (p i₃) c]) : SignType.sign (w i₂) = SignType.sign (w i₃)

views.nl_informal: The point in a simplex constructed with `mkOfPoint`.

views.nl_informal: The points of a face of a simplex are given by `mono_of_fin`.

faces are given by the same subset of points.

views.lean_signature: theorem AffineSubspace.affineSpan_eq_top_iff_vectorSpan_eq_top_of_nonempty {s : Set P} (hs : s.Nonempty) : affineSpan k s = ⊤ ↔ vectorSpan k s = ⊤

views.nl_informal: For a non-trivial space, the affine span of a set is `⊤` iff its vector span is `⊤`.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineSubspace.affineSpan_eq_top_iff_vectorSpan_eq_top_of_nontrivial {s : Set P} [Nontrivial P] : affineSpan k s = ⊤ ↔ vectorSpan k s = ⊤

views.nl_informal: No points are in `⊥`.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineSubspace.not_mem_bot (p : P) : p ∉ (⊥ : AffineSubspace k P)

views.nl_informal: The direction of `⊥` is the submodule `⊥`.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineSubspace.direction_bot : (⊥ : AffineSubspace k P).direction = ⊥

views.nl_informal: A nonempty affine subspace is `⊤` if and only if its direction is `⊤`.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineSubspace.direction_eq_top_iff_of_nonempty {s : AffineSubspace k P} (h : (s : Set P).Nonempty) : s.direction = ⊤ ↔ s = ⊤

views.nl_informal:
The inf of two affine subspaces, coerced to a set, is the intersection of the two sets of
points.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineSubspace.inf_coe (s₁ s₂ : AffineSubspace k P) : (s₁ ⊓ s₂ : Set P) = (s₁ : Set P) ∩ s₂

views.nl_informal: A point is in the inf of two affine subspaces if and only if it is in both of them.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineSubspace.mem_inf_iff (p : P) (s₁ s₂ : AffineSubspace k P) : p ∈ s₁ ⊓ s₂ ↔ p ∈ s₁ ∧ p ∈ s₂

views.nl_informal:
The direction of the inf of two affine subspaces is less than or equal to the inf of their
directions.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineSubspace.direction_inf (s₁ s₂ : AffineSubspace k P) : (s₁ ⊓ s₂).direction ≤ s₁.direction ⊓ s₂.direction

views.nl_informal:
If two affine subspaces have a point in common, the direction of their inf equals the inf of
their directions.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineSubspace.direction_inf_of_mem {s₁ s₂ : AffineSubspace k P} {p : P} (h₁ : p ∈ s₁) (h₂ : p ∈ s₂) : (s₁ ⊓ s₂).direction = s₁.direction ⊓ s₂.direction

views.nl_informal:
If two affine subspaces have a point in their inf, the direction of their inf equals the inf of
their directions.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineSubspace.direction_inf_of_mem_inf {s₁ s₂ : AffineSubspace k P} {p : P} (h : p ∈ s₁ ⊓ s₂) : (s₁ ⊓ s₂).direction = s₁.direction ⊓ s₂.direction

views.nl_informal:
If one affine subspace is less than or equal to another, the same applies to their
directions.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineSubspace.direction_le {s₁ s₂ : AffineSubspace k P} (h : s₁ ≤ s₂) : s₁.direction ≤ s₂.direction

views.nl_informal:

their sup.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineSubspace.sup_direction_le (s₁ s₂ : AffineSubspace k P) : s₁.direction ⊔ s₂.direction ≤ (s₁ ⊔ s₂).direction

the direction of their sup.

If the directions of two nonempty affine subspaces span the whole module, they have nonempty
intersection.

views.nl_informal:
If the directions of two nonempty affine subspaces are complements of each other, they intersect
in exactly one point.

views.nl_informal: Coercing a subspace to a set then taking the affine span produces the original subspace.
views.lean_signature: theorem AffineSubspace.affineSpan_coe (s : AffineSubspace k P) : affineSpan k (s : Set P) = s

views.nl_informal: The affine span of a set is nonempty if and only if that set is.

views.nl_informal: The affine span of a set is `⊥` if and only if that set is empty.

views.nl_informal: The difference between two points lies in their `vectorSpan`.
views.lean_signature: theorem vsub_mem_vectorSpan_pair (p₁ p₂ : P) : p₁ -ᵥ p₂ ∈ vectorSpan k ({p₁, p₂} : Set P)

views.nl_informal: The difference between two points (reversed) lies in their `vectorSpan`.

views.nl_informal: A multiple of the difference between two points lies in their `vectorSpan`.

views.nl_informal: A multiple of the difference between two points (reversed) lies in their `vectorSpan`.

views.nl_informal: The first of two points lies in their affine span.
views.lean_signature: theorem left_mem_affineSpan_pair (p₁ p₂ : P) : p₁ ∈ line[k, p₁, p₂]

views.nl_informal: The second of two points lies in their affine span.

views.nl_informal:
One line is contained in another differing in the first point if the first point of the first
line is contained in the second line.

views.nl_informal:
One line is contained in another differing in the second point if the second point of the
first line is contained in the second line.

views.nl_informal: `affineSpan` is monotone.

views.nl_informal:

results as adding the point to the set and taking the span.
views.lean_signature: theorem affineSpan_insert_affineSpan (p : P) (ps : Set P) : affineSpan k (insert p (affineSpan k ps : Set P)) = affineSpan k (insert p ps)

views.nl_informal:
If a point is in the affine span of a set, adding it to that set does not change the affine
span.
views.lean_signature: theorem affineSpan_insert_eq_affineSpan {p : P} {ps : Set P} (h : p ∈ affineSpan k ps) : affineSpan k (insert p ps) = affineSpan k ps

views.nl_informal:
If a point is in the affine span of a set, adding it to that set does not change the vector
span.
views.lean_signature: theorem vectorSpan_insert_eq_vectorSpan {p : P} {ps : Set P} (h : p ∈ affineSpan k ps) : vectorSpan k (insert p ps) = vectorSpan k ps

views.nl_informal:

span.

views.nl_informal:

the same as composing with their composition.

views.nl_informal: Composing an alternating map with the identity linear map in each argument.
views.lean_signature: theorem AlternatingMap.compLinearMap_id (f : M [⋀^ι]→ₗ[R] N) : f.compLinearMap LinearMap.id = f

views.nl_informal: Composing with a surjective linear map is injective.

Taking the `MultilinearMap.alternatization` of the `MultilinearMap.domCoprod` of two

views.nl_informal:

views.lean_signature: theorem Basis.mk_coord_apply_ne {i j : ι} (h : j ≠ i) : (Basis.mk hli hsp).coord i (v j) = 0

views.lean_signature: theorem Basis.mk_coord_apply [DecidableEq ι] {i j : ι} : (Basis.mk hli hsp).coord i (v j) = if j = i then 1 else 0

views.nl_informal:
Over any ring `R`, if `b` is an infinite basis for a module `M`,
and `s` is a maximal linearly independent set,
then the cardinality of `b` is bounded by the cardinality of `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem infinite_basis_le_maximal_linearIndependent {ι : Type w} (b : Basis ι R M) [Infinite ι] {κ : Type w} (v : κ → M) (i : LinearIndependent R v) (m : i.Maximal) : #ι ≤ #κ

views.nl_informal: Two linear maps are equal if they are equal on basis vectors.
views.lean_signature: theorem Basis.ext {f₁ f₂ : M →ₛₗ[σ] M₁} (h : ∀ i, f₁ (b i) = f₂ (b i)) : f₁ = f₂

views.nl_informal: Two linear equivs are equal if they are equal on basis vectors.
views.lean_signature: theorem Basis.ext' {f₁ f₂ : M ≃ₛₗ[σ] M₁} (h : ∀ i, f₁ (b i) = f₂ (b i)) : f₁ = f₂

views.nl_informal: Two elements are equal iff their coordinates are equal.
views.lean_signature: theorem Basis.ext_elem_iff {x y : M} : x = y ↔ ∀ i, b.repr x i = b.repr y i

views.nl_informal: Two bases are equal if they assign the same coordinates.

views.nl_informal: Two bases are equal if their basis vectors are the same.
views.lean_signature: theorem Basis.eq_of_apply_eq {b₁ b₂ : Basis ι R M} : (∀ i, b₁ i = b₂ i) → b₁ = b₂

views.nl_informal: When the group in question is the automorphisms, `•` coincides with `Basis.map`.

views.nl_informal: If the submodule `P` has a basis, `x ∈ P` iff it is a linear combination of basis vectors.

views.nl_informal:

`x ∈ P` iff it is a linear combination of basis vectors.

views.nl_informal:
An element of a non-unital-non-associative algebra is in the center exactly when it commutes

views.nl_informal:
