views.nl_informal:
Any linear map `f : p →ₗ[K] V'` defined on a subspace `p` can be extended to the whole
space.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.exists_extend {p : Submodule K V} (f : p →ₗ[K] V') : ∃ g : V →ₗ[K] V', g.comp p.subtype = f

views.nl_informal:
If `p < ⊤` is a subspace of a vector space `V`, then there exists a nonzero linear map
`f : V →ₗ[K] K` such that `p ≤ ker f`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Submodule.exists_le_ker_of_lt_top (p : Submodule K V) (hp : p < ⊤) : ∃ (f : V →ₗ[K] K), f ≠ 0 ∧ p ≤ ker f

views.nl_informal: Two bilinear forms are equal when they are equal on all basis vectors.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.BilinForm.ext_basis (h : ∀ i j, B (b i) (b j) = F₂ (b i) (b j)) : B = F₂

views.nl_informal: Write out `B x y` as a sum over `B (b i) (b j)` if `b` is a basis.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.BilinForm.sum_repr_mul_repr_mul (x y : M) : ((b.repr x).sum fun i xi => (b.repr y).sum fun j yj => xi • yj • B (b i) (b j)) = B x y

views.nl_informal:
A set of orthogonal vectors `v` with respect to some bilinear form `B` is linearly independent
if for all `i`, `B (v i) (v i) ≠ 0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.BilinForm.linearIndependent_of_iIsOrtho {n : Type w} {B : BilinForm K V} {v : n → V} (hv₁ : B.iIsOrtho v) (hv₂ : ∀ i, ¬B.IsOrtho (v i) (v i)) : LinearIndependent K v

views.nl_informal:
Given a bilinear form `B` and some `x` such that `B x x ≠ 0`, the span of the singleton of `x`
is complement to its orthogonal complement.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.BilinForm.isCompl_span_singleton_orthogonal {B : BilinForm K V} {x : V} (hx : ¬B.IsOrtho x x) : IsCompl (K ∙ x) (B.orthogonal <| K ∙ x)

views.nl_informal:
The restriction of a reflexive bilinear form `B` onto a submodule `W` is
nondegenerate if `Disjoint W (B.orthogonal W)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.BilinForm.nondegenerate_restrict_of_disjoint_orthogonal (B : BilinForm R₁ M₁) (b : B.IsRefl) {W : Submodule R₁ M₁} (hW : Disjoint W (B.orthogonal W)) : (B.restrict W).Nondegenerate

views.nl_informal:
An orthogonal basis with respect to a nondegenerate bilinear form has no self-orthogonal
elements.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.BilinForm.iIsOrtho.not_isOrtho_basis_self_of_nondegenerate {n : Type w} [Nontrivial R] {B : BilinForm R M} {v : Basis n R M} (h : B.iIsOrtho v) (hB : B.Nondegenerate) (i : n) : ¬B.IsOrtho (v i) (v i)

views.nl_informal:
Given an orthogonal basis with respect to a bilinear form, the bilinear form is nondegenerate
iff the basis has no elements which are self-orthogonal.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.BilinForm.iIsOrtho.nondegenerate_iff_not_isOrtho_basis_self {n : Type w} [Nontrivial R] [NoZeroDivisors R] (B : BilinForm R M) (v : Basis n R M) (hO : B.iIsOrtho v) : B.Nondegenerate ↔ ∀ i, ¬B.IsOrtho (v i) (v i)

views.nl_informal:
A subspace is complement to its orthogonal complement with respect to some
reflexive bilinear form if that bilinear form restricted on to the subspace is nondegenerate.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.BilinForm.isCompl_orthogonal_of_restrict_nondegenerate (b₁ : B.IsRefl) (b₂ : (B.restrict W).Nondegenerate) : IsCompl W (B.orthogonal W)

views.nl_informal:
A subspace is complement to its orthogonal complement with respect to some reflexive bilinear
form if and only if that bilinear form restricted on to the subspace is nondegenerate.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.BilinForm.restrict_nondegenerate_iff_isCompl_orthogonal (b₁ : B.IsRefl) : (B.restrict W).Nondegenerate ↔ IsCompl W (B.orthogonal W)

views.nl_informal:
The restriction of a reflexive, non-degenerate bilinear form on the orthogonal complement of
the span of a singleton is also non-degenerate.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.BilinForm.restrict_nondegenerate_orthogonal_spanSingleton (B : BilinForm K V) (b₁ : B.Nondegenerate) (b₂ : B.IsRefl) {x : V} (hx : ¬B.IsOrtho x x) : Nondegenerate <| B.restrict <| B.orthogonal (K ∙ x)

views.nl_informal: The restriction of a symmetric bilinear form on a submodule is also symmetric.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.BilinForm.IsSymm.restrict {B : BilinForm R M} (b : B.IsSymm) (W : Submodule R M) : (B.restrict W).IsSymm

views.nl_informal: In a non-trivial module, zero is not non-degenerate.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.BilinForm.not_nondegenerate_zero [Nontrivial M] : ¬(0 : BilinForm R M).Nondegenerate

views.nl_informal: A bilinear form is nondegenerate if and only if it has a trivial kernel.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.BilinForm.nondegenerate_iff_ker_eq_bot {B : BilinForm R M} : B.Nondegenerate ↔ LinearMap.ker B = ⊥

views.nl_informal:
Given the nondegenerate bilinear form `B`, the linear map `φ` has a unique left adjoint given by
`BilinForm.leftAdjointOfNondegenerate`.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.BilinForm.isAdjointPair_iff_eq_of_nondegenerate (B : BilinForm K V) (b : B.Nondegenerate) (ψ φ : V →ₗ[K] V) : IsAdjointPair B B ψ φ ↔ ψ = B.leftAdjointOfNondegenerate b φ

views.nl_informal: A tensor product of symmetric bilinear maps is symmetric.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.BilinMap.tmul_isSymm {B₁ : BilinMap A M₁ N₁} {B₂ : BilinMap R M₂ N₂} (hB₁ : ∀ x y, B₁ x y = B₁ y x) (hB₂ : ∀ x y, B₂ x y = B₂ y x) (x y : M₁ ⊗[R] M₂) : B₁.tmul B₂ x y = B₁.tmul B₂ y x

views.nl_informal: A tensor product of symmetric bilinear forms is symmetric.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.IsSymm.tmul {B₁ : BilinForm A M₁} {B₂ : BilinForm R M₂} (hB₁ : B₁.IsSymm) (hB₂ : B₂.IsSymm) : (B₁.tmul B₂).IsSymm

views.nl_informal: The base change of a symmetric bilinear form is symmetric.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.BilinForm.IsSymm.baseChange {B₂ : BilinForm R M₂} (hB₂ : B₂.IsSymm) : (B₂.baseChange A).IsSymm

views.nl_informal:
The **Cayley-Hamilton Theorem**, that the characteristic polynomial of a linear map, applied
to the linear map itself, is zero.

See `Matrix.aeval_self_charpoly` for the equivalent statement about matrices.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.aeval_self_charpoly : aeval f f.charpoly = 0

views.nl_informal:
Any endomorphism polynomial `p` is equivalent under evaluation to `p %ₘ f.charpoly`; that is,
`p` is equivalent to a polynomial with degree less than the dimension of the module.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.aeval_eq_aeval_mod_charpoly (p : R[X]) : aeval f p = aeval f (p %ₘ f.charpoly)

views.nl_informal:
Any endomorphism power can be computed as the sum of endomorphism powers less than the
dimension of the module.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.pow_eq_aeval_mod_charpoly (k : ℕ) : f ^ k = aeval f (X ^ k %ₘ f.charpoly)

views.nl_informal: `charpoly f` is the characteristic polynomial of the matrix of `f` in any basis.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.charpoly_toMatrix {ι : Type w} [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι] (b : Basis ι R M) : (toMatrix b b f).charpoly = f.charpoly

views.nl_informal: The involution acts only on the right of the tensor product.
views.lean_signature: theorem CliffordAlgebra.toBaseChange_involute (Q : QuadraticForm R V) (x : CliffordAlgebra (Q.baseChange A)) : toBaseChange A Q (involute x) = TensorProduct.map LinearMap.id (involute.toLinearMap) (toBaseChange A Q x)

views.nl_informal: `reverse` acts only on the right of the tensor product.
views.lean_signature: theorem CliffordAlgebra.toBaseChange_reverse (Q : QuadraticForm R V) (x : CliffordAlgebra (Q.baseChange A)) : toBaseChange A Q (reverse x) = TensorProduct.map LinearMap.id reverse (toBaseChange A Q x)

views.nl_informal: As well as being linear, `ι Q` squares to the quadratic form
views.lean_signature: theorem CliffordAlgebra.ι_sq_scalar (m : M) : ι Q m * ι Q m = algebraMap R _ (Q m)

views.nl_informal:
If `C` holds for the `algebraMap` of `r : R` into `CliffordAlgebra Q`, the `ι` of `x : M`,
and is preserved under addition and multiplication, then it holds for all of `CliffordAlgebra Q`.

See also the stronger `CliffordAlgebra.left_induction` and `CliffordAlgebra.right_induction`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CliffordAlgebra.induction {C : CliffordAlgebra Q → Prop} (algebraMap : ∀ r, C (algebraMap R (CliffordAlgebra Q) r)) (ι : ∀ x, C (ι Q x)) (mul : ∀ a b, C a → C b → C (a * b)) (add : ∀ a b, C a → C b → C (a + b)) (a : CliffordAlgebra Q) : C a

views.nl_informal:
An alternative way to provide the argument to `CliffordAlgebra.lift` when `2` is invertible.

To show a function squares to the quadratic form, it suffices to show that
`f x * f y + f y * f x = algebraMap _ _ (polar Q x y)`
views.lean_signature: theorem CliffordAlgebra.forall_mul_self_eq_iff {A : Type*} [Ring A] [Algebra R A] (h2 : IsUnit (2 : A)) (f : M →ₗ[R] A) : (∀ x, f x * f x = algebraMap _ _ (Q x)) ↔ (LinearMap.mul R A).compl₂ f ∘ₗ f + (LinearMap.mul R A).flip.compl₂ f ∘ₗ f = Q.polarBilin.compr₂ (Algebra.linearMap R A)

views.nl_informal: The symmetric product of vectors is a scalar
views.lean_signature: theorem CliffordAlgebra.ι_mul_ι_add_swap (a b : M) : ι Q a * ι Q b + ι Q b * ι Q a = algebraMap R _ (QuadraticMap.polar Q a b)

views.nl_informal: $aba$ is a vector.
views.lean_signature: theorem CliffordAlgebra.ι_mul_ι_mul_ι (a b : M) : ι Q a * ι Q b * ι Q a = ι Q (QuadraticMap.polar Q a b • a - Q a • b)

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is a linear map from `M₁` to `M₂` that preserves the quadratic forms, and if it has
a linear retraction `g` that also preserves the quadratic forms, then `CliffordAlgebra.map g`
is a retraction of `CliffordAlgebra.map f`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CliffordAlgebra.leftInverse_map_of_leftInverse {Q₁ : QuadraticForm R M₁} {Q₂ : QuadraticForm R M₂} (f : Q₁ →qᵢ Q₂) (g : Q₂ →qᵢ Q₁) (h : LeftInverse g f) : LeftInverse (map g) (map f)

views.nl_informal:
If a linear map preserves the quadratic forms and is surjective, then the algebra
maps it induces between Clifford algebras is also surjective.
views.lean_signature: theorem CliffordAlgebra.map_surjective {Q₁ : QuadraticForm R M₁} {Q₂ : QuadraticForm R M₂} (f : Q₁ →qᵢ Q₂) (hf : Function.Surjective f) : Function.Surjective (CliffordAlgebra.map f)

views.nl_informal:
`CliffordAlgebra.reverse` and `CliffordAlgebra.involute` commute. Note that the composition
is sometimes referred to as the "clifford conjugate".
views.lean_signature: theorem CliffordAlgebra.reverse_involute_commute : Function.Commute (reverse (Q := Q)) involute

views.nl_informal:
Taking the reverse of the product a list of $n$ vectors lifted via `ι` is equivalent to
taking the product of the reverse of that list.
views.lean_signature: theorem CliffordAlgebra.reverse_prod_map_ι : ∀ l : List M, reverse (l.map <| ι Q).prod = (l.map <| ι Q).reverse.prod

views.nl_informal:
Taking the involute of the product a list of $n$ vectors lifted via `ι` is equivalent to
premultiplying by ${-1}^n$.
views.lean_signature: theorem CliffordAlgebra.involute_prod_map_ι : ∀ l : List M, involute (l.map <| ι Q).prod = (-1 : R) ^ l.length • (l.map <| ι Q).prod

views.nl_informal: `CliffordAlgebra.involute` is analogous to `Complex.conj`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CliffordAlgebraComplex.toComplex_involute (c : CliffordAlgebra Q) : toComplex (involute c) = conj (toComplex c)

views.nl_informal: `reverse` is a no-op over `CliffordAlgebraComplex.Q`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CliffordAlgebraComplex.reverse_apply (x : CliffordAlgebra Q) : x.reverse = x

views.nl_informal: `Complex.conj` is analogous to `CliffordAlgebra.involute`.
views.lean_signature: theorem CliffordAlgebraComplex.ofComplex_conj (c : ℂ) : ofComplex (conj c) = involute (ofComplex c)

views.nl_informal: The "clifford conjugate" maps to the quaternion conjugate.
views.lean_signature: theorem CliffordAlgebraQuaternion.toQuaternion_star (c : CliffordAlgebra (Q c₁ c₂)) : toQuaternion (star c) = star (toQuaternion c)

views.nl_informal: The quaternion conjugate maps to the "clifford conjugate" (aka `star`).
views.lean_signature: theorem CliffordAlgebraQuaternion.ofQuaternion_star (q : ℍ[R,c₁,0,c₂]) : ofQuaternion (star q) = star (ofQuaternion q)

views.nl_informal:
Two algebra morphisms from the even subalgebra are equal if they agree on pairs of generators.

See note [partially-applied ext lemmas].
views.lean_signature: theorem CliffordAlgebra.even.algHom_ext ⦃f g : even Q →ₐ[R] A⦄ (h : (even.ι Q).compr₂ f = (even.ι Q).compr₂ g) : f = g

views.nl_informal:
The representation of the clifford conjugate (i.e. the reverse of the involute) in the even
subalgebra is just the reverse of the representation.
views.lean_signature: theorem CliffordAlgebra.coe_toEven_reverse_involute (x : CliffordAlgebra Q) : ↑(toEven Q (reverse (involute x))) = reverse (Q := Q' Q) (toEven Q x : CliffordAlgebra (Q' Q))

views.nl_informal:
To show a property is true on the even or odd part, it suffices to show it is true on the
scalars or vectors (respectively), closed under addition, and under left-multiplication by a pair
of vectors.
views.lean_signature: theorem CliffordAlgebra.evenOdd_induction (n : ZMod 2) {motive : ∀ x, x ∈ evenOdd Q n → Prop} (range_ι_pow : ∀ (v) (h : v ∈ LinearMap.range (ι Q) ^ n.val), motive v (Submodule.mem_iSup_of_mem ⟨n.val, n.natCast_zmod_val⟩ h)) (add : ∀ x y hx hy, motive x hx → motive y hy → motive (x + y) (Submodule.add_mem _ hx hy)) (ι_mul_ι_mul : ∀ m₁ m₂ x hx, motive x hx → motive (ι Q m₁ * ι Q m₂ * x) (zero_add n ▸ SetLike.mul_mem_graded (ι_mul_ι_mem_evenOdd_zero Q m₁ m₂) hx)) (x : CliffordAlgebra Q) (hx : x ∈ evenOdd Q n) : motive x hx

views.nl_informal:
To show a property is true on the even parts, it suffices to show it is true on the
scalars, closed under addition, and under left-multiplication by a pair of vectors.
views.lean_signature: theorem CliffordAlgebra.even_induction {motive : ∀ x, x ∈ evenOdd Q 0 → Prop} (algebraMap : ∀ r : R, motive (algebraMap _ _ r) (SetLike.algebraMap_mem_graded _ _)) (add : ∀ x y hx hy, motive x hx → motive y hy → motive (x + y) (Submodule.add_mem _ hx hy)) (ι_mul_ι_mul : ∀ m₁ m₂ x hx, motive x hx → motive (ι Q m₁ * ι Q m₂ * x) (zero_add (0 : ZMod 2) ▸ SetLike.mul_mem_graded (ι_mul_ι_mem_evenOdd_zero Q m₁ m₂) hx)) (x : CliffordAlgebra Q) (hx : x ∈ evenOdd Q 0) : motive x hx

views.nl_informal:
To show a property is true on the odd parts, it suffices to show it is true on the
vectors, closed under addition, and under left-multiplication by a pair of vectors.
views.lean_signature: theorem CliffordAlgebra.odd_induction {P : ∀ x, x ∈ evenOdd Q 1 → Prop} (ι : ∀ v, P (ι Q v) (ι_mem_evenOdd_one _ _)) (add : ∀ x y hx hy, P x hx → P y hy → P (x + y) (Submodule.add_mem _ hx hy)) (ι_mul_ι_mul : ∀ m₁ m₂ x hx, P x hx → P (CliffordAlgebra.ι Q m₁ * CliffordAlgebra.ι Q m₂ * x) (zero_add (1 : ZMod 2) ▸ SetLike.mul_mem_graded (ι_mul_ι_mem_evenOdd_zero Q m₁ m₂) hx)) (x : CliffordAlgebra Q) (hx : x ∈ evenOdd Q 1) : P x hx

views.nl_informal: For a vector with invertible quadratic form, $v^{-1} = \frac{v}{Q(v)}$
views.lean_signature: theorem CliffordAlgebra.invOf_ι (m : M) [Invertible (Q m)] [Invertible (ι Q m)] : ⅟ (ι Q m) = ι Q (⅟ (Q m) • m)

views.nl_informal: $aba^{-1}$ is a vector.
views.lean_signature: theorem CliffordAlgebra.ι_mul_ι_mul_invOf_ι (a b : M) [Invertible (ι Q a)] [Invertible (Q a)] : ι Q a * ι Q b * ⅟ (ι Q a) = ι Q ((⅟ (Q a) * QuadraticMap.polar Q a b) • a - b)

views.nl_informal: $a^{-1}ba$ is a vector.
views.lean_signature: theorem CliffordAlgebra.invOf_ι_mul_ι_mul_ι (a b : M) [Invertible (ι Q a)] [Invertible (Q a)] : ⅟ (ι Q a) * ι Q b * ι Q a = ι Q ((⅟ (Q a) * QuadraticMap.polar Q a b) • a - b)

views.nl_informal:
If `m₁` and `m₂` are both homogeneous,
and the quadratic spaces `Q₁` and `Q₂` map into
orthogonal subspaces of `Qₙ` (for instance, when `Qₙ = Q₁.prod Q₂`),
then the product of the embedding in `CliffordAlgebra Q` commutes up to a sign factor.
views.lean_signature: theorem CliffordAlgebra.map_mul_map_of_isOrtho_of_mem_evenOdd {i₁ i₂ : ZMod 2} (hm₁ : m₁ ∈ evenOdd Q₁ i₁) (hm₂ : m₂ ∈ evenOdd Q₂ i₂) : map f₁ m₁ * map f₂ m₂ = (-1 : ℤˣ) ^ (i₂ * i₁) • (map f₂ m₂ * map f₁ m₁)

views.nl_informal: The conjugation action by elements of the Lipschitz group keeps vectors as vectors.
views.lean_signature: theorem lipschitzGroup.conjAct_smul_ι_mem_range_ι {x : (CliffordAlgebra Q)ˣ} (hx : x ∈ lipschitzGroup Q) [Invertible (2 : R)] (m : M) : ConjAct.toConjAct x • ι Q m ∈ LinearMap.range (ι Q)

views.nl_informal:
If x is in `lipschitzGroup Q`, then `(ι Q).range` is closed under twisted conjugation.
The reverse statement presumably is true only in finite dimensions.
views.lean_signature: theorem lipschitzGroup.conjAct_smul_range_ι {x : (CliffordAlgebra Q)ˣ} (hx : x ∈ lipschitzGroup Q) [Invertible (2 : R)] : ConjAct.toConjAct x • LinearMap.range (ι Q) = LinearMap.range (ι Q)

views.nl_informal: An element is in `pinGroup Q` if and only if it is in `lipschitzGroup Q` and `unitary`.
views.lean_signature: theorem pinGroup.mem_iff {x : CliffordAlgebra Q} : x ∈ pinGroup Q ↔ x ∈ (lipschitzGroup Q).toSubmonoid.map (Units.coeHom <| CliffordAlgebra Q) ∧ x ∈ unitary (CliffordAlgebra Q)

views.nl_informal: The conjugation action by elements of the spin group keeps vectors as vectors.
views.lean_signature: theorem pinGroup.conjAct_smul_ι_mem_range_ι {x : (CliffordAlgebra Q)ˣ} (hx : ↑x ∈ pinGroup Q) [Invertible (2 : R)] (y : M) : ConjAct.toConjAct x • ι Q y ∈ LinearMap.range (ι Q)

views.nl_informal:
If x is in `pinGroup Q`, then `(ι Q).range` is closed under twisted conjugation. The reverse
statement presumably being true only in finite dimensions.
views.lean_signature: theorem pinGroup.conjAct_smul_range_ι {x : (CliffordAlgebra Q)ˣ} (hx : ↑x ∈ pinGroup Q) [Invertible (2 : R)] : ConjAct.toConjAct x • LinearMap.range (ι Q) = LinearMap.range (ι Q)

views.nl_informal:
An element is in `pinGroup Q` if and only if `star x` is in `pinGroup Q`.
See `star_mem` for only one direction.
views.lean_signature: theorem pinGroup.star_mem_iff {x : CliffordAlgebra Q} : star x ∈ pinGroup Q ↔ x ∈ pinGroup Q

views.nl_informal: An element is in `spinGroup Q` if and only if it is in `pinGroup Q` and `even Q`.
views.lean_signature: theorem spinGroup.mem_iff {x : CliffordAlgebra Q} : x ∈ spinGroup Q ↔ x ∈ pinGroup Q ∧ x ∈ even Q

views.nl_informal: If x is in `spinGroup Q`, then `involute x` is equal to x.
views.lean_signature: theorem spinGroup.involute_eq {x : CliffordAlgebra Q} (hx : x ∈ spinGroup Q) : involute x = x

views.nl_informal: The conjugation action by elements of the spin group keeps vectors as vectors.
views.lean_signature: theorem spinGroup.conjAct_smul_ι_mem_range_ι {x : (CliffordAlgebra Q)ˣ} (hx : ↑x ∈ spinGroup Q) [Invertible (2 : R)] (y : M) : ConjAct.toConjAct x • ι Q y ∈ LinearMap.range (ι Q)

views.nl_informal:
An element is in `spinGroup Q` if and only if `star x` is in `spinGroup Q`.
See `star_mem` for only one direction.
views.lean_signature: theorem spinGroup.star_mem_iff {x : CliffordAlgebra Q} : star x ∈ spinGroup Q ↔ x ∈ spinGroup Q

views.nl_informal:
If `M / R` and `M' / R'` are modules, `i : R' → R` is an injective map
non-zero elements, `j : M →+ M'` is an injective monoid homomorphism, such that the scalar
multiplications on `M` and `M'` are compatible, then the rank of `M / R` is smaller than or equal to
the rank of `M' / R'`. As a special case, taking `R = R'` it is
`LinearMap.lift_rank_le_of_injective`.
views.lean_signature: theorem lift_rank_le_of_injective_injectiveₛ (i : R' → R) (j : M →+ M') (hi : Injective i) (hj : Injective j) (hc : ∀ (r : R') (m : M), j (i r • m) = r • j m) : lift.{v'} (Module.rank R M) ≤ lift.{v} (Module.rank R' M')

views.nl_informal:
If `M / R` and `M' / R'` are modules, `i : R → R'` is a surjective map, and
`j : M →+ M'` is an injective monoid homomorphism, such that the scalar multiplications on `M` and
`M'` are compatible, then the rank of `M / R` is smaller than or equal to the rank of `M' / R'`.
As a special case, taking `R = R'` it is `LinearMap.lift_rank_le_of_injective`.
views.lean_signature: theorem lift_rank_le_of_surjective_injective (i : R → R') (j : M →+ M') (hi : Surjective i) (hj : Injective j) (hc : ∀ (r : R) (m : M), j (r • m) = i r • j m) : lift.{v'} (Module.rank R M) ≤ lift.{v} (Module.rank R' M')

views.nl_informal:
If `M / R` and `M' / R'` are modules, `i : R → R'` is a bijective map which maps zero to zero,
`j : M ≃+ M'` is a group isomorphism, such that the scalar multiplications on `M` and `M'` are
compatible, then the rank of `M / R` is equal to the rank of `M' / R'`.
As a special case, taking `R = R'` it is `LinearEquiv.lift_rank_eq`.
views.lean_signature: theorem lift_rank_eq_of_equiv_equiv (i : R → R') (j : M ≃+ M') (hi : Bijective i) (hc : ∀ (r : R) (m : M), j (r • m) = i r • j m) : lift.{v'} (Module.rank R M) = lift.{v} (Module.rank R' M')

views.nl_informal:
If `M / R` and `M' / R'` are modules, `i : R' → R` is a map which sends non-zero elements to
non-zero elements, `j : M →+ M'` is an injective group homomorphism, such that the scalar
multiplications on `M` and `M'` are compatible, then the rank of `M / R` is smaller than or equal to
the rank of `M' / R'`. As a special case, taking `R = R'` it is
`LinearMap.lift_rank_le_of_injective`.
views.lean_signature: theorem lift_rank_le_of_injective_injective [AddCommGroup M'] [Module R' M'] (i : R' → R) (j : M →+ M') (hi : ∀ r, i r = 0 → r = 0) (hj : Injective j) (hc : ∀ (r : R') (m : M), j (i r • m) = r • j m) : lift.{v'} (Module.rank R M) ≤ lift.{v} (Module.rank R' M')

views.nl_informal:
If `S / R` and `S' / R'` are algebras, `i : R' →+* R` and `j : S →+* S'` are injective ring
homomorphisms, such that `R' → R → S → S'` and `R' → S'` commute, then the rank of `S / R` is
smaller than or equal to the rank of `S' / R'`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Algebra.lift_rank_le_of_injective_injective (i : R' →+* R) (j : S →+* S') (hi : Injective i) (hj : Injective j) (hc : (j.comp (algebraMap R S)).comp i = algebraMap R' S') : lift.{v'} (Module.rank R S) ≤ lift.{v} (Module.rank R' S')

views.nl_informal:
If `S / R` and `S' / R'` are algebras, `i : R →+* R'` is a surjective ring homomorphism,
`j : S →+* S'` is an injective ring homomorphism, such that `R → R' → S'` and `R → S → S'` commute,
then the rank of `S / R` is smaller than or equal to the rank of `S' / R'`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Algebra.lift_rank_le_of_surjective_injective (i : R →+* R') (j : S →+* S') (hi : Surjective i) (hj : Injective j) (hc : (algebraMap R' S').comp i = j.comp (algebraMap R S)) : lift.{v'} (Module.rank R S) ≤ lift.{v} (Module.rank R' S')

views.nl_informal:
If `S / R` and `S' / R'` are algebras, `i : R ≃+* R'` and `j : S ≃+* S'` are
ring isomorphisms, such that `R → R' → S'` and `R → S → S'` commute,
then the rank of `S / R` is equal to the rank of `S' / R'`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Algebra.lift_rank_eq_of_equiv_equiv (i : R ≃+* R') (j : S ≃+* S') (hc : (algebraMap R' S').comp i.toRingHom = j.toRingHom.comp (algebraMap R S)) : lift.{v'} (Module.rank R S) = lift.{v} (Module.rank R' S')

views.nl_informal: The rank of the range of a linear map is at most the rank of the source.
views.lean_signature: theorem lift_rank_range_le (f : M →ₗ[R] M') : Cardinal.lift.{v} (Module.rank R (LinearMap.range f)) ≤ Cardinal.lift.{v'} (Module.rank R M)

views.nl_informal:
Two linearly equivalent vector spaces have the same dimension, a version with different
universes.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearEquiv.lift_rank_eq (f : M ≃ₗ[R] M') : Cardinal.lift.{v'} (Module.rank R M) = Cardinal.lift.{v} (Module.rank R M')

views.nl_informal: Two linearly equivalent vector spaces have the same dimension.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearEquiv.rank_eq (f : M ≃ₗ[R] M₁) : Module.rank R M = Module.rank R M₁

views.nl_informal: Pushforwards of submodules along a `LinearEquiv` have the same dimension.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearEquiv.rank_map_eq (f : M ≃ₗ[R] M₁) (p : Submodule R M) : Module.rank R (p.map (f : M →ₗ[R] M₁)) = Module.rank R p

views.nl_informal: The dimension of a quotient is bounded by the dimension of the ambient space.
views.lean_signature: theorem Submodule.finrank_quotient_le [StrongRankCondition R] [Module.Finite R M] (s : Submodule R M) : finrank R (M ⧸ s) ≤ finrank R M

views.nl_informal:
If `M` and `M'` are free, then the rank of `M × M'` is
`(Module.rank R M).lift + (Module.rank R M').lift`.
views.lean_signature: theorem rank_prod : Module.rank R (M × M') = Cardinal.lift.{v'} (Module.rank R M) + Cardinal.lift.{v, v'} (Module.rank R M')

views.nl_informal:
If `M` and `M'` are free (and lie in the same universe), the rank of `M × M'` is
`(Module.rank R M) + (Module.rank R M')`.
views.lean_signature: theorem rank_prod' : Module.rank R (M × M₁) = Module.rank R M + Module.rank R M₁

views.nl_informal: The finrank of `M × M'` is `(finrank R M) + (finrank R M')`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.finrank_prod [Module.Finite R M] [Module.Finite R M'] : finrank R (M × M') = finrank R M + finrank R M'

views.nl_informal: The rank of `(ι →₀ R)` is `(#ι).lift`.
views.lean_signature: theorem rank_finsupp_self (ι : Type w) : Module.rank R (ι →₀ R) = Cardinal.lift.{u} #ι

views.nl_informal: If `R` and `ι` lie in the same universe, the rank of `(ι →₀ R)` is `# ι`.
views.lean_signature: theorem rank_finsupp_self' {ι : Type u} : Module.rank R (ι →₀ R) = #ι

views.nl_informal: The rank of the direct sum is the sum of the ranks.
views.lean_signature: theorem rank_directSum {ι : Type v} (M : ι → Type w) [∀ i : ι, AddCommMonoid (M i)] [∀ i : ι, Module R (M i)] [∀ i : ι, Module.Free R (M i)] : Module.rank R (⨁ i, M i) = Cardinal.sum fun i => Module.rank R (M i)

views.nl_informal:
If `m` and `n` are finite, the rank of `m × n` matrices over a module `M` is
`(#m).lift * (#n).lift * rank R M`.
views.lean_signature: theorem rank_matrix_module (m : Type w) (n : Type w') [Finite m] [Finite n] : Module.rank R (Matrix m n M) = lift.{max v w'} #m * lift.{max v w} #n * lift.{max w w'} (Module.rank R M)

views.nl_informal:
If `m` and `n` are finite and lie in the same universe, the rank of `m × n` matrices over a
module `M` is `(#m * #n).lift * rank R M`.
views.lean_signature: theorem rank_matrix_module' (m n : Type w) [Finite m] [Finite n] : Module.rank R (Matrix m n M) = lift.{max v} (#m * #n) * lift.{w} (Module.rank R M)

views.nl_informal: If `m` and `n` are finite, the rank of `m × n` matrices is `(#m).lift * (#n).lift`.
views.lean_signature: theorem rank_matrix (m : Type v) (n : Type w) [Finite m] [Finite n] : Module.rank R (Matrix m n R) = Cardinal.lift.{max v w u, v} #m * Cardinal.lift.{max v w u, w} #n

views.nl_informal:
If `m` and `n` are finite and lie in the same universe, the rank of `m × n` matrices is
`(#n * #m).lift`.
views.lean_signature: theorem rank_matrix' (m n : Type v) [Finite m] [Finite n] : Module.rank R (Matrix m n R) = Cardinal.lift.{u} (#m * #n)

views.nl_informal:
If `m` and `n` are finite and lie in the same universe as `R`, the rank of `m × n` matrices
is `# m * # n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem rank_matrix'' (m n : Type u) [Finite m] [Finite n] : Module.rank R (Matrix m n R) = #m * #n

views.nl_informal: The finrank of `(ι →₀ R)` is `Fintype.card ι`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.finrank_finsupp_self {ι : Type v} [Fintype ι] : finrank R (ι →₀ R) = card ι

views.nl_informal: The finrank of the direct sum is the sum of the finranks.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.finrank_directSum {ι : Type v} [Fintype ι] (M : ι → Type w) [∀ i : ι, AddCommMonoid (M i)] [∀ i : ι, Module R (M i)] [∀ i : ι, Module.Free R (M i)] [∀ i : ι, Module.Finite R (M i)] : finrank R (⨁ i, M i) = ∑ i, finrank R (M i)

views.nl_informal:
If `m` and `n` are `Fintype`, the finrank of `m × n` matrices over a module `M` is
`(Fintype.card m) * (Fintype.card n) * finrank R M`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.finrank_matrix (m n : Type*) [Fintype m] [Fintype n] : finrank R (Matrix m n M) = card m * card n * finrank R M

views.nl_informal: The rank of a finite product of free modules is the sum of the ranks.
views.lean_signature: theorem rank_pi [Finite η] : Module.rank R (∀ i, φ i) = Cardinal.sum fun i => Module.rank R (φ i)

views.nl_informal: The finrank of `(ι → R)` is `Fintype.card ι`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.finrank_pi {ι : Type v} [Fintype ι] : finrank R (ι → R) = Fintype.card ι

views.nl_informal: The finrank of a finite product is the sum of the finranks.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.finrank_pi_fintype {ι : Type v} [Fintype ι] {M : ι → Type w} [∀ i : ι, AddCommMonoid (M i)] [∀ i : ι, Module R (M i)] [∀ i : ι, Module.Free R (M i)] [∀ i : ι, Module.Finite R (M i)] : finrank R (∀ i, M i) = ∑ i, finrank R (M i)

views.nl_informal: The vector space of functions on a `Fintype ι` has finrank equal to the cardinality of `ι`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.finrank_fintype_fun_eq_card : finrank R (η → R) = Fintype.card η

views.nl_informal: The vector space of functions on `Fin n` has finrank equal to `n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.finrank_fin_fun {n : ℕ} : finrank R (Fin n → R) = n

views.nl_informal: The `S`-rank of `M ⊗[R] M'` is `(Module.rank S M).lift * (Module.rank R M').lift`.
views.lean_signature: theorem rank_tensorProduct : Module.rank R (M ⊗[S] M') = Cardinal.lift.{v'} (Module.rank R M) * Cardinal.lift.{v} (Module.rank S M')

views.nl_informal:
If `M` and `M'` lie in the same universe, the `S`-rank of `M ⊗[R] M'` is
`(Module.rank S M) * (Module.rank R M')`.
views.lean_signature: theorem rank_tensorProduct' : Module.rank R (M ⊗[S] M₁) = Module.rank R M * Module.rank S M₁

views.nl_informal: The `S`-finrank of `M ⊗[R] M'` is `(finrank S M) * (finrank R M')`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.finrank_tensorProduct : finrank R (M ⊗[S] M') = finrank R M * finrank S M'

views.nl_informal: The dimension of a submodule is bounded by the dimension of the ambient space.
views.lean_signature: theorem Submodule.finrank_le [Module.Finite R M] (s : Submodule R M) : finrank R s ≤ finrank R M

views.nl_informal: Pushforwards of finite submodules have a smaller finrank.
views.lean_signature: theorem Submodule.finrank_map_le [Module R M'] (f : M →ₗ[R] M') (p : Submodule R M) [Module.Finite R p] : finrank R (p.map f) ≤ finrank R p

views.nl_informal: If a vector space has a finite dimension, the index set of `Basis.ofVectorSpace` is finite.
views.lean_signature: theorem Basis.finite_ofVectorSpaceIndex_of_rank_lt_aleph0 (h : Module.rank K V < ℵ₀) : (Basis.ofVectorSpaceIndex K V).Finite

views.nl_informal:
A finite family of vectors is linearly independent if and only if
its cardinality equals the dimension of its span.
views.lean_signature: theorem linearIndependent_iff_card_eq_finrank_span {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] {b : ι → V} : LinearIndependent K b ↔ Fintype.card ι = (Set.range b).finrank K

views.nl_informal:
The **Erdős-Kaplansky Theorem**: the dual of an infinite-dimensional vector space
over a division ring has dimension equal to its cardinality.
views.lean_signature: theorem rank_dual_eq_card_dual_of_aleph0_le_rank' {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] (h : ℵ₀ ≤ Module.rank K V) : Module.rank Kᵐᵒᵖ (V →ₗ[K] K) = #(V →ₗ[K] K)

views.nl_informal: The **Erdős-Kaplansky Theorem** over a field.
views.lean_signature: theorem rank_dual_eq_card_dual_of_aleph0_le_rank {K V} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] (h : ℵ₀ ≤ Module.rank K V) : Module.rank K (V →ₗ[K] K) = #(V →ₗ[K] K)

views.nl_informal:
If every finite set of linearly independent vectors has cardinality at most `n`,
then the same is true for arbitrary sets of linearly independent vectors.
views.lean_signature: theorem linearIndependent_bounded_of_finset_linearIndependent_bounded {n : ℕ} (H : ∀ s : Finset M, (LinearIndependent R fun i : s => (i : M)) → s.card ≤ n) : ∀ s : Set M, LinearIndependent R ((↑) : s → M) → #s ≤ n

views.nl_informal: If a module has a finite dimension, all bases are indexed by a finite type.
views.lean_signature: theorem Basis.nonempty_fintype_index_of_rank_lt_aleph0 {ι : Type*} (b : Basis ι R M) (h : Module.rank R M < ℵ₀) : Nonempty (Fintype ι)

views.nl_informal: If a module has a finite dimension, all bases are indexed by a finite set.
views.lean_signature: theorem Basis.finite_index_of_rank_lt_aleph0 {ι : Type*} {s : Set ι} (b : Basis s R M) (h : Module.rank R M < ℵ₀) : s.Finite

views.nl_informal:
If `p` is an independent family of submodules of a `R`-finite module `M`, then the
number of nontrivial subspaces in the family `p` is bounded above by the dimension of `M`.

Note that the `Fintype` hypothesis required here can be provided by
`iSupIndep.fintypeNeBotOfFiniteDimensional`.
views.lean_signature: theorem iSupIndep.subtype_ne_bot_le_finrank {p : ι → Submodule R M} (hp : iSupIndep p) [Fintype { i // p i ≠ ⊥ }] : Fintype.card { i // p i ≠ ⊥ } ≤ finrank R M

views.nl_informal:
If a finset has cardinality larger than the rank of a module,
then there is a nontrivial linear relation amongst its elements.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.exists_nontrivial_relation_of_finrank_lt_card {t : Finset M} (h : finrank R M < t.card) : ∃ f : M → R, ∑ e ∈ t, f e • e = 0 ∧ ∃ x ∈ t, f x ≠ 0

views.nl_informal:
If a finset has cardinality larger than `finrank + 1`,
then there is a nontrivial linear relation amongst its elements,
such that the coefficients of the relation sum to zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.exists_nontrivial_relation_sum_zero_of_finrank_succ_lt_card {t : Finset M} (h : finrank R M + 1 < t.card) : ∃ f : M → R, ∑ e ∈ t, f e • e = 0 ∧ ∑ e ∈ t, f e = 0 ∧ ∃ x ∈ t, f x ≠ 0

views.nl_informal: A (finite dimensional) space that is a subsingleton has zero `finrank`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.finrank_zero_of_subsingleton [Subsingleton M] : finrank R M = 0

views.nl_informal: A finite dimensional space is nontrivial if it has positive `finrank`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.nontrivial_of_finrank_pos (h : 0 < finrank R M) : Nontrivial M

views.nl_informal:
A finite dimensional space is nontrivial if it has `finrank` equal to the successor of a
natural number.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.nontrivial_of_finrank_eq_succ {n : ℕ} (hn : finrank R M = n.succ) : Nontrivial M

views.nl_informal: A finite rank torsion-free module has positive `finrank` iff it has a nonzero element.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.finrank_pos_iff_exists_ne_zero [NoZeroSMulDivisors R M] : 0 < finrank R M ↔ ∃ x : M, x ≠ 0

views.nl_informal: An `R`-finite torsion-free module has positive `finrank` iff it is nontrivial.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.finrank_pos_iff [NoZeroSMulDivisors R M] : 0 < finrank R M ↔ Nontrivial M

views.nl_informal: A nontrivial finite dimensional space has positive `finrank`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.finrank_pos [NoZeroSMulDivisors R M] [h : Nontrivial M] : 0 < finrank R M

views.nl_informal:
A finite dimensional space has zero `finrank` iff it is a subsingleton.
This is the `finrank` version of `rank_zero_iff`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.finrank_zero_iff [NoZeroSMulDivisors R M] : finrank R M = 0 ↔ Subsingleton M

views.nl_informal:
If there is a nonzero vector and every other vector is a multiple of it,
then the module has dimension one.
views.lean_signature: theorem rank_eq_one (v : M) (n : v ≠ 0) (h : ∀ w : M, ∃ c : R, c • v = w) : Module.rank R M = 1

views.nl_informal:
If there is a nonzero vector and every other vector is a multiple of it,
then the module has dimension one.
views.lean_signature: theorem finrank_eq_one (v : M) (n : v ≠ 0) (h : ∀ w : M, ∃ c : R, c • v = w) : finrank R M = 1

views.nl_informal: If every vector is a multiple of some `v : M`, then `M` has dimension at most one.
views.lean_signature: theorem finrank_le_one (v : M) (h : ∀ w : M, ∃ c : R, c • v = w) : finrank R M ≤ 1

views.nl_informal: The dimension of a finite dimensional space is preserved under linear equivalence.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearEquiv.finrank_eq (f : M ≃ₗ[R] N) : finrank R M = finrank R N

views.nl_informal: Pushforwards of finite-dimensional submodules along a `LinearEquiv` have the same finrank.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearEquiv.finrank_map_eq (f : M ≃ₗ[R] N) (p : Submodule R M) : finrank R (p.map (f : M →ₗ[R] N)) = finrank R p

views.nl_informal: The dimensions of the domain and range of an injective linear map are equal.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj {f : M →ₗ[R] N} (hf : Function.Injective f) : finrank R (LinearMap.range f) = finrank R M

views.nl_informal:
Tower law: if `A` is a `K`-module and `K` is an extension of `F` then
$\operatorname{rank}_F(A) = \operatorname{rank}_F(K) * \operatorname{rank}_K(A)$.

The universe polymorphic version of `rank_mul_rank` below.
views.lean_signature: theorem lift_rank_mul_lift_rank : Cardinal.lift.{w} (Module.rank F K) * Cardinal.lift.{v} (Module.rank K A) = Cardinal.lift.{v} (Module.rank F A)

views.nl_informal:
Tower law: if `A` is a `K`-module and `K` is an extension of `F` then
$\operatorname{rank}_F(A) = \operatorname{rank}_F(K) * \operatorname{rank}_K(A)$.

This is a simpler version of `lift_rank_mul_lift_rank` with `K` and `A` in the same universe.
views.lean_signature: theorem rank_mul_rank (A : Type v) [AddCommMonoid A] [Module K A] [Module F A] [IsScalarTower F K A] [Module.Free K A] : Module.rank F K * Module.rank K A = Module.rank F A

views.nl_informal:
Tower law: if `A` is a `K`-module and `K` is an extension of `F` then
$\operatorname{rank}_F(A) = \operatorname{rank}_F(K) * \operatorname{rank}_K(A)$.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.finrank_mul_finrank : finrank F K * finrank K A = finrank F A

views.nl_informal: The rank of a free module `M` over `R` is the cardinality of `ChooseBasisIndex R M`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.Free.rank_eq_card_chooseBasisIndex : Module.rank R M = #(ChooseBasisIndex R M)

views.nl_informal: The finrank of a free module `M` over `R` is the cardinality of `ChooseBasisIndex R M`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.finrank_eq_card_chooseBasisIndex [Module.Finite R M] : finrank R M = Fintype.card (ChooseBasisIndex R M)

views.nl_informal:
The rank of a free module `M` over an infinite scalar ring `R` is the cardinality of `M`
whenever `#R < #M`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.Free.rank_eq_mk_of_infinite_lt [Infinite R] (h_lt : lift.{v} #R < lift.{u} #M) : Module.rank R M = #M

views.nl_informal: Two vector spaces are isomorphic if they have the same dimension.
views.lean_signature: theorem nonempty_linearEquiv_of_lift_rank_eq (cnd : Cardinal.lift.{v'} (Module.rank R M) = Cardinal.lift.{v} (Module.rank R M')) : Nonempty (M ≃ₗ[R] M')

views.nl_informal: Two vector spaces are isomorphic if they have the same dimension.
views.lean_signature: theorem nonempty_linearEquiv_of_rank_eq (cond : Module.rank R M = Module.rank R M₁) : Nonempty (M ≃ₗ[R] M₁)

views.nl_informal: Two vector spaces are isomorphic if and only if they have the same dimension.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearEquiv.nonempty_equiv_iff_lift_rank_eq : Nonempty (M ≃ₗ[R] M') ↔ Cardinal.lift.{v'} (Module.rank R M) = Cardinal.lift.{v} (Module.rank R M')

views.nl_informal: Two vector spaces are isomorphic if and only if they have the same dimension.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearEquiv.nonempty_equiv_iff_rank_eq : Nonempty (M ≃ₗ[R] M₁) ↔ Module.rank R M = Module.rank R M₁

views.nl_informal: Two finite and free modules are isomorphic if they have the same (finite) rank.
views.lean_signature: theorem FiniteDimensional.nonempty_linearEquiv_of_finrank_eq [Module.Finite R M] [Module.Finite R M'] (cond : finrank R M = finrank R M') : Nonempty (M ≃ₗ[R] M')

views.nl_informal: Two finite and free modules are isomorphic if and only if they have the same (finite) rank.
views.lean_signature: theorem FiniteDimensional.nonempty_linearEquiv_iff_finrank_eq [Module.Finite R M] [Module.Finite R M'] : Nonempty (M ≃ₗ[R] M') ↔ finrank R M = finrank R M'

views.nl_informal: A free module of rank zero is trivial.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.subsingleton_of_rank_zero (h : Module.rank R M = 0) : Subsingleton M

views.nl_informal:
A vector space has dimension at most `1` if and only if there is a
single vector of which all vectors are multiples.
views.lean_signature: theorem rank_le_one_iff [Module.Free K V] : Module.rank K V ≤ 1 ↔ ∃ v₀ : V, ∀ v, ∃ r : K, r • v₀ = v

views.nl_informal:
A vector space has dimension `1` if and only if there is a
single non-zero vector of which all vectors are multiples.
views.lean_signature: theorem rank_eq_one_iff [Module.Free K V] : Module.rank K V = 1 ↔ ∃ v₀ : V, v₀ ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ v, ∃ r : K, r • v₀ = v

views.nl_informal:
A submodule has dimension at most `1` if and only if there is a
single vector in the submodule such that the submodule is contained in
its span.
views.lean_signature: theorem rank_submodule_le_one_iff (s : Submodule K V) [Module.Free K s] : Module.rank K s ≤ 1 ↔ ∃ v₀ ∈ s, s ≤ K ∙ v₀

views.nl_informal:
A submodule has dimension `1` if and only if there is a
single non-zero vector in the submodule such that the submodule is contained in
its span.
views.lean_signature: theorem rank_submodule_eq_one_iff (s : Submodule K V) [Module.Free K s] : Module.rank K s = 1 ↔ ∃ v₀ ∈ s, v₀ ≠ 0 ∧ s ≤ K ∙ v₀

views.nl_informal:
A submodule has dimension at most `1` if and only if there is a
single vector, not necessarily in the submodule, such that the
submodule is contained in its span.
views.lean_signature: theorem rank_submodule_le_one_iff' (s : Submodule K V) [Module.Free K s] : Module.rank K s ≤ 1 ↔ ∃ v₀, s ≤ K ∙ v₀

views.nl_informal: A module has dimension 1 iff there is some `v : V` so `{v}` is a basis.
views.lean_signature: theorem finrank_eq_one_iff [Module.Free K V] (ι : Type*) [Unique ι] : finrank K V = 1 ↔ Nonempty (Basis ι K V)

views.nl_informal: A module has dimension 1 iff there is some nonzero `v : V` so every vector is a multiple of `v`.
views.lean_signature: theorem finrank_eq_one_iff' [Module.Free K V] : finrank K V = 1 ↔ ∃ v ≠ 0, ∀ w : V, ∃ c : K, c • v = w

views.nl_informal:
A finite dimensional module has dimension at most 1 iff
there is some `v : V` so every vector is a multiple of `v`.
views.lean_signature: theorem finrank_le_one_iff [Module.Free K V] [Module.Finite K V] : finrank K V ≤ 1 ↔ ∃ v : V, ∀ w : V, ∃ c : K, c • v = w

views.nl_informal: The rank of the composition of two maps is less than the minimum of their ranks.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.lift_rank_comp_le (g : V →ₗ[K] V') (f : V' →ₗ[K] V'') : Cardinal.lift.{v'} (rank (f.comp g)) ≤ min (Cardinal.lift.{v'} (rank f)) (Cardinal.lift.{v''} (rank g))

views.nl_informal:
The rank of the composition of two maps is less than the minimum of their ranks.

views.nl_informal:
Eigenvalues of a diagonal linear operator with respect to standard basis

views.nl_informal: An endomorphism of a finite-dimensional vector space has a finite spectrum.

views.nl_informal:
Given a family of endomorphisms `i ↦ f i`, a family of candidate eigenvalues `i ↦ μ i`, and a

generalised eigenspace of the `f i` restricted to `p`.

views.nl_informal:
Given a family of endomorphisms `i ↦ f i`, a family of candidate eigenvalues `i ↦ μ i`, and a

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:
In finite dimensions, over an algebraically closed field, every linear endomorphism has an

views.lean_signature: theorem ExteriorAlgebra.lhom_ext ⦃f g : ExteriorAlgebra R M →ₗ[R] N⦄ (h : ∀ i, f.compAlternatingMap (ιMulti R i) = g.compAlternatingMap (ιMulti R i)) : f = g

views.nl_informal:
The image of `ExteriorAlgebra.ιMulti R n` spans the `n`th exterior power. Variant of

views.lean_signature: theorem exteriorPower.ιMulti_span_fixedDegree : Submodule.span R (Set.range (ExteriorAlgebra.ιMulti R n)) = ⋀[R]^n M

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:
If a submodule is contained in a finite-dimensional
submodule with the same or smaller dimension, they are equal.

views.nl_informal:
If a submodule is contained in a finite-dimensional
submodule with the same dimension, they are equal.
views.lean_signature: theorem Submodule.eq_of_le_of_finrank_eq {S₁ S₂ : Submodule K V} [FiniteDimensional K S₂] (hle : S₁ ≤ S₂) (hd : finrank K S₁ = finrank K S₂) : S₁ = S₂

views.nl_informal:
If a subalgebra is contained in a finite-dimensional
subalgebra with the same or smaller dimension, they are equal.

views.nl_informal:
If a subalgebra is contained in a finite-dimensional
subalgebra with the same dimension, they are equal.
views.lean_signature: theorem Subalgebra.eq_of_le_of_finrank_eq (h_le : F ≤ E) (h_finrank : finrank K F = finrank K E) : F = E

views.nl_informal: On a finite-dimensional space, an injective linear map is surjective.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.surjective_of_injective [FiniteDimensional K V] {f : V →ₗ[K] V} (hinj : Injective f) : Surjective f

views.nl_informal:
In a finite-dimensional space, linear maps are inverse to each other on one side if and only if
they are inverse to each other on the other side.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.mul_eq_one_comm [FiniteDimensional K V] {f g : V →ₗ[K] V} : f * g = 1 ↔ g * f = 1

views.nl_informal:
In a finite-dimensional space, linear maps are inverse to each other on one side if and only if
they are inverse to each other on the other side.

views.lean_signature: theorem Module.finrank_eq_rank' [FiniteDimensional K V] : (finrank K V : Cardinal.{v}) = Module.rank K V

rank-nullity theorem : the dimensions of the kernel and the range of a linear map add up to

views.nl_informal:
If `B` is a basis of the `R`-algebra `S` such that `B i = 1` for some index `i`, then
each `r : R` gets represented as `s • B i` as an element of `S`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.Basis.repr_algebraMap {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {B : Basis ι R S} {i : ι} (hBi : B i = 1) (r : R) : B.repr ((algebraMap R S) r) = fun j : ι ↦ if i = j then r else 0

views.nl_informal:
A nonzero ideal over a free finite extension of `ℤ` has a finite quotient.
It can't be an instance because of the side condition `I ≠ ⊥`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Ideal.finiteQuotientOfFreeOfNeBot [Module.Free ℤ S] [Module.Finite ℤ S] (I : Ideal S) (hI : I ≠ ⊥) : Finite (S ⧸ I)

views.nl_informal:
Given a submodule `N` in Smith normal form of a free `R`-module, its index as an additive
subgroup is an appropriate power of the cardinality of `R` multiplied by the product of the
indexes of the ideals generated by each basis vector.
views.lean_signature: theorem Basis.SmithNormalForm.toAddSubgroup_index_eq_pow_mul_prod [Module R M] {N : Submodule R M} (snf : Basis.SmithNormalForm N ι n) : N.toAddSubgroup.index = Nat.card R ^ (Fintype.card ι - n) * ∏ i : Fin n, (Ideal.span {snf.a i}).toAddSubgroup.index

views.nl_informal:
Given a submodule `N` in Smith normal form of a free `R`-module, its index as an additive
subgroup is infinite (represented as zero) if the submodule basis has fewer vectors than the basis
for the module, and otherwise equals the product of the indexes of the ideals generated by each
basis vector.
views.lean_signature: theorem Basis.SmithNormalForm.toAddSubgroup_index_eq_ite [Infinite R] [Module R M] {N : Submodule R M} (snf : Basis.SmithNormalForm N ι n) : N.toAddSubgroup.index = (if n = Fintype.card ι then ∏ i : Fin n, (Ideal.span {snf.a i}).toAddSubgroup.index else 0)

views.nl_informal:
Given a submodule `N` in Smith normal form of a free ℤ-module, it has finite index as an
additive subgroup (i.e., `N.toAddSubgroup.index ≠ 0`) if and only if the submodule basis has as
many vectors as the basis for the module.
views.lean_signature: theorem Basis.SmithNormalForm.toAddSubgroup_index_ne_zero_iff {N : Submodule ℤ M} (snf : Basis.SmithNormalForm N ι n) : N.toAddSubgroup.index ≠ 0 ↔ n = Fintype.card ι

views.nl_informal:
For a nonzero element `f` in an algebra `S` over a principal ideal domain `R` that is finite and
free as an `R`-module, the norm of `f` relative to `R` is associated to the product of the Smith
coefficients of the ideal generated by `f`.
views.lean_signature: theorem associated_norm_prod_smith [Fintype ι] (b : Basis ι R S) {f : S} (hf : f ≠ 0) : Associated (Algebra.norm R f) (∏ i, smithCoeffs b _ (span_singleton_eq_bot.not.2 hf) i)

views.nl_informal:
For a nonzero element `f` in a `F[X]`-module `S`, the dimension of $S/\langle f \rangle$ as an
`F`-vector space is the degree of the norm of `f` relative to `F[X]`.
views.lean_signature: theorem finrank_quotient_span_eq_natDegree_norm [Algebra F S] [IsScalarTower F F[X] S] (b : Basis ι F[X] S) {f : S} (hf : f ≠ 0) : Module.finrank F (S ⧸ span ({f} : Set S)) = (Algebra.norm F[X] f).natDegree

views.nl_informal:
The induction hypothesis of `Submodule.basisOfPid` and `Submodule.smithNormalForm`.

Basically, it says: let `N ≤ M` be a pair of submodules, then we can find a pair of
submodules `N' ≤ M'` of strictly smaller rank, whose basis we can extend to get a basis
of `N` and `M`. Moreover, if the basis for `M'` is up to scalars a basis for `N'`,
then the basis we find for `M` is up to scalars a basis for `N`.

For `basis_of_pid` we only need the first half and can fix `M = ⊤`,
for `smith_normal_form` we need the full statement,
but must also feed in a basis for `M` using `basis_of_pid` to keep the induction going.
views.lean_signature: theorem Submodule.basis_of_pid_aux [Finite ι] {O : Type*} [AddCommGroup O] [Module R O] (M N : Submodule R O) (b'M : Basis ι R M) (N_bot : N ≠ ⊥) (N_le_M : N ≤ M) : ∃ y ∈ M, ∃ a : R, a • y ∈ N ∧ ∃ M' ≤ M, ∃ N' ≤ N, N' ≤ M' ∧ (∀ (c : R) (z : O), z ∈ M' → c • y + z = 0 → c = 0) ∧ (∀ (c : R) (z : O), z ∈ N' → c • a • y + z = 0 → c = 0) ∧ ∀ (n') (bN' : Basis (Fin n') R N'), ∃ bN : Basis (Fin (n' + 1)) R N, ∀ (m') (hn'm' : n' ≤ m') (bM' : Basis (Fin m') R M'), ∃ (hnm : n' + 1 ≤ m' + 1) (bM : Basis (Fin (m' + 1)) R M), ∀ as : Fin n' → R, (∀ i : Fin n', (bN' i : O) = as i • (bM' (Fin.castLE hn'm' i) : O)) → ∃ as' : Fin (n' + 1) → R, ∀ i : Fin (n' + 1), (bN i : O) = as' i • (bM (Fin.castLE hnm i) : O)

views.nl_informal:
A submodule of a free `R`-module of finite rank is also a free `R`-module of finite rank,
if `R` is a principal ideal domain.

This is a `lemma` to make the induction a bit easier. To actually access the basis,
see `Submodule.basisOfPid`.

See also the stronger version `Submodule.smithNormalForm`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Submodule.nonempty_basis_of_pid {ι : Type*} [Finite ι] (b : Basis ι R M) (N : Submodule R M) : ∃ n : ℕ, Nonempty (Basis (Fin n) R N)

views.nl_informal:
Given a Smith-normal-form pair of bases for `N ⊆ M`, and a linear endomorphism `f` of `M`
that preserves `N`, the diagonal of the matrix of the restriction `f` to `N` does not depend on
which of the two bases for `N` is used.
views.lean_signature: theorem Basis.SmithNormalForm.toMatrix_restrict_eq_toMatrix [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (f : M →ₗ[R] M) (hf : ∀ x, f x ∈ N) (hf' : ∀ x ∈ N, f x ∈ N := fun x _ ↦ hf x) {i : Fin n} : LinearMap.toMatrix snf.bN snf.bN (LinearMap.restrict f hf') i i = LinearMap.toMatrix snf.bM snf.bM f (snf.f i) (snf.f i)

views.nl_informal:
If `M` is finite free over a PID `R`, then any submodule `N` is free
and we can find a basis for `M` and `N` such that the inclusion map is a diagonal matrix
in Smith normal form.

See `Submodule.smithNormalFormOfLE` for a version of this theorem that returns
a `Basis.SmithNormalForm`.

This is a strengthening of `Submodule.basisOfPidOfLE`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Submodule.exists_smith_normal_form_of_le [Finite ι] (b : Basis ι R M) (N O : Submodule R M) (N_le_O : N ≤ O) : ∃ (n o : ℕ) (hno : n ≤ o) (bO : Basis (Fin o) R O) (bN : Basis (Fin n) R N) (a : Fin n → R), ∀ i, (bN i : M) = a i • bO (Fin.castLE hno i)

views.nl_informal:
If `M` is finite free over a PID `R`, then for any submodule `N` of the same rank,
we can find basis for `M` and `N` with the same indexing such that the inclusion map
is a square diagonal matrix.

See also `Submodule.smithNormalFormOfRankEq` for a version of this theorem that returns
a `Basis.SmithNormalForm`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Submodule.exists_smith_normal_form_of_rank_eq (b : Basis ι R M) (h : Module.finrank R N = Module.finrank R M) : ∃ (b' : Basis ι R M) (a : ι → R) (ab' : Basis ι R N), ∀ i, (ab' i : M) = a i • b' i

views.nl_informal:
If `S` a finite-dimensional ring extension of a PID `R` which is free as an `R`-module,
then any nonzero `S`-ideal `I` is free as an `R`-submodule of `S`, and we can
find a basis for `S` and `I` such that the inclusion map is a square diagonal
matrix.

See also `Ideal.smithNormalForm` for a version of this theorem that returns
a `Basis.SmithNormalForm`.

The definitions `Ideal.ringBasis`, `Ideal.selfBasis`, `Ideal.smithCoeffs` are (noncomputable)
choices of values for this existential quantifier.
views.lean_signature: theorem Ideal.exists_smith_normal_form (b : Basis ι R S) (I : Ideal S) (hI : I ≠ ⊥) : ∃ (b' : Basis ι R S) (a : ι → R) (ab' : Basis ι R I), ∀ i, (ab' i : S) = a i • b' i

views.nl_informal: A free module with a basis indexed by a `Fintype` is finite.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.Finite.of_basis {R M ι : Type*} [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [_root_.Finite ι] (b : Basis ι R M) : Module.Finite R M

views.nl_informal:
Let `e : M ≃ N` be an additive isomorphism (therefore a `ℤ`-linear equiv).
Then an alternative way to compute the cardinality of the quotient `M ⧸ N` is given by taking
the determinant of `e`.
See `natAbs_det_basis_change` for a more familiar formulation of this result.
views.lean_signature: theorem Submodule.natAbs_det_equiv (N : Submodule ℤ M) {E : Type*} [EquivLike E M N] [AddEquivClass E M N] (e : E) : Int.natAbs (LinearMap.det (N.subtype ∘ₗ AddMonoidHom.toIntLinearMap (e : M →+ N))) = Nat.card (M ⧸ N)

views.nl_informal:
Let `b` be a basis for `M` over `ℤ` and `bN` a basis for `N` over `ℤ` of the same dimension.
Then an alternative way to compute the cardinality of `M ⧸ N` is given by taking the determinant
of `bN` over `b`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Submodule.natAbs_det_basis_change {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (b : Basis ι ℤ M) (N : Submodule ℤ M) (bN : Basis ι ℤ N) : (b.det ((↑) ∘ bN)).natAbs = Nat.card (M ⧸ N)

views.nl_informal: The finrank of `M →ₗ[R] N` as an `S`-module is `(finrank R M) * (finrank S N)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.finrank_linearMap : finrank S (M →ₗ[R] N) = finrank R M * finrank S N

views.nl_informal:
A submodule of full rank of a free finite `ℤ`-module has a finite quotient.
It can't be an instance because of the side condition `Module.finrank ℤ N = Module.finrank ℤ M`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Submodule.finiteQuotientOfFreeOfRankEq [Module.Free ℤ M] [Module.Finite ℤ M] (N : Submodule ℤ M) (h : Module.finrank ℤ N = Module.finrank ℤ M) : Finite (M ⧸ N)

views.nl_informal: The injection into the free product of any `1 : A i` is the 1 of the free product.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearAlgebra.FreeProduct.identify_one (i : I) : ι' R A (DirectSum.lof R I A i 1) = 1

views.nl_informal:
Multiplication in the free product of the injections of any two `aᵢ aᵢ': A i` for
the same `i` is just the injection of multiplication `aᵢ * aᵢ'` in `A i`.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearAlgebra.FreeProduct.mul_injections (a₁ a₂ : A i) : ι' R A (DirectSum.lof R I A i a₁) * ι' R A (DirectSum.lof R I A i a₂) = ι' R A (DirectSum.lof R I A i (a₁ * a₂))

views.nl_informal: `lof R A i 1 = 1` for all `i`.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearAlgebra.FreeProduct.lof_map_one (i : I) : lof R A i 1 = 1

views.nl_informal:
Universal property of the free product of algebras, property:
for every `R`-algebra `B`, every family of maps `maps : (i : I) → (A i →ₐ[R] B)` lifts
to a unique arrow `π` from `FreeProduct R A` such that  `π ∘ ι i = maps i`.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearAlgebra.FreeProduct.lift_comp_ι : (lift R A maps) ∘ₐ (ι R A i) = maps

views.nl_informal:
A set of linearly independent vectors in a module `M` over a semiring `K` is also linearly
independent over a subring `R` of `K`.

See also `LinearIndependent.restrict_scalars'` for a version with more convenient typeclass
assumptions.

TODO : `LinearIndepOn` version.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearIndependent.restrict_scalars [Semiring K] [SMulWithZero R K] [Module K M] [IsScalarTower R K M] (hinj : Injective fun r : R ↦ r • (1 : K)) (li : LinearIndependent K v) : LinearIndependent R v

views.nl_informal:
If `v` is an injective family of vectors such that `f ∘ v` is linearly independent, then `v`
    spans a submodule disjoint from the kernel of `f`.
TODO : `LinearIndepOn` version.
views.lean_signature: theorem Submodule.range_ker_disjoint {f : M →ₗ[R] M'} (hv : LinearIndependent R (f ∘ v)) : Disjoint (span R (range v)) (LinearMap.ker f)

views.nl_informal:
If `M / R` and `M' / R'` are modules, `i : R' → R` is a map, `j : M →+ M'` is a monoid map,
such that they are both injective, and compatible with the scalar
multiplications on `M` and `M'`, then `j` sends linearly independent families of vectors to
linearly independent families of vectors. As a special case, taking `R = R'`
it is `LinearIndependent.map_injOn`.
TODO : `LinearIndepOn` version.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearIndependent.map_of_injective_injectiveₛ {R' M' : Type*} [Semiring R'] [AddCommMonoid M'] [Module R' M'] (hv : LinearIndependent R v) (i : R' → R) (j : M →+ M') (hi : Injective i) (hj : Injective j) (hc : ∀ (r : R') (m : M), j (i r • m) = r • j m) : LinearIndependent R' (j ∘ v)

views.nl_informal:
If `M / R` and `M' / R'` are modules, `i : R → R'` is a surjective map,
and `j : M →+ M'` is an injective monoid map, such that the scalar multiplications
on `M` and `M'` are compatible, then `j` sends linearly independent families
of vectors to linearly independent families of vectors. As a special case, taking `R = R'`
it is `LinearIndependent.map_injOn`.
TODO : `LinearIndepOn` version.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearIndependent.map_of_surjective_injectiveₛ {R' M' : Type*} [Semiring R'] [AddCommMonoid M'] [Module R' M'] (hv : LinearIndependent R v) (i : R → R') (j : M →+ M') (hi : Surjective i) (hj : Injective j) (hc : ∀ (r : R) (m : M), j (r • m) = i r • j m) : LinearIndependent R' (j ∘ v)

views.nl_informal:
If a linear map is injective on the span of a family of linearly independent vectors, then
the family stays linearly independent after composing with the linear map.
See `LinearIndependent.map` for the version with `Set.InjOn` replaced by `Disjoint`
when working over a ring.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearIndependent.map_injOn (hv : LinearIndependent R v) (f : M →ₗ[R] M') (hf_inj : Set.InjOn f (span R (Set.range v))) : LinearIndependent R (f ∘ v)

views.nl_informal: Every finite subset of a linearly independent set is linearly independent.
views.lean_signature: theorem linearIndependent_finset_map_embedding_subtype (s : Set M) (li : LinearIndependent R ((↑) : s → M)) (t : Finset s) : LinearIndependent R ((↑) : Finset.map (Embedding.subtype s) t → M)

views.nl_informal: Linear independent families are injective, even if you multiply either side.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearIndependent.eq_of_smul_apply_eq_smul_apply {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] {v : ι → M} (li : LinearIndependent R v) (c d : R) (i j : ι) (hc : c ≠ 0) (h : c • v i = d • v j) : i = j

views.nl_informal: If `∑ i, f i • v i = ∑ i, g i • v i`, then for all `i`, `f i = g i`.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearIndependent.eq_coords_of_eq [Fintype ι] {v : ι → M} (hv : LinearIndependent R v) {f : ι → R} {g : ι → R} (heq : ∑ i, f i • v i = ∑ i, g i • v i) (i : ι) : f i = g i

views.nl_informal:
If `v` is a linearly independent family of vectors and the kernel of a linear map `f` is
disjoint with the submodule spanned by the vectors of `v`, then `f ∘ v` is a linearly independent
family of vectors. See also `LinearIndependent.map'` for a special case assuming `ker f = ⊥`.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearIndependent.map (hv : LinearIndependent R v) {f : M →ₗ[R] M'} (hf_inj : Disjoint (span R (range v)) (LinearMap.ker f)) : LinearIndependent R (f ∘ v)

views.nl_informal:
An injective linear map sends linearly independent families of vectors to linearly independent
families of vectors. See also `LinearIndependent.map` for a more general statement.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearIndependent.map' (hv : LinearIndependent R v) (f : M →ₗ[R] M') (hf_inj : LinearMap.ker f = ⊥) : LinearIndependent R (f ∘ v)

views.nl_informal:
If `M / R` and `M' / R'` are modules, `i : R' → R` is a map, `j : M →+ M'` is a monoid map,
such that they send non-zero elements to non-zero elements, and compatible with the scalar
multiplications on `M` and `M'`, then `j` sends linearly independent families of vectors to
linearly independent families of vectors. As a special case, taking `R = R'`
it is `LinearIndependent.map'`.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearIndependent.map_of_injective_injective {R' M' : Type*} [Ring R'] [AddCommGroup M'] [Module R' M'] (hv : LinearIndependent R v) (i : R' → R) (j : M →+ M') (hi : ∀ r, i r = 0 → r = 0) (hj : ∀ m, j m = 0 → m = 0) (hc : ∀ (r : R') (m : M), j (i r • m) = r • j m) : LinearIndependent R' (j ∘ v)

views.nl_informal:
If `M / R` and `M' / R'` are modules, `i : R → R'` is a surjective map which maps zero to zero,
`j : M →+ M'` is a monoid map which sends non-zero elements to non-zero elements, such that the
scalar multiplications on `M` and `M'` are compatible, then `j` sends linearly independent families
of vectors to linearly independent families of vectors. As a special case, taking `R = R'`
it is `LinearIndependent.map'`.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearIndependent.map_of_surjective_injective {R' M' : Type*} [Semiring R'] [AddCommMonoid M'] [Module R' M'] (hv : LinearIndependent R v) (i : R → R') (j : M →+ M') (hi : Surjective i) (hj : ∀ m, j m = 0 → m = 0) (hc : ∀ (r : R) (m : M), j (r • m) = i r • j m) : LinearIndependent R' (j ∘ v)

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is an injective linear map, then the family `f ∘ v` is linearly independent
if and only if the family `v` is linearly independent.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.linearIndependent_iff (f : M →ₗ[R] M') (hf_inj : LinearMap.ker f = ⊥) : LinearIndependent R (f ∘ v) ↔ LinearIndependent R v

views.nl_informal: Dedekind's linear independence of characters
views.lean_signature: theorem linearIndependent_monoidHom (G : Type*) [MulOneClass G] (L : Type*) [CommRing L] [NoZeroDivisors L] : LinearIndependent L (M := G → L) (fun f => f : (G →* L) → G → L)

views.nl_informal:
A subfamily of a linearly independent family (i.e., a composition with an injective map) is a
linearly independent family.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearIndependent.comp (h : LinearIndependent R v) (f : ι' → ι) (hf : Injective f) : LinearIndependent R (v ∘ f)

views.nl_informal:
A family is linearly independent if and only if all of its finite subfamily is
linearly independent.
views.lean_signature: theorem linearIndependent_iff_finset_linearIndependent : LinearIndependent R v ↔ ∀ (s : Finset ι), LinearIndependent R (v ∘ (Subtype.val : s → ι))

views.nl_informal:
If the image of a family of vectors under a linear map is linearly independent, then so is
the original family.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearIndependent.of_comp (f : M →ₗ[R] M') (hfv : LinearIndependent R (f ∘ v)) : LinearIndependent R v

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is a linear map injective on the span of the range of `v`, then the family `f ∘ v`
is linearly independent if and only if the family `v` is linearly independent.
See `LinearMap.linearIndependent_iff_of_disjoint` for the version with `Set.InjOn` replaced
by `Disjoint` when working over a ring.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.linearIndependent_iff_of_injOn (f : M →ₗ[R] M') (hf_inj : Set.InjOn f (span R (Set.range v))) : LinearIndependent R (f ∘ v) ↔ LinearIndependent R v

views.nl_informal:
An indexed set of vectors is linearly dependent iff there are two distinct
`Finsupp.LinearCombination`s of the vectors with the same value.
views.lean_signature: theorem linearDepOn_iff'ₛ : ¬LinearIndepOn R v s ↔ ∃ f g : ι →₀ R, f ∈ Finsupp.supported R R s ∧ g ∈ Finsupp.supported R R s ∧ Finsupp.linearCombination R v f = Finsupp.linearCombination R v g ∧ f ≠ g

views.nl_informal:
An alternative characterization of a maximal linearly independent family,
quantifying over types (in the same universe as `M`) into which the indexing family injects.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearIndependent.maximal_iff {ι : Type w} {R : Type u} [Semiring R] [Nontrivial R] {M : Type v} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] {v : ι → M} (i : LinearIndependent R v) : i.Maximal ↔ ∀ (κ : Type v) (w : κ → M) (_i' : LinearIndependent R w) (j : ι → κ) (_h : w ∘ j = v), Surjective j

views.nl_informal:
If the kernel of a linear map is disjoint from the span of a family of vectors,
then the family is linearly independent iff it is linearly independent after composing with
the linear map.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.linearIndependent_iff_of_disjoint (f : M →ₗ[R] M') (hf_inj : Disjoint (span R (Set.range v)) (LinearMap.ker f)) : LinearIndependent R (f ∘ v) ↔ LinearIndependent R v

views.nl_informal:
An indexed set of vectors is linearly dependent iff there is a nontrivial
`Finsupp.linearCombination` of the vectors that is zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem linearDepOn_iff' : ¬LinearIndepOn R v s ↔ ∃ f : ι →₀ R, f ∈ Finsupp.supported R R s ∧ Finsupp.linearCombination R v f = 0 ∧ f ≠ 0

views.nl_informal:
A finite family of vectors `v i` is linear independent iff the linear map that sends
`c : ι → R` to `∑ i, c i • v i` is injective.
views.lean_signature: theorem Fintype.linearIndependent_iff'ₛ [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] : LinearIndependent R v ↔ Injective (LinearMap.lsum R (fun _ ↦ R) ℕ fun i ↦ LinearMap.id.smulRight (v i))

views.nl_informal:
A finite family of vectors `v i` is linear independent iff the linear map that sends
`c : ι → R` to `∑ i, c i • v i` has the trivial kernel.
views.lean_signature: theorem Fintype.linearIndependent_iff' [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] : LinearIndependent R v ↔ LinearMap.ker (LinearMap.lsum R (fun _ ↦ R) ℕ fun i ↦ LinearMap.id.smulRight (v i)) = ⊥

views.nl_informal: Use linearity of `cramer` to take it out of a summation.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.sum_cramer {β} (s : Finset β) (f : β → n → α) : (∑ x ∈ s, cramer A (f x)) = cramer A (∑ x ∈ s, f x)

views.nl_informal: Use linearity of `cramer` and vector evaluation to take `cramer A _ i` out of a summation.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.sum_cramer_apply {β} (s : Finset β) (f : n → β → α) (i : n) : (∑ x ∈ s, cramer A (fun j => f j x) i) = cramer A (fun j : n => ∑ x ∈ s, f j x) i

views.nl_informal:
Since the map `b ↦ cramer A b` is linear in `b`, it must be multiplication by some matrix. This
matrix is `A.adjugate`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.cramer_eq_adjugate_mulVec (A : Matrix n n α) (b : n → α) : cramer A b = A.adjugate *ᵥ b

views.nl_informal:
A stronger form of **Cramer's rule** that allows us to solve some instances of `A * x = b` even
if the determinant is not a unit. A sufficient (but still not necessary) condition is that `A.det`
divides `b`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.mulVec_cramer (A : Matrix n n α) (b : n → α) : A *ᵥ cramer A b = A.det • b

views.nl_informal: The basis constructed by `unitsSMul` has vectors given by a diagonal matrix.

views.nl_informal:

* It wouldn't work for 0×0 matrices.
* More things are true about diagonal matrices than constant matrices, and so more lemmas exist.

The **Matrix determinant lemma**

A vector with coprime entries, left-multiplied by a matrix in `SL(2, R)`, has

the `i`-th row.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.updateRow_eq_transvection [Finite n] (c : R) : updateRow (1 : Matrix n n R) i ((1 : Matrix n n R) i + c • (1 : Matrix n n R) j) = transvection i j c

views.nl_informal: Multiplying by some of the matrices in `listTransvecCol M` does not change the last row.

There exist two lists of `TransvectionStruct` such that multiplying by them on the left and
on the right makes a matrix block-diagonal.

views.nl_informal:
Inductive step for the reduction: if one knows that any size `r` matrix can be reduced to
diagonal form by elementary operations, then one deduces it for matrices over `Fin r ⊕ Unit`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.Pivot.exists_list_transvec_mul_mul_list_transvec_eq_diagonal_induction (IH : ∀ M : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) 𝕜, ∃ (L₀ L₀' : List (TransvectionStruct (Fin r) 𝕜)) (D₀ : Fin r → 𝕜), (L₀.map toMatrix).prod * M * (L₀'.map toMatrix).prod = diagonal D₀) (M : Matrix (Fin r ⊕ Unit) (Fin r ⊕ Unit) 𝕜) : ∃ (L L' : List (TransvectionStruct (Fin r ⊕ Unit) 𝕜)) (D : Fin r ⊕ Unit → 𝕜), (L.map toMatrix).prod * M * (L'.map toMatrix).prod = diagonal D

views.nl_informal:
Any matrix can be reduced to diagonal form by elementary operations. Formulated here on `Type 0`
because we will make an induction using `Fin r`.
See `exists_list_transvec_mul_mul_list_transvec_eq_diagonal` for the general version (which follows
from this one and reindexing).

views.nl_informal: Any matrix can be reduced to diagonal form by elementary operations.

Any matrix can be written as the product of transvections, a diagonal matrix, and

views.nl_informal:
Induction principle for matrices based on transvections: if a property is true for all diagonal
matrices, all transvections, and is stable under product, then it is true for all matrices. This is
the useful way to say that matrices are generated by diagonal matrices and transvections.

We state a slightly more general version: to prove a property for a matrix `M`, it suffices to
assume that the diagonal matrices we consider have the same determinant as `M`. This is useful to
obtain similar principles for `SLₙ` or `GLₙ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.diagonal_transvection_induction (P : Matrix n n 𝕜 → Prop) (M : Matrix n n 𝕜) (hdiag : ∀ D : n → 𝕜, det (diagonal D) = det M → P (diagonal D)) (htransvec : ∀ t : TransvectionStruct n 𝕜, P t.toMatrix) (hmul : ∀ A B, P A → P B → P (A * B)) : P M

views.nl_informal:
Induction principle for invertible matrices based on transvections: if a property is true for
all invertible diagonal matrices, all transvections, and is stable under product of invertible
matrices, then it is true for all invertible matrices. This is the useful way to say that
invertible matrices are generated by invertible diagonal matrices and transvections.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.diagonal_transvection_induction_of_det_ne_zero (P : Matrix n n 𝕜 → Prop) (M : Matrix n n 𝕜) (hMdet : det M ≠ 0) (hdiag : ∀ D : n → 𝕜, det (diagonal D) ≠ 0 → P (diagonal D)) (htransvec : ∀ t : TransvectionStruct n 𝕜, P t.toMatrix) (hmul : ∀ A B, det A ≠ 0 → det B ≠ 0 → P A → P B → P (A * B)) : P M

views.nl_informal:
The **Cayley-Hamilton Theorem**, that the characteristic polynomial of a matrix,
applied to the matrix itself, is zero.

This holds over any commutative ring.

See `LinearMap.aeval_self_charpoly` for the equivalent statement about endomorphisms.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.aeval_self_charpoly (M : Matrix n n R) : aeval M M.charpoly = 0

views.nl_informal: The derivative of `det (1 + M X)` at `0` is the trace of `M`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.derivative_det_one_add_X_smul (M : Matrix n n R) : (derivative <| det (1 + (X : R[X]) • M.map C)).eval 0 = trace M

views.nl_informal: The first two terms of the taylor expansion of `det (1 + r • M)` at `r = 0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.det_one_add_smul (r : R) (M : Matrix n n R) : det (1 + r • M) = 1 + trace M * r + (det (1 + (X : R[X]) • M.map C)).divX.divX.eval r * r ^ 2

views.nl_informal:
Any matrix polynomial `p` is equivalent under evaluation to `p %ₘ M.charpoly`; that is, `p`
is equivalent to a polynomial with degree less than the dimension of the matrix.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.aeval_eq_aeval_mod_charpoly (M : Matrix n n R) (p : R[X]) : aeval M p = aeval M (p %ₘ M.charpoly)

views.nl_informal:
Any matrix power can be computed as the sum of matrix powers less than `Fintype.card n`.

TODO: add the statement for negative powers phrased with `zpow`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.pow_eq_aeval_mod_charpoly (M : Matrix n n R) (k : ℕ) : M ^ k = aeval M (X ^ k %ₘ M.charpoly)

views.nl_informal:
The **Cayley-Hamilton Theorem** for f.g. modules over arbitrary rings states that for each
`R`-endomorphism `φ` of an `R`-module `M` such that `φ(M) ≤ I • M` for some ideal `I`, there
exists some `n` and some `aᵢ ∈ Iⁱ` such that `φⁿ + a₁ φⁿ⁻¹ + ⋯ + aₙ = 0`.

This is the version found in Eisenbud 4.3, which is slightly weaker than Matsumura 2.1
(this lacks the constraint on `n`), and is slightly stronger than Atiyah-Macdonald 2.4.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.exists_monic_and_coeff_mem_pow_and_aeval_eq_zero_of_range_le_smul [Module.Finite R M] (f : Module.End R M) (I : Ideal R) (hI : LinearMap.range f ≤ I • ⊤) : ∃ p : R[X], p.Monic ∧ (∀ k, p.coeff k ∈ I ^ (p.natDegree - k)) ∧ Polynomial.aeval f p = 0

views.nl_informal:
The characteristic polynomial of the map `fun x => a * x` is the minimal polynomial of `a`.

In combination with `det_eq_sign_charpoly_coeff` or `trace_eq_neg_charpoly_coeff`
and a bit of rewriting, this will allow us to conclude the
field norm resp. trace of `x` is the product resp. sum of `x`'s conjugates.
views.lean_signature: theorem charpoly_leftMulMatrix {S : Type*} [Ring S] [Algebra R S] (h : PowerBasis R S) : (leftMulMatrix h.basis h.gen).charpoly = minpoly R h.gen

views.nl_informal:
If `n` has only one element, the determinant of an `n` by `n` matrix is just that element.
