not be syntactically equal. Thus, we need to fill in the args explicitly.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.det_unique {n : Type*} [Unique n] [DecidableEq n] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n R) : det A = A default default

views.nl_informal: On square matrices, `mul_comm` applies under `det`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.det_mul_comm (M N : Matrix m m R) : det (M * N) = det (N * M)

views.nl_informal: On square matrices, `mul_left_comm` applies under `det`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.det_mul_left_comm (M N P : Matrix m m R) : det (M * (N * P)) = det (N * (M * P))

views.nl_informal: On square matrices, `mul_right_comm` applies under `det`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.det_mul_right_comm (M N P : Matrix m m R) : det (M * N * P) = det (M * P * N)

views.nl_informal: Transposing a matrix preserves the determinant.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.det_transpose (M : Matrix n n R) : Mᵀ.det = M.det

views.nl_informal: Permuting the columns changes the sign of the determinant.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.det_permute (σ : Perm n) (M : Matrix n n R) : (M.submatrix σ id).det = Perm.sign σ * M.det

views.nl_informal: Permuting the rows changes the sign of the determinant.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.det_permute' (σ : Perm n) (M : Matrix n n R) : (M.submatrix id σ).det = Perm.sign σ * M.det

views.nl_informal: Permuting rows and columns with the same equivalence does not change the determinant.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.det_submatrix_equiv_self (e : n ≃ m) (A : Matrix m m R) : det (A.submatrix e e) = det A

views.nl_informal:
Permuting rows and columns with two equivalences does not change the absolute value of the
determinant.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.abs_det_submatrix_equiv_equiv {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [LinearOrder R] [IsStrictOrderedRing R] (e₁ e₂ : n ≃ m) (A : Matrix m m R) : |(A.submatrix e₁ e₂).det| = |A.det|

views.nl_informal:
Reindexing both indices along the same equivalence preserves the determinant.

For the `simp` version of this lemma, see `det_submatrix_equiv_self`; this one is unsuitable because
`Matrix.reindex_apply` unfolds `reindex` first.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.det_reindex_self (e : m ≃ n) (A : Matrix m m R) : det (reindex e e A) = det A
theorem Matrix.abs_det_reindex {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [LinearOrder R] [IsStrictOrderedRing R] (e₁ e₂ : m ≃ n) (A : Matrix m m R) : |det (reindex e₁ e₂ A)| = |det A|

views.nl_informal:
Multiplying each row by a fixed `v i` multiplies the determinant by
the product of the `v`s.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.det_mul_row (v : n → R) (A : Matrix n n R) : det (of fun i j => v j * A i j) = (∏ i, v i) * det A

views.nl_informal:
Multiplying each column by a fixed `v j` multiplies the determinant by
the product of the `v`s.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.det_mul_column (v : n → R) (A : Matrix n n R) : det (of fun i j => v i * A i j) = (∏ i, v i) * det A

views.nl_informal: If a matrix has a repeated row, the determinant will be zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.det_zero_of_row_eq (i_ne_j : i ≠ j) (hij : M i = M j) : M.det = 0

views.nl_informal: If a matrix has a repeated column, the determinant will be zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.det_zero_of_column_eq (i_ne_j : i ≠ j) (hij : ∀ k, M k i = M k j) : M.det = 0

views.nl_informal: If we repeat a row of a matrix, we get a matrix of determinant zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.det_updateRow_eq_zero (h : i ≠ j) : (M.updateRow j (M i)).det = 0

views.nl_informal: If we repeat a column of a matrix, we get a matrix of determinant zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.det_updateCol_eq_zero (h : i ≠ j) : (M.updateCol j (fun k ↦ M k i)).det = 0

views.nl_informal:
If we replace a row of a matrix by a linear combination of its rows, then the determinant is
multiplied by the coefficient of that row.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.det_updateRow_sum (A : Matrix n n R) (j : n) (c : n → R) : (A.updateRow j (∑ k, (c k) • A k)).det = (c j) • A.det

views.nl_informal:
If we replace a column of a matrix by a linear combination of its columns, then the determinant
is multiplied by the coefficient of that column.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.det_updateCol_sum (A : Matrix n n R) (j : n) (c : n → R) : (A.updateCol j (fun k ↦ ∑ i, (c i) • A k i)).det = (c j) • A.det

views.nl_informal: If you add multiples of row `B k` to other rows, the determinant doesn't change.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.det_eq_of_forall_row_eq_smul_add_const {A B : Matrix n n R} (c : n → R) (k : n) (hk : c k = 0) (A_eq : ∀ i j, A i j = B i j + c i * B k j) : det A = det B

views.nl_informal: If you add multiples of previous rows to the next row, the determinant doesn't change.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.det_eq_of_forall_row_eq_smul_add_pred {n : ℕ} {A B : Matrix (Fin (n + 1)) (Fin (n + 1)) R} (c : Fin n → R) (A_zero : ∀ j, A 0 j = B 0 j) (A_succ : ∀ (i : Fin n) (j), A i.succ j = B i.succ j + c i * A (Fin.castSucc i) j) : det A = det B

views.nl_informal: If you add multiples of previous columns to the next columns, the determinant doesn't change.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.det_eq_of_forall_col_eq_smul_add_pred {n : ℕ} {A B : Matrix (Fin (n + 1)) (Fin (n + 1)) R} (c : Fin n → R) (A_zero : ∀ i, A i 0 = B i 0) (A_succ : ∀ (i) (j : Fin n), A i j.succ = B i j.succ + c j * A i (Fin.castSucc j)) : det A = det B

views.nl_informal:
The determinant of a 2×2 block matrix with the lower-left block equal to zero is the product of
the determinants of the diagonal blocks. For the generalization to any number of blocks, see
`Matrix.det_of_upperTriangular`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.det_fromBlocks_zero₂₁ (A : Matrix m m R) (B : Matrix m n R) (D : Matrix n n R) : (Matrix.fromBlocks A B 0 D).det = A.det * D.det

views.nl_informal:
The determinant of a 2×2 block matrix with the upper-right block equal to zero is the product of
the determinants of the diagonal blocks. For the generalization to any number of blocks, see
`Matrix.det_of_lowerTriangular`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.det_fromBlocks_zero₁₂ (A : Matrix m m R) (C : Matrix n m R) (D : Matrix n n R) : (Matrix.fromBlocks A 0 C D).det = A.det * D.det

views.nl_informal: Laplacian expansion of the determinant of an `n+1 × n+1` matrix along column 0.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.det_succ_column_zero {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin n.succ) (Fin n.succ) R) : det A = ∑ i : Fin n.succ, (-1) ^ (i : ℕ) * A i 0 * det (A.submatrix i.succAbove Fin.succ)

views.nl_informal: Laplacian expansion of the determinant of an `n+1 × n+1` matrix along row 0.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.det_succ_row_zero {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin n.succ) (Fin n.succ) R) : det A = ∑ j : Fin n.succ, (-1) ^ (j : ℕ) * A 0 j * det (A.submatrix Fin.succ j.succAbove)

views.nl_informal: Laplacian expansion of the determinant of an `n+1 × n+1` matrix along row `i`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.det_succ_row {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin n.succ) (Fin n.succ) R) (i : Fin n.succ) : det A = ∑ j : Fin n.succ, (-1) ^ (i + j : ℕ) * A i j * det (A.submatrix i.succAbove j.succAbove)

views.nl_informal: Laplacian expansion of the determinant of an `n+1 × n+1` matrix along column `j`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.det_succ_column {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin n.succ) (Fin n.succ) R) (j : Fin n.succ) : det A = ∑ i : Fin n.succ, (-1) ^ (i + j : ℕ) * A i j * det (A.submatrix i.succAbove j.succAbove)

views.nl_informal: Determinant of 0x0 matrix
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.det_fin_zero {A : Matrix (Fin 0) (Fin 0) R} : det A = 1

views.nl_informal: Determinant of 1x1 matrix
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.det_fin_one (A : Matrix (Fin 1) (Fin 1) R) : det A = A 0 0

views.nl_informal: Determinant of 2x2 matrix
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.det_fin_two (A : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) R) : det A = A 0 0 * A 1 1 - A 0 1 * A 1 0

views.nl_informal: Determinant of 3x3 matrix
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.det_fin_three (A : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) R) : det A = A 0 0 * A 1 1 * A 2 2 - A 0 0 * A 1 2 * A 2 1 - A 0 1 * A 1 0 * A 2 2 + A 0 1 * A 1 2 * A 2 0 + A 0 2 * A 1 0 * A 2 1 - A 0 2 * A 1 1 * A 2 0

views.nl_informal:
Let `M` be a `(n+1) × n` matrix whose row sums to zero. Then all the matrices obtained by
deleting one row have the same determinant up to a sign.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.submatrix_succAbove_det_eq_negOnePow_submatrix_succAbove_det {n : ℕ} (M : Matrix (Fin (n + 1)) (Fin n) R) (hv : ∑ j, M j = 0) (j₁ j₂ : Fin (n + 1)) : (M.submatrix (Fin.succAbove j₁) id).det = Int.negOnePow (j₁ - j₂) • (M.submatrix (Fin.succAbove j₂) id).det

views.nl_informal:
Let `M` be a `(n+1) × n` matrix whose column sums to zero. Then all the matrices obtained by
deleting one column have the same determinant up to a sign.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.submatrix_succAbove_det_eq_negOnePow_submatrix_succAbove_det' {n : ℕ} (M : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin (n + 1)) R) (hv : ∀ i, ∑ j, M i j = 0) (j₁ j₂ : Fin (n + 1)) : (M.submatrix id (Fin.succAbove j₁)).det = Int.negOnePow (j₁ - j₂) • (M.submatrix id (Fin.succAbove j₂)).det

views.nl_informal:
Let `M` be a `(n+1) × (n+1)` matrix. Assume that all columns, but the `j₀`-column, sums to zero.
Then its determinant is, up to sign, the sum of the `j₀`-column times the determinant of the
matrix obtained by deleting any row and the `j₀`-column.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.det_eq_sum_column_mul_submatrix_succAbove_succAbove_det {n : ℕ} (M : Matrix (Fin (n + 1)) (Fin (n + 1)) R) (i₀ j₀ : Fin (n + 1)) (hv : ∀ j ≠ j₀, ∑ i, M i j = 0) : M.det = (-1) ^ (i₀ + j₀ : ℕ) * (∑ i, M i j₀) * (M.submatrix (Fin.succAbove i₀) (Fin.succAbove j₀)).det

views.nl_informal:
Let `M` be a `(n+1) × (n+1)` matrix. Assume that all rows, but the `i₀`-row, sums to zero.
Then its determinant is, up to sign, the sum of the `i₀`-row times the determinant of the
matrix obtained by deleting the `i₀`-row and any column.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.det_eq_sum_row_mul_submatrix_succAbove_succAbove_det {n : ℕ} (M : Matrix (Fin (n + 1)) (Fin (n + 1)) R) (i₀ j₀ : Fin (n + 1)) (hv : ∀ i ≠ i₀, ∑ j, M i j = 0) : M.det = (-1) ^ (i₀ + j₀ : ℕ) * (∑ j, M i₀ j) * (M.submatrix (Fin.succAbove i₀) (Fin.succAbove j₀)).det

views.nl_informal:
If `A` is totally unimodular and each row of `B` is all zeros except for at most a single `1` or
a single `-1` then `fromRows A B` is totally unimodular.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.IsTotallyUnimodular.fromRows_unitlike [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix m n R} {B : Matrix m' n R} (hA : A.IsTotallyUnimodular) (hB : Nonempty n → ∀ i : m', ∃ j : n, ∃ s : SignType, B i = Pi.single j s.cast) : (fromRows A B).IsTotallyUnimodular

views.nl_informal:
If `A` is totally unimodular and each row of `B` is all zeros except for at most a single `1`,
then `fromRows A B` is totally unimodular.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.fromRows_isTotallyUnimodular_iff_rows [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix m n R} {B : Matrix m' n R} (hB : Nonempty n → ∀ i : m', ∃ j : n, ∃ s : SignType, B i = Pi.single j s.cast) : (fromRows A B).IsTotallyUnimodular ↔ A.IsTotallyUnimodular

views.nl_informal:
The cardinal of the set of linearly independent vectors over a finite dimensional vector space
over a finite field.
views.lean_signature: theorem card_linearIndependent {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ n) : Nat.card { s : Fin k → V // LinearIndependent K s } = ∏ i : Fin k, (q ^ n - q ^ i.val)

views.nl_informal: The cardinal of the general linear group over a finite field.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.card_GL_field : Nat.card (GL (Fin n) 𝔽) = ∏ i : (Fin n), (q ^ n - q ^ ( i : ℕ ))

views.nl_informal:
Coercing a `Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup` via `GL_pos` and `GL` is the same as coercing straight to
a matrix.
views.lean_signature: theorem Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.coe_GLPos_coe_GL_coe_matrix (g : SpecialLinearGroup n R) : (↑(↑(↑g : GLPos n R) : GL n R) : Matrix n n R) = ↑g

views.nl_informal:
In the specific case of multilinear maps on spaces indexed by `Fin (n+1)`, where one can build
an element of `∀ (i : Fin (n+1)), M i` using `cons`, one can express directly the additivity of a
multilinear map along the first variable.
views.lean_signature: theorem MultilinearMap.cons_add (f : MultilinearMap R M M₂) (m : ∀ i : Fin n, M i.succ) (x y : M 0) : f (cons (x + y) m) = f (cons x m) + f (cons y m)

views.nl_informal:
In the specific case of multilinear maps on spaces indexed by `Fin (n+1)`, where one can build
an element of `∀ (i : Fin (n+1)), M i` using `cons`, one can express directly the multiplicativity
of a multilinear map along the first variable.
views.lean_signature: theorem MultilinearMap.cons_smul (f : MultilinearMap R M M₂) (m : ∀ i : Fin n, M i.succ) (c : R) (x : M 0) : f (cons (c • x) m) = c • f (cons x m)

views.nl_informal:
In the specific case of multilinear maps on spaces indexed by `Fin (n+1)`, where one can build
an element of `∀ (i : Fin (n+1)), M i` using `snoc`, one can express directly the additivity of a
multilinear map along the first variable.
views.lean_signature: theorem MultilinearMap.snoc_add (f : MultilinearMap R M M₂) (m : ∀ i : Fin n, M (castSucc i)) (x y : M (last n)) : f (snoc m (x + y)) = f (snoc m x) + f (snoc m y)

views.nl_informal:
In the specific case of multilinear maps on spaces indexed by `Fin (n+1)`, where one can build
an element of `∀ (i : Fin (n+1)), M i` using `cons`, one can express directly the multiplicativity
of a multilinear map along the first variable.
views.lean_signature: theorem MultilinearMap.snoc_smul (f : MultilinearMap R M M₂) (m : ∀ i : Fin n, M (castSucc i)) (c : R) (x : M (last n)) : f (snoc m (c • x)) = c • f (snoc m x)

views.nl_informal:
Composing a multilinear map twice with a linear map in each argument is
the same as composing with their composition.
views.lean_signature: theorem MultilinearMap.compLinearMap_assoc (g : MultilinearMap R M₁'' M₂) (f₁ : ∀ i, M₁' i →ₗ[R] M₁'' i) (f₂ : ∀ i, M₁ i →ₗ[R] M₁' i) : (g.compLinearMap f₁).compLinearMap f₂ = g.compLinearMap fun i => f₁ i ∘ₗ f₂ i

views.nl_informal: Composing the zero multilinear map with a linear map in each argument.
views.lean_signature: theorem MultilinearMap.zero_compLinearMap (f : ∀ i, M₁ i →ₗ[R] M₁' i) : (0 : MultilinearMap R M₁' M₂).compLinearMap f = 0

views.nl_informal: Composing a multilinear map with the identity linear map in each argument.
views.lean_signature: theorem MultilinearMap.compLinearMap_id (g : MultilinearMap R M₁' M₂) : (g.compLinearMap fun _ => LinearMap.id) = g

views.nl_informal: Composing with a family of surjective linear maps is injective.
views.lean_signature: theorem MultilinearMap.compLinearMap_injective (f : ∀ i, M₁ i →ₗ[R] M₁' i) (hf : ∀ i, Surjective (f i)) : Injective fun g : MultilinearMap R M₁' M₂ => g.compLinearMap f

views.nl_informal:
Composing a multilinear map with a linear equiv on each argument gives the zero map
if and only if the multilinear map is the zero map.
views.lean_signature: theorem MultilinearMap.comp_linearEquiv_eq_zero_iff (g : MultilinearMap R M₁' M₂) (f : ∀ i, M₁ i ≃ₗ[R] M₁' i) : (g.compLinearMap fun i => (f i : M₁ i →ₗ[R] M₁' i)) = 0 ↔ g = 0

views.nl_informal:
If one adds to a vector `m'` another vector `m`, but only for coordinates in a finset `t`, then
the image under a multilinear map `f` is the sum of `f (s.piecewise m m')` along all subsets `s` of
`t`. This is mainly an auxiliary statement to prove the result when `t = univ`, given in
`map_add_univ`, although it can be useful in its own right as it does not require the index set `ι`
to be finite.
views.lean_signature: theorem MultilinearMap.map_piecewise_add [DecidableEq ι] (m m' : ∀ i, M₁ i) (t : Finset ι) : f (t.piecewise (m + m') m') = ∑ s ∈ t.powerset, f (s.piecewise m m')

views.nl_informal:
Additivity of a multilinear map along all coordinates at the same time,
writing `f (m + m')` as the sum of `f (s.piecewise m m')` over all sets `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MultilinearMap.map_add_univ [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι] (m m' : ∀ i, M₁ i) : f (m + m') = ∑ s : Finset ι, f (s.piecewise m m')

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is multilinear, then `f (Σ_{j₁ ∈ A₁} g₁ j₁, ..., Σ_{jₙ ∈ Aₙ} gₙ jₙ)` is the sum of
`f (g₁ (r 1), ..., gₙ (r n))` where `r` ranges over all functions with `r 1 ∈ A₁`, ...,
`r n ∈ Aₙ`. This follows from multilinearity by expanding successively with respect to each
coordinate. Here, we give an auxiliary statement tailored for an inductive proof. Use instead
`map_sum_finset`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MultilinearMap.map_sum_finset_aux [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι] {n : ℕ} (h : (∑ i, #(A i)) = n) : (f fun i => ∑ j ∈ A i, g i j) = ∑ r ∈ piFinset A, f fun i => g i (r i)

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is multilinear, then `f (Σ_{j₁ ∈ A₁} g₁ j₁, ..., Σ_{jₙ ∈ Aₙ} gₙ jₙ)` is the sum of
`f (g₁ (r 1), ..., gₙ (r n))` where `r` ranges over all functions with `r 1 ∈ A₁`, ...,
`r n ∈ Aₙ`. This follows from multilinearity by expanding successively with respect to each
coordinate.
views.lean_signature: theorem MultilinearMap.map_sum_finset [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι] : (f fun i => ∑ j ∈ A i, g i j) = ∑ r ∈ piFinset A, f fun i => g i (r i)

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is multilinear, then `f (Σ_{j₁} g₁ j₁, ..., Σ_{jₙ} gₙ jₙ)` is the sum of
`f (g₁ (r 1), ..., gₙ (r n))` where `r` ranges over all functions `r`. This follows from
multilinearity by expanding successively with respect to each coordinate.
views.lean_signature: theorem MultilinearMap.map_sum [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι] [∀ i, Fintype (α i)] : (f fun i => ∑ j, g i j) = ∑ r : ∀ i, α i, f fun i => g i (r i)

views.nl_informal:
The results of applying `domDomCongr` to two maps are equal if
and only if those maps are.
views.lean_signature: theorem MultilinearMap.domDomCongr_eq_iff (σ : ι₁ ≃ ι₂) (f g : MultilinearMap R (fun _ : ι₁ => M₂) M₃) : f.domDomCongr σ = g.domDomCongr σ ↔ f = g

views.nl_informal:
If one multiplies by `c i` the coordinates in a finset `s`, then the image under a multilinear
map is multiplied by `∏ i ∈ s, c i`. This is mainly an auxiliary statement to prove the result when
`s = univ`, given in `map_smul_univ`, although it can be useful in its own right as it does not
require the index set `ι` to be finite.
views.lean_signature: theorem MultilinearMap.map_piecewise_smul [DecidableEq ι] (c : ι → R) (m : ∀ i, M₁ i) (s : Finset ι) : f (s.piecewise (fun i => c i • m i) m) = (∏ i ∈ s, c i) • f m

views.nl_informal:
Multiplicativity of a multilinear map along all coordinates at the same time,
writing `f (fun i => c i • m i)` as `(∏ i, c i) • f m`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MultilinearMap.map_smul_univ [Fintype ι] (c : ι → R) (m : ∀ i, M₁ i) : (f fun i => c i • m i) = (∏ i, c i) • f m

views.nl_informal:
This calculates the differences between the values of a multilinear map at
two arguments that differ on a finset `s` of `ι`. It requires a
linear order on `ι` in order to express the result.
views.lean_signature: theorem MultilinearMap.map_piecewise_sub_map_piecewise [LinearOrder ι] (a b v : (i : ι) → M₁ i) (s : Finset ι) : f (s.piecewise a v) - f (s.piecewise b v) = ∑ i ∈ s, f fun j ↦ if j ∈ s then if j < i then a j else if j = i then a j - b j else b j else v j

views.nl_informal:
This expresses the difference between the values of a multilinear map
at two points "close to `x`" in terms of the "derivative" of the multilinear map at `x`
and of "second-order" terms.
views.lean_signature: theorem MultilinearMap.map_add_sub_map_add_sub_linearDeriv [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι] (x h h' : (i : ι) → M₁ i) : f (x + h) - f (x + h') - f.linearDeriv x (h - h') = ∑ s with 2 ≤ #s, (f (s.piecewise h x) - f (s.piecewise h' x))

views.nl_informal: The map is always nonempty. This lemma is needed to apply `SubMulAction.zero_mem`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MultilinearMap.map_nonempty [Nonempty ι] (f : MultilinearMap R M₁ M₂) (p : ∀ i, Submodule R (M₁ i)) : (map f p : Set M₂).Nonempty

views.nl_informal:
Two multilinear maps indexed by `Fin n` are equal if they are equal when all arguments are
basis vectors.
views.lean_signature: theorem Basis.ext_multilinear_fin {f g : MultilinearMap R M M₂} {ι₁ : Fin n → Type*} (e : ∀ i, Basis (ι₁ i) R (M i)) (h : ∀ v : ∀ i, ι₁ i, (f fun i => e i (v i)) = g fun i => e i (v i)) : f = g

views.nl_informal:
Two multilinear maps indexed by a `Fintype` are equal if they are equal when all arguments
are basis vectors. Unlike `Basis.ext_multilinear_fin`, this only uses a single basis; a
dependently-typed version would still be true, but the proof would need a dependently-typed
version of `dom_dom_congr`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Basis.ext_multilinear [Finite ι] {f g : MultilinearMap R (fun _ : ι => M₂) M₃} {ι₁ : Type*} (e : Basis ι₁ R M₂) (h : ∀ v : ι → ι₁, (f fun i => e (v i)) = g fun i => e (v i)) : f = g

views.nl_informal:
Two multilinear maps from finitely supported functions are equal if they agree on the
generators.

This is a multilinear version of `DFinsupp.lhom_ext'`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MultilinearMap.dfinsupp_ext [∀ i, DecidableEq (κ i)] ⦃f g : MultilinearMap R (fun i ↦ Π₀ j : κ i, M i j) N⦄ (h : ∀ p : Π i, κ i, f.compLinearMap (fun i => DFinsupp.lsingle (p i)) = g.compLinearMap (fun i => DFinsupp.lsingle (p i))) : f = g

views.nl_informal:
When applied to a family of finitely-supported functions each supported on a single element,
`dfinsuppFamily` is itself supported on a single element, with value equal to the map `f` applied
at that point.
views.lean_signature: theorem MultilinearMap.dfinsuppFamily_single [∀ i, DecidableEq (κ i)] (f : Π (p : Π i, κ i), MultilinearMap R (fun i ↦ M i (p i)) (N p)) (p : ∀ i, κ i) (m : ∀ i, M i (p i)) : dfinsuppFamily f (fun i => .single (p i) (m i)) = DFinsupp.single p (f p m)

views.nl_informal:
When only one member of the family of multilinear maps is nonzero, the result consists only of
the component from that member.
views.lean_signature: theorem MultilinearMap.dfinsuppFamily_single_left_apply [∀ i, DecidableEq (κ i)] (p : Π i, κ i) (f : MultilinearMap R (fun i ↦ M i (p i)) (N p)) (x : Π i, Π₀ j, M i j) : dfinsuppFamily (Pi.single p f) x = DFinsupp.single p (f fun i => x _ (p i))

views.nl_informal:
Two multilinear maps from finite families are equal if they agree on the generators.

This is a multilinear version of `LinearMap.pi_ext`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MultilinearMap.pi_ext [Finite ι] [∀ i, Finite (κ i)] [∀ i, DecidableEq (κ i)] ⦃f g : MultilinearMap R (fun i ↦ Π j : κ i, M i j) N⦄ (h : ∀ p : Π i, κ i, f.compLinearMap (fun i => LinearMap.single R _ (p i)) = g.compLinearMap (fun i => LinearMap.single R _ (p i))) : f = g

views.nl_informal:
When applied to a family of finitely-supported functions each supported on a single element,
`piFamily` is itself supported on a single element, with value equal to the map `f` applied
at that point.

views.nl_informal:
**Equational criterion for vanishing**
[A. Altman and S. Kleiman, *A term of commutative algebra* (Lemma 8.16)][altman2021term],
backward direction.

If the expression $\sum_i m_i \otimes n_i$ vanishes trivially, then it vanishes.
That is, $\sum_i m_i \otimes n_i = 0$.
views.lean_signature: theorem TensorProduct.sum_tmul_eq_zero_of_vanishesTrivially (hmn : VanishesTrivially R m n) : ∑ i, m i ⊗ₜ n i = (0 : M ⊗[R] N)

views.nl_informal:
**Equational criterion for vanishing**
[A. Altman and S. Kleiman, *A term of commutative algebra* (Lemma 8.16)][altman2021term],
forward direction.

Assume that the $m_i$ generate $M$. If the expression $\sum_i m_i \otimes n_i$
vanishes, then it vanishes trivially.
views.lean_signature: theorem TensorProduct.vanishesTrivially_of_sum_tmul_eq_zero (hm : Submodule.span R (Set.range m) = ⊤) (hmn : ∑ i, m i ⊗ₜ n i = (0 : M ⊗[R] N)) : VanishesTrivially R m n

views.nl_informal:
**Equational criterion for vanishing**
[A. Altman and S. Kleiman, *A term of commutative algebra* (Lemma 8.16)][altman2021term].

Assume that the $m_i$ generate $M$. Then the expression $\sum_i m_i \otimes n_i$ vanishes
trivially if and only if it vanishes.
views.lean_signature: theorem TensorProduct.vanishesTrivially_iff_sum_tmul_eq_zero (hm : Submodule.span R (Set.range m) = ⊤) : VanishesTrivially R m n ↔ ∑ i, m i ⊗ₜ n i = (0 : M ⊗[R] N)

views.nl_informal:
**Equational criterion for vanishing**
[A. Altman and S. Kleiman, *A term of commutative algebra* (Lemma 8.16)][altman2021term],
forward direction, generalization.

Assume that the submodule $M' \subseteq M$ generated by the $m_i$
satisfies the property that the map $M' \otimes N \to M \otimes N$ is injective. If the expression
$\sum_i m_i \otimes n_i$ vanishes, then it vanishes trivially.
views.lean_signature: theorem TensorProduct.vanishesTrivially_of_sum_tmul_eq_zero_of_rTensor_injective (hm : Injective (rTensor N (span R (Set.range m)).subtype)) (hmn : ∑ i, m i ⊗ₜ n i = (0 : M ⊗[R] N)) : VanishesTrivially R m n

views.nl_informal:
**Equational criterion for vanishing**
[A. Altman and S. Kleiman, *A term of commutative algebra* (Lemma 8.16)][altman2021term],
generalization.

Assume that the submodule $M' \subseteq M$ generated by the $m_i$ satisfies the
property that the map $M' \otimes N \to M \otimes N$ is injective. Then the expression
$\sum_i m_i \otimes n_i$ vanishes trivially if and only if it vanishes.
views.lean_signature: theorem TensorProduct.vanishesTrivially_iff_sum_tmul_eq_zero_of_rTensor_injective (hm : Injective (rTensor N (span R (Set.range m)).subtype)) : VanishesTrivially R m n ↔ ∑ i, m i ⊗ₜ n i = (0 : M ⊗[R] N)

views.nl_informal:
Converse of `TensorProduct.vanishesTrivially_of_sum_tmul_eq_zero_of_rTensor_injective`.

Assume that every expression $\sum_i m_i \otimes n_i$ which vanishes also vanishes trivially.
Then, for every submodule $M' \subseteq M$, the map $M' \otimes N \to M \otimes N$ is injective.
views.lean_signature: theorem TensorProduct.rTensor_injective_of_forall_vanishesTrivially (hMN : ∀ {l : ℕ} {m : Fin l → M} {n : Fin l → N}, ∑ i, m i ⊗ₜ n i = (0 : M ⊗[R] N) → VanishesTrivially R m n) (M' : Submodule R M) : Injective (rTensor N M'.subtype)

views.nl_informal:

for every submodule $M' \subseteq M$, the map $M' \otimes N \to M \otimes N$ is injective.
views.lean_signature: theorem TensorProduct.forall_vanishesTrivially_iff_forall_rTensor_injective : (∀ {l : ℕ} {m : Fin l → M} {n : Fin l → N}, ∑ i, m i ⊗ₜ n i = (0 : M ⊗[R] N) → VanishesTrivially R m n) ↔ ∀ M' : Submodule R M, Injective (rTensor N M'.subtype)

additionally that it is non-empty, but we drop this condition in the formalization).

The topological Besicovitch covering theorem: there exist finitely many families of disjoint
balls covering all the centers in a package. More specifically, one can use `N` families if there
are no satellite configurations with `N+1` points.

views.nl_informal:
Consider, for each `x` in a set `s`, a radius `r x ∈ (0, 1]`. Then one can find finitely
many disjoint balls of the form `closedBall x (r x)` covering a proportion `1/(N+1)` of `s`, if
there are no satellite configurations with `N+1` points.

views.nl_informal:
The **measurable Besicovitch covering theorem**. Assume that, for any `x` in a set `s`,
one is given a set of admissible closed balls centered at `x`, with arbitrarily small radii.
Then there exists a disjoint covering of almost all `s` by admissible closed balls centered at some
points of `s`.
This version requires that the underlying measure is finite, and that the space has the Besicovitch
covering property (which is satisfied for instance by normed real vector spaces). It expresses the
conclusion in a slightly awkward form (with a subset of `α × ℝ`) coming from the proof technique.
For a version assuming that the measure is sigma-finite,
see `exists_disjoint_closedBall_covering_ae_aux`.
For a version giving the conclusion in a nicer form, see `exists_disjoint_closedBall_covering_ae`.

views.nl_informal:
The measurable **Besicovitch covering theorem**.

Assume that, for any `x` in a set `s`, one is given a set of admissible closed balls centered at
`x`, with arbitrarily small radii. Then there exists a disjoint covering of almost all `s` by
admissible closed balls centered at some points of `s`.

This version requires the underlying measure to be sigma-finite, and the space to have the
Besicovitch covering property (which is satisfied for instance by normed real vector spaces).
It expresses the conclusion in a slightly awkward form (with a subset of `α × ℝ`) coming from the
proof technique.

For a version giving the conclusion in a nicer form, see `exists_disjoint_closedBall_covering_ae`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Besicovitch.exists_disjoint_closedBall_covering_ae_aux (μ : Measure α) [SFinite μ] (f : α → Set ℝ) (s : Set α) (hf : ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ δ > 0, (f x ∩ Ioo 0 δ).Nonempty) : ∃ t : Set (α × ℝ), t.Countable ∧ (∀ p ∈ t, p.1 ∈ s) ∧ (∀ p ∈ t, p.2 ∈ f p.1) ∧ μ (s \ ⋃ (p : α × ℝ) (_ : p ∈ t), closedBall p.1 p.2) = 0 ∧ t.PairwiseDisjoint fun p => closedBall p.1 p.2

views.nl_informal:
The measurable **Besicovitch covering theorem**.

Assume that, for any `x` in a set `s`, one is given a set of admissible closed balls centered at
`x`, with arbitrarily small radii. Then there exists a disjoint covering of almost all `s` by
admissible closed balls centered at some points of `s`. We can even require that the radius at `x`
is bounded by a given function `R x`. (Take `R = 1` if you don't need this additional feature).

This version requires the underlying measure to be sigma-finite, and the space to have the
Besicovitch covering property (which is satisfied for instance by normed real vector spaces).

views.nl_informal:
In a space with the Besicovitch property, any set `s` can be covered with balls whose measures
add up to at most `μ s + ε`, for any positive `ε`. This works even if one restricts the set of
allowed radii around a point `x` to a set `f x` which accumulates at `0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Besicovitch.exists_closedBall_covering_tsum_measure_le (μ : Measure α) [SFinite μ] [Measure.OuterRegular μ] {ε : ℝ≥0∞} (hε : ε ≠ 0) (f : α → Set ℝ) (s : Set α) (hf : ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ δ > 0, (f x ∩ Ioo 0 δ).Nonempty) : ∃ (t : Set α) (r : α → ℝ), t.Countable ∧ t ⊆ s ∧ (∀ x ∈ t, r x ∈ f x) ∧ (s ⊆ ⋃ x ∈ t, closedBall x (r x)) ∧ (∑' x : t, μ (closedBall x (r x))) ≤ μ s + ε

views.nl_informal:
The main feature of the Besicovitch Vitali family is that its filter at a point `x` corresponds
to convergence along closed balls. We record one of the two implications here, which will enable us
to deduce specific statements on differentiation of measures in this context from the general
versions.
views.lean_signature: theorem Besicovitch.tendsto_filterAt (μ : Measure α) [SFinite μ] (x : α) : Tendsto (fun r => closedBall x r) (𝓝[>] 0) ((Besicovitch.vitaliFamily μ).filterAt x)

views.nl_informal:
In a space with the Besicovitch covering property, the ratio of the measure of balls converges
almost surely to the Radon-Nikodym derivative.
views.lean_signature: theorem Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_rnDeriv (ρ μ : Measure β) [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μ] [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure ρ] : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, Tendsto (fun r => ρ (closedBall x r) / μ (closedBall x r)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (ρ.rnDeriv μ x))

views.nl_informal:
Given a measurable set `s`, then `μ (s ∩ closedBall x r) / μ (closedBall x r)` converges when
`r` tends to `0`, for almost every `x`. The limit is `1` for `x ∈ s` and `0` for `x ∉ s`.
This shows that almost every point of `s` is a Lebesgue density point for `s`.
A version for non-measurable sets holds, but it only gives the first conclusion,
see `ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div_of_measurableSet (μ : Measure β) [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μ] {s : Set β} (hs : MeasurableSet s) : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, Tendsto (fun r => μ (s ∩ closedBall x r) / μ (closedBall x r)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (s.indicator 1 x))

views.nl_informal:
Given an arbitrary set `s`, then `μ (s ∩ closedBall x r) / μ (closedBall x r)` converges
to `1` when `r` tends to `0`, for almost every `x` in `s`.
This shows that almost every point of `s` is a Lebesgue density point for `s`.
A stronger version holds for measurable sets, see `ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div_of_measurableSet`.

See also `IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div (μ : Measure β) [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μ] (s : Set β) : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ.restrict s, Tendsto (fun r => μ (s ∩ closedBall x r) / μ (closedBall x r)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 1)

views.nl_informal:
Any `1`-separated set in the ball of radius `2` has cardinality at most `5 ^ dim`. This is
useful to show that the supremum in the definition of `Besicovitch.multiplicity E` is
well behaved.
views.lean_signature: theorem Besicovitch.card_le_of_separated (s : Finset E) (hs : ∀ c ∈ s, ‖c‖ ≤ 2) (h : ∀ c ∈ s, ∀ d ∈ s, c ≠ d → 1 ≤ ‖c - d‖) : s.card ≤ 5 ^ finrank ℝ E

views.nl_informal:
If `δ` is small enough, a `(1-δ)`-separated set in the ball of radius `2` also has cardinality
at most `multiplicity E`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Besicovitch.exists_goodδ : ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ δ < 1 ∧ ∀ s : Finset E, (∀ c ∈ s, ‖c‖ ≤ 2) → (∀ c ∈ s, ∀ d ∈ s, c ≠ d → 1 - δ ≤ ‖c - d‖) → s.card ≤ multiplicity E

views.nl_informal:
In a normed vector space `E`, there can be no satellite configuration with `multiplicity E + 1`
points and the parameter `goodτ E`. This will ensure that in the inductive construction to get
the Besicovitch covering families, there will never be more than `multiplicity E` nonempty
families.
views.lean_signature: theorem Besicovitch.isEmpty_satelliteConfig_multiplicity : IsEmpty (SatelliteConfig E (multiplicity E) (goodτ E))

views.nl_informal:
In the Vitali family `IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure.vitaliFamily K`, the sets based at `x`
contain all balls `closedBall y r` when `dist x y ≤ K * r`.

views.nl_informal:
A version of **Lebesgue's density theorem** for a sequence of closed balls whose centers are
not required to be fixed.

See also `Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div`.

views.nl_informal:
A version of **Lebesgue differentiation theorem** for a sequence of closed balls whose
centers are not required to be fixed.

views.nl_informal:
A version of **Lebesgue differentiation theorem** for a sequence of closed balls whose
centers are not required to be fixed.

views.nl_informal:
For almost every point `x`, sufficiently small sets in a Vitali family around `x` have positive
measure. (This is a nontrivial result, following from the covering property of Vitali families).
views.lean_signature: theorem VitaliFamily.ae_eventually_measure_pos [SecondCountableTopology α] : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∀ᶠ a in v.filterAt x, 0 < μ a

views.nl_informal:
For every point `x`, sufficiently small sets in a Vitali family around `x` have finite measure.
(This is a trivial result, following from the fact that the measure is locally finite).
views.lean_signature: theorem VitaliFamily.eventually_measure_lt_top [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μ] (x : α) : ∀ᶠ a in v.filterAt x, μ a < ∞

views.nl_informal:
If two measures `ρ` and `ν` have, at every point of a set `s`, arbitrarily small sets in a
Vitali family satisfying `ρ a ≤ ν a`, then `ρ s ≤ ν s` if `ρ ≪ μ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem VitaliFamily.measure_le_of_frequently_le [SecondCountableTopology α] [BorelSpace α] {ρ : Measure α} (ν : Measure α) [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure ν] (hρ : ρ ≪ μ) (s : Set α) (hs : ∀ x ∈ s, ∃ᶠ a in v.filterAt x, ρ a ≤ ν a) : ρ s ≤ ν s

views.nl_informal:
If a measure `ρ` is singular with respect to `μ`, then for `μ` almost every `x`, the ratio
`ρ a / μ a` tends to zero when `a` shrinks to `x` along the Vitali family. This makes sense
as `μ a` is eventually positive by `ae_eventually_measure_pos`.
views.lean_signature: theorem VitaliFamily.ae_eventually_measure_zero_of_singular (hρ : ρ ⟂ₘ μ) : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, Tendsto (fun a => ρ a / μ a) (v.filterAt x) (𝓝 0)

views.nl_informal:
A set of points `s` satisfying both `ρ a ≤ c * μ a` and `ρ a ≥ d * μ a` at arbitrarily small
sets in a Vitali family has measure `0` if `c < d`. Indeed, the first inequality should imply
that `ρ s ≤ c * μ s`, and the second one that `ρ s ≥ d * μ s`, a contradiction if `0 < μ s`.

views.nl_informal:
If `ρ` is absolutely continuous with respect to `μ`, then for almost every `x`,
the ratio `ρ a / μ a` converges as `a` shrinks to `x` along a Vitali family for `μ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_div : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∃ c, Tendsto (fun a => ρ a / μ a) (v.filterAt x) (𝓝 c)

views.nl_informal:
Given two thresholds `p < q`, the sets `{x | v.limRatio ρ x < p}`
and `{x | q < v.limRatio ρ x}` are obviously disjoint. The key to proving that `v.limRatio ρ` is
almost everywhere measurable is to show that these sets have measurable supersets which are also
disjoint, up to zero measure. This is the content of this lemma.
views.lean_signature: theorem VitaliFamily.exists_measurable_supersets_limRatio {p q : ℝ≥0} (hpq : p < q) : ∃ a b, MeasurableSet a ∧ MeasurableSet b ∧ {x | v.limRatio ρ x < p} ⊆ a ∧ {x | (q : ℝ≥0∞) < v.limRatio ρ x} ⊆ b ∧ μ (a ∩ b) = 0

views.nl_informal:
If, for all `x` in a set `s`, one has frequently `ρ a / μ a < p`, then `ρ s ≤ p * μ s`, as
proved in `measure_le_of_frequently_le`. Since `ρ a / μ a` tends almost everywhere to
`v.limRatioMeas hρ x`, the same property holds for sets `s` on which `v.limRatioMeas hρ < p`.
views.lean_signature: theorem VitaliFamily.measure_le_mul_of_subset_limRatioMeas_lt {p : ℝ≥0} {s : Set α} (h : s ⊆ {x | v.limRatioMeas hρ x < p}) : ρ s ≤ p * μ s

views.nl_informal:
If, for all `x` in a set `s`, one has frequently `q < ρ a / μ a`, then `q * μ s ≤ ρ s`, as
proved in `measure_le_of_frequently_le`. Since `ρ a / μ a` tends almost everywhere to
`v.limRatioMeas hρ x`, the same property holds for sets `s` on which `q < v.limRatioMeas hρ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem VitaliFamily.mul_measure_le_of_subset_lt_limRatioMeas {q : ℝ≥0} {s : Set α} (h : s ⊆ {x | (q : ℝ≥0∞) < v.limRatioMeas hρ x}) : (q : ℝ≥0∞) * μ s ≤ ρ s

views.nl_informal: The points with `v.limRatioMeas hρ x = ∞` have measure `0` for `μ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem VitaliFamily.measure_limRatioMeas_top : μ {x | v.limRatioMeas hρ x = ∞} = 0

views.nl_informal: The points with `v.limRatioMeas hρ x = 0` have measure `0` for `ρ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem VitaliFamily.measure_limRatioMeas_zero : ρ {x | v.limRatioMeas hρ x = 0} = 0

views.nl_informal:
As an intermediate step to show that `μ.withDensity (v.limRatioMeas hρ) = ρ`, we show here
that `μ.withDensity (v.limRatioMeas hρ) ≤ t^2 ρ` for any `t > 1`.

views.nl_informal:
As an intermediate step to show that `μ.withDensity (v.limRatioMeas hρ) = ρ`, we show here
that `ρ ≤ t μ.withDensity (v.limRatioMeas hρ)` for any `t > 1`.

views.nl_informal:
Weak version of the main theorem on differentiation of measures: given a Vitali family `v`
for a locally finite measure `μ`, and another locally finite measure `ρ`, then for `μ`-almost
every `x` the ratio `ρ a / μ a` converges, when `a` shrinks to `x` along the Vitali family,
towards the Radon-Nikodym derivative of `ρ` with respect to `μ`.

This version assumes that `ρ` is absolutely continuous with respect to `μ`. The general version
without this superfluous assumption is `VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_rnDeriv`.

views.nl_informal:
Main theorem on differentiation of measures: given a Vitali family `v` for a locally finite
measure `μ`, and another locally finite measure `ρ`, then for `μ`-almost every `x` the
ratio `ρ a / μ a` converges, when `a` shrinks to `x` along the Vitali family, towards the
Radon-Nikodym derivative of `ρ` with respect to `μ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_rnDeriv : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, Tendsto (fun a => ρ a / μ a) (v.filterAt x) (𝓝 (ρ.rnDeriv μ x))

views.nl_informal:
Given a measurable set `s`, then `μ (s ∩ a) / μ a` converges when `a` shrinks to a typical
point `x` along a Vitali family. The limit is `1` for `x ∈ s` and `0` for `x ∉ s`. This shows that
almost every point of `s` is a Lebesgue density point for `s`. A version for non-measurable sets
holds, but it only gives the first conclusion, see `ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div`.
views.lean_signature: theorem VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div_of_measurableSet {s : Set α} (hs : MeasurableSet s) : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, Tendsto (fun a => μ (s ∩ a) / μ a) (v.filterAt x) (𝓝 (s.indicator 1 x))

views.nl_informal:
Given an arbitrary set `s`, then `μ (s ∩ a) / μ a` converges to `1` when `a` shrinks to a
typical point of `s` along a Vitali family. This shows that almost every point of `s` is a
Lebesgue density point for `s`. A stronger version for measurable sets is given
in `ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div_of_measurableSet`.
views.lean_signature: theorem VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div (s : Set α) : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ.restrict s, Tendsto (fun a => μ (s ∩ a) / μ a) (v.filterAt x) (𝓝 1)

views.nl_informal:
*Lebesgue differentiation theorem*: for almost every point `x`, the
average of `‖f y - f x‖` on `a` tends to `0` as `a` shrinks to `x` along a Vitali family.
views.lean_signature: theorem VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub {f : α → E} (hf : LocallyIntegrable f μ) : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, Tendsto (fun a => ⨍ y in a, ‖f y - f x‖ ∂μ) (v.filterAt x) (𝓝 0)

views.nl_informal:
*Lebesgue differentiation theorem*: for almost every point `x`, the
average of `f` on `a` tends to `f x` as `a` shrinks to `x` along a Vitali family.
views.lean_signature: theorem VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_average [NormedSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E] {f : α → E} (hf : LocallyIntegrable f μ) : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, Tendsto (fun a => ⨍ y in a, f y ∂μ) (v.filterAt x) (𝓝 (f x))

views.nl_informal:
Given a sequence of subsets `sᵢ` of a metric space, together with a sequence of radii `rᵢ`
such that `rᵢ → 0`, the set of points which belong to infinitely many of the closed

the `rᵢ` are all scaled by a positive constant.

[J.W.S. Cassels, *Some metrical theorems in Diophantine approximation. I*](cassels1950).

https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib/issues/16932.

Given a sequence of subsets `sᵢ` of a metric space, together with a sequence of radii `rᵢ`
such that `rᵢ → 0`, the set of points which belong to infinitely many of the

the `rᵢ` are all scaled by a positive constant.

This lemma is a generalisation of Lemma 9 appearing on page 217 of
[J.W.S. Cassels, *Some metrical theorems in Diophantine approximation. I*](cassels1950).

See also `blimsup_cthickening_mul_ae_eq`.

views.nl_informal:
**Vitali covering theorem**: given a set `t` of subsets of a type, one may extract a disjoint
subfamily `u` such that the `τ`-enlargement of this family covers all elements of `t`, where `τ > 1`
is any fixed number.

Let `f` be a function which is sufficiently close (in the Lipschitz sense) to a given linear
map `A`. Then it expands the volume of any set by at least `m` for any `m < det A`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.mul_le_addHaar_image_of_lt_det (A : E →L[ℝ] E) {m : ℝ≥0} (hm : (m : ℝ≥0∞) < ENNReal.ofReal |A.det|) : ∀ᶠ δ in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ≥0), ∀ (s : Set E) (f : E → E), ApproximatesLinearOn f A s δ → (m : ℝ≥0∞) * μ s ≤ μ (f '' s)

views.nl_informal:
If a differentiable function `f` is approximated by a linear map `A` on a set `s`, up to `δ`,
then at almost every `x` in `s` one has `‖f' x - A‖ ≤ δ`.

views.nl_informal: A differentiable function maps sets of measure zero to sets of measure zero.

A version of Sard lemma in fixed dimension: given a differentiable function from `E` to `E` and
a set where the differential is not invertible, then the image of this set has zero measure.

views.nl_informal:
The derivative of a function on a measurable set is almost everywhere measurable on this set
with respect to Lebesgue measure. Note that, in general, it is not genuinely measurable there,
as `f'` is not unique (but only on a set of measure `0`, as the argument shows).

views.nl_informal:
If a function is differentiable and injective on a measurable set,
then the image is measurable.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.measurable_image_of_fderivWithin (hs : MeasurableSet s) (hf' : ∀ x ∈ s, HasFDerivWithinAt f (f' x) s x) (hf : InjOn f s) : MeasurableSet (f '' s)

views.nl_informal:
If a function is differentiable and injective on a measurable set `s`, then its restriction
to `s` is a measurable embedding.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.measurableEmbedding_of_fderivWithin (hs : MeasurableSet s) (hf' : ∀ x ∈ s, HasFDerivWithinAt f (f' x) s x) (hf : InjOn f s) : MeasurableEmbedding (s.restrict f)

views.nl_informal:
Change of variable formula for differentiable functions, set version: if a function `f` is
injective and differentiable on a measurable set `s`, then the measure of `f '' s` is given by the
integral of `|(f' x).det|` on `s`.
Note that the measurability of `f '' s` is given by `measurable_image_of_fderivWithin`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.lintegral_abs_det_fderiv_eq_addHaar_image (hs : MeasurableSet s) (hf' : ∀ x ∈ s, HasFDerivWithinAt f (f' x) s x) (hf : InjOn f s) : (∫⁻ x in s, ENNReal.ofReal |(f' x).det| ∂μ) = μ (f '' s)

views.nl_informal:
Change of variable formula for differentiable functions, set version: if a function `f` is
injective and differentiable on a measurable set `s`, then the pushforward of the measure with
density `|(f' x).det|` on `s` is the Lebesgue measure on the image set. This version requires
that `f` is measurable, as otherwise `Measure.map f` is zero per our definitions.
For a version without measurability assumption but dealing with the restricted
function `s.restrict f`, see `restrict_map_withDensity_abs_det_fderiv_eq_addHaar`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.map_withDensity_abs_det_fderiv_eq_addHaar (hs : MeasurableSet s) (hf' : ∀ x ∈ s, HasFDerivWithinAt f (f' x) s x) (hf : InjOn f s) (h'f : Measurable f) : Measure.map f ((μ.restrict s).withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal |(f' x).det|) = μ.restrict (f '' s)

views.nl_informal:
Change of variable formula for differentiable functions, set version: if a function `f` is
injective and differentiable on a measurable set `s`, then the pushforward of the measure with
density `|(f' x).det|` on `s` is the Lebesgue measure on the image set. This version is expressed
in terms of the restricted function `s.restrict f`.
For a version for the original function, but with a measurability assumption,
see `map_withDensity_abs_det_fderiv_eq_addHaar`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.restrict_map_withDensity_abs_det_fderiv_eq_addHaar (hs : MeasurableSet s) (hf' : ∀ x ∈ s, HasFDerivWithinAt f (f' x) s x) (hf : InjOn f s) : Measure.map (s.restrict f) (comap (↑) (μ.withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal |(f' x).det|)) = μ.restrict (f '' s)

views.nl_informal:
Integrability in the change of variable formula for differentiable functions: if a
function `f` is injective and differentiable on a measurable set `s`, then a function
`g : E → F` is integrable on `f '' s` if and only if `|(f' x).det| • g ∘ f` is
integrable on `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.integrableOn_image_iff_integrableOn_abs_det_fderiv_smul (hs : MeasurableSet s) (hf' : ∀ x ∈ s, HasFDerivWithinAt f (f' x) s x) (hf : InjOn f s) (g : E → F) : IntegrableOn g (f '' s) μ ↔ IntegrableOn (fun x => |(f' x).det| • g (f x)) s μ

views.nl_informal:
Change of variable formula for differentiable functions: if a function `f` is
injective and differentiable on a measurable set `s`, then the Bochner integral of a function
`g : E → F` on `f '' s` coincides with the integral of `|(f' x).det| • g ∘ f` on `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.integral_image_eq_integral_abs_det_fderiv_smul (hs : MeasurableSet s) (hf' : ∀ x ∈ s, HasFDerivWithinAt f (f' x) s x) (hf : InjOn f s) (g : E → F) : ∫ x in f '' s, g x ∂μ = ∫ x in s, |(f' x).det| • g (f x) ∂μ

views.nl_informal:
Integrability in the change of variable formula for differentiable functions (one-variable
version): if a function `f` is injective and differentiable on a measurable set `s ⊆ ℝ`, then a
function `g : ℝ → F` is integrable on `f '' s` if and only if `|(f' x)| • g ∘ f` is integrable on
`s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.integrableOn_image_iff_integrableOn_abs_deriv_smul {s : Set ℝ} {f : ℝ → ℝ} {f' : ℝ → ℝ} (hs : MeasurableSet s) (hf' : ∀ x ∈ s, HasDerivWithinAt f (f' x) s x) (hf : InjOn f s) (g : ℝ → F) : IntegrableOn g (f '' s) ↔ IntegrableOn (fun x => |f' x| • g (f x)) s

views.nl_informal:
Change of variable formula for differentiable functions (one-variable version): if a function
`f` is injective and differentiable on a measurable set `s ⊆ ℝ`, then the Bochner integral of a
function `g : ℝ → F` on `f '' s` coincides with the integral of `|(f' x)| • g ∘ f` on `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.integral_image_eq_integral_abs_deriv_smul {s : Set ℝ} {f : ℝ → ℝ} {f' : ℝ → ℝ} (hs : MeasurableSet s) (hf' : ∀ x ∈ s, HasDerivWithinAt f (f' x) s x) (hf : InjOn f s) (g : ℝ → F) : ∫ x in f '' s, g x = ∫ x in s, |f' x| • g (f x)

views.nl_informal:
The inner product in `L2` of the indicator of a set `indicatorConstLp 2 hs hμs c` and `f` is
equal to the integral of the inner product over `s`: `∫ x in s, ⟪c, f x⟫ ∂μ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.L2.inner_indicatorConstLp_eq_setIntegral_inner (f : Lp E 2 μ) (hs : MeasurableSet s) (c : E) (hμs : μ s ≠ ∞) : (⟪indicatorConstLp 2 hs hμs c, f⟫ : 𝕜) = ∫ x in s, ⟪c, f x⟫ ∂μ

views.nl_informal:
The inner product in `L2` of the indicator of a set `indicatorConstLp 2 hs hμs c` and `f` is
equal to the inner product of the constant `c` and the integral of `f` over `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.L2.inner_indicatorConstLp_eq_inner_setIntegral [CompleteSpace E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] (hs : MeasurableSet s) (hμs : μ s ≠ ∞) (c : E) (f : Lp E 2 μ) : (⟪indicatorConstLp 2 hs hμs c, f⟫ : 𝕜) = ⟪c, ∫ x in s, f x ∂μ⟫

views.nl_informal:
The inner product in `L2` of the indicator of a set `indicatorConstLp 2 hs hμs (1 : 𝕜)` and
a real or complex function `f` is equal to the integral of `f` over `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.L2.inner_indicatorConstLp_one (hs : MeasurableSet s) (hμs : μ s ≠ ∞) (f : Lp 𝕜 2 μ) : ⟪indicatorConstLp 2 hs hμs (1 : 𝕜), f⟫ = ∫ x in s, f x ∂μ

views.nl_informal:
For bounded continuous functions `f`, `g` on a finite-measure topological space `α`, the L^2
inner product is the integral of their pointwise inner product.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.BoundedContinuousFunction.inner_toLp (f g : α →ᵇ 𝕜) : ⟪BoundedContinuousFunction.toLp 2 μ 𝕜 f, BoundedContinuousFunction.toLp 2 μ 𝕜 g⟫ = ∫ x, g x * conj (f x) ∂μ

views.nl_informal:
For continuous functions `f`, `g` on a compact, finite-measure topological space `α`, the L^2
inner product is the integral of their pointwise inner product.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.ContinuousMap.inner_toLp (f g : C(α, 𝕜)) : ⟪ContinuousMap.toLp (E := 𝕜) 2 μ 𝕜 f, ContinuousMap.toLp (E := 𝕜) 2 μ 𝕜 g⟫ = ∫ x, g x * conj (f x) ∂μ

views.nl_informal: If a function is locally integrable on a compact set, then it is integrable on that set.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.LocallyIntegrableOn.integrableOn_isCompact (hf : LocallyIntegrableOn f s μ) (hs : IsCompact s) : IntegrableOn f s μ

views.nl_informal:
If a function `f` is locally integrable on a set `s` in a second countable topological space,
then there exist countably many open sets `u` covering `s` such that `f` is integrable on each
set `u ∩ s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.LocallyIntegrableOn.exists_countable_integrableOn [SecondCountableTopology X] (hf : LocallyIntegrableOn f s μ) : ∃ T : Set (Set X), T.Countable ∧ (∀ u ∈ T, IsOpen u) ∧ (s ⊆ ⋃ u ∈ T, u) ∧ (∀ u ∈ T, IntegrableOn f (u ∩ s) μ)

views.nl_informal:
If a function `f` is locally integrable on a set `s` in a second countable topological space,
then there exists a sequence of open sets `u n` covering `s` such that `f` is integrable on each
set `u n ∩ s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.LocallyIntegrableOn.exists_nat_integrableOn [SecondCountableTopology X] (hf : LocallyIntegrableOn f s μ) : ∃ u : ℕ → Set X, (∀ n, IsOpen (u n)) ∧ (s ⊆ ⋃ n, u n) ∧ (∀ n, IntegrableOn f (u n ∩ s) μ)

views.nl_informal:
If `s` is locally closed (e.g. open or closed), then `f` is locally integrable on `s` iff it is
integrable on every compact subset contained in `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.locallyIntegrableOn_iff [LocallyCompactSpace X] (hs : IsLocallyClosed s) : LocallyIntegrableOn f s μ ↔ ∀ (k : Set X), k ⊆ s → IsCompact k → IntegrableOn f k μ

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is locally integrable with respect to `μ.restrict s`, it is locally integrable on `s`.
(See `locallyIntegrableOn_iff_locallyIntegrable_restrict` for an iff statement when `s` is
closed.)
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.locallyIntegrableOn_of_locallyIntegrable_restrict [OpensMeasurableSpace X] (hf : LocallyIntegrable f (μ.restrict s)) : LocallyIntegrableOn f s μ

views.nl_informal:
If `s` is closed, being locally integrable on `s` wrt `μ` is equivalent to being locally
integrable with respect to `μ.restrict s`. For the one-way implication without assuming `s` closed,
see `locallyIntegrableOn_of_locallyIntegrable_restrict`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.locallyIntegrableOn_iff_locallyIntegrable_restrict [OpensMeasurableSpace X] (hs : IsClosed s) : LocallyIntegrableOn f s μ ↔ LocallyIntegrable f (μ.restrict s)

views.nl_informal: If a function is locally integrable, then it is integrable on any compact set.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.LocallyIntegrable.integrableOn_isCompact {k : Set X} (hf : LocallyIntegrable f μ) (hk : IsCompact k) : IntegrableOn f k μ

views.nl_informal:
If a function is locally integrable, then it is integrable on an open neighborhood of any
compact set.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.LocallyIntegrable.integrableOn_nhds_isCompact (hf : LocallyIntegrable f μ) {k : Set X} (hk : IsCompact k) : ∃ u, IsOpen u ∧ k ⊆ u ∧ IntegrableOn f u μ

views.nl_informal:
If a function is locally integrable in a second countable topological space,
then there exists a sequence of open sets covering the space on which it is integrable.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.LocallyIntegrable.exists_nat_integrableOn [SecondCountableTopology X] (hf : LocallyIntegrable f μ) : ∃ u : ℕ → Set X, (∀ n, IsOpen (u n)) ∧ ((⋃ n, u n) = univ) ∧ (∀ n, IntegrableOn f (u n) μ)

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is locally integrable and `g` is continuous with compact support,
then `g • f` is integrable.

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is locally integrable and `g` is continuous with compact support,
then `f • g` is integrable.

views.nl_informal: A continuous function `f` is locally integrable with respect to any locally finite measure.
views.lean_signature: theorem Continuous.locallyIntegrable [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μ] [SecondCountableTopologyEither X E] (hf : Continuous f) : LocallyIntegrable f μ

views.nl_informal:

locally finite measure.

views.nl_informal: A continuous function with compact support is integrable on the whole space.

views.nl_informal: A simple function is measurable
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.measurable [MeasurableSpace β] (f : α →ₛ β) : Measurable f

views.nl_informal: Calculate the integral of `(g ∘ f)`, where `g : β → ℝ≥0∞` and `f : α →ₛ β`.

views.nl_informal:
To prove something for an arbitrary simple function, it suffices to show
that the property holds for (multiples of) characteristic functions and is closed under
addition (of functions with disjoint support).

It is possible to make the hypotheses in `h_add` a bit stronger, and such conditions can be added
once we need them (for example it is only necessary to consider the case where `g` is a multiple
of a characteristic function, and that this multiple doesn't appear in the image of `f`).

To use in an induction proof, the syntax is `induction f using SimpleFunc.induction with`.

views.nl_informal:
To prove something for an arbitrary simple function, it suffices to show
that the property holds for constant functions and that it is closed under piecewise combinations
of functions.

To use in an induction proof, the syntax is `induction f with`.

views.nl_informal:
In a topological vector space, the addition of a simple function and a measurable function is
measurable.

views.nl_informal:
To prove something for an arbitrary measurable function into `ℝ≥0∞`, it suffices to show
that the property holds for (multiples of) characteristic functions and is closed under addition
and supremum of increasing sequences of functions.

It is possible to make the hypotheses in the induction steps a bit stronger, and such conditions
can be added once we need them (for example in `h_add` it is only necessary to consider the sum of
a simple function with a multiple of a characteristic function and that the intersection
of their images is a subset of `{0}`.

views.nl_informal:

that the property holds for (multiples of) characteristic functions with finite mass according to
some sigma-finite measure and is closed under addition and supremum of increasing sequences of
functions.

can be added once we need them (for example in `h_add` it is only necessary to consider the sum of
a simple function with a multiple of a characteristic function and that the intersection
of their images is a subset of `{0}`.

product of the Borel sigma algebras might not contain all open sets, but still it contains enough

views.nl_informal:
To prove something for an arbitrary `MemLp` function in a second countable
Borel normed group, it suffices to show that
* the property holds for (multiples of) characteristic functions;
* is closed under addition;
* the set of functions in the `Lᵖ` space for which the property holds is closed.
* the property is closed under the almost-everywhere equal relation.

It is possible to make the hypotheses in the induction steps a bit stronger, and such conditions
can be added once we need them (for example in `h_add` it is only necessary to consider the sum of
a simple function with a multiple of a characteristic function and that the intersection
of their images is a subset of `{0}`).

views.nl_informal:
To prove something for an arbitrary integrable function in a normed group,

of `fun x ↦ f x + g x`.

of `fun x ↦ g x + f x`.

Unlike `StrongMeasurable.norm` and `StronglyMeasurable.nnnorm`, this lemma proves measurability,
**not** strong measurability. This is an intentional decision: for functions taking values in
ℝ≥0∞, measurability is much more useful than strong measurability.

views.nl_informal:
If a function `f` is strongly measurable w.r.t. a sub-σ-algebra `m` and the measure is σ-finite
on `m`, then there exists spanning measurable sets with finite measure on which `f` has bounded
norm. In particular, `f` is integrable on each of those sets.

is a fundamental domain for the action of `G` on `α`.

`MeasureTheory.AEDisjoint (g • s) s` for `g ≠ 1`.

views.nl_informal:
If a measurable space has a finite measure `μ` and a countable group `G` acts
quasi-measure-preservingly, then to show that a set `s` is a fundamental domain, it is sufficient
to check that its translates `g • s` are (almost) disjoint and that the sum `∑' g, μ (g • s)` is
sufficiently large.

views.nl_informal:
Given a measure space with an action of a finite group `G`, the measure of any `G`-invariant set
is determined by the measure of its intersection with a fundamental domain for the action of `G`.

views.nl_informal: If `s` and `t` are two fundamental domains of the same action, then their measures are equal.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.IsFundamentalDomain.measure_eq (hs : IsFundamentalDomain G s μ) (ht : IsFundamentalDomain G t μ) : μ s = μ t

views.nl_informal:
If the action of a countable group `G` admits an invariant measure `μ` with a fundamental domain
`s`, then every null-measurable set `t` such that the sets `g • t ∩ s` are pairwise a.e.-disjoint
has measure at most `μ s`.

views.nl_informal:
If the action of a countable group `G` admits an invariant measure `μ` with a fundamental domain
`s`, then every null-measurable set `t` of measure strictly greater than `μ s` contains two
points `x y` such that `g • x = y` for some `g ≠ 1`.

If `f` is invariant under the action of a countable group `G`, and `μ` is a `G`-invariant
measure with a fundamental domain `s`, then the `essSup` of `f` restricted to `s` is the same as
that of `f` on all of its domain.

lattice point of `L`.

`exists_ne_zero_mem_lattice_of_measure_mul_two_pow_lt_measure`, this version requires in addition
that `s` is compact and `L` is discrete but provides a weaker inequality rather than a strict

views.nl_informal:
The multiplicative shear mapping `(x, y) ↦ (x, xy)` preserves the measure `μ × ν`.
This condition is part of the definition of a measurable group in [Halmos, §59].
There, the map in this lemma is called `S`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.measurePreserving_prod_mul [IsMulLeftInvariant ν] : MeasurePreserving (fun z : G × G => (z.1, z.1 * z.2)) (μ.prod ν) (μ.prod ν)

views.nl_informal:
The map `(x, y) ↦ (y, yx)` sends the measure `μ × ν` to `ν × μ`.
This is the map `SR` in [Halmos, §59].
`S` is the map `(x, y) ↦ (x, xy)` and `R` is `Prod.swap`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.measurePreserving_prod_mul_swap [IsMulLeftInvariant μ] : MeasurePreserving (fun z : G × G => (z.2, z.2 * z.1)) (μ.prod ν) (ν.prod μ)

views.nl_informal:
The map `(x, y) ↦ (x, x⁻¹y)` is measure-preserving.
This is the function `S⁻¹` in [Halmos, §59],
where `S` is the map `(x, y) ↦ (x, xy)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.measurePreserving_prod_inv_mul [IsMulLeftInvariant ν] : MeasurePreserving (fun z : G × G => (z.1, z.1⁻¹ * z.2)) (μ.prod ν) (μ.prod ν)

views.nl_informal:
The map `(x, y) ↦ (y, y⁻¹x)` sends `μ × ν` to `ν × μ`.
This is the function `S⁻¹R` in [Halmos, §59],
where `S` is the map `(x, y) ↦ (x, xy)` and `R` is `Prod.swap`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.measurePreserving_prod_inv_mul_swap : MeasurePreserving (fun z : G × G => (z.2, z.2⁻¹ * z.1)) (μ.prod ν) (ν.prod μ)

views.nl_informal:
The map `(x, y) ↦ (yx, x⁻¹)` is measure-preserving.

where `S` is the map `(x, y) ↦ (x, xy)` and `R` is `Prod.swap`.

views.nl_informal:
A technical lemma relating two different measures. This is basically [Halmos, §60 Th. A].
Note that if `f` is the characteristic function of a measurable set `t` this states that
`μ t = c * μ s` for a constant `c` that does not depend on `μ`.

Note: There is a gap in the last step of the proof in [Halmos].
In the last line, the equality `g(x⁻¹)ν(sx⁻¹) = f(x)` holds if we can prove that
`0 < ν(sx⁻¹) < ∞`. The first inequality follows from §59, Th. D, but the second inequality is
not justified. We prove this inequality for almost all `x` in
`MeasureTheory.ae_measure_preimage_mul_right_lt_top_of_ne_zero`.

views.nl_informal:
**Divergence theorem** for Bochner integral. If `f : ℝⁿ⁺¹ → Eⁿ⁺¹` is continuous on a rectangular
box `[a, b] : Set ℝⁿ⁺¹`, `a ≤ b`, is differentiable on its interior with derivative
`f' : ℝⁿ⁺¹ → ℝⁿ⁺¹ →L[ℝ] Eⁿ⁺¹` and the divergence `fun x ↦ ∑ i, f' x eᵢ i` is integrable on `[a, b]`,
where `eᵢ = Pi.single i 1` is the `i`-th basis vector, then its integral is equal to the sum of
integrals of `f` over the faces of `[a, b]`, taken with appropriate signs.

Moreover, the same is true if the function is not differentiable at countably many
points of the interior of `[a, b]`.

We represent both faces `x i = a i` and `x i = b i` as the box
`face i = [a ∘ Fin.succAbove i, b ∘ Fin.succAbove i]` in `ℝⁿ`, where
`Fin.succAbove : Fin n ↪o Fin (n + 1)` is the order embedding with range `{i}ᶜ`. The restrictions
of `f : ℝⁿ⁺¹ → Eⁿ⁺¹` to these faces are given by `f ∘ backFace i` and `f ∘ frontFace i`, where
`backFace i = Fin.insertNth i (a i)` and `frontFace i = Fin.insertNth i (b i)` are embeddings
`ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ⁺¹` that take `y : ℝⁿ` and insert `a i` (resp., `b i`) as `i`-th coordinate.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.integral_divergence_of_hasFDerivWithinAt_off_countable (hle : a ≤ b) (f : ℝⁿ⁺¹ → Eⁿ⁺¹) (f' : ℝⁿ⁺¹ → ℝⁿ⁺¹ →L[ℝ] Eⁿ⁺¹) (s : Set ℝⁿ⁺¹) (hs : s.Countable) (Hc : ContinuousOn f (Icc a b)) (Hd : ∀ x ∈ (Set.pi univ fun i => Ioo (a i) (b i)) \ s, HasFDerivAt f (f' x) x) (Hi : IntegrableOn (fun x => ∑ i, f' x (e i) i) (Icc a b)) : (∫ x in Icc a b, ∑ i, f' x (e i) i) = ∑ i : Fin (n + 1), ((∫ x in face i, f (frontFace i x) i) - ∫ x in face i, f (backFace i x) i)

views.nl_informal:
**Divergence theorem** for a family of functions `f : Fin (n + 1) → ℝⁿ⁺¹ → E`. See also
`MeasureTheory.integral_divergence_of_hasFDerivWithinAt_off_countable'` for a version formulated
in terms of a vector-valued function `f : ℝⁿ⁺¹ → Eⁿ⁺¹`.

**Fundamental theorem of calculus, part 2**. This version assumes that `f` is continuous on the
interval and is differentiable off a countable set `s`.

See also

* `intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDeriv_right_of_le` for a version that only assumes right
differentiability of `f`;

* `MeasureTheory.integral_eq_of_hasDerivWithinAt_off_countable` for a version that works both

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:
**Divergence theorem** for functions on the plane along rectangles. It is formulated in terms of
two functions `f g : ℝ × ℝ → E` and an integral over `Icc a b = [a.1, b.1] × [a.2, b.2]`, where
`a b : ℝ × ℝ`, `a ≤ b`. When thinking of `f` and `g` as the two coordinates of a single function
`F : ℝ × ℝ → E × E` and when `E = ℝ`, this is the usual statement that the integral of the
divergence of `F` inside the rectangle equals the integral of the normal derivative of `F` along the
boundary.

See also `MeasureTheory.integral2_divergence_prod_of_hasFDerivWithinAt_off_countable` for a
version that does not assume `a ≤ b` and uses iterated interval integral instead of the integral
over `Icc a b`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.integral_divergence_prod_Icc_of_hasFDerivWithinAt_off_countable_of_le (f g : ℝ × ℝ → E) (f' g' : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ × ℝ →L[ℝ] E) (a b : ℝ × ℝ) (hle : a ≤ b) (s : Set (ℝ × ℝ)) (hs : s.Countable) (Hcf : ContinuousOn f (Icc a b)) (Hcg : ContinuousOn g (Icc a b)) (Hdf : ∀ x ∈ Ioo a.1 b.1 ×ˢ Ioo a.2 b.2 \ s, HasFDerivAt f (f' x) x) (Hdg : ∀ x ∈ Ioo a.1 b.1 ×ˢ Ioo a.2 b.2 \ s, HasFDerivAt g (g' x) x) (Hi : IntegrableOn (fun x => f' x (1, 0) + g' x (0, 1)) (Icc a b)) : (∫ x in Icc a b, f' x (1, 0) + g' x (0, 1)) = (((∫ x in a.1..b.1, g (x, b.2)) - ∫ x in a.1..b.1, g (x, a.2)) + ∫ y in a.2..b.2, f (b.1, y)) - ∫ y in a.2..b.2, f (a.1, y)

views.nl_informal:
**Divergence theorem** for functions on the plane. It is formulated in terms of two functions
`f g : ℝ × ℝ → E` and iterated integral `∫ x in a₁..b₁, ∫ y in a₂..b₂, _`, where
`a₁ a₂ b₁ b₂ : ℝ`. When thinking of `f` and `g` as the two coordinates of a single function
`F : ℝ × ℝ → E × E` and when `E = ℝ`, this is the usual statement that the integral of the
divergence of `F` inside the rectangle with vertices `(aᵢ, bⱼ)`, `i, j =1,2`, equals the integral of
the normal derivative of `F` along the boundary.

See also `MeasureTheory.integral_divergence_prod_Icc_of_hasFDerivWithinAt_off_countable_of_le`
for a version that uses an integral over `Icc a b`, where `a b : ℝ × ℝ`, `a ≤ b`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.integral2_divergence_prod_of_hasFDerivWithinAt_off_countable (f g : ℝ × ℝ → E) (f' g' : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ × ℝ →L[ℝ] E) (a₁ a₂ b₁ b₂ : ℝ) (s : Set (ℝ × ℝ)) (hs : s.Countable) (Hcf : ContinuousOn f ([[a₁, b₁]] ×ˢ [[a₂, b₂]])) (Hcg : ContinuousOn g ([[a₁, b₁]] ×ˢ [[a₂, b₂]])) (Hdf : ∀ x ∈ Ioo (min a₁ b₁) (max a₁ b₁) ×ˢ Ioo (min a₂ b₂) (max a₂ b₂) \ s, HasFDerivAt f (f' x) x) (Hdg : ∀ x ∈ Ioo (min a₁ b₁) (max a₁ b₁) ×ˢ Ioo (min a₂ b₂) (max a₂ b₂) \ s, HasFDerivAt g (g' x) x) (Hi : IntegrableOn (fun x => f' x (1, 0) + g' x (0, 1)) ([[a₁, b₁]] ×ˢ [[a₂, b₂]])) : (∫ x in a₁..b₁, ∫ y in a₂..b₂, f' (x, y) (1, 0) + g' (x, y) (0, 1)) = (((∫ x in a₁..b₁, g (x, b₂)) - ∫ x in a₁..b₁, g (x, a₂)) + ∫ y in a₂..b₂, f (b₁, y)) - ∫ y in a₂..b₂, f (a₁, y)

views.nl_informal:
The layer cake formula / **Cavalieri's principle** / tail probability formula:

Let `f` be a non-negative measurable function on a measure space. Let `G` be an
increasing absolutely continuous function on the positive real line, vanishing at the origin,
with derivative `G' = g`. Then the integral of the composition `G ∘ f` can be written as
the integral over the positive real line of the "tail measures" `μ {ω | f(ω) ≥ t}` of `f`
weighted by `g`.

Roughly speaking, the statement is: `∫⁻ (G ∘ f) ∂μ = ∫⁻ t in 0..∞, g(t) * μ {ω | f(ω) ≥ t}`.

See `MeasureTheory.lintegral_comp_eq_lintegral_meas_lt_mul` for a version with sets of the form
`{ω | f(ω) > t}` instead.

views.nl_informal:
Fundamental theorem of calculus for set integrals:
if `μ` is a measure that is finite at a filter `l` and
`f` is a measurable function that has a finite limit `b` at `l ⊓ ae μ`, then
`∫ x in s i, f x ∂μ = μ (s i) • b + o(μ (s i))` at a filter `li` provided that
`s i` tends to `l.smallSets` along `li`.
Since `μ (s i)` is an `ℝ≥0∞` number, we use `μ.real (s i)` in the actual statement.

Often there is a good formula for `μ.real (s i)`, so the formalization can take an optional
argument `m` with this formula and a proof of `(fun i => μ.real (s i)) =ᶠ[li] m`. Without these
arguments, `m i = μ.real (s i)` is used in the output.

number, we use `μ.real (s i)` in the actual statement.

views.nl_informal:

**Fundamental theorem of calculus-1**, local version for any measure.
Let filters `l` and `l'` be related by `TendstoIxxClass Ioc`.
If `f` has a finite limit `c` at `l' ⊓ ae μ`, where `μ` is a measure
finite at `l'`, then `∫ x in u..v, f x ∂μ = ∫ x in u..v, c ∂μ + o(∫ x in u..v, 1 ∂μ)` as both
`u` and `v` tend to `l`.

See also `measure_integral_sub_linear_isLittleO_of_tendsto_ae` for a version assuming
`[intervalIntegral.FTCFilter a l l']` and `[MeasureTheory.IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μ]`. If `l` is one
of `𝓝[≥] a`, `𝓝[≤] a`, `𝓝 a`, then it's easier to apply the non-primed version.  The primed version
also works, e.g., for `l = l' = atTop`.

We use integrals of constants instead of measures because this way it is easier to formulate
a statement that works in both cases `u ≤ v` and `v ≤ u`.

views.nl_informal:
**Fundamental theorem of calculus-1**, strict derivative in both limits for a locally finite

respectively.

  ∫ x in ub..vb, cb ∂μ - ∫ x in ua..va, ca ∂μ +

as `ua` and `va` tend to `la` while `ub` and `vb` tend to `lb`.

considered with respect to the standard measure (defined to be the Haar measure of total mass `T`)

interval (t, t + T].

views.nl_informal:

depend on `t`.

views.nl_informal: The positivity of a linear functional `Λ` implies that `Λ` is monotone.

views.nl_informal:
For any compact subset `K ⊆ X`, there exist some compactly supported continuous nonnegative
functions `f` on `X` such that `f ≥ 1` on `K`.
views.lean_signature: theorem rieszContentAux_image_nonempty (K : Compacts X) : (Λ '' { f : C_c(X, ℝ≥0) | ∀ x ∈ K, (1 : ℝ≥0) ≤ f x }).Nonempty

views.nl_informal:
Riesz content `λ` (associated with a positive linear functional `Λ`) is
monotone: if `K₁ ⊆ K₂` are compact subsets in `X`, then `λ(K₁) ≤ λ(K₂)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem rieszContentAux_mono {K₁ K₂ : Compacts X} (h : K₁ ≤ K₂) : rieszContentAux Λ K₁ ≤ rieszContentAux Λ K₂

views.nl_informal:
Any compactly supported continuous nonnegative `f` such that `f ≥ 1` on `K` gives an upper bound
on the content of `K`; namely `λ(K) ≤ Λ f`.
views.lean_signature: theorem rieszContentAux_le {K : Compacts X} {f : C_c(X, ℝ≥0)} (h : ∀ x ∈ K, (1 : ℝ≥0) ≤ f x) : rieszContentAux Λ K ≤ Λ f

views.nl_informal:
The Riesz content can be approximated arbitrarily well by evaluating the positive linear
functional on test functions: for any `ε > 0`, there exists a compactly supported continuous
nonnegative function `f` on `X` such that `f ≥ 1` on `K` and such that `λ(K) ≤ Λ f < λ(K) + ε`.
views.lean_signature: theorem exists_lt_rieszContentAux_add_pos (K : Compacts X) {ε : ℝ≥0} (εpos : 0 < ε) : ∃ f : C_c(X, ℝ≥0), (∀ x ∈ K, (1 : ℝ≥0) ≤ f x) ∧ Λ f < rieszContentAux Λ K + ε

views.nl_informal:
The Riesz content `λ` associated to a given positive linear functional `Λ` is
finitely subadditive: `λ(K₁ ∪ K₂) ≤ λ(K₁) + λ(K₂)` for any compact subsets `K₁, K₂ ⊆ X`.
views.lean_signature: theorem rieszContentAux_sup_le (K1 K2 : Compacts X) : rieszContentAux Λ (K1 ⊔ K2) ≤ rieszContentAux Λ K1 + rieszContentAux Λ K2

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal: If `f` assumes the value `1` on a compact set `K` then `rieszMeasure K ≤ Λ f`.

views.nl_informal:
Let `X` and `Y` be R₁ topological spaces
with Borel σ-algebras and measures `μ` and `ν`, respectively.
Suppose that `μ` is inner regular for finite measure sets with respect to compact sets
and `ν` is a locally finite measure.
Let `f : α → C(X, Y)` be a family of continuous maps
that converges to a continuous map `g : C(X, Y)` in the compact-open topology along a filter `l`.
Suppose that `g` is a measure preserving map
and `f a` is a measure preserving map eventually along `l`.
Then for any finite measure measurable set `s`,
the preimages `f a ⁻¹' s` tend to the preimage `g ⁻¹' s` in measure.
More precisely, the measure of the symmetric difference of these two sets tends to zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.tendsto_measure_symmDiff_preimage_nhds_zero {l : Filter α} {f : α → C(X, Y)} {g : C(X, Y)} {s : Set Y} (hfg : Tendsto f l (𝓝 g)) (hf : ∀ᶠ a in l, MeasurePreserving (f a) μ ν) (hg : MeasurePreserving g μ ν) (hs : NullMeasurableSet s ν) (hνs : ν s ≠ ∞) : Tendsto (fun a ↦ μ ((f a ⁻¹' s) ∆ (g ⁻¹' s))) l (𝓝 0)

views.nl_informal:
Let `f : Z → C(X, Y)` be a continuous (in the compact open topology) family
of continuous measure preserving maps.
Let `t : Set Y` be a null measurable set of finite measure.
Then for any `s`, the set of parameters `z`
such that the preimage of `t` under `f_z` is a.e. equal to `s`
is a closed set.

In particular, if `X = Y` and `s = t`,
then we see that the a.e. stabilizer of a set is a closed set.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.isClosed_setOf_preimage_ae_eq {f : Z → C(X, Y)} (hf : Continuous f) (hfm : ∀ z, MeasurePreserving (f z) μ ν) (s : Set X) {t : Set Y} (htm : NullMeasurableSet t ν) (ht : ν t ≠ ∞) : IsClosed {z | f z ⁻¹' t =ᵐ[μ] s}

limit, then their integrals against the finite measure tend to the integral of the limit.

 * the limit is in the almost everywhere sense;
 * boundedness holds almost everywhere;
 * integration is the pairing against non-negative continuous test functions

`MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.tendsto_lintegral_nn_filter_of_le_const`.

tend pointwise to a limit, then their integrals (`MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.testAgainstNN`)
against the finite measure tend to the integral of the limit.

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:
Even if `s` is not measurable, we can bound `map f μ s` from below.

views.nl_informal:

satisfies, for any measurable set `s`, the equality `μ (toMeasurable μ t ∩ s) = μ (u ∩ s)`.

when the measure is s-finite (for example when it is σ-finite),
see `measure_toMeasurable_inter_of_sFinite`.

views.nl_informal:
Given a predicate on `β` and `Set α` where both `α` and `β` are measurable spaces, if the
predicate holds for almost every `x : β` and
- `∅ : Set α`
- a family of sets generating the σ-algebra of `α`
Moreover, if for almost every `x : β`, the predicate is closed under complements and countable
disjoint unions, then the predicate holds for almost every `x : β` and all measurable sets of `α`.

This is an AE version of `MeasurableSpace.induction_on_inter` where the condition is dependent
on a measurable space `β`.

views.nl_informal:
If `sᵢ` is a countable family of (null) measurable pairwise `μ`-a.e. disjoint sets, then there
exists a subordinate family `tᵢ ⊆ sᵢ` of measurable pairwise disjoint sets such that
`tᵢ =ᵐ[μ] sᵢ`.

views.nl_informal:
A null measurable set `t` is Carathéodory measurable: for any `s`, we have
`μ (s ∩ t) + μ (s \ t) = μ s`.

views.nl_informal:
If `s` and `t` are null measurable sets of equal measure
and their intersection has finite measure,
then `s \ t` and `t \ s` have equal measures too.

views.nl_informal: An open null set w.r.t. an `IsOpenPosMeasure` is empty.

views.nl_informal: A null set has empty interior.

views.nl_informal: A property satisfied almost everywhere is satisfied on a dense subset.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.Measure.dense_of_ae {p : X → Prop} (hp : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, p x) : Dense {x | p x}

views.nl_informal:
If two functions are a.e. equal on an open set and are continuous on this set, then they are
equal on this set.

views.nl_informal: If two continuous functions are a.e. equal, then they are equal.

views.nl_informal:
A *closed* measure zero subset is nowhere dense. (Closedness is required: for instance, the
rational numbers are countable (thus have measure zero), but are dense (hence not nowhere dense).

views.nl_informal:
A σ-compact measure zero subset is meagre.
(More generally, every Fσ set of measure zero is meagre.)

views.nl_informal:
One pair of implications of the portmanteau theorem:
For a sequence of Borel probability measures, the following two are equivalent:

(C) The limsup of the measures of any closed set is at most the measure of the closed set
under a candidate limit measure.

(O) The liminf of the measures of any open set is at least the measure of the open set
under a candidate limit measure.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.limsup_measure_closed_le_iff_liminf_measure_open_ge {ι : Type*} {L : Filter ι} {μ : Measure Ω} {μs : ι → Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [∀ i, IsProbabilityMeasure (μs i)] : (∀ F, IsClosed F → (L.limsup fun i ↦ μs i F) ≤ μ F) ↔ ∀ G, IsOpen G → μ G ≤ L.liminf fun i ↦ μs i G

views.nl_informal:
One implication of the portmanteau theorem:
For a sequence of Borel probability measures, if the liminf of the measures of any open set is at
least the measure of the open set under a candidate limit measure, then for any set whose
boundary carries no probability mass under the candidate limit measure, then its measures under the
sequence converge to its measure under the candidate limit measure.
