views.nl_informal: If `z ∈ 𝒟ᵒ`, and `n : ℤ`, then `|z + n| > 1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ModularGroup.one_lt_normSq_T_zpow_smul (hz : z ∈ 𝒟ᵒ) (n : ℤ) : 1 < normSq (T ^ n • z : ℍ)

views.nl_informal:
First Fundamental Domain Lemma: Any `z : ℍ` can be moved to `𝒟` by an element of
`SL(2,ℤ)`
views.lean_signature: theorem ModularGroup.exists_smul_mem_fd (z : ℍ) : ∃ g : SL(2, ℤ), g • z ∈ 𝒟

views.nl_informal:
Second Fundamental Domain Lemma: if both `z` and `g • z` are in the open domain `𝒟ᵒ`,
where `z : ℍ` and `g : SL(2,ℤ)`, then `z = g • z`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ModularGroup.eq_smul_self_of_mem_fdo_mem_fdo (hz : z ∈ 𝒟ᵒ) (hg : g • z ∈ 𝒟ᵒ) : z = g • z

views.nl_informal:
For every `τ : ℍ` there is some `γ ∈ SL(2, ℤ)` that sends it to an element whose
imaginary part is at least `1/2` and such that `denom γ τ` has norm at most 1.
views.lean_signature: theorem ModularGroup.exists_one_half_le_im_smul_and_norm_denom_le (τ : ℍ) : ∃ γ : SL(2, ℤ), 1 / 2 ≤ im (γ • τ) ∧ ‖denom γ τ‖ ≤ 1

views.nl_informal: **Lifting the exponent lemma** for odd primes.
views.lean_signature: theorem Int.emultiplicity_pow_sub_pow {x y : ℤ} (hxy : ↑p ∣ x - y) (hx : ¬↑p ∣ x) (n : ℕ) : emultiplicity (↑p) (x ^ n - y ^ n) = emultiplicity (↑p) (x - y) + emultiplicity p n

views.nl_informal: **Lifting the exponent lemma** for `p = 2`
views.lean_signature: theorem Int.two_pow_sub_pow {x y : ℤ} {n : ℕ} (hxy : 2 ∣ x - y) (hx : ¬2 ∣ x) (hn : Even n) : emultiplicity 2 (x ^ n - y ^ n) + 1 = emultiplicity 2 (x + y) + emultiplicity 2 (x - y) + emultiplicity (2 : ℤ) n

views.nl_informal:
Values of an absolute value on the rationals are determined by the values on the natural
numbers.
views.lean_signature: theorem Rat.AbsoluteValue.eq_on_nat_iff_eq : (∀ n : ℕ , f n = g n) ↔ f = g

views.nl_informal:
The equivalence class of an absolute value on the rationals is determined by its values on
the natural numbers.
views.lean_signature: theorem Rat.AbsoluteValue.equiv_on_nat_iff_equiv : (∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ n : ℕ , f n ^ c = g n) ↔ f ≈ g

views.nl_informal: There exists a minimal positive integer with absolute value smaller than 1.
views.lean_signature: theorem Rat.AbsoluteValue.exists_minimal_nat_zero_lt_and_lt_one : ∃ p : ℕ, (0 < f p ∧ f p < 1) ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, 0 < f m ∧ f m < 1 → p ≤ m

views.nl_informal: The minimal positive integer with absolute value smaller than 1 is a prime number.
views.lean_signature: theorem Rat.AbsoluteValue.is_prime_of_minimal_nat_zero_lt_and_lt_one : p.Prime

views.nl_informal: A natural number not divisible by `p` has absolute value 1.
views.lean_signature: theorem Rat.AbsoluteValue.eq_one_of_not_dvd {m : ℕ} (hpm : ¬ p ∣ m) : f m = 1

views.nl_informal: The absolute value of `p` is `p ^ (-t)` for some positive real number `t`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Rat.AbsoluteValue.exists_pos_eq_pow_neg : ∃ t : ℝ, 0 < t ∧ f p = p ^ (-t)

views.nl_informal: If `f` is bounded and not trivial, then it is equivalent to a p-adic absolute value.
views.lean_signature: theorem Rat.AbsoluteValue.equiv_padic_of_bounded : ∃! p, ∃ (_ : Fact p.Prime), f ≈ (padic p)

views.nl_informal:
Given any two integers `n`, `m` with `m > 1`, the absolute value of `n` is bounded by
`m + m * f m + m * (f m) ^ 2 + ... + m * (f m) ^ d` where `d` is the number of digits of the
expansion of `n` in base `m`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Rat.AbsoluteValue.apply_le_sum_digits (n : ℕ) {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 < m) : f n ≤ ((Nat.digits m n).mapIdx fun i _ ↦ m * (f m) ^ i).sum

views.nl_informal: If `f n > 1` for some `n` then `f n > 1` for all `n ≥ 2`
views.lean_signature: theorem Rat.AbsoluteValue.one_lt_of_not_bounded (notbdd : ¬ ∀ n : ℕ, f n ≤ 1) {n₀ : ℕ} (hn₀ : 1 < n₀) : 1 < f n₀

views.nl_informal: Given two natural numbers `n, m` greater than 1 we have `f n ≤ f m ^ logb m n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Rat.AbsoluteValue.le_pow_log : f n ≤ f m ^ logb m n

views.nl_informal: Given `m, n ≥ 2` and `f m = m ^ s`, `f n = n ^ t` for `s, t > 0`, we have `t ≤ s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Rat.AbsoluteValue.le_of_eq_pow {s t : ℝ} (hfm : f m = m ^ s) (hfn : f n = n ^ t) : t ≤ s

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is not bounded and not trivial, then it is equivalent to the standard absolute value on
`ℚ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Rat.AbsoluteValue.equiv_real_of_unbounded : f ≈ real

views.nl_informal:
**Ostrowski's Theorem**: every absolute value (with values in `ℝ`) on `ℚ` is equivalent
to either the standard absolute value or a `p`-adic absolute value for a prime `p`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Rat.AbsoluteValue.equiv_real_or_padic (f : AbsoluteValue ℚ ℝ) (hf_nontriv : f.IsNontrivial) : f ≈ real ∨ ∃! p, ∃ (_ : Fact p.Prime), f ≈ (padic p)

views.nl_informal: The standard absolute value on `ℚ` is not equivalent to any `p`-adic absolute value.
views.lean_signature: theorem Rat.AbsoluteValue.not_real_equiv_padic (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] : ¬ real ≈ (padic p)

views.nl_informal:
An element of `ℤ√d` has norm one (i.e., `a.re^2 - d*a.im^2 = 1`) if and only if
it is contained in the submonoid of unitary elements.

TODO: merge this result with `Pell.isPell_iff_mem_unitary`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.is_pell_solution_iff_mem_unitary {d : ℤ} {a : ℤ√d} : a.re ^ 2 - d * a.im ^ 2 = 1 ↔ a ∈ unitary (ℤ√d)

views.nl_informal: The proof that `a` is a solution to the Pell equation `x^2 - d*y^2 = 1`
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.Solution₁.prop (a : Solution₁ d) : a.x ^ 2 - d * a.y ^ 2 = 1

views.nl_informal: Two solutions are equal if their `x` and `y` components are equal.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.Solution₁.ext {a b : Solution₁ d} (hx : a.x = b.x) (hy : a.y = b.y) : a = b

views.nl_informal: When `d` is negative, then `x` or `y` must be zero in a solution.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.Solution₁.eq_zero_of_d_neg (h₀ : d < 0) (a : Solution₁ d) : a.x = 0 ∨ a.y = 0

views.nl_informal: A solution has `x ≠ 0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.Solution₁.x_ne_zero (h₀ : 0 ≤ d) (a : Solution₁ d) : a.x ≠ 0

views.nl_informal: A solution with `x > 1` must have `y ≠ 0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.Solution₁.y_ne_zero_of_one_lt_x {a : Solution₁ d} (ha : 1 < a.x) : a.y ≠ 0

views.nl_informal: If a solution has `x > 1`, then `d` is positive.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.Solution₁.d_pos_of_one_lt_x {a : Solution₁ d} (ha : 1 < a.x) : 0 < d

views.nl_informal: If a solution has `x > 1`, then `d` is not a square.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.Solution₁.d_nonsquare_of_one_lt_x {a : Solution₁ d} (ha : 1 < a.x) : ¬IsSquare d

views.nl_informal: A solution with `x = 1` is trivial.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.Solution₁.eq_one_of_x_eq_one (h₀ : d ≠ 0) {a : Solution₁ d} (ha : a.x = 1) : a = 1

views.nl_informal: A solution is `1` or `-1` if and only if `y = 0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.Solution₁.eq_one_or_neg_one_iff_y_eq_zero {a : Solution₁ d} : a = 1 ∨ a = -1 ↔ a.y = 0

views.nl_informal: The set of solutions with `x > 0` is closed under multiplication.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.Solution₁.x_mul_pos {a b : Solution₁ d} (ha : 0 < a.x) (hb : 0 < b.x) : 0 < (a * b).x

views.nl_informal: The set of solutions with `x` and `y` positive is closed under multiplication.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.Solution₁.y_mul_pos {a b : Solution₁ d} (hax : 0 < a.x) (hay : 0 < a.y) (hbx : 0 < b.x) (hby : 0 < b.y) : 0 < (a * b).y

views.nl_informal:
If `(x, y)` is a solution with `x` positive, then all its powers with natural exponents
have positive `x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.Solution₁.x_pow_pos {a : Solution₁ d} (hax : 0 < a.x) (n : ℕ) : 0 < (a ^ n).x

views.nl_informal:
If `(x, y)` is a solution with `x` and `y` positive, then all its powers with positive
natural exponents have positive `y`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.Solution₁.y_pow_succ_pos {a : Solution₁ d} (hax : 0 < a.x) (hay : 0 < a.y) (n : ℕ) : 0 < (a ^ n.succ).y

views.nl_informal:
If `(x, y)` is a solution with `x` and `y` positive, then all its powers with positive
exponents have positive `y`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.Solution₁.y_zpow_pos {a : Solution₁ d} (hax : 0 < a.x) (hay : 0 < a.y) {n : ℤ} (hn : 0 < n) : 0 < (a ^ n).y

views.nl_informal: If `(x, y)` is a solution with `x` positive, then all its powers have positive `x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.Solution₁.x_zpow_pos {a : Solution₁ d} (hax : 0 < a.x) (n : ℤ) : 0 < (a ^ n).x

views.nl_informal:
If `(x, y)` is a solution with `x` and `y` positive, then the `y` component of any power
has the same sign as the exponent.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.Solution₁.sign_y_zpow_eq_sign_of_x_pos_of_y_pos {a : Solution₁ d} (hax : 0 < a.x) (hay : 0 < a.y) (n : ℤ) : (a ^ n).y.sign = n.sign

views.nl_informal:
If `a` is any solution, then one of `a`, `a⁻¹`, `-a`, `-a⁻¹` has
positive `x` and nonnegative `y`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.Solution₁.exists_pos_variant (h₀ : 0 < d) (a : Solution₁ d) : ∃ b : Solution₁ d, 0 < b.x ∧ 0 ≤ b.y ∧ a ∈ ({b, b⁻¹, -b, -b⁻¹} : Set (Solution₁ d))

views.nl_informal:
If `d` is a positive integer that is not a square, then there is a nontrivial solution
to the Pell equation `x^2 - d*y^2 = 1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.exists_of_not_isSquare (h₀ : 0 < d) (hd : ¬IsSquare d) : ∃ x y : ℤ, x ^ 2 - d * y ^ 2 = 1 ∧ y ≠ 0

views.nl_informal:
If `d` is a positive integer, then there is a nontrivial solution
to the Pell equation `x^2 - d*y^2 = 1` if and only if `d` is not a square.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.exists_iff_not_isSquare (h₀ : 0 < d) : (∃ x y : ℤ, x ^ 2 - d * y ^ 2 = 1 ∧ y ≠ 0) ↔ ¬IsSquare d

views.nl_informal:
If `d` is a positive integer that is not a square, then there exists a nontrivial solution
to the Pell equation `x^2 - d*y^2 = 1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.Solution₁.exists_nontrivial_of_not_isSquare (h₀ : 0 < d) (hd : ¬IsSquare d) : ∃ a : Solution₁ d, a ≠ 1 ∧ a ≠ -1

views.nl_informal:
If `d` is a positive integer that is not a square, then there exists a solution
to the Pell equation `x^2 - d*y^2 = 1` with `x > 1` and `y > 0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.Solution₁.exists_pos_of_not_isSquare (h₀ : 0 < d) (hd : ¬IsSquare d) : ∃ a : Solution₁ d, 1 < a.x ∧ 0 < a.y

views.nl_informal: A fundamental solution has positive `x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.IsFundamental.x_pos {a : Solution₁ d} (h : IsFundamental a) : 0 < a.x

views.nl_informal: If a fundamental solution exists, then `d` must be positive.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.IsFundamental.d_pos {a : Solution₁ d} (h : IsFundamental a) : 0 < d

views.nl_informal: If a fundamental solution exists, then `d` must be a non-square.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.IsFundamental.d_nonsquare {a : Solution₁ d} (h : IsFundamental a) : ¬IsSquare d

views.nl_informal: If there is a fundamental solution, it is unique.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.IsFundamental.subsingleton {a b : Solution₁ d} (ha : IsFundamental a) (hb : IsFundamental b) : a = b

views.nl_informal: If `d` is positive and not a square, then a fundamental solution exists.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.IsFundamental.exists_of_not_isSquare (h₀ : 0 < d) (hd : ¬IsSquare d) : ∃ a : Solution₁ d, IsFundamental a

views.nl_informal:
The map sending an integer `n` to the `y`-coordinate of `a^n` for a fundamental
solution `a` is stritcly increasing.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.IsFundamental.y_strictMono {a : Solution₁ d} (h : IsFundamental a) : StrictMono fun n : ℤ => (a ^ n).y

views.nl_informal: If `a` is a fundamental solution, then `(a^m).y < (a^n).y` if and only if `m < n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.IsFundamental.zpow_y_lt_iff_lt {a : Solution₁ d} (h : IsFundamental a) (m n : ℤ) : (a ^ m).y < (a ^ n).y ↔ m < n

views.nl_informal: The `n`th power of a fundamental solution is trivial if and only if `n = 0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.IsFundamental.zpow_eq_one_iff {a : Solution₁ d} (h : IsFundamental a) (n : ℤ) : a ^ n = 1 ↔ n = 0

views.nl_informal:
A power of a fundamental solution is never equal to the negative of a power of this
fundamental solution.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.IsFundamental.zpow_ne_neg_zpow {a : Solution₁ d} (h : IsFundamental a) {n n' : ℤ} : a ^ n ≠ -a ^ n'

views.nl_informal:
The `x`-coordinate of a fundamental solution is a lower bound for the `x`-coordinate
of any positive solution.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.IsFundamental.x_le_x {a₁ : Solution₁ d} (h : IsFundamental a₁) {a : Solution₁ d} (hax : 1 < a.x) : a₁.x ≤ a.x

views.nl_informal:
The `y`-coordinate of a fundamental solution is a lower bound for the `y`-coordinate
of any positive solution.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.IsFundamental.y_le_y {a₁ : Solution₁ d} (h : IsFundamental a₁) {a : Solution₁ d} (hax : 1 < a.x) (hay : 0 < a.y) : a₁.y ≤ a.y

views.nl_informal:
If we multiply a positive solution with the inverse of a fundamental solution,
the `y`-coordinate remains nonnegative.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.IsFundamental.mul_inv_y_nonneg {a₁ : Solution₁ d} (h : IsFundamental a₁) {a : Solution₁ d} (hax : 1 < a.x) (hay : 0 < a.y) : 0 ≤ (a * a₁⁻¹).y

views.nl_informal:
If we multiply a positive solution with the inverse of a fundamental solution,
the `x`-coordinate stays positive.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.IsFundamental.mul_inv_x_pos {a₁ : Solution₁ d} (h : IsFundamental a₁) {a : Solution₁ d} (hax : 1 < a.x) (hay : 0 < a.y) : 0 < (a * a₁⁻¹).x

views.nl_informal:
If we multiply a positive solution with the inverse of a fundamental solution,
the `x`-coordinate decreases.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.IsFundamental.mul_inv_x_lt_x {a₁ : Solution₁ d} (h : IsFundamental a₁) {a : Solution₁ d} (hax : 1 < a.x) (hay : 0 < a.y) : (a * a₁⁻¹).x < a.x

views.nl_informal: Any nonnegative solution is a power with nonnegative exponent of a fundamental solution.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.IsFundamental.eq_pow_of_nonneg {a₁ : Solution₁ d} (h : IsFundamental a₁) {a : Solution₁ d} (hax : 0 < a.x) (hay : 0 ≤ a.y) : ∃ n : ℕ, a = a₁ ^ n

views.nl_informal: Every solution is, up to a sign, a power of a given fundamental solution.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.IsFundamental.eq_zpow_or_neg_zpow {a₁ : Solution₁ d} (h : IsFundamental a₁) (a : Solution₁ d) : ∃ n : ℤ, a = a₁ ^ n ∨ a = -a₁ ^ n

views.nl_informal:
When `d` is positive and not a square, then the group of solutions to the Pell equation
`x^2 - d*y^2 = 1` has a unique positive generator (up to sign).
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.existsUnique_pos_generator (h₀ : 0 < d) (hd : ¬IsSquare d) : ∃! a₁ : Solution₁ d, 1 < a₁.x ∧ 0 < a₁.y ∧ ∀ a : Solution₁ d, ∃ n : ℤ, a = a₁ ^ n ∨ a = -a₁ ^ n

views.nl_informal:
A positive solution is a generator (up to sign) of the group of all solutions to the
Pell equation `x^2 - d*y^2 = 1` if and only if it is a fundamental solution.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.pos_generator_iff_fundamental (a : Solution₁ d) : (1 < a.x ∧ 0 < a.y ∧ ∀ b : Solution₁ d, ∃ n : ℤ, b = a ^ n ∨ b = -a ^ n) ↔ IsFundamental a

views.nl_informal:
Every solution to **Pell's equation** is recursively obtained from the initial solution
`(1,0)` using the recursion `pell`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pell.eq_pell {x y : ℕ} (hp : x * x - d a1 * y * y = 1) : ∃ n, x = xn a1 n ∧ y = yn a1 n

views.nl_informal: The `n`th prime is greater or equal to `n + 2`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.add_two_le_nth_prime (n : ℕ) : n + 2 ≤ nth Prime n

views.nl_informal:
The cardinality of the finset `primesBelow n` equals the counting function
`primeCounting'` at `n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.primesBelow_card_eq_primeCounting' (n : ℕ) : #n.primesBelow = primeCounting' n

views.nl_informal: A linear upper bound on the size of the `primeCounting'` function
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.primeCounting'_add_le {a k : ℕ} (h0 : 0 < a) (h1 : a < k) (n : ℕ) : π' (k + n) ≤ π' k + Nat.totient a * (n / a + 1)

views.nl_informal:
For any positive `k : ℕ` there exists an arbitrarily large prime `p` such that
`p ≡ 1 [MOD k]`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.exists_prime_gt_modEq_one {k : ℕ} (n : ℕ) (hk0 : k ≠ 0) : ∃ p : ℕ, Nat.Prime p ∧ n < p ∧ p ≡ 1 [MOD k]

views.nl_informal: For any positive `k : ℕ` there are infinitely many primes `p` such that `p ≡ 1 [MOD k]`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.infinite_setOf_prime_modEq_one {k : ℕ} (hk0 : k ≠ 0) : Set.Infinite {p : ℕ | Nat.Prime p ∧ p ≡ 1 [MOD k]}

views.nl_informal:
Pythagorean triples are interchangeable, i.e `x * x + y * y = y * y + x * x = z * z`.
This comes from additive commutativity.
views.lean_signature: theorem pythagoreanTriple_comm {x y z : ℤ} : PythagoreanTriple x y z ↔ PythagoreanTriple y x z

views.nl_informal: The zeroth Pythagorean triple is all zeros.
views.lean_signature: theorem PythagoreanTriple.zero : PythagoreanTriple 0 0 0

views.nl_informal:
A triple is still a triple if you multiply `x`, `y` and `z`
by a constant `k`.
views.lean_signature: theorem PythagoreanTriple.mul (h : PythagoreanTriple x y z) (k : ℤ) : PythagoreanTriple (k * x) (k * y) (k * z)

views.nl_informal:
`(k*x, k*y, k*z)` is a Pythagorean triple if and only if
`(x, y, z)` is also a triple.
views.lean_signature: theorem PythagoreanTriple.mul_iff (k : ℤ) (hk : k ≠ 0) : PythagoreanTriple (k * x) (k * y) (k * z) ↔ PythagoreanTriple x y z

views.nl_informal:
By assuming `x` is odd and `z` is positive we get a slightly more precise classification of
the Pythagorean triple `x ^ 2 + y ^ 2 = z ^ 2`.
views.lean_signature: theorem PythagoreanTriple.coprime_classification' {x y z : ℤ} (h : PythagoreanTriple x y z) (h_coprime : Int.gcd x y = 1) (h_parity : x % 2 = 1) (h_pos : 0 < z) : ∃ m n, x = m ^ 2 - n ^ 2 ∧ y = 2 * m * n ∧ z = m ^ 2 + n ^ 2 ∧ Int.gcd m n = 1 ∧ (m % 2 = 0 ∧ n % 2 = 1 ∨ m % 2 = 1 ∧ n % 2 = 0) ∧ 0 ≤ m

views.nl_informal: **Formula for Pythagorean Triples**
views.lean_signature: theorem PythagoreanTriple.classification : PythagoreanTriple x y z ↔ ∃ k m n, (x = k * (m ^ 2 - n ^ 2) ∧ y = k * (2 * m * n) ∨ x = k * (2 * m * n) ∧ y = k * (m ^ 2 - n ^ 2)) ∧ (z = k * (m ^ 2 + n ^ 2) ∨ z = -k * (m ^ 2 + n ^ 2))

views.nl_informal: Let `r > 1` and `1/r + 1/s = 1`. Then `B_r` and `B'_s` are disjoint (i.e. no collision exists).
views.lean_signature: theorem Beatty.no_collision (hrs : r.HolderConjugate s) : Disjoint {beattySeq r k | k} {beattySeq' s k | k}

views.nl_informal:
Let `r > 1` and `1/r + 1/s = 1`. Suppose there is an integer `j` where `B_r` and `B'_s` both
jump over `j` (i.e. an anti-collision). Then this leads to a contradiction.
views.lean_signature: theorem Beatty.no_anticollision (hrs : r.HolderConjugate s) : ¬∃ j k m : ℤ, k < j / r ∧ (j + 1) / r ≤ k + 1 ∧ m ≤ j / s ∧ (j + 1) / s < m + 1

views.nl_informal: Let `0 < r ∈ ℝ` and `j ∈ ℤ`. Then either `j ∈ B_r` or `B_r` jumps over `j`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Beatty.hit_or_miss (h : r > 0) : j ∈ {beattySeq r k | k} ∨ ∃ k : ℤ, k < j / r ∧ (j + 1) / r ≤ k + 1

views.nl_informal: Let `0 < r ∈ ℝ` and `j ∈ ℤ`. Then either `j ∈ B'_r` or `B'_r` jumps over `j`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Beatty.hit_or_miss' (h : r > 0) : j ∈ {beattySeq' r k | k} ∨ ∃ k : ℤ, k ≤ j / r ∧ (j + 1) / r < k + 1

views.nl_informal:
Generalization of Rayleigh's theorem on Beatty sequences. Let `r` be a real number greater
than 1, and `1/r + 1/s = 1`. Then the complement of `B_r` is `B'_s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem compl_beattySeq {r s : ℝ} (hrs : r.HolderConjugate s) : {beattySeq r k | k}ᶜ = {beattySeq' s k | k}

views.nl_informal:
Generalization of Rayleigh's theorem on Beatty sequences. Let `r` be a real number greater
than 1, and `1/r + 1/s = 1`. Then `B⁺_r` and `B⁺'_s` partition the positive integers.
views.lean_signature: theorem beattySeq_symmDiff_beattySeq'_pos {r s : ℝ} (hrs : r.HolderConjugate s) : {beattySeq r k | k > 0} ∆ {beattySeq' s k | k > 0} = {n | 0 < n}

views.nl_informal: Let `r` be an irrational number. Then `B⁺_r` and `B⁺'_r` are equal.
views.lean_signature: theorem Irrational.beattySeq'_pos_eq {r : ℝ} (hr : Irrational r) : {beattySeq' r k | k > 0} = {beattySeq r k | k > 0}

views.nl_informal:
**Rayleigh's theorem** on Beatty sequences. Let `r` be an irrational number greater than 1, and
`1/r + 1/s = 1`. Then `B⁺_r` and `B⁺_s` partition the positive integers.
views.lean_signature: theorem Irrational.beattySeq_symmDiff_beattySeq_pos {r s : ℝ} (hrs : r.HolderConjugate s) (hr : Irrational r) : {beattySeq r k | k > 0} ∆ {beattySeq s k | k > 0} = {n | 0 < n}

views.nl_informal: The sup norm of a non-zero integer matrix is at least one
views.lean_signature: theorem Int.Matrix.one_le_norm_A_of_ne_zero (hA : A ≠ 0) : 1 ≤ ‖A‖

views.nl_informal: A number that divides an `s`-factored number is itself `s`-factored.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.mem_factoredNumbers_of_dvd {s : Finset ℕ} {m k : ℕ} (h : m ∈ factoredNumbers s) (h' : k ∣ m) : k ∈ factoredNumbers s

views.nl_informal:
`m` is `s`-factored if and only if `m` is nonzero and all prime divisors `≤ m` of `m`
are in `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.mem_factoredNumbers_iff_forall_le {s : Finset ℕ} {m : ℕ} : m ∈ factoredNumbers s ↔ m ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ p ≤ m, p.Prime → p ∣ m → p ∈ s

views.nl_informal: `m` is `s`-factored if and only if all prime divisors of `m` are in `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.mem_factoredNumbers' {s : Finset ℕ} {m : ℕ} : m ∈ factoredNumbers s ↔ ∀ p, p.Prime → p ∣ m → p ∈ s

views.nl_informal: The `Finset` of prime factors of an `s`-factored number is contained in `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.primeFactors_subset_of_mem_factoredNumbers {s : Finset ℕ} {m : ℕ} (hm : m ∈ factoredNumbers s) : m.primeFactors ⊆ s

views.nl_informal:
If `m ≠ 0` and the `Finset` of prime factors of `m` is contained in `s`, then `m`
is `s`-factored.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.mem_factoredNumbers_of_primeFactors_subset {s : Finset ℕ} {m : ℕ} (hm : m ≠ 0) (hp : m.primeFactors ⊆ s) : m ∈ factoredNumbers s

views.nl_informal:
`m` is `s`-factored if and only if `m ≠ 0` and its `Finset` of prime factors
is contained in `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.mem_factoredNumbers_iff_primeFactors_subset {s : Finset ℕ} {m : ℕ} : m ∈ factoredNumbers s ↔ m ≠ 0 ∧ m.primeFactors ⊆ s

views.nl_informal: The product of two `s`-factored numbers is again `s`-factored.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.mul_mem_factoredNumbers {s : Finset ℕ} {m n : ℕ} (hm : m ∈ factoredNumbers s) (hn : n ∈ factoredNumbers s) : m * n ∈ factoredNumbers s

views.nl_informal: The product of the prime factors of `n` that are in `s` is an `s`-factored number.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.prod_mem_factoredNumbers (s : Finset ℕ) (n : ℕ) : (n.primeFactorsList.filter (· ∈ s)).prod ∈ factoredNumbers s

views.nl_informal:
The sets of `s`-factored and of `s ∪ {N}`-factored numbers are the same when `N` is not prime.
See `Nat.equivProdNatFactoredNumbers` for when `N` is prime.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.factoredNumbers_insert (s : Finset ℕ) {N : ℕ} (hN : ¬ N.Prime) : factoredNumbers (insert N s) = factoredNumbers s

views.nl_informal: The non-zero non-`s`-factored numbers are `≥ N` when `s` contains all primes less than `N`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.factoredNumbers_compl {N : ℕ} {s : Finset ℕ} (h : primesBelow N ≤ s) : (factoredNumbers s)ᶜ \ {0} ⊆ {n | N ≤ n}

views.nl_informal:
If `p` is a prime and `n` is `s`-factored, then every product `p^e * n`
is `s ∪ {p}`-factored.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.pow_mul_mem_factoredNumbers {s : Finset ℕ} {p n : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (e : ℕ) (hn : n ∈ factoredNumbers s) : p ^ e * n ∈ factoredNumbers (insert p s)

views.nl_informal: If `p ∉ s` is a prime and `n` is `s`-factored, then `p` and `n` are coprime.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.Prime.factoredNumbers_coprime {s : Finset ℕ} {p n : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hs : p ∉ s) (hn : n ∈ factoredNumbers s) : Nat.Coprime p n

views.nl_informal:
If `f : ℕ → F` is multiplicative on coprime arguments, `p ∉ s` is a prime and `m`
is `s`-factored, then `f (p^e * m) = f (p^e) * f m`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.factoredNumbers.map_prime_pow_mul {F : Type*} [Mul F] {f : ℕ → F} (hmul : ∀ {m n}, Coprime m n → f (m * n) = f m * f n) {s : Finset ℕ} {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hs : p ∉ s) (e : ℕ) {m : factoredNumbers s} : f (p ^ e * m) = f (p ^ e) * f m

views.nl_informal: The `n`-smooth numbers agree with the `Finset.range n`-factored numbers.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.smoothNumbers_eq_factoredNumbers (n : ℕ) : smoothNumbers n = factoredNumbers (Finset.range n)

views.nl_informal: The `n`-smooth numbers agree with the `primesBelow n`-factored numbers.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.smmoothNumbers_eq_factoredNumbers_primesBelow (n : ℕ) : smoothNumbers n = factoredNumbers n.primesBelow

views.nl_informal: A number that divides an `n`-smooth number is itself `n`-smooth.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.mem_smoothNumbers_of_dvd {n m k : ℕ} (h : m ∈ smoothNumbers n) (h' : k ∣ m) : k ∈ smoothNumbers n

views.nl_informal:
`m` is `n`-smooth if and only if `m` is nonzero and all prime divisors `≤ m` of `m`
are less than `n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.mem_smoothNumbers_iff_forall_le {n m : ℕ} : m ∈ smoothNumbers n ↔ m ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ p ≤ m, p.Prime → p ∣ m → p < n

views.nl_informal: `m` is `n`-smooth if and only if all prime divisors of `m` are less than `n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.mem_smoothNumbers' {n m : ℕ} : m ∈ smoothNumbers n ↔ ∀ p, p.Prime → p ∣ m → p < n

views.nl_informal:
The `Finset` of prime factors of an `n`-smooth number is contained in the `Finset`
of primes below `n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.primeFactors_subset_of_mem_smoothNumbers {m n : ℕ} (hms : m ∈ n.smoothNumbers) : m.primeFactors ⊆ n.primesBelow

views.nl_informal: `m` is an `n`-smooth number if the `Finset` of its prime factors consists of numbers `< n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.mem_smoothNumbers_of_primeFactors_subset {m n : ℕ} (hm : m ≠ 0) (hp : m.primeFactors ⊆ Finset.range n) : m ∈ n.smoothNumbers

views.nl_informal:
`m` is an `n`-smooth number if and only if `m ≠ 0` and the `Finset` of its prime factors
is contained in the `Finset` of primes below `n`
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.mem_smoothNumbers_iff_primeFactors_subset {m n : ℕ} : m ∈ n.smoothNumbers ↔ m ≠ 0 ∧ m.primeFactors ⊆ n.primesBelow

views.nl_informal: Zero is never a smooth number
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.ne_zero_of_mem_smoothNumbers {n m : ℕ} (h : m ∈ smoothNumbers n) : m ≠ 0

views.nl_informal: The product of two `n`-smooth numbers is an `n`-smooth number.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.mul_mem_smoothNumbers {m₁ m₂ n : ℕ} (hm1 : m₁ ∈ n.smoothNumbers) (hm2 : m₂ ∈ n.smoothNumbers) : m₁ * m₂ ∈ n.smoothNumbers

views.nl_informal: The product of the prime factors of `n` that are less than `N` is an `N`-smooth number.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.prod_mem_smoothNumbers (n N : ℕ) : (n.primeFactorsList.filter (· < N)).prod ∈ smoothNumbers N

views.nl_informal:
The sets of `N`-smooth and of `(N+1)`-smooth numbers are the same when `N` is not prime.
See `Nat.equivProdNatSmoothNumbers` for when `N` is prime.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.smoothNumbers_succ {N : ℕ} (hN : ¬ N.Prime) : (N + 1).smoothNumbers = N.smoothNumbers

views.nl_informal: All `m`, `0 < m < n` are `n`-smooth numbers
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.mem_smoothNumbers_of_lt {m n : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m) (hmn : m < n) : m ∈ n.smoothNumbers

views.nl_informal: The non-zero non-`N`-smooth numbers are `≥ N`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.smoothNumbers_compl (N : ℕ) : (N.smoothNumbers)ᶜ \ {0} ⊆ {n | N ≤ n}

views.nl_informal: If `p` is positive and `n` is `p`-smooth, then every product `p^e * n` is `(p+1)`-smooth.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.pow_mul_mem_smoothNumbers {p n : ℕ} (hp : p ≠ 0) (e : ℕ) (hn : n ∈ smoothNumbers p) : p ^ e * n ∈ smoothNumbers (succ p)

views.nl_informal: If `p` is a prime and `n` is `p`-smooth, then `p` and `n` are coprime.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.Prime.smoothNumbers_coprime {p n : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hn : n ∈ smoothNumbers p) : Nat.Coprime p n

views.nl_informal:
If `f : ℕ → F` is multiplicative on coprime arguments, `p` is a prime and `m` is `p`-smooth,
then `f (p^e * m) = f (p^e) * f m`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.map_prime_pow_mul {F : Type*} [Mul F] {f : ℕ → F} (hmul : ∀ {m n}, Nat.Coprime m n → f (m * n) = f m * f n) {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (e : ℕ) {m : p.smoothNumbers} : f (p ^ e * m) = f (p ^ e) * f m

views.nl_informal: A `k`-smooth number can be written as a square times a product of distinct primes `< k`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.eq_prod_primes_mul_sq_of_mem_smoothNumbers {n k : ℕ} (h : n ∈ smoothNumbers k) : ∃ s ∈ k.primesBelow.powerset, ∃ m, n = m ^ 2 * (s.prod id)

views.nl_informal:
The set of `k`-smooth numbers `≤ N` is contained in the set of numbers of the form `m^2 * P`,
where `m ≤ √N` and `P` is a product of distinct primes `< k`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.smoothNumbersUpTo_subset_image (N k : ℕ) : smoothNumbersUpTo N k ⊆ Finset.image (fun (s, m) ↦ m ^ 2 * (s.prod id)) (k.primesBelow.powerset ×ˢ (Finset.range (N.sqrt + 1)).erase 0)

views.nl_informal: The cardinality of the set of `k`-smooth numbers `≤ N` is bounded by `2^π(k-1) * √N`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.smoothNumbersUpTo_card_le (N k : ℕ) : #(smoothNumbersUpTo N k) ≤ 2 ^ #k.primesBelow * N.sqrt

views.nl_informal:
The set of `k`-rough numbers `≤ N` can be written as the union of the sets of multiples `≤ N`
of primes `k ≤ p ≤ N`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.roughNumbersUpTo_eq_biUnion (N k) : roughNumbersUpTo N k = ((N + 1).primesBelow \ k.primesBelow).biUnion fun p ↦ {m ∈ Finset.range (N + 1) | m ≠ 0 ∧ p ∣ m}

views.nl_informal:
The cardinality of the set of `k`-rough numbers `≤ N` is bounded by the sum of `⌊N/p⌋`
over the primes `k ≤ p ≤ N`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.roughNumbersUpTo_card_le (N k : ℕ) : #(roughNumbersUpTo N k) ≤ ((N + 1).primesBelow \ k.primesBelow).sum (fun p ↦ N / p)

views.nl_informal: **Euler's four-square identity**.
views.lean_signature: theorem euler_four_squares {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (a b c d x y z w : R) : (a * x - b * y - c * z - d * w) ^ 2 + (a * y + b * x + c * w - d * z) ^ 2 + (a * z - b * w + c * x + d * y) ^ 2 + (a * w + b * z - c * y + d * x) ^ 2 = (a ^ 2 + b ^ 2 + c ^ 2 + d ^ 2) * (x ^ 2 + y ^ 2 + z ^ 2 + w ^ 2)

views.nl_informal: **Euler's four-square identity**, a version for natural numbers.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.euler_four_squares (a b c d x y z w : ℕ) : ((a : ℤ) * x - b * y - c * z - d * w).natAbs ^ 2 + ((a : ℤ) * y + b * x + c * w - d * z).natAbs ^ 2 + ((a : ℤ) * z - b * w + c * x + d * y).natAbs ^ 2 + ((a : ℤ) * w + b * z - c * y + d * x).natAbs ^ 2 = (a ^ 2 + b ^ 2 + c ^ 2 + d ^ 2) * (x ^ 2 + y ^ 2 + z ^ 2 + w ^ 2)

views.nl_informal: Lagrange's **four squares theorem** for a prime number. Use `Nat.sum_four_squares` instead.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.Prime.sum_four_squares {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) : ∃ a b c d : ℕ, a ^ 2 + b ^ 2 + c ^ 2 + d ^ 2 = p

views.nl_informal: **Four squares theorem**
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.sum_four_squares (n : ℕ) : ∃ a b c d : ℕ, a ^ 2 + b ^ 2 + c ^ 2 + d ^ 2 = n

views.nl_informal:
The cardinality of the set of `k`-rough numbers `≤ N` is bounded by `N` times the sum
of `1/p` over the primes `k ≤ p ≤ N`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.roughNumbersUpTo_card_le' (N k : ℕ) : (roughNumbersUpTo N k).card ≤ N * (N.succ.primesBelow \ k.primesBelow).sum (fun p ↦ (1 : ℝ) / p)

views.nl_informal: The sum over primes `k ≤ p ≤ 4^(π(k-1)+1)` over `1/p` (as a real number) is at least `1/2`.
views.lean_signature: theorem one_half_le_sum_primes_ge_one_div (k : ℕ) : 1 / 2 ≤ ∑ p ∈ (4 ^ (k.primesBelow.card + 1)).succ.primesBelow \ k.primesBelow, (1 / p : ℝ)

views.nl_informal: The sum over the reciprocals of the primes diverges.
views.lean_signature: theorem not_summable_one_div_on_primes : ¬ Summable (indicator {p | p.Prime} (fun n : ℕ ↦ (1 : ℝ) / n))

views.nl_informal: The sum over the reciprocals of the primes diverges.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.Primes.not_summable_one_div : ¬ Summable (fun p : Nat.Primes ↦ (1 / p : ℝ))

views.nl_informal: The series over `p^r` for primes `p` converges if and only if `r < -1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.Primes.summable_rpow {r : ℝ} : Summable (fun p : Nat.Primes ↦ (p : ℝ) ^ r) ↔ r < -1

views.nl_informal:
**Fermat's theorem on the sum of two squares**. Every prime not congruent to 3 mod 4 is the sum
of two squares. Also known as **Fermat's Christmas theorem**.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.Prime.sq_add_sq {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (hp : p % 4 ≠ 3) : ∃ a b : ℕ, a ^ 2 + b ^ 2 = p

views.nl_informal:
The set of sums of two squares is closed under multiplication in any commutative ring.
See also `sq_add_sq_mul_sq_add_sq`.
views.lean_signature: theorem sq_add_sq_mul {R} [CommRing R] {a b x y u v : R} (ha : a = x ^ 2 + y ^ 2) (hb : b = u ^ 2 + v ^ 2) : ∃ r s : R, a * b = r ^ 2 + s ^ 2

views.nl_informal: The set of natural numbers that are sums of two squares is closed under multiplication.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.sq_add_sq_mul {a b x y u v : ℕ} (ha : a = x ^ 2 + y ^ 2) (hb : b = u ^ 2 + v ^ 2) : ∃ r s : ℕ, a * b = r ^ 2 + s ^ 2

views.nl_informal: If `-1` is a square modulo `n` and `m` divides `n`, then `-1` is also a square modulo `m`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.isSquare_neg_one_of_dvd {m n : ℕ} (hd : m ∣ n) (hs : IsSquare (-1 : ZMod n)) : IsSquare (-1 : ZMod m)

views.nl_informal:
If `-1` is a square modulo coprime natural numbers `m` and `n`, then `-1` is also
a square modulo `m*n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.isSquare_neg_one_mul {m n : ℕ} (hc : m.Coprime n) (hm : IsSquare (-1 : ZMod m)) (hn : IsSquare (-1 : ZMod n)) : IsSquare (-1 : ZMod (m * n))

views.nl_informal: If a prime `p` divides `n` such that `-1` is a square modulo `n`, then `p % 4 ≠ 3`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.Prime.mod_four_ne_three_of_dvd_isSquare_neg_one {p n : ℕ} (hpp : p.Prime) (hp : p ∣ n) (hs : IsSquare (-1 : ZMod n)) : p % 4 ≠ 3

views.nl_informal:
If `n` is a squarefree natural number, then `-1` is a square modulo `n` if and only if
`n` is not divisible by a prime `q` such that `q % 4 = 3`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.isSquare_neg_one_iff {n : ℕ} (hn : Squarefree n) : IsSquare (-1 : ZMod n) ↔ ∀ {q : ℕ}, q.Prime → q ∣ n → q % 4 ≠ 3

views.nl_informal:
If `n` is a squarefree natural number, then `-1` is a square modulo `n` if and only if
`n` has no divisor `q` that is `≡ 3 mod 4`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.isSquare_neg_one_iff' {n : ℕ} (hn : Squarefree n) : IsSquare (-1 : ZMod n) ↔ ∀ {q : ℕ}, q ∣ n → q % 4 ≠ 3

views.nl_informal: If `-1` is a square modulo the natural number `n`, then `n` is a sum of two squares.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.eq_sq_add_sq_of_isSquare_mod_neg_one {n : ℕ} (h : IsSquare (-1 : ZMod n)) : ∃ x y : ℕ, n = x ^ 2 + y ^ 2

views.nl_informal:
If the integer `n` is a sum of two squares of coprime integers,
then `-1` is a square modulo `n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.isSquare_neg_one_of_eq_sq_add_sq_of_isCoprime {n x y : ℤ} (h : n = x ^ 2 + y ^ 2) (hc : IsCoprime x y) : IsSquare (-1 : ZMod n.natAbs)

views.nl_informal:
If the natural number `n` is a sum of two squares of coprime natural numbers, then
`-1` is a square modulo `n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.isSquare_neg_one_of_eq_sq_add_sq_of_coprime {n x y : ℕ} (h : n = x ^ 2 + y ^ 2) (hc : x.Coprime y) : IsSquare (-1 : ZMod n)

views.nl_informal:
A natural number `n` is a sum of two squares if and only if `n = a^2 * b` with natural
numbers `a` and `b` such that `-1` is a square modulo `b`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.eq_sq_add_sq_iff_eq_sq_mul {n : ℕ} : (∃ x y : ℕ, n = x ^ 2 + y ^ 2) ↔ ∃ a b : ℕ, n = a ^ 2 * b ∧ IsSquare (-1 : ZMod b)

views.nl_informal:
A (positive) natural number `n` is a sum of two squares if and only if the exponent of
every prime `q` such that `q % 4 = 3` in the prime factorization of `n` is even.
(The assumption `0 < n` is not present, since for `n = 0`, both sides are satisfied;
the right hand side holds, since `padicValNat q 0 = 0` by definition.)
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.eq_sq_add_sq_iff {n : ℕ} : (∃ x y : ℕ, n = x ^ 2 + y ^ 2) ↔ ∀ {q : ℕ}, q.Prime → q % 4 = 3 → Even (padicValNat q n)

views.nl_informal: **Wilson's Lemma**: the product of `1`, ..., `p-1` is `-1` modulo `p`.

views.nl_informal:
We can partition a finite family into `partition_card ε` sets, such that the remainders
in each set are close together.
views.lean_signature: theorem AbsoluteValue.exists_partition_int (n : ℕ) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) {b : ℤ} (hb : b ≠ 0) (A : Fin n → ℤ) : ∃ t : Fin n → Fin ⌈1 / ε⌉₊, ∀ i₀ i₁, t i₀ = t i₁ → ↑(abs (A i₁ % b - A i₀ % b)) < abs b • ε

views.nl_informal:
For all `ε > 0` and finite families `A`, we can partition the remainders of `A` mod `b`
into `abv.card ε` sets, such that all elements in each part of remainders are close together.
views.lean_signature: theorem AbsoluteValue.IsAdmissible.exists_partition {ι : Type*} [Finite ι] {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) {b : R} (hb : b ≠ 0) (A : ι → R) (h : abv.IsAdmissible) : ∃ t : ι → Fin (h.card ε), ∀ i₀ i₁, t i₀ = t i₁ → (abv (A i₁ % b - A i₀ % b) : ℝ) < abv b • ε

views.nl_informal:
Any large enough family of vectors in `R^n` has a pair of elements
whose remainders are close together, pointwise.
views.lean_signature: theorem AbsoluteValue.IsAdmissible.exists_approx_aux (n : ℕ) (h : abv.IsAdmissible) : ∀ {ε : ℝ} (_hε : 0 < ε) {b : R} (_hb : b ≠ 0) (A : Fin (h.card ε ^ n).succ → Fin n → R), ∃ i₀ i₁, i₀ ≠ i₁ ∧ ∀ k, (abv (A i₁ k % b - A i₀ k % b) : ℝ) < abv b • ε

views.nl_informal:
Any large enough family of vectors in `R^ι` has a pair of elements
whose remainders are close together, pointwise.
views.lean_signature: theorem AbsoluteValue.IsAdmissible.exists_approx {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) {b : R} (hb : b ≠ 0) (h : abv.IsAdmissible) (A : Fin (h.card ε ^ Fintype.card ι).succ → ι → R) : ∃ i₀ i₁, i₀ ≠ i₁ ∧ ∀ k, (abv (A i₁ k % b - A i₀ k % b) : ℝ) < abv b • ε

views.nl_informal:
If `A` is a family of enough low-degree polynomials over a finite semiring, there is a
pair of equal elements in `A`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Polynomial.exists_eq_polynomial [Semiring Fq] {d : ℕ} {m : ℕ} (hm : Fintype.card Fq ^ d ≤ m) (b : Fq[X]) (hb : natDegree b ≤ d) (A : Fin m.succ → Fq[X]) (hA : ∀ i, degree (A i) < degree b) : ∃ i₀ i₁, i₀ ≠ i₁ ∧ A i₁ = A i₀

views.nl_informal:
If `A` is a family of enough low-degree polynomials over a finite ring,
there is a pair of elements in `A` (with different indices but not necessarily
distinct), such that their difference has small degree.
views.lean_signature: theorem Polynomial.exists_approx_polynomial_aux [Ring Fq] {d : ℕ} {m : ℕ} (hm : Fintype.card Fq ^ d ≤ m) (b : Fq[X]) (A : Fin m.succ → Fq[X]) (hA : ∀ i, degree (A i) < degree b) : ∃ i₀ i₁, i₀ ≠ i₁ ∧ degree (A i₁ - A i₀) < ↑(natDegree b - d)

views.nl_informal:
If `A` is a family of enough low-degree polynomials over a finite field,
there is a pair of elements in `A` (with different indices but not necessarily
distinct), such that the difference of their remainders is close together.
views.lean_signature: theorem Polynomial.exists_approx_polynomial {b : Fq[X]} (hb : b ≠ 0) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (A : Fin (Fintype.card Fq ^ ⌈-log ε / log (Fintype.card Fq)⌉₊).succ → Fq[X]) : ∃ i₀ i₁, i₀ ≠ i₁ ∧ (cardPowDegree (A i₁ % b - A i₀ % b) : ℝ) < cardPowDegree b • ε

views.nl_informal: If `x` is close to `y` and `y` is close to `z`, then `x` and `z` are at least as close.
views.lean_signature: theorem Polynomial.cardPowDegree_anti_archimedean {x y z : Fq[X]} {a : ℤ} (hxy : cardPowDegree (x - y) < a) (hyz : cardPowDegree (y - z) < a) : cardPowDegree (x - z) < a

views.nl_informal:
A slightly stronger version of `exists_partition` on which we perform induction on `n`:
for all `ε > 0`, we can partition the remainders of any family of polynomials `A`
into equivalence classes, where the equivalence(!) relation is "closer than `ε`".
views.lean_signature: theorem Polynomial.exists_partition_polynomial_aux (n : ℕ) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) {b : Fq[X]} (hb : b ≠ 0) (A : Fin n → Fq[X]) : ∃ t : Fin n → Fin (Fintype.card Fq ^ ⌈-log ε / log (Fintype.card Fq)⌉₊), ∀ i₀ i₁ : Fin n, t i₀ = t i₁ ↔ (cardPowDegree (A i₁ % b - A i₀ % b) : ℝ) < cardPowDegree b • ε

views.nl_informal:
For all `ε > 0`, we can partition the remainders of any family of polynomials `A`
into classes, where all remainders in a class are close together.
views.lean_signature: theorem Polynomial.exists_partition_polynomial (n : ℕ) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) {b : Fq[X]} (hb : b ≠ 0) (A : Fin n → Fq[X]) : ∃ t : Fin n → Fin (Fintype.card Fq ^ ⌈-log ε / log (Fintype.card Fq)⌉₊), ∀ i₀ i₁ : Fin n, t i₀ = t i₁ → (cardPowDegree (A i₁ % b - A i₀ % b) : ℝ) < cardPowDegree b • ε

views.nl_informal:
If the `R`-integral element `a : S` has coordinates `≤ y` with respect to some basis `b`,

views.lean_signature: theorem ClassGroup.norm_le (a : S) {y : ℤ} (hy : ∀ k, abv (bS.repr a k) ≤ y) : abv (Algebra.norm R a) ≤ normBound abv bS * y ^ Fintype.card ι

views.nl_informal:
If the `R`-integral element `a : S` has coordinates `< y` with respect to some basis `b`,
its norm is strictly less than `normBound abv b * y ^ dim S`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ClassGroup.norm_lt {T : Type*} [Ring T] [LinearOrder T] [IsStrictOrderedRing T] (a : S) {y : T} (hy : ∀ k, (abv (bS.repr a k) : T) < y) : (abv (Algebra.norm R a) : T) < normBound abv bS * y ^ Fintype.card ι

views.nl_informal: A nonzero ideal has an element of minimal norm.
views.lean_signature: theorem ClassGroup.exists_min (I : (Ideal S)⁰) : ∃ b ∈ (I : Ideal S), b ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ c ∈ (I : Ideal S), abv (Algebra.norm R c) < abv (Algebra.norm R b) → c = (0 : S)

views.nl_informal: We can approximate `a / b : L` with `q / r`, where `r` has finitely many options for `L`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ClassGroup.exists_mem_finsetApprox (a : S) {b} (hb : b ≠ (0 : R)) : ∃ q : S, ∃ r ∈ finsetApprox bS adm, abv (Algebra.norm R (r • a - b • q)) < abv (Algebra.norm R (algebraMap R S b))

views.nl_informal: We can approximate `a / b : L` with `q / r`, where `r` has finitely many options for `L`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ClassGroup.exists_mem_finset_approx' [Algebra.IsAlgebraic R S] (a : S) {b : S} (hb : b ≠ 0) : ∃ q : S, ∃ r ∈ finsetApprox bS adm, abv (Algebra.norm R (r • a - q * b)) < abv (Algebra.norm R b)

views.nl_informal:
Each class in the class group contains an ideal `J`

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:

views.lean_signature: theorem IsCyclotomicExtension.iff_union_of_dvd (h : ∀ s ∈ S, n ∣ s) (hS : S.Nonempty) : IsCyclotomicExtension S A B ↔ IsCyclotomicExtension (S ∪ {n}) A B

views.lean_signature: theorem IsCyclotomicExtension.numberField [h : NumberField K] [Finite S] [IsCyclotomicExtension S K L] : NumberField L

views.lean_signature: theorem IsCyclotomicExtension.splits_X_pow_sub_one [H : IsCyclotomicExtension S K L] (hS : n ∈ S) : Splits (algebraMap K L) (X ^ (n : ℕ) - 1)

views.lean_signature: theorem IsCyclotomicExtension.splitting_field_cyclotomic : IsSplittingField K L (cyclotomic n K)

The relationship between `IsPrimitiveRoot.autToPow` and

views.lean_signature: theorem IsPrimitiveRoot.autToPow_eq_ModularCyclotomicCharacter (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [Algebra R L] {μ : L} (hμ : IsPrimitiveRoot μ n) (g : L ≃ₐ[R] L) : hμ.autToPow R g = ModularCyclotomicCharacter L hμ.card_rootsOfUnity g

views.nl_informal:
The discriminant of the power basis given by a primitive root of unity `ζ` is the same as the
discriminant of the power basis given by `ζ - 1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsPrimitiveRoot.discr_zeta_eq_discr_zeta_sub_one (hζ : IsPrimitiveRoot ζ n) : discr ℚ (hζ.powerBasis ℚ).basis = discr ℚ (hζ.subOnePowerBasis ℚ).basis

views.nl_informal:
If `p` is a prime and `IsCyclotomicExtension {p ^ (k + 1)} K L`, then the discriminant of
`hζ.powerBasis K` is `(-1) ^ ((p ^ (k + 1).totient) / 2) * p ^ (p ^ k * ((p - 1) * (k + 1) - 1))`
if `Irreducible (cyclotomic (p ^ (k + 1)) K))`, and `p ^ (k + 1) ≠ 2`.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsCyclotomicExtension.discr_prime_pow_ne_two [IsCyclotomicExtension {p ^ (k + 1)} K L] [hp : Fact (p : ℕ).Prime] (hζ : IsPrimitiveRoot ζ ↑(p ^ (k + 1))) (hirr : Irreducible (cyclotomic (↑(p ^ (k + 1)) : ℕ) K)) (hk : p ^ (k + 1) ≠ 2) : discr K (hζ.powerBasis K).basis = (-1) ^ ((p ^ (k + 1) : ℕ).totient / 2) * p ^ ((p : ℕ) ^ k * ((p - 1) * (k + 1) - 1))

views.nl_informal:
If `p` is a prime and `IsCyclotomicExtension {p ^ (k + 1)} K L`, then the discriminant of
`hζ.powerBasis K` is `(-1) ^ (p ^ k * (p - 1) / 2) * p ^ (p ^ k * ((p - 1) * (k + 1) - 1))`
if `Irreducible (cyclotomic (p ^ (k + 1)) K))`, and `p ^ (k + 1) ≠ 2`.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsCyclotomicExtension.discr_prime_pow_ne_two' [IsCyclotomicExtension {p ^ (k + 1)} K L] [hp : Fact (p : ℕ).Prime] (hζ : IsPrimitiveRoot ζ ↑(p ^ (k + 1))) (hirr : Irreducible (cyclotomic (↑(p ^ (k + 1)) : ℕ) K)) (hk : p ^ (k + 1) ≠ 2) : discr K (hζ.powerBasis K).basis = (-1) ^ ((p : ℕ) ^ k * (p - 1) / 2) * p ^ ((p : ℕ) ^ k * ((p - 1) * (k + 1) - 1))

views.nl_informal:
If `p` is a prime and `IsCyclotomicExtension {p ^ k} K L`, then the discriminant of
`hζ.powerBasis K` is `(-1) ^ ((p ^ k).totient / 2) * p ^ (p ^ (k - 1) * ((p - 1) * k - 1))`
if `Irreducible (cyclotomic (p ^ k) K))`. Beware that in the cases `p ^ k = 1` and `p ^ k = 2`
the formula uses `1 / 2 = 0` and `0 - 1 = 0`. It is useful only to have a uniform result.
See also `IsCyclotomicExtension.discr_prime_pow_eq_unit_mul_pow`.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsCyclotomicExtension.discr_prime_pow [hcycl : IsCyclotomicExtension {p ^ k} K L] [hp : Fact (p : ℕ).Prime] (hζ : IsPrimitiveRoot ζ ↑(p ^ k)) (hirr : Irreducible (cyclotomic (↑(p ^ k) : ℕ) K)) : discr K (hζ.powerBasis K).basis = (-1) ^ ((p ^ k : ℕ).totient / 2) * p ^ ((p : ℕ) ^ (k - 1) * ((p - 1) * k - 1))

views.nl_informal:
If `p` is a prime and `IsCyclotomicExtension {p ^ k} K L`, then there are `u : ℤˣ` and
`n : ℕ` such that the discriminant of `hζ.powerBasis K` is `u * p ^ n`. Often this is enough and
less cumbersome to use than `IsCyclotomicExtension.discr_prime_pow`.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsCyclotomicExtension.discr_prime_pow_eq_unit_mul_pow [IsCyclotomicExtension {p ^ k} K L] [hp : Fact (p : ℕ).Prime] (hζ : IsPrimitiveRoot ζ ↑(p ^ k)) (hirr : Irreducible (cyclotomic (↑(p ^ k) : ℕ) K)) : ∃ (u : ℤˣ) (n : ℕ), discr K (hζ.powerBasis K).basis = u * p ^ n

views.nl_informal:
If `p` is an odd prime and `IsCyclotomicExtension {p} K L`, then
`discr K (hζ.powerBasis K).basis = (-1) ^ ((p - 1) / 2) * p ^ (p - 2)` if
`Irreducible (cyclotomic p K)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsCyclotomicExtension.discr_odd_prime [IsCyclotomicExtension {p} K L] [hp : Fact (p : ℕ).Prime] (hζ : IsPrimitiveRoot ζ p) (hirr : Irreducible (cyclotomic p K)) (hodd : p ≠ 2) : discr K (hζ.powerBasis K).basis = (-1) ^ (((p : ℕ) - 1) / 2) * p ^ ((p : ℕ) - 2)

views.nl_informal:
If `x` is a root of unity (spelled as `IsOfFinOrder x`) in an `n`-th cyclotomic extension of

views.nl_informal:
If `x` is a root of unity (spelled as `IsOfFinOrder x`) in an `n`-th cyclotomic extension of

views.nl_informal: We have that `x ^ 3 - 1 = (x - 1) * (x - η) * (x - η ^ 2)`.

views.nl_informal: We have that `λ` divides `x * (x - 1) * (x - (η + 1))`.

views.nl_informal:
*Dirichlet's approximation theorem:*
For any real number `ξ` and positive natural `n`, there are integers `j` and `k`,
with `0 < k ≤ n` and `|k*ξ - j| ≤ 1/(n+1)`.

See also `Real.exists_nat_abs_mul_sub_round_le`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Real.exists_int_int_abs_mul_sub_le (ξ : ℝ) {n : ℕ} (n_pos : 0 < n) : ∃ j k : ℤ, 0 < k ∧ k ≤ n ∧ |↑k * ξ - j| ≤ 1 / (n + 1)

views.nl_informal:
*Dirichlet's approximation theorem:*
For any real number `ξ` and positive natural `n`, there is a natural number `k`,
with `0 < k ≤ n` such that `|k*ξ - round(k*ξ)| ≤ 1/(n+1)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Real.exists_nat_abs_mul_sub_round_le (ξ : ℝ) {n : ℕ} (n_pos : 0 < n) : ∃ k : ℕ, 0 < k ∧ k ≤ n ∧ |↑k * ξ - round (↑k * ξ)| ≤ 1 / (n + 1)

views.nl_informal:
*Dirichlet's approximation theorem:*
For any real number `ξ` and positive natural `n`, there is a fraction `q`
such that `q.den ≤ n` and `|ξ - q| ≤ 1/((n+1)*q.den)`.

See also `AddCircle.exists_norm_nsmul_le`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Real.exists_rat_abs_sub_le_and_den_le (ξ : ℝ) {n : ℕ} (n_pos : 0 < n) : ∃ q : ℚ, |ξ - q| ≤ 1 / ((n + 1) * q.den) ∧ q.den ≤ n

views.nl_informal:
Given any rational approximation `q` to the irrational real number `ξ`, there is
a good rational approximation `q'` such that `|ξ - q'| < |ξ - q|`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Real.exists_rat_abs_sub_lt_and_lt_of_irrational {ξ : ℝ} (hξ : Irrational ξ) (q : ℚ) : ∃ q' : ℚ, |ξ - q'| < 1 / (q'.den : ℝ) ^ 2 ∧ |ξ - q'| < |ξ - q|

views.nl_informal:
If `ξ` is an irrational real number, then there are infinitely many good
rational approximations to `ξ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Real.infinite_rat_abs_sub_lt_one_div_den_sq_of_irrational {ξ : ℝ} (hξ : Irrational ξ) : {q : ℚ | |ξ - q| < 1 / (q.den : ℝ) ^ 2}.Infinite

views.nl_informal:
If `ξ` is rational, then the good rational approximations to `ξ` have bounded
numerator and denominator.
views.lean_signature: theorem Rat.den_le_and_le_num_le_of_sub_lt_one_div_den_sq {ξ q : ℚ} (h : |ξ - q| < 1 / (q.den : ℚ) ^ 2) : q.den ≤ ξ.den ∧ ⌈ξ * q.den⌉ - 1 ≤ q.num ∧ q.num ≤ ⌊ξ * q.den⌋ + 1

views.nl_informal: A rational number has only finitely many good rational approximations.
views.lean_signature: theorem Rat.finite_rat_abs_sub_lt_one_div_den_sq (ξ : ℚ) : {q : ℚ | |ξ - q| < 1 / (q.den : ℚ) ^ 2}.Finite

views.nl_informal:
The set of good rational approximations to a real number `ξ` is infinite if and only if
`ξ` is irrational.
views.lean_signature: theorem Real.infinite_rat_abs_sub_lt_one_div_den_sq_iff_irrational (ξ : ℝ) : {q : ℚ | |ξ - q| < 1 / (q.den : ℝ) ^ 2}.Infinite ↔ Irrational ξ

views.nl_informal: The zeroth convergent of `ξ` is `⌊ξ⌋`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Real.convergent_zero (ξ : ℝ) : ξ.convergent 0 = ⌊ξ⌋

views.nl_informal: The `(n+1)`th convergent of `ξ` is the `n`th convergent of `1/(fract ξ)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Real.convergent_succ (ξ : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : ξ.convergent (n + 1) = ⌊ξ⌋ + ((fract ξ)⁻¹.convergent n)⁻¹

views.nl_informal: All convergents of `0` are zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem Real.convergent_of_zero (n : ℕ) : convergent 0 n = 0

views.nl_informal: If `ξ` is an integer, all its convergents equal `ξ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Real.convergent_of_int {ξ : ℤ} (n : ℕ) : convergent ξ n = ξ

views.nl_informal: The technical version of *Legendre's Theorem*.
views.lean_signature: theorem Real.exists_rat_eq_convergent' {v : ℕ} (h : ContfracLegendre.Ass ξ u v) : ∃ n, (u / v : ℚ) = ξ.convergent n

views.nl_informal:
The main result, *Legendre's Theorem* on rational approximation:
if `ξ` is a real number and `q` is a rational number such that `|ξ - q| < 1/(2*q.den^2)`,
then `q` is a convergent of the continued fraction expansion of `ξ`.
This version uses `Real.convergent`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Real.exists_rat_eq_convergent {q : ℚ} (h : |ξ - q| < 1 / (2 * (q.den : ℝ) ^ 2)) : ∃ n, q = ξ.convergent n

views.nl_informal: The `n`th convergent of the `GenContFract.of ξ` agrees with `ξ.convergent n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Real.convs_eq_convergent (ξ : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : (GenContFract.of ξ).convs n = ξ.convergent n

views.nl_informal:
The main result, *Legendre's Theorem* on rational approximation:
if `ξ` is a real number and `q` is a rational number such that `|ξ - q| < 1/(2*q.den^2)`,
then `q` is a convergent of the continued fraction expansion of `ξ`.
This is the version using `GenContFract.convs`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Real.exists_convs_eq_rat {q : ℚ} (h : |ξ - q| < 1 / (2 * (q.den : ℝ) ^ 2)) : ∃ n, (GenContFract.of ξ).convs n = q

views.nl_informal: The `changeLevel` map is injective (except in the degenerate case `m = 0`).
views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.changeLevel_injective {m : ℕ} [NeZero m] (hm : n ∣ m) : Function.Injective (changeLevel (R := R) hm)

views.nl_informal: The fact that `d` divides `n` when `χ` factors through a Dirichlet character at level `d`
views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.FactorsThrough.dvd {d : ℕ} (h : FactorsThrough χ d) : d ∣ n

views.nl_informal: The fact that `χ` factors through `χ₀` of level `d`
views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.FactorsThrough.eq_changeLevel {d : ℕ} (h : FactorsThrough χ d) : χ = changeLevel h.dvd h.χ₀

views.nl_informal: The character of level `d` through which `χ` factors is uniquely determined.
views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.FactorsThrough.existsUnique {d : ℕ} [NeZero n] (h : FactorsThrough χ d) : ∃! χ' : DirichletCharacter R d, χ = changeLevel h.dvd χ'

views.nl_informal:
A Dirichlet character `χ` factors through `d | n` iff its associated unit-group hom is trivial
on the kernel of `ZMod.unitsMap`.
views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.factorsThrough_iff_ker_unitsMap {d : ℕ} [NeZero n] (hd : d ∣ n) : FactorsThrough χ d ↔ (ZMod.unitsMap hd).ker ≤ χ.toUnitHom.ker

views.nl_informal: A Dirichlet character of modulus `≠ 1` maps `0` to `0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.map_zero' (hn : n ≠ 1) : χ 0 = 0

views.nl_informal: The conductor of the trivial character is 1.
views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.conductor_one (hn : n ≠ 0) : conductor (1 : DirichletCharacter R n) = 1

views.nl_informal: An even Dirichlet character is an even function.
views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.Even.to_fun {χ : DirichletCharacter S m} (hχ : Even χ) : Function.Even χ

views.nl_informal: An odd Dirichlet character is an odd function.
views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.Odd.to_fun {χ : DirichletCharacter S m} (hχ : Odd χ) : Function.Odd χ

views.nl_informal: The value at a unit of a Dirichlet character with target a normed field has norm `1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.unit_norm_eq_one (a : (ZMod n)ˣ) : ‖χ a‖ = 1

views.nl_informal: The values of a Dirichlet character with target a normed field have norm bounded by `1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.norm_le_one (a : ZMod n) : ‖χ a‖ ≤ 1

views.nl_informal:
If `gaussSum χ e ≠ 0`, and `d` is such that `e.mulShift d = 1`, then `χ` must factor through
`d`. (This will be used to show that Gauss sums vanish when `χ` is primitive and `e` is not.)
views.lean_signature: theorem factorsThrough_of_gaussSum_ne_zero [IsDomain R] {χ : DirichletCharacter R N} {d : ℕ} (hd : d ∣ N) (he : e.mulShift d = 1) (h_ne : gaussSum χ e ≠ 0) : χ.FactorsThrough d

views.nl_informal: If `χ` is primitive, but `e` is not, then `gaussSum χ e = 0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem gaussSum_eq_zero_of_isPrimitive_of_not_isPrimitive [IsDomain R] {χ : DirichletCharacter R N} (hχ : IsPrimitive χ) (he : ¬IsPrimitive e) : gaussSum χ e = 0

views.nl_informal:
If `χ` is a primitive character, then the function `a ↦ gaussSum χ (e.mulShift a)`, for any
fixed additive character `e`, is a constant multiple of `χ⁻¹`.
views.lean_signature: theorem gaussSum_mulShift_of_isPrimitive [IsDomain R] {χ : DirichletCharacter R N} (hχ : IsPrimitive χ) (a : ZMod N) : gaussSum χ (e.mulShift a) = χ⁻¹ a * gaussSum χ e

views.nl_informal:
The group of Dirichlet characters mod `n` with values in a ring `R` that has enough
roots of unity is (noncanonically) isomorphic to `(ZMod n)ˣ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.mulEquiv_units : Nonempty (DirichletCharacter R n ≃* (ZMod n)ˣ)

views.nl_informal:
There are `n.totient` Dirichlet characters mod `n` with values in a ring that has enough
roots of unity.
views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.card_eq_totient_of_hasEnoughRootsOfUnity : Nat.card (DirichletCharacter R n) = n.totient

views.nl_informal:
If `R` is a ring that has enough roots of unity and `n ≠ 0`, then for each
`a ≠ 1` in `ZMod n`, there exists a Dirichlet character `χ` mod `n` with values in `R`
such that `χ a ≠ 1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.exists_apply_ne_one_of_hasEnoughRootsOfUnity [Nontrivial R] ⦃a : ZMod n⦄ (ha : a ≠ 1) : ∃ χ : DirichletCharacter R n, χ a ≠ 1

views.nl_informal:
If `R` is an integral domain that has enough roots of unity and `n ≠ 0`, then
for each `a ≠ 1` in `ZMod n`, the sum of `χ a` over all Dirichlet characters mod `n`
with values in `R` vanishes.
views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.sum_characters_eq_zero ⦃a : ZMod n⦄ (ha : a ≠ 1) : ∑ χ : DirichletCharacter R n, χ a = 0

views.nl_informal:
If `R` is an integral domain that has enough roots of unity and `n ≠ 0`, then
for `a` in `ZMod n`, the sum of `χ a` over all Dirichlet characters mod `n`
with values in `R` vanishes if `a ≠ 1` and has the value `n.totient` if `a = 1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.sum_characters_eq (a : ZMod n) : ∑ χ : DirichletCharacter R n, χ a = if a = 1 then (n.totient : R) else 0

views.nl_informal:
If `R` is an integral domain that has enough roots of unity and `n ≠ 0`, then for `a` and `b`
in `ZMod n` with `a` a unit, the sum of `χ a⁻¹ * χ b` over all Dirichlet characters
mod `n` with values in `R` vanishes if `a ≠ b` and has the value `n.totient` if `a = b`.
views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.sum_char_inv_mul_char_eq {a : ZMod n} (ha : IsUnit a) (b : ZMod n) : ∑ χ : DirichletCharacter R n, χ a⁻¹ * χ b = if a = b then (n.totient : R) else 0

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is multiplicative and summable, then its values at natural numbers `> 1`
have norm strictly less than `1`.

views.nl_informal: We relate a finite product over primes in `s` to an infinite sum over `s`-factored numbers.
views.lean_signature: theorem EulerProduct.summable_and_hasSum_factoredNumbers_prod_filter_prime_tsum (hsum : ∀ {p : ℕ}, p.Prime → Summable (fun n : ℕ ↦ ‖f (p ^ n)‖)) (s : Finset ℕ) : Summable (fun m : factoredNumbers s ↦ ‖f m‖) ∧ HasSum (fun m : factoredNumbers s ↦ f m) (∏ p ∈ s with p.Prime, ∑' n : ℕ, f (p ^ n))

views.nl_informal:
The following statement says that summing over `s`-factored numbers such that
`s` contains `primesBelow N` for large enough `N` gets us arbitrarily close to the sum
over all natural numbers (assuming `f` is summable and `f 0 = 0`; the latter since
`0` is not `s`-factored).
views.lean_signature: theorem EulerProduct.norm_tsum_factoredNumbers_sub_tsum_lt (hsum : Summable f) (hf₀ : f 0 = 0) {ε : ℝ} (εpos : 0 < ε) : ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ s : Finset ℕ, primesBelow N ≤ s → ‖(∑' m : ℕ, f m) - ∑' m : factoredNumbers s, f m‖ < ε

views.nl_informal: We relate a finite product over primes to an infinite sum over smooth numbers.
views.lean_signature: theorem EulerProduct.summable_and_hasSum_smoothNumbers_prod_primesBelow_tsum (hsum : ∀ {p : ℕ}, p.Prime → Summable (fun n : ℕ ↦ ‖f (p ^ n)‖)) (N : ℕ) : Summable (fun m : N.smoothNumbers ↦ ‖f m‖) ∧ HasSum (fun m : N.smoothNumbers ↦ f m) (∏ p ∈ N.primesBelow, ∑' n : ℕ, f (p ^ n))

views.nl_informal:
The following statement says that summing over `N`-smooth numbers
for large enough `N` gets us arbitrarily close to the sum over all natural numbers
(assuming `f` is norm-summable and `f 0 = 0`; the latter since `0` is not smooth).
views.lean_signature: theorem EulerProduct.norm_tsum_smoothNumbers_sub_tsum_lt (hsum : Summable f) (hf₀ : f 0 = 0) {ε : ℝ} (εpos : 0 < ε) : ∃ N₀ : ℕ, ∀ N ≥ N₀, ‖(∑' m : ℕ, f m) - ∑' m : N.smoothNumbers, f m‖ < ε

multiplicative on coprime arguments, and `‖f ·‖` is summable, then

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:
Given a (completely) multiplicative function `f : ℕ → F`, where `F` is a normed field,
such that `‖f p‖ < 1` for all primes `p`, we can express the sum of `f n` over all `s`-factored
positive integers `n` as a product of `(1 - f p)⁻¹` over the primes `p ∈ s`. At the same time,
we show that the sum involved converges absolutely.
views.lean_signature: theorem EulerProduct.summable_and_hasSum_factoredNumbers_prod_filter_prime_geometric {f : ℕ →* F} (h : ∀ {p : ℕ}, p.Prime → ‖f p‖ < 1) (s : Finset ℕ) : Summable (fun m : factoredNumbers s ↦ ‖f m‖) ∧ HasSum (fun m : factoredNumbers s ↦ f m) (∏ p ∈ s with p.Prime, (1 - f p)⁻¹)

views.nl_informal:
Given a (completely) multiplicative function `f : ℕ → F`, where `F` is a normed field,
such that `‖f p‖ < 1` for all primes `p`, we can express the sum of `f n` over all `N`-smooth
positive integers `n` as a product of `(1 - f p)⁻¹` over the primes `p < N`. At the same time,
we show that the sum involved converges absolutely.
views.lean_signature: theorem EulerProduct.summable_and_hasSum_smoothNumbers_prod_primesBelow_geometric {f : ℕ →* F} (h : ∀ {p : ℕ}, p.Prime → ‖f p‖ < 1) (N : ℕ) : Summable (fun m : N.smoothNumbers ↦ ‖f m‖) ∧ HasSum (fun m : N.smoothNumbers ↦ f m) (∏ p ∈ N.primesBelow, (1 - f p)⁻¹)

views.lean_signature: theorem jacobiSum_mem_algebraAdjoin_of_pow_eq_one {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] {χ φ : MulChar F R} (hχ : χ ^ n = 1) (hφ : φ ^ n = 1) {μ : R} (hμ : IsPrimitiveRoot μ n) : jacobiSum χ φ ∈ Algebra.adjoin ℤ {μ}

views.nl_informal:
If `χ` and `ψ` are multiplicative characters of order dividing `n` on a finite field `F`
with values in an integral domain `R` and `μ` is a primitive `n`th root of unity in `R`,
then `J(χ,ψ) = -1 + z*(μ - 1)^2` for some `z ∈ ℤ[μ] ⊆ R`. (We assume that `#F ≡ 1 mod n`.)
Note that we do not state this as a divisibility in `R`, as this would give a weaker statement.
views.lean_signature: theorem exists_jacobiSum_eq_neg_one_add {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 < n) {χ ψ : MulChar F R} {μ : R} (hχ : χ ^ n = 1) (hψ : ψ ^ n = 1) (hn' : n ∣ Fintype.card F - 1) (hμ : IsPrimitiveRoot μ n) : ∃ z ∈ Algebra.adjoin ℤ {μ}, jacobiSum χ ψ = -1 + z * (μ - 1) ^ 2

views.nl_informal:
If `χ` is a multiplicative character of order `n ≥ 2` on a finite field `F`,
then `g(χ)^n = χ(-1) * #F * J(χ,χ) * J(χ,χ²) * ... * J(χ,χⁿ⁻²)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem gaussSum_pow_eq_prod_jacobiSum {χ : MulChar F R} {ψ : AddChar F R} (hχ : 2 ≤ orderOf χ) (hψ : ψ.IsPrimitive) : gaussSum χ ψ ^ orderOf χ = χ (-1) * Fintype.card F * ∏ i ∈ Ico 1 (orderOf χ - 1), jacobiSum χ (χ ^ i)

views.nl_informal: Functional equation formulated for `Λ`.

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:
If `f` and `g` agree on large `n : ℕ` and the `LSeries` of `f` converges at `s`,
then so does that of `g`.
views.lean_signature: theorem LSeriesSummable.congr' {f g : ℕ → ℂ} (s : ℂ) (h : f =ᶠ[atTop] g) (hf : LSeriesSummable f s) : LSeriesSummable g s

views.nl_informal:
If `f` and `g` agree on large `n : ℕ`, then the `LSeries` of `f` converges at `s`
if and only if that of `g` does.
views.lean_signature: theorem LSeriesSummable_congr' {f g : ℕ → ℂ} (s : ℂ) (h : f =ᶠ[atTop] g) : LSeriesSummable f s ↔ LSeriesSummable g s

views.nl_informal: The L-series of `δ` is the constant function `1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem LSeries_delta : LSeries δ = 1

views.nl_informal:
If the `LSeries` of `f` is summable at `s`, then `f n` is bounded in absolute value
by a constant times `n^(re s)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem LSeriesSummable.le_const_mul_rpow {f : ℕ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} (h : LSeriesSummable f s) : ∃ C, ∀ n ≠ 0, ‖f n‖ ≤ C * n ^ s.re

views.nl_informal: If the `LSeries` of `f` is summable at `s`, then `f = O(n^(re s))`.
views.lean_signature: theorem LSeriesSummable.isBigO_rpow {f : ℕ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} (h : LSeriesSummable f s) : f =O[atTop] fun n ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ s.re

views.nl_informal:
If `f n` is bounded in absolute value by a constant times `n^(x-1)` and `re s > x`,
then the `LSeries` of `f` is summable at `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem LSeriesSummable_of_le_const_mul_rpow {f : ℕ → ℂ} {x : ℝ} {s : ℂ} (hs : x < s.re) (h : ∃ C, ∀ n ≠ 0, ‖f n‖ ≤ C * n ^ (x - 1)) : LSeriesSummable f s

views.nl_informal: If `f = O(n^(x-1))` and `re s > x`, then the `LSeries` of `f` is summable at `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem LSeriesSummable_of_isBigO_rpow {f : ℕ → ℂ} {x : ℝ} {s : ℂ} (hs : x < s.re) (h : f =O[atTop] fun n ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (x - 1)) : LSeriesSummable f s

views.nl_informal: If `f` is bounded, then its `LSeries` is summable at `s` when `re s > 1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem LSeriesSummable_of_bounded_of_one_lt_re {f : ℕ → ℂ} {m : ℝ} (h : ∀ n ≠ 0, ‖f n‖ ≤ m) {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < s.re) : LSeriesSummable f s

views.nl_informal: If `f` is bounded, then its `LSeries` is summable at `s : ℝ` when `s > 1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem LSeriesSummable_of_bounded_of_one_lt_real {f : ℕ → ℂ} {m : ℝ} (h : ∀ n ≠ 0, ‖f n‖ ≤ m) {s : ℝ} (hs : 1 < s) : LSeriesSummable f s

views.nl_informal:
If `f` and `g` agree on large `n : ℕ`, then their `LSeries` have the same
abscissa of absolute convergence.
views.lean_signature: theorem LSeries.abscissaOfAbsConv_congr' {f g : ℕ → ℂ} (h : f =ᶠ[atTop] g) : abscissaOfAbsConv f = abscissaOfAbsConv g

views.nl_informal:
If `‖f n‖` is bounded by a constant times `n^x`, then the abscissa of absolute convergence
of `f` is bounded by `x + 1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem LSeries.abscissaOfAbsConv_le_of_le_const_mul_rpow {f : ℕ → ℂ} {x : ℝ} (h : ∃ C, ∀ n ≠ 0, ‖f n‖ ≤ C * n ^ x) : abscissaOfAbsConv f ≤ x + 1

views.nl_informal:
If `‖f n‖` is `O(n^x)`, then the abscissa of absolute convergence
of `f` is bounded by `x + 1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem LSeries.abscissaOfAbsConv_le_of_isBigO_rpow {f : ℕ → ℂ} {x : ℝ} (h : f =O[atTop] fun n ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ x) : abscissaOfAbsConv f ≤ x + 1

views.nl_informal: If `f` is bounded, then the abscissa of absolute convergence of `f` is bounded above by `1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem LSeries.abscissaOfAbsConv_le_of_le_const {f : ℕ → ℂ} (h : ∃ C, ∀ n ≠ 0, ‖f n‖ ≤ C) : abscissaOfAbsConv f ≤ 1

views.nl_informal: If `f` is `O(1)`, then the abscissa of absolute convergence of `f` is bounded above by `1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem LSeries.abscissaOfAbsConv_le_one_of_isBigO_one {f : ℕ → ℂ} (h : f =O[atTop] fun _ ↦ (1 : ℝ)) : abscissaOfAbsConv f ≤ 1

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is real-valued and `x` is strictly greater than the abscissa of absolute convergence
of `f`, then the real series `∑' n, f n / n ^ x` converges.
views.lean_signature: theorem LSeries.summable_real_of_abscissaOfAbsConv_lt {f : ℕ → ℝ} {x : ℝ} (h : abscissaOfAbsConv (f ·) < x) : Summable fun n : ℕ ↦ f n / (n : ℝ) ^ x

views.nl_informal:
If `F` is a binary operation on `ℕ → ℂ` with the property that the `LSeries` of `F f g`
converges whenever the `LSeries` of `f` and `g` do, then the abscissa of absolute convergence
of `F f g` is at most the maximum of the abscissa of absolute convergence of `f`
and that of `g`.

views.nl_informal:
If we consider an arithmetic function just as a function and turn it back into an
arithmetic function, it is the same as before.
views.lean_signature: theorem ArithmeticFunction.toArithmeticFunction_eq_self {R : Type*} [Zero R] (f : ArithmeticFunction R) : toArithmeticFunction f = f

views.nl_informal:
The product of two arithmetic functions defines the same function as the Dirichlet convolution
of the functions defined by them.
views.lean_signature: theorem ArithmeticFunction.coe_mul {R : Type*} [Semiring R] (f g : ArithmeticFunction R) : f ⍟ g = ⇑(f * g)

views.nl_informal:
We give an expression of the `LSeries.term` of the convolution of two functions
in terms of a sum over `Nat.divisorsAntidiagonal`.
views.lean_signature: theorem LSeries.term_convolution (f g : ℕ → ℂ) (s : ℂ) (n : ℕ) : term (f ⍟ g) s n = ∑ p ∈ n.divisorsAntidiagonal, term f s p.1 * term g s p.2

views.nl_informal:
We give an expression of the `LSeries.term` of the convolution of two functions
in terms of an a priori infinite sum over all pairs `(k, m)` with `k * m = n`
(the set we sum over is infinite when `n = 0`). This is the version needed for the
proof that `L (f ⍟ g) = L f * L g`.
views.lean_signature: theorem LSeries.term_convolution' (f g : ℕ → ℂ) (s : ℂ) : term (f ⍟ g) s = fun n ↦ ∑' (b : (fun p : ℕ × ℕ ↦ p.1 * p.2) ⁻¹' {n}), term f s b.val.1 * term g s b.val.2

views.nl_informal:
The L-series of the convolution product `f ⍟ g` of two sequences `f` and `g`
equals the product of their L-series, assuming both L-series converge.

views.nl_informal:
The L-series of the convolution product `f ⍟ g` of two sequences `f` and `g`
equals the product of their L-series, assuming both L-series converge.

views.nl_informal:
The L-series of the convolution product `f ⍟ g` of two sequences `f` and `g`
equals the product of their L-series in their common half-plane of absolute convergence.

views.nl_informal:
The L-series of the convolution product `f ⍟ g` of two sequences `f` and `g`
is summable when both L-series are summable.

views.nl_informal:
The abscissa of absolute convergence of `f ⍟ g` is at most the maximum of those
of `f` and `g`.

views.nl_informal:

equals the product of their L-series, assuming both L-series converge.

views.nl_informal:
The L-series of the (convolution) product of two `ℂ`-valued arithmetic functions `f` and `g`
equals the product of their L-series, assuming both L-series converge.

views.nl_informal:
The L-series of the (convolution) product of two `ℂ`-valued arithmetic functions `f` and `g`
equals the product of their L-series in their common half-plane of absolute convergence.

views.nl_informal:
The L-series of the (convolution) product of two `ℂ`-valued arithmetic functions `f` and `g`
is summable when both L-series are summable.

views.nl_informal: The derivative of the terms of an L-series.

views.nl_informal:
If `re s` is greater than the abscissa of absolute convergence of `f`, then the L-series

views.nl_informal:
If `re s` is greater than the abscissa of absolute convergence of `f`, then
the derivative of this L-series at `s` is the negative of the L-series of `log * f`.
views.lean_signature: theorem LSeries_deriv {f : ℕ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} (h : abscissaOfAbsConv f < s.re) : deriv (LSeries f) s = - LSeries (logMul f) s

views.nl_informal:
The derivative of the L-series of `f` agrees with the negative of the L-series of
`log * f` on the right half-plane of absolute convergence.

views.nl_informal:
If the L-series of `f` is summable at `s` and `re s < re s'`, then the L-series of the

views.lean_signature: theorem LSeriesSummable_logMul_of_lt_re {f : ℕ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} (h : abscissaOfAbsConv f < s.re) : LSeriesSummable (logMul f) s

views.nl_informal:
The abscissa of absolute convergence of the point-wise product of `log` and `f`
is the same as that of `f`.
views.lean_signature: theorem LSeries.abscissaOfAbsConv_logMul {f : ℕ → ℂ} : abscissaOfAbsConv (logMul f) = abscissaOfAbsConv f

views.nl_informal:
The abscissa of absolute convergence of the point-wise product of a power of `log` and `f`
is the same as that of `f`.
views.lean_signature: theorem LSeries.absicssaOfAbsConv_logPowMul {f : ℕ → ℂ} {m : ℕ} : abscissaOfAbsConv (logMul^[m] f) = abscissaOfAbsConv f

views.nl_informal:
If `re s` is greater than the abscissa of absolute convergence of `f`, then
the `m`th derivative of this L-series is `(-1)^m` times the L-series of `log^m * f`.

views.nl_informal:

convergence.
views.lean_signature: theorem LSeries_differentiableOn (f : ℕ → ℂ) : DifferentiableOn ℂ (LSeries f) {s | abscissaOfAbsConv f < s.re}

views.nl_informal: The L-series of `f` is holomorphic on its open half-plane of absolute convergence.
views.lean_signature: theorem LSeries_analyticOnNhd (f : ℕ → ℂ) : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ (LSeries f) {s | abscissaOfAbsConv f < s.re}

views.nl_informal: `δ` is the function underlying the arithmetic function `1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ArithmeticFunction.one_eq_delta : ↗(1 : ArithmeticFunction ℂ) = δ

views.nl_informal: The L-series of the Möbius function converges absolutely at `s` if and only if `re s > 1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ArithmeticFunction.LSeriesSummable_moebius_iff {s : ℂ} : LSeriesSummable ↗μ s ↔ 1 < s.re

views.nl_informal: The abscissa of absolute convergence of the L-series of the Möbius function is `1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ArithmeticFunction.abscissaOfAbsConv_moebius : abscissaOfAbsConv ↗μ = 1

views.nl_informal: The arithmetic function associated to a Dirichlet character is multiplicative.

the indicator function of `{1}`.

views.nl_informal: The Dirichlet character mod `1` corresponds to the constant function `1`.

views.nl_informal: The L-series of a Dirichlet character mod `N > 0` does not converge absolutely at `s = 1`.

views.nl_informal: The L-series of a Dirichlet character converges absolutely at `s` if `re s > 1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.LSeriesSummable_of_one_lt_re {N : ℕ} (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ N) {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < s.re) : LSeriesSummable ↗χ s

views.nl_informal:

`re s > 1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.LSeriesSummable_iff {N : ℕ} (hN : N ≠ 0) (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ N) {s : ℂ} : LSeriesSummable ↗χ s ↔ 1 < s.re

views.nl_informal:
The abscissa of absolute convergence of the L-series of a Dirichlet character mod `N > 0`
is `1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.absicssaOfAbsConv_eq_one {N : ℕ} (hn : N ≠ 0) (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ N) : abscissaOfAbsConv ↗χ = 1

views.nl_informal:

of `f` does.
views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.LSeriesSummable_mul {N : ℕ} (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ N) {f : ℕ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} (h : LSeriesSummable f s) : LSeriesSummable (↗χ * f) s

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:
A translation of the relation `Λ * ↑ζ = log` of (real-valued) arithmetic functions
to an equality of complex sequences.

views.lean_signature: theorem ArithmeticFunction.LSeriesSummable_vonMangoldt {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < s.re) : LSeriesSummable ↗Λ s

views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.convolution_twist_vonMangoldt {N : ℕ} (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ N) : (↗χ * ↗Λ) ⍟ ↗χ = ↗χ * ↗Complex.log

views.nl_informal:
The L-series of the twist of the von Mangoldt function `Λ` by a Dirichlet character `χ` at `s`

views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.LSeries_twist_vonMangoldt_eq {N : ℕ} (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ N) {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < s.re) : L (↗χ * ↗Λ) s = - deriv (L ↗χ) s / L ↗χ s

views.nl_informal:

views.lean_signature: theorem ArithmeticFunction.LSeries_vonMangoldt_eq_deriv_riemannZeta_div {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < s.re) : L ↗Λ s = - deriv riemannZeta s / riemannZeta s

views.nl_informal:
The L-function of the (unique) Dirichlet character mod 1 is the Riemann zeta function.
(Compare `DirichletCharacter.LSeries_modOne_eq`.)

views.nl_informal:

trivial.
views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.differentiableAt_LFunction (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ N) (s : ℂ) (hs : s ≠ 1 ∨ χ ≠ 1) : DifferentiableAt ℂ (LFunction χ) s

views.nl_informal: The L-function of a non-trivial Dirichlet character is differentiable everywhere.
views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.differentiable_LFunction {χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ N} (hχ : χ ≠ 1) : Differentiable ℂ (LFunction χ)

views.nl_informal: The L-function of an even Dirichlet character vanishes at strictly negative even integers.
views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.Even.LFunction_neg_two_mul_nat_add_one {χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ N} (hχ : Even χ) (n : ℕ) : LFunction χ (-(2 * (n + 1))) = 0

views.nl_informal: The L-function of an even Dirichlet character vanishes at strictly negative even integers.
views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.Even.LFunction_neg_two_mul_nat {χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ N} (hχ : Even χ) (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] : LFunction χ (-(2 * n)) = 0

views.nl_informal: The L-function of an odd Dirichlet character vanishes at negative odd integers.
views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.Odd.LFunction_neg_two_mul_nat_sub_one {χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ N} (hχ : Odd χ) (n : ℕ) : LFunction χ (-(2 * n) - 1) = 0

views.nl_informal:
If `χ` is a Dirichlet character and its level `M` divides `N`, then we obtain the L function
of `χ` considered as a Dirichlet character of level `N` from the L function of `χ` by multiplying
with `∏ p ∈ N.primeFactors, (1 - χ p * p ^ (-s))`.
(Note that `1 - χ p * p ^ (-s) = 1` when `p` divides `M`).
views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.LFunction_changeLevel {M N : ℕ} [NeZero M] [NeZero N] (hMN : M ∣ N) (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ M) {s : ℂ} (h : χ ≠ 1 ∨ s ≠ 1) : LFunction (changeLevel hMN χ) s = LFunction χ s * ∏ p ∈ N.primeFactors, (1 - χ p * p ^ (-s))

views.nl_informal:
The L function of the trivial Dirichlet character mod `N` is obtained from the Riemann
zeta function by multiplying with `∏ p ∈ N.primeFactors, (1 - (p : ℂ) ^ (-s))`.
views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.LFunctionTrivChar_eq_mul_riemannZeta {s : ℂ} (hs : s ≠ 1) : LFunctionTrivChar N s = (∏ p ∈ N.primeFactors, (1 - (p : ℂ) ^ (-s))) * riemannZeta s

views.nl_informal:
The L function of the trivial Dirichlet character mod `N` has a simple pole with
residue `∏ p ∈ N.primeFactors, (1 - p⁻¹)` at `s = 1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.LFunctionTrivChar_residue_one : Tendsto (fun s ↦ (s - 1) * LFunctionTrivChar N s) (𝓝[≠] 1) (𝓝 <| ∏ p ∈ N.primeFactors, (1 - (p : ℂ)⁻¹))

views.nl_informal:
The completed L-function of the (unique) Dirichlet character mod 1 is the completed Riemann zeta
function.
views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.completedLFunction_modOne_eq {χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ 1} : completedLFunction χ = completedRiemannZeta

views.nl_informal:
The completed L-function of a Dirichlet character is differentiable, with the following
exceptions: at `s = 1` if `χ` is the trivial character (to any modulus); and at `s = 0` if the
modulus is 1. This result is best possible.

Note both `χ` and `s` are explicit arguments: we will always be able to infer one or other
of them from the hypotheses, but it's not clear which!
views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.differentiableAt_completedLFunction (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ N) (s : ℂ) (hs₀ : s ≠ 0 ∨ N ≠ 1) (hs₁ : s ≠ 1 ∨ χ ≠ 1) : DifferentiableAt ℂ (completedLFunction χ) s

views.nl_informal: The completed L-function of a non-trivial Dirichlet character is differentiable everywhere.
views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.differentiable_completedLFunction {χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ N} (hχ : χ ≠ 1) : Differentiable ℂ (completedLFunction χ)

views.nl_informal:
Relation between the completed L-function and the usual one. We state it this way around so
it holds at the poles of the gamma factor as well.
views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.LFunction_eq_completed_div_gammaFactor (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ N) (s : ℂ) (h : s ≠ 0 ∨ N ≠ 1) : LFunction χ s = completedLFunction χ s / gammaFactor χ s

views.nl_informal: The root number of the unique Dirichlet character modulo 1 is 1.
views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.rootNumber_modOne (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ 1) : rootNumber χ = 1

views.nl_informal: **Functional equation** for primitive Dirichlet L-functions.
views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.IsPrimitive.completedLFunction_one_sub {χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ N} (hχ : IsPrimitive χ) (s : ℂ) : completedLFunction χ (1 - s) = N ^ (s - 1 / 2) * rootNumber χ * completedLFunction χ⁻¹ s

views.nl_informal: `s ↦ (s - 1) * L χ s` is an entire function when `χ` is a trivial Dirichlet character.
views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.differentiable_LFunctionTrivChar₁ : Differentiable ℂ (LFunctionTrivChar₁ n)

views.nl_informal:
The negative logarithmtic derivative of `s ↦ (s - 1) * L χ s` for a trivial
Dirichlet character `χ` is continuous away from the zeros of `L χ` (including at `s = 1`).
views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.continuousOn_neg_logDeriv_LFunctionTrivChar₁ : ContinuousOn (fun s ↦ -deriv (LFunctionTrivChar₁ n) s / LFunctionTrivChar₁ n s) {s | s = 1 ∨ LFunctionTrivChar n s ≠ 0}

views.nl_informal:
The negative logarithmic derivative of the L-function of a nontrivial Dirichlet character
is continuous away from the zeros of the L-function.
views.lean_signature: theorem DirichletCharacter.continuousOn_neg_logDeriv_LFunction_of_nontriv (hχ : χ ≠ 1) : ContinuousOn (fun s ↦ -deriv (LFunction χ) s / LFunction χ s) {s | LFunction χ s ≠ 0}

views.nl_informal: The Hurwitz zeta function is differentiable away from `s = 1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem HurwitzZeta.differentiableAt_hurwitzZeta (a : UnitAddCircle) {s : ℂ} (hs : s ≠ 1) : DifferentiableAt ℂ (hurwitzZeta a) s

views.nl_informal:
Formula for `hurwitzZeta s` as a Dirichlet series in the convergence range. We
