views.nl_informal: The residue of the Hurwitz zeta function at `s = 1` is `1`.

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal: The difference of two Hurwitz zeta functions is differentiable everywhere.
views.lean_signature: theorem HurwitzZeta.differentiable_hurwitzZeta_sub_hurwitzZeta (a b : UnitAddCircle) : Differentiable ℂ (fun s ↦ hurwitzZeta a s - hurwitzZeta b s)

views.nl_informal: If `a ≠ 0` then the exponential zeta function is analytic everywhere.
views.lean_signature: theorem HurwitzZeta.differentiable_expZeta_of_ne_zero {a : UnitAddCircle} (ha : a ≠ 0) : Differentiable ℂ (expZeta a)

views.nl_informal: Functional equation for the exponential zeta function.
views.lean_signature: theorem HurwitzZeta.expZeta_one_sub (a : UnitAddCircle) {s : ℂ} (hs : ∀ (n : ℕ), s ≠ 1 - n) : expZeta a (1 - s) = (2 * π) ^ (-s) * Gamma s * (exp (π * I * s / 2) * hurwitzZeta a s + exp (-π * I * s / 2) * hurwitzZeta (-a) s)

views.nl_informal: For `x ≤ 0` the defining sum diverges, so the kernel is 0.

views.nl_informal:
The function `evenKernel a - L` has exponential decay at `+∞`, where `L = 1` if

views.nl_informal: Functional equation for the even Hurwitz zeta function.

views.nl_informal: Functional equation for the even Hurwitz zeta function with poles removed.
views.lean_signature: theorem HurwitzZeta.completedHurwitzZetaEven₀_one_sub (a : UnitAddCircle) (s : ℂ) : completedHurwitzZetaEven₀ a (1 - s) = completedCosZeta₀ a s

views.nl_informal: Functional equation for the even Hurwitz zeta function (alternative form).
views.lean_signature: theorem HurwitzZeta.completedCosZeta_one_sub (a : UnitAddCircle) (s : ℂ) : completedCosZeta a (1 - s) = completedHurwitzZetaEven a s

views.nl_informal: Functional equation for the even Hurwitz zeta function with poles removed (alternative form).
views.lean_signature: theorem HurwitzZeta.completedCosZeta₀_one_sub (a : UnitAddCircle) (s : ℂ) : completedCosZeta₀ a (1 - s) = completedHurwitzZetaEven₀ a s

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal: The difference of two completed even Hurwitz zeta functions is differentiable at `s = 1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem HurwitzZeta.differentiableAt_one_completedHurwitzZetaEven_sub_completedHurwitzZetaEven (a b : UnitAddCircle) : DifferentiableAt ℂ (fun s ↦ completedHurwitzZetaEven a s - completedHurwitzZetaEven b s) 1

views.nl_informal: The residue of `completedHurwitzZetaEven a s` at `s = 1` is equal to `1`.

views.nl_informal: The trivial zeroes of the even Hurwitz zeta function.

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal: Formula for `hurwitzZetaEven` as a Dirichlet series in the convergence range, with sum over `ℤ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem HurwitzZeta.hasSum_int_hurwitzZetaEven (a : ℝ) {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < re s) : HasSum (fun n : ℤ ↦ 1 / (↑|n + a| : ℂ) ^ s / 2) (hurwitzZetaEven a s)

views.nl_informal:
Formula for `hurwitzZetaEven` as a Dirichlet series in the convergence range, with sum over `ℕ`
(version with absolute values)
views.lean_signature: theorem HurwitzZeta.hasSum_nat_hurwitzZetaEven (a : ℝ) {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < re s) : HasSum (fun n : ℕ ↦ (1 / (↑|n + a| : ℂ) ^ s + 1 / (↑|n + 1 - a| : ℂ) ^ s) / 2) (hurwitzZetaEven a s)

views.nl_informal:

(version without absolute values, assuming `a ∈ Icc 0 1`)

views.nl_informal: The trivial zeroes of the cosine zeta function.

views.nl_informal: The cosine zeta function is differentiable everywhere, except at `s = 1` if `a = 0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem HurwitzZeta.differentiableAt_cosZeta (a : UnitAddCircle) {s : ℂ} (hs' : s ≠ 1 ∨ a ≠ 0) : DifferentiableAt ℂ (cosZeta a) s

views.nl_informal: If `a ≠ 0` then the cosine zeta function is entire.
views.lean_signature: theorem HurwitzZeta.differentiable_cosZeta_of_ne_zero {a : UnitAddCircle} (ha : a ≠ 0) : Differentiable ℂ (cosZeta a)

views.nl_informal: Formula for `cosZeta` as a Dirichlet series in the convergence range, with sum over `ℤ`.

views.nl_informal: Formula for `cosZeta` as a Dirichlet series in the convergence range, with sum over `ℕ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem HurwitzZeta.hasSum_nat_cosZeta (a : ℝ) {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < re s) : HasSum (fun n : ℕ ↦ Real.cos (2 * π * a * n) / (n : ℂ) ^ s) (cosZeta a s)

views.nl_informal:

`hurwitzZetaEven a (1 - s)` is an explicit multiple of `cosZeta s`.

views.nl_informal:

then `f n = g n` whenever `n ≠ 0`.

characters mod `q` (including at `s = 1`).
views.lean_signature: theorem ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt.continuousOn_LFunctionResidueClassAux' : ContinuousOn (LFunctionResidueClassAux a) {s | s = 1 ∨ ∀ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, LFunction χ s ≠ 0}

views.nl_informal:
The L-series of the von Mangoldt function restricted to the prime residue class `a` mod `q`
is continuous on `re s ≥ 1` except for a simple pole at `s = 1` with residue `(q.totient)⁻¹`.
The statement as given here in terms of `ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt.LFunctionResidueClassAux`
is equivalent.
views.lean_signature: theorem ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt.continuousOn_LFunctionResidueClassAux : ContinuousOn (LFunctionResidueClassAux a) {s | 1 ≤ s.re}

views.nl_informal:
The auxiliary function agrees on `re s > 1` with the L-series of the von Mangoldt function
restricted to the residue class `a : ZMod q` minus the principal part `(q.totient)⁻¹/(s-1)`
of its pole at `s = 1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt.eqOn_LFunctionResidueClassAux (ha : IsUnit a) : Set.EqOn (LFunctionResidueClassAux a) (fun s ↦ L ↗(residueClass a) s - (q.totient : ℂ)⁻¹ / (s - 1)) {s | 1 < s.re}

views.nl_informal: The auxiliary function takes real values for real arguments `x > 1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt.LFunctionResidueClassAux_real (ha : IsUnit a) {x : ℝ} (hx : 1 < x) : LFunctionResidueClassAux a x = (LFunctionResidueClassAux a x).re

views.nl_informal:
As `x` approaches `1` from the right along the real axis, the L-series of
`ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt.residueClass` is bounded below by `(q.totient)⁻¹/(x-1) - C`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt.LSeries_residueClass_lower_bound (ha : IsUnit a) : ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ {x : ℝ} (_ : x ∈ Set.Ioc 1 2), (q.totient : ℝ)⁻¹ / (x - 1) - C ≤ ∑' n, residueClass a n / (n : ℝ) ^ x

views.nl_informal:
The function `n ↦ Λ n / n` restricted to primes in an invertible residue class
is not summable. This then implies that there must be infinitely many such primes.
views.lean_signature: theorem ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt.not_summable_residueClass_prime_div (ha : IsUnit a) : ¬ Summable fun n : ℕ ↦ (if n.Prime then residueClass a n else 0) / n

views.nl_informal:
**Dirichlet's Theorem** on primes in arithmetic progression: if `q` is a positive
integer and `a : ZMod q` is a unit, then there are infinitely many prime numbers `p`
such that `(p : ZMod q) = a`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.setOf_prime_and_eq_mod_infinite (ha : IsUnit a) : {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ (p : ZMod q) = a}.Infinite

views.nl_informal:
**Dirichlet's Theorem** on primes in arithmetic progression: if `q` is a positive
integer and `a : ZMod q` is a unit, then there are infinitely many prime numbers `p`
such that `(p : ZMod q) = a`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.forall_exists_prime_gt_and_eq_mod (ha : IsUnit a) (n : ℕ) : ∃ p > n, p.Prime ∧ (p : ZMod q) = a

views.nl_informal: The modified completed Riemann zeta function `Λ(s) + 1 / s + 1 / (1 - s)` is entire.
views.lean_signature: theorem differentiable_completedZeta₀ : Differentiable ℂ completedRiemannZeta₀

views.nl_informal: The completed Riemann zeta function `Λ(s)` is differentiable away from `s = 0` and `s = 1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem differentiableAt_completedZeta {s : ℂ} (hs : s ≠ 0) (hs' : s ≠ 1) : DifferentiableAt ℂ completedRiemannZeta s

views.nl_informal:
Riemann zeta functional equation, formulated for `Λ₀`: for any complex `s` we have
`Λ₀(1 - s) = Λ₀ s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem completedRiemannZeta₀_one_sub (s : ℂ) : completedRiemannZeta₀ (1 - s) = completedRiemannZeta₀ s

views.nl_informal:
Riemann zeta functional equation, formulated for `Λ`: for any complex `s` we have
`Λ (1 - s) = Λ s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem completedRiemannZeta_one_sub (s : ℂ) : completedRiemannZeta (1 - s) = completedRiemannZeta s

views.nl_informal: The residue of `Λ(s)` at `s = 1` is equal to `1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem completedRiemannZeta_residue_one : Tendsto (fun s ↦ (s - 1) * completedRiemannZeta s) (𝓝[≠] 1) (𝓝 1)

views.nl_informal: The Riemann zeta function is differentiable away from `s = 1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem differentiableAt_riemannZeta {s : ℂ} (hs' : s ≠ 1) : DifferentiableAt ℂ riemannZeta s
theorem riemannZeta_zero : riemannZeta 0 = -1 / 2

views.nl_informal: The trivial zeroes of the zeta function.
views.lean_signature: theorem riemannZeta_neg_two_mul_nat_add_one (n : ℕ) : riemannZeta (-2 * (n + 1)) = 0

views.nl_informal:
Riemann zeta functional equation, formulated for `ζ`: if `1 - s ∉ ℕ`, then we have

views.nl_informal:
The Riemann zeta function agrees with the naive Dirichlet-series definition when the latter
converges. (Note that this is false without the assumption: when `re s ≤ 1` the sum is divergent,
and we use a different definition to obtain the analytic continuation to all `s`.)
views.lean_signature: theorem zeta_eq_tsum_one_div_nat_cpow {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < re s) : riemannZeta s = ∑' n : ℕ, 1 / (n : ℂ) ^ s

views.nl_informal: The residue of `ζ(s)` at `s = 1` is equal to 1.
views.lean_signature: theorem riemannZeta_residue_one : Tendsto (fun s ↦ (s - 1) * riemannZeta s) (𝓝[≠] 1) (𝓝 1)

views.nl_informal: The residue of `ζ(s)` at `s = 1` is equal to 1, expressed using `tsum`.
views.lean_signature: theorem tendsto_sub_mul_tsum_nat_cpow : Tendsto (fun s : ℂ ↦ (s - 1) * ∑' (n : ℕ), 1 / (n : ℂ) ^ s) (𝓝[{s | 1 < re s}] 1) (𝓝 1)

views.nl_informal:
The residue of `ζ(s)` at `s = 1` is equal to 1 expressed using `tsum` and for a
real variable.
views.lean_signature: theorem tendsto_sub_mul_tsum_nat_rpow : Tendsto (fun s : ℝ ↦ (s - 1) * ∑' (n : ℕ), 1 / (n : ℝ) ^ s) (𝓝[>] 1) (𝓝 1)

views.nl_informal:
If the partial sums `∑ k ∈ Icc 1 n, ‖f k‖` are `O(n ^ r)` for some real `0 ≤ r`, then the
L-series `LSeries f` converges at `s : ℂ` for all `s` such that `r < s.re`.
views.lean_signature: theorem LSeriesSummable_of_sum_norm_bigO (hO : (fun n ↦ ∑ k ∈ Icc 1 n, ‖f k‖) =O[atTop] fun n ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ r) (hr : 0 ≤ r) (hs : r < s.re) : LSeriesSummable f s

views.nl_informal:
If `f` takes nonnegative real values and the partial sums `∑ k ∈ Icc 1 n, f k` are `O(n ^ r)`
for some real `0 ≤ r`, then the L-series `LSeries f` converges at `s : ℂ` for all `s`
such that `r < s.re`.
views.lean_signature: theorem LSeriesSummable_of_sum_norm_bigO_and_nonneg {f : ℕ → ℝ} (hO : (fun n ↦ ∑ k ∈ Icc 1 n, f k) =O[atTop] fun n ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ r) (hf : ∀ n, 0 ≤ f n) (hr : 0 ≤ r) (hs : r < s.re) : LSeriesSummable (fun n ↦ f n) s

views.nl_informal:
If the partial sums `∑ k ∈ Icc 1 n, f k` are `O(n ^ r)` for some real `0 ≤ r` and the
L-series `LSeries f` converges at `s : ℂ` with `r < s.re`, then
`LSeries f s = s * ∫ t in Set.Ioi 1, (∑ k ∈ Icc 1 ⌊t⌋₊, f k) * t ^ (-(s + 1))`.
views.lean_signature: theorem LSeries_eq_mul_integral (f : ℕ → ℂ) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 ≤ r) {s : ℂ} (hs : r < s.re) (hS : LSeriesSummable f s) (hO : (fun n ↦ ∑ k ∈ Icc 1 n, f k) =O[atTop] fun n ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ r) : LSeries f s = s * ∫ t in Set.Ioi (1 : ℝ), (∑ k ∈ Icc 1 ⌊t⌋₊, f k) * t ^ (-(s + 1))

views.nl_informal:
If `f` takes nonnegative real values and the partial sums `∑ k ∈ Icc 1 n, f k` are `O(n ^ r)`
for some real `0 ≤ r`, then for `s : ℂ` with `r < s.re`, we have
`LSeries f s = s * ∫ t in Set.Ioi 1, (∑ k ∈ Icc 1 ⌊t⌋₊, f k) * t ^ (-(s + 1))`.
views.lean_signature: theorem LSeries_eq_mul_integral_of_nonneg (f : ℕ → ℝ) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 ≤ r) {s : ℂ} (hs : r < s.re) (hO : (fun n ↦ ∑ k ∈ Icc 1 n, f k) =O[atTop] fun n ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ r) (hf : ∀ n, 0 ≤ f n) : LSeries (fun n ↦ f n) s = s * ∫ t in Set.Ioi (1 : ℝ), (∑ k ∈ Icc 1 ⌊t⌋₊, (f k : ℂ)) * t ^ (-(s + 1))

views.nl_informal: If `Φ` is a periodic function, then the L-series of `Φ` converges for `1 < re s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.LSeriesSummable_of_one_lt_re (Φ : ZMod N → ℂ) {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < re s) : LSeriesSummable (Φ ·) s

views.nl_informal: The L-function of a function on `ZMod 1` is a scalar multiple of the Riemann zeta function.
views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.LFunction_modOne_eq (Φ : ZMod 1 → ℂ) (s : ℂ) : LFunction Φ s = Φ 0 * riemannZeta s

views.nl_informal: For `1 < re s` the congruence L-function agrees with the sum of the Dirichlet series.
views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.LFunction_eq_LSeries (Φ : ZMod N → ℂ) {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < re s) : LFunction Φ s = LSeries (Φ ·) s

views.nl_informal: The L-function of `Φ` has a residue at `s = 1` equal to the average value of `Φ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.LFunction_residue_one (Φ : ZMod N → ℂ) : Tendsto (fun s ↦ (s - 1) * LFunction Φ s) (𝓝[≠] 1) (𝓝 (∑ j, Φ j / N))

views.nl_informal:
The `LFunction` of the function `x ↦ e (j * x)`, where `e : ZMod N → ℂ` is the standard additive
character, agrees with `expZeta (j / N)` on `1 < re s`. Private since it is a stepping-stone to
the more general result `LFunction_stdAddChar_eq_expZeta` below.
views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.LFunction_stdAddChar_eq_expZeta_of_one_lt_re (j : ZMod N) {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < s.re) : LFunction (fun k ↦ 𝕖 (j * k)) s = expZeta (ZMod.toAddCircle j) s

views.nl_informal:
The `LFunction` of the function `x ↦ e (j * x)`, where `e : ZMod N → ℂ` is the standard additive
character, is `expZeta (j / N)`.

Note this is not at all obvious from the definitions, and we prove it by analytic continuation
from the convergence range.
views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.LFunction_stdAddChar_eq_expZeta (j : ZMod N) (s : ℂ) (hjs : j ≠ 0 ∨ s ≠ 1) : LFunction (fun k ↦ 𝕖 (j * k)) s = expZeta (ZMod.toAddCircle j) s

views.nl_informal: Explicit formula for the L-function of `𝓕 Φ`, where `𝓕` is the discrete Fourier transform.
views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.LFunction_dft (Φ : ZMod N → ℂ) {s : ℂ} (hs : Φ 0 = 0 ∨ s ≠ 1) : LFunction (𝓕 Φ) s = ∑ j : ZMod N, Φ j * expZeta (toAddCircle (-j)) s

views.nl_informal: Functional equation for `ZMod` L-functions, in terms of discrete Fourier transform.
views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.LFunction_one_sub (Φ : ZMod N → ℂ) {s : ℂ} (hs : ∀ (n : ℕ), s ≠ -n) (hs' : Φ 0 = 0 ∨ s ≠ 1) : LFunction Φ (1 - s) = N ^ (s - 1) * (2 * π) ^ (-s) * Gamma s * (cexp (π * I * s / 2) * LFunction (𝓕 Φ) s + cexp (-π * I * s / 2) * LFunction (𝓕 fun x ↦ Φ (-x)) s)

views.nl_informal: Explicit formula for `LFunction Φ 0` when `Φ` is even.
views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.LFunction_apply_zero_of_even (hΦ : Φ.Even) : LFunction Φ 0 = -Φ 0 / 2

views.nl_informal: The L-function of an even function vanishes at negative even integers.
views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.LFunction_neg_two_mul_nat_add_one (hΦ : Φ.Even) (n : ℕ) : LFunction Φ (-(2 * (n + 1))) = 0

views.nl_informal: The L-function of an odd function vanishes at negative odd integers.
views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.LFunction_neg_two_mul_nat_sub_one (hΦ : Φ.Odd) (n : ℕ) : LFunction Φ (-(2 * n) - 1) = 0

views.nl_informal:
The completed L-function of a function `ZMod 1 → ℂ` is a scalar multiple of the completed Riemann
zeta function.
views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.completedLFunction_modOne_eq (Φ : ZMod 1 → ℂ) (s : ℂ) : completedLFunction Φ s = Φ 1 * completedRiemannZeta s

views.nl_informal: The function `completedLFunction₀ Φ` is differentiable.
views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.differentiable_completedLFunction₀ (Φ : ZMod N → ℂ) : Differentiable ℂ (completedLFunction₀ Φ)

views.nl_informal:
The completed L-function of a function `ZMod N → ℂ` is differentiable, with the following
exceptions: at `s = 1` if `∑ j, Φ j ≠ 0`; and at `s = 0` if `Φ 0 ≠ 0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.differentiableAt_completedLFunction (Φ : ZMod N → ℂ) (s : ℂ) (hs₀ : s ≠ 0 ∨ Φ 0 = 0) (hs₁ : s ≠ 1 ∨ ∑ j, Φ j = 0) : DifferentiableAt ℂ (completedLFunction Φ) s

views.nl_informal:
Special case of `differentiableAt_completedLFunction` asserting differentiability everywhere
under suitable hypotheses.
views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.differentiable_completedLFunction (hΦ₂ : Φ 0 = 0) (hΦ₃ : ∑ j, Φ j = 0) : Differentiable ℂ (completedLFunction Φ)

views.nl_informal:
Relation between the completed L-function and the usual one (even case).
We state it this way around so it holds at the poles of the gamma factor as well

views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.LFunction_eq_completed_div_gammaFactor_even (hΦ : Φ.Even) (s : ℂ) (hs : s ≠ 0 ∨ Φ 0 = 0) : LFunction Φ s = completedLFunction Φ s / Gammaℝ s

views.nl_informal:
Relation between the completed L-function and the usual one (odd case).
We state it this way around so it holds at the poles of the gamma factor as well.

First form of functional equation for completed L-functions (even case).

Private because it is superseded by `completedLFunction_one_sub_even` below, which is valid for a
much wider range of `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.completedLFunction_one_sub_of_one_lt_even (hΦ : Φ.Even) {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < re s) : completedLFunction Φ (1 - s) = N ^ (s - 1) * completedLFunction (𝓕 Φ) s

views.nl_informal:
First form of functional equation for completed L-functions (odd case).

Private because it is superseded by `completedLFunction_one_sub_odd` below, which is valid for a
much wider range of `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.completedLFunction_one_sub_of_one_lt_odd (hΦ : Φ.Odd) {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < re s) : completedLFunction Φ (1 - s) = N ^ (s - 1) * I * completedLFunction (𝓕 Φ) s

views.nl_informal: Functional equation for completed L-functions (even case), valid at all points of differentiability.
views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.completedLFunction_one_sub_even (hΦ : Φ.Even) (s : ℂ) (hs₀ : s ≠ 0 ∨ ∑ j, Φ j = 0) (hs₁ : s ≠ 1 ∨ Φ 0 = 0) : completedLFunction Φ (1 - s) = N ^ (s - 1) * completedLFunction (𝓕 Φ) s

views.nl_informal: Functional equation for completed L-functions (odd case), valid for all `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.completedLFunction_one_sub_odd (hΦ : Φ.Odd) (s : ℂ) : completedLFunction Φ (1 - s) = N ^ (s - 1) * I * completedLFunction (𝓕 Φ) s

views.nl_informal: The values of an additive character on a ring of positive characteristic are roots of unity.

views.nl_informal:
The map associating to `a : R` the multiplicative shift of `ψ` by `a`
is injective when `ψ` is primitive.
views.lean_signature: theorem AddChar.to_mulShift_inj_of_isPrimitive {ψ : AddChar R R'} (hψ : IsPrimitive ψ) : Function.Injective ψ.mulShift

views.nl_informal: When `R` is a field `F`, then a nontrivial additive character is primitive

views.lean_signature: theorem AddChar.exists_divisor_of_not_isPrimitive (he : ¬e.IsPrimitive) : ∃ d : ℕ, d ∣ N ∧ d < N ∧ e.mulShift d = 1

views.nl_informal: The additive character on `ZMod n` defined using `ζ` sends `a` to `ζ^a`.
views.lean_signature: theorem AddChar.zmodChar_apply {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] {ζ : C} (hζ : ζ ^ n = 1) (a : ZMod n) : zmodChar n hζ a = ζ ^ a.val

views.nl_informal: A primitive additive character on `ZMod n` takes the value `1` only at `0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem AddChar.IsPrimitive.zmod_char_eq_one_iff (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] {ψ : AddChar (ZMod n) C} (hψ : IsPrimitive ψ) (a : ZMod n) : ψ a = 1 ↔ a = 0

views.nl_informal:
The converse: if the additive character takes the value `1` only at `0`,
then it is primitive.

The additive character on `ZMod n` associated to a primitive `n`th root of unity
is primitive

The sum over the values of a nontrivial additive character vanishes if the target ring

views.nl_informal: The sum over the values of the trivial additive character is the cardinality of the source.

views.nl_informal: Euler's Criterion: A unit `x` of `ZMod p` is a square if and only if `x ^ (p / 2) = 1`.

views.nl_informal: We have the congruence `legendreSym p a ≡ a ^ (p / 2) mod p`.
views.lean_signature: theorem legendreSym.eq_pow (a : ℤ) : (legendreSym p a : ZMod p) = (a : ZMod p) ^ (p / 2)

views.nl_informal: If `p ∤ a`, then `legendreSym p a` is `1` or `-1`.

views.nl_informal: The Legendre symbol of `p` and `a` is zero iff `p ∣ a`.

views.nl_informal: The Legendre symbol is multiplicative in `a` for `p` fixed.

views.nl_informal: The square of the symbol is 1 if `p ∤ a`.

views.nl_informal: The Legendre symbol depends only on `a` mod `p`.

views.nl_informal:
The Legendre symbol `legendreSym p a = 1` if there is a solution in `ℤ/pℤ`
of the equation `x^2 - a*y^2 = 0` with `y ≠ 0`.

views.nl_informal:
The Legendre symbol `legendreSym p a = 1` if there is a solution in `ℤ/pℤ`
of the equation `x^2 - a*y^2 = 0` with `x ≠ 0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem legendreSym.eq_one_of_sq_sub_mul_sq_eq_zero' {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {a : ℤ} (ha : (a : ZMod p) ≠ 0) {x y : ZMod p} (hx : x ≠ 0) (hxy : x ^ 2 - a * y ^ 2 = 0) : legendreSym p a = 1

views.nl_informal:
If `legendreSym p a = -1`, then the only solution of `x^2 - a*y^2 = 0` in `ℤ/pℤ`
is the trivial one.
views.lean_signature: theorem legendreSym.eq_zero_mod_of_eq_neg_one {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {a : ℤ} (h : legendreSym p a = -1) {x y : ZMod p} (hxy : x ^ 2 - a * y ^ 2 = 0) : x = 0 ∧ y = 0

views.nl_informal: If `legendreSym p a = -1` and `p` divides `x^2 - a*y^2`, then `p` must divide `x` and `y`.
views.lean_signature: theorem legendreSym.prime_dvd_of_eq_neg_one {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {a : ℤ} (h : legendreSym p a = -1) {x y : ℤ} (hxy : (p : ℤ) ∣ x ^ 2 - a * y ^ 2) : ↑p ∣ x ∧ ↑p ∣ y

views.nl_informal: `legendreSym p (-1)` is given by `χ₄ p`.

views.nl_informal: `-1` is a square in `ZMod p` iff `p` is not congruent to `3` mod `4`.

views.nl_informal: If two nonzero squares are negatives of each other in `ZMod p`, then `p % 4 ≠ 3`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.mod_four_ne_three_of_sq_eq_neg_sq' {x y : ZMod p} (hy : y ≠ 0) (hxy : x ^ 2 = -y ^ 2) : p % 4 ≠ 3

views.nl_informal:
The image of the map sending a nonzero natural number `x ≤ p / 2` to the absolute value
of the integer in `(-p/2, p/2]` that is congruent to `a * x mod p` is the set
of nonzero natural numbers `x` such that `x ≤ p / 2`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.Ico_map_valMinAbs_natAbs_eq_Ico_map_id (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact p.Prime] (a : ZMod p) (hap : a ≠ 0) : ((Ico 1 (p / 2).succ).1.map fun (x : ℕ) => (a * x).valMinAbs.natAbs) = (Ico 1 (p / 2).succ).1.map fun a => a

views.nl_informal:
**Gauss' lemma**. The Legendre symbol can be computed by considering the number of naturals less
than `p/2` such that `(a * x) % p > p / 2`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.gauss_lemma {p : ℕ} [h : Fact p.Prime] {a : ℤ} (hp : p ≠ 2) (ha0 : (a : ZMod p) ≠ 0) : legendreSym p a = (-1) ^ #{x ∈ Ico 1 (p / 2).succ | p / 2 < (a * x.cast : ZMod p).val}

views.nl_informal:
The given sum is the number of integer points in the triangle formed by the diagonal of the
rectangle `(0, p/2) × (0, q/2)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.sum_Ico_eq_card_lt {p q : ℕ} : ∑ a ∈ Ico 1 (p / 2).succ, a * q / p = #{x ∈ Ico 1 (p / 2).succ ×ˢ Ico 1 (q / 2).succ | x.2 * p ≤ x.1 * q}

views.nl_informal:
Each of the sums in this lemma is the cardinality of the set of integer points in each of the
two triangles formed by the diagonal of the rectangle `(0, p/2) × (0, q/2)`. Adding them
gives the number of points in the rectangle.
views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.sum_mul_div_add_sum_mul_div_eq_mul (p q : ℕ) [hp : Fact p.Prime] (hq0 : (q : ZMod p) ≠ 0) : ∑ a ∈ Ico 1 (p / 2).succ, a * q / p + ∑ a ∈ Ico 1 (q / 2).succ, a * p / q = p / 2 * (q / 2)

views.lean_signature: theorem ZMod.eisenstein_lemma {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (hp : p ≠ 2) {a : ℕ} (ha1 : a % 2 = 1) (ha0 : (a : ZMod p) ≠ 0) : legendreSym p a = (-1) ^ ∑ x ∈ Ico 1 (p / 2).succ, x * a / p

views.nl_informal: The Jacobi symbol is multiplicative in its first argument.
