views.lean_signature: theorem MulChar.IsQuadratic.sq_eq_one {χ : MulChar R R'} (hχ : χ.IsQuadratic) : χ ^ 2 = 1

views.nl_informal:
The `p`th power of a quadratic character is itself, when `p` is the (prime) characteristic
of the target ring.
views.lean_signature: theorem MulChar.IsQuadratic.pow_char {χ : MulChar R R'} (hχ : χ.IsQuadratic) (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact p.Prime] [CharP R' p] : χ ^ p = χ

views.nl_informal: The `n`th power of a quadratic character is the trivial character, when `n` is even.
views.lean_signature: theorem MulChar.IsQuadratic.pow_even {χ : MulChar R R'} (hχ : χ.IsQuadratic) {n : ℕ} (hn : Even n) : χ ^ n = 1

views.nl_informal: The `n`th power of a quadratic character is itself, when `n` is odd.
views.lean_signature: theorem MulChar.IsQuadratic.pow_odd {χ : MulChar R R'} (hχ : χ.IsQuadratic) {n : ℕ} (hn : Odd n) : χ ^ n = χ

views.nl_informal:
A multiplicative character `χ` into an integral domain is quadratic
if and only if `χ^2 = 1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MulChar.isQuadratic_iff_sq_eq_one {M R : Type*} [CommMonoid M] [CommRing R] [NoZeroDivisors R] [Nontrivial R] {χ : MulChar M R} : IsQuadratic χ ↔ χ ^ 2 = 1

views.nl_informal:
If `χ` is a multiplicative character on a commutative monoid `M` with finitely many units,
then `χ ^ #Mˣ = 1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MulChar.pow_card_eq_one [Fintype Mˣ] (χ : MulChar M R) : χ ^ (Fintype.card Mˣ) = 1

views.nl_informal:
A multiplicative character on a commutative monoid with finitely many units
has finite (= positive) order.
views.lean_signature: theorem MulChar.orderOf_pos [Finite Mˣ] (χ : MulChar M R) : 0 < orderOf χ

views.nl_informal:
The sum over all values of a nontrivial multiplicative character on a finite ring is zero
(when the target is a domain).
views.lean_signature: theorem MulChar.sum_eq_zero_of_ne_one [IsDomain R'] {χ : MulChar R R'} (hχ : χ ≠ 1) : ∑ a, χ a = 0

views.nl_informal:
The sum over all values of the trivial multiplicative character on a finite ring is
the cardinality of its unit group.
views.lean_signature: theorem MulChar.sum_one_eq_card_units [DecidableEq R] : (∑ a, (1 : MulChar R R') a) = Fintype.card Rˣ

views.nl_informal: If `χ` is of odd order, then `χ(-1) = 1`
views.lean_signature: theorem MulChar.val_neg_one_eq_one_of_odd_order {χ : MulChar R R'} {n : ℕ} (hn : Odd n) (hχ : χ ^ n = 1) : χ (-1) = 1

views.nl_informal:
If `M` is a finite commutative monoid and `R` is a ring that has enough roots of unity,
then for each `a ≠ 1` in `M`, there exists a multiplicative character `χ : M → R` such that
`χ a ≠ 1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MulChar.exists_apply_ne_one_of_hasEnoughRootsOfUnity [Nontrivial R] {a : M} (ha : a ≠ 1) : ∃ χ : MulChar M R, χ a ≠ 1

views.nl_informal:
The group of `R`-valued multiplicative characters on a finite commutative monoid `M` is
(noncanonically) isomorphic to its unit group `Mˣ` when `R` is a ring that has enough roots
of unity.
views.lean_signature: theorem MulChar.mulEquiv_units : Nonempty (MulChar M R ≃* Mˣ)

views.nl_informal:
The cardinality of the group of `R`-valued multiplicative characters on a finite commutative
monoid `M` is the same as that of its unit group `Mˣ` when `R` is a ring that has enough roots
of unity.
views.lean_signature: theorem MulChar.card_eq_card_units_of_hasEnoughRootsOfUnity : Nat.card (MulChar M R) = Nat.card Mˣ

views.nl_informal:
Two multiplicative characters on a monoid whose unit group is generated by `g`
are equal if and only if they agree on `g`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MulChar.eq_iff {R R' : Type*} [CommMonoid R] [CommMonoidWithZero R'] {g : Rˣ} (hg : ∀ x, x ∈ Subgroup.zpowers g) (χ₁ χ₂ : MulChar R R') : χ₁ = χ₂ ↔ χ₁ g.val = χ₂ g.val

views.nl_informal: The values of a multiplicative character on `R` are `n`th roots of unity, where `n = #Rˣ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MulChar.apply_mem_rootsOfUnity [Fintype Rˣ] (a : Rˣ) {χ : MulChar R R'} : equivToUnitHom χ a ∈ rootsOfUnity (Fintype.card Rˣ) R'

views.nl_informal: The conjugate of a multiplicative character with values in `ℂ` is its inverse.
views.lean_signature: theorem MulChar.star_eq_inv (χ : MulChar R ℂ) : star χ = χ⁻¹

views.nl_informal:
There is a character of order `n` on `F` if `#F ≡ 1 mod n` and the target contains
a primitive `n`th root of unity.
views.lean_signature: theorem MulChar.exists_mulChar_orderOf {n : ℕ} (h : n ∣ Fintype.card F - 1) {ζ : R} (hζ : IsPrimitiveRoot ζ n) : ∃ χ : MulChar F R, orderOf χ = n

views.nl_informal: If there is a multiplicative character of order `n` on `F`, then `#F ≡ 1 mod n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MulChar.orderOf_dvd_card_sub_one (χ : MulChar F R) : orderOf χ ∣ Fintype.card F - 1

views.nl_informal:
There is always a character on `F` of order `#F-1` with values in a ring that has
a primitive `(#F-1)`th root of unity.
views.lean_signature: theorem MulChar.exists_mulChar_orderOf_eq_card_units [DecidableEq F] {ζ : R} (hζ : IsPrimitiveRoot ζ (Fintype.card Fˣ)) : ∃ χ : MulChar F R, orderOf χ = Fintype.card Fˣ

views.nl_informal:
The non-zero values of a multiplicative character `χ` such that `χ^n = 1`
are `n`th roots of unity.
views.lean_signature: theorem MulChar.apply_mem_rootsOfUnity_of_pow_eq_one {χ : MulChar F R} {n : ℕ} (hχ : χ ^ n = 1) {a : F} (ha : a ≠ 0) : ∃ ζ ∈ rootsOfUnity n R, ζ = χ a

views.nl_informal:
If `χ` is a multiplicative character with `χ^n = 1` and `μ` is a primitive `n`th root
of unity, then, for `a ≠ 0`, there is some `k` such that `χ a = μ^k`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MulChar.exists_apply_eq_pow {χ : MulChar F R} {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] (hχ : χ ^ n = 1) {μ : R} (hμ : IsPrimitiveRoot μ n) {a : F} (ha : a ≠ 0) : ∃ k < n, χ a = μ ^ k

views.nl_informal:
The values of a multiplicative character `χ` such that `χ^n = 1` are contained in `ℤ[μ]` when
`μ` is a primitive `n`th root of unity.
views.lean_signature: theorem MulChar.apply_mem_algebraAdjoin_of_pow_eq_one {χ : MulChar F R} {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] (hχ : χ ^ n = 1) {μ : R} (hμ : IsPrimitiveRoot μ n) (a : F) : χ a ∈ Algebra.adjoin ℤ {μ}

views.nl_informal:
The values of a multiplicative character of order `n` are contained in `ℤ[μ]` when
`μ` is a primitive `n`th root of unity.
views.lean_signature: theorem MulChar.apply_mem_algebraAdjoin {χ : MulChar F R} {μ : R} (hμ : IsPrimitiveRoot μ (orderOf χ)) (a : F) : χ a ∈ Algebra.adjoin ℤ {μ}

views.nl_informal:
Transfers the embedding of `x ↦ (x)ᵥ` of the number field `K` into its infinite adele
ring to the mixed embedding `x ↦ (φᵢ(x))ᵢ` of `K` into the space `ℝ ^ r₁ × ℂ ^ r₂`, where
`(r₁, r₂)` is the signature of `K` and `φᵢ` are the complex embeddings of `K`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.InfiniteAdeleRing.mixedEmbedding_eq_algebraMap_comp {x : K} : mixedEmbedding K x = ringEquiv_mixedSpace K (algebraMap K _ x)

views.nl_informal: `ℤ` with its usual ring structure is not a field.
views.lean_signature: theorem Int.not_isField : ¬IsField ℤ

views.nl_informal: A finite extension of a number field is a number field.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.of_module_finite [NumberField K] [Algebra K L] [Module.Finite K L] : NumberField L

views.nl_informal:
The canonical map from `𝓞 K` to `K` is injective.

This is a convenient abbreviation for `FaithfulSMul.algebraMap_injective`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.RingOfIntegers.coe_injective : Function.Injective (algebraMap (𝓞 K) K)

views.nl_informal:
The canonical map from `𝓞 K` to `K` is injective.

This is a convenient abbreviation for `map_eq_zero_iff` applied to
`FaithfulSMul.algebraMap_injective`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.RingOfIntegers.coe_eq_zero_iff {x : 𝓞 K} : algebraMap _ K x = 0 ↔ x = 0

views.nl_informal:
The canonical map from `𝓞 K` to `K` is injective.

This is a convenient abbreviation for `map_ne_zero_iff` applied to
`FaithfulSMul.algebraMap_injective`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.RingOfIntegers.coe_ne_zero_iff {x : 𝓞 K} : algebraMap _ K x ≠ 0 ↔ x ≠ 0

views.nl_informal: The ring of integers of a number field is not a field.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.RingOfIntegers.not_isField : ¬IsField (𝓞 K)

views.nl_informal: The kernel of the algebraMap between ring of integers is `⊥`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.RingOfIntegers.ker_algebraMap_eq_bot : RingHom.ker (algebraMap (𝓞 K) (𝓞 L)) = ⊥

views.nl_informal: The algebraMap between ring of integers is injective.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.RingOfIntegers.algebraMap.injective : Function.Injective (algebraMap (𝓞 K) (𝓞 L))

views.nl_informal: The class number of a number field is `1` iff the ring of integers is a PID.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.classNumber_eq_one_iff : classNumber K = 1 ↔ IsPrincipalIdealRing (𝓞 K)

views.nl_informal: The coercion from the rationals to its completion along an infinite place is `Rat.cast`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.InfinitePlace.Completion.WithAbs.ratCast_equiv (v : InfinitePlace ℚ) (x : WithAbs v.1) : Rat.cast (WithAbs.equiv _ x) = (x : v.Completion)

views.nl_informal: The embedding `v.Completion →+* ℂ` is an isometry.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.InfinitePlace.Completion.isometry_extensionEmbedding : Isometry (extensionEmbedding v)

views.nl_informal: The embedding `v.Completion →+* ℝ` at a real infinite place is an isometry.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.InfinitePlace.Completion.isometry_extensionEmbedding_of_isReal {v : InfinitePlace K} (hv : IsReal v) : Isometry (extensionEmbeddingOfIsReal hv)

views.nl_informal: The embedding `v.Completion →+* ℂ` has closed image inside `ℂ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.InfinitePlace.Completion.isClosed_image_extensionEmbedding : IsClosed (Set.range (extensionEmbedding v))

views.nl_informal:
The embedding `v.Completion →+* ℝ` associated to a real infinite place has closed image
inside `ℝ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.InfinitePlace.Completion.isClosed_image_extensionEmbedding_of_isReal {v : InfinitePlace K} (hv : IsReal v) : IsClosed (Set.range (extensionEmbeddingOfIsReal hv))

views.nl_informal: If `v` is a complex infinite place, then the embedding `v.Completion →+* ℂ` is surjective.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.InfinitePlace.Completion.surjective_extensionEmbedding_of_isComplex {v : InfinitePlace K} (hv : IsComplex v) : Function.Surjective (extensionEmbedding v)

views.nl_informal: If `v` is a complex infinite place, then the embedding `v.Completion →+* ℂ` is bijective.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.InfinitePlace.Completion.bijective_extensionEmbedding_of_isComplex {v : InfinitePlace K} (hv : IsComplex v) : Function.Bijective (extensionEmbedding v)

views.nl_informal: If `v` is a real infinite place, then the embedding `v.Completion →+* ℝ` is surjective.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.InfinitePlace.Completion.surjective_extensionEmbedding_of_isReal {v : InfinitePlace K} (hv : IsReal v) : Function.Surjective (extensionEmbeddingOfIsReal hv)

views.nl_informal: If `v` is a real infinite place, then the embedding `v.Completion →+* ℝ` is bijective.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.InfinitePlace.Completion.bijective_extensionEmbedding_of_isReal {v : InfinitePlace K} (hv : IsReal v) : Function.Bijective (extensionEmbeddingOfIsReal hv)

views.nl_informal: The number of embeddings of a number field is equal to its finrank.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.Embeddings.card : Fintype.card (K →+* A) = finrank ℚ K

views.nl_informal:
Let `A` be an algebraically closed field and let `x ∈ K`, with `K` a number field.
The images of `x` by the embeddings of `K` in `A` are exactly the roots in `A` of
the minimal polynomial of `x` over `ℚ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.Embeddings.range_eval_eq_rootSet_minpoly : (range fun φ : K →+* A => φ x) = (minpoly ℚ x).rootSet A

views.nl_informal:
Let `B` be a real number. The set of algebraic integers in `K` whose conjugates are all
smaller in norm than `B` is finite.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.Embeddings.finite_of_norm_le (B : ℝ) : {x : K | IsIntegral ℤ x ∧ ∀ φ : K →+* A, ‖φ x‖ ≤ B}.Finite

views.nl_informal: An algebraic integer whose conjugates are all of norm one is a root of unity.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.Embeddings.pow_eq_one_of_norm_eq_one {x : K} (hxi : IsIntegral ℤ x) (hx : ∀ φ : K →+* A, ‖φ x‖ = 1) : ∃ (n : ℕ) (_ : 0 < n), x ^ n = 1

views.nl_informal:
The infinite part of the product formula : for `x ∈ K`, we have `Π_w ‖x‖_w = |norm(x)|` where
`‖·‖_w` is the normalized absolute value for `w`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.InfinitePlace.prod_eq_abs_norm (x : K) : ∏ w : InfinitePlace K, w x ^ mult w = abs (Algebra.norm ℚ x)

views.nl_informal: The norm of a maximal ideal is `> 1`
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.RingOfIntegers.HeightOneSpectrum.one_lt_absNorm : 1 < absNorm v.asIdeal

views.nl_informal: The norm of a maximal ideal as an element of `ℝ≥0` is `> 1`
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.RingOfIntegers.HeightOneSpectrum.one_lt_absNorm_nnreal : 1 < (absNorm v.asIdeal : NNReal)

views.nl_informal: The norm of a maximal ideal as an element of `ℝ≥0` is `≠ 0`
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.RingOfIntegers.HeightOneSpectrum.absNorm_ne_zero : (absNorm v.asIdeal : NNReal) ≠ 0

views.nl_informal:
The norm of the image after the embedding associated to `v` is equal to the `v`-adic absolute
value.
views.lean_signature: theorem FinitePlace.norm_def (x : WithVal (v.valuation K)) : ‖embedding v x‖ = adicAbv v x

views.nl_informal:
The norm of the image after the embedding associated to `v` is equal to the norm of `v` raised
to the power of the `v`-adic valuation.
views.lean_signature: theorem FinitePlace.norm_def' (x : WithVal (v.valuation K)) : ‖embedding v x‖ = toNNReal (absNorm_ne_zero v) (v.valuation K x)

views.nl_informal:
The norm of the image after the embedding associated to `v` is equal to the norm of `v` raised
to the power of the `v`-adic valuation for integers.
views.lean_signature: theorem FinitePlace.norm_def_int (x : 𝓞 (WithVal (v.valuation K))) : ‖embedding v x‖ = toNNReal (absNorm_ne_zero v) (v.intValuationDef x)

views.nl_informal: The `v`-adic absolute value satisfies the ultrametric inequality.
views.lean_signature: theorem RingOfIntegers.HeightOneSpectrum.adicAbv_add_le_max (x y : K) : adicAbv v (x + y) ≤ (adicAbv v x) ⊔ (adicAbv v y)

views.nl_informal: The `v`-adic absolute value of a natural number is `≤ 1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem RingOfIntegers.HeightOneSpectrum.adicAbv_natCast_le_one (n : ℕ) : adicAbv v n ≤ 1

views.nl_informal: The `v`-adic absolute value of an integer is `≤ 1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem RingOfIntegers.HeightOneSpectrum.adicAbv_intCast_le_one (n : ℤ) : adicAbv v n ≤ 1

views.nl_informal: The `v`-adic norm of an integer is at most 1.
views.lean_signature: theorem FinitePlace.norm_le_one (x : 𝓞 (WithVal (v.valuation K))) : ‖embedding v x‖ ≤ 1

views.nl_informal: The `v`-adic norm of an integer is 1 if and only if it is not in the ideal.
views.lean_signature: theorem FinitePlace.norm_eq_one_iff_not_mem (x : 𝓞 (WithVal (v.valuation K))) : ‖embedding v x‖ = 1 ↔ x ∉ v.asIdeal

views.nl_informal: The `v`-adic norm of an integer is less than 1 if and only if it is in the ideal.
views.lean_signature: theorem FinitePlace.norm_lt_one_iff_mem (x : 𝓞 (WithVal (v.valuation K))) : ‖embedding v x‖ < 1 ↔ x ∈ v.asIdeal

views.nl_informal:
The absolute value of the determinant of the base change from `integralBasis` to
`basisOfFractionalIdeal I` is equal to the norm of `I`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.det_basisOfFractionalIdeal_eq_absNorm (I : (FractionalIdeal (𝓞 K)⁰ K)ˣ) (e : (Free.ChooseBasisIndex ℤ (𝓞 K)) ≃ (Free.ChooseBasisIndex ℤ I)) : |(integralBasis K).det ((basisOfFractionalIdeal K I).reindex e.symm)| = FractionalIdeal.absNorm I.1

views.nl_informal: The house is the largest of the modulus of the conjugates of an algebraic number.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.house_eq_sup' (α : K) : house α = univ.sup' univ_nonempty (fun φ : K →+* ℂ ↦ ‖φ α‖₊)

views.nl_informal:
There exists a "small" non-zero algebraic integral solution of an
non-trivial underdetermined system of linear equations with algebraic integer coefficients.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.house.exists_ne_zero_int_vec_house_le : ∃ (ξ : β → 𝓞 K), ξ ≠ 0 ∧ a *ᵥ ξ = 0 ∧ ∀ l, house (ξ l).1 ≤ c₁ K * ((c₁ K * q * A) ^ ((p : ℝ) / (q - p)))

views.nl_informal:
If `L/K` is a finite Galois extension of fields, then, for all `(x : 𝓞 L)` we have that
`x ∣ algebraMap (𝓞 K) (𝓞 L) (norm K x)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem RingOfIntegers.dvd_norm [IsGalois K L] (x : 𝓞 L) : x ∣ algebraMap (𝓞 K) (𝓞 L) (norm K x)

views.nl_informal:
For any non-zero `x` in `𝓞 K`, the prduct of `w x`, where `w` runs over `FinitePlace K`, is
equal to the inverse of the absolute value of `Algebra.norm ℤ x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.FinitePlace.prod_eq_inv_abs_norm_int {x : 𝓞 K} (h_x_nezero : x ≠ 0) : ∏ᶠ w : FinitePlace K, w x = (|norm ℤ x| : ℝ)⁻¹

views.nl_informal:
For any non-zero `x` in `K`, the prduct of `w x`, where `w` runs over `FinitePlace K`, is
equal to the inverse of the absolute value of `Algebra.norm ℚ x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.FinitePlace.prod_eq_inv_abs_norm {x : K} (h_x_nezero : x ≠ 0) : ∏ᶠ w : FinitePlace K, w x = |(Algebra.norm ℚ) x|⁻¹

views.nl_informal: The Product Formula for the Number Field `K`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.prod_abs_eq_one {x : K} (h_x_nezero : x ≠ 0) : (∏ w : InfinitePlace K, w x ^ w.mult) * ∏ᶠ w : FinitePlace K, w x = 1

views.nl_informal:
The image of `canonicalEmbedding` lives in the `ℝ`-submodule of the `x ∈ ((K →+* ℂ) → ℂ)` such
that `conj x_φ = x_(conj φ)` for all `∀ φ : K →+* ℂ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.canonicalEmbedding.conj_apply {x : ((K →+* ℂ) → ℂ)} (φ : K →+* ℂ) (hx : x ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range (canonicalEmbedding K))) : conj (x φ) = x (ComplexEmbedding.conjugate φ)

views.nl_informal:
The set of points in the mixedSpace that are equal to `0` at a fixed (real) place has
volume zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.mixedEmbedding.volume_eq_zero (w : {w // IsReal w}) : volume ({x : mixedSpace K | x.1 w = 0}) = 0

views.nl_informal:
Let `x : (K →+* ℂ) → ℂ` such that `x_φ = conj x_(conj φ)` for all `φ : K →+* ℂ`, then the
representation of `commMap K x` on `stdBasis` is given (up to reindexing) by the product of
`matrixToStdBasis` by `x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.mixedEmbedding.stdBasis_repr_eq_matrixToStdBasis_mul (x : (K →+* ℂ) → ℂ) (hx : ∀ φ, conj (x φ) = x (ComplexEmbedding.conjugate φ)) (c : index K) : ((stdBasis K).repr (commMap K x) c : ℂ) = (matrixToStdBasis K *ᵥ (x ∘ (indexEquiv K))) c

views.nl_informal:
The generalized index of the lattice generated by `I` in the lattice generated by
`𝓞 K` is equal to the norm of the ideal `I`. The result is stated in terms of base change
determinant and is the translation of `NumberField.det_basisOfFractionalIdeal_eq_absNorm` in
the mixed space. This is useful, in particular, to prove that the family obtained from
the `ℤ`-basis of `I` is actually an `ℝ`-basis of the mixed space, see
`fractionalIdealLatticeBasis`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.mixedEmbedding.det_basisOfFractionalIdeal_eq_norm (e : (ChooseBasisIndex ℤ (𝓞 K)) ≃ (ChooseBasisIndex ℤ I)) : |Basis.det (latticeBasis K) ((mixedEmbedding K ∘ (basisOfFractionalIdeal K I) ∘ e))| = FractionalIdeal.absNorm I.1

views.nl_informal: `negAt` preserves the volume .
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.mixedEmbedding.volume_preserving_negAt [NumberField K] : MeasurePreserving (negAt s)

views.nl_informal: `negAt` preserves `normAtPlace`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.mixedEmbedding.normAtPlace_negAt (x : mixedSpace K) (w : InfinitePlace K) : normAtPlace w (negAt s x) = normAtPlace w x

views.nl_informal: `negAt` preserves the `norm`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.mixedEmbedding.norm_negAt [NumberField K] (x : mixedSpace K) : mixedEmbedding.norm (negAt s x) = mixedEmbedding.norm x

views.nl_informal: `negAt` is its own inverse.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.mixedEmbedding.negAt_symm : (negAt s).symm = negAt s

views.nl_informal:
`negAt s A` is also equal to the preimage of `A` by `negAt s`. This fact is used to simplify
some proofs.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.mixedEmbedding.negAt_preimage : negAt s ⁻¹' A = negAt s '' A

views.nl_informal: The images of `plusPart` by `negAt` are pairwise disjoint.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.mixedEmbedding.disjoint_negAt_plusPart : Pairwise (Disjoint on (fun s ↦ negAt s '' (plusPart A)))

views.nl_informal:
Assume that `A`  is symmetric at real places then, the union of the images of `plusPart`
by `negAt` and of the set of elements of `A` that are zero at at least one real place
is equal to `A`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.mixedEmbedding.iUnion_negAt_plusPart_union : (⋃ s, negAt s '' (plusPart A)) ∪ (A ∩ (⋃ w, {x | x.1 w = 0})) = A

views.nl_informal: The image of the `plusPart` of `A` by `negAt` have all the same volume as `plusPart A`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.mixedEmbedding.volume_negAt_plusPart (hm : MeasurableSet A) : volume (negAt s '' (plusPart A)) = volume (plusPart A)

views.nl_informal:
If a subset `A` of the `mixedSpace` is symmetric at real places, then its volume is
`2^ nrRealPlaces K` times the volume of its `plusPart`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.mixedEmbedding.volume_eq_two_pow_mul_volume_plusPart (hm : MeasurableSet A) : volume A = 2 ^ nrRealPlaces K * volume (plusPart A)

views.nl_informal: The set of points in the `realSpace` that are equal to `0` at a fixed place has volume zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.mixedEmbedding.realSpace.volume_eq_zero [NumberField K] (w : InfinitePlace K) : volume ({x : realSpace K | x w = 0}) = 0

views.nl_informal:
The volume of `(ConvexBodyLt K f)` where `convexBodyLT K f` is the set of points `x`
such that `‖x w‖ < f w` for all infinite places `w`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.mixedEmbedding.convexBodyLT_volume : volume (convexBodyLT K f) = (convexBodyLTFactor K) * ∏ w, (f w) ^ (mult w)

views.nl_informal:
This is a technical result: quite often, we want to impose conditions at all infinite places
but one and choose the value at the remaining place so that we can apply
`exists_ne_zero_mem_ringOfIntegers_lt`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.mixedEmbedding.adjust_f {w₁ : InfinitePlace K} (B : ℝ≥0) (hf : ∀ w, w ≠ w₁ → f w ≠ 0) : ∃ g : InfinitePlace K → ℝ≥0, (∀ w, w ≠ w₁ → g w = f w) ∧ ∏ w, (g w) ^ mult w = B

views.nl_informal:
Let `I` be a fractional ideal of `K`. Assume that `f : InfinitePlace K → ℝ≥0` is such that
`minkowskiBound K I < volume (convexBodyLT K f)` where `convexBodyLT K f` is the set of
points `x` such that `‖x w‖ < f w` for all infinite places `w` (see `convexBodyLT_volume` for
the computation of this volume), then there exists a nonzero algebraic number `a` in `I` such
that `w a < f w` for all infinite places `w`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.mixedEmbedding.exists_ne_zero_mem_ideal_lt (h : minkowskiBound K I < volume (convexBodyLT K f)) : ∃ a ∈ (I : FractionalIdeal (𝓞 K)⁰ K), a ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ w : InfinitePlace K, w a < f w

views.nl_informal:
A version of `exists_ne_zero_mem_ideal_lt` where the absolute value of the real part of `a` is
smaller than `1` at some fixed complex place. This is useful to ensure that `a` is not real.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.mixedEmbedding.exists_ne_zero_mem_ideal_lt' (w₀ : {w : InfinitePlace K // IsComplex w}) (h : minkowskiBound K I < volume (convexBodyLT' K f w₀)) : ∃ a ∈ (I : FractionalIdeal (𝓞 K)⁰ K), a ≠ 0 ∧ (∀ w : InfinitePlace K, w ≠ w₀ → w a < f w) ∧ |(w₀.val.embedding a).re| < 1 ∧ |(w₀.val.embedding a).im| < (f w₀ : ℝ) ^ 2

views.nl_informal:
Let `I` be a fractional ideal of `K`. Assume that `B : ℝ` is such that
`minkowskiBound K I < volume (convexBodySum K B)` where `convexBodySum K B` is the set of points
`x` such that `∑ w real, ‖x w‖ + 2 * ∑ w complex, ‖x w‖ ≤ B` (see `convexBodySum_volume` for
the computation of this volume), then there exists a nonzero algebraic number `a` in `I` such
that `|Norm a| < (B / d) ^ d` where `d` is the degree of `K`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.mixedEmbedding.exists_ne_zero_mem_ideal_of_norm_le {B : ℝ} (h : (minkowskiBound K I) ≤ volume (convexBodySum K B)) : ∃ a ∈ (I : FractionalIdeal (𝓞 K)⁰ K), a ≠ 0 ∧ |Algebra.norm ℚ (a : K)| ≤ (B / finrank ℚ K) ^ finrank ℚ K

views.nl_informal:
If `a` is in `integerSet`, then there is a *unique* algebraic integer in `𝓞 K` such
that `mixedEmbedding K x = a`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.mixedEmbedding.fundamentalCone.existsUnique_preimage_of_mem_integerSet {a : mixedSpace K} (ha : a ∈ integerSet K) : ∃! x : 𝓞 K, mixedEmbedding K x = a

views.nl_informal:
If `x : mixedSpace K` is nonzero and the image of an algebraic integer, then there exists a
unit such that `u • x ∈ integerSet K`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.mixedEmbedding.fundamentalCone.exists_unitSMul_mem_integerSet {x : mixedSpace K} (hx : x ≠ 0) (hx' : x ∈ mixedEmbedding K '' (Set.range (algebraMap (𝓞 K) K))) : ∃ u : (𝓞 K)ˣ, u • x ∈ integerSet K

views.nl_informal: The set `integerSet K` is stable under the action of the torsion.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.mixedEmbedding.fundamentalCone.torsion_unitSMul_mem_integerSet {x : mixedSpace K} {ζ : (𝓞 K)ˣ} (hζ : ζ ∈ torsion K) (hx : x ∈ integerSet K) : ζ • x ∈ integerSet K

views.nl_informal:
For `n` positive, the number of principal ideals in `𝓞 K` of norm `n` multiplied by the order
of the torsion of `K` is equal to the number of elements in `integerSet K` of norm `n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.mixedEmbedding.fundamentalCone.card_isPrincipal_norm_eq_mul_torsion (n : ℕ) : Nat.card {I : (Ideal (𝓞 K))⁰ | IsPrincipal (I : Ideal (𝓞 K)) ∧ absNorm (I : Ideal (𝓞 K)) = n} * torsionOrder K = Nat.card {a : integerSet K | mixedEmbedding.norm (a : mixedSpace K) = n}

views.nl_informal:
For `s : ℝ`, the number of principal nonzero ideals in `𝓞 K` divisible par `J` of norm `≤ s`
multiplied by the order of the torsion of `K` is equal to the number of elements in `idealSet K J`
of norm `≤ s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.mixedEmbedding.fundamentalCone.card_isPrincipal_dvd_norm_le (s : ℝ) : Nat.card {I : (Ideal (𝓞 K))⁰ // (J : Ideal (𝓞 K)) ∣ I ∧ IsPrincipal (I : Ideal (𝓞 K)) ∧ absNorm (I : Ideal (𝓞 K)) ≤ s} * torsionOrder K = Nat.card {a : idealSet K J // mixedEmbedding.norm (a : mixedSpace K) ≤ s}

views.nl_informal:
If the measurable set `A` is norm-stable at complex places in the sense that
`normAtComplexPlaces⁻¹ (normAtComplexPlaces '' A) = A`, then its volume can be computed via an
integral over `normAtComplexPlaces '' A`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.mixedEmbedding.volume_eq_two_pi_pow_mul_integral [NumberField K] (hA : normAtComplexPlaces ⁻¹' (normAtComplexPlaces '' A) = A) (hm : MeasurableSet A) : volume A = .ofReal (2 * π) ^ nrComplexPlaces K * ∫⁻ x in normAtComplexPlaces '' A, ∏ w : {w // IsComplex w}, ENNReal.ofReal (x w.1)

views.nl_informal:
If the measurable set `A` is norm-stable in the sense that
`normAtAllPlaces⁻¹ (normAtAllPlaces '' A) = A`, then its volume can be computed via an integral
over `normAtAllPlaces '' A`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.mixedEmbedding.volume_eq_two_pow_mul_two_pi_pow_mul_integral [NumberField K] (hA : normAtAllPlaces ⁻¹' (normAtAllPlaces '' A) = A) (hm : MeasurableSet A) : volume A = 2 ^ nrRealPlaces K * .ofReal (2 * π) ^ nrComplexPlaces K * ∫⁻ x in normAtAllPlaces '' A, ∏ w : {w // IsComplex w}, ENNReal.ofReal (x w.1)

views.nl_informal:
The Minkowski lower bound `n^{2n}/((4/pi)^{2r_2}*n!^2)` for the absolute value of the discriminant
of a number field of degree n.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.abs_discr_ge' : (finrank ℚ K) ^ (2 * finrank ℚ K) / ((4 / π) ^ (2 * nrComplexPlaces K) * (finrank ℚ K).factorial ^ 2) ≤ |discr K|

views.nl_informal: **Hermite-Minkowski Theorem**. A nontrivial number field has discriminant greater than `2`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.abs_discr_gt_two (h : 1 < finrank ℚ K) : 2 < |discr K|

views.nl_informal: If `|discr K| ≤ N` then the degree of `K` is at most `rankOfDiscrBdd`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.hermiteTheorem.rank_le_rankOfDiscrBdd : finrank ℚ K ≤ rankOfDiscrBdd N

views.nl_informal: If `|discr K| ≤ N` then the Minkowski bound of `K` is less than `boundOfDiscrBdd`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.hermiteTheorem.minkowskiBound_lt_boundOfDiscBdd : minkowskiBound K ↑1 < boundOfDiscBdd N

views.nl_informal:
**Hermite Theorem**. Let `N` be an integer. There are only finitely many number fields
(in some fixed extension of `ℚ`) of discriminant bounded by `N`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.finite_of_discr_bdd : {K : { F : IntermediateField ℚ A // FiniteDimensional ℚ F} | haveI : NumberField K := @NumberField.mk _ _ inferInstance K.prop |discr K| ≤ N }.Finite

views.nl_informal: The absolute discriminant of the number field `ℚ` is 1.
views.lean_signature: theorem Rat.numberField_discr : discr ℚ = 1

views.nl_informal:
If `b` and `b'` are `ℚ`-bases of a number field `K` such that
`∀ i j, IsIntegral ℤ (b.toMatrix b' i j)` and `∀ i j, IsIntegral ℤ (b'.toMatrix b i j)` then
`discr ℚ b = discr ℚ b'`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Algebra.discr_eq_discr_of_toMatrix_coeff_isIntegral [NumberField K] {b : Basis ι ℚ K} {b' : Basis ι' ℚ K} (h : ∀ i j, IsIntegral ℤ (b.toMatrix b' i j)) (h' : ∀ i j, IsIntegral ℤ (b'.toMatrix b i j)) : discr ℚ b = discr ℚ b'

views.nl_informal:
If `k` does not divide `torsionOrder` then there are no nontrivial roots of unity of
order dividing `k`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.Units.rootsOfUnity_eq_one [NumberField K] {k : ℕ+} (hc : Nat.Coprime k (torsionOrder K)) {ζ : (𝓞 K)ˣ} : ζ ∈ rootsOfUnity k (𝓞 K) ↔ ζ = 1

views.nl_informal:
The group of roots of unity of order dividing `torsionOrder` is equal to the torsion
group.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.Units.rootsOfUnity_eq_torsion [NumberField K] : rootsOfUnity (torsionOrder K) (𝓞 K) = torsion K

views.nl_informal: This result shows that there always exists a next term in the sequence.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.Units.dirichletUnitTheorem.seq_next {x : 𝓞 K} (hx : x ≠ 0) : ∃ y : 𝓞 K, y ≠ 0 ∧ (∀ w, w ≠ w₁ → w y < w x) ∧ |Algebra.norm ℚ (y : K)| ≤ B

views.nl_informal: The terms of the sequence are nonzero.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.Units.dirichletUnitTheorem.seq_ne_zero (n : ℕ) : algebraMap (𝓞 K) K (seq K w₁ hB n) ≠ 0

views.nl_informal: The sequence is strictly decreasing at infinite places distinct from `w₁`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.Units.dirichletUnitTheorem.seq_decreasing {n m : ℕ} (h : n < m) (w : InfinitePlace K) (hw : w ≠ w₁) : w (algebraMap (𝓞 K) K (seq K w₁ hB m)) < w (algebraMap (𝓞 K) K (seq K w₁ hB n))

views.nl_informal: The terms of the sequence have norm bounded by `B`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.Units.dirichletUnitTheorem.seq_norm_le (n : ℕ) : Int.natAbs (Algebra.norm ℤ (seq K w₁ hB n : 𝓞 K)) ≤ B

views.nl_informal:
The exponents that appear in the unique decomposition of a unit as the product of
a root of unity and powers of the units of the fundamental system `fundSystem` (see
`exist_unique_eq_mul_prod`) are given by the representation of the unit on `basisModTorsion`.
views.lean_signature: theorem fun_eq_repr {x ζ : (𝓞 K)ˣ} {f : Fin (rank K) → ℤ} (hζ : ζ ∈ torsion K) (h : x = ζ * ∏ i, (fundSystem K i) ^ (f i)) : f = (basisModTorsion K).repr (Additive.ofMul ↑x)

views.nl_informal:
**Dirichlet Unit Theorem**. Any unit `x` of `𝓞 K` can be written uniquely as the product of
a root of unity and powers of the units of the fundamental system `fundSystem`.
views.lean_signature: theorem exist_unique_eq_mul_prod (x : (𝓞 K)ˣ) : ∃! ζe : torsion K × (Fin (rank K) → ℤ), x = ζe.1 * ∏ i, (fundSystem K i) ^ (ζe.2 i)

views.nl_informal:
Let `u : Fin (rank K) → (𝓞 K)ˣ` be a family of units and let `w₁` and `w₂` be two infinite
places. Then, the two square matrices with entries `(mult w * log w (u i))_i` where `w ≠ w_j` for
`j = 1, 2` have the same determinant in absolute value.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.Units.abs_det_eq_abs_det (u : Fin (rank K) → (𝓞 K)ˣ) {w₁ w₂ : InfinitePlace K} (e₁ : {w // w ≠ w₁} ≃ Fin (rank K)) (e₂ : {w // w ≠ w₂} ≃ Fin (rank K)) : |(Matrix.of fun i w : {w // w ≠ w₁} ↦ (mult w.val : ℝ) * (w.val (u (e₁ i) : K)).log).det| = |(Matrix.of fun i w : {w // w ≠ w₂} ↦ (mult w.val : ℝ) * (w.val (u (e₂ i) : K)).log).det|

views.nl_informal:
For any infinite place `w'`, the regulator is equal to the absolute value of the determinant
of the matrix with entries `(mult w * log w (fundSystem K i))_i` for `w ≠ w'`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.Units.regulator_eq_det (w' : InfinitePlace K) (e : {w // w ≠ w'} ≃ Fin (rank K)) : regulator K = |(Matrix.of fun i w : {w // w ≠ w'} ↦ (mult w.val : ℝ) * Real.log (w.val (fundSystem K (e i) : K))).det|

views.nl_informal:
The degree of `K` times the regulator of `K` is equal to the absolute value of the determinant of
the matrix whose columns are `(mult w * log w (fundSystem K i))_i, w` and the column `(mult w)_w`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NumberField.Units.finrank_mul_regulator_eq_det (w' : InfinitePlace K) (e : {w // w ≠ w'} ≃ Fin (rank K)) : finrank ℚ K * regulator K = |(Matrix.of (fun i w : InfinitePlace K ↦ if h : i = w' then (w.mult : ℝ) else w.mult * (w (fundSystem K (e ⟨i, h⟩))).log)).det|

views.nl_informal: Bound for norms of ascending Pochhammer symbols.
views.lean_signature: theorem PadicInt.norm_ascPochhammer_le (k : ℕ) (x : ℤ_[p]) : ‖(ascPochhammer ℤ_[p] k).eval x‖ ≤ ‖(k.factorial : ℤ_[p])‖

views.nl_informal: The function `mahler k` extends `n ↦ n.choose k` on `ℕ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem mahler_natCast_eq (k n : ℕ) : mahler k (n : ℤ_[p]) = n.choose k

views.nl_informal:
Bound for iterated forward differences of a continuous function from a compact space to a
nonarchimedean seminormed group.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsUltrametricDist.norm_fwdDiff_iter_apply_le [TopologicalSpace M] [CompactSpace M] [AddCommMonoid M] [SeminormedAddCommGroup G] [IsUltrametricDist G] (h : M) (f : C(M, G)) (m : M) (n : ℕ) : ‖Δ_[h]^[n] f m‖ ≤ ‖f‖

views.nl_informal:
First step in Bojanić's proof of Mahler's theorem (equation (10) of [bojanic74]): rewrite
`Δ^[n + R] f 0` in a shape that makes it easy to bound `p`-adically.
views.lean_signature: theorem bojanic_mahler_step1 [AddCommMonoidWithOne M] [AddCommGroup G] (f : M → G) (n : ℕ) {R : ℕ} (hR : 1 ≤ R) : Δ_[1]^[n + R] f 0 = -∑ j ∈ range (R - 1), R.choose (j + 1) • Δ_[1]^[n + (j + 1)] f 0 + ∑ k ∈ range (n + 1), ((-1 : ℤ) ^ (n - k) * n.choose k) • (f (k + R) - f k)

views.nl_informal:
Second step in Bojanić's proof of Mahler's theorem (equation (11) of [bojanic74]): show that values
`Δ_[1]^[n + p ^ t] f 0` for large enough `n` are bounded by the max of `(‖f‖ / p ^ s)` and `1 / p`
times a sup over values for smaller `n`.

We use `nnnorm`s on the RHS since `Finset.sup` requires an order with a bottom element.
views.lean_signature: theorem PadicInt.bojanic_mahler_step2 {f : C(ℤ_[p], E)} {s t : ℕ} (hst : ∀ x y : ℤ_[p], ‖x - y‖ ≤ p ^ (-t : ℤ) → ‖f x - f y‖ ≤ ‖f‖ / p ^ s) (n : ℕ) : ‖Δ_[1]^[n + p ^ t] f 0‖ ≤ max ↑((Finset.range (p ^ t - 1)).sup fun j ↦ ‖Δ_[1]^[n + (j + 1)] f 0‖₊ / p) (‖f‖ / p ^ s)

views.nl_informal:
Explicit bound for the decay rate of the Mahler coefficients of a continuous function on `ℤ_[p]`.
This will be used to prove Mahler's theorem.
views.lean_signature: theorem PadicInt.fwdDiff_iter_le_of_forall_le {f : C(ℤ_[p], E)} {s t : ℕ} (hst : ∀ x y : ℤ_[p], ‖x - y‖ ≤ p ^ (-t : ℤ) → ‖f x - f y‖ ≤ ‖f‖ / p ^ s) (n : ℕ) : ‖Δ_[1]^[n + s * p ^ t] f 0‖ ≤ ‖f‖ / p ^ s

views.nl_informal:
Key lemma for Mahler's theorem: for `f` a continuous function on `ℤ_[p]`, the sequence
`n ↦ Δ^[n] f 0` tends to 0. See `PadicInt.fwdDiff_iter_le_of_forall_le` for an explicit
estimate of the decay rate.
views.lean_signature: theorem PadicInt.fwdDiff_tendsto_zero (f : C(ℤ_[p], E)) : Tendsto (Δ_[1]^[·] f 0) atTop (𝓝 0)

views.nl_informal: The uniform norm of the `k`-th Mahler basis function is 1, for every `k`.
views.lean_signature: theorem PadicInt.norm_mahler_eq (k : ℕ) : ‖(mahler k : C(ℤ_[p], ℤ_[p]))‖ = 1

views.nl_informal: A Mahler series whose coefficients tend to 0 is convergent.
views.lean_signature: theorem PadicInt.hasSum_mahlerSeries (ha : Tendsto a atTop (𝓝 0)) : HasSum (fun n ↦ mahlerTerm (a n) n) (mahlerSeries a : C(ℤ_[p], E))

views.nl_informal: Evaluation of a Mahler series is just the pointwise sum.
views.lean_signature: theorem PadicInt.mahlerSeries_apply (ha : Tendsto a atTop (𝓝 0)) (x : ℤ_[p]) : mahlerSeries a x = ∑' n, mahler n x • a n

views.nl_informal:
The value of a Mahler series at a natural number `n` is given by the finite sum of the first `m`
terms, for any `n ≤ m`.
views.lean_signature: theorem PadicInt.mahlerSeries_apply_nat (ha : Tendsto a atTop (𝓝 0)) {m n : ℕ} (hmn : m ≤ n) : mahlerSeries a (m : ℤ_[p]) = ∑ i ∈ range (n + 1), m.choose i • a i

views.nl_informal:
The coefficients of a Mahler series can be recovered from the sum by taking forward differences at
`0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem PadicInt.fwdDiff_mahlerSeries (ha : Tendsto a atTop (𝓝 0)) (n) : Δ_[1]^[n] (mahlerSeries a) (0 : ℤ_[p]) = a n

views.nl_informal:
**Mahler's theorem**: for any continuous function `f` from `ℤ_[p]` to a `p`-adic Banach space, the
Mahler series with coefficients `n ↦ Δ_[1]^[n] f 0` converges to the original function `f`.
views.lean_signature: theorem PadicInt.hasSum_mahler (f : C(ℤ_[p], E)) : HasSum (fun n ↦ mahlerTerm (Δ_[1]^[n] f 0) n) f

views.nl_informal: Unfolds the definition of the `p`-adic norm of `q` when `q ≠ 0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicNorm.eq_zpow_of_nonzero {q : ℚ} (hq : q ≠ 0) : padicNorm p q = (p : ℚ) ^ (-padicValRat p q)

views.nl_informal: The `p`-adic norm is nonnegative.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicNorm.nonneg (q : ℚ) : 0 ≤ padicNorm p q

views.nl_informal: The `p`-adic norm of `0` is `0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicNorm.zero : padicNorm p 0 = 0

views.nl_informal: The `p`-adic norm of `1` is `1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicNorm.one : padicNorm p 1 = 1

views.nl_informal:
The `p`-adic norm of `p` is `p⁻¹` if `p > 1`.

See also `padicNorm.padicNorm_p_of_prime` for a version assuming `p` is prime.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicNorm.padicNorm_p (hp : 1 < p) : padicNorm p p = (p : ℚ)⁻¹

views.nl_informal:
The `p`-adic norm of `p` is `p⁻¹` if `p` is prime.

See also `padicNorm.padicNorm_p` for a version assuming `1 < p`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicNorm.padicNorm_p_of_prime [Fact p.Prime] : padicNorm p p = (p : ℚ)⁻¹

views.nl_informal: The `p`-adic norm of `q` is `1` if `q` is prime and not equal to `p`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicNorm.padicNorm_of_prime_of_ne {q : ℕ} [p_prime : Fact p.Prime] [q_prime : Fact q.Prime] (neq : p ≠ q) : padicNorm p q = 1

views.nl_informal:
The `p`-adic norm of `p` is less than `1` if `1 < p`.

See also `padicNorm.padicNorm_p_lt_one_of_prime` for a version assuming `p` is prime.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicNorm.padicNorm_p_lt_one (hp : 1 < p) : padicNorm p p < 1

views.nl_informal:
The `p`-adic norm of `p` is less than `1` if `p` is prime.

See also `padicNorm.padicNorm_p_lt_one` for a version assuming `1 < p`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicNorm.padicNorm_p_lt_one_of_prime [Fact p.Prime] : padicNorm p p < 1

views.nl_informal: `padicNorm p q` takes discrete values `p ^ -z` for `z : ℤ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicNorm.values_discrete {q : ℚ} (hq : q ≠ 0) : ∃ z : ℤ, padicNorm p q = (p : ℚ) ^ (-z)

views.nl_informal: `padicNorm p` is symmetric.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicNorm.neg (q : ℚ) : padicNorm p (-q) = padicNorm p q

views.nl_informal: If `q ≠ 0`, then `padicNorm p q ≠ 0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicNorm.nonzero {q : ℚ} (hq : q ≠ 0) : padicNorm p q ≠ 0

views.nl_informal: If the `p`-adic norm of `q` is 0, then `q` is `0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicNorm.zero_of_padicNorm_eq_zero {q : ℚ} (h : padicNorm p q = 0) : q = 0

views.nl_informal: The `p`-adic norm is multiplicative.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicNorm.mul (q r : ℚ) : padicNorm p (q * r) = padicNorm p q * padicNorm p r

views.nl_informal: The `p`-adic norm respects division.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicNorm.div (q r : ℚ) : padicNorm p (q / r) = padicNorm p q / padicNorm p r

views.nl_informal: The `p`-adic norm of an integer is at most `1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicNorm.of_int (z : ℤ) : padicNorm p z ≤ 1

views.nl_informal:
The `p`-adic norm is nonarchimedean: the norm of `p + q` is at most the max of the norm of `p`
and the norm of `q`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicNorm.nonarchimedean {q r : ℚ} : padicNorm p (q + r) ≤ max (padicNorm p q) (padicNorm p r)

views.nl_informal:
The `p`-adic norm respects the triangle inequality: the norm of `p + q` is at most the norm of
`p` plus the norm of `q`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicNorm.triangle_ineq (q r : ℚ) : padicNorm p (q + r) ≤ padicNorm p q + padicNorm p r

views.nl_informal:
The `p`-adic norm of a difference is at most the max of each component. Restates the archimedean
property of the `p`-adic norm.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicNorm.sub {q r : ℚ} : padicNorm p (q - r) ≤ max (padicNorm p q) (padicNorm p r)

views.nl_informal:
If the `p`-adic norms of `q` and `r` are different, then the norm of `q + r` is equal to the max
of the norms of `q` and `r`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicNorm.add_eq_max_of_ne {q r : ℚ} (hne : padicNorm p q ≠ padicNorm p r) : padicNorm p (q + r) = max (padicNorm p q) (padicNorm p r)

views.nl_informal: The `p`-adic norm of an integer `m` is one iff `p` doesn't divide `m`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicNorm.int_eq_one_iff (m : ℤ) : padicNorm p m = 1 ↔ ¬(p : ℤ) ∣ m

views.nl_informal: The `p`-adic norm of a natural `m` is one iff `p` doesn't divide `m`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicNorm.nat_eq_one_iff (m : ℕ) : padicNorm p m = 1 ↔ ¬p ∣ m

views.nl_informal: If a rational is not a p-adic integer, it is not an integer.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicNorm.not_int_of_not_padic_int (p : ℕ) {a : ℚ} [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (H : 1 < padicNorm p a) : ¬ a.isInt

views.nl_informal:
The `p`-adic norm of the entries of a nonzero Cauchy sequence of rationals is eventually
constant.
views.lean_signature: theorem PadicSeq.stationary {f : CauSeq ℚ (padicNorm p)} (hf : ¬f ≈ 0) : ∃ N, ∀ m n, N ≤ m → N ≤ n → padicNorm p (f n) = padicNorm p (f m)

views.nl_informal: The set of p-adic integers `ℤ_[p]` is totally bounded.
views.lean_signature: theorem PadicInt.totallyBounded_univ : TotallyBounded (Set.univ : Set ℤ_[p])

views.nl_informal:
`z - (toZMod z : ℤ_[p])` is contained in the maximal ideal of `ℤ_[p]`, for every `z : ℤ_[p]`.

The coercion from `ZMod p` to `ℤ_[p]` is `ZMod.cast`,
which coerces `ZMod p` into arbitrary rings.
This is unfortunate, but a consequence of the fact that we allow `ZMod p`
to coerce to rings of arbitrary characteristic, instead of only rings of characteristic `p`.
This coercion is only a ring homomorphism if it coerces into a ring whose characteristic divides
`p`. While this is not the case here we can still make use of the coercion.
views.lean_signature: theorem PadicInt.toZMod_spec : x - (ZMod.cast (toZMod x) : ℤ_[p]) ∈ maximalIdeal ℤ_[p]

views.nl_informal:
One part of the universal property of `ℤ_[p]` as a projective limit.
See also `PadicInt.lift_unique`.
views.lean_signature: theorem PadicInt.lift_spec (n : ℕ) : (toZModPow n).comp (lift f_compat) = f n

views.nl_informal:
One part of the universal property of `ℤ_[p]` as a projective limit.
See also `PadicInt.lift_spec`.
views.lean_signature: theorem PadicInt.lift_unique (g : R →+* ℤ_[p]) (hg : ∀ n, (toZModPow n).comp g = f n) : lift f_compat = g

views.nl_informal: If `p ≠ 0` and `p ≠ 1`, then `padicValNat p p` is `1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicValNat.self (hp : 1 < p) : padicValNat p p = 1

views.nl_informal: `padicValInt p 0` is `0` for any `p`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicValInt.zero : padicValInt p 0 = 0

views.nl_informal: `padicValInt p 1` is `0` for any `p`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicValInt.one : padicValInt p 1 = 0

views.nl_informal: The `p`-adic value of a natural is its `p`-adic value as an integer.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicValInt.of_nat {n : ℕ} : padicValInt p n = padicValNat p n

views.nl_informal: If `p ≠ 0` and `p ≠ 1`, then `padicValInt p p` is `1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicValInt.self (hp : 1 < p) : padicValInt p p = 1

views.nl_informal: `padicValRat p q` is symmetric in `q`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicValRat.neg (q : ℚ) : padicValRat p (-q) = padicValRat p q

views.nl_informal: `padicValRat p 0` is `0` for any `p`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicValRat.zero : padicValRat p 0 = 0

views.nl_informal: `padicValRat p 1` is `0` for any `p`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicValRat.one : padicValRat p 1 = 0

views.nl_informal: The `p`-adic value of an integer `z ≠ 0` is its `p`-adic_value as a rational.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicValRat.of_int {z : ℤ} : padicValRat p z = padicValInt p z

views.nl_informal: The `p`-adic value of an integer `z ≠ 0` is the multiplicity of `p` in `z`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicValRat.of_int_multiplicity {z : ℤ} (hp : p ≠ 1) (hz : z ≠ 0) : padicValRat p (z : ℚ) = multiplicity (p : ℤ) z

views.nl_informal: The `p`-adic value of an integer `z ≠ 0` is its `p`-adic value as a rational.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicValRat.of_nat {n : ℕ} : padicValRat p n = padicValNat p n

views.nl_informal: If `p ≠ 0` and `p ≠ 1`, then `padicValRat p p` is `1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicValRat.self (hp : 1 < p) : padicValRat p p = 1

views.nl_informal: `padicValRat` coincides with `padicValNat`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicValRat_of_nat (n : ℕ) : ↑(padicValNat p n) = padicValRat p n

views.nl_informal: The multiplicity of `p : ℕ` in `a : ℤ` is finite exactly when `a ≠ 0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicValRat.finite_int_prime_iff {a : ℤ} : FiniteMultiplicity (p : ℤ) a ↔ a ≠ 0

views.nl_informal: A rewrite lemma for `padicValRat p q` when `q` is expressed in terms of `Rat.mk`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicValRat.defn (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact p.Prime] {q : ℚ} {n d : ℤ} (hqz : q ≠ 0) (qdf : q = n /. d) : padicValRat p q = multiplicity (p : ℤ) n - multiplicity (p : ℤ) d

views.nl_informal: A rewrite lemma for `padicValRat p (q * r)` with conditions `q ≠ 0`, `r ≠ 0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicValRat.mul {q r : ℚ} (hq : q ≠ 0) (hr : r ≠ 0) : padicValRat p (q * r) = padicValRat p q + padicValRat p r

views.nl_informal: A rewrite lemma for `padicValRat p (q^k)` with condition `q ≠ 0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicValRat.pow {q : ℚ} (hq : q ≠ 0) {k : ℕ} : padicValRat p (q ^ k) = k * padicValRat p q

views.nl_informal: A rewrite lemma for `padicValRat p (q⁻¹)` with condition `q ≠ 0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicValRat.inv (q : ℚ) : padicValRat p q⁻¹ = -padicValRat p q

views.nl_informal: A rewrite lemma for `padicValRat p (q / r)` with conditions `q ≠ 0`, `r ≠ 0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicValRat.div {q r : ℚ} (hq : q ≠ 0) (hr : r ≠ 0) : padicValRat p (q / r) = padicValRat p q - padicValRat p r

views.nl_informal:
A condition for `padicValRat p (n₁ / d₁) ≤ padicValRat p (n₂ / d₂)`, in terms of
divisibility by `p^n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicValRat.padicValRat_le_padicValRat_iff {n₁ n₂ d₁ d₂ : ℤ} (hn₁ : n₁ ≠ 0) (hn₂ : n₂ ≠ 0) (hd₁ : d₁ ≠ 0) (hd₂ : d₂ ≠ 0) : padicValRat p (n₁ /. d₁) ≤ padicValRat p (n₂ /. d₂) ↔ ∀ n : ℕ, (p : ℤ) ^ n ∣ n₁ * d₂ → (p : ℤ) ^ n ∣ n₂ * d₁

views.nl_informal:
Sufficient conditions to show that the `p`-adic valuation of `q` is less than or equal to the
`p`-adic valuation of `q + r`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicValRat.le_padicValRat_add_of_le {q r : ℚ} (hqr : q + r ≠ 0) (h : padicValRat p q ≤ padicValRat p r) : padicValRat p q ≤ padicValRat p (q + r)

views.nl_informal: The minimum of the valuations of `q` and `r` is at most the valuation of `q + r`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicValRat.min_le_padicValRat_add {q r : ℚ} (hqr : q + r ≠ 0) : min (padicValRat p q) (padicValRat p r) ≤ padicValRat p (q + r)

views.nl_informal: Ultrametric property of a p-adic valuation.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicValRat.add_eq_min {q r : ℚ} (hqr : q + r ≠ 0) (hq : q ≠ 0) (hr : r ≠ 0) (hval : padicValRat p q ≠ padicValRat p r) : padicValRat p (q + r) = min (padicValRat p q) (padicValRat p r)

views.nl_informal:
A finite sum of rationals with positive `p`-adic valuation has positive `p`-adic valuation
(if the sum is non-zero).
views.lean_signature: theorem padicValRat.sum_pos_of_pos {n : ℕ} {F : ℕ → ℚ} (hF : ∀ i, i < n → 0 < padicValRat p (F i)) (hn0 : ∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, F i ≠ 0) : 0 < padicValRat p (∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, F i)

views.nl_informal:
If the p-adic valuation of a finite set of positive rationals is greater than a given rational
number, then the p-adic valuation of their sum is also greater than the same rational number.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicValRat.lt_sum_of_lt {p j : ℕ} [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] {F : ℕ → ℚ} {S : Finset ℕ} (hS : S.Nonempty) (hF : ∀ i, i ∈ S → padicValRat p (F j) < padicValRat p (F i)) (hn1 : ∀ i : ℕ, 0 < F i) : padicValRat p (F j) < padicValRat p (∑ i ∈ S, F i)

views.nl_informal: A rewrite lemma for `padicValNat p (a * b)` with conditions `a ≠ 0`, `b ≠ 0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicValNat.mul : a ≠ 0 → b ≠ 0 → padicValNat p (a * b) = padicValNat p a + padicValNat p b

views.nl_informal: Dividing out by a prime factor reduces the `padicValNat` by `1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicValNat.div (dvd : p ∣ b) : padicValNat p (b / p) = padicValNat p b - 1

views.nl_informal: The p-adic valuation of `n` is less than or equal to its logarithm w.r.t `p`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicValNat_le_nat_log (n : ℕ) : padicValNat p n ≤ Nat.log p n

views.nl_informal:
The p-adic valuation of `n` is equal to the logarithm w.r.t `p` iff
`n` is less than `p` raised to one plus the p-adic valuation of `n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem nat_log_eq_padicValNat_iff {n : ℕ} [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (hn : 0 < n) : Nat.log p n = padicValNat p n ↔ n < p ^ (padicValNat p n + 1)

views.nl_informal: The `p`-adic valuation of `(p * n)!` is `n` more than that of `n!`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicValNat_factorial_mul (n : ℕ) [hp : Fact p.Prime] : padicValNat p (p * n) ! = padicValNat p n ! + n

views.nl_informal:
The `p`-adic valuation of `m` equals zero if it is between `p * k` and `p * (k + 1)` for
some `k`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicValNat_eq_zero_of_mem_Ioo {m k : ℕ} (hm : m ∈ Set.Ioo (p * k) (p * (k + 1))) : padicValNat p m = 0

views.nl_informal:
The `p`-adic valuation of `n!` is equal to the `p`-adic valuation of the factorial of the
largest multiple of `p` below `n`, i.e. `(p * ⌊n / p⌋)!`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicValNat_mul_div_factorial (n : ℕ) [hp : Fact p.Prime] : padicValNat p (p * (n / p))! = padicValNat p n !

views.nl_informal:
**Legendre's Theorem**

The `p`-adic valuation of `n!` is the sum of the quotients `n / p ^ i`. This sum is expressed
over the finset `Ico 1 b` where `b` is any bound greater than `log p n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicValNat_factorial {n b : ℕ} [hp : Fact p.Prime] (hnb : log p n < b) : padicValNat p (n !) = ∑ i ∈ Finset.Ico 1 b, n / p ^ i

views.nl_informal:
**Legendre's Theorem**

Taking (`p - 1`) times the `p`-adic valuation of `n!` equals `n` minus the sum of base `p` digits
of `n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem sub_one_mul_padicValNat_factorial [hp : Fact p.Prime] (n : ℕ) : (p - 1) * padicValNat p (n !) = n - (p.digits n).sum

views.nl_informal:
**Kummer's Theorem**

The `p`-adic valuation of `n.choose k` is the number of carries when `k` and `n - k` are added
in base `p`. This sum is expressed over the finset `Ico 1 b` where `b` is any bound greater than
`log p n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicValNat_choose {n k b : ℕ} [hp : Fact p.Prime] (hkn : k ≤ n) (hnb : log p n < b) : padicValNat p (choose n k) = #{i ∈ Finset.Ico 1 b | p ^ i ≤ k % p ^ i + (n - k) % p ^ i}

views.nl_informal:
**Kummer's Theorem**

The `p`-adic valuation of `(n + k).choose k` is the number of carries when `k` and `n` are added
in base `p`. This sum is expressed over the finset `Ico 1 b` where `b` is any bound greater than
`log p (n + k)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicValNat_choose' {n k b : ℕ} [hp : Fact p.Prime] (hnb : log p (n + k) < b) : padicValNat p (choose (n + k) k) = #{i ∈ Finset.Ico 1 b | p ^ i ≤ k % p ^ i + n % p ^ i}

views.nl_informal:
**Kummer's Theorem**
Taking (`p - 1`) times the `p`-adic valuation of the binomial `n + k` over `k` equals the sum of the
digits of `k` plus the sum of the digits of `n` minus the sum of digits of `n + k`, all base `p`.
views.lean_signature: theorem sub_one_mul_padicValNat_choose_eq_sub_sum_digits' {k n : ℕ} [hp : Fact p.Prime] : (p - 1) * padicValNat p (choose (n + k) k) = (p.digits k).sum + (p.digits n).sum - (p.digits (n + k)).sum

views.nl_informal:
**Kummer's Theorem**
Taking (`p - 1`) times the `p`-adic valuation of the binomial `n` over `k` equals the sum of the
digits of `k` plus the sum of the digits of `n - k` minus the sum of digits of `n`, all base `p`.
views.lean_signature: theorem sub_one_mul_padicValNat_choose_eq_sub_sum_digits {k n : ℕ} [hp : Fact p.Prime] (h : k ≤ n) : (p - 1) * padicValNat p (choose n k) = (p.digits k).sum + (p.digits (n - k)).sum - (p.digits n).sum

views.nl_informal: `padicValNat p 0` is `0` for any `p`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicValNat.zero : padicValNat p 0 = 0

views.nl_informal: `padicValNat p 1` is `0` for any `p`.
views.lean_signature: theorem padicValNat.one : padicValNat p 1 = 0

views.nl_informal:
If `b` mod `p` spans `S/p` as `R/p`-space, then `b` itself spans `Frac(S)` as `K`-space.

Here,
 * `p` is an ideal of `R` such that `R / p` is nontrivial
 * `K` is a field that has an embedding of `R` (in particular we can take `K = Frac(R)`)
 * `L` is a field extension of `K`
 * `S` is the integral closure of `R` in `L`

More precisely, we avoid quotients in this statement and instead require that `b ∪ pS` spans `S`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Ideal.FinrankQuotientMap.span_eq_top [IsDomain R] [IsDomain S] [Algebra K L] [Module.Finite R S] [Algebra R L] [IsScalarTower R S L] [IsScalarTower R K L] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic R S] [NoZeroSMulDivisors R K] (hp : p ≠ ⊤) (b : Set S) (hb' : Submodule.span R b ⊔ (p.map (algebraMap R S)).restrictScalars R = ⊤) : Submodule.span K (algebraMap S L '' b) = ⊤

views.nl_informal:
Let `V` be a vector space over `K = Frac(R)`, `S / R` a ring extension
and `V'` a module over `S`. If `b`, in the intersection `V''` of `V` and `V'`,
is linear independent over `S` in `V'`, then it is linear independent over `R` in `V`.

The statement we prove is actually slightly more general:
 * it suffices that the inclusion `algebraMap R S : R → S` is nontrivial
 * the function `f' : V'' → V'` doesn't need to be injective
views.lean_signature: theorem Ideal.FinrankQuotientMap.linearIndependent_of_nontrivial [IsDedekindDomain R] (hRS : RingHom.ker (algebraMap R S) ≠ ⊤) (f : V'' →ₗ[R] V) (hf : Function.Injective f) (f' : V'' →ₗ[R] V') {ι : Type*} {b : ι → V''} (hb' : LinearIndependent S (f' ∘ b)) : LinearIndependent K (f ∘ b)

views.nl_informal:
If `p` is a maximal ideal of `R`, and `S` is the integral closure of `R` in `L`,
then the dimension `[S/pS : R/p]` is equal to `[Frac(S) : Frac(R)]`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Ideal.finrank_quotient_map [IsDomain S] [IsDedekindDomain R] [Algebra K L] [Algebra R L] [IsScalarTower R K L] [IsScalarTower R S L] [hp : p.IsMaximal] [Module.Finite R S] : finrank (R ⧸ p) (S ⧸ map (algebraMap R S) p) = finrank K L

views.nl_informal:
Since the inclusion `(P^(i + 1) / P^e) ⊂ (P^i / P^e)` has a kernel isomorphic to `P / S`,
`[P^i / P^e : R / p] = [P^(i+1) / P^e : R / p] + [P / S : R / p]`
views.lean_signature: theorem Ideal.rank_pow_quot_aux [IsDedekindDomain S] [p.IsMaximal] [P.IsPrime] (hP0 : P ≠ ⊥) {i : ℕ} (hi : i < e) : Module.rank (R ⧸ p) (Ideal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (P ^ e)) (P ^ i)) = Module.rank (R ⧸ p) (S ⧸ P) + Module.rank (R ⧸ p) (Ideal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (P ^ e)) (P ^ (i + 1)))

views.nl_informal:
If `p` is a maximal ideal of `R`, `S` extends `R` and `P^e` lies over `p`,
then the dimension `[S/(P^e) : R/p]` is equal to `e * [S/P : R/p]`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Ideal.rank_prime_pow_ramificationIdx [IsDedekindDomain S] [p.IsMaximal] [P.IsPrime] (hP0 : P ≠ ⊥) (he : e ≠ 0) : Module.rank (R ⧸ p) (S ⧸ P ^ e) = e • @Module.rank (R ⧸ p) (S ⧸ P) _ _ (@Algebra.toModule _ _ _ _ <| @Quotient.algebraQuotientOfRamificationIdxNeZero _ _ _ _ _ _ _ ⟨he⟩)

views.nl_informal:
If `p` is a maximal ideal of `R`, `S` extends `R` and `P^e` lies over `p`,
then the dimension `[S/(P^e) : R/p]`, as a natural number, is equal to `e * [S/P : R/p]`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Ideal.finrank_prime_pow_ramificationIdx [IsDedekindDomain S] (hP0 : P ≠ ⊥) [p.IsMaximal] [P.IsPrime] (he : e ≠ 0) : finrank (R ⧸ p) (S ⧸ P ^ e) = e * @finrank (R ⧸ p) (S ⧸ P) _ _ (@Algebra.toModule _ _ _ _ <| @Quotient.algebraQuotientOfRamificationIdxNeZero _ _ _ _ _ _ _ ⟨he⟩)

views.nl_informal:
The **fundamental identity** of ramification index `e` and inertia degree `f`:
for `P` ranging over the primes lying over `p`, `∑ P, e P * f P = [Frac(S) : Frac(R)]`;
here `S` is a finite `R`-module (and thus `Frac(S) : Frac(R)` is a finite extension) and `p`
is maximal.
views.lean_signature: theorem Ideal.sum_ramification_inertia (K L : Type*) [Field K] [Field L] [IsDedekindDomain R] [Algebra R K] [IsFractionRing R K] [Algebra S L] [IsFractionRing S L] [Algebra K L] [Algebra R L] [IsScalarTower R S L] [IsScalarTower R K L] [Module.Finite R S] [p.IsMaximal] (hp0 : p ≠ ⊥) : (∑ P ∈ (factors (map (algebraMap R S) p)).toFinset, ramificationIdx (algebraMap R S) p P * inertiaDeg p P) = finrank K L

views.nl_informal:
Let `T / S / R` be a tower of algebras, `p, P, Q` be ideals in `R, S, T` respectively,
and `P` and `Q` are prime. If `P = Q ∩ S`, then `e (Q | p) = e (P | p) * e (Q | P)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Ideal.ramificationIdx_algebra_tower [IsDedekindDomain S] [IsDedekindDomain T] {p : Ideal R} {P : Ideal S} {Q : Ideal T} [hpm : P.IsPrime] [hqm : Q.IsPrime] (hg0 : map (algebraMap S T) P ≠ ⊥) (hfg : map (algebraMap R T) p ≠ ⊥) (hg : map (algebraMap S T) P ≤ Q) : ramificationIdx (algebraMap R T) p Q = ramificationIdx (algebraMap R S) p P * ramificationIdx (algebraMap S T) P Q

views.nl_informal:
Let `T / S / R` be a tower of algebras, `p, P, I` be ideals in `R, S, T`, respectively,
and `p` and `P` are maximal. If `p = P ∩ S` and `P = I ∩ S`,
then `f (I | p) = f (P | p) * f (I | P)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Ideal.inertiaDeg_algebra_tower (p : Ideal R) (P : Ideal S) (I : Ideal T) [p.IsMaximal] [P.IsMaximal] [P.LiesOver p] [I.LiesOver P] : inertiaDeg p I = inertiaDeg p P * inertiaDeg P I

views.nl_informal:
If `p` is a maximal ideal of `A`, `P` and `Q` are prime ideals
lying over `p`, then there exists `σ ∈ Aut (B / A)` such that `σ P = Q`. In other words,
the Galois group `Gal(L / K)` acts transitively on the set of all prime ideals lying over `p`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Ideal.exists_map_eq_of_isGalois [IsGalois K L] : ∃ σ : B ≃ₐ[A] B, map σ P = Q

views.nl_informal: All the `ramificationIdx` over a fixed maximal ideal are the same.
views.lean_signature: theorem Ideal.ramificationIdx_eq_of_isGalois [IsGalois K L] : ramificationIdx (algebraMap A B) p P = ramificationIdx (algebraMap A B) p Q

views.nl_informal: All the `inertiaDeg` over a fixed maximal ideal are the same.
views.lean_signature: theorem Ideal.inertiaDeg_eq_of_isGalois [p.IsMaximal] [IsGalois K L] : inertiaDeg p P = inertiaDeg p Q

views.nl_informal: The `ramificationIdxIn` is equal to any ramification index over the same ideal.
views.lean_signature: theorem Ideal.ramificationIdxIn_eq_ramificationIdx [IsGalois K L] : ramificationIdxIn p B = ramificationIdx (algebraMap A B) p P

views.nl_informal: The `inertiaDegIn` is equal to any ramification index over the same ideal.
views.lean_signature: theorem Ideal.inertiaDegIn_eq_inertiaDeg [p.IsMaximal] [IsGalois K L] : inertiaDegIn p B = inertiaDeg p P

views.nl_informal: The form of the **fundamental identity** in the case of Galois extension.
views.lean_signature: theorem Ideal.ncard_primesOver_mul_ramificationIdxIn_mul_inertiaDegIn [IsGalois K L] : (primesOver p B).ncard * (ramificationIdxIn p B * inertiaDegIn p B) = Module.finrank K L

views.nl_informal:
Given a sequence of complex polynomials `fₚ`, a complex constant `s`, and a real constant `c` such
that `|fₚ(xs)| ≤ c ^ p` for all `p ∈ ℕ` and `x ∈ Ioc 0 1`, then there is also a nonnegative
constant `c'` such that for all nonzero `p ∈ ℕ`, `|P(fₚ, s)| ≤ c' ^ p`.
views.lean_signature: theorem LindemannWeierstrass.P_le (f : ℕ → ℂ[X]) (s : ℂ) (c : ℝ) (hc : ∀ p : ℕ, ∀ x ∈ Set.Ioc (0 : ℝ) 1, ‖(f p).eval (x • s)‖ ≤ c ^ p) : ∃ c' ≥ 0, ∀ p ≠ 0, ‖P (f p) s‖ ≤ c' ^ p

views.nl_informal:
Given a polynomial with integer coefficients `p` and a complex constant `s`, there is a nonnegative
`c` such that for all nonzero `q ∈ ℕ`, `|P(X ^ (q - 1) * p ^ q, s)| ≤ c ^ q`.

Note: Jacobson writes `h(x)` for `x ^ (q - 1) * p(x) ^ q` and `bⱼ` for its coefficients.
views.lean_signature: theorem LindemannWeierstrass.exp_polynomial_approx_aux (f : ℤ[X]) (s : ℂ) : ∃ c ≥ 0, ∀ p ≠ 0, ‖P (map (algebraMap ℤ ℂ) (X ^ (p - 1) * f ^ p)) s‖ ≤ c ^ p

views.nl_informal:
See equation (68), page 285 of [Jacobson, *Basic Algebra I, 4.12*][jacobson1974].

Given a polynomial `f` with integer coefficients, we can find a constant `c : ℝ` and for each prime
`p > |f₀|`, `nₚ : ℤ` and `gₚ : ℤ[X]` such that

* `p` does not divide `nₚ`
* `deg(gₚ) < p * deg(f)`
* all complex roots `r` of `f` satisfy `|nₚ * e ^ r - p * gₚ(r)| ≤ c ^ p / (p - 1)!`

In the proof of Lindemann-Weierstrass, we will take `f` to be a polynomial whose complex roots
are the algebraic numbers whose exponentials we want to prove to be linearly independent.

Note: Jacobson writes `Nₚ` for our `nₚ` and `M` for our `c` (modulo a constant factor).
views.lean_signature: theorem LindemannWeierstrass.exp_polynomial_approx (f : ℤ[X]) (hf : f.eval 0 ≠ 0) : ∃ c, ∀ p > (eval 0 f).natAbs, p.Prime → ∃ n : ℤ, ¬ ↑p ∣ n ∧ ∃ gp : ℤ[X], gp.natDegree ≤ p * f.natDegree - 1 ∧ ∀ {r : ℂ}, r ∈ f.aroots ℂ → ‖n • exp r - p • aeval r gp‖ ≤ c ^ p / (p - 1)!

views.nl_informal:
Let `Z, N` be types, let `R` be a metric space, let `α : R` be a point and let
`j : Z → N → R` be a function.  We aim to estimate how close we can get to `α`, while staying
in the image of `j`.  The points `j z a` of `R` in the image of `j` come with a "cost" equal to
`d a`.  As we get closer to `α` while staying in the image of `j`, we are interested in bounding
the quantity `d a * dist α (j z a)` from below by a strictly positive amount `1 / A`: the intuition
is that approximating well `α` with the points in the image of `j` should come at a high cost.  The
hypotheses on the function `f : R → R` provide us with sufficient conditions to ensure our goal.
The first hypothesis is that `f` is Lipschitz at `α`: this yields a bound on the distance.
The second hypothesis is specific to the Liouville argument and provides the missing bound
involving the cost function `d`.

This lemma collects the properties used in the proof of `exists_pos_real_of_irrational_root`.
It is stated in more general form than needed: in the intended application, `Z = ℤ`, `N = ℕ`,
`R = ℝ`, `d a = (a + 1) ^ f.nat_degree`, `j z a = z / (a + 1)`, `f ∈ ℤ[x]`, `α` is an irrational
root of `f`, `ε` is small, `M` is a bound on the Lipschitz constant of `f` near `α`, `n` is
the degree of the polynomial `f`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Liouville.exists_one_le_pow_mul_dist {Z N R : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace R] {d : N → ℝ} {j : Z → N → R} {f : R → R} {α : R} {ε M : ℝ} -- denominators are positive (d0 : ∀ a : N, 1 ≤ d a) (e0 : 0 < ε) -- function is Lipschitz at α (B : ∀ ⦃y : R⦄, y ∈ closedBall α ε → dist (f α) (f y) ≤ dist α y * M) -- clear denominators (L : ∀ ⦃z : Z⦄, ∀ ⦃a : N⦄, j z a ∈ closedBall α ε → 1 ≤ d a * dist (f α) (f (j z a))) : ∃ A : ℝ, 0 < A ∧ ∀ z : Z, ∀ a : N, 1 ≤ d a * (dist α (j z a) * A)

views.nl_informal:
Given a `CompositionSeries`, `s`, and an element `x`
such that `x` is maximal inside `s.last` there is a series, `t`,
such that `t.last = x`, `t.head = s.head`
and `snoc t s.last _` is equivalent to `s`.

views.nl_informal:
**Kőnig's infinity lemma** : if each element in a strongly atomic order
is covered by only finitely many others, and `b` is an element with infinitely many things above it,
then there is a sequence starting with `b` in which each element is covered by the next.
views.lean_signature: theorem exists_seq_covby_of_forall_covby_finite (hfin : ∀ (a : α), {x | a ⋖ x}.Finite) (hb : (Ici b).Infinite) : ∃ f : ℕ → α, f 0 = b ∧ ∀ i, f i ⋖ f (i+1)

views.nl_informal: The sequence given by Kőnig's lemma as an order embedding
views.lean_signature: theorem exists_orderEmbedding_covby_of_forall_covby_finite (hfin : ∀ (a : α), {x | a ⋖ x}.Finite) (hb : (Ici b).Infinite) : ∃ f : ℕ ↪o α, f 0 = b ∧ ∀ i, f i ⋖ f (i+1)

views.nl_informal:
A formulation of Kőnig's infinity lemma, useful in applications.
Given a sequence `α 0, α 1, ...` of nonempty types with `α 0` finite,
and a well-behaved family of projections `π : α j → α i` for all `i ≤ j`,
if each term in each `α i` is the projection of only finitely many terms in `α (i+1)`,
then we can find a sequence `(f 0 : α 0), (f 1 : α 1), ...`
where `f i` is the projection of `f j` for all `i ≤ j`.

In a typical application, the `α i` are function types with increasingly large domains,
and `π hij (f : α j)` is the restriction of the domain of `f` to that of `α i`.
In this case, the sequence given by the lemma is essentially a function whose domain
is the limit of the `α i`.

See also `nonempty_sections_of_finite_cofiltered_system`.
views.lean_signature: theorem exists_seq_forall_proj_of_forall_finite {α : ℕ → Type*} [Finite (α 0)] [∀ i, Nonempty (α i)] (π : {i j : ℕ} → (hij : i ≤ j) → α j → α i) (π_refl : ∀ ⦃i⦄ (a : α i), π rfl.le a = a) (π_trans : ∀ ⦃i j k⦄ (hij : i ≤ j) (hjk : j ≤ k) a, π hij (π hjk a) = π (hij.trans hjk) a) (hfin : ∀ i a, {b : α (i+1) | π (Nat.le_add_right i 1) b = a}.Finite) : ∃ f : (i : ℕ) → α i, ∀ ⦃i j⦄ (hij : i ≤ j), π hij (f j) = f i

views.nl_informal:
The **coheight** of an element `a` in a preorder `α` is the supremum of the rightmost index of all
relation series of `α` ordered by `<` and beginning with `a`.

This is not the definition of `coheight`. The definition of `coheight` is via the `height` in the
dual order, in order to easily transfer theorems between `height` and `coheight`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Order.coheight_eq (a : α) : coheight a = ⨆ (p : LTSeries α) (_ : a ≤ p.head), (p.length : ℕ∞)

views.nl_informal: Alternative definition of height, with the supremum ranging only over those series that end at `a`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Order.height_eq_iSup_last_eq (a : α) : height a = ⨆ (p : LTSeries α) (_ : p.last = a), ↑(p.length)

views.nl_informal:
Alternative definition of coheight, with the supremum only ranging over those series
that begin at `a`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Order.coheight_eq_iSup_head_eq (a : α) : coheight a = ⨆ (p : LTSeries α) (_ : p.head = a), ↑(p.length)

views.nl_informal: The height of the last element in a series is larger or equal to the length of the series.
views.lean_signature: theorem Order.length_le_height_last {p : LTSeries α} : p.length ≤ height p.last

views.nl_informal: The coheight of the first element in a series is larger or equal to the length of the series.
views.lean_signature: theorem Order.length_le_coheight_head {p : LTSeries α} : p.length ≤ coheight p.head

views.nl_informal: The height of an element in a series is larger or equal to its index in the series.
views.lean_signature: theorem Order.index_le_height (p : LTSeries α) (i : Fin (p.length + 1)) : i ≤ height (p i)

views.nl_informal: The coheight of an element in a series is larger or equal to its reverse index in the series.
views.lean_signature: theorem Order.rev_index_le_coheight (p : LTSeries α) (i : Fin (p.length + 1)) : i.rev ≤ coheight (p i)

views.nl_informal:
In a maximally long series, i.e one as long as the height of the last element, the height of each
element is its index in the series.
views.lean_signature: theorem Order.height_eq_index_of_length_eq_height_last {p : LTSeries α} (h : p.length = height p.last) (i : Fin (p.length + 1)) : height (p i) = i

views.nl_informal:
In a maximally long series, i.e one as long as the coheight of the first element, the coheight of
each element is its reverse index in the series.
views.lean_signature: theorem Order.coheight_eq_index_of_length_eq_head_coheight {p : LTSeries α} (h : p.length = coheight p.head) (i : Fin (p.length + 1)) : coheight (p i) = i.rev

views.lean_signature: theorem Order.exists_series_of_le_height (a : α) {n : ℕ} (h : n ≤ height a) : ∃ p : LTSeries α, p.last = a ∧ p.length = n

views.nl_informal: Another characterization of height, based on the supremum of the heights of elements below.
views.lean_signature: theorem Order.height_eq_iSup_lt_height (x : α) : height x = ⨆ y < x, height y + 1

views.nl_informal: Another characterization of coheight, based on the supremum of the coheights of elements above.
views.lean_signature: theorem Order.coheight_eq_iSup_gt_coheight (x : α) : coheight x = ⨆ y > x, coheight y + 1

views.nl_informal:
The height of an element is infinite iff there exist series of arbitrary length ending in that
element.
views.lean_signature: theorem Order.height_eq_top_iff {x : α} : height x = ⊤ ↔ ∀ n, ∃ p : LTSeries α, p.last = x ∧ p.length = n

views.nl_informal:
The coheight of an element is infinite iff there exist series of arbitrary length ending in that
element.

views.nl_informal:
The Krull dimension is the supremum of the elements' coheights.

views.nl_informal:
The Krull dimension is the supremum of the elements' heights.

If `α` is `Nonempty`, then `krullDim_eq_iSup_height_of_nonempty`, with the coercion from

views.nl_informal:
The Krull dimension is the supremum of the elements' coheights.

views.nl_informal:
Let `r` be a relation on `α`, let `f : α → β` be a function, let `C : β → Prop`, and
let `bot : α`. This induction principle shows that `C (f bot)` holds, given that
* some `a` that is accessible by `r` satisfies `C (f a)`, and
* for each `b` such that `f b ≠ f bot` and `C (f b)` holds, there is `c`
  satisfying `r c b` and `C (f c)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Acc.induction_bot' {α β} {r : α → α → Prop} {a bot : α} (ha : Acc r a) {C : β → Prop} {f : α → β} (ih : ∀ b, f b ≠ f bot → C (f b) → ∃ c, r c b ∧ C (f c)) : C (f a) → C (f bot)

views.nl_informal:
Let `r` be a relation on `α`, let `C : α → Prop` and let `bot : α`.
This induction principle shows that `C bot` holds, given that
* some `a` that is accessible by `r` satisfies `C a`, and
* for each `b ≠ bot` such that `C b` holds, there is `c` satisfying `r c b` and `C c`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Acc.induction_bot {α} {r : α → α → Prop} {a bot : α} (ha : Acc r a) {C : α → Prop} (ih : ∀ b, b ≠ bot → C b → ∃ c, r c b ∧ C c) : C a → C bot

views.nl_informal:
Let `r` be a well-founded relation on `α`, let `f : α → β` be a function,
let `C : β → Prop`, and let `bot : α`.
This induction principle shows that `C (f bot)` holds, given that
* some `a` satisfies `C (f a)`, and
* for each `b` such that `f b ≠ f bot` and `C (f b)` holds, there is `c`
  satisfying `r c b` and `C (f c)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem WellFounded.induction_bot' {α β} {r : α → α → Prop} (hwf : WellFounded r) {a bot : α} {C : β → Prop} {f : α → β} (ih : ∀ b, f b ≠ f bot → C (f b) → ∃ c, r c b ∧ C (f c)) : C (f a) → C (f bot)

views.nl_informal:
Let `r` be a well-founded relation on `α`, let `C : α → Prop`, and let `bot : α`.
This induction principle shows that `C bot` holds, given that
* some `a` satisfies `C a`, and
* for each `b` that satisfies `C b`, there is `c` satisfying `r c b` and `C c`.

The naming is inspired by the fact that when `r` is transitive, it follows that `bot` is
the smallest element w.r.t. `r` that satisfies `C`.

views.nl_informal:
A compact element `k` has the property that any `b < k` lies below a "maximal element below

views.nl_informal:
Introduction rule to prove that `b` is the supremum of `s`: it suffices to check that `b`
is larger than all elements of `s`, and that this is not the case of any `w < b`.
See `csSup_eq_of_forall_le_of_forall_lt_exists_gt` for a version in conditionally complete
lattices.
views.lean_signature: theorem sSup_eq_of_forall_le_of_forall_lt_exists_gt (h₁ : ∀ a ∈ s, a ≤ b) (h₂ : ∀ w, w < b → ∃ a ∈ s, w < a) : sSup s = b

views.nl_informal:
Introduction rule to prove that `b` is the infimum of `s`: it suffices to check that `b`
is smaller than all elements of `s`, and that this is not the case of any `w > b`.
See `csInf_eq_of_forall_ge_of_forall_gt_exists_lt` for a version in conditionally complete
lattices.
views.lean_signature: theorem sInf_eq_of_forall_ge_of_forall_gt_exists_lt : (∀ a ∈ s, b ≤ a) → (∀ w, b < w → ∃ a ∈ s, a < w) → sInf s = b

views.nl_informal:
Introduction rule to prove that `b` is the supremum of `f`: it suffices to check that `b`
is larger than `f i` for all `i`, and that this is not the case of any `w<b`.
See `ciSup_eq_of_forall_le_of_forall_lt_exists_gt` for a version in conditionally complete
lattices.
views.lean_signature: theorem iSup_eq_of_forall_le_of_forall_lt_exists_gt {f : ι → α} (h₁ : ∀ i, f i ≤ b) (h₂ : ∀ w, w < b → ∃ i, w < f i) : ⨆ i : ι, f i = b

views.nl_informal:
Introduction rule to prove that `b` is the infimum of `f`: it suffices to check that `b`
is smaller than `f i` for all `i`, and that this is not the case of any `w>b`.
See `ciInf_eq_of_forall_ge_of_forall_gt_exists_lt` for a version in conditionally complete
lattices.
views.lean_signature: theorem iInf_eq_of_forall_ge_of_forall_gt_exists_lt : (∀ i, b ≤ f i) → (∀ w, b < w → ∃ i, f i < w) → ⨅ i, f i = b

views.nl_informal:
When taking the supremum of `f : ι → α`, the elements of `ι` on which `f` gives `⊥` can be

views.lean_signature: theorem iSup_ne_bot_subtype (f : ι → α) : ⨆ i : { i // f i ≠ ⊥ }, f i = ⨆ i, f i

views.nl_informal:
When taking the infimum of `f : ι → α`, the elements of `ι` on which `f` gives `⊤` can be
dropped, without changing the result.
views.lean_signature: theorem iInf_ne_top_subtype (f : ι → α) : ⨅ i : { i // f i ≠ ⊤ }, f i = ⨅ i, f i

views.nl_informal:
**Hausdorff's maximality principle**

There exists a maximal totally ordered set of `α`.
