views.lean_signature: theorem maxChain_spec : IsMaxChain r (maxChain r)

views.nl_informal:
Supremum of `s i`, `i : ι`, is equal to the supremum over `t : Finset ι` of suprema
`⨆ i ∈ t, s i`. This version assumes `ι` is a `Type*`. See `iSup_eq_iSup_finset'` for a version
that works for `ι : Sort*`.
views.lean_signature: theorem iSup_eq_iSup_finset (s : ι → α) : ⨆ i, s i = ⨆ t : Finset ι, ⨆ i ∈ t, s i

views.nl_informal:
Supremum of `s i`, `i : ι`, is equal to the supremum over `t : Finset ι` of suprema
`⨆ i ∈ t, s i`. This version works for `ι : Sort*`. See `iSup_eq_iSup_finset` for a version
that assumes `ι : Type*` but has no `PLift`s.
views.lean_signature: theorem iSup_eq_iSup_finset' (s : ι' → α) : ⨆ i, s i = ⨆ t : Finset (PLift ι'), ⨆ i ∈ t, s (PLift.down i)

views.nl_informal:
Infimum of `s i`, `i : ι`, is equal to the infimum over `t : Finset ι` of infima
`⨅ i ∈ t, s i`. This version assumes `ι` is a `Type*`. See `iInf_eq_iInf_finset'` for a version
that works for `ι : Sort*`.
views.lean_signature: theorem iInf_eq_iInf_finset (s : ι → α) : ⨅ i, s i = ⨅ (t : Finset ι) (i ∈ t), s i

views.nl_informal:
Infimum of `s i`, `i : ι`, is equal to the infimum over `t : Finset ι` of infima
`⨅ i ∈ t, s i`. This version works for `ι : Sort*`. See `iInf_eq_iInf_finset` for a version
that assumes `ι : Type*` but has no `PLift`s.
views.lean_signature: theorem iInf_eq_iInf_finset' (s : ι' → α) : ⨅ i, s i = ⨅ t : Finset (PLift ι'), ⨅ i ∈ t, s (PLift.down i)

views.nl_informal:
Union of an indexed family of sets `s : ι → Set α` is equal to the union of the unions
of finite subfamilies. This version assumes `ι : Type*`. See also `iUnion_eq_iUnion_finset'` for
a version that works for `ι : Sort*`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Set.iUnion_eq_iUnion_finset (s : ι → Set α) : ⋃ i, s i = ⋃ t : Finset ι, ⋃ i ∈ t, s i

views.nl_informal:
Union of an indexed family of sets `s : ι → Set α` is equal to the union of the unions
of finite subfamilies. This version works for `ι : Sort*`. See also `iUnion_eq_iUnion_finset` for
a version that assumes `ι : Type*` but avoids `PLift`s in the right hand side.
views.lean_signature: theorem Set.iUnion_eq_iUnion_finset' (s : ι' → Set α) : ⋃ i, s i = ⋃ t : Finset (PLift ι'), ⋃ i ∈ t, s (PLift.down i)

views.nl_informal:
Intersection of an indexed family of sets `s : ι → Set α` is equal to the intersection of the
intersections of finite subfamilies. This version assumes `ι : Type*`. See also
`iInter_eq_iInter_finset'` for a version that works for `ι : Sort*`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Set.iInter_eq_iInter_finset (s : ι → Set α) : ⋂ i, s i = ⋂ t : Finset ι, ⋂ i ∈ t, s i

views.nl_informal:
Intersection of an indexed family of sets `s : ι → Set α` is equal to the intersection of the
intersections of finite subfamilies. This version works for `ι : Sort*`. See also
`iInter_eq_iInter_finset` for a version that assumes `ι : Type*` but avoids `PLift`s in the right
hand side.
views.lean_signature: theorem Set.iInter_eq_iInter_finset' (s : ι' → Set α) : ⋂ i, s i = ⋂ t : Finset (PLift ι'), ⋂ i ∈ t, s (PLift.down i)

views.nl_informal: A greatest element of a set is the supremum of this set.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsGreatest.csSup_eq (H : IsGreatest s a) : sSup s = a

views.nl_informal: A least element of a set is the infimum of this set.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsLeast.csInf_eq (H : IsLeast s a) : sInf s = a

views.nl_informal:
Introduction rule to prove that `b` is the supremum of `s`: it suffices to check that `b`
is larger than all elements of `s`, and that this is not the case of any `w<b`.
See `sSup_eq_of_forall_le_of_forall_lt_exists_gt` for a version in complete lattices.
views.lean_signature: theorem csSup_eq_of_forall_le_of_forall_lt_exists_gt (hs : s.Nonempty) (H : ∀ a ∈ s, a ≤ b) (H' : ∀ w, w < b → ∃ a ∈ s, w < a) : sSup s = b

views.nl_informal:
Introduction rule to prove that `b` is the infimum of `s`: it suffices to check that `b`
is smaller than all elements of `s`, and that this is not the case of any `w>b`.
See `sInf_eq_of_forall_ge_of_forall_gt_exists_lt` for a version in complete lattices.
views.lean_signature: theorem csInf_eq_of_forall_ge_of_forall_gt_exists_lt : s.Nonempty → (∀ a ∈ s, b ≤ a) → (∀ w, b < w → ∃ a ∈ s, a < w) → sInf s = b

views.nl_informal:
`b < sSup s` when there is an element `a` in `s` with `b < a`, when `s` is bounded above.
This is essentially an iff, except that the assumptions for the two implications are
slightly different (one needs boundedness above for one direction, nonemptiness and linear
order for the other one), so we formulate separately the two implications, contrary to
the `CompleteLattice` case.
views.lean_signature: theorem lt_csSup_of_lt (hs : BddAbove s) (ha : a ∈ s) (h : b < a) : b < sSup s

views.nl_informal:
`sInf s < b` when there is an element `a` in `s` with `a < b`, when `s` is bounded below.
This is essentially an iff, except that the assumptions for the two implications are
slightly different (one needs boundedness below for one direction, nonemptiness and linear
order for the other one), so we formulate separately the two implications, contrary to
the `CompleteLattice` case.
views.lean_signature: theorem csInf_lt_of_lt : BddBelow s → a ∈ s → a < b → sInf s < b

views.nl_informal:
If all elements of a nonempty set `s` are less than or equal to all elements
of a nonempty set `t`, then there exists an element between these sets.
views.lean_signature: theorem exists_between_of_forall_le (sne : s.Nonempty) (tne : t.Nonempty) (hst : ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ t, x ≤ y) : (upperBounds s ∩ lowerBounds t).Nonempty

views.nl_informal: The supremum of a singleton is the element of the singleton
views.lean_signature: theorem csSup_singleton (a : α) : sSup {a} = a

views.nl_informal: The infimum of a singleton is the element of the singleton
views.lean_signature: theorem csInf_singleton (a : α) : sInf {a} = a

views.nl_informal:
If a set is bounded below and above, and nonempty, its infimum is less than or equal to
its supremum.
views.lean_signature: theorem csInf_le_csSup (hb : BddBelow s) (ha : BddAbove s) (ne : s.Nonempty) : sInf s ≤ sSup s

views.nl_informal:
The `sSup` of a union of two sets is the max of the suprema of each subset, under the
assumptions that all sets are bounded above and nonempty.
views.lean_signature: theorem csSup_union (hs : BddAbove s) (sne : s.Nonempty) (ht : BddAbove t) (tne : t.Nonempty) : sSup (s ∪ t) = sSup s ⊔ sSup t

views.nl_informal:
The `sInf` of a union of two sets is the min of the infima of each subset, under the assumptions
that all sets are bounded below and nonempty.
views.lean_signature: theorem csInf_union (hs : BddBelow s) (sne : s.Nonempty) (ht : BddBelow t) (tne : t.Nonempty) : sInf (s ∪ t) = sInf s ⊓ sInf t

views.nl_informal:
The supremum of an intersection of two sets is bounded by the minimum of the suprema of each
set, if all sets are bounded above and nonempty.
views.lean_signature: theorem csSup_inter_le (hs : BddAbove s) (ht : BddAbove t) (hst : (s ∩ t).Nonempty) : sSup (s ∩ t) ≤ sSup s ⊓ sSup t

views.nl_informal:
The infimum of an intersection of two sets is bounded below by the maximum of the
infima of each set, if all sets are bounded below and nonempty.
views.lean_signature: theorem le_csInf_inter : BddBelow s → BddBelow t → (s ∩ t).Nonempty → sInf s ⊔ sInf t ≤ sInf (s ∩ t)

views.nl_informal:
The supremum of `insert a s` is the maximum of `a` and the supremum of `s`, if `s` is
nonempty and bounded above.
views.lean_signature: theorem csSup_insert (hs : BddAbove s) (sne : s.Nonempty) : sSup (insert a s) = a ⊔ sSup s

views.nl_informal:
The infimum of `insert a s` is the minimum of `a` and the infimum of `s`, if `s` is
nonempty and bounded below.
views.lean_signature: theorem csInf_insert (hs : BddBelow s) (sne : s.Nonempty) : sInf (insert a s) = a ⊓ sInf s

views.nl_informal:
Introduction rule to prove that `b` is the supremum of `s`: it suffices to check that

2) every other upper bound `b'` satisfies `b ≤ b'`.

views.nl_informal:
When `b < sSup s`, there is an element `a` in `s` with `b < a`, if `s` is nonempty and the order

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:
When every element of a set `s` is bounded by an element of a set `t`, and conversely, then

Introduction rule to prove that `b` is the infimum of `f`: it suffices to check that `b`

views.nl_informal:
If `f : ι → Filter α` is directed, `α` is not empty, and `∀ i, f i ≠ ⊥`, then `iInf f ≠ ⊥`.

views.nl_informal: If `α` is a preorder with no bottom element, then `atBot ≤ cofinite`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.atBot_le_cofinite [Preorder α] [NoBotOrder α] : (atBot : Filter α) ≤ cofinite

views.nl_informal: The coproduct of the cofinite filters on two types is the cofinite filter on their product.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.coprod_cofinite : (cofinite : Filter α).coprod (cofinite : Filter β) = cofinite

views.nl_informal: If `l ≥ Filter.cofinite` is a countably generated filter, then `l.ker` is cocountable.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.countable_compl_ker [l.IsCountablyGenerated] (h : cofinite ≤ l) : Set.Countable l.kerᶜ

views.nl_informal:
If `f` tends to a countably generated filter `l` along `Filter.cofinite`,
then for all but countably many elements, `f x ∈ l.ker`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.Tendsto.countable_compl_preimage_ker {f : α → β} {l : Filter β} [l.IsCountablyGenerated] (h : Tendsto f cofinite l) : Set.Countable (f ⁻¹' l.ker)ᶜ
theorem Filter.univ_pi_mem_pi {α : ι → Type*} {s : ∀ i, Set (α i)} {l : ∀ i, Filter (α i)} (h : ∀ i, s i ∈ l i) (hfin : ∀ᶠ i in cofinite, s i = univ) : univ.pi s ∈ pi l

views.nl_informal:
Given a family of maps `f i : α i → β i` and a family of filters `l i : Filter (α i)`,
if all but finitely many of `f i` are surjective,
then the indexed product of `f i`s maps the indexed product of the filters `l i`
to the indexed products of their pushforwards under individual `f i`s.

See also `map_piMap_pi_finite` for the case of a finite index type.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.map_piMap_pi {α β : ι → Type*} {f : ∀ i, α i → β i} (hf : ∀ᶠ i in cofinite, Surjective (f i)) (l : ∀ i, Filter (α i)) : map (Pi.map f) (pi l) = pi fun i ↦ map (f i) (l i)

views.nl_informal:
Given finite families of maps `f i : α i → β i` and of filters `l i : Filter (α i)`,
the indexed product of `f i`s maps the indexed product of the filters `l i`
to the indexed products of their pushforwards under individual `f i`s.

See also `map_piMap_pi` for a more general case.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.map_piMap_pi_finite {α β : ι → Type*} [Finite ι] (f : ∀ i, α i → β i) (l : ∀ i, Filter (α i)) : map (Pi.map f) (pi l) = pi fun i ↦ map (f i) (l i)

views.nl_informal: For natural numbers the filters `Filter.cofinite` and `Filter.atTop` coincide.
views.lean_signature: theorem Nat.cofinite_eq_atTop : @cofinite ℕ = atTop

views.nl_informal:
For an injective function `f`, inverse images of finite sets are finite. See also
`Filter.comap_cofinite_le` and `Function.Injective.comap_cofinite_eq`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Function.Injective.tendsto_cofinite {f : α → β} (hf : Injective f) : Tendsto f cofinite cofinite

views.nl_informal: For a function with finite fibres, inverse images of finite sets are finite.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.Tendsto.cofinite_of_finite_preimage_singleton {f : α → β} (hf : ∀ b, Finite (f ⁻¹' {b})) : Tendsto f cofinite cofinite

views.nl_informal:
The pullback of the `Filter.cofinite` under an injective function is equal to `Filter.cofinite`.
See also `Filter.comap_cofinite_le` and `Function.Injective.tendsto_cofinite`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Function.Injective.comap_cofinite_eq {f : α → β} (hf : Injective f) : comap f cofinite = cofinite

views.nl_informal: An injective sequence `f : ℕ → ℕ` tends to infinity at infinity.
views.lean_signature: theorem Function.Injective.nat_tendsto_atTop {f : ℕ → ℕ} (hf : Injective f) : Tendsto f atTop atTop

views.nl_informal:
A set is in the `countableInterFilter` generated by `g` if and only if
it contains a countable intersection of elements of `g`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.mem_countableGenerate_iff {s : Set α} : s ∈ countableGenerate g ↔ ∃ S : Set (Set α), S ⊆ g ∧ S.Countable ∧ ⋂₀ S ⊆ s

views.nl_informal: `countableGenerate g` is the greatest `countableInterFilter` containing `g`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.countableGenerate_isGreatest : IsGreatest { f : Filter α | CountableInterFilter f ∧ g ⊆ f.sets } (countableGenerate g)

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is countably generated and `f.HasBasis p s`, then `f` admits a decreasing basis
enumerated by natural numbers such that all sets have the form `s i`. More precisely, there is a
sequence `i n` such that `p (i n)` for all `n` and `s (i n)` is a decreasing sequence of sets which
forms a basis of `f`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.HasBasis.exists_antitone_subbasis {f : Filter α} [h : f.IsCountablyGenerated] {p : ι' → Prop} {s : ι' → Set α} (hs : f.HasBasis p s) : ∃ x : ℕ → ι', (∀ i, p (x i)) ∧ f.HasAntitoneBasis fun i => s (x i)

views.nl_informal: A countably generated filter admits a basis formed by an antitone sequence of sets.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.exists_antitone_basis (f : Filter α) [f.IsCountablyGenerated] : ∃ x : ℕ → Set α, f.HasAntitoneBasis x

views.nl_informal:
`f` is eventually bounded if and only if, there exists an admissible set on which it is
bounded.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.isBounded_iff : f.IsBounded r ↔ ∃ s ∈ f.sets, ∃ b, s ⊆ { x | r x b }

views.nl_informal: A bounded function `u` is in particular eventually bounded.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.isBoundedUnder_of {f : Filter β} {u : β → α} : (∃ b, ∀ x, r (u x) b) → f.IsBoundedUnder r u

views.nl_informal: A bounded above function `u` is in particular eventually bounded above.
views.lean_signature: theorem BddAbove.isBoundedUnder_of_range (hu : BddAbove (Set.range u)) : f.IsBoundedUnder (· ≤ ·) u

views.nl_informal: A bounded below function `u` is in particular eventually bounded below.
views.lean_signature: theorem BddBelow.isBoundedUnder_of_range (hu : BddBelow (Set.range u)) : f.IsBoundedUnder (· ≥ ·) u

views.nl_informal:
To check that a filter is frequently bounded, it suffices to have a witness
which bounds `f` at some point for every admissible set.

This is only an implication, as the other direction is wrong for the trivial filter.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.IsCobounded.mk [IsTrans α r] (a : α) (h : ∀ s ∈ f, ∃ x ∈ s, r a x) : f.IsCobounded r

views.nl_informal:
A filter which is eventually bounded is in particular frequently bounded (in the opposite
direction). At least if the filter is not trivial.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.IsBounded.isCobounded_flip [IsTrans α r] [NeBot f] : f.IsBounded r → f.IsCobounded (flip r)

views.nl_informal:
For nontrivial filters in linear orders, coboundedness for `≤` implies frequent boundedness
from below.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.IsCobounded.frequently_ge [LinearOrder α] [NeBot f] (cobdd : IsCobounded (· ≤ ·) f) : ∃ l, ∃ᶠ x in f, l ≤ x

views.nl_informal:
For nontrivial filters in linear orders, coboundedness for `≥` implies frequent boundedness
from above.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.IsCobounded.frequently_le [LinearOrder α] [NeBot f] (cobdd : IsCobounded (· ≥ ·) f) : ∃ u, ∃ᶠ x in f, x ≤ u

views.nl_informal: In linear orders, frequent boundedness from below implies coboundedness for `≤`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.IsCobounded.of_frequently_ge [LinearOrder α] {l : α} (freq_ge : ∃ᶠ x in f, l ≤ x) : IsCobounded (· ≤ ·) f

views.nl_informal: In linear orders, frequent boundedness from above implies coboundedness for `≥`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.IsCobounded.of_frequently_le [LinearOrder α] {u : α} (freq_le : ∃ᶠ r in f, r ≤ u) : IsCobounded (· ≥ ·) f

views.nl_informal:
If `(p : ι → Prop, s : ι → Set α)` is a basis of a filter `f`, `g` is a monotone function
`Set α → Filter γ`, and for each `i`, `(pg : β i → Prop, sg : β i → Set α)` is a basis
of the filter `g (s i)`, then
`(fun (i : ι) (x : β i) ↦ p i ∧ pg i x, fun (i : ι) (x : β i) ↦ sg i x)` is a basis
of the filter `f.lift g`.

This basis is parametrized by `i : ι` and `x : β i`, so in order to formulate this fact using
`Filter.HasBasis` one has to use `Σ i, β i` as the index type, see `Filter.HasBasis.lift`.
This lemma states the corresponding `mem_iff` statement without using a sigma type.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.HasBasis.mem_lift_iff {ι} {p : ι → Prop} {s : ι → Set α} {f : Filter α} (hf : f.HasBasis p s) {β : ι → Type*} {pg : ∀ i, β i → Prop} {sg : ∀ i, β i → Set γ} {g : Set α → Filter γ} (hg : ∀ i, (g <| s i).HasBasis (pg i) (sg i)) (gm : Monotone g) {s : Set γ} : s ∈ f.lift g ↔ ∃ i, p i ∧ ∃ x, pg i x ∧ sg i x ⊆ s

views.nl_informal:
If `(p : ι → Prop, s : ι → Set α)` is a basis of a filter `f`, `g` is a monotone function
`Set α → Filter γ`, and for each `i`, `(pg : β i → Prop, sg : β i → Set α)` is a basis
of the filter `g (s i)`, then
`(fun (i : ι) (x : β i) ↦ p i ∧ pg i x, fun (i : ι) (x : β i) ↦ sg i x)`
is a basis of the filter `f.lift g`.

This basis is parametrized by `i : ι` and `x : β i`, so in order to formulate this fact using
`has_basis` one has to use `Σ i, β i` as the index type. See also `Filter.HasBasis.mem_lift_iff`
for the corresponding `mem_iff` statement formulated without using a sigma type.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.HasBasis.lift {ι} {p : ι → Prop} {s : ι → Set α} {f : Filter α} (hf : f.HasBasis p s) {β : ι → Type*} {pg : ∀ i, β i → Prop} {sg : ∀ i, β i → Set γ} {g : Set α → Filter γ} (hg : ∀ i, (g (s i)).HasBasis (pg i) (sg i)) (gm : Monotone g) : (f.lift g).HasBasis (fun i : Σi, β i => p i.1 ∧ pg i.1 i.2) fun i : Σi, β i => sg i.1 i.2

views.nl_informal:
If functions `m₁` and `m₂` are eventually equal at a filter `f`, then
they map this filter to the same filter.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.map_congr {m₁ m₂ : α → β} {f : Filter α} (h : m₁ =ᶠ[f] m₂) : map m₁ f = map m₂ f

views.nl_informal:
If `a` is a left identity for `f : α → β → β`, then `pure a` is a left identity for
`Filter.map₂ f`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.map₂_left_identity {f : α → β → β} {a : α} (h : ∀ b, f a b = b) (l : Filter β) : map₂ f (pure a) l = l

views.nl_informal:
If `b` is a right identity for `f : α → β → α`, then `pure b` is a right identity for
`Filter.map₂ f`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.map₂_right_identity {f : α → β → α} {b : β} (h : ∀ a, f a b = a) (l : Filter α) : map₂ f l (pure b) = l

views.nl_informal:
The indexed product of finitely many principal filters
is the principal filter corresponding to the cylinder `Set.univ.pi s`.

If the index type is infinite, then `mem_pi_principal` and `hasBasis_pi_principal` may be useful.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.pi_principal [Finite ι] (s : (i : ι) → Set (α i)) : pi (fun i ↦ 𝓟 (s i)) = 𝓟 (univ.pi s)

views.nl_informal:
The indexed product of a (possibly, infinite) family of principal filters
is generated by the finite `Set.pi` cylinders.

If the index type is finite, then the indexed product of principal filters
is a pricipal filter, see `pi_principal`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.mem_pi_principal {t : Set ((i : ι) → α i)} : t ∈ pi (fun i ↦ 𝓟 (s i)) ↔ ∃ I : Set ι, I.Finite ∧ I.pi s ⊆ t

views.nl_informal:
The indexed product of a (possibly, infinite) family of principal filters
is generated by the finite `Set.pi` cylinders.

If the index type is finite, then the indexed product of principal filters
is a pricipal filter, see `pi_principal`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.hasBasis_pi_principal (s : (i : ι) → Set (α i)) : HasBasis (pi fun i ↦ 𝓟 (s i)) Set.Finite (Set.pi · s)

views.nl_informal:
The indexed product of finitely many pure filters `pure (f i)` is the pure filter `pure f`.

If the index type is infinite, then `mem_pi_pure` and `hasBasis_pi_pure` below may be useful.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.pi_pure [Finite ι] (f : (i : ι) → α i) : pi (pure <| f ·) = pure f

views.nl_informal:
The indexed product of a (possibly, infinite) family of pure filters `pure (f i)`
is generated by the sets of functions that are equal to `f` on a finite set.

If the index type is finite, then the indexed product of pure filters is a pure filter,
see `pi_pure`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.mem_pi_pure {f : (i : ι) → α i} {s : Set ((i : ι) → α i)} : s ∈ pi (fun i ↦ pure (f i)) ↔ ∃ I : Set ι, I.Finite ∧ ∀ g, (∀ i ∈ I, g i = f i) → g ∈ s

views.nl_informal:
The indexed product of a (possibly, infinite) family of pure filters `pure (f i)`
is generated by the sets of functions that are equal to `f` on a finite set.

If the index type is finite, then the indexed product of pure filters is a pure filter,
see `pi_pure`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.hasBasis_pi_pure (f : (i : ι) → α i) : HasBasis (pi fun i ↦ pure (f i)) Set.Finite (fun I ↦ {g | ∀ i ∈ I, g i = f i})

views.nl_informal:
If a function tends to a product `g ×ˢ h` of filters, then its first component tends to
`g`. See also `Filter.Tendsto.fst_nhds` for the special case of converging to a point in a
product of two topological spaces.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.Tendsto.fst {h : Filter γ} {m : α → β × γ} (H : Tendsto m f (g ×ˢ h)) : Tendsto (fun a ↦ (m a).1) f g

views.nl_informal:
If a function tends to a product `g ×ˢ h` of filters, then its second component tends to
`h`. See also `Filter.Tendsto.snd_nhds` for the special case of converging to a point in a
product of two topological spaces.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.Tendsto.snd {h : Filter γ} {m : α → β × γ} (H : Tendsto m f (g ×ˢ h)) : Tendsto (fun a ↦ (m a).2) f h

views.nl_informal:
A fact that is eventually true about all pairs `l ×ˢ l` is eventually true about
all diagonal pairs `(i, i)`
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.Eventually.diag_of_prod {p : α × α → Prop} (h : ∀ᶠ i in f ×ˢ f, p i) : ∀ᶠ i in f, p (i, i)

views.nl_informal:
`p ∧ q` occurs frequently along the product of two filters
iff both `p` and `q` occur frequently along the corresponding filters.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.frequently_prod_and {p : α → Prop} {q : β → Prop} : (∃ᶠ x in f ×ˢ g, p x.1 ∧ q x.2) ↔ (∃ᶠ a in f, p a) ∧ ∃ᶠ b in g, q b

views.nl_informal:
Characterization of the coproduct of the `Filter.map`s of two principal filters `𝓟 {a}` and
`𝓟 {i}`, the first under the constant function `fun a => b` and the second under the identity
function. Together with the next lemma, `map_prodMap_const_id_principal_coprod_principal`, this
provides an example showing that the inequality in the lemma `map_prodMap_coprod_le` can be strict.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.map_const_principal_coprod_map_id_principal {α β ι : Type*} (a : α) (b : β) (i : ι) : (map (fun _ => b) (𝓟 {a})).coprod (map id (𝓟 {i})) = 𝓟 ((({b} : Set β) ×ˢ univ) ∪ (univ ×ˢ ({i} : Set ι)))

views.nl_informal:
Characterization of the `Filter.map` of the coproduct of two principal filters `𝓟 {a}` and
`𝓟 {i}`, under the `Prod.map` of two functions, respectively the constant function `fun a => b` and
the identity function.  Together with the previous lemma,
`map_const_principal_coprod_map_id_principal`, this provides an example showing that the inequality
in the lemma `map_prodMap_coprod_le` can be strict.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.map_prodMap_const_id_principal_coprod_principal {α β ι : Type*} (a : α) (b : β) (i : ι) : map (Prod.map (fun _ : α => b) id) ((𝓟 {a}).coprod (𝓟 {i})) = 𝓟 (({b} : Set β) ×ˢ (univ : Set ι))

views.nl_informal: `g` converges to `f.smallSets` if for all `s ∈ f`, eventually we have `g x ⊆ s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.tendsto_smallSets_iff {f : α → Set β} : Tendsto f la lb.smallSets ↔ ∀ t ∈ lb, ∀ᶠ x in la, f x ⊆ t

views.nl_informal:
Generalized **squeeze theorem** (also known as **sandwich theorem**). If `s : α → Set β` is a
family of sets that tends to `Filter.smallSets lb` along `la` and `f : α → β` is a function such
that `f x ∈ s x` eventually along `la`, then `f` tends to `lb` along `la`.

If `s x` is the closed interval `[g x, h x]` for some functions `g`, `h` that tend to the same limit
`𝓝 y`, then we obtain the standard squeeze theorem, see
`tendsto_of_tendsto_of_tendsto_of_le_of_le'`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.Tendsto.of_smallSets {s : α → Set β} {f : α → β} (hs : Tendsto s la lb.smallSets) (hf : ∀ᶠ x in la, f x ∈ s x) : Tendsto f la lb

views.nl_informal: A nontrivial subsingleton filter is equal to `pure a` for some `a`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.Subsingleton.exists_eq_pure [l.NeBot] (hl : l.Subsingleton) : ∃ a, l = pure a

views.nl_informal: A filter is a subsingleton iff it is equal to `⊥` or to `pure a` for some `a`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.subsingleton_iff_bot_or_pure : l.Subsingleton ↔ l = ⊥ ∨ ∃ a, l = pure a

views.nl_informal:
In a nonempty type, a filter is a subsingleton iff
it is less than or equal to a pure filter.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.subsingleton_iff_exists_le_pure [Nonempty α] : l.Subsingleton ↔ ∃ a, l ≤ pure a

views.nl_informal:
If two filters are disjoint, then a function cannot tend to both of them along a non-trivial
filter.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.Tendsto.not_tendsto {f : α → β} {a : Filter α} {b₁ b₂ : Filter β} (hf : Tendsto f a b₁) [NeBot a] (hb : Disjoint b₁ b₂) : ¬Tendsto f a b₂

views.nl_informal:
If a function tends to infinity along a filter, then this function multiplied by a positive
constant (on the left) also tends to infinity. The archimedean assumption is convenient to get a
statement that works on `ℕ`, `ℤ` and `ℝ`, although not necessary (a version in ordered fields is
given in `Filter.Tendsto.const_mul_atTop`).
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.Tendsto.const_mul_atTop' (hr : 0 < r) (hf : Tendsto f l atTop) : Tendsto (fun x => r * f x) l atTop

views.nl_informal:
If a function tends to infinity along a filter, then this function multiplied by a positive
constant (on the right) also tends to infinity. The archimedean assumption is convenient to get a
statement that works on `ℕ`, `ℤ` and `ℝ`, although not necessary (a version in ordered fields is
given in `Filter.Tendsto.atTop_mul_const`).
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.Tendsto.atTop_mul_const' (hr : 0 < r) (hf : Tendsto f l atTop) : Tendsto (fun x => f x * r) l atTop

views.nl_informal:
A function `f` maps upwards closed sets (atTop sets) to upwards closed sets when it is a
Galois insertion. The Galois "insertion" and "connection" is weakened to only require it to be an
insertion and a connection above `b`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.map_atTop_eq_of_gc_preorder [Preorder α] [IsDirected α (· ≤ ·)] [Preorder β] [IsDirected β (· ≤ ·)] {f : α → β} (hf : Monotone f) (b : β) (hgi : ∀ c ≥ b, ∃ x, f x = c ∧ ∀ a, f a ≤ c ↔ a ≤ x) : map f atTop = atTop

views.nl_informal:
A function `f` maps upwards closed sets (atTop sets) to upwards closed sets when it is a
Galois insertion. The Galois "insertion" and "connection" is weakened to only require it to be an
insertion and a connection above `b`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.map_atTop_eq_of_gc [Preorder α] [IsDirected α (· ≤ ·)] [PartialOrder β] [IsDirected β (· ≤ ·)] {f : α → β} (g : β → α) (b : β) (hf : Monotone f) (gc : ∀ a, ∀ c ≥ b, f a ≤ c ↔ a ≤ g c) (hgi : ∀ c ≥ b, c ≤ f (g c)) : map f atTop = atTop

views.nl_informal: The image of the filter `atTop` on `Ici a` under the coercion equals `atTop`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.map_val_Ici_atTop [Preorder α] [IsDirected α (· ≤ ·)] (a : α) : map ((↑) : Ici a → α) atTop = atTop

views.nl_informal: The image of the filter `atTop` on `Ioi a` under the coercion equals `atTop`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.map_val_Ioi_atTop [Preorder α] [IsDirected α (· ≤ ·)] [NoMaxOrder α] (a : α) : map ((↑) : Ioi a → α) atTop = atTop

views.nl_informal:
The `atTop` filter for an open interval `Ioi a` comes from the `atTop` filter in the ambient
order.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.atTop_Ioi_eq [Preorder α] [IsDirected α (· ≤ ·)] (a : α) : atTop = comap ((↑) : Ioi a → α) atTop

views.nl_informal:
The `atTop` filter for an open interval `Ici a` comes from the `atTop` filter in the ambient
order.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.atTop_Ici_eq [Preorder α] [IsDirected α (· ≤ ·)] (a : α) : atTop = comap ((↑) : Ici a → α) atTop

views.nl_informal:
The `atBot` filter for an open interval `Iio a` comes from the `atBot` filter in the ambient
order.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.map_val_Iio_atBot [Preorder α] [IsDirected α (· ≥ ·)] [NoMinOrder α] (a : α) : map ((↑) : Iio a → α) atBot = atBot

views.nl_informal:
The `atBot` filter for an open interval `Iio a` comes from the `atBot` filter in the ambient
order.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.atBot_Iio_eq [Preorder α] [IsDirected α (· ≥ ·)] (a : α) : atBot = comap ((↑) : Iio a → α) atBot

views.nl_informal:
The `atBot` filter for an open interval `Iic a` comes from the `atBot` filter in the ambient
order.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.map_val_Iic_atBot [Preorder α] [IsDirected α (· ≥ ·)] (a : α) : map ((↑) : Iic a → α) atBot = atBot

views.nl_informal:
The `atBot` filter for an open interval `Iic a` comes from the `atBot` filter in the ambient
order.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.atBot_Iic_eq [Preorder α] [IsDirected α (· ≥ ·)] (a : α) : atBot = comap ((↑) : Iic a → α) atBot

views.nl_informal:
Let `f` and `g` be two maps to the same commutative monoid. This lemma gives a sufficient
condition for comparison of the filter `atTop.map (fun s ↦ ∏ b ∈ s, f b)` with
`atTop.map (fun s ↦ ∏ b ∈ s, g b)`. This is useful to compare the set of limit points of
`Π b in s, f b` as `s → atTop` with the similar set for `g`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.map_atTop_finset_prod_le_of_prod_eq {f : α → M} {g : β → M} (h_eq : ∀ u : Finset β, ∃ v : Finset α, ∀ v', v ⊆ v' → ∃ u', u ⊆ u' ∧ ∏ x ∈ u', g x = ∏ b ∈ v', f b) : (atTop.map fun s : Finset α => ∏ b ∈ s, f b) ≤ atTop.map fun s : Finset β => ∏ x ∈ s, g x

views.nl_informal:

to a commutative monoid. Suppose that `f x = 1` outside of the range of `g`. Then the filters
`atTop.map (fun s ↦ ∏ i ∈ s, f (g i))` and `atTop.map (fun s ↦ ∏ i ∈ s, f i)` coincide.

the same assumptions.

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:

if a filter `k` is countably generated then `Tendsto f k l` iff for every sequence `u`
converging to `k`, `f ∘ u` tends to `l`.

views.nl_informal:
If `x`, `y`, `x'`, and `y'` are functions `Π i : ι, α i`, then
the set difference between the box `[x, y]` and the product of the open intervals `(x' i, y' i)`
is covered by the union of the following boxes: for each `i : ι`, we take
`[x, update y i (x' i)]` and `[update x i (y' i), y]`.

E.g., if `x' = x` and `y' = y`, then this lemma states that the difference between a closed box
`[x, y]` and the corresponding open box `{z | ∀ i, x i < z i < y i}` is covered by the union
of the faces of `[x, y]`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Set.Icc_diff_pi_univ_Ioo_subset (x y x' y' : ∀ i, α i) : (Icc x y \ pi univ fun i ↦ Ioo (x' i) (y' i)) ⊆ (⋃ i : ι, Icc x (update y i (x' i))) ∪ ⋃ i : ι, Icc (update x i (y' i)) y

views.nl_informal:
If `x`, `y`, `z` are functions `Π i : ι, α i`, then
the set difference between the box `[x, z]` and the product of the intervals `(y i, z i]`
is covered by the union of the boxes `[x, update z i (y i)]`.

E.g., if `x = y`, then this lemma states that the difference between a closed box
`[x, y]` and the product of half-open intervals `{z | ∀ i, x i < z i ≤ y i}` is covered by the union
of the faces of `[x, y]` adjacent to `x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Set.Icc_diff_pi_univ_Ioc_subset (x y z : ∀ i, α i) : (Icc x z \ pi univ fun i ↦ Ioc (y i) (z i)) ⊆ ⋃ i : ι, Icc x (update z i (y i))

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:

This is a form of **Bayes' theorem**.
The condition is true for example for countable `Ω`.

function of `a`.

If a kernel `κ` is finite, then `withDensity κ f` is s-finite.

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:

as first applying the kernel then copying.

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:

measures.

views.lean_signature: theorem ProbabilityTheory.condCDF_nonneg (ρ : Measure (α × ℝ)) (a : α) (r : ℝ) : 0 ≤ condCDF ρ a r

views.lean_signature: theorem ProbabilityTheory.condCDF_le_one (ρ : Measure (α × ℝ)) (a : α) (x : ℝ) : condCDF ρ a x ≤ 1

views.lean_signature: theorem ProbabilityTheory.tendsto_condCDF_atTop (ρ : Measure (α × ℝ)) (a : α) : Tendsto (condCDF ρ a) atTop (𝓝 1)

views.nl_informal: The conditional cdf is a measurable function of `a : α` for all `x : ℝ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ProbabilityTheory.measurable_condCDF (ρ : Measure (α × ℝ)) (x : ℝ) : Measurable fun a ↦ condCDF ρ a x

views.nl_informal: The conditional cdf is a strongly measurable function of `a : α` for all `x : ℝ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ProbabilityTheory.stronglyMeasurable_condCDF (ρ : Measure (α × ℝ)) (x : ℝ) : StronglyMeasurable fun a ↦ condCDF ρ a x

views.nl_informal: The function `a ↦ (condCDF ρ a).measure` is measurable.
views.lean_signature: theorem ProbabilityTheory.measurable_measure_condCDF (ρ : Measure (α × ℝ)) : Measurable fun a => (condCDF ρ a).measure

views.nl_informal:
A measurable function `α → StieltjesFunction` with limits 0 at -∞ and 1 at +∞ gives a measurable
function `α → Measure ℝ` by taking `StieltjesFunction.measure` at each point.

For `κ' := map κ (Prod.map (id : β → β) e)`, the hypothesis `hη` is `fst κ' ⊗ₖ η = κ'`.
The conclusion of the lemma is `fst κ ⊗ₖ borelMarkovFromReal Ω η = comapRight (fst κ' ⊗ₖ η) _`.

views.nl_informal:
For `κ' := map κ (Prod.map (id : β → β) e)`, the hypothesis `hη` is `fst κ' ⊗ₖ η = κ'`.
With that hypothesis, `fst κ ⊗ₖ borelMarkovFromReal κ η = κ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.compProd_fst_borelMarkovFromReal (κ : Kernel α (β × Ω)) [IsSFiniteKernel κ] (η : Kernel (α × β) ℝ) [IsSFiniteKernel η] (hη : (fst (map κ (Prod.map (id : β → β) (embeddingReal Ω)))) ⊗ₖ η = map κ (Prod.map (id : β → β) (embeddingReal Ω))) : fst κ ⊗ₖ borelMarkovFromReal Ω η = κ

views.nl_informal:
If the singleton `{x}` has non-zero mass for `ρ.fst`, then for all `s : Set Ω`,
`ρ.condKernel x s = (ρ.fst {x})⁻¹ * ρ ({x} ×ˢ s)` .
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.Measure.condKernel_apply_of_ne_zero [MeasurableSingletonClass α] {x : α} (hx : ρ.fst {x} ≠ 0) (s : Set Ω) : ρ.condKernel x s = (ρ.fst {x})⁻¹ * ρ ({x} ×ˢ s)

views.nl_informal:
A s-finite kernel which satisfy the disintegration property of the given measure `ρ` is almost
everywhere equal to the disintegration kernel of `ρ` when evaluated on a measurable set.

This theorem in the case of finite kernels is weaker than `eq_condKernel_of_measure_eq_compProd`
which asserts that the kernels are equal almost everywhere and not just on a given measurable
set.
views.lean_signature: theorem ProbabilityTheory.eq_condKernel_of_measure_eq_compProd' (κ : Kernel α Ω) [IsSFiniteKernel κ] (hκ : ρ = ρ.fst ⊗ₘ κ) {s : Set Ω} (hs : MeasurableSet s) : ∀ᵐ x ∂ρ.fst, κ x s = ρ.condKernel x s

views.nl_informal:
Auxiliary lemma for `eq_condKernel_of_measure_eq_compProd`.
Uniqueness of the disintegration kernel on ℝ.
views.lean_signature: theorem ProbabilityTheory.eq_condKernel_of_measure_eq_compProd_real {ρ : Measure (α × ℝ)} [IsFiniteMeasure ρ] (κ : Kernel α ℝ) [IsFiniteKernel κ] (hκ : ρ = ρ.fst ⊗ₘ κ) : ∀ᵐ x ∂ρ.fst, κ x = ρ.condKernel x

views.nl_informal:
A finite kernel which satisfies the disintegration property is almost everywhere equal to the
disintegration kernel.
views.lean_signature: theorem ProbabilityTheory.eq_condKernel_of_measure_eq_compProd (κ : Kernel α Ω) [IsFiniteKernel κ] (hκ : ρ = ρ.fst ⊗ₘ κ) : ∀ᵐ x ∂ρ.fst, κ x = ρ.condKernel x

views.nl_informal:
For `fst κ a`-almost all `b`, the conditional kernel `Kernel.condKernel κ` applied to `(a, b)`
is equal to the conditional kernel of the measure `κ a` applied to `b`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.condKernel_apply_eq_condKernel [CountableOrCountablyGenerated α β] (κ : Kernel α (β × Ω)) [IsFiniteKernel κ] (a : α) : (fun b ↦ Kernel.condKernel κ (a, b)) =ᵐ[Kernel.fst κ a] (κ a).condKernel

views.nl_informal:
A finite kernel which satisfies the disintegration property is almost everywhere equal to the
disintegration kernel.
views.lean_signature: theorem ProbabilityTheory.eq_condKernel_of_kernel_eq_compProd [CountableOrCountablyGenerated α β] {ρ : Kernel α (β × Ω)} [IsFiniteKernel ρ] {κ : Kernel (α × β) Ω} [IsFiniteKernel κ] (hκ : Kernel.fst ρ ⊗ₖ κ = ρ) (a : α) : ∀ᵐ x ∂(Kernel.fst ρ a), κ (a, x) = Kernel.condKernel ρ (a, x)

views.nl_informal:
If `b ≤ a`, given the trajectory up to time `a`, the trajectory up to time `b` is
deterministic and is equal to the restriction of the trajectory up to time `a`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.partialTraj_le (hba : b ≤ a) : partialTraj κ a b = deterministic (frestrictLe₂ hba) (measurable_frestrictLe₂ _)

views.nl_informal:
Given the trajectory up to time `a`, `partialTraj κ a b` gives the distribution of
the trajectory up to time `b`. Then plugging this into `partialTraj κ b c` gives
the distribution of the trajectory up to time `c`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.partialTraj_comp_partialTraj (hab : a ≤ b) (hbc : b ≤ c) : partialTraj κ b c ∘ₖ partialTraj κ a b = partialTraj κ a c

views.nl_informal:
This is a technical lemma saying that `partialTraj κ a b` consists of two independent parts, the
first one being the identity. It allows to compute integrals.
views.lean_signature: theorem ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.partialTraj_eq_prod [∀ n, IsSFiniteKernel (κ n)] (a b : ℕ) : partialTraj κ a b = (Kernel.id ×ₖ (partialTraj κ a b).map (restrict₂ Ioc_subset_Iic_self)).map (IicProdIoc a b)

views.nl_informal:
If we restrict the distribution of the trajectory up to time `c` to times `≤ b` we get
the trajectory up to time `b`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.partialTraj_map_frestrictLe₂ (a : ℕ) (hbc : b ≤ c) : (partialTraj κ a c).map (frestrictLe₂ hbc) = partialTraj κ a b

views.nl_informal: If `b ≤ a`, then integrating `f` against `partialTraj κ a b` does nothing.
views.lean_signature: theorem ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.lmarginalPartialTraj_le (hba : b ≤ a) {f : (Π n, X n) → ℝ≥0∞} (mf : Measurable f) : lmarginalPartialTraj κ a b f = f

views.nl_informal:
Integrating `f` against `partialTraj κ a b x` is the same as integrating only over the variables
from `x_{a+1}` to `x_b`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.lmarginalPartialTraj_eq_lintegral_map [∀ n, IsSFiniteKernel (κ n)] {f : (Π n, X n) → ℝ≥0∞} (mf : Measurable f) (x₀ : Π n, X n) : lmarginalPartialTraj κ a b f x₀ = ∫⁻ x : (Π i : Ioc a b, X i), f (updateFinset x₀ _ x) ∂(partialTraj κ a b).map (restrict₂ Ioc_subset_Iic_self) (frestrictLe a x₀)

views.nl_informal: Integrating `f` against `partialTraj κ a (a + 1)` is the same as integrating against `κ a`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.lmarginalPartialTraj_succ [∀ n, IsSFiniteKernel (κ n)] (a : ℕ) {f : (Π n, X n) → ℝ≥0∞} (mf : Measurable f) (x₀ : Π n, X n) : lmarginalPartialTraj κ a (a + 1) f x₀ = ∫⁻ x : X (a + 1), f (update x₀ _ x) ∂κ a (frestrictLe a x₀)

views.nl_informal:
Integrating `f` against `partialTraj κ a b` and then against `partialTraj κ b c` is the same
as integrating `f` against `partialTraj κ a c`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.lmarginalPartialTraj_self (hab : a ≤ b) (hbc : b ≤ c) {f : (Π n, X n) → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : Measurable f) : lmarginalPartialTraj κ a b (lmarginalPartialTraj κ b c f) = lmarginalPartialTraj κ a c f

views.nl_informal:
If `f` only depends on the variables up to rank `a` and `a ≤ b`, integrating `f` against
`partialTraj κ b c` does nothing.
views.lean_signature: theorem DependsOn.lmarginalPartialTraj_of_le [∀ n, IsMarkovKernel (κ n)] (c : ℕ) {f : (Π n, X n) → ℝ≥0∞} (mf : Measurable f) (hf : DependsOn f (Iic a)) (hab : a ≤ b) : lmarginalPartialTraj κ b c f = f

views.nl_informal:
If `f` only depends on the variables uo to rank `a`, integrating beyond rank `a` is the same
as integrating up to rank `a`.
views.lean_signature: theorem DependsOn.lmarginalPartialTraj_const_right [∀ n, IsMarkovKernel (κ n)] {d : ℕ} {f : (Π n, X n) → ℝ≥0∞} (mf : Measurable f) (hf : DependsOn f (Iic a)) (hac : a ≤ c) (had : a ≤ d) : lmarginalPartialTraj κ b c f = lmarginalPartialTraj κ b d f

views.nl_informal:
If `f` only depends on variables up to rank `b`, its integral from `a` to `b` only depends on
variables up to rank `a`.
views.lean_signature: theorem DependsOn.dependsOn_lmarginalPartialTraj [∀ n, IsSFiniteKernel (κ n)] (a : ℕ) {f : (Π n, X n) → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : DependsOn f (Iic b)) (mf : Measurable f) : DependsOn (lmarginalPartialTraj κ a b f) (Iic a)

views.nl_informal:
To check that a measure `ν` is the projective limit of a projective family of measures indexed
by `Finset ℕ`, it is enough to check on intervals of the form `Iic n`, where `n` is larger than
a given integer.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.isProjectiveLimit_nat_iff' {μ : (I : Finset ℕ) → Measure (Π i : I, X i)} (hμ : IsProjectiveMeasureFamily μ) (ν : Measure (Π n, X n)) (a : ℕ) : IsProjectiveLimit ν μ ↔ ∀ ⦃n⦄, a ≤ n → ν.map (frestrictLe n) = μ (Iic n)

views.nl_informal:
To check that a measure `ν` is the projective limit of a projective family of measures indexed
by `Finset ℕ`, it is enough to check on intervals of the form `Iic n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.isProjectiveLimit_nat_iff {μ : (I : Finset ℕ) → Measure (Π i : I, X i)} (hμ : IsProjectiveMeasureFamily μ) (ν : Measure (Π n, X n)) : IsProjectiveLimit ν μ ↔ ∀ n, ν.map (frestrictLe n) = μ (Iic n)

views.nl_informal:
Given a family of measures `μ : (n : ℕ) → Measure (Π i : Iic n, X i)`, the induced family
equals `μ` over the intervals `Iic n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.inducedFamily_Iic (n : ℕ) : inducedFamily μ (Iic n) = μ n

views.nl_informal:
Given a family of measures `μ : (n : ℕ) → Measure (Π i : Iic n, X i)`, the induced family
will be projective only if `μ` is projective, in the sense that if `a ≤ b`, then projecting
`μ b` gives `μ a`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.isProjectiveMeasureFamily_inducedFamily (h : ∀ a b : ℕ, ∀ hab : a ≤ b, (μ b).map (frestrictLe₂ hab) = μ a) : IsProjectiveMeasureFamily (inducedFamily μ)

views.nl_informal: The `trajContent κ x₀` of a cylinder indexed by first coordinates is given by `partialTraj`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.trajContent_cylinder {a b : ℕ} {S : Set (Π i : Iic b, X i)} (mS : MeasurableSet S) (x₀ : Π i : Iic a, X i) : trajContent κ x₀ (cylinder (Iic b) S) = partialTraj κ a b x₀ S

views.nl_informal:
The `trajContent` of a cylinder is equal to the integral of its indicator function against
`partialTraj`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.trajContent_eq_lmarginalPartialTraj {b : ℕ} {S : Set (Π i : Iic b, X i)} (mS : MeasurableSet S) (x₀ : Π n, X n) (a : ℕ) : trajContent κ (frestrictLe a x₀) (cylinder (Iic b) S) = lmarginalPartialTraj κ a b ((cylinder (Iic b) S).indicator 1) x₀

views.nl_informal:
This is an auxiliary result for `trajContent_tendsto_zero`. Consider `f` a sequence of bounded
measurable functions such that `f n` depends only on the first coordinates up to `a n`.
Assume that when integrating `f n` against `partialTraj (k + 1) (a n)`, one gets a non-increasing
sequence of functions which converges to `l`.
Assume then that there exists `ε` and `y : Π i : Iic k, X i` such that
when integrating `f n` against `partialTraj k (a n) y`, you get something at least
`ε` for all `n`. Then there exists `z` such that this remains true when integrating
`f` against `partialTraj (k + 1) (a n) (update y (k + 1) z)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.le_lmarginalPartialTraj_succ {f : ℕ → (Π n, X n) → ℝ≥0∞} {a : ℕ → ℕ} (hcte : ∀ n, DependsOn (f n) (Iic (a n))) (mf : ∀ n, Measurable (f n)) {bound : ℝ≥0∞} (fin_bound : bound ≠ ∞) (le_bound : ∀ n x, f n x ≤ bound) {k : ℕ} (anti : ∀ x, Antitone (fun n ↦ lmarginalPartialTraj κ (k + 1) (a n) (f n) x)) {l : (Π n, X n) → ℝ≥0∞} (htendsto : ∀ x, Tendsto (fun n ↦ lmarginalPartialTraj κ (k + 1) (a n) (f n) x) atTop (𝓝 (l x))) (ε : ℝ≥0∞) (y : Π i : Iic k, X i) (hpos : ∀ x n, ε ≤ lmarginalPartialTraj κ k (a n) (f n) (updateFinset x (Iic k) y)) : ∃ z, ∀ x n, ε ≤ lmarginalPartialTraj κ (k + 1) (a n) (f n) (update (updateFinset x (Iic k) y) (k + 1) z)

views.nl_informal:
This is the key theorem to prove the existence of the `traj`:
the `trajContent` of a decreasing sequence of cylinders with empty intersection
converges to `0`.

This implies the `σ`-additivity of `trajContent`
(see `addContent_iUnion_eq_sum_of_tendsto_zero`),
which allows to extend it to the `σ`-algebra by Carathéodory's theorem.
views.lean_signature: theorem ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.trajContent_tendsto_zero {A : ℕ → Set (Π n, X n)} (A_mem : ∀ n, A n ∈ measurableCylinders X) (A_anti : Antitone A) (A_inter : ⋂ n, A n = ∅) {p : ℕ} (x₀ : Π i : Iic p, X i) : Tendsto (fun n ↦ trajContent κ x₀ (A n)) atTop (𝓝 0)

views.nl_informal: The `trajContent` is sigma-subadditive.
views.lean_signature: theorem ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.isSigmaSubadditive_trajContent {a : ℕ} (x₀ : Π i : Iic a, X i) : (trajContent κ x₀).IsSigmaSubadditive

views.nl_informal:
To check that `η = traj κ a` it is enough to show that the restriction of `η` to variables `≤ b`
is `partialTraj κ a b` for any `b ≥ n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.eq_traj' {a : ℕ} (n : ℕ) (η : Kernel (Π i : Iic a, X i) (Π n, X n)) (hη : ∀ b ≥ n, η.map (frestrictLe b) = partialTraj κ a b) : η = traj κ a

views.nl_informal:
To check that `η = traj κ a` it is enough to show that the restriction of `η` to variables `≤ b`
is `partialTraj κ a b`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.eq_traj {a : ℕ} (η : Kernel (Π i : Iic a, X i) (Π n, X n)) (hη : ∀ b, η.map (frestrictLe b) = partialTraj κ a b) : η = traj κ a

views.nl_informal:
Given the distribution up to tome `a`, `partialTraj κ a b` gives the distribution
of the trajectory up to time `b`, and composing this with `traj κ b` gives the distribution
of the whole trajectory.
views.lean_signature: theorem ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.traj_comp_partialTraj {a b : ℕ} (hab : a ≤ b) : (traj κ b) ∘ₖ (partialTraj κ a b) = traj κ a

views.nl_informal:
This theorem shows that `traj κ n` is, up to an equivalence, the product of
a deterministic kernel with another kernel. This is an intermediate result to compute integrals
with respect to this kernel.
views.lean_signature: theorem ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.traj_eq_prod (a : ℕ) : traj κ a = (Kernel.id ×ₖ (traj κ a).map (Set.Ioi a).restrict).map (IicProdIoi a)

views.nl_informal:
When computing `∫ x, f x ∂traj κ n x₀`, because the trajectory up to time `n` is
determined by `x₀` we can replace `x` by `updateFinset x (Iic a) x₀`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.integral_traj {a : ℕ} (x₀ : Π i : Iic a, X i) {f : (Π n, X n) → E} (mf : AEStronglyMeasurable f (traj κ a x₀)) : ∫ x, f x ∂traj κ a x₀ = ∫ x, f (updateFinset x (Iic a) x₀) ∂traj κ a x₀

views.nl_informal: A predictable submartingale is a.e. greater equal than its initial state.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.Submartingale.zero_le_of_predictable [Preorder E] [SigmaFiniteFiltration μ 𝒢] {f : ℕ → Ω → E} (hfmgle : Submartingale f 𝒢 μ) (hfadp : Adapted 𝒢 fun n => f (n + 1)) (n : ℕ) : f 0 ≤ᵐ[μ] f n

views.nl_informal: A predictable supermartingale is a.e. less equal than its initial state.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.Supermartingale.le_zero_of_predictable [Preorder E] [SigmaFiniteFiltration μ 𝒢] {f : ℕ → Ω → E} (hfmgle : Supermartingale f 𝒢 μ) (hfadp : Adapted 𝒢 fun n => f (n + 1)) (n : ℕ) : f n ≤ᵐ[μ] f 0

views.nl_informal: A predictable martingale is a.e. equal to its initial state.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.Martingale.eq_zero_of_predictable [SigmaFiniteFiltration μ 𝒢] {f : ℕ → Ω → E} (hfmgle : Martingale f 𝒢 μ) (hfadp : Adapted 𝒢 fun n => f (n + 1)) (n : ℕ) : f n =ᵐ[μ] f 0

views.nl_informal:
Given a discrete submartingale `f` and a predictable process `ξ` (i.e. `ξ (n + 1)` is adapted)
the process defined by `fun n => ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, ξ (k + 1) * (f (k + 1) - f k)` is also a
submartingale.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.Submartingale.sum_mul_sub' [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {R : ℝ} {ξ f : ℕ → Ω → ℝ} (hf : Submartingale f 𝒢 μ) (hξ : Adapted 𝒢 fun n => ξ (n + 1)) (hbdd : ∀ n ω, ξ n ω ≤ R) (hnonneg : ∀ n ω, 0 ≤ ξ n ω) : Submartingale (fun n => ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, ξ (k + 1) * (f (k + 1) - f k)) 𝒢 μ

views.nl_informal:
One sided martingale bound: If `f` is a submartingale which has uniformly bounded differences,
then for almost every `ω`, `f n ω` is bounded above (in `n`) if and only if it converges.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.Submartingale.bddAbove_iff_exists_tendsto [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hf : Submartingale f ℱ μ) (hbdd : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, ∀ i, |f (i + 1) ω - f i ω| ≤ R) : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, BddAbove (Set.range fun n => f n ω) ↔ ∃ c, Tendsto (fun n => f n ω) atTop (𝓝 c)

views.nl_informal:
An a.e. monotone adapted process `f` with uniformly bounded differences converges to `+∞` if
and only if its predictable part also converges to `+∞`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.tendsto_sum_indicator_atTop_iff [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hfmono : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, ∀ n, f n ω ≤ f (n + 1) ω) (hf : Adapted ℱ f) (hint : ∀ n, Integrable (f n) μ) (hbdd : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, ∀ n, |f (n + 1) ω - f n ω| ≤ R) : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n => f n ω) atTop atTop ↔ Tendsto (fun n => predictablePart f ℱ μ n ω) atTop atTop

views.nl_informal:
**Lévy's generalization of the Borel-Cantelli lemma**: given a sequence of sets `s` and a
filtration `ℱ` such that for all `n`, `s n` is `ℱ n`-measurable, `limsup s atTop` is almost
everywhere equal to the set for which `∑ k, ℙ(s (k + 1) | ℱ k) = ∞`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.ae_mem_limsup_atTop_iff (μ : Measure Ω) [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {s : ℕ → Set Ω} (hs : ∀ n, MeasurableSet[ℱ n] (s n)) : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, ω ∈ limsup s atTop ↔ Tendsto (fun n => ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, (μ[(s (k + 1)).indicator (1 : Ω → ℝ)|ℱ k]) ω) atTop atTop

views.nl_informal:
If a stochastic process has bounded upcrossing from below `a` to above `b`,
then it does not frequently visit both below `a` and above `b`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.not_frequently_of_upcrossings_lt_top (hab : a < b) (hω : upcrossings a b f ω ≠ ∞) : ¬((∃ᶠ n in atTop, f n ω < a) ∧ ∃ᶠ n in atTop, b < f n ω)

views.nl_informal: A stochastic process that frequently visits below `a` and above `b` has infinite upcrossings.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.upcrossings_eq_top_of_frequently_lt (hab : a < b) (h₁ : ∃ᶠ n in atTop, f n ω < a) (h₂ : ∃ᶠ n in atTop, b < f n ω) : upcrossings a b f ω = ∞

views.nl_informal:
A realization of a stochastic process with bounded upcrossings and bounded liminfs is
convergent.

We use the spelling `< ∞` instead of the standard `≠ ∞` in the assumptions since it is not as easy
to change `<` to `≠` under binders.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.tendsto_of_uncrossing_lt_top (hf₁ : liminf (fun n => (‖f n ω‖₊ : ℝ≥0∞)) atTop < ∞) (hf₂ : ∀ a b : ℚ, a < b → upcrossings a b f ω < ∞) : ∃ c, Tendsto (fun n => f n ω) atTop (𝓝 c)

views.nl_informal: An L¹-bounded submartingale has bounded upcrossings almost everywhere.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.Submartingale.upcrossings_ae_lt_top' [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hf : Submartingale f ℱ μ) (hbdd : ∀ n, eLpNorm (f n) 1 μ ≤ R) (hab : a < b) : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, upcrossings a b f ω < ∞

views.nl_informal: An L¹-bounded submartingale converges almost everywhere.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.Submartingale.exists_ae_tendsto_of_bdd [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hf : Submartingale f ℱ μ) (hbdd : ∀ n, eLpNorm (f n) 1 μ ≤ R) : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, ∃ c, Tendsto (fun n => f n ω) atTop (𝓝 c)

views.nl_informal:
**Almost everywhere martingale convergence theorem**: An L¹-bounded submartingale converges
almost everywhere to a `⨆ n, ℱ n`-measurable function.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.Submartingale.ae_tendsto_limitProcess [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hf : Submartingale f ℱ μ) (hbdd : ∀ n, eLpNorm (f n) 1 μ ≤ R) : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n => f n ω) atTop (𝓝 (ℱ.limitProcess f μ ω))

views.nl_informal: The limiting process of an Lᵖ-bounded submartingale is Lᵖ.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.Submartingale.memLp_limitProcess {p : ℝ≥0∞} (hf : Submartingale f ℱ μ) (hbdd : ∀ n, eLpNorm (f n) p μ ≤ R) : MemLp (ℱ.limitProcess f μ) p μ

views.nl_informal:
Part a of the **L¹ martingale convergence theorem**: a uniformly integrable submartingale
adapted to the filtration `ℱ` converges a.e. and in L¹ to an integrable function which is
measurable with respect to the σ-algebra `⨆ n, ℱ n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.Submartingale.tendsto_eLpNorm_one_limitProcess (hf : Submartingale f ℱ μ) (hunif : UniformIntegrable f 1 μ) : Tendsto (fun n => eLpNorm (f n - ℱ.limitProcess f μ) 1 μ) atTop (𝓝 0)

views.nl_informal:
If a martingale `f` adapted to `ℱ` converges in L¹ to `g`, then for all `n`, `f n` is almost
everywhere equal to `𝔼[g | ℱ n]`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.Martingale.eq_condExp_of_tendsto_eLpNorm {μ : Measure Ω} (hf : Martingale f ℱ μ) (hg : Integrable g μ) (hgtends : Tendsto (fun n => eLpNorm (f n - g) 1 μ) atTop (𝓝 0)) (n : ℕ) : f n =ᵐ[μ] μ[g|ℱ n]

views.nl_informal:
Part b of the **L¹ martingale convergence theorem**: if `f` is a uniformly integrable martingale
adapted to the filtration `ℱ`, then for all `n`, `f n` is almost everywhere equal to the conditional
expectation of its limiting process wrt. `ℱ n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.Martingale.ae_eq_condExp_limitProcess (hf : Martingale f ℱ μ) (hbdd : UniformIntegrable f 1 μ) (n : ℕ) : f n =ᵐ[μ] μ[ℱ.limitProcess f μ|ℱ n]

views.nl_informal:
Part c of the **L¹ martingale convergence theorem**: Given an integrable function `g` which
is measurable with respect to `⨆ n, ℱ n` where `ℱ` is a filtration, the martingale defined by
`𝔼[g | ℱ n]` converges almost everywhere to `g`.

This martingale also converges to `g` in L¹ and this result is provided by
`MeasureTheory.Integrable.tendsto_eLpNorm_condExp`
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.Integrable.tendsto_ae_condExp (hg : Integrable g μ) (hgmeas : StronglyMeasurable[⨆ n, ℱ n] g) : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n => (μ[g|ℱ n]) x) atTop (𝓝 (g x))

views.nl_informal:
Part c of the **L¹ martingale convergence theorem**: Given an integrable function `g` which
is measurable with respect to `⨆ n, ℱ n` where `ℱ` is a filtration, the martingale defined by
`𝔼[g | ℱ n]` converges in L¹ to `g`.

This martingale also converges to `g` almost everywhere and this result is provided by
`MeasureTheory.Integrable.tendsto_ae_condExp`
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.Integrable.tendsto_eLpNorm_condExp (hg : Integrable g μ) (hgmeas : StronglyMeasurable[⨆ n, ℱ n] g) : Tendsto (fun n => eLpNorm (μ[g|ℱ n] - g) 1 μ) atTop (𝓝 0)

views.nl_informal:
**Lévy's upward theorem**, almost everywhere version: given a function `g` and a filtration
`ℱ`, the sequence defined by `𝔼[g | ℱ n]` converges almost everywhere to `𝔼[g | ⨆ n, ℱ n]`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.tendsto_ae_condExp (g : Ω → ℝ) : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n => (μ[g|ℱ n]) x) atTop (𝓝 ((μ[g|⨆ n, ℱ n]) x))

views.nl_informal:
**Lévy's upward theorem**, L¹ version: given a function `g` and a filtration `ℱ`, the
sequence defined by `𝔼[g | ℱ n]` converges in L¹ to `𝔼[g | ⨆ n, ℱ n]`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.tendsto_eLpNorm_condExp (g : Ω → ℝ) : Tendsto (fun n => eLpNorm (μ[g|ℱ n] - μ[g|⨆ n, ℱ n]) 1 μ) atTop (𝓝 0)

views.nl_informal:
The value of a martingale `f` at a stopping time `τ` bounded by `n` is the conditional
expectation of `f n` with respect to the σ-algebra generated by `τ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.Martingale.stoppedValue_ae_eq_condExp_of_le_const_of_countable_range (h : Martingale f ℱ μ) (hτ : IsStoppingTime ℱ τ) (hτ_le : ∀ x, τ x ≤ n) (h_countable_range : (Set.range τ).Countable) [SigmaFinite (μ.trim (hτ.measurableSpace_le_of_le hτ_le))] : stoppedValue f τ =ᵐ[μ] μ[f n|hτ.measurableSpace]

views.nl_informal:
The value of a martingale `f` at a stopping time `τ` bounded by `n` is the conditional
expectation of `f n` with respect to the σ-algebra generated by `τ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.Martingale.stoppedValue_ae_eq_condExp_of_le_const [Countable ι] (h : Martingale f ℱ μ) (hτ : IsStoppingTime ℱ τ) (hτ_le : ∀ x, τ x ≤ n) [SigmaFinite (μ.trim (hτ.measurableSpace_le_of_le hτ_le))] : stoppedValue f τ =ᵐ[μ] μ[f n|hτ.measurableSpace]

views.nl_informal:
If `τ` and `σ` are two stopping times with `σ ≤ τ` and `τ` is bounded, then the value of a
martingale `f` at `σ` is the conditional expectation of its value at `τ` with respect to the
σ-algebra generated by `σ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.Martingale.stoppedValue_ae_eq_condExp_of_le_of_countable_range (h : Martingale f ℱ μ) (hτ : IsStoppingTime ℱ τ) (hσ : IsStoppingTime ℱ σ) (hσ_le_τ : σ ≤ τ) (hτ_le : ∀ x, τ x ≤ n) (hτ_countable_range : (Set.range τ).Countable) (hσ_countable_range : (Set.range σ).Countable) [SigmaFinite (μ.trim (hσ.measurableSpace_le_of_le fun x => (hσ_le_τ x).trans (hτ_le x)))] : stoppedValue f σ =ᵐ[μ] μ[stoppedValue f τ|hσ.measurableSpace]

views.nl_informal:
If `τ` and `σ` are two stopping times with `σ ≤ τ` and `τ` is bounded, then the value of a
martingale `f` at `σ` is the conditional expectation of its value at `τ` with respect to the
σ-algebra generated by `σ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.Martingale.stoppedValue_ae_eq_condExp_of_le [Countable ι] (h : Martingale f ℱ μ) (hτ : IsStoppingTime ℱ τ) (hσ : IsStoppingTime ℱ σ) (hσ_le_τ : σ ≤ τ) (hτ_le : ∀ x, τ x ≤ n) [SigmaFinite (μ.trim hσ.measurableSpace_le)] : stoppedValue f σ =ᵐ[μ] μ[stoppedValue f τ|hσ.measurableSpace]

views.nl_informal:
**Optional Sampling theorem**. If `τ` is a bounded stopping time and `σ` is another stopping
time, then the value of a martingale `f` at the stopping time `min τ σ` is almost everywhere equal
to the conditional expectation of `f` stopped at `τ` with respect to the σ-algebra generated
by `σ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.Martingale.stoppedValue_min_ae_eq_condExp [SigmaFiniteFiltration μ ℱ] (h : Martingale f ℱ μ) (hτ : IsStoppingTime ℱ τ) (hσ : IsStoppingTime ℱ σ) {n : ι} (hτ_le : ∀ x, τ x ≤ n) [h_sf_min : SigmaFinite (μ.trim (hτ.min hσ).measurableSpace_le)] : (stoppedValue f fun x => min (σ x) (τ x)) =ᵐ[μ] μ[stoppedValue f τ|hσ.measurableSpace]

views.nl_informal:
Given a submartingale `f` and bounded stopping times `τ` and `π` such that `τ ≤ π`, the
expectation of `stoppedValue f τ` is less than or equal to the expectation of `stoppedValue f π`.
This is the forward direction of the optional stopping theorem.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.Submartingale.expected_stoppedValue_mono [SigmaFiniteFiltration μ 𝒢] (hf : Submartingale f 𝒢 μ) (hτ : IsStoppingTime 𝒢 τ) (hπ : IsStoppingTime 𝒢 π) (hle : τ ≤ π) {N : ℕ} (hbdd : ∀ ω, π ω ≤ N) : μ[stoppedValue f τ] ≤ μ[stoppedValue f π]

views.nl_informal:
The converse direction of the optional stopping theorem, i.e. an adapted integrable process `f`
is a submartingale if for all bounded stopping times `τ` and `π` such that `τ ≤ π`, the
stopped value of `f` at `τ` has expectation smaller than its stopped value at `π`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.submartingale_of_expected_stoppedValue_mono [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hadp : Adapted 𝒢 f) (hint : ∀ i, Integrable (f i) μ) (hf : ∀ τ π : Ω → ℕ, IsStoppingTime 𝒢 τ → IsStoppingTime 𝒢 π → τ ≤ π → (∃ N, ∀ ω, π ω ≤ N) → μ[stoppedValue f τ] ≤ μ[stoppedValue f π]) : Submartingale f 𝒢 μ

views.nl_informal:
**The optional stopping theorem** (fair game theorem): an adapted integrable process `f`
is a submartingale if and only if for all bounded stopping times `τ` and `π` such that `τ ≤ π`, the
stopped value of `f` at `τ` has expectation smaller than its stopped value at `π`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.submartingale_iff_expected_stoppedValue_mono [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hadp : Adapted 𝒢 f) (hint : ∀ i, Integrable (f i) μ) : Submartingale f 𝒢 μ ↔ ∀ τ π : Ω → ℕ, IsStoppingTime 𝒢 τ → IsStoppingTime 𝒢 π → τ ≤ π → (∃ N, ∀ x, π x ≤ N) → μ[stoppedValue f τ] ≤ μ[stoppedValue f π]

views.nl_informal: The stopped process of a submartingale with respect to a stopping time is a submartingale.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.Submartingale.stoppedProcess [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (h : Submartingale f 𝒢 μ) (hτ : IsStoppingTime 𝒢 τ) : Submartingale (stoppedProcess f τ) 𝒢 μ

views.nl_informal:
**Doob's maximal inequality**: Given a non-negative submartingale `f`, for all `ε : ℝ≥0`,
we have `ε • μ {ε ≤ f* n} ≤ ∫ ω in {ε ≤ f* n}, f n` where `f* n ω = max_{k ≤ n}, f k ω`.

In some literature, the Doob's maximal inequality refers to what we call Doob's Lp inequality
(which is a corollary of this lemma and will be proved in an upcoming PR).
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.maximal_ineq [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hsub : Submartingale f 𝒢 μ) (hnonneg : 0 ≤ f) {ε : ℝ≥0} (n : ℕ) : ε • μ {ω | (ε : ℝ) ≤ (range (n + 1)).sup' nonempty_range_succ fun k => f k ω} ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (∫ ω in {ω | (ε : ℝ) ≤ (range (n + 1)).sup' nonempty_range_succ fun k => f k ω}, f n ω ∂μ)

views.nl_informal:
**Doob's upcrossing estimate**: given a real valued discrete submartingale `f` and real
values `a` and `b`, we have `(b - a) * 𝔼[upcrossingsBefore a b f N] ≤ 𝔼[(f N - a)⁺]` where
`upcrossingsBefore a b f N` is the number of times the process `f` crossed from below `a` to above
`b` before the time `N`.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.Submartingale.mul_integral_upcrossingsBefore_le_integral_pos_part [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (a b : ℝ) (hf : Submartingale f ℱ μ) (N : ℕ) : (b - a) * μ[upcrossingsBefore a b f N] ≤ μ[fun ω => (f N ω - a)⁺]

views.nl_informal: A variant of Doob's upcrossing estimate obtained by taking the supremum on both sides.
views.lean_signature: theorem MeasureTheory.Submartingale.mul_lintegral_upcrossings_le_lintegral_pos_part [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (a b : ℝ) (hf : Submartingale f ℱ μ) : ENNReal.ofReal (b - a) * ∫⁻ ω, upcrossings a b f ω ∂μ ≤ ⨆ N, ∫⁻ ω, ENNReal.ofReal ((f N ω - a)⁺) ∂μ

views.nl_informal: The moment generating function is monotone in the random variable for `t ≥ 0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ProbabilityTheory.mgf_mono_of_nonneg {Y : Ω → ℝ} (hXY : X ≤ᵐ[μ] Y) (ht : 0 ≤ t) (htY : Integrable (fun ω ↦ exp (t * Y ω)) μ) : mgf X μ t ≤ mgf Y μ t

views.nl_informal: The moment generating function is antitone in the random variable for `t ≤ 0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ProbabilityTheory.mgf_anti_of_nonpos {Y : Ω → ℝ} (hXY : X ≤ᵐ[μ] Y) (ht : t ≤ 0) (htX : Integrable (fun ω ↦ exp (t * X ω)) μ) : mgf Y μ t ≤ mgf X μ t

views.nl_informal: **Chernoff bound** on the upper tail of a real random variable.
views.lean_signature: theorem ProbabilityTheory.measure_ge_le_exp_mul_mgf [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (ε : ℝ) (ht : 0 ≤ t) (h_int : Integrable (fun ω => exp (t * X ω)) μ) : μ.real {ω | ε ≤ X ω} ≤ exp (-t * ε) * mgf X μ t

views.nl_informal: **Chernoff bound** on the lower tail of a real random variable.
views.lean_signature: theorem ProbabilityTheory.measure_le_le_exp_mul_mgf [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (ε : ℝ) (ht : t ≤ 0) (h_int : Integrable (fun ω => exp (t * X ω)) μ) : μ.real {ω | X ω ≤ ε} ≤ exp (-t * ε) * mgf X μ t

views.nl_informal: **Chernoff bound** on the upper tail of a real random variable.
views.lean_signature: theorem ProbabilityTheory.measure_ge_le_exp_cgf [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (ε : ℝ) (ht : 0 ≤ t) (h_int : Integrable (fun ω => exp (t * X ω)) μ) : μ.real {ω | ε ≤ X ω} ≤ exp (-t * ε + cgf X μ t)

views.nl_informal: **Chernoff bound** on the lower tail of a real random variable.
views.lean_signature: theorem ProbabilityTheory.measure_le_le_exp_cgf [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (ε : ℝ) (ht : t ≤ 0) (h_int : Integrable (fun ω => exp (t * X ω)) μ) : μ.real {ω | X ω ≤ ε} ≤ exp (-t * ε + cgf X μ t)

views.nl_informal:
For `z : ℂ` with `z.re ∈ interior (integrableExpSet X μ)`, the derivative of the function
`z' ↦ μ[X ^ n * cexp (z' * X)]` at `z` is `μ[X ^ (n + 1) * cexp (z * X)]`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ProbabilityTheory.hasDerivAt_integral_pow_mul_exp (hz : z.re ∈ interior (integrableExpSet X μ)) (n : ℕ) : HasDerivAt (fun z ↦ μ[fun ω ↦ X ω ^ n * cexp (z * X ω)]) μ[fun ω ↦ X ω ^ (n + 1) * cexp (z * X ω)] z

views.nl_informal:
For all `z : ℂ` with `z.re ∈ interior (integrableExpSet X μ)`,
`complexMGF X μ` is differentiable at `z` with derivative `μ[X * exp (z * X)]`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ProbabilityTheory.hasDerivAt_complexMGF (hz : z.re ∈ interior (integrableExpSet X μ)) : HasDerivAt (complexMGF X μ) μ[fun ω ↦ X ω * cexp (z * X ω)] z

views.nl_informal:

```

  |                    |

  |                    |
  v                    v
```

```
    |                      |
    |                      |
    v                      v
```

views.nl_informal:
Induction principle for finitely presented ring homomorphisms.

For a property to hold for all finitely presented ring homs, it suffices for it to hold for
`Polynomial.C : R → R[X]`, surjective ring homs with finitely generated kernels, and to be closed
under composition.

Note that to state this conveniently for ring homs between rings of different universes, we carry
around two predicates `P` and `Q`, which should be "the same" apart from universes:
* `P`, for ring homs `(R : Type u) → (S : Type u)`.
* `Q`, for ring homs `(R : Type u) → (S : Type v)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem RingHom.FinitePresentation.polynomial_induction (P : ∀ (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (S : Type u) [CommRing S], (R →+* S) → Prop) (Q : ∀ (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (S : Type v) [CommRing S], (R →+* S) → Prop) (polynomial : ∀ (R) [CommRing R], P R R[X] C) (fg_ker : ∀ (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (S : Type v) [CommRing S] (f : R →+* S), Surjective f → (ker f).FG → Q R S f) (comp : ∀ (R) [CommRing R] (S) [CommRing S] (T) [CommRing T] (f : R →+* S) (g : S →+* T), P R S f → Q S T g → Q R T (g.comp f)) {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (f : R →+* S) (hf : f.FinitePresentation) : Q R S f

views.nl_informal:
Let the following be a commutative diagram of rings
```
  R  →  S  →  T
  ↓     ↓     ↓
  R' →  S' →  T'
```
where the left-hand square is a pushout. Then the following are equivalent:
- the big rectangle is a pushout.
- the right-hand square is a pushout.

views.lean_signature: theorem Algebra.isAlgebraic_adjoin_singleton_iff [NoZeroDivisors R] {s : S} : (adjoin R {s}).IsAlgebraic ↔ IsAlgebraic R s

views.nl_informal:
If `x = {x_i : A | i : ι}` and `f = {f_i : MvPolynomial ι R | i : ι}` are algebraically
independent over `R`, then `{f_i(x) | i : ι}` is also algebraically independent over `R`.

views.nl_informal:
If `{f_i(x) | i : ι}` is algebraically independent over `R`, then
`{f_i : MvPolynomial ι R | i : ι}` is also algebraically independent over `R`.

is a field and `ι` is finite; the proof needs transcendence degree.

A set of algebraically independent elements in an algebra `A` over a ring `K` is also
algebraically independent over a subring `R` of `K`.

If `x` is a transcendence basis of `A/R`, then it is empty if and only if
`A/R` is algebraic.

`A/R` is transcendental.

If `s ⊆ t` are subsets in an `R`-algebra `A` such that `s` is algebraically independent over
`R`, and `A` is algebraic over the `R`-algebra generated by `t`, then there is a transcendence
basis of `A` over `R` between `s` and `t`, provided that `A` is a domain.

This may fail if only `R` is assumed to be a domain but `A` is not, because of failure of
transitivity of algebraicity: there may exist `a : A` such that `S := R[a]` is algebraic over
`R` and `A` is algebraic over `S`, but `A` nonetheless contains a transcendental element over `R`.
The only `R`-algebraically independent subset of `{a}` is `∅`, which is not a transcendence basis.

The inductively defined smallest congruence relation containing a binary relation `r` equals
the infimum of the set of congruence relations containing `r`.
views.lean_signature: theorem RingCon.ringConGen_eq (r : R → R → Prop) : ringConGen r = sInf {s : RingCon R | ∀ x y, r x y → s x y}

views.nl_informal:
The smallest congruence relation containing a binary relation `r` is contained in any
congruence relation containing `r`.
views.lean_signature: theorem RingCon.ringConGen_le {r : R → R → Prop} {c : RingCon R} (h : ∀ x y, r x y → c x y) : ringConGen r ≤ c

views.nl_informal:
Given binary relations `r, s` with `r` contained in `s`, the smallest congruence relation

views.lean_signature: theorem RingCon.ringConGen_mono {r s : R → R → Prop} (h : ∀ x y, r x y → s x y) : ringConGen r ≤ ringConGen s

views.lean_signature: theorem RingCon.ringConGen_of_ringCon (c : RingCon R) : ringConGen c = c

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:
The supremum of two congruence relations equals the smallest congruence relation containing

views.nl_informal:
Let `(R, m, k)` be a noetherian local domain (possibly a field).
The following are equivalent:
0. `R` is a PID
1. `R` is a valuation ring
2. `R` is a dedekind domain
3. `R` is integrally closed with at most one non-zero prime ideal
4. `m` is principal
5. `dimₖ m/m² ≤ 1`
6. Every nonzero ideal is a power of `m`.

Also see `IsDiscreteValuationRing.TFAE` for a version assuming `¬ IsField R`.
views.lean_signature: theorem tfae_of_isNoetherianRing_of_isLocalRing_of_isDomain [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsDomain R] : List.TFAE [IsPrincipalIdealRing R, ValuationRing R, IsDedekindDomain R, IsIntegrallyClosed R ∧ ∀ P : Ideal R, P ≠ ⊥ → P.IsPrime → P = maximalIdeal R, (maximalIdeal R).IsPrincipal, finrank (ResidueField R) (CotangentSpace R) ≤ 1, ∀ I ≠ ⊥, ∃ n : ℕ, I = maximalIdeal R ^ n]

views.nl_informal:
The following are equivalent for a
noetherian local domain that is not a field `(R, m, k)`:
0. `R` is a discrete valuation ring
1. `R` is a valuation ring
2. `R` is a dedekind domain
3. `R` is integrally closed with a unique non-zero prime ideal
4. `m` is principal
5. `dimₖ m/m² = 1`
6. Every nonzero ideal is a power of `m`.

Also see `tfae_of_isNoetherianRing_of_isLocalRing_of_isDomain` for a version without `¬ IsField R`.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsDiscreteValuationRing.TFAE [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsDomain R] (h : ¬IsField R) : List.TFAE [IsDiscreteValuationRing R, ValuationRing R, IsDedekindDomain R, IsIntegrallyClosed R ∧ ∃! P : Ideal R, P ≠ ⊥ ∧ P.IsPrime, (maximalIdeal R).IsPrincipal, finrank (ResidueField R) (CotangentSpace R) = 1, ∀ (I) (_ : I ≠ ⊥), ∃ n : ℕ, I = maximalIdeal R ^ n]

views.nl_informal:
**Equational criterion for flatness**, combined form.

Let $M$ be a module over a commutative ring $R$. The following are equivalent:
* $M$ is flat.
* For all ideals $I \subseteq R$, the map $I \otimes M \to M$ is injective.
* Every $\sum_i f_i \otimes x_i$ that vanishes in $R \otimes M$ vanishes trivially.
* Every relation $\sum_i f_i x_i = 0$ in $M$ is trivial.
* For all finite free modules $R^l$, all elements $f \in R^l$, and all linear maps
$x \colon R^l \to M$ such that $x(f) = 0$, there exist a finite free module $R^k$ and
linear maps $a \colon R^l \to R^k$ and $y \colon R^k \to M$ such
that $x = y \circ a$ and $a(f) = 0$.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.Flat.tfae_equational_criterion : List.TFAE [ Flat R M, ∀ I : Ideal R, Function.Injective (rTensor M I.subtype), ∀ {l : ℕ} {f : Fin l → R} {x : Fin l → M}, ∑ i, f i ⊗ₜ x i = (0 : R ⊗[R] M) → VanishesTrivially R f x, ∀ {l : ℕ} {f : Fin l → R} {x : Fin l → M}, ∑ i, f i • x i = 0 → IsTrivialRelation f x, ∀ {l : ℕ} {f : Fin l →₀ R} {x : (Fin l →₀ R) →ₗ[R] M}, x f = 0 → ∃ (k : ℕ) (a : (Fin l →₀ R) →ₗ[R] (Fin k →₀ R)) (y : (Fin k →₀ R) →ₗ[R] M), x = y ∘ₗ a ∧ a f = 0]

a module $M$ is flat if and only if every relation $\sum_i f_i x_i = 0$ in $M$ is trivial.

views.nl_informal:
**Equational criterion for flatness**, alternate form.

A module $M$ is flat if and only if for all finite free modules $R^l$,
all $f \in R^l$, and all linear maps $x \colon R^l \to M$ such that $x(f) = 0$, there
exist a finite free module $R^k$ and linear maps $a \colon R^l \to R^k$ and
$y \colon R^k \to M$ such that $x = y \circ a$ and $a(f) = 0$.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.Flat.iff_forall_exists_factorization : Flat R M ↔ ∀ {l : ℕ} {f : Fin l →₀ R} {x : (Fin l →₀ R) →ₗ[R] M}, x f = 0 → ∃ (k : ℕ) (a : (Fin l →₀ R) →ₗ[R] (Fin k →₀ R)) (y : (Fin k →₀ R) →ₗ[R] M), x = y ∘ₗ a ∧ a f = 0

views.nl_informal:
**Equational criterion for flatness**, backward direction, alternate form.

Let $M$ be a module over a commutative ring $R$. Suppose that for all finite free modules $R^l$,
all $f \in R^l$, and all linear maps $x \colon R^l \to M$ such that $x(f) = 0$, there
exist a finite free module $R^k$ and linear maps $a \colon R^l \to R^k$ and
$y \colon R^k \to M$ such that $x = y \circ a$ and $a(f) = 0$. Then $M$ is flat.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.Flat.of_forall_exists_factorization (h : ∀ {l : ℕ} {f : Fin l →₀ R} {x : (Fin l →₀ R) →ₗ[R] M}, x f = 0 → ∃ (k : ℕ) (a : (Fin l →₀ R) →ₗ[R] (Fin k →₀ R)) (y : (Fin k →₀ R) →ₗ[R] M), x = y ∘ₗ a ∧ a f = 0) : Flat R M

views.nl_informal:
**Equational criterion for flatness**, forward direction, second alternate form.

Let $M$ be a flat module over a commutative ring $R$. Let $N$ be a finite free module over $R$,
let $f \in N$, and let $x \colon N \to M$ be a linear map such that $x(f) = 0$. Then there exist a
finite free module $R^k$ and linear maps $a \colon N \to R^k$ and
$y \colon R^k \to M$ such that $x = y \circ a$ and $a(f) = 0$.

free, and let $f \colon K \to N$ and $x \colon N \to M$ be linear maps such that
$x \circ f = 0$. Then there exist a finite free module $R^k$ and linear maps
$a \colon N \to R^k$ and $y \colon R^k \to M$ such that $x = y \circ a$ and
$a \circ f = 0$.

If `f : A` has degree `d`, then `𝒜_(f)` is generated (as a module) over `𝒜₀` by

is injective.

```
    ↓          ↓
R[x] / P → (R / (P ∩ R))[x] / (P / (P ∩ R))
```

views.nl_informal: For a prime ideal, its height equals its prime height.

views.nl_informal: The height of the maximal ideal equals the Krull dimension in a local ring.

dimension if and only if it is the maximal ideal.

views.nl_informal: A finitely generated idempotent ideal is generated by an idempotent element

views.lean_signature: theorem Ideal.isPrimary_iff {I : Ideal R} : I.IsPrimary ↔ I ≠ ⊤ ∧ ∀ {x y : R}, x * y ∈ I → x ∈ I ∨ y ∈ radical I

views.nl_informal: All ideals in a division (semi)ring are trivial.
views.lean_signature: theorem Ideal.eq_bot_or_top : I = ⊥ ∨ I = ⊤

then `comap f (comap f.symm I) = I`.

views.lean_signature: theorem Ideal.map_comap_of_equiv {I : Ideal R} (f : R ≃+* S) : I.map (f : R →+* S) = I.comap f.symm

views.lean_signature: theorem Ideal.comap_symm {I : Ideal R} (f : R ≃+* S) : I.comap f.symm = I.map f

views.nl_informal: If `f : R ≃+* S` is a ring isomorphism and `I : Ideal R`, then `map f.symm I = comap f I`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Ideal.map_symm {I : Ideal S} (f : R ≃+* S) : I.map f.symm = I.comap f

views.nl_informal: An element is in the kernel if and only if it maps to zero.

views.nl_informal: An ideal is radical iff it is equal to its radical.

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal: Prime avoidance. Atiyah-Macdonald 1.11, Eisenbud 3.3, Matsumura Ex.1.6.

views.nl_informal:
If `I` divides `J`, then `I` contains `J`.

views.nl_informal:

```
R   → S
↓     ↓
R/p → S/P
```

then `P` lies over `p`.

views.nl_informal:
Every ideal of the product ring is of the form `I × J`, where `I` and `J` can be explicitly
given as the image under the projection maps.

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:

contained in the union of those of `M` and `M''`.

views.nl_informal:

the union of those of the two modules.

views.nl_informal: minimal primes are contained in zero divisors.

views.nl_informal:
If `a ∈ P^i \ P^(i+1)` and `c ∈ P^i`, then `a * d + e = c` for `e ∈ P^(i+1)`.

views.nl_informal:
The choice of `d` in `Ideal.exists_mul_add_mem_pow_succ` is unique, up to `P`.
Inspired by [Neukirch], proposition 6.1

views.nl_informal:
Let `e : S ≃ I` be an additive isomorphism (therefore a `ℤ`-linear equiv).

views.nl_informal:
Let `b` be a basis for `S` over `ℤ` and `bI` a basis for `I` over `ℤ` of the same dimension.

views.nl_informal:
An ideal equals its Jacobson radical iff it is the intersection of a set of maximal ideals.
Allowing the set to include ⊤ is equivalent, and is included only to simplify some proofs.

views.nl_informal:
An ideal `I` equals its Jacobson radical if and only if every element outside `I`
also lies outside of a maximal ideal containing `I`.

the Jacobson radical of the quotient ring `R/I` is the zero ideal
views.lean_signature: theorem Ideal.jacobson_eq_iff_jacobson_quotient_eq_bot : I.jacobson = I ↔ jacobson (⊥ : Ideal (R ⧸ I)) = ⊥

views.nl_informal:

the nilradical and Jacobson radical of the quotient ring `R/I` coincide
views.lean_signature: theorem Ideal.radical_eq_jacobson_iff_radical_quotient_eq_jacobson_bot : I.radical = I.jacobson ↔ radical (⊥ : Ideal (R ⧸ I)) = jacobson ⊥

views.nl_informal:

views.lean_signature: theorem Module.jacobson_pi_eq_bot (h : ∀ i, jacobson R (M i) = ⊥) : jacobson R (Π i, M i) = ⊥

views.nl_informal: A form of Nakayama's lemma for modules over noncommutative rings.
views.lean_signature: theorem Submodule.FG.eq_bot_of_le_jacobson_smul {N : Submodule R M} (fg : N.FG) (le : N ≤ Ring.jacobson R • N) : N = ⊥

views.nl_informal:
A ring is a Jacobson ring if and only if for all prime ideals `P`,
the Jacobson radical of `P` is equal to `P`.
views.lean_signature: theorem isJacobsonRing_iff_prime_eq : IsJacobsonRing R ↔ ∀ P : Ideal R, IsPrime P → P.jacobson = P

views.nl_informal:
A ring `R` is Jacobson if and only if for every prime ideal `I`,
`I` can be written as the infimum of some collection of maximal ideals.
Allowing ⊤ in the set `M` of maximal ideals is equivalent, but makes some proofs cleaner.
views.lean_signature: theorem isJacobsonRing_iff_sInf_maximal : IsJacobsonRing R ↔ ∀ {I : Ideal R}, I.IsPrime → ∃ M : Set (Ideal R), (∀ J ∈ M, IsMaximal J ∨ J = ⊤) ∧ I = sInf M

views.nl_informal:
If `R` is a Jacobson ring, then maximal ideals in the localization at `y`
correspond to maximal ideals in the original ring `R` that don't contain `y`.
This lemma gives the correspondence in the particular case of an ideal and its comap.
See `le_relIso_of_maximal` for the more general relation isomorphism
views.lean_signature: theorem IsLocalization.isMaximal_iff_isMaximal_disjoint [H : IsJacobsonRing R] (J : Ideal S) : J.IsMaximal ↔ (comap (algebraMap R S) J).IsMaximal ∧ y ∉ Ideal.comap (algebraMap R S) J

views.nl_informal:
If `R` is a Jacobson ring, then maximal ideals in the localization at `y`
correspond to maximal ideals in the original ring `R` that don't contain `y`.
This lemma gives the correspondence in the particular case of an ideal and its map.
See `le_relIso_of_maximal` for the more general statement, and the reverse of this implication

views.nl_informal:

views.lean_signature: theorem isJacobsonRing_localization [H : IsJacobsonRing R] : IsJacobsonRing S

views.nl_informal:
If `I` is a prime ideal of `R[X]` and `pX ∈ I` is a non-constant polynomial,
then the map `R →+* R[x]/I` descends to an integral map when localizing at `pX.leadingCoeff`.
