views.nl_informal:
The core unit-propagation step.

We have a local context of assumptions `¬l'` (sometimes called an assignment)
and we wish to add `¬l` to the context, that is, we want to prove `l` is also falsified.
This is because there is a clause `a ∨ b ∨ ¬l` in the global context
such that all literals in the clause are falsified except for `¬l`;
so in the context `h₁` where we suppose that `¬l` is falsified,
the clause itself is falsified so we can prove `False`.
We continue the proof in `h₂`, with the assumption that `l` is falsified.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sat.Valuation.by_cases {v : Valuation} {l} (h₁ : v.neg l.negate → False) (h₂ : v.neg l → False) : False

views.nl_informal:
The fundamental relationship between `mk` and `implies`:
`(mk ps).implies p ps 0` is equivalent to `p`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sat.Valuation.mk_implies {p} {as ps} (as₁) : as = List.reverseAux as₁ ps → (Valuation.mk as).implies p ps as₁.length → p

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is unsatisfiable, and every `v` which agrees with `ps` implies `¬⟦f⟧_v → p`, then `p`.
Equivalently, there exists a valuation `v` which agrees with `ps`,
and every such valuation yields `¬⟦f⟧_v` because `f` is unsatisfiable.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sat.Fmla.refute {p : Prop} {ps} (f : Fmla) (hf : f.proof []) (hv : ∀ v, Valuation.implies v (Fmla.reify v f p) ps 0) : p

views.nl_informal: Negation turns AND into OR, so `¬⟦f₁ ∧ f₂⟧_v ≡ ¬⟦f₁⟧_v ∨ ¬⟦f₂⟧_v`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sat.Fmla.reify_or {f₁ : Fmla} {a : Prop} {f₂ : Fmla} {b : Prop} (h₁ : Fmla.reify v f₁ a) (h₂ : Fmla.reify v f₂ b) : Fmla.reify v (f₁.and f₂) (a ∨ b)

views.nl_informal: Reification of a single clause formula.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sat.Fmla.reify_one {c : Clause} {a : Prop} (h : Clause.reify v c a) : Fmla.reify v (Fmla.one c) a

views.nl_informal: Negation turns OR into AND, so `¬⟦l ∨ c⟧_v ≡ ¬⟦l⟧_v ∧ ¬⟦c⟧_v`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sat.Clause.reify_and {l : Literal} {a : Prop} {c : Clause} {b : Prop} (h₁ : Literal.reify v l a) (h₂ : Clause.reify v c b) : Clause.reify v (Clause.cons l c) (a ∧ b)

views.nl_informal: The reification of the empty clause is `True`: `¬⟦⊥⟧_v ≡ True`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sat.Clause.reify_zero : Clause.reify v Clause.nil True

views.nl_informal: The reification of a singleton clause `¬⟦l⟧_v ≡ ¬⟦l⟧_v`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sat.Clause.reify_one {l : Literal} {a : Prop} (h₁ : Literal.reify v l a) : Clause.reify v (Clause.nil.cons l) a

views.nl_informal: The reification of a positive literal `¬⟦a⟧_v ≡ ¬a`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sat.Literal.reify_pos {a : Prop} {n : ℕ} (h : v n ↔ a) : (Literal.pos n).reify v ¬a

views.nl_informal: The reification of a negative literal `¬⟦¬a⟧_v ≡ a`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Sat.Literal.reify_neg {a : Prop} {n : ℕ} (h : v n ↔ a) : (Literal.neg n).reify v a

views.nl_informal: A unital magma with a topology and bornology has the trivial approximate unit `pure 1`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.IsApproximateUnit.pure_one : IsApproximateUnit (pure (1 : α))

views.nl_informal: If `l` is an approximate unit and `⊥ < l' ≤ l`, then `l'` is also an approximate unit.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.IsApproximateUnit.mono {l l' : Filter α} (hl : l.IsApproximateUnit) (hle : l' ≤ l) [hl' : l'.NeBot] : l'.IsApproximateUnit

views.nl_informal: In a topological unital magma, `𝓝 1` is an approximate unit.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.IsApproximateUnit.nhds_one [ContinuousMul α] : IsApproximateUnit (𝓝 (1 : α))

views.nl_informal: In a topological unital magma, `𝓝 1` is the largest approximate unit.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.IsApproximateUnit.iff_neBot_and_le_nhds_one [ContinuousMul α] {l : Filter α} : IsApproximateUnit l ↔ l.NeBot ∧ l ≤ 𝓝 1

views.nl_informal: In a topological unital magma, `𝓝 1` is the largest approximate unit.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.IsApproximateUnit.iff_le_nhds_one [ContinuousMul α] {l : Filter α} [l.NeBot] : IsApproximateUnit l ↔ l ≤ 𝓝 1

views.nl_informal:
If a family of sets `s` generates the topology, then intersections of finite
subcollections of `s` form a topological basis.
views.lean_signature: theorem TopologicalSpace.isTopologicalBasis_of_subbasis {s : Set (Set α)} (hs : t = generateFrom s) : IsTopologicalBasis ((fun f => ⋂₀ f) '' { f : Set (Set α) | f.Finite ∧ f ⊆ s })

views.nl_informal:
If a family of open sets `s` is such that every open neighbourhood contains some
member of `s`, then `s` is a topological basis.
views.lean_signature: theorem TopologicalSpace.isTopologicalBasis_of_isOpen_of_nhds {s : Set (Set α)} (h_open : ∀ u ∈ s, IsOpen u) (h_nhds : ∀ (a : α) (u : Set α), a ∈ u → IsOpen u → ∃ v ∈ s, a ∈ v ∧ v ⊆ u) : IsTopologicalBasis s

views.nl_informal:
A set `s` is in the neighbourhood of `a` iff there is some basis set `t`, which
contains `a` and is itself contained in `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem TopologicalSpace.IsTopologicalBasis.mem_nhds_iff {a : α} {s : Set α} {b : Set (Set α)} (hb : IsTopologicalBasis b) : s ∈ 𝓝 a ↔ ∃ t ∈ b, a ∈ t ∧ t ⊆ s

views.nl_informal: Any open set is the union of the basis sets contained in it.
views.lean_signature: theorem TopologicalSpace.IsTopologicalBasis.open_eq_sUnion' {B : Set (Set α)} (hB : IsTopologicalBasis B) {u : Set α} (ou : IsOpen u) : u = ⋃₀ { s ∈ B | s ⊆ u }

views.nl_informal: A point `a` is in the closure of `s` iff all basis sets containing `a` intersect `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem TopologicalSpace.IsTopologicalBasis.mem_closure_iff {b : Set (Set α)} (hb : IsTopologicalBasis b) {s : Set α} {a : α} : a ∈ closure s ↔ ∀ o ∈ b, a ∈ o → (o ∩ s).Nonempty

views.nl_informal: A set is dense iff it has non-trivial intersection with all basis sets.
views.lean_signature: theorem TopologicalSpace.IsTopologicalBasis.dense_iff {b : Set (Set α)} (hb : IsTopologicalBasis b) {s : Set α} : Dense s ↔ ∀ o ∈ b, Set.Nonempty o → (o ∩ s).Nonempty

views.nl_informal:
A nonempty separable space admits a sequence with dense range. Instead of running `cases` on the
conclusion of this lemma, you might want to use `TopologicalSpace.denseSeq` and
`TopologicalSpace.denseRange_denseSeq`.

If `α` might be empty, then `TopologicalSpace.exists_countable_dense` is the main way to use
separability of `α`.
views.lean_signature: theorem TopologicalSpace.exists_dense_seq [SeparableSpace α] [Nonempty α] : ∃ u : ℕ → α, DenseRange u

views.nl_informal: The sequence `TopologicalSpace.denseSeq α` has dense range.
views.lean_signature: theorem TopologicalSpace.denseRange_denseSeq [SeparableSpace α] [Nonempty α] : DenseRange (denseSeq α)

views.nl_informal:
If `f` has a dense range and its domain is countable, then its codomain is a separable space.
See also `DenseRange.separableSpace`.
views.lean_signature: theorem TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace.of_denseRange {ι : Sort _} [Countable ι] (u : ι → α) (hu : DenseRange u) : SeparableSpace α

views.nl_informal:
If `α` is a separable space and `f : α → β` is a continuous map with dense range, then `β` is
a separable space as well. E.g., the completion of a separable uniform space is separable.
views.lean_signature: theorem DenseRange.separableSpace [SeparableSpace α] [TopologicalSpace β] {f : α → β} (h : DenseRange f) (h' : Continuous f) : SeparableSpace β

views.nl_informal: A topological space with discrete topology is separable iff it is countable.
views.lean_signature: theorem TopologicalSpace.separableSpace_iff_countable [DiscreteTopology α] : SeparableSpace α ↔ Countable α

views.nl_informal: In a separable space, a family of nonempty disjoint open sets is countable.
views.lean_signature: theorem Pairwise.countable_of_isOpen_disjoint [SeparableSpace α] {ι : Type*} {s : ι → Set α} (hd : Pairwise (Disjoint on s)) (ho : ∀ i, IsOpen (s i)) (hne : ∀ i, (s i).Nonempty) : Countable ι

views.nl_informal: In a separable space, a family of nonempty disjoint open sets is countable.
views.lean_signature: theorem Set.PairwiseDisjoint.countable_of_isOpen [SeparableSpace α] {ι : Type*} {s : ι → Set α} {a : Set ι} (h : a.PairwiseDisjoint s) (ho : ∀ i ∈ a, IsOpen (s i)) (hne : ∀ i ∈ a, (s i).Nonempty) : a.Countable

views.nl_informal: In a separable space, a family of disjoint sets with nonempty interiors is countable.
views.lean_signature: theorem Set.PairwiseDisjoint.countable_of_nonempty_interior [SeparableSpace α] {ι : Type*} {s : ι → Set α} {a : Set ι} (h : a.PairwiseDisjoint s) (ha : ∀ i ∈ a, (interior (s i)).Nonempty) : a.Countable

views.nl_informal:
Let `s` be a dense set in a topological space `α` with partial order structure. If `s` is a
separable space (e.g., if `α` has a second countable topology), then there exists a countable
dense subset `t ⊆ s` such that `t` contains bottom/top element of `α` when they exist and belong
to `s`. For a dense subset containing neither bot nor top elements, see
`Dense.exists_countable_dense_subset_no_bot_top`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Dense.exists_countable_dense_subset_bot_top {α : Type*} [TopologicalSpace α] [PartialOrder α] {s : Set α} [SeparableSpace s] (hs : Dense s) : ∃ t ⊆ s, t.Countable ∧ Dense t ∧ (∀ x, IsBot x → x ∈ s → x ∈ t) ∧ ∀ x, IsTop x → x ∈ s → x ∈ t

views.nl_informal:
If `α` is a separable topological space with a partial order, then there exists a countable
dense set `s : Set α` that contains those of both bottom and top elements of `α` that actually
exist. For a dense set containing neither bot nor top elements, see
`exists_countable_dense_no_bot_top`.
views.lean_signature: theorem exists_countable_dense_bot_top (α : Type*) [TopologicalSpace α] [SeparableSpace α] [PartialOrder α] : ∃ s : Set α, s.Countable ∧ Dense s ∧ (∀ x, IsBot x → x ∈ s) ∧ ∀ x, IsTop x → x ∈ s

views.nl_informal:
If `β` is a first-countable space, then its induced topology via `f` on `α` is also
first-countable.
views.lean_signature: theorem TopologicalSpace.firstCountableTopology_induced (α β : Type*) [t : TopologicalSpace β] [FirstCountableTopology β] (f : α → β) : @FirstCountableTopology α (t.induced f)

views.nl_informal:
In a first-countable space, a cluster point `x` of a sequence
is the limit of some subsequence.
views.lean_signature: theorem TopologicalSpace.FirstCountableTopology.tendsto_subseq [FirstCountableTopology α] {u : ℕ → α} {x : α} (hx : MapClusterPt x atTop u) : ∃ ψ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono ψ ∧ Tendsto (u ∘ ψ) atTop (𝓝 x)

views.nl_informal:
If `β` is a second-countable space, then its induced topology via
`f` on `α` is also second-countable.
views.lean_signature: theorem TopologicalSpace.secondCountableTopology_induced (α β) [t : TopologicalSpace β] [SecondCountableTopology β] (f : α → β) : @SecondCountableTopology α (t.induced f)

views.nl_informal:
A countable open cover induces a second-countable topology if all open covers
are themselves second countable.
views.lean_signature: theorem TopologicalSpace.secondCountableTopology_of_countable_cover {ι} [Countable ι] {U : ι → Set α} [∀ i, SecondCountableTopology (U i)] (Uo : ∀ i, IsOpen (U i)) (hc : ⋃ i, U i = univ) : SecondCountableTopology α

views.nl_informal:
In a second-countable space, an open set, given as a union of open sets,
is equal to the union of countably many of those sets.
In particular, any open covering of `α` has a countable subcover: α is a Lindelöf space.
views.lean_signature: theorem TopologicalSpace.isOpen_iUnion_countable [SecondCountableTopology α] {ι} (s : ι → Set α) (H : ∀ i, IsOpen (s i)) : ∃ T : Set ι, T.Countable ∧ ⋃ i ∈ T, s i = ⋃ i, s i

views.nl_informal:
In a topological space with second countable topology, if `f` is a function that sends each
point `x` to a neighborhood of `x`, then for some countable set `s`, the neighborhoods `f x`,
`x ∈ s`, cover the whole space.
views.lean_signature: theorem TopologicalSpace.countable_cover_nhds [SecondCountableTopology α] {f : α → Set α} (hf : ∀ x, f x ∈ 𝓝 x) : ∃ s : Set α, s.Countable ∧ ⋃ x ∈ s, f x = univ

views.nl_informal:
In a disjoint union space `Σ i, E i`, one can form a topological basis by taking the union of
topological bases on each of the parts of the space.
views.lean_signature: theorem TopologicalSpace.IsTopologicalBasis.sigma {s : ∀ i : ι, Set (Set (E i))} (hs : ∀ i, IsTopologicalBasis (s i)) : IsTopologicalBasis (⋃ i : ι, (fun u => (Sigma.mk i '' u : Set (Σi, E i))) '' s i)

views.nl_informal:
In a sum space `α ⊕ β`, one can form a topological basis by taking the union of
topological bases on each of the two components.
views.lean_signature: theorem TopologicalSpace.IsTopologicalBasis.sum {s : Set (Set α)} (hs : IsTopologicalBasis s) {t : Set (Set β)} (ht : IsTopologicalBasis t) : IsTopologicalBasis ((fun u => Sum.inl '' u) '' s ∪ (fun u => Sum.inr '' u) '' t)

views.nl_informal: The image of a topological basis under an open quotient map is a topological basis.
views.lean_signature: theorem TopologicalSpace.IsTopologicalBasis.isQuotientMap {V : Set (Set X)} (hV : IsTopologicalBasis V) (h' : IsQuotientMap π) (h : IsOpenMap π) : IsTopologicalBasis (Set.image π '' V)

views.nl_informal: A second countable space is mapped by an open quotient map to a second countable space.
views.lean_signature: theorem Topology.IsQuotientMap.secondCountableTopology [SecondCountableTopology X] (h' : IsQuotientMap π) (h : IsOpenMap π) : SecondCountableTopology Y

views.nl_informal: The image of a topological basis "downstairs" in an open quotient is a topological basis.
views.lean_signature: theorem TopologicalSpace.IsTopologicalBasis.quotient {V : Set (Set X)} (hV : IsTopologicalBasis V) (h : IsOpenMap (Quotient.mk' : X → Quotient S)) : IsTopologicalBasis (Set.image (Quotient.mk' : X → Quotient S) '' V)

views.nl_informal: An open quotient of a second countable space is second countable.
views.lean_signature: theorem TopologicalSpace.Quotient.secondCountableTopology [SecondCountableTopology X] (h : IsOpenMap (Quotient.mk' : X → Quotient S)) : SecondCountableTopology (Quotient S)

views.nl_informal:
If a filter `f` is majorated by some `𝓝 x`, then it is majorated by `𝓝 (Filter.lim f)`. We
formulate this lemma with a `[Nonempty X]` argument of `lim` derived from `h` to make it useful for
types without a `[Nonempty X]` instance. Because of the built-in proof irrelevance, Lean will unify
this instance with any other instance.
views.lean_signature: theorem le_nhds_lim {f : Filter X} (h : ∃ x, f ≤ 𝓝 x) : f ≤ 𝓝 (@lim _ _ (nonempty_of_exists h) f)

views.nl_informal:
If `g` tends to some `𝓝 x` along `f`, then it tends to `𝓝 (Filter.limUnder f g)`. We formulate
this lemma with a `[Nonempty X]` argument of `lim` derived from `h` to make it useful for types
without a `[Nonempty X]` instance. Because of the built-in proof irrelevance, Lean will unify this
instance with any other instance.
views.lean_signature: theorem tendsto_nhds_limUnder {f : Filter α} {g : α → X} (h : ∃ x, Tendsto g f (𝓝 x)) : Tendsto g f (𝓝 (@limUnder _ _ _ (nonempty_of_exists h) f g))

views.nl_informal: The intersection of a disjoint covering by two open sets of a clopen set will be clopen.
views.lean_signature: theorem isClopen_inter_of_disjoint_cover_clopen {s a b : Set X} (h : IsClopen s) (cover : s ⊆ a ∪ b) (ha : IsOpen a) (hb : IsOpen b) (hab : Disjoint a b) : IsClopen (s ∩ a)

views.nl_informal:
Every clopen set in a product of two compact spaces
is a union of finitely many clopen boxes.
views.lean_signature: theorem TopologicalSpace.Clopens.exists_finset_eq_sup_prod (W : Clopens (X × Y)) : ∃ (I : Finset (Clopens X × Clopens Y)), W = I.sup fun i ↦ i.1 ×ˢ i.2

views.nl_informal: The closure of a set `s` is dense if and only if `s` is dense.
views.lean_signature: theorem dense_closure : Dense (closure s) ↔ Dense s

views.nl_informal: A set is dense if and only if it has a nonempty intersection with each nonempty open set.
views.lean_signature: theorem dense_iff_inter_open : Dense s ↔ ∀ U, IsOpen U → U.Nonempty → (U ∩ s).Nonempty

views.nl_informal: Complement to a singleton is dense if and only if the singleton is not an open set.
views.lean_signature: theorem dense_compl_singleton_iff_not_open : Dense ({x}ᶜ : Set X) ↔ ¬IsOpen ({x} : Set X)

views.nl_informal: If a closed property holds for a dense subset, it holds for the whole space.
views.lean_signature: theorem Dense.induction (hs : Dense s) {P : X → Prop} (mem : ∀ x ∈ s, P x) (isClosed : IsClosed { x | P x }) (x : X) : P x

views.nl_informal: Interior and frontier are disjoint.
views.lean_signature: theorem disjoint_interior_frontier : Disjoint (interior s) (frontier s)

views.nl_informal: The complement of a set has the same frontier as the original set.
views.lean_signature: theorem frontier_compl (s : Set X) : frontier sᶜ = frontier s

views.nl_informal: The frontier of a set is closed.
views.lean_signature: theorem isClosed_frontier : IsClosed (frontier s)

views.nl_informal: The frontier of a closed set has no interior point.
views.lean_signature: theorem interior_frontier (h : IsClosed s) : interior (frontier s) = ∅

views.nl_informal:
`x` is a cluster point of a set `s` if every neighbourhood of `x` meets `s` on a nonempty
set. See also `mem_closure_iff_clusterPt`.
views.lean_signature: theorem clusterPt_principal_iff : ClusterPt x (𝓟 s) ↔ ∀ U ∈ 𝓝 x, (U ∩ s).Nonempty

views.nl_informal: `x` is an accumulation point of a set `C` iff it is a cluster point of `C ∖ {x}`.
views.lean_signature: theorem accPt_principal_iff_clusterPt {x : X} {C : Set X} : AccPt x (𝓟 C) ↔ ClusterPt x (𝓟 (C \ { x }))

views.nl_informal:
`x` is an accumulation point of a set `C` iff every neighborhood
of `x` contains a point of `C` other than `x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem accPt_iff_nhds {x : X} {C : Set X} : AccPt x (𝓟 C) ↔ ∀ U ∈ 𝓝 x, ∃ y ∈ U ∩ C, y ≠ x

views.nl_informal:
`x` is an accumulation point of a set `C` iff
there are points near `x` in `C` and different from `x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem accPt_iff_frequently {x : X} {C : Set X} : AccPt x (𝓟 C) ↔ ∃ᶠ y in 𝓝 x, y ≠ x ∧ y ∈ C

views.nl_informal:
If `x` is an accumulation point of `F` and `F ≤ G`, then
`x` is an accumulation point of `G`.
views.lean_signature: theorem AccPt.mono {F G : Filter X} (h : AccPt x F) (hFG : F ≤ G) : AccPt x G

views.nl_informal:
The set of cluster points of a filter is closed. In particular, the set of limit points
of a sequence is closed.
views.lean_signature: theorem isClosed_setOf_clusterPt {f : Filter X} : IsClosed { x | ClusterPt x f }

views.nl_informal:
If `x` is not an isolated point of a topological space, then `{x}ᶜ` is dense in the whole
space.
views.lean_signature: theorem dense_compl_singleton (x : X) [NeBot (𝓝[≠] x)] : Dense ({x}ᶜ : Set X)

views.nl_informal:
If `x` is not an isolated point of a topological space, then the closure of `{x}ᶜ` is the whole
space.
views.lean_signature: theorem closure_compl_singleton (x : X) [NeBot (𝓝[≠] x)] : closure {x}ᶜ = (univ : Set X)

views.nl_informal: If `x` is not an isolated point of a topological space, then the interior of `{x}` is empty.
views.lean_signature: theorem interior_singleton (x : X) [NeBot (𝓝[≠] x)] : interior {x} = (∅ : Set X)

views.nl_informal:
If `X` is a sequential space
and `S` contains each set of the form `insert x (Set.range u)`
where `u : ℕ → X` is a sequence and `x` is its limit,
then topology on `X` is generated by its restrictions to the sets of `S`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Topology.IsCoherentWith.of_seq [SequentialSpace X] (h : ∀ ⦃u : ℕ → X⦄ ⦃x : X⦄, Tendsto u atTop (𝓝 x) → insert x (range u) ∈ S) : IsCoherentWith S

views.nl_informal: A sequential space is compactly generated.
views.lean_signature: theorem Topology.IsCoherentWith.isCompact_of_seq [SequentialSpace X] : IsCoherentWith {K : Set X | IsCompact K}

views.nl_informal:
If each point of the space has a neighborhood from the family `S`,
then the topology is generated by its restrictions to the sets of `S`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Topology.IsCoherentWith.of_nhds (h : ∀ x, ∃ s ∈ S, s ∈ 𝓝 x) : IsCoherentWith S

views.nl_informal: A weakly locally compact space is compactly generated.
views.lean_signature: theorem Topology.IsCoherentWith.isCompact_of_weaklyLocallyCompact [WeaklyLocallyCompactSpace X] : IsCoherentWith {K : Set X | IsCompact K}

views.nl_informal: Definition of `ContinuousMap.compactOpen`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContinuousMap.compactOpen_eq : @compactOpen X Y _ _ = .generateFrom (image2 (fun K U ↦ {f | MapsTo f K U}) {K | IsCompact K} {t | IsOpen t})

views.nl_informal:
If `g : C(Y, Z)` is a topology inducing map,
then the composition `ContinuousMap.comp g : C(X, Y) → C(X, Z)` is a topology inducing map too.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContinuousMap.isInducing_postcomp (g : C(Y, Z)) (hg : IsInducing g) : IsInducing (g.comp : C(X, Y) → C(X, Z))

views.nl_informal:
If `g : C(Y, Z)` is a topological embedding,
then the composition `ContinuousMap.comp g : C(X, Y) → C(X, Z)` is an embedding too.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContinuousMap.isEmbedding_postcomp (g : C(Y, Z)) (hg : IsEmbedding g) : IsEmbedding (g.comp : C(X, Y) → C(X, Z))

views.nl_informal:
Composition is a continuous map from `C(X, Y) × C(Y, Z)` to `C(X, Z)`,
provided that `Y` is locally compact.
This is Prop. 9 of Chap. X, §3, №. 4 of Bourbaki's *Topologie Générale*.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContinuousMap.continuous_comp' : Continuous fun x : C(X, Y) × C(Y, Z) => x.2.comp x.1

views.nl_informal:
For any subset `s` of `X`, the restriction of continuous functions to `s` is continuous
as a function from `C(X, Y)` to `C(s, Y)` with their respective compact-open topologies.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContinuousMap.continuous_restrict (s : Set X) : Continuous fun F : C(X, Y) => F.restrict s

views.nl_informal:
The compact-open topology on `C(X, Y)`
is equal to the infimum of the compact-open topologies on `C(s, Y)` for `s` a compact subset of `X`.
The key point of the proof is that for every compact set `K`,
the universal set `Set.univ : Set K` is a compact set as well.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContinuousMap.compactOpen_eq_iInf_induced : (ContinuousMap.compactOpen : TopologicalSpace C(X, Y)) = ⨅ (K : Set X) (_ : IsCompact K), .induced (.restrict K) ContinuousMap.compactOpen

views.nl_informal:
A family `F` of functions in `C(X, Y)` converges in the compact-open topology, if and only if
it converges in the compact-open topology on each compact subset of `X`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContinuousMap.exists_tendsto_compactOpen_iff_forall [WeaklyLocallyCompactSpace X] [T2Space Y] {ι : Type*} {l : Filter ι} [Filter.NeBot l] (F : ι → C(X, Y)) : (∃ f, Filter.Tendsto F l (𝓝 f)) ↔ ∀ s : Set X, IsCompact s → ∃ f, Filter.Tendsto (fun i => (F i).restrict s) l (𝓝 f)

views.nl_informal: The coevaluation map `Y → C(X, Y × X)` is continuous (always).
views.lean_signature: theorem ContinuousMap.continuous_coev : Continuous (coev X Y)

views.nl_informal:
To show continuity of a map `α → C(β, γ)`, it suffices to show that its uncurried form
`α × β → γ` is continuous.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContinuousMap.continuous_of_continuous_uncurry (f : X → C(Y, Z)) (h : Continuous (Function.uncurry fun x y => f x y)) : Continuous f

views.nl_informal: The currying process is a continuous map between function spaces.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContinuousMap.continuous_curry [LocallyCompactSpace (X × Y)] : Continuous (curry : C(X × Y, Z) → C(X, C(Y, Z)))

views.nl_informal: The uncurried form of a continuous map `X → C(Y, Z)` is a continuous map `X × Y → Z`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContinuousMap.continuous_uncurry_of_continuous [LocallyCompactSpace Y] (f : C(X, C(Y, Z))) : Continuous (Function.uncurry fun x y => f x y)

views.nl_informal: The uncurrying process is a continuous map between function spaces.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContinuousMap.continuous_uncurry [LocallyCompactSpace X] [LocallyCompactSpace Y] : Continuous (uncurry : C(X, C(Y, Z)) → C(X × Y, Z))

views.nl_informal:
An induction principle for constructible sets. If `p` holds for all open retrocompact
sets, and is preserved under union and complement, then `p` holds for all constructible sets.
views.lean_signature: theorem Topology.IsConstructible.empty_union_induction {p : ∀ s : Set X, IsConstructible s → Prop} (open_retrocompact : ∀ U (hUopen : IsOpen U) (hUcomp : IsRetrocompact U), p U (BooleanSubalgebra.subset_closure ⟨hUopen, hUcomp⟩)) (union : ∀ s hs t ht, p s hs → p t ht → p (s ∪ t) (hs.union ht)) (compl : ∀ s hs, p s hs → p sᶜ hs.compl) {s} (hs : IsConstructible s) : p s hs

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is continuous and is such that preimages of open retrocompact sets are retrocompact,
then preimages of constructible sets are constructible.
views.lean_signature: theorem Topology.IsConstructible.preimage {s : Set Y} (hfcont : Continuous f) (hf : ∀ s, IsOpen s → IsRetrocompact s → IsRetrocompact (f ⁻¹' s)) (hs : IsConstructible s) : IsConstructible (f ⁻¹' s)

views.nl_informal: The image of a dense set under `Quotient.mk'` is a dense set.
views.lean_signature: theorem Dense.quotient [Setoid X] [TopologicalSpace X] {s : Set X} (H : Dense s) : Dense (Quotient.mk' '' s)

views.nl_informal: The composition of `Quotient.mk'` and a function with dense range has dense range.
views.lean_signature: theorem DenseRange.quotient [Setoid X] [TopologicalSpace X] {f : Y → X} (hf : DenseRange f) : DenseRange (Quotient.mk' ∘ f)

views.nl_informal:
Let `s, t ⊆ X` be two subsets of a topological space `X`.  If `t ⊆ s` and the topology induced
by `X`on `s` is discrete, then also the topology induces on `t` is discrete.
views.lean_signature: theorem DiscreteTopology.of_subset {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] {s t : Set X} (_ : DiscreteTopology s) (ts : t ⊆ s) : DiscreteTopology t

views.nl_informal:
Let `s` be a discrete subset of a topological space. Then the preimage of `s` by
a continuous injective map is also discrete.
views.lean_signature: theorem DiscreteTopology.preimage_of_continuous_injective {X Y : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] (s : Set Y) [DiscreteTopology s] {f : X → Y} (hc : Continuous f) (hinj : Function.Injective f) : DiscreteTopology (f ⁻¹' s)

views.nl_informal:
If `f : X → Y` is a quotient map,
then its restriction to the preimage of an open set is a quotient map too.
views.lean_signature: theorem Topology.IsQuotientMap.restrictPreimage_isOpen {f : X → Y} (hf : IsQuotientMap f) {s : Set Y} (hs : IsOpen s) : IsQuotientMap (s.restrictPreimage f)

views.nl_informal: `Function.update f i x` is continuous in `(f, x)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem continuous_update [DecidableEq ι] (i : ι) : Continuous fun f : (∀ j, π j) × π i => update f.1 i f.2

views.nl_informal: `Pi.mulSingle i x` is continuous in `x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem continuous_mulSingle [∀ i, One (π i)] [DecidableEq ι] (i : ι) : Continuous fun x => (Pi.mulSingle i x : ∀ i, π i)

views.nl_informal:
Suppose `π i` is a family of topological spaces indexed by `i : ι`, and `X` is a type
endowed with a family of maps `f i : X → π i` for every `i : ι`, hence inducing a
map `g : X → Π i, π i`. This lemma shows that infimum of the topologies on `X` induced by
the `f i` as `i : ι` varies is simply the topology on `X` induced by `g : X → Π i, π i`
where `Π i, π i` is endowed with the usual product topology.
views.lean_signature: theorem inducing_iInf_to_pi {X : Type*} (f : ∀ i, X → π i) : @IsInducing X (∀ i, π i) (⨅ i, induced (f i) inferInstance) _ fun x i => f i x

views.nl_informal: A map out of a sum type is continuous iff its restriction to each summand is.
views.lean_signature: theorem continuous_sigma_iff {f : Sigma σ → X} : Continuous f ↔ ∀ i, Continuous fun a => f ⟨i, a⟩

views.nl_informal: A map out of a sum type is continuous if its restriction to each summand is.
views.lean_signature: theorem continuous_sigma {f : Sigma σ → X} (hf : ∀ i, Continuous fun a => f ⟨i, a⟩) : Continuous f

views.nl_informal:
A map defined on a sigma type (a.k.a. the disjoint union of an indexed family of topological
spaces) is inducing iff its restriction to each component is inducing and each the image of each
component under `f` can be separated from the images of all other components by an open set.
views.lean_signature: theorem inducing_sigma {f : Sigma σ → X} : IsInducing f ↔ (∀ i, IsInducing (f ∘ Sigma.mk i)) ∧ (∀ i, ∃ U, IsOpen U ∧ ∀ x, f x ∈ U ↔ x.1 = i)

views.nl_informal:
The product of a neighborhood of `s` and a neighborhood of `t` is a neighborhood of `s ×ˢ t`,
formulated in terms of a filter inequality.
views.lean_signature: theorem nhdsSet_prod_le (s : Set X) (t : Set Y) : 𝓝ˢ (s ×ˢ t) ≤ 𝓝ˢ s ×ˢ 𝓝ˢ t

views.nl_informal:
If `f x ∈ s ∈ 𝓝 (f x)` for continuous `f`, then `f y ∈ s` near `x`.

This is essentially `Filter.Tendsto.eventually_mem`, but infers in more cases when applied.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContinuousAt.eventually_mem {f : X → Y} {x : X} (hf : ContinuousAt f x) {s : Set Y} (hs : s ∈ 𝓝 (f x)) : ∀ᶠ y in 𝓝 x, f y ∈ s

views.nl_informal:
If a function `f` tends to somewhere other than `𝓝 (f x)` at `x`,
then `f` is not continuous at `x`
views.lean_signature: theorem not_continuousAt_of_tendsto {f : X → Y} {l₁ : Filter X} {l₂ : Filter Y} {x : X} (hf : Tendsto f l₁ l₂) [l₁.NeBot] (hl₁ : l₁ ≤ 𝓝 x) (hl₂ : Disjoint (𝓝 (f x)) l₂) : ¬ ContinuousAt f x

views.nl_informal: If a continuous map `f` maps `s` to `t`, then it maps `closure s` to `closure t`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Set.MapsTo.closure {t : Set Y} (h : MapsTo f s t) (hc : Continuous f) : MapsTo f (closure s) (closure t)

views.nl_informal: If a continuous map `f` maps `s` to a closed set `t`, then it maps `closure s` to `t`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Set.MapsTo.closure_left {t : Set Y} (h : MapsTo f s t) (hc : Continuous f) (ht : IsClosed t) : MapsTo f (closure s) t

views.nl_informal: A surjective map has dense range.
views.lean_signature: theorem Function.Surjective.denseRange (hf : Function.Surjective f) : DenseRange f

views.nl_informal: The image of a dense set under a continuous map with dense range is a dense set.
views.lean_signature: theorem DenseRange.dense_image {f : X → Y} (hf' : DenseRange f) (hf : Continuous f) (hs : Dense s) : Dense (f '' s)

views.nl_informal:
If `f` has dense range and `s` is an open set in the codomain of `f`, then the image of the
preimage of `s` under `f` is dense in `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem DenseRange.subset_closure_image_preimage_of_isOpen (hf : DenseRange f) (hs : IsOpen s) : s ⊆ closure (f '' (f ⁻¹' s))

views.nl_informal:
If a continuous map with dense range maps a dense set to a subset of `t`, then `t` is a dense
set.
views.lean_signature: theorem DenseRange.dense_of_mapsTo {f : X → Y} (hf' : DenseRange f) (hf : Continuous f) (hs : Dense s) {t : Set Y} (ht : MapsTo f s t) : Dense t

views.nl_informal:
Composition of a continuous map with dense range and a function with dense range has dense
range.
views.lean_signature: theorem DenseRange.comp {g : Y → Z} {f : α → Y} (hg : DenseRange g) (hf : DenseRange f) (cg : Continuous g) : DenseRange (g ∘ f)

views.nl_informal:
If `L` and `R` are neighborhoods of `b` within sets whose union is `Set.univ`, then
`L ∪ R` is a neighborhood of `b`.
views.lean_signature: theorem union_mem_nhds_of_mem_nhdsWithin {b : α} {I₁ I₂ : Set α} (h : Set.univ = I₁ ∪ I₂) {L : Set α} (hL : L ∈ nhdsWithin b I₁) {R : Set α} (hR : R ∈ nhdsWithin b I₂) : L ∪ R ∈ nhds b

views.nl_informal: Writing a punctured neighborhood filter as a sup of left and right filters.
views.lean_signature: theorem punctured_nhds_eq_nhdsWithin_sup_nhdsWithin [LinearOrder α] {x : α} : 𝓝[≠] x = 𝓝[<] x ⊔ 𝓝[>] x

views.nl_informal: Obtain a "predictably-sided" neighborhood of `b` from two one-sided neighborhoods.
views.lean_signature: theorem nhds_of_Ici_Iic [LinearOrder α] {b : α} {L : Set α} (hL : L ∈ 𝓝[≤] b) {R : Set α} (hR : R ∈ 𝓝[≥] b) : L ∩ Iic b ∪ R ∩ Ici b ∈ 𝓝 b

views.nl_informal:
Two functions agree on a neighborhood of `x` if they agree at `x` and in a punctured
neighborhood.
views.lean_signature: theorem eventuallyEq_nhds_of_eventuallyEq_nhdsNE {f g : α → β} {a : α} (h₁ : f =ᶠ[𝓝[≠] a] g) (h₂ : f a = g a) : f =ᶠ[𝓝 a] g

views.nl_informal:
If a function is continuous within `s` at `x`, then it tends to `f x` within `s` by definition.
We register this fact for use with the dot notation, especially to use `Filter.Tendsto.comp` as
`ContinuousWithinAt.comp` will have a different meaning.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContinuousWithinAt.tendsto (h : ContinuousWithinAt f s x) : Tendsto f (𝓝[s] x) (𝓝 (f x))

views.nl_informal:
If a function is continuous on a set for some topologies, then it is
continuous on the same set with respect to any finer topology on the source space.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContinuousOn.mono_dom {α β : Type*} {t₁ t₂ : TopologicalSpace α} {t₃ : TopologicalSpace β} (h₁ : t₂ ≤ t₁) {s : Set α} {f : α → β} (h₂ : @ContinuousOn α β t₁ t₃ f s) : @ContinuousOn α β t₂ t₃ f s

views.nl_informal:
If a function is continuous on a set for some topologies, then it is
continuous on the same set with respect to any coarser topology on the target space.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContinuousOn.mono_rng {α β : Type*} {t₁ : TopologicalSpace α} {t₂ t₃ : TopologicalSpace β} (h₁ : t₂ ≤ t₃) {s : Set α} {f : α → β} (h₂ : @ContinuousOn α β t₁ t₂ f s) : @ContinuousOn α β t₁ t₃ f s

views.nl_informal:
If two sets coincide around `x`, then being continuous within one or the other at `x` is
equivalent. See also `continuousWithinAt_congr_set'` which requires that the sets coincide
locally away from a point `y`, in a T1 space.
views.lean_signature: theorem continuousWithinAt_congr_set (h : s =ᶠ[𝓝 x] t) : ContinuousWithinAt f s x ↔ ContinuousWithinAt f t x

views.nl_informal:
If a function `f a b` is such that `y ↦ f a b` is continuous for all `a`, and `a` lives in a
discrete space, then `f` is continuous, and vice versa.
views.lean_signature: theorem continuous_prod_of_discrete_left [DiscreteTopology α] {f : α × β → γ} : Continuous f ↔ ∀ a, Continuous (f ⟨a, ·⟩)

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is continuous on an open set `s` and continuous at each point of another
set `t` then `f` is continuous on `s ∪ t`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContinuousOn.union_continuousAt {f : α → β} (s_op : IsOpen s) (hs : ContinuousOn f s) (ht : ∀ x ∈ t, ContinuousAt f x) : ContinuousOn f (s ∪ t)

views.nl_informal: If a function is continuous on two closed sets, it is also continuous on their union.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContinuousOn.union_isClosed (hs : IsClosed s) (ht : IsClosed t) {f : α → β} (hfs : ContinuousOn f s) (hft : ContinuousOn f t) : ContinuousOn f (s ∪ t)

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is continuous on some neighbourhood `s'` of `s` and `f` maps `s` to `t`,
the preimage of a set neighbourhood of `t` is a set neighbourhood of `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContinuousOn.tendsto_nhdsSet {f : α → β} {s s' : Set α} {t : Set β} (hf : ContinuousOn f s') (hs' : s' ∈ 𝓝ˢ s) (hst : MapsTo f s t) : Tendsto f (𝓝ˢ s) (𝓝ˢ t)

views.nl_informal:
Preimage of a set neighborhood of `t` under a continuous map `f` is a set neighborhood of `s`
provided that `f` maps `s` to `t`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Continuous.tendsto_nhdsSet {f : α → β} {t : Set β} (hf : Continuous f) (hst : MapsTo f s t) : Tendsto f (𝓝ˢ s) (𝓝ˢ t)

views.nl_informal:
If `i : α → β` is a dense embedding with dense complement of the range, then any compact set in
`α` has empty interior.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsDenseInducing.interior_compact_eq_empty [T2Space β] (di : IsDenseInducing i) (hd : Dense (range i)ᶜ) {s : Set α} (hs : IsCompact s) : interior s = ∅

views.nl_informal: The product of two dense inducings is a dense inducing
views.lean_signature: theorem IsDenseInducing.prodMap [TopologicalSpace γ] [TopologicalSpace δ] {e₁ : α → β} {e₂ : γ → δ} (de₁ : IsDenseInducing e₁) (de₂ : IsDenseInducing e₂) : IsDenseInducing (Prod.map e₁ e₂)

views.nl_informal: If the domain of a `IsDenseInducing` map is a separable space, then so is the codomain.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsDenseInducing.separableSpace [SeparableSpace α] (di : IsDenseInducing i) : SeparableSpace β

views.nl_informal: If the domain of a `IsDenseEmbedding` is a separable space, then so is its codomain.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsDenseEmbedding.separableSpace [SeparableSpace α] (de : IsDenseEmbedding e) : SeparableSpace β

views.nl_informal: The product of two dense embeddings is a dense embedding.

views.nl_informal: Two continuous functions to a t2-space that agree on the dense range of a function are equal.

a continuous surjection $\pi$ from a compact space $D$ to a Fréchet space $A$ restricts to
a compact subset $E$ of $D$, such that $\pi$ maps $E$ onto $A$ and satisfies the

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:
A set `s` is irreducible if and only if
for every finite collection of open sets all of whose members intersect `s`,
`s` also intersects the intersection of the entire collection

views.lean_signature: theorem isPreirreducible_iff_isClosed_union_isClosed : IsPreirreducible s ↔ ∀ z₁ z₂ : Set X, IsClosed z₁ → IsClosed z₂ → s ⊆ z₁ ∪ z₂ → s ⊆ z₁ ∨ s ⊆ z₂

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:
A set `s` is locally closed if one of the equivalent conditions below hold
1. It is the intersection of some open set and some closed set.
2. The coborder `(closure s \ s)ᶜ` is open.
3. `s` is closed in some neighborhood of `x` for all `x ∈ s`.
4. Every `x ∈ s` has some open neighborhood `U` such that `U ∩ closure s ⊆ s`.
5. `s` is open in the closure of `s`.

views.nl_informal:
Let `f : ℕ → Π a, β a` be a sequence of (dependent) functions on a topological space. Suppose
that the family of sets `s n = {x | f (n + 1) x ≠ f n x}` is locally finite. Then there exists a

views.nl_informal:
One step in the proof of the Tietze extension theorem. If `e : C(X, Y)` is a closed embedding
of a topological space into a normal topological space and `f : X →ᵇ ℝ` is a bounded continuous
function, then there exists a bounded continuous function `g : Y →ᵇ ℝ` of the norm `‖g‖ ≤ ‖f‖ / 3`
such that the distance between `g ∘ e` and `f` is at most `(2 / 3) * ‖f‖`.

embedding and bundled composition. If `e : C(X, Y)` is a closed embedding of a topological space

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:
**Tietze extension theorem** for real-valued bounded continuous maps, a version for a closed
embedding and a bounded continuous function that takes values in a non-trivial closed interval.
See also `exists_extension_forall_mem_of_isClosedEmbedding` for a more general statement that works
for any interval (finite or infinite, open or closed).

If `e : X → Y` is a closed embedding and `f : X →ᵇ ℝ` is a bounded continuous function such that
`f x ∈ [a, b]` for all `x`, where `a ≤ b`, then there exists a bounded continuous function
`g : Y →ᵇ ℝ` such that `g y ∈ [a, b]` for all `y` and `g ∘ e = f`.

views.nl_informal:
**Tietze extension theorem** for real-valued bounded continuous maps, a version for a closed
embedding. Let `e` be a closed embedding of a nonempty topological space `X` into a normal
topological space `Y`. Let `f` be a bounded continuous real-valued function on `X`. Then there

space `X`, with `s` compact and `t` closed, then there exists a continuous compactly supported

* `0 ≤ f x ≤ 1` for all `x`.

then `a + b` is topologically nilpotent.

views.nl_informal:

ring homomorphism is a completable topological field.

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:
In a linearly ordered group with zero element adjoined, `U` is a neighbourhood of `0` if and
only if there exists a nonzero element `γ₀` such that `Iio γ₀ ⊆ U`.

views.nl_informal:
If `γ` is an invertible element of a linearly ordered group with zero element adjoined, then
`Iio (γ : Γ₀)` is a neighbourhood of `0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem WithZeroTopology.nhds_zero_of_units (γ : Γ₀ˣ) : Iio ↑γ ∈ 𝓝 (0 : Γ₀)

views.nl_informal:
The neighbourhood filter of a nonzero element consists of all sets containing that
element.
views.lean_signature: theorem WithZeroTopology.nhds_of_ne_zero {γ : Γ₀} (h₀ : γ ≠ 0) : 𝓝 γ = pure γ

views.nl_informal:
The neighbourhood filter of an invertible element consists of all sets containing that
element.
views.lean_signature: theorem WithZeroTopology.nhds_coe_units (γ : Γ₀ˣ) : 𝓝 (γ : Γ₀) = pure (γ : Γ₀)

views.nl_informal:
If `γ` is an invertible element of a linearly ordered group with zero element adjoined, then
`{γ}` is a neighbourhood of `γ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem WithZeroTopology.singleton_mem_nhds_of_units (γ : Γ₀ˣ) : ({↑γ} : Set Γ₀) ∈ 𝓝 (γ : Γ₀)

views.nl_informal:
If `γ` is a nonzero element of a linearly ordered group with zero element adjoined, then `{γ}`
is a neighbourhood of `γ`.
views.lean_signature: theorem WithZeroTopology.singleton_mem_nhds_of_ne_zero (h : γ ≠ 0) : ({γ} : Set Γ₀) ∈ 𝓝 (γ : Γ₀)

views.nl_informal: Conjugation is jointly continuous on `G × G` when both `mul` and `inv` are continuous.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsTopologicalGroup.continuous_conj_prod [ContinuousInv G] : Continuous fun g : G × G => g.fst * g.snd * g.fst⁻¹

views.nl_informal:
Conjugation acting on fixed element of the group is continuous when both `mul` and
`inv` are continuous.

views.nl_informal:
A monoid homomorphism (a bundled morphism of a type that implements `MonoidHomClass`) from a
topological group to a topological monoid is continuous provided that it is continuous at one. See
also `uniformContinuous_of_continuousAt_one`.
views.lean_signature: theorem continuous_of_continuousAt_one {M hom : Type*} [MulOneClass M] [TopologicalSpace M] [ContinuousMul M] [FunLike hom G M] [MonoidHomClass hom G M] (f : hom) (hf : ContinuousAt f 1) : Continuous f

views.nl_informal:
Let `A` and `B` be topological groups, and let `φ : A → B` be a continuous surjective group
homomorphism. Assume furthermore that `φ` is a quotient map (i.e., `V ⊆ B`
is open iff `φ⁻¹ V` is open). Then `φ` is an open quotient map, and in particular an open map.
views.lean_signature: theorem MonoidHom.isOpenQuotientMap_of_isQuotientMap {A : Type*} [Group A] [TopologicalSpace A] [ContinuousMul A] {B : Type*} [Group B] [TopologicalSpace B] {F : Type*} [FunLike F A B] [MonoidHomClass F A B] {φ : F} (hφ : IsQuotientMap φ) : IsOpenQuotientMap φ

views.nl_informal:
Any first countable topological group has an antitone neighborhood basis `u : ℕ → Set G` for
which `(u (n + 1)) ^ 2 ⊆ u n`. The existence of such a neighborhood basis is a key tool for
`QuotientGroup.completeSpace`
views.lean_signature: theorem IsTopologicalGroup.exists_antitone_basis_nhds_one [FirstCountableTopology G] : ∃ u : ℕ → Set G, (𝓝 1).HasAntitoneBasis u ∧ ∀ n, u (n + 1) * u (n + 1) ⊆ u n

views.nl_informal:
A subgroup `S` of a topological group `G` acts on `G` properly discontinuously on the left, if
it is discrete in the sense that `S ∩ K` is finite for all compact `K`. (See also
`DiscreteTopology`.)
views.lean_signature: theorem Subgroup.properlyDiscontinuousSMul_of_tendsto_cofinite (S : Subgroup G) (hS : Tendsto S.subtype cofinite (cocompact G)) : ProperlyDiscontinuousSMul S G

views.nl_informal:
A subgroup `S` of a topological group `G` acts on `G` properly discontinuously on the right, if
it is discrete in the sense that `S ∩ K` is finite for all compact `K`. (See also
`DiscreteTopology`.)

If `G` is Hausdorff, this can be combined with `t2Space_of_properlyDiscontinuousSMul_of_t2Space`
to show that the quotient group `G ⧸ S` is Hausdorff.
views.lean_signature: theorem Subgroup.properlyDiscontinuousSMul_opposite_of_tendsto_cofinite (S : Subgroup G) (hS : Tendsto S.subtype cofinite (cocompact G)) : ProperlyDiscontinuousSMul S.op G

views.nl_informal:
Given a compact set `K` inside an open set `U`, there is an open neighborhood `V` of `1`
such that `K * V ⊆ U`.

views.nl_informal:
Given a compact set `K` inside an open set `U`, there is an open neighborhood `V` of `1`
such that `V * K ⊆ U`.
views.lean_signature: theorem compact_open_separated_mul_left {K U : Set G} (hK : IsCompact K) (hU : IsOpen U) (hKU : K ⊆ U) : ∃ V ∈ 𝓝 (1 : G), V * K ⊆ U

views.nl_informal:
A compact set is covered by finitely many left multiplicative translates of a set
with non-empty interior.
views.lean_signature: theorem compact_covered_by_mul_left_translates {K V : Set G} (hK : IsCompact K) (hV : (interior V).Nonempty) : ∃ t : Finset G, K ⊆ ⋃ g ∈ t, (g * ·) ⁻¹' V

views.nl_informal:
Given two compact sets in a noncompact topological group, there is a translate of the second
one that is disjoint from the first one.
views.lean_signature: theorem exists_disjoint_smul_of_isCompact [NoncompactSpace G] {K L : Set G} (hK : IsCompact K) (hL : IsCompact L) : ∃ g : G, Disjoint K (g • L)

views.nl_informal:
Every topological group in which there exists a compact set with nonempty interior
is locally compact.
views.lean_signature: theorem TopologicalSpace.PositiveCompacts.locallyCompactSpace_of_group (K : PositiveCompacts G) : LocallyCompactSpace G

views.nl_informal:
If a function converges to a value in a multiplicative topological group, then its inverse
converges to the inverse of this value.

assuming additionally that the limit is nonzero, use `Filter.Tendsto.inv₀`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.Tendsto.inv {f : α → G} {l : Filter α} {y : G} (h : Tendsto f l (𝓝 y)) : Tendsto (fun x => (f x)⁻¹) l (𝓝 y⁻¹)

views.nl_informal:
Consider a sigma-compact group acting continuously and transitively on a Baire space. Then
the orbit map is open around the identity. It follows in `isOpenMap_smul_of_sigmaCompact` that it
is open around any point.
views.lean_signature: theorem smul_singleton_mem_nhds_of_sigmaCompact {U : Set G} (hU : U ∈ 𝓝 1) (x : X) : U • {x} ∈ 𝓝 x

views.nl_informal:
Consider a sigma-compact group acting continuously and transitively on a Baire space. Then
the orbit map is open. This is a version of the open mapping theorem, valid notably for the
action of a sigma-compact locally compact group on a locally compact space.
views.lean_signature: theorem isOpenMap_smul_of_sigmaCompact (x : X) : IsOpenMap (fun (g : G) ↦ g • x)

views.nl_informal:
A surjective morphism of topological groups is open when the source group is sigma-compact and
the target group is a Baire space (for instance a locally compact group).
views.lean_signature: theorem MonoidHom.isOpenMap_of_sigmaCompact {H : Type*} [Group H] [TopologicalSpace H] [BaireSpace H] [T2Space H] [ContinuousMul H] (f : G →* H) (hf : Function.Surjective f) (h'f : Continuous f) : IsOpenMap f

views.nl_informal:
Given a neighborhood `U` of the identity, one may find a neighborhood `V` of the identity which
is closed, symmetric, and satisfies `V * V ⊆ U`.

views.nl_informal:
If a point in a topological group has a compact neighborhood, then the group is
locally compact.

views.nl_informal:
If a function defined on a topological group has a support contained in a
compact set, then either the function is trivial or the group is locally compact.

views.nl_informal:
If a function defined on a topological group has compact support, then either
the function is trivial or the group is locally compact.
views.lean_signature: theorem HasCompactSupport.eq_zero_or_locallyCompactSpace_of_group [TopologicalSpace α] [Zero α] [T1Space α] {f : G → α} (hf : HasCompactSupport f) (h'f : Continuous f) : f = 0 ∨ LocallyCompactSpace G

views.nl_informal: Constant one function has product `1`

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:

views.lean_signature: theorem tendsto_prod_nat_add [T2Space G] (f : ℕ → G) : Tendsto (fun i ↦ ∏' k, f (k + i)) atTop (𝓝 1)

views.nl_informal:
If `f₀, f₁, f₂, ...` and `g₀, g₁, g₂, ...` have products `a`, `b` respectively, then
the `ℤ`-indexed sequence: `..., g₂, g₁, g₀, f₀, f₁, f₂, ...` (with `f₀` at the `0`-th position) has
product `a + b`.
views.lean_signature: theorem HasProd.int_rec {f g : ℕ → M} (hf : HasProd f m) (hg : HasProd g m') : HasProd (Int.rec f g) (m * m')

views.nl_informal:
If `f₀, f₁, f₂, ...` and `g₀, g₁, g₂, ...` are both multipliable then so is the
`ℤ`-indexed sequence: `..., g₂, g₁, g₀, f₀, f₁, f₂, ...` (with `f₀` at the `0`-th position).
views.lean_signature: theorem Multipliable.int_rec {f g : ℕ → M} (hf : Multipliable f) (hg : Multipliable g) : Multipliable (Int.rec f g)

views.nl_informal:
If `f₀, f₁, f₂, ...` and `g₀, g₁, g₂, ...` are both multipliable, then the product of the
`ℤ`-indexed sequence: `..., g₂, g₁, g₀, f₀, f₁, f₂, ...` (with `f₀` at the `0`-th position) is
`(∏' n, f n) * ∏' n, g n`.
views.lean_signature: theorem tprod_int_rec [T2Space M] {f g : ℕ → M} (hf : Multipliable f) (hg : Multipliable g) : ∏' n : ℤ, Int.rec f g n = (∏' n : ℕ, f n) * ∏' n : ℕ, g n

views.nl_informal:
Let `G` be a nonarchimedean multiplicative abelian group, and let `f : α → G` be a function that
tends to one on the filter of cofinite sets. For each finite subset of `α`, consider the partial
product of `f` on that subset. These partial products form a Cauchy filter.
views.lean_signature: theorem NonarchimedeanGroup.cauchySeq_prod_of_tendsto_cofinite_one {f : α → G} (hf : Tendsto f cofinite (𝓝 1)) : CauchySeq (fun s ↦ ∏ i ∈ s, f i)

views.nl_informal:
Let `G` be a nonarchimedean abelian group, and let `f : ℕ → G` be a function
such that the quotients `f (n + 1) / f n` tend to one. Then the function is a Cauchy sequence.
views.lean_signature: theorem NonarchimedeanGroup.cauchySeq_of_tendsto_div_nhds_one {f : ℕ → G} (hf : Tendsto (fun n ↦ f (n + 1) / f n) atTop (𝓝 1)) : CauchySeq f

views.nl_informal:
Let `G` be a complete nonarchimedean multiplicative abelian group, and let `f : α → G` be a
function that tends to one on the filter of cofinite sets. Then `f` is unconditionally
multipliable.
views.lean_signature: theorem NonarchimedeanGroup.multipliable_of_tendsto_cofinite_one [CompleteSpace G] {f : α → G} (hf : Tendsto f cofinite (𝓝 1)) : Multipliable f

views.nl_informal:
Let `G` be a complete nonarchimedean multiplicative abelian group. Then a function `f : α → G`
is unconditionally multipliable if and only if it tends to one on the filter of cofinite sets.
views.lean_signature: theorem NonarchimedeanGroup.multipliable_iff_tendsto_cofinite_one [CompleteSpace G] (f : α → G) : Multipliable f ↔ Tendsto f cofinite (𝓝 1)

views.nl_informal:
Let `R` be a nonarchimedean ring, let `f : α → R` be a function that sums to `a : R`,
and let `g : β → R` be a function that sums to `b : R`. Then `fun i : α × β ↦ f i.1 * g i.2`
sums to `a * b`.
views.lean_signature: theorem HasSum.mul_of_nonarchimedean {f : α → R} {g : β → R} {a b : R} (hf : HasSum f a) (hg : HasSum g b) : HasSum (fun i : α × β ↦ f i.1 * g i.2) (a * b)

views.nl_informal:
Let `R` be a nonarchimedean ring. If functions `f : α → R` and `g : β → R` are summable, then
so is `fun i : α × β ↦ f i.1 * g i.2`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Summable.mul_of_nonarchimedean {f : α → R} {g : β → R} (hf : Summable f) (hg : Summable g) : Summable (fun i : α × β ↦ f i.1 * g i.2)

views.nl_informal:
If the distance between consecutive points of a sequence is estimated by a summable series,
then the original sequence is a Cauchy sequence.
views.lean_signature: theorem cauchySeq_of_dist_le_of_summable (d : ℕ → ℝ) (hf : ∀ n, dist (f n) (f n.succ) ≤ d n) (hd : Summable d) : CauchySeq f

views.nl_informal:
If a sequence `f` with non-negative terms is dominated by a sequence `g` with summable
series and at least one term of `f` is strictly smaller than the corresponding term in `g`,
then the series of `f` is strictly smaller than the series of `g`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Summable.tsum_lt_tsum_of_nonneg {i : ℕ} {f g : ℕ → ℝ} (h0 : ∀ b : ℕ, 0 ≤ f b) (h : ∀ b : ℕ, f b ≤ g b) (hi : f i < g i) (hg : Summable g) : ∑' n, f n < ∑' n, g n

views.nl_informal:
Product of two infinites sums indexed by arbitrary types.
See also `tsum_mul_tsum_of_summable_norm` if `f` and `g` are absolutely summable.
views.lean_signature: theorem Summable.tsum_mul_tsum (hf : Summable f) (hg : Summable g) (hfg : Summable fun x : ι × κ ↦ f x.1 * g x.2) : ((∑' x, f x) * ∑' y, g y) = ∑' z : ι × κ, f z.1 * g z.2

views.nl_informal:
The family `(k, l) : ℕ × ℕ ↦ f k * g l` is summable if and only if the family
`(n, k, l) : Σ (n : ℕ), antidiagonal n ↦ f k * g l` is summable.
views.lean_signature: theorem summable_mul_prod_iff_summable_mul_sigma_antidiagonal : (Summable fun x : A × A ↦ f x.1 * g x.2) ↔ Summable fun x : Σn : A, antidiagonal n ↦ f (x.2 : A × A).1 * g (x.2 : A × A).2

views.nl_informal:
The **Cauchy product formula** for the product of two infinites sums indexed by `ℕ`, expressed
by summing on `Finset.antidiagonal`.

See also `tsum_mul_tsum_eq_tsum_sum_antidiagonal_of_summable_norm` if `f` and `g` are absolutely
summable.
views.lean_signature: theorem Summable.tsum_mul_tsum_eq_tsum_sum_antidiagonal (hf : Summable f) (hg : Summable g) (hfg : Summable fun x : A × A ↦ f x.1 * g x.2) : ((∑' n, f n) * ∑' n, g n) = ∑' n, ∑ kl ∈ antidiagonal n, f kl.1 * g kl.2

views.nl_informal:
The **Cauchy product formula** for the product of two infinites sums indexed by `ℕ`, expressed
by summing on `Finset.range`.

See also `tsum_mul_tsum_eq_tsum_sum_range_of_summable_norm` if `f` and `g` are absolutely summable.
views.lean_signature: theorem Summable.tsum_mul_tsum_eq_tsum_sum_range (hf : Summable f) (hg : Summable g) (hfg : Summable fun x : ℕ × ℕ ↦ f x.1 * g x.2) : ((∑' n, f n) * ∑' n, g n) = ∑' n, ∑ k ∈ range (n + 1), f k * g (n - k)

views.nl_informal:
Bourbaki GT III.6.5 Theorem I:
ℤ-bilinear continuous maps from dense images into a complete Hausdorff group extend by continuity.
Note: Bourbaki assumes that α and β are also complete Hausdorff, but this is not necessary.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsDenseInducing.extend_Z_bilin : Continuous (extend (de.prodMap df) (fun p : β × δ => φ p.1 p.2))

views.nl_informal:
A group homomorphism (a bundled morphism of a type that implements `MonoidHomClass`) between
two uniform groups is uniformly continuous provided that it is continuous at one. See also
`continuous_of_continuousAt_one`.
views.lean_signature: theorem uniformContinuous_of_continuousAt_one {hom : Type*} [UniformSpace β] [Group β] [IsUniformGroup β] [FunLike hom α β] [MonoidHomClass hom α β] (f : hom) (hf : ContinuousAt f 1) : UniformContinuous f

views.nl_informal:
A homomorphism from a uniform group to a discrete uniform group is continuous if and only if
its kernel is open.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsUniformGroup.uniformContinuous_iff_isOpen_ker {hom : Type*} [UniformSpace β] [DiscreteTopology β] [Group β] [IsUniformGroup β] [FunLike hom α β] [MonoidHomClass hom α β] {f : hom} : UniformContinuous f ↔ IsOpen ((f : α →* β).ker : Set α)

views.nl_informal:
A topological module over a ring has continuous negation.

This cannot be an instance, because it would cause search for `[Module ?R M]` with unknown `R`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContinuousNeg.of_continuousConstSMul [ContinuousConstSMul R M] : ContinuousNeg M

views.nl_informal:
If `M` is a topological module over `R` and `0` is a limit of invertible elements of `R`, then
`⊤` is the only submodule of `M` with a nonempty interior.
This is the case, e.g., if `R` is a nontrivially normed field.
views.lean_signature: theorem Submodule.eq_top_of_nonempty_interior' [NeBot (𝓝[{ x : R | IsUnit x }] 0)] (s : Submodule R M) (hs : (interior (s : Set M)).Nonempty) : s = ⊤

views.nl_informal:
Let `R` be a topological ring such that zero is not an isolated point (e.g., a nontrivially
normed field, see `NormedField.punctured_nhds_neBot`). Let `M` be a nontrivial module over `R`
such that `c • x = 0` implies `c = 0 ∨ x = 0`. Then `M` has no isolated points. We formulate this
using `NeBot (𝓝[≠] x)`.

This lemma is not an instance because Lean would need to find `[ContinuousSMul ?m_1 M]` with
unknown `?m_1`. We register this as an instance for `R = ℝ` in `Real.punctured_nhds_module_neBot`.
One can also use `haveI := Module.punctured_nhds_neBot R M` in a proof.
views.lean_signature: theorem Module.punctured_nhds_neBot [Nontrivial M] [NeBot (𝓝[≠] (0 : R))] [NoZeroSMulDivisors R M] (x : M) : NeBot (𝓝[≠] x)

views.nl_informal: The span of a separable subset with respect to a separable scalar ring is again separable.
views.lean_signature: theorem TopologicalSpace.IsSeparable.span {R M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] [Semiring R] [Module R M] [TopologicalSpace M] [TopologicalSpace R] [SeparableSpace R] [ContinuousAdd M] [ContinuousSMul R M] {s : Set M} (hs : IsSeparable s) : IsSeparable (Submodule.span R s : Set M)

views.nl_informal: The topological closure of a closed submodule `s` is equal to `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsClosed.submodule_topologicalClosure_eq {s : Submodule R M} (hs : IsClosed (s : Set M)) : s.topologicalClosure = s

views.nl_informal: A subspace is dense iff its topological closure is the entire space.
views.lean_signature: theorem Submodule.dense_iff_topologicalClosure_eq_top {s : Submodule R M} : Dense (s : Set M) ↔ s.topologicalClosure = ⊤

views.nl_informal:
A maximal proper subspace of a topological module (i.e a `Submodule` satisfying `IsCoatom`)
is either closed or dense.
views.lean_signature: theorem Submodule.isClosed_or_dense_of_isCoatom (s : Submodule R M) (hs : IsCoatom s) : IsClosed (s : Set M) ∨ Dense (s : Set M)

views.nl_informal:
If `s i` is a family of submodules, each is in its module,
then the closure of their span in the indexed product of the modules
is the product of their closures.

In case of a finite index type, this statement immediately follows from `Submodule.iSup_map_single`.
However, the statement is true for an infinite index type as well.
views.lean_signature: theorem Submodule.closure_coe_iSup_map_single (s : ∀ i, Submodule R (M i)) : closure (↑(⨆ i, (s i).map (LinearMap.single R M i)) : Set (∀ i, M i)) = Set.univ.pi fun i ↦ closure (s i)

views.nl_informal:
If `s i` is a family of submodules, each is in its module,
then the closure of their span in the indexed product of the modules
is the product of their closures.

In case of a finite index type, this statement immediately follows from `Submodule.iSup_map_single`.
However, the statement is true for an infinite index type as well.

This version is stated in terms of `Submodule.topologicalClosure`,
thus assumes that `M i`s are topological modules over `R`.
However, the statement is true without assuming continuity of the operations,
see `Submodule.closure_coe_iSup_map_single` above.
views.lean_signature: theorem Submodule.topologicalClosure_iSup_map_single [∀ i, ContinuousAdd (M i)] [∀ i, ContinuousConstSMul R (M i)] (s : ∀ i, Submodule R (M i)) : topologicalClosure (⨆ i, (s i).map (LinearMap.single R M i)) = pi Set.univ fun i ↦ (s i).topologicalClosure

views.nl_informal: A complete nontrivially normed field has cardinality at least continuum.
views.lean_signature: theorem continuum_le_cardinal_of_nontriviallyNormedField (𝕜 : Type*) [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [CompleteSpace 𝕜] : 𝔠 ≤ #𝕜

views.nl_informal:
A nontrivial module over a complete nontrivially normed field has cardinality at least
continuum.
views.lean_signature: theorem continuum_le_cardinal_of_module (𝕜 : Type u) (E : Type v) [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [CompleteSpace 𝕜] [AddCommGroup E] [Module 𝕜 E] [Nontrivial E] : 𝔠 ≤ #E

views.nl_informal:
In a topological vector space over a nontrivially normed field, any neighborhood of zero has
the same cardinality as the whole space.

See also `cardinal_eq_of_mem_nhds`.
views.lean_signature: theorem cardinal_eq_of_mem_nhds_zero {E : Type*} (𝕜 : Type*) [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [Zero E] [MulActionWithZero 𝕜 E] [TopologicalSpace E] [ContinuousSMul 𝕜 E] {s : Set E} (hs : s ∈ 𝓝 (0 : E)) : #s = #E

views.nl_informal:
In a topological vector space over a nontrivially normed field, any neighborhood of a point has
the same cardinality as the whole space.
views.lean_signature: theorem cardinal_eq_of_mem_nhds {E : Type*} (𝕜 : Type*) [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [AddGroup E] [MulActionWithZero 𝕜 E] [TopologicalSpace E] [ContinuousAdd E] [ContinuousSMul 𝕜 E] {s : Set E} {x : E} (hs : s ∈ 𝓝 x) : #s = #E

views.nl_informal:
In a topological vector space over a nontrivially normed field, any nonempty open set has
the same cardinality as the whole space.
views.lean_signature: theorem cardinal_eq_of_isOpen {E : Type*} (𝕜 : Type*) [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [AddGroup E] [MulActionWithZero 𝕜 E] [TopologicalSpace E] [ContinuousAdd E] [ContinuousSMul 𝕜 E] {s : Set E} (hs : IsOpen s) (h's : s.Nonempty) : #s = #E

views.nl_informal:
In a nontrivial topological vector space over a complete nontrivially normed field, any nonempty
open set has cardinality at least continuum.
views.lean_signature: theorem continuum_le_cardinal_of_isOpen {E : Type*} (𝕜 : Type*) [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [CompleteSpace 𝕜] [AddCommGroup E] [Module 𝕜 E] [Nontrivial E] [TopologicalSpace E] [ContinuousAdd E] [ContinuousSMul 𝕜 E] {s : Set E} (hs : IsOpen s) (h's : s.Nonempty) : 𝔠 ≤ #s

views.nl_informal:
In a nontrivial topological vector space over a complete nontrivially normed field, any
countable set has dense complement.
views.lean_signature: theorem Set.Countable.dense_compl {E : Type u} (𝕜 : Type*) [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [CompleteSpace 𝕜] [AddCommGroup E] [Module 𝕜 E] [Nontrivial E] [TopologicalSpace E] [ContinuousAdd E] [ContinuousSMul 𝕜 E] {s : Set E} (hs : s.Countable) : Dense sᶜ

views.nl_informal: The `characterSpace 𝕜 A` along with `0` is always a closed set in `WeakDual 𝕜 A`.
views.lean_signature: theorem WeakDual.CharacterSpace.union_zero_isClosed [T2Space 𝕜] [ContinuousMul 𝕜] : IsClosed (characterSpace 𝕜 A ∪ {0})

views.nl_informal:
under suitable mild assumptions on `𝕜`, the character space is a closed set in
`WeakDual 𝕜 A`.
views.lean_signature: theorem WeakDual.CharacterSpace.isClosed [Nontrivial 𝕜] [T2Space 𝕜] [ContinuousMul 𝕜] : IsClosed (characterSpace 𝕜 A)

views.nl_informal: The inverse of `equivOfInverse'` is obtained by swapping the order of its parameters.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContinuousLinearEquiv.symm_equivOfInverse' (f₁ : M₁ →SL[σ₁₂] M₂) (f₂ h₁ h₂) : (equivOfInverse' f₁ f₂ h₁ h₂).symm = equivOfInverse' f₂ f₁ h₂ h₁

views.nl_informal: By definition, if `f` is invertible then `inverse f = f.symm`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContinuousLinearMap.inverse_equiv (e : M ≃L[R] M₂) : inverse (e : M →L[R] M₂) = e.symm

views.nl_informal: By definition, if `f` is not invertible then `inverse f = 0`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContinuousLinearMap.inverse_of_not_isInvertible {f : M →L[R] M₂} (hf : ¬ f.IsInvertible) : f.inverse = 0

views.nl_informal:
The function `ContinuousLinearEquiv.inverse` can be written in terms of `Ring.inverse` for the
ring of self-maps of the domain.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContinuousLinearMap.inverse_eq_ringInverse (e : M ≃L[R] M₂) (f : M →L[R] M₂) : inverse f = Ring.inverse ((e.symm : M₂ →L[R] M).comp f) ∘L e.symm

views.nl_informal:
If `p` is a closed complemented submodule,
then there exists a submodule `q` and a continuous linear equivalence `M ≃L[R] (p × q)` such that
`e (x : p) = (x, 0)`, `e (y : q) = (0, y)`, and `e.symm x = x.1 + x.2`.

In fact, the properties of `e` imply the properties of `e.symm` and vice versa,
but we provide both for convenience.
views.lean_signature: theorem Submodule.ClosedComplemented.exists_submodule_equiv_prod [IsTopologicalAddGroup M] {p : Submodule R M} (hp : p.ClosedComplemented) : ∃ (q : Submodule R M) (e : M ≃L[R] (p × q)), (∀ x : p, e x = (x, 0)) ∧ (∀ y : q, e y = (0, y)) ∧ (∀ x, e.symm x = x.1 + x.2)

views.nl_informal:
If `𝕜` is a nontrivially normed field, any T2 topology on `𝕜` which makes it a topological
vector space over itself (with the norm topology) is *equal* to the norm topology.
views.lean_signature: theorem unique_topology_of_t2 {t : TopologicalSpace 𝕜} (h₁ : @IsTopologicalAddGroup 𝕜 t _) (h₂ : @ContinuousSMul 𝕜 𝕜 _ hnorm.toUniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace t) (h₃ : @T2Space 𝕜 t) : t = hnorm.toUniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace

views.nl_informal:
Any linear form on a topological vector space over a nontrivially normed field is continuous if
its kernel is closed.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.continuous_of_isClosed_ker (l : E →ₗ[𝕜] 𝕜) (hl : IsClosed (LinearMap.ker l : Set E)) : Continuous l

views.nl_informal:
Any linear form on a topological vector space over a nontrivially normed field is continuous if
and only if its kernel is closed.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.continuous_iff_isClosed_ker (l : E →ₗ[𝕜] 𝕜) : Continuous l ↔ IsClosed (LinearMap.ker l : Set E)

views.nl_informal:
Over a nontrivially normed field, any linear form which is nonzero on a nonempty open set is
automatically continuous.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.continuous_of_nonzero_on_open (l : E →ₗ[𝕜] 𝕜) (s : Set E) (hs₁ : IsOpen s) (hs₂ : s.Nonempty) (hs₃ : ∀ x ∈ s, l x ≠ 0) : Continuous l

views.nl_informal: Any linear map on a finite dimensional space over a complete field is continuous.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.continuous_of_finiteDimensional [T2Space E] [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 E] (f : E →ₗ[𝕜] F') : Continuous f

views.nl_informal:
In finite dimensions over a non-discrete complete normed field, the canonical identification
(in terms of a basis) with `𝕜^n` (endowed with the product topology) is continuous.
This is the key fact which makes all linear maps from a T2 finite dimensional TVS over such a field
continuous (see `LinearMap.continuous_of_finiteDimensional`), which in turn implies that all
norms are equivalent in finite dimensions.
views.lean_signature: theorem continuous_equivFun_basis [T2Space E] {ι : Type*} [Finite ι] (ξ : Basis ι 𝕜 E) : Continuous ξ.equivFun

views.nl_informal: A surjective linear map `f` with finite dimensional codomain is an open map.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.isOpenMap_of_finiteDimensional (f : F →ₗ[𝕜] E) (hf : Function.Surjective f) : IsOpenMap f

views.nl_informal:
Two finite-dimensional topological vector spaces over a complete normed field are continuously
linearly equivalent if they have the same (finite) dimension.
views.lean_signature: theorem FiniteDimensional.nonempty_continuousLinearEquiv_of_finrank_eq (cond : finrank 𝕜 E = finrank 𝕜 F) : Nonempty (E ≃L[𝕜] F)

views.nl_informal:
Two finite-dimensional topological vector spaces over a complete normed field are continuously
linearly equivalent if and only if they have the same (finite) dimension.
views.lean_signature: theorem FiniteDimensional.nonempty_continuousLinearEquiv_iff_finrank_eq : Nonempty (E ≃L[𝕜] F) ↔ finrank 𝕜 E = finrank 𝕜 F

views.nl_informal: A finite-dimensional subspace is complete.
views.lean_signature: theorem Submodule.complete_of_finiteDimensional (s : Submodule 𝕜 E) [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 s] : IsComplete (s : Set E)

views.nl_informal: A finite-dimensional subspace is closed.
views.lean_signature: theorem Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional [T2Space E] (s : Submodule 𝕜 E) [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 s] : IsClosed (s : Set E)

views.nl_informal: An injective linear map with finite-dimensional domain is a closed embedding.
views.lean_signature: theorem LinearMap.isClosedEmbedding_of_injective [T2Space E] [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 E] {f : E →ₗ[𝕜] F} (hf : LinearMap.ker f = ⊥) : IsClosedEmbedding f

views.nl_informal:
If two continuous linear maps are equal on a set `s`, then they are equal on the closure
of the `Submodule.span` of this set.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContinuousLinearMap.eqOn_closure_span [T2Space M₂] {s : Set M₁} {f g : M₁ →SL[σ₁₂] M₂} (h : Set.EqOn f g s) : Set.EqOn f g (closure (Submodule.span R₁ s : Set M₁))

views.nl_informal:
If the submodule generated by a set `s` is dense in the ambient module, then two continuous
linear maps equal on `s` are equal.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContinuousLinearMap.ext_on [T2Space M₂] {s : Set M₁} (hs : Dense (Submodule.span R₁ s : Set M₁)) {f g : M₁ →SL[σ₁₂] M₂} (h : Set.EqOn f g s) : f = g

views.nl_informal:
Under a continuous linear map, the image of the `TopologicalClosure` of a submodule is
contained in the `TopologicalClosure` of its image.
views.lean_signature: theorem Submodule.topologicalClosure_map [RingHomSurjective σ₁₂] [TopologicalSpace R₁] [TopologicalSpace R₂] [ContinuousSMul R₁ M₁] [ContinuousAdd M₁] [ContinuousSMul R₂ M₂] [ContinuousAdd M₂] (f : M₁ →SL[σ₁₂] M₂) (s : Submodule R₁ M₁) : s.topologicalClosure.map (f : M₁ →ₛₗ[σ₁₂] M₂) ≤ (s.map (f : M₁ →ₛₗ[σ₁₂] M₂)).topologicalClosure

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal:
Given an open subgroup `U` and an element `r` of a nonarchimedean ring, there is an open
subgroup `V` such that `r • V` is contained in `U`.
views.lean_signature: theorem NonarchimedeanRing.left_mul_subset (U : OpenAddSubgroup R) (r : R) : ∃ V : OpenAddSubgroup R, r • (V : Set R) ⊆ U

views.nl_informal: An open subgroup of a nonarchimedean ring contains the square of another one.
views.lean_signature: theorem NonarchimedeanRing.mul_subset (U : OpenAddSubgroup R) : ∃ V : OpenAddSubgroup R, (V : Set R) * V ⊆ U

views.nl_informal: Rational numbers are dense in a linear ordered archimedean field.
views.lean_signature: theorem Rat.denseRange_cast {𝕜} [Field 𝕜] [LinearOrder 𝕜] [IsStrictOrderedRing 𝕜] [TopologicalSpace 𝕜] [OrderTopology 𝕜] [Archimedean 𝕜] : DenseRange ((↑) : ℚ → 𝕜)

views.nl_informal:
A subgroup of an archimedean linear ordered multiplicative commutative group with order
topology is dense provided that for all `ε > 1` there exists an element of the subgroup
that belongs to `(1, ε)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Subgroup.dense_of_not_isolated_one (S : Subgroup G) (hS : ∀ ε > 1, ∃ g ∈ S, g ∈ Ioo 1 ε) : Dense (S : Set G)

views.nl_informal:
Let `S` be a nontrivial subgroup in an archimedean linear ordered multiplicative commutative
group `G` with order topology. If the set of elements of `S` that are greater than one
 does not have a minimal element, then `S` is dense `G`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Subgroup.dense_of_no_min (S : Subgroup G) (hbot : S ≠ ⊥) (H : ¬∃ a : G, IsLeast { g : G | g ∈ S ∧ 1 < g } a) : Dense (S : Set G)

views.nl_informal:
A subgroup of an archimedean linear ordered multiplicative commutative group `G` with order
topology either is dense in `G` or is a cyclic subgroup.
views.lean_signature: theorem Subgroup.dense_or_cyclic (S : Subgroup G) : Dense (S : Set G) ∨ ∃ a : G, S = closure {a}

views.nl_informal:
In a nontrivial densely linear ordered archimedean topological multiplicative group,
a subgroup is either dense or is cyclic, but not both.

For a non-exclusive `Or` version with weaker assumptions,
see `Subgroup.dense_or_cyclic` above.
views.lean_signature: theorem Subgroup.dense_xor'_cyclic (s : Subgroup G) : Xor' (Dense (s : Set G)) (∃ a, s = .zpowers a)

views.nl_informal:
If a (possibly non-unital and/or non-associative) ring `R` admits a submultiplicative
nonnegative norm `norm : R → 𝕜`, where `𝕜` is a linear ordered field, and the open balls
`{ x | norm x < ε }`, `ε > 0`, form a basis of neighborhoods of zero, then `R` is a topological
ring.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsTopologicalRing.of_norm {R 𝕜 : Type*} [NonUnitalNonAssocRing R] [Field 𝕜] [LinearOrder 𝕜] [IsStrictOrderedRing 𝕜] [TopologicalSpace R] [IsTopologicalAddGroup R] (norm : R → 𝕜) (norm_nonneg : ∀ x, 0 ≤ norm x) (norm_mul_le : ∀ x y, norm (x * y) ≤ norm x * norm y) (nhds_basis : (𝓝 (0 : R)).HasBasis ((0 : 𝕜) < ·) (fun ε ↦ { x | norm x < ε })) : IsTopologicalRing R

views.nl_informal:

views.nl_informal: The function `x ↦ x⁻¹` tends to `+∞` on the right of `0`.

views.nl_informal: The function `r ↦ r⁻¹` tends to `0` on the right as `r → +∞`.
views.lean_signature: theorem tendsto_inv_atTop_nhdsGT_zero : Tendsto (fun r : 𝕜 => r⁻¹) atTop (𝓝[>] (0 : 𝕜))

views.nl_informal:
If `g` tends to zero and there exists a constant `C : 𝕜` such that eventually `|f x| ≤ C`,
then the product `f * g` tends to zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem bdd_le_mul_tendsto_zero' {f g : α → 𝕜} (C : 𝕜) (hf : ∀ᶠ x in l, |f x| ≤ C) (hg : Tendsto g l (𝓝 0)) : Tendsto (fun x ↦ f x * g x) l (𝓝 0)

views.nl_informal:
If `g` tends to zero and there exist constants `b B : 𝕜` such that eventually `b ≤ f x| ≤ B`,
then the product `f * g` tends to zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem bdd_le_mul_tendsto_zero {f g : α → 𝕜} {b B : 𝕜} (hb : ∀ᶠ x in l, b ≤ f x) (hB : ∀ᶠ x in l, f x ≤ B) (hg : Tendsto g l (𝓝 0)) : Tendsto (fun x ↦ f x * g x) l (𝓝 0)

views.nl_informal:
If `g` tends to `atTop` and there exist constants `b B : 𝕜` such that eventually
`b ≤ f x| ≤ B`, then the quotient `f / g` tends to zero.
views.lean_signature: theorem tendsto_bdd_div_atTop_nhds_zero {f g : α → 𝕜} {b B : 𝕜} (hb : ∀ᶠ x in l, b ≤ f x) (hB : ∀ᶠ x in l, f x ≤ B) (hg : Tendsto g l atTop) : Tendsto (fun x => f x / g x) l (𝓝 0)

views.nl_informal:
The function `x^(-n)` tends to `0` at `+∞` for any positive natural `n`.
A version for positive real powers exists as `tendsto_rpow_neg_atTop`.
views.lean_signature: theorem tendsto_pow_neg_atTop {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : Tendsto (fun x : 𝕜 => x ^ (-(n : ℤ))) atTop (𝓝 0)

views.nl_informal:
In a linearly ordered multiplicative group, the integer powers of an element are dense
iff they are the whole group.
views.lean_signature: theorem denseRange_zpow_iff_surjective {a : G} : DenseRange (a ^ · : ℤ → G) ↔ Surjective (a ^ · : ℤ → G)

views.nl_informal:
In a nontrivial densely linearly ordered commutative group,
the integer powers of an element can't be dense.
views.lean_signature: theorem not_denseRange_zpow [Nontrivial G] [DenselyOrdered G] {a : G} : ¬DenseRange (a ^ · : ℤ → G)

views.nl_informal:
If the liminf and the limsup of a filter coincide, then this filter converges to
their common value, at least if the filter is eventually bounded above and below.
views.lean_signature: theorem le_nhds_of_limsSup_eq_limsInf {f : Filter α} {a : α} (hl : f.IsBounded (· ≤ ·)) (hg : f.IsBounded (· ≥ ·)) (hs : f.limsSup = a) (hi : f.limsInf = a) : f ≤ 𝓝 a

views.nl_informal: If a filter is converging, its limsup coincides with its limit.
views.lean_signature: theorem limsInf_eq_of_le_nhds {f : Filter α} {a : α} [NeBot f] (h : f ≤ 𝓝 a) : f.limsInf = a

views.nl_informal: If a filter is converging, its liminf coincides with its limit.
views.lean_signature: theorem limsSup_eq_of_le_nhds {f : Filter α} {a : α} [NeBot f] (h : f ≤ 𝓝 a) : f.limsSup = a

views.nl_informal: If a function has a limit, then its limsup coincides with its limit.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.Tendsto.limsup_eq {f : Filter β} {u : β → α} {a : α} [NeBot f] (h : Tendsto u f (𝓝 a)) : limsup u f = a

views.nl_informal: If a function has a limit, then its liminf coincides with its limit.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.Tendsto.liminf_eq {f : Filter β} {u : β → α} {a : α} [NeBot f] (h : Tendsto u f (𝓝 a)) : liminf u f = a

views.nl_informal:
If the liminf and the limsup of a function coincide, then the limit of the function
exists and has the same value.
views.lean_signature: theorem tendsto_of_liminf_eq_limsup {f : Filter β} {u : β → α} {a : α} (hinf : liminf u f = a) (hsup : limsup u f = a) (h : f.IsBoundedUnder (· ≤ ·) u := by isBoundedDefault) (h' : f.IsBoundedUnder (· ≥ ·) u := by isBoundedDefault) : Tendsto u f (𝓝 a)

views.nl_informal:
If a number `a` is less than or equal to the `liminf` of a function `f` at some filter
and is greater than or equal to the `limsup` of `f`, then `f` tends to `a` along this filter.
views.lean_signature: theorem tendsto_of_le_liminf_of_limsup_le {f : Filter β} {u : β → α} {a : α} (hinf : a ≤ liminf u f) (hsup : limsup u f ≤ a) (h : f.IsBoundedUnder (· ≤ ·) u := by isBoundedDefault) (h' : f.IsBoundedUnder (· ≥ ·) u := by isBoundedDefault) : Tendsto u f (𝓝 a)

views.nl_informal:
Assume that, for any `a < b`, a sequence can not be infinitely many times below `a` and
above `b`. If it is also ultimately bounded above and below, then it has to converge. This even
works if `a` and `b` are restricted to a dense subset.
views.lean_signature: theorem tendsto_of_no_upcrossings [DenselyOrdered α] {f : Filter β} {u : β → α} {s : Set α} (hs : Dense s) (H : ∀ a ∈ s, ∀ b ∈ s, a < b → ¬((∃ᶠ n in f, u n < a) ∧ ∃ᶠ n in f, b < u n)) (h : f.IsBoundedUnder (· ≤ ·) u := by isBoundedDefault) (h' : f.IsBoundedUnder (· ≥ ·) u := by isBoundedDefault) : ∃ c : α, Tendsto u f (𝓝 c)

views.nl_informal:
A group `G` acts properly on a topological space `X` if and only if for all ultrafilters
`𝒰` on `X × G`, if `𝒰` converges to `(x₁, x₂)` along the map `(g, x) ↦ (g • x, x)`,
then there exists `g : G` such that `g • x₂ = x₁` and `𝒰.fst` converges to `g`.
views.lean_signature: theorem properSMul_iff_continuousSMul_ultrafilter_tendsto : ProperSMul G X ↔ ContinuousSMul G X ∧ (∀ 𝒰 : Ultrafilter (G × X), ∀ x₁ x₂ : X, Tendsto (fun gx : G × X ↦ (gx.1 • gx.2, gx.2)) 𝒰 (𝓝 (x₁, x₂)) → ∃ g : G, g • x₂ = x₁ ∧ Tendsto (Prod.fst : G × X → G) 𝒰 (𝓝 g))

views.nl_informal:
A group `G` acts properly on a T2 topological space `X` if and only if for all ultrafilters
`𝒰` on `X × G`, if `𝒰` converges to `(x₁, x₂)` along the map `(g, x) ↦ (g • x, x)`,
then there exists `g : G` such that `𝒰.fst` converges to `g`.
views.lean_signature: theorem properSMul_iff_continuousSMul_ultrafilter_tendsto_t2 [T2Space X] : ProperSMul G X ↔ ContinuousSMul G X ∧ (∀ 𝒰 : Ultrafilter (G × X), ∀ x₁ x₂ : X, Tendsto (fun gx : G × X ↦ (gx.1 • gx.2, gx.2)) 𝒰 (𝓝 (x₁, x₂)) → ∃ g : G, Tendsto (Prod.fst : G × X → G) 𝒰 (𝓝 g))

views.nl_informal: If `G` acts properly on `X`, then the quotient space is Hausdorff (T2).
views.lean_signature: theorem t2Space_quotient_mulAction_of_properSMul [ProperSMul G X] : T2Space (Quotient (MulAction.orbitRel G X))

views.nl_informal: If a T1 group acts properly on a topological space, then this topological space is T2.
views.lean_signature: theorem t2Space_of_properSMul_of_t1Group [h_proper : ProperSMul G X] [T1Space G] : T2Space X

views.nl_informal:
If two groups `H` and `G` act on a topological space `X` such that `G` acts properly and
there exists a group homomorphims `H → G` which is a closed embedding compatible with the actions,
then `H` also acts properly on `X`.

X ⟶ Z

views.nl_informal:

cannot be generalized from `T2Space` to `T1Space`.

Let `α = OnePoint ℕ` be the one-point compactification of `ℕ`, and let `β` be the same space

`id : α → β` is a continuous equivalence that is not a homeomorphism.

views.nl_informal:

If `s : Set (X × Y)` belongs to `l ×ˢ 𝓝 y` for all `y` from a compact set `K`,

views.nl_informal:
Let `X` be a locally compact sigma compact Hausdorff topological space, let `s` be a closed set
in `X`. Suppose that for each `x ∈ s` the sets `B x : ι x → Set X` with the predicate
`p x : ι x → Prop` form a basis of the filter `𝓝 x`. Then there exists a locally finite covering
`fun i ↦ B (c i) (r i)` of `s` such that all “centers” `c i` belong to `s` and each `r i` satisfies
`p (c i)`.

The notation is inspired by the case `B x r = Metric.ball x r` but the theorem applies to
`nhds_basis_opens` as well. If the covering must be subordinate to some open covering of `s`, then
the user should use a basis obtained by `Filter.HasBasis.restrict_subset` or a similar lemma, see
the proof of `paracompact_of_locallyCompact_sigmaCompact` for an example.

The formalization is based on two [ncatlab](https://ncatlab.org/) proofs:
* [locally compact and sigma compact spaces are paracompact](https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/locally+compact+and+sigma-compact+spaces+are+paracompact);
* [open cover of smooth manifold admits locally finite refinement by closed balls](https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/partition+of+unity#ExistenceOnSmoothManifolds).

See also `refinement_of_locallyCompact_sigmaCompact_of_nhds_basis` for a version of this lemma
dealing with a covering of the whole space.

In most cases (namely, if `B c r ∪ B c r'` is again a set of the form `B c r''`) it is possible
to choose `α = X`. This fact is not yet formalized in `mathlib`.
views.lean_signature: theorem refinement_of_locallyCompact_sigmaCompact_of_nhds_basis_set [WeaklyLocallyCompactSpace X] [SigmaCompactSpace X] [T2Space X] {ι : X → Type u} {p : ∀ x, ι x → Prop} {B : ∀ x, ι x → Set X} {s : Set X} (hs : IsClosed s) (hB : ∀ x ∈ s, (𝓝 x).HasBasis (p x) (B x)) : ∃ (α : Type v) (c : α → X) (r : ∀ a, ι (c a)), (∀ a, c a ∈ s ∧ p (c a) (r a)) ∧ (s ⊆ ⋃ a, B (c a) (r a)) ∧ LocallyFinite fun a ↦ B (c a) (r a)
