views.lean_signature: theorem UniformEquicontinuous.uniformContinuous {F : ι → β → α} (h : UniformEquicontinuous F) (i : ι) : UniformContinuous (F i)

views.nl_informal: Each function of a family uniformly equicontinuous on `S` is uniformly continuous on `S`.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformEquicontinuousOn.uniformContinuousOn {F : ι → β → α} {S : Set β} (h : UniformEquicontinuousOn F S) (i : ι) : UniformContinuousOn (F i) S

views.nl_informal: Taking sub-families preserves equicontinuity at a point.
views.lean_signature: theorem EquicontinuousAt.comp {F : ι → X → α} {x₀ : X} (h : EquicontinuousAt F x₀) (u : κ → ι) : EquicontinuousAt (F ∘ u) x₀

views.nl_informal: Taking sub-families preserves equicontinuity at a point within a subset.
views.lean_signature: theorem EquicontinuousWithinAt.comp {F : ι → X → α} {S : Set X} {x₀ : X} (h : EquicontinuousWithinAt F S x₀) (u : κ → ι) : EquicontinuousWithinAt (F ∘ u) S x₀

views.nl_informal: Taking sub-families preserves equicontinuity.
views.lean_signature: theorem Equicontinuous.comp {F : ι → X → α} (h : Equicontinuous F) (u : κ → ι) : Equicontinuous (F ∘ u)

views.nl_informal: Taking sub-families preserves equicontinuity on a subset.
views.lean_signature: theorem EquicontinuousOn.comp {F : ι → X → α} {S : Set X} (h : EquicontinuousOn F S) (u : κ → ι) : EquicontinuousOn (F ∘ u) S

views.nl_informal: Taking sub-families preserves uniform equicontinuity.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformEquicontinuous.comp {F : ι → β → α} (h : UniformEquicontinuous F) (u : κ → ι) : UniformEquicontinuous (F ∘ u)

views.nl_informal: Taking sub-families preserves uniform equicontinuity on a subset.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformEquicontinuousOn.comp {F : ι → β → α} {S : Set β} (h : UniformEquicontinuousOn F S) (u : κ → ι) : UniformEquicontinuousOn (F ∘ u) S

views.nl_informal:
A family `𝓕 : ι → X → α` is equicontinuous at `x₀` iff `range 𝓕` is equicontinuous at `x₀`,
i.e the family `(↑) : range F → X → α` is equicontinuous at `x₀`.
views.lean_signature: theorem equicontinuousAt_iff_range {F : ι → X → α} {x₀ : X} : EquicontinuousAt F x₀ ↔ EquicontinuousAt ((↑) : range F → X → α) x₀

views.nl_informal:
A family `𝓕 : ι → X → α` is equicontinuous at `x₀` within `S` iff `range 𝓕` is equicontinuous
at `x₀` within `S`, i.e the family `(↑) : range F → X → α` is equicontinuous at `x₀` within `S`.
views.lean_signature: theorem equicontinuousWithinAt_iff_range {F : ι → X → α} {S : Set X} {x₀ : X} : EquicontinuousWithinAt F S x₀ ↔ EquicontinuousWithinAt ((↑) : range F → X → α) S x₀

views.nl_informal:
A family `𝓕 : ι → X → α` is equicontinuous iff `range 𝓕` is equicontinuous,
i.e the family `(↑) : range F → X → α` is equicontinuous.
views.lean_signature: theorem equicontinuous_iff_range {F : ι → X → α} : Equicontinuous F ↔ Equicontinuous ((↑) : range F → X → α)

views.nl_informal:
A family `𝓕 : ι → X → α` is equicontinuous on `S` iff `range 𝓕` is equicontinuous on `S`,
i.e the family `(↑) : range F → X → α` is equicontinuous on `S`.
views.lean_signature: theorem equicontinuousOn_iff_range {F : ι → X → α} {S : Set X} : EquicontinuousOn F S ↔ EquicontinuousOn ((↑) : range F → X → α) S

views.nl_informal:
A family `𝓕 : ι → β → α` is uniformly equicontinuous iff `range 𝓕` is uniformly equicontinuous,
i.e the family `(↑) : range F → β → α` is uniformly equicontinuous.
views.lean_signature: theorem uniformEquicontinuous_iff_range {F : ι → β → α} : UniformEquicontinuous F ↔ UniformEquicontinuous ((↑) : range F → β → α)

views.nl_informal:
A family `𝓕 : ι → β → α` is uniformly equicontinuous on `S` iff `range 𝓕` is uniformly
equicontinuous on `S`, i.e the family `(↑) : range F → β → α` is uniformly equicontinuous on `S`.
views.lean_signature: theorem uniformEquicontinuousOn_iff_range {F : ι → β → α} {S : Set β} : UniformEquicontinuousOn F S ↔ UniformEquicontinuousOn ((↑) : range F → β → α) S

views.nl_informal:
A family `𝓕 : ι → X → α` is equicontinuous at `x₀` iff the function `swap 𝓕 : X → ι → α` is
continuous at `x₀` *when `ι → α` is equipped with the topology of uniform convergence*. This is
very useful for developing the equicontinuity API, but it should not be used directly for other
purposes.
views.lean_signature: theorem equicontinuousAt_iff_continuousAt {F : ι → X → α} {x₀ : X} : EquicontinuousAt F x₀ ↔ ContinuousAt (ofFun ∘ Function.swap F : X → ι →ᵤ α) x₀

views.nl_informal:
A family `𝓕 : ι → X → α` is equicontinuous at `x₀` within `S` iff the function
`swap 𝓕 : X → ι → α` is continuous at `x₀` within `S`
*when `ι → α` is equipped with the topology of uniform convergence*. This is very useful for
developing the equicontinuity API, but it should not be used directly for other purposes.
views.lean_signature: theorem equicontinuousWithinAt_iff_continuousWithinAt {F : ι → X → α} {S : Set X} {x₀ : X} : EquicontinuousWithinAt F S x₀ ↔ ContinuousWithinAt (ofFun ∘ Function.swap F : X → ι →ᵤ α) S x₀

views.nl_informal:
A family `𝓕 : ι → X → α` is equicontinuous iff the function `swap 𝓕 : X → ι → α` is
continuous *when `ι → α` is equipped with the topology of uniform convergence*. This is
very useful for developing the equicontinuity API, but it should not be used directly for other
purposes.
views.lean_signature: theorem equicontinuous_iff_continuous {F : ι → X → α} : Equicontinuous F ↔ Continuous (ofFun ∘ Function.swap F : X → ι →ᵤ α)

views.nl_informal:
A family `𝓕 : ι → X → α` is equicontinuous on `S` iff the function `swap 𝓕 : X → ι → α` is
continuous on `S` *when `ι → α` is equipped with the topology of uniform convergence*. This is
very useful for developing the equicontinuity API, but it should not be used directly for other
purposes.
views.lean_signature: theorem equicontinuousOn_iff_continuousOn {F : ι → X → α} {S : Set X} : EquicontinuousOn F S ↔ ContinuousOn (ofFun ∘ Function.swap F : X → ι →ᵤ α) S

views.nl_informal:
A family `𝓕 : ι → β → α` is uniformly equicontinuous iff the function `swap 𝓕 : β → ι → α` is
uniformly continuous *when `ι → α` is equipped with the uniform structure of uniform convergence*.
This is very useful for developing the equicontinuity API, but it should not be used directly
for other purposes.
views.lean_signature: theorem uniformEquicontinuous_iff_uniformContinuous {F : ι → β → α} : UniformEquicontinuous F ↔ UniformContinuous (ofFun ∘ Function.swap F : β → ι →ᵤ α)

views.nl_informal:
A family `𝓕 : ι → β → α` is uniformly equicontinuous on `S` iff the function
`swap 𝓕 : β → ι → α` is uniformly continuous on `S`
*when `ι → α` is equipped with the uniform structure of uniform convergence*. This is very useful
for developing the equicontinuity API, but it should not be used directly for other purposes.
views.lean_signature: theorem uniformEquicontinuousOn_iff_uniformContinuousOn {F : ι → β → α} {S : Set β} : UniformEquicontinuousOn F S ↔ UniformContinuousOn (ofFun ∘ Function.swap F : β → ι →ᵤ α) S

views.nl_informal:
Given `u : α → β` a uniform inducing map, a family `𝓕 : ι → X → α` is equicontinuous at a point
`x₀ : X` iff the family `𝓕'`, obtained by composing each function of `𝓕` by `u`, is
equicontinuous at `x₀`.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsUniformInducing.equicontinuousAt_iff {F : ι → X → α} {x₀ : X} {u : α → β} (hu : IsUniformInducing u) : EquicontinuousAt F x₀ ↔ EquicontinuousAt ((u ∘ ·) ∘ F) x₀

views.nl_informal:
Given `u : α → β` a uniform inducing map, a family `𝓕 : ι → X → α` is equicontinuous at a point
`x₀ : X` within a subset `S : Set X` iff the family `𝓕'`, obtained by composing each function
of `𝓕` by `u`, is equicontinuous at `x₀` within `S`.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsUniformInducing.equicontinuousWithinAt_iff {F : ι → X → α} {S : Set X} {x₀ : X} {u : α → β} (hu : IsUniformInducing u) : EquicontinuousWithinAt F S x₀ ↔ EquicontinuousWithinAt ((u ∘ ·) ∘ F) S x₀

views.nl_informal:
Given `u : α → β` a uniform inducing map, a family `𝓕 : ι → X → α` is equicontinuous iff the
family `𝓕'`, obtained by composing each function of `𝓕` by `u`, is equicontinuous.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsUniformInducing.equicontinuous_iff {F : ι → X → α} {u : α → β} (hu : IsUniformInducing u) : Equicontinuous F ↔ Equicontinuous ((u ∘ ·) ∘ F)

views.nl_informal:
Given `u : α → β` a uniform inducing map, a family `𝓕 : ι → X → α` is equicontinuous on a
subset `S : Set X` iff the family `𝓕'`, obtained by composing each function of `𝓕` by `u`, is
equicontinuous on `S`.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsUniformInducing.equicontinuousOn_iff {F : ι → X → α} {S : Set X} {u : α → β} (hu : IsUniformInducing u) : EquicontinuousOn F S ↔ EquicontinuousOn ((u ∘ ·) ∘ F) S

views.nl_informal:
Given `u : α → γ` a uniform inducing map, a family `𝓕 : ι → β → α` is uniformly equicontinuous
iff the family `𝓕'`, obtained by composing each function of `𝓕` by `u`, is uniformly
equicontinuous.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsUniformInducing.uniformEquicontinuous_iff {F : ι → β → α} {u : α → γ} (hu : IsUniformInducing u) : UniformEquicontinuous F ↔ UniformEquicontinuous ((u ∘ ·) ∘ F)

views.nl_informal:
Given `u : α → γ` a uniform inducing map, a family `𝓕 : ι → β → α` is uniformly equicontinuous
on a subset `S : Set β` iff the family `𝓕'`, obtained by composing each function of `𝓕` by `u`,
is uniformly equicontinuous on `S`.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsUniformInducing.uniformEquicontinuousOn_iff {F : ι → β → α} {S : Set β} {u : α → γ} (hu : IsUniformInducing u) : UniformEquicontinuousOn F S ↔ UniformEquicontinuousOn ((u ∘ ·) ∘ F) S

views.nl_informal:
If a set of functions is equicontinuous at some `x₀` within a set `S`, the same is true for its
closure in *any* topology for which evaluation at any `x ∈ S ∪ {x₀}` is continuous. Since
this will be applied to `DFunLike` types, we state it for any topological space with a map
to `X → α` satisfying the right continuity conditions. See also `Set.EquicontinuousWithinAt.closure`
for a more familiar (but weaker) statement.

Note: This could *technically* be called `EquicontinuousWithinAt.closure` without name clashes
with `Set.EquicontinuousWithinAt.closure`, but we don't do it because, even with a `protected`
marker, it would introduce ambiguities while working in namespace `Set` (e.g, in the proof of
any theorem called `Set.something`).
views.lean_signature: theorem EquicontinuousWithinAt.closure' {A : Set Y} {u : Y → X → α} {S : Set X} {x₀ : X} (hA : EquicontinuousWithinAt (u ∘ (↑) : A → X → α) S x₀) (hu₁ : Continuous (S.restrict ∘ u)) (hu₂ : Continuous (eval x₀ ∘ u)) : EquicontinuousWithinAt (u ∘ (↑) : closure A → X → α) S x₀

views.nl_informal:
If a set of functions is equicontinuous at some `x₀`, the same is true for its closure in *any*
topology for which evaluation at any point is continuous. Since this will be applied to
`DFunLike` types, we state it for any topological space with a map to `X → α` satisfying the right
continuity conditions. See also `Set.EquicontinuousAt.closure` for a more familiar statement.
views.lean_signature: theorem EquicontinuousAt.closure' {A : Set Y} {u : Y → X → α} {x₀ : X} (hA : EquicontinuousAt (u ∘ (↑) : A → X → α) x₀) (hu : Continuous u) : EquicontinuousAt (u ∘ (↑) : closure A → X → α) x₀

views.nl_informal:
If a set of functions is equicontinuous at some `x₀`, its closure for the product topology is
also equicontinuous at `x₀`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Set.EquicontinuousAt.closure {A : Set (X → α)} {x₀ : X} (hA : A.EquicontinuousAt x₀) : (closure A).EquicontinuousAt x₀

views.nl_informal:
If a set of functions is equicontinuous at some `x₀` within a set `S`, its closure for the
product topology is also equicontinuous at `x₀` within `S`. This would also be true for the coarser
topology of pointwise convergence on `S ∪ {x₀}`, see `Set.EquicontinuousWithinAt.closure'`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Set.EquicontinuousWithinAt.closure {A : Set (X → α)} {S : Set X} {x₀ : X} (hA : A.EquicontinuousWithinAt S x₀) : (closure A).EquicontinuousWithinAt S x₀

views.nl_informal:
If a set of functions is equicontinuous, the same is true for its closure in *any*
topology for which evaluation at any point is continuous. Since this will be applied to
`DFunLike` types, we state it for any topological space with a map to `X → α` satisfying the right
continuity conditions. See also `Set.Equicontinuous.closure` for a more familiar statement.
views.lean_signature: theorem Equicontinuous.closure' {A : Set Y} {u : Y → X → α} (hA : Equicontinuous (u ∘ (↑) : A → X → α)) (hu : Continuous u) : Equicontinuous (u ∘ (↑) : closure A → X → α)

views.nl_informal:
If a set of functions is equicontinuous on a set `S`, the same is true for its closure in *any*
topology for which evaluation at any `x ∈ S` is continuous. Since this will be applied to
`DFunLike` types, we state it for any topological space with a map to `X → α` satisfying the right
continuity conditions. See also `Set.EquicontinuousOn.closure` for a more familiar
(but weaker) statement.
views.lean_signature: theorem EquicontinuousOn.closure' {A : Set Y} {u : Y → X → α} {S : Set X} (hA : EquicontinuousOn (u ∘ (↑) : A → X → α) S) (hu : Continuous (S.restrict ∘ u)) : EquicontinuousOn (u ∘ (↑) : closure A → X → α) S

views.nl_informal:
If a set of functions is equicontinuous, its closure for the product topology is also
equicontinuous.
views.lean_signature: theorem Set.Equicontinuous.closure {A : Set <| X → α} (hA : A.Equicontinuous) : (closure A).Equicontinuous

views.nl_informal:
If a set of functions is equicontinuous, its closure for the product topology is also
equicontinuous. This would also be true for the coarser topology of pointwise convergence on `S`,
see `EquicontinuousOn.closure'`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Set.EquicontinuousOn.closure {A : Set <| X → α} {S : Set X} (hA : A.EquicontinuousOn S) : (closure A).EquicontinuousOn S

views.nl_informal:
If a set of functions is uniformly equicontinuous on a set `S`, the same is true for its
closure in *any* topology for which evaluation at any `x ∈ S` i continuous. Since this will be
applied to `DFunLike` types, we state it for any topological space with a map to `β → α` satisfying
the right continuity conditions. See also `Set.UniformEquicontinuousOn.closure` for a more familiar
(but weaker) statement.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformEquicontinuousOn.closure' {A : Set Y} {u : Y → β → α} {S : Set β} (hA : UniformEquicontinuousOn (u ∘ (↑) : A → β → α) S) (hu : Continuous (S.restrict ∘ u)) : UniformEquicontinuousOn (u ∘ (↑) : closure A → β → α) S

views.nl_informal:
If a set of functions is uniformly equicontinuous, the same is true for its closure in *any*
topology for which evaluation at any point is continuous. Since this will be applied to
`DFunLike` types, we state it for any topological space with a map to `β → α` satisfying the right
continuity conditions. See also `Set.UniformEquicontinuous.closure` for a more familiar statement.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformEquicontinuous.closure' {A : Set Y} {u : Y → β → α} (hA : UniformEquicontinuous (u ∘ (↑) : A → β → α)) (hu : Continuous u) : UniformEquicontinuous (u ∘ (↑) : closure A → β → α)

views.nl_informal:
If a set of functions is uniformly equicontinuous, its closure for the product topology is also
uniformly equicontinuous.
views.lean_signature: theorem Set.UniformEquicontinuous.closure {A : Set <| β → α} (hA : A.UniformEquicontinuous) : (closure A).UniformEquicontinuous

views.nl_informal:
If a set of functions is uniformly equicontinuous on a set `S`, its closure for the product
topology is also uniformly equicontinuous. This would also be true for the coarser topology of
pointwise convergence on `S`, see `UniformEquicontinuousOn.closure'`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Set.UniformEquicontinuousOn.closure {A : Set <| β → α} {S : Set β} (hA : A.UniformEquicontinuousOn S) : (closure A).UniformEquicontinuousOn S

views.nl_informal:
If `𝓕 : ι → X → α` tends to `f : X → α` *pointwise on `S ∪ {x₀} : Set X`* along some nontrivial
filter, and if the family `𝓕` is equicontinuous at `x₀ : X` within `S`, then the limit is
continuous at `x₀` within `S`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.Tendsto.continuousWithinAt_of_equicontinuousWithinAt {l : Filter ι} [l.NeBot] {F : ι → X → α} {f : X → α} {S : Set X} {x₀ : X} (h₁ : ∀ x ∈ S, Tendsto (F · x) l (𝓝 (f x))) (h₂ : Tendsto (F · x₀) l (𝓝 (f x₀))) (h₃ : EquicontinuousWithinAt F S x₀) : ContinuousWithinAt f S x₀

views.nl_informal:
If `𝓕 : ι → X → α` tends to `f : X → α` *pointwise* along some nontrivial filter, and if the
family `𝓕` is equicontinuous at some `x₀ : X`, then the limit is continuous at `x₀`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.Tendsto.continuousAt_of_equicontinuousAt {l : Filter ι} [l.NeBot] {F : ι → X → α} {f : X → α} {x₀ : X} (h₁ : Tendsto F l (𝓝 f)) (h₂ : EquicontinuousAt F x₀) : ContinuousAt f x₀

views.nl_informal:
If `𝓕 : ι → X → α` tends to `f : X → α` *pointwise* along some nontrivial filter, and if the
family `𝓕` is equicontinuous, then the limit is continuous.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.Tendsto.continuous_of_equicontinuous {l : Filter ι} [l.NeBot] {F : ι → X → α} {f : X → α} (h₁ : Tendsto F l (𝓝 f)) (h₂ : Equicontinuous F) : Continuous f

views.nl_informal:
If `𝓕 : ι → X → α` tends to `f : X → α` *pointwise on `S : Set X`* along some nontrivial
filter, and if the family `𝓕` is equicontinuous, then the limit is continuous on `S`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.Tendsto.continuousOn_of_equicontinuousOn {l : Filter ι} [l.NeBot] {F : ι → X → α} {f : X → α} {S : Set X} (h₁ : ∀ x ∈ S, Tendsto (F · x) l (𝓝 (f x))) (h₂ : EquicontinuousOn F S) : ContinuousOn f S

views.nl_informal:
If `𝓕 : ι → β → α` tends to `f : β → α` *pointwise on `S : Set β`* along some nontrivial
filter, and if the family `𝓕` is uniformly equicontinuous on `S`, then the limit is uniformly
continuous on `S`.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.Tendsto.uniformContinuousOn_of_uniformEquicontinuousOn {l : Filter ι} [l.NeBot] {F : ι → β → α} {f : β → α} {S : Set β} (h₁ : ∀ x ∈ S, Tendsto (F · x) l (𝓝 (f x))) (h₂ : UniformEquicontinuousOn F S) : UniformContinuousOn f S

views.nl_informal:
If `𝓕 : ι → β → α` tends to `f : β → α` *pointwise* along some nontrivial filter, and if the
family `𝓕` is uniformly equicontinuous, then the limit is uniformly continuous.
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.Tendsto.uniformContinuous_of_uniformEquicontinuous {l : Filter ι} [l.NeBot] {F : ι → β → α} {f : β → α} (h₁ : Tendsto F l (𝓝 f)) (h₂ : UniformEquicontinuous F) : UniformContinuous f

views.nl_informal:
If `F : ι → X → α` is a family of functions equicontinuous at `x`,
it tends to `f y` along a filter `l` for any `y ∈ s`,
the limit function `f` tends to `z` along `𝓝[s] x`, and `x ∈ closure s`,
then `(F · x)` tends to `z` along `l`.

In some sense, this is a converse of `EquicontinuousAt.closure`.
views.lean_signature: theorem EquicontinuousAt.tendsto_of_mem_closure {l : Filter ι} {F : ι → X → α} {f : X → α} {s : Set X} {x : X} {z : α} (hF : EquicontinuousAt F x) (hf : Tendsto f (𝓝[s] x) (𝓝 z)) (hs : ∀ y ∈ s, Tendsto (F · y) l (𝓝 (f y))) (hx : x ∈ closure s) : Tendsto (F · x) l (𝓝 z)

views.nl_informal:
If `F : ι → X → α` is an equicontinuous family of functions,
`f : X → α` is a continuous function, and `l` is a filter on `ι`,
then `{x | Filter.Tendsto (F · x) l (𝓝 (f x))}` is a closed set.
views.lean_signature: theorem Equicontinuous.isClosed_setOf_tendsto {l : Filter ι} {F : ι → X → α} {f : X → α} (hF : Equicontinuous F) (hf : Continuous f) : IsClosed {x | Tendsto (F · x) l (𝓝 (f x))}

views.nl_informal:
Heine-Cantor: a continuous function on a compact uniform space is uniformly
continuous.
views.lean_signature: theorem CompactSpace.uniformContinuous_of_continuous [CompactSpace α] {f : α → β} (h : Continuous f) : UniformContinuous f

views.nl_informal:
Heine-Cantor: a continuous function on a compact set of a uniform space is uniformly
continuous.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsCompact.uniformContinuousOn_of_continuous {s : Set α} {f : α → β} (hs : IsCompact s) (hf : ContinuousOn f s) : UniformContinuousOn f s

views.nl_informal:
If `s` is compact and `f` is continuous at all points of `s`, then `f` is
"uniformly continuous at the set `s`", i.e. `f x` is close to `f y` whenever `x ∈ s` and `y` is
close to `x` (even if `y` is not itself in `s`, so this is a stronger assertion than
`UniformContinuousOn s`).
views.lean_signature: theorem IsCompact.uniformContinuousAt_of_continuousAt {r : Set (β × β)} {s : Set α} (hs : IsCompact s) (f : α → β) (hf : ∀ a ∈ s, ContinuousAt f a) (hr : r ∈ 𝓤 β) : { x : α × α | x.1 ∈ s → (f x.1, f x.2) ∈ r } ∈ 𝓤 α

views.nl_informal:
A family of functions `α → β → γ` tends uniformly to its value at `x` if `α` is locally compact,
`β` is compact and `f` is continuous on `U × (univ : Set β)` for some neighborhood `U` of `x`.

views.nl_informal:
A continuous family of functions `α → β → γ` tends uniformly to its value at `x`
if `α` is weakly locally compact and `β` is compact.
views.lean_signature: theorem Continuous.tendstoUniformly [WeaklyLocallyCompactSpace α] [CompactSpace β] [UniformSpace γ] (f : α → β → γ) (h : Continuous ↿f) (x : α) : TendstoUniformly f (f x) (𝓝 x)

views.nl_informal:
In a product space `α × β`, assume that a function `f` is continuous on `s × k` where `k` is
compact. Then, along the fiber above any `q ∈ s`, `f` is transversely uniformly continuous, i.e.,
if `p ∈ s` is close enough to `q`, then `f p x` is uniformly close to `f q x` for all `x ∈ k`.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsCompact.mem_uniformity_of_prod {α β E : Type*} [TopologicalSpace α] [TopologicalSpace β] [UniformSpace E] {f : α → β → E} {s : Set α} {k : Set β} {q : α} {u : Set (E × E)} (hk : IsCompact k) (hf : ContinuousOn f.uncurry (s ×ˢ k)) (hq : q ∈ s) (hu : u ∈ 𝓤 E) : ∃ v ∈ 𝓝[s] q, ∀ p ∈ v, ∀ x ∈ k, (f p x, f q x) ∈ u

views.nl_informal:
An equicontinuous family of functions defined on a compact uniform space is automatically
uniformly equicontinuous.
views.lean_signature: theorem CompactSpace.uniformEquicontinuous_of_equicontinuous {ι : Type*} {F : ι → β → α} [CompactSpace β] (h : Equicontinuous F) : UniformEquicontinuous F

views.nl_informal: On a compact space, locally uniform convergence is just uniform convergence.
views.lean_signature: theorem tendstoLocallyUniformly_iff_tendstoUniformly_of_compactSpace [CompactSpace α] : TendstoLocallyUniformly F f p ↔ TendstoUniformly F f p

views.nl_informal: For a compact set `s`, locally uniform convergence on `s` is just uniform convergence on `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn_iff_tendstoUniformlyOn_of_compact (hs : IsCompact s) : TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn F f p s ↔ TendstoUniformlyOn F f p s

views.nl_informal:
A continuous function on `X × Y`, taking values in an `R`-module with a uniform structure,
can be uniformly approximated by sums of functions of the form `(x, y) ↦ f x • g y`.

Note that no continuity properties are assumed either for multiplication on `R`, or for the scalar
multiplication of `R` on `V`.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContinuousMap.exists_finite_sum_smul_approximation_of_mem_uniformity [TopologicalSpace R] [MonoidWithZero R] [MulActionWithZero R V] (f : C(X × Y, V)) (hS : S ∈ 𝓤 V) : ∃ (n : ℕ) (g : Fin n → C(X, R)) (h : Fin n → C(Y, V)), ∀ x y, (f (x, y), ∑ i, g i x • h i y) ∈ S

views.nl_informal:
A continuous function on `X × Y`, taking values in a ring `R` equipped with a uniformity
compatible with addition, can be uniformly approximated by sums of functions of the form
`(x, y) ↦ f x * g y`.

Note that no assumption is needed relating the multiplication on `R` to the uniformity.

A function which can be locally uniformly approximated by functions which are continuous at

views.nl_informal:
A function which can be locally uniformly approximated by functions which are continuous

views.nl_informal:
A function which can be uniformly approximated by functions which are continuous on a set
is continuous on this set.

views.nl_informal: A function which can be locally uniformly approximated by continuous functions is continuous.
views.lean_signature: theorem continuous_of_locally_uniform_approx_of_continuousAt (L : ∀ x : α, ∀ u ∈ 𝓤 β, ∃ t ∈ 𝓝 x, ∃ F, ContinuousAt F x ∧ ∀ y ∈ t, (f y, F y) ∈ u) : Continuous f

views.nl_informal: A function which can be uniformly approximated by continuous functions is continuous.
views.lean_signature: theorem continuous_of_uniform_approx_of_continuous (L : ∀ u ∈ 𝓤 β, ∃ F, Continuous F ∧ ∀ y, (f y, F y) ∈ u) : Continuous f

A locally uniform limit on a set of functions which are continuous on this set is itself
continuous on this set.
views.lean_signature: theorem TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn.continuousOn (h : TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn F f p s) (hc : ∀ᶠ n in p, ContinuousOn (F n) s) [NeBot p] : ContinuousOn f s

A uniform limit on a set of functions which are continuous on this set is itself continuous

views.lean_signature: theorem TendstoLocallyUniformly.continuous (h : TendstoLocallyUniformly F f p) (hc : ∀ᶠ n in p, Continuous (F n)) [NeBot p] : Continuous f

views.nl_informal:
If `Fₙ` converges locally uniformly on a neighborhood of `x` within a set `s` to a function `f`
which is continuous at `x` within `s`, and `gₙ` tends to `x` within `s`, then `Fₙ (gₙ)` tends
to `f x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem tendsto_comp_of_locally_uniform_limit_within (h : ContinuousWithinAt f s x) (hg : Tendsto g p (𝓝[s] x)) (hunif : ∀ u ∈ 𝓤 β, ∃ t ∈ 𝓝[s] x, ∀ᶠ n in p, ∀ y ∈ t, (f y, F n y) ∈ u) : Tendsto (fun n => F n (g n)) p (𝓝 (f x))

views.nl_informal:
If `Fₙ` converges locally uniformly on a neighborhood of `x` to a function `f` which is
continuous at `x`, and `gₙ` tends to `x`, then `Fₙ (gₙ)` tends to `f x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem tendsto_comp_of_locally_uniform_limit (h : ContinuousAt f x) (hg : Tendsto g p (𝓝 x)) (hunif : ∀ u ∈ 𝓤 β, ∃ t ∈ 𝓝 x, ∀ᶠ n in p, ∀ y ∈ t, (f y, F n y) ∈ u) : Tendsto (fun n => F n (g n)) p (𝓝 (f x))

views.nl_informal:
If `Fₙ` tends locally uniformly to `f` on a set `s`, and `gₙ` tends to `x` within `s`, then
`Fₙ gₙ` tends to `f x` if `f` is continuous at `x` within `s` and `x ∈ s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn.tendsto_comp (h : TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn F f p s) (hf : ContinuousWithinAt f s x) (hx : x ∈ s) (hg : Tendsto g p (𝓝[s] x)) : Tendsto (fun n => F n (g n)) p (𝓝 (f x))

views.nl_informal:
If `Fₙ` tends uniformly to `f` on a set `s`, and `gₙ` tends to `x` within `s`, then `Fₙ gₙ`
tends to `f x` if `f` is continuous at `x` within `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem TendstoUniformlyOn.tendsto_comp (h : TendstoUniformlyOn F f p s) (hf : ContinuousWithinAt f s x) (hg : Tendsto g p (𝓝[s] x)) : Tendsto (fun n => F n (g n)) p (𝓝 (f x))

views.nl_informal: If `Fₙ` tends locally uniformly to `f`, and `gₙ` tends to `x`, then `Fₙ gₙ` tends to `f x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem TendstoLocallyUniformly.tendsto_comp (h : TendstoLocallyUniformly F f p) (hf : ContinuousAt f x) (hg : Tendsto g p (𝓝 x)) : Tendsto (fun n => F n (g n)) p (𝓝 (f x))

views.nl_informal: If `Fₙ` tends uniformly to `f`, and `gₙ` tends to `x`, then `Fₙ gₙ` tends to `f x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem TendstoUniformly.tendsto_comp (h : TendstoUniformly F f p) (hf : ContinuousAt f x) (hg : Tendsto g p (𝓝 x)) : Tendsto (fun n => F n (g n)) p (𝓝 (f x))

views.nl_informal:
A sequence of functions `Fₙ` converges uniformly on a filter `p'` to a limiting function `f` w.r.t.
filter `p` iff the function `(n, x) ↦ (f x, Fₙ x)` converges along `p ×ˢ p'` to the uniformity.
In other words: one knows nothing about the behavior of `x` in this limit besides it being in `p'`.
views.lean_signature: theorem tendstoUniformlyOnFilter_iff_tendsto : TendstoUniformlyOnFilter F f p p' ↔ Tendsto (fun q : ι × α => (f q.2, F q.1 q.2)) (p ×ˢ p') (𝓤 β)

views.nl_informal:
A sequence of functions `Fₙ` converges uniformly on a set `s` to a limiting function `f` w.r.t.
filter `p` iff the function `(n, x) ↦ (f x, Fₙ x)` converges along `p ×ˢ 𝓟 s` to the uniformity.
In other words: one knows nothing about the behavior of `x` in this limit besides it being in `s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem tendstoUniformlyOn_iff_tendsto : TendstoUniformlyOn F f p s ↔ Tendsto (fun q : ι × α => (f q.2, F q.1 q.2)) (p ×ˢ 𝓟 s) (𝓤 β)

views.nl_informal:
A sequence of functions `Fₙ` converges uniformly to a limiting function `f` w.r.t.
filter `p` iff the function `(n, x) ↦ (f x, Fₙ x)` converges along `p ×ˢ ⊤` to the uniformity.
In other words: one knows nothing about the behavior of `x` in this limit.
views.lean_signature: theorem tendstoUniformly_iff_tendsto : TendstoUniformly F f p ↔ Tendsto (fun q : ι × α => (f q.2, F q.1 q.2)) (p ×ˢ ⊤) (𝓤 β)

views.nl_informal: Uniform convergence implies pointwise convergence.
views.lean_signature: theorem TendstoUniformlyOnFilter.tendsto_at (h : TendstoUniformlyOnFilter F f p p') (hx : 𝓟 {x} ≤ p') : Tendsto (fun n => F n x) p <| 𝓝 (f x)

views.nl_informal: Uniform convergence implies pointwise convergence.
views.lean_signature: theorem TendstoUniformlyOn.tendsto_at (h : TendstoUniformlyOn F f p s) (hx : x ∈ s) : Tendsto (fun n => F n x) p <| 𝓝 (f x)

views.nl_informal: Uniform convergence implies pointwise convergence.
views.lean_signature: theorem TendstoUniformly.tendsto_at (h : TendstoUniformly F f p) (x : α) : Tendsto (fun n => F n x) p <| 𝓝 (f x)

views.nl_informal: Composing on the right by a function preserves uniform convergence
views.lean_signature: theorem TendstoUniformly.comp (h : TendstoUniformly F f p) (g : γ → α) : TendstoUniformly (fun n => F n ∘ g) (f ∘ g) p

views.nl_informal:
Composing on the left by a uniformly continuous function preserves

views.lean_signature: theorem UniformContinuous.comp_tendstoUniformlyOnFilter [UniformSpace γ] {g : β → γ} (hg : UniformContinuous g) (h : TendstoUniformlyOnFilter F f p p') : TendstoUniformlyOnFilter (fun i => g ∘ F i) (g ∘ f) p p'

Composing on the left by a uniformly continuous function preserves
uniform convergence on a set

views.nl_informal:
Uniform convergence on a filter `p'` to a constant function is equivalent to convergence in
`p ×ˢ p'`.
views.lean_signature: theorem tendsto_prod_filter_iff {c : β} : Tendsto (↿F) (p ×ˢ p') (𝓝 c) ↔ TendstoUniformlyOnFilter F (fun _ => c) p p'

views.nl_informal:
Uniform convergence on a set `s` to a constant function is equivalent to convergence in
`p ×ˢ 𝓟 s`.
views.lean_signature: theorem tendsto_prod_principal_iff {c : β} : Tendsto (↿F) (p ×ˢ 𝓟 s) (𝓝 c) ↔ TendstoUniformlyOn F (fun _ => c) p s

views.nl_informal: Uniform convergence to a constant function is equivalent to convergence in `p ×ˢ ⊤`.
views.lean_signature: theorem tendsto_prod_top_iff {c : β} : Tendsto (↿F) (p ×ˢ ⊤) (𝓝 c) ↔ TendstoUniformly F (fun _ => c) p

views.nl_informal: Uniform convergence on the empty set is vacuously true
views.lean_signature: theorem tendstoUniformlyOn_empty : TendstoUniformlyOn F f p ∅

views.nl_informal: Uniform convergence on a singleton is equivalent to regular convergence
views.lean_signature: theorem tendstoUniformlyOn_singleton_iff_tendsto : TendstoUniformlyOn F f p {x} ↔ Tendsto (fun n : ι => F n x) p (𝓝 (f x))

views.nl_informal:
If a sequence `g` converges to some `b`, then the sequence of constant functions

views.nl_informal:
If a sequence `g` converges to some `b`, then the sequence of constant functions
`fun n ↦ fun a ↦ g n` converges to the constant function `fun a ↦ b` on any set `s`
views.lean_signature: theorem Filter.Tendsto.tendstoUniformlyOn_const {g : ι → β} {b : β} (hg : Tendsto g p (𝓝 b)) (s : Set α) : TendstoUniformlyOn (fun n : ι => fun _ : α => g n) (fun _ : α => b) p s

views.lean_signature: theorem TendstoUniformlyOnFilter.uniformCauchySeqOnFilter (hF : TendstoUniformlyOnFilter F f p p') : UniformCauchySeqOnFilter F p p'

views.nl_informal: A sequence that converges uniformly is also uniformly Cauchy
views.lean_signature: theorem TendstoUniformlyOn.uniformCauchySeqOn (hF : TendstoUniformlyOn F f p s) : UniformCauchySeqOn F p s

views.lean_signature: theorem UniformCauchySeqOnFilter.comp {γ : Type*} (hf : UniformCauchySeqOnFilter F p p') (g : γ → α) : UniformCauchySeqOnFilter (fun n => F n ∘ g) p (p'.comap g)

views.nl_informal: Composing on the right by a function preserves uniform Cauchy sequences
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformCauchySeqOn.comp {γ : Type*} (hf : UniformCauchySeqOn F p s) (g : γ → α) : UniformCauchySeqOn (fun n => F n ∘ g) p (g ⁻¹' s)

Composing on the left by a uniformly continuous function preserves
uniform Cauchy sequences

views.nl_informal:
If a sequence of functions is uniformly Cauchy on a set, then the values at each point form
a Cauchy sequence.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformCauchySeqOn.cauchy_map [hp : NeBot p] (hf : UniformCauchySeqOn F p s) (hx : x ∈ s) : Cauchy (map (fun i => F i x) p)

views.nl_informal:
If a sequence of functions is uniformly Cauchy on a set, then the values at each point form
a Cauchy sequence.  See `UniformCauchSeqOn.cauchy_map` for the non-`atTop` case.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformCauchySeqOn.cauchySeq [Nonempty ι] [SemilatticeSup ι] (hf : UniformCauchySeqOn F atTop s) (hx : x ∈ s) : CauchySeq fun i ↦ F i x

views.nl_informal:
If `𝓕` is a filter on `β × β`, then the set of all `UniformFun.gen α β V` for
`V ∈ 𝓕` is a filter basis on `(α →ᵤ β) × (α →ᵤ β)`. This will only be applied to `𝓕 = 𝓤 β` when
`β` is equipped with a `UniformSpace` structure, but it is useful to define it for any filter in
order to be able to state that it has a lower adjoint (see `UniformFun.gc`).
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformFun.isBasis_gen (𝓑 : Filter <| β × β) : IsBasis (fun V : Set (β × β) => V ∈ 𝓑) (UniformFun.gen α β)

views.nl_informal:
The function `UniformFun.filter α β : Filter (β × β) → Filter ((α →ᵤ β) × (α →ᵤ β))`
has a lower adjoint `l` (in the sense of `GaloisConnection`). The exact definition of `l` is not
interesting; we will only use that it exists (in `UniformFun.mono` and
`UniformFun.iInf_eq`) and that
`l (Filter.map (Prod.map f f) 𝓕) = Filter.map (Prod.map ((∘) f) ((∘) f)) (l 𝓕)` for each
`𝓕 : Filter (γ × γ)` and `f : γ → α` (in `UniformFun.comap_eq`).
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformFun.gc : GaloisConnection lowerAdjoint fun 𝓕 => UniformFun.filter α β 𝓕

views.nl_informal:
By definition, the uniformity of `α →ᵤ β` admits the family `{(f, g) | ∀ x, (f x, g x) ∈ V}`
for `V ∈ 𝓤 β` as a filter basis.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformFun.hasBasis_uniformity : (𝓤 (α →ᵤ β)).HasBasis (· ∈ 𝓤 β) (UniformFun.gen α β)

views.nl_informal:
The uniformity of `α →ᵤ β` admits the family `{(f, g) | ∀ x, (f x, g x) ∈ V}` for `V ∈ 𝓑` as
a filter basis, for any basis `𝓑` of `𝓤 β` (in the case `𝓑 = (𝓤 β).as_basis` this is true by
definition).
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformFun.hasBasis_uniformity_of_basis {ι : Sort*} {p : ι → Prop} {s : ι → Set (β × β)} (h : (𝓤 β).HasBasis p s) : (𝓤 (α →ᵤ β)).HasBasis p (UniformFun.gen α β ∘ s)

views.nl_informal:
For `f : α →ᵤ β`, `𝓝 f` admits the family `{g | ∀ x, (f x, g x) ∈ V}` for `V ∈ 𝓑` as a filter
basis, for any basis `𝓑` of `𝓤 β`.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformFun.hasBasis_nhds_of_basis (f) {p : ι → Prop} {s : ι → Set (β × β)} (h : HasBasis (𝓤 β) p s) : (𝓝 f).HasBasis p fun i => { g | (f, g) ∈ UniformFun.gen α β (s i) }

views.nl_informal:
For `f : α →ᵤ β`, `𝓝 f` admits the family `{g | ∀ x, (f x, g x) ∈ V}` for `V ∈ 𝓤 β` as a
filter basis.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformFun.hasBasis_nhds (f) : (𝓝 f).HasBasis (fun V => V ∈ 𝓤 β) fun V => { g | (f, g) ∈ UniformFun.gen α β V }

views.nl_informal: Evaluation at a fixed point is uniformly continuous on `α →ᵤ β`.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformFun.uniformContinuous_eval (x : α) : UniformContinuous (Function.eval x ∘ toFun : (α →ᵤ β) → β)

views.nl_informal:
If `u₁` and `u₂` are two uniform structures on `γ` and `u₁ ≤ u₂`, then
`𝒰(α, γ, u₁) ≤ 𝒰(α, γ, u₂)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformFun.mono : Monotone (@UniformFun.uniformSpace α γ)

views.nl_informal:
If `u` is a family of uniform structures on `γ`, then
`𝒰(α, γ, (⨅ i, u i)) = ⨅ i, 𝒰(α, γ, u i)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformFun.iInf_eq {u : ι → UniformSpace γ} : 𝒰(α, γ, (⨅ i, u i)) = ⨅ i, 𝒰(α, γ, u i)

views.nl_informal:
If `u₁` and `u₂` are two uniform structures on `γ`, then
`𝒰(α, γ, u₁ ⊓ u₂) = 𝒰(α, γ, u₁) ⊓ 𝒰(α, γ, u₂)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformFun.inf_eq {u₁ u₂ : UniformSpace γ} : 𝒰(α, γ, u₁ ⊓ u₂) = 𝒰(α, γ, u₁) ⊓ 𝒰(α, γ, u₂)

views.nl_informal:
Post-composition by a uniform inducing function is
a uniform inducing function for the uniform structures of uniform convergence.

More precisely, if `f : γ → β` is uniform inducing,
then `(f ∘ ·) : (α →ᵤ γ) → (α →ᵤ β)` is uniform inducing.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformFun.postcomp_isUniformInducing [UniformSpace γ] {f : γ → β} (hf : IsUniformInducing f) : IsUniformInducing (ofFun ∘ (f ∘ ·) ∘ toFun : (α →ᵤ γ) → α →ᵤ β)

views.nl_informal:
Post-composition by a uniform embedding is
a uniform embedding for the uniform structures of uniform convergence.

More precisely, if `f : γ → β` is a uniform embedding,
then `(f ∘ ·) : (α →ᵤ γ) → (α →ᵤ β)` is a uniform embedding.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformFun.postcomp_isUniformEmbedding [UniformSpace γ] {f : γ → β} (hf : IsUniformEmbedding f) : IsUniformEmbedding (ofFun ∘ (f ∘ ·) ∘ toFun : (α →ᵤ γ) → α →ᵤ β)

views.nl_informal:
If `u` is a uniform structures on `β` and `f : γ → β`, then
`𝒰(α, γ, comap f u) = comap (fun g ↦ f ∘ g) 𝒰(α, γ, u₁)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformFun.comap_eq {f : γ → β} : 𝒰(α, γ, ‹UniformSpace β›.comap f) = 𝒰(α, β, _).comap (f ∘ ·)

views.nl_informal:
Post-composition by a uniformly continuous function is uniformly continuous on `α →ᵤ β`.

More precisely, if `f : γ → β` is uniformly continuous, then `(fun g ↦ f ∘ g) : (α →ᵤ γ) → (α →ᵤ β)`
is uniformly continuous.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformFun.postcomp_uniformContinuous [UniformSpace γ] {f : γ → β} (hf : UniformContinuous f) : UniformContinuous (ofFun ∘ (f ∘ ·) ∘ toFun : (α →ᵤ γ) → α →ᵤ β)

views.nl_informal:
Pre-composition by any function is uniformly continuous for the uniform structures of
uniform convergence.

More precisely, for any `f : γ → α`, the function `(· ∘ f) : (α →ᵤ β) → (γ →ᵤ β)` is uniformly
continuous.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformFun.precomp_uniformContinuous {f : γ → α} : UniformContinuous fun g : α →ᵤ β => ofFun (toFun g ∘ f)

views.nl_informal:
The natural map `UniformFun.toFun` from `α →ᵤ β` to `α → β` is uniformly continuous.

In other words, the uniform structure of uniform convergence is finer than that of pointwise
convergence, aka the product uniform structure.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformFun.uniformContinuous_toFun : UniformContinuous (toFun : (α →ᵤ β) → α → β)

views.nl_informal:
The topology of uniform convergence indeed gives the same notion of convergence as
`TendstoUniformly`.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformFun.tendsto_iff_tendstoUniformly {F : ι → α →ᵤ β} {f : α →ᵤ β} : Tendsto F p (𝓝 f) ↔ TendstoUniformly (toFun ∘ F) (toFun f) p

views.nl_informal:
The set of continuous functions is closed in the uniform convergence topology.
This is a simple wrapper over `TendstoUniformly.continuous`.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformFun.isClosed_setOf_continuous [TopologicalSpace α] : IsClosed {f : α →ᵤ β | Continuous (toFun f)}

views.nl_informal:
For `S : Set α` and `V : Set (β × β)`, we have
`UniformOnFun.gen 𝔖 S V = (S.restrict × S.restrict) ⁻¹' (UniformFun.gen S β V)`.
This is the crucial fact for proving that the family `UniformOnFun.gen S V` for `S ∈ 𝔖` and
`V ∈ 𝓤 β` is indeed a basis for the uniformity `α →ᵤ[𝔖] β` endowed with `𝒱(α, β, 𝔖, uβ)`
the uniform structure of `𝔖`-convergence, as defined in `UniformOnFun.uniformSpace`.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformOnFun.gen_eq_preimage_restrict {𝔖} (S : Set α) (V : Set (β × β)) : UniformOnFun.gen 𝔖 S V = Prod.map (S.restrict ∘ UniformFun.toFun) (S.restrict ∘ UniformFun.toFun) ⁻¹' UniformFun.gen S β V

views.nl_informal: `UniformOnFun.gen` is antitone in the first argument and monotone in the second.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformOnFun.gen_mono {𝔖} {S S' : Set α} {V V' : Set (β × β)} (hS : S' ⊆ S) (hV : V ⊆ V') : UniformOnFun.gen 𝔖 S V ⊆ UniformOnFun.gen 𝔖 S' V'

views.nl_informal:
If `𝔖 : Set (Set α)` is nonempty and directed and `𝓑` is a filter basis on `β × β`, then the
family `UniformOnFun.gen 𝔖 S V` for `S ∈ 𝔖` and `V ∈ 𝓑` is a filter basis on
`(α →ᵤ[𝔖] β) × (α →ᵤ[𝔖] β)`.
We will show in `has_basis_uniformity_of_basis` that, if `𝓑` is a basis for `𝓤 β`, then the
corresponding filter is the uniformity of `α →ᵤ[𝔖] β`.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformOnFun.isBasis_gen (𝔖 : Set (Set α)) (h : 𝔖.Nonempty) (h' : DirectedOn (· ⊆ ·) 𝔖) (𝓑 : FilterBasis <| β × β) : IsBasis (fun SV : Set α × Set (β × β) => SV.1 ∈ 𝔖 ∧ SV.2 ∈ 𝓑) fun SV => UniformOnFun.gen 𝔖 SV.1 SV.2

views.nl_informal:
The topology of `𝔖`-convergence is the infimum, for `S ∈ 𝔖`, of topology induced by the map
of `S.restrict : (α →ᵤ[𝔖] β) → (↥S →ᵤ β)` of restriction to `S`, where `↥S →ᵤ β` is endowed with
the topology of uniform convergence.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformOnFun.topologicalSpace_eq : UniformOnFun.topologicalSpace α β 𝔖 = ⨅ (s : Set α) (_ : s ∈ 𝔖), TopologicalSpace.induced (UniformFun.ofFun ∘ s.restrict ∘ toFun 𝔖) (UniformFun.topologicalSpace s β)

views.nl_informal:
If `𝔖 : Set (Set α)` is nonempty and directed and `𝓑` is a filter basis of `𝓤 β`, then the
uniformity of `α →ᵤ[𝔖] β` admits the family `{(f, g) | ∀ x ∈ S, (f x, g x) ∈ V}` for `S ∈ 𝔖` and
`V ∈ 𝓑` as a filter basis.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformOnFun.hasBasis_uniformity_of_basis (h : 𝔖.Nonempty) (h' : DirectedOn (· ⊆ ·) 𝔖) {p : ι → Prop} {s : ι → Set (β × β)} (hb : HasBasis (𝓤 β) p s) : (𝓤 (α →ᵤ[𝔖] β)).HasBasis (fun Si : Set α × ι => Si.1 ∈ 𝔖 ∧ p Si.2) fun Si => UniformOnFun.gen 𝔖 Si.1 (s Si.2)

views.nl_informal:
If `𝔖 : Set (Set α)` is nonempty and directed, then the uniformity of `α →ᵤ[𝔖] β` admits the
family `{(f, g) | ∀ x ∈ S, (f x, g x) ∈ V}` for `S ∈ 𝔖` and `V ∈ 𝓤 β` as a filter basis.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformOnFun.hasBasis_uniformity (h : 𝔖.Nonempty) (h' : DirectedOn (· ⊆ ·) 𝔖) : (𝓤 (α →ᵤ[𝔖] β)).HasBasis (fun SV : Set α × Set (β × β) => SV.1 ∈ 𝔖 ∧ SV.2 ∈ 𝓤 β) fun SV => UniformOnFun.gen 𝔖 SV.1 SV.2

views.nl_informal:
Let `t i` be a nonempty directed subfamily of `𝔖`
such that every `s ∈ 𝔖` is included in some `t i`.
Let `V` bounded by `p` be a basis of entourages of `β`.

Then `UniformOnFun.gen 𝔖 (t i) (V j)` bounded by `p j` is a basis of entourages of `α →ᵤ[𝔖] β`.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformOnFun.hasBasis_uniformity_of_covering_of_basis {ι ι' : Type*} [Nonempty ι] {t : ι → Set α} {p : ι' → Prop} {V : ι' → Set (β × β)} (ht : ∀ i, t i ∈ 𝔖) (hdir : Directed (· ⊆ ·) t) (hex : ∀ s ∈ 𝔖, ∃ i, s ⊆ t i) (hb : HasBasis (𝓤 β) p V) : (𝓤 (α →ᵤ[𝔖] β)).HasBasis (fun i : ι × ι' ↦ p i.2) fun i ↦ UniformOnFun.gen 𝔖 (t i.1) (V i.2)

views.nl_informal:
If `t n` is a monotone sequence of sets in `𝔖`
such that each `s ∈ 𝔖` is included in some `t n`
and `V n` is an antitone basis of entourages of `β`,
then `UniformOnFun.gen 𝔖 (t n) (V n)` is an antitone basis of entourages of `α →ᵤ[𝔖] β`.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformOnFun.hasAntitoneBasis_uniformity {ι : Type*} [Preorder ι] [IsDirected ι (· ≤ ·)] {t : ι → Set α} {V : ι → Set (β × β)} (ht : ∀ n, t n ∈ 𝔖) (hmono : Monotone t) (hex : ∀ s ∈ 𝔖, ∃ n, s ⊆ t n) (hb : HasAntitoneBasis (𝓤 β) V) : (𝓤 (α →ᵤ[𝔖] β)).HasAntitoneBasis fun n ↦ UniformOnFun.gen 𝔖 (t n) (V n)

views.nl_informal:
For `f : α →ᵤ[𝔖] β`, where `𝔖 : Set (Set α)` is nonempty and directed, `𝓝 f` admits the
family `{g | ∀ x ∈ S, (f x, g x) ∈ V}` for `S ∈ 𝔖` and `V ∈ 𝓑` as a filter basis, for any basis
`𝓑` of `𝓤 β`.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformOnFun.hasBasis_nhds_of_basis (f : α →ᵤ[𝔖] β) (h : 𝔖.Nonempty) (h' : DirectedOn (· ⊆ ·) 𝔖) {p : ι → Prop} {s : ι → Set (β × β)} (hb : HasBasis (𝓤 β) p s) : (𝓝 f).HasBasis (fun Si : Set α × ι => Si.1 ∈ 𝔖 ∧ p Si.2) fun Si => { g | (g, f) ∈ UniformOnFun.gen 𝔖 Si.1 (s Si.2) }

views.nl_informal:
For `f : α →ᵤ[𝔖] β`, where `𝔖 : Set (Set α)` is nonempty and directed, `𝓝 f` admits the
family `{g | ∀ x ∈ S, (f x, g x) ∈ V}` for `S ∈ 𝔖` and `V ∈ 𝓤 β` as a filter basis.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformOnFun.hasBasis_nhds (f : α →ᵤ[𝔖] β) (h : 𝔖.Nonempty) (h' : DirectedOn (· ⊆ ·) 𝔖) : (𝓝 f).HasBasis (fun SV : Set α × Set (β × β) => SV.1 ∈ 𝔖 ∧ SV.2 ∈ 𝓤 β) fun SV => { g | (g, f) ∈ UniformOnFun.gen 𝔖 SV.1 SV.2 }

views.nl_informal:
If `S ∈ 𝔖`, then the restriction to `S` is a uniformly continuous map from `α →ᵤ[𝔖] β` to
`↥S →ᵤ β`.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformOnFun.uniformContinuous_restrict (h : s ∈ 𝔖) : UniformContinuous (UniformFun.ofFun ∘ (s.restrict : (α → β) → s → β) ∘ toFun 𝔖)

views.nl_informal:
Let `u₁`, `u₂` be two uniform structures on `γ` and `𝔖₁ 𝔖₂ : Set (Set α)`. If `u₁ ≤ u₂` and
`𝔖₂ ⊆ 𝔖₁` then `𝒱(α, γ, 𝔖₁, u₁) ≤ 𝒱(α, γ, 𝔖₂, u₂)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformOnFun.mono ⦃u₁ u₂ : UniformSpace γ⦄ (hu : u₁ ≤ u₂) ⦃𝔖₁ 𝔖₂ : Set (Set α)⦄ (h𝔖 : 𝔖₂ ⊆ 𝔖₁) : 𝒱(α, γ, 𝔖₁, u₁) ≤ 𝒱(α, γ, 𝔖₂, u₂)

views.nl_informal:
If `x : α` is in some `S ∈ 𝔖`, then evaluation at `x` is uniformly continuous on
`α →ᵤ[𝔖] β`.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformOnFun.uniformContinuous_eval_of_mem {x : α} (hxs : x ∈ s) (hs : s ∈ 𝔖) : UniformContinuous ((Function.eval x : (α → β) → β) ∘ toFun 𝔖)

views.nl_informal:
If `u` is a family of uniform structures on `γ`, then
`𝒱(α, γ, 𝔖, (⨅ i, u i)) = ⨅ i, 𝒱(α, γ, 𝔖, u i)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformOnFun.iInf_eq {u : ι → UniformSpace γ} : 𝒱(α, γ, 𝔖, ⨅ i, u i) = ⨅ i, 𝒱(α, γ, 𝔖, u i)

views.nl_informal:
If `u₁` and `u₂` are two uniform structures on `γ`, then
`𝒱(α, γ, 𝔖, u₁ ⊓ u₂) = 𝒱(α, γ, 𝔖, u₁) ⊓ 𝒱(α, γ, 𝔖, u₂)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformOnFun.inf_eq {u₁ u₂ : UniformSpace γ} : 𝒱(α, γ, 𝔖, u₁ ⊓ u₂) = 𝒱(α, γ, 𝔖, u₁) ⊓ 𝒱(α, γ, 𝔖, u₂)

views.nl_informal:
If `u` is a uniform structure on `β` and `f : γ → β`, then
`𝒱(α, γ, 𝔖, comap f u) = comap (fun g ↦ f ∘ g) 𝒱(α, γ, 𝔖, u₁)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformOnFun.comap_eq {f : γ → β} : 𝒱(α, γ, 𝔖, ‹UniformSpace β›.comap f) = 𝒱(α, β, 𝔖, _).comap (f ∘ ·)

views.nl_informal:
Post-composition by a uniformly continuous function is uniformly continuous for the
uniform structures of `𝔖`-convergence.

More precisely, if `f : γ → β` is uniformly continuous, then
`(fun g ↦ f ∘ g) : (α →ᵤ[𝔖] γ) → (α →ᵤ[𝔖] β)` is uniformly continuous.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformOnFun.postcomp_uniformContinuous [UniformSpace γ] {f : γ → β} (hf : UniformContinuous f) : UniformContinuous (ofFun 𝔖 ∘ (f ∘ ·) ∘ toFun 𝔖)

views.nl_informal:
Post-composition by a uniform inducing is a uniform inducing for the
uniform structures of `𝔖`-convergence.

More precisely, if `f : γ → β` is a uniform inducing, then
`(fun g ↦ f ∘ g) : (α →ᵤ[𝔖] γ) → (α →ᵤ[𝔖] β)` is a uniform inducing.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformOnFun.postcomp_isUniformInducing [UniformSpace γ] {f : γ → β} (hf : IsUniformInducing f) : IsUniformInducing (ofFun 𝔖 ∘ (f ∘ ·) ∘ toFun 𝔖)

views.nl_informal:
Post-composition by a uniform embedding is a uniform embedding for the
uniform structures of `𝔖`-convergence.

More precisely, if `f : γ → β` is a uniform embedding, then
`(fun g ↦ f ∘ g) : (α →ᵤ[𝔖] γ) → (α →ᵤ[𝔖] β)` is a uniform embedding.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformOnFun.postcomp_isUniformEmbedding [UniformSpace γ] {f : γ → β} (hf : IsUniformEmbedding f) : IsUniformEmbedding (ofFun 𝔖 ∘ (f ∘ ·) ∘ toFun 𝔖)

views.nl_informal:
Let `f : γ → α`, `𝔖 : Set (Set α)`, `𝔗 : Set (Set γ)`, and assume that `∀ T ∈ 𝔗, f '' T ∈ 𝔖`.
Then, the function `(fun g ↦ g ∘ f) : (α →ᵤ[𝔖] β) → (γ →ᵤ[𝔗] β)` is uniformly continuous.

Note that one can easily see that assuming `∀ T ∈ 𝔗, ∃ S ∈ 𝔖, f '' T ⊆ S` would work too, but
we will get this for free when we prove that `𝒱(α, β, 𝔖, uβ) = 𝒱(α, β, 𝔖', uβ)` where `𝔖'` is the
***noncovering*** bornology generated by `𝔖`.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformOnFun.precomp_uniformContinuous {𝔗 : Set (Set γ)} {f : γ → α} (hf : MapsTo (f '' ·) 𝔗 𝔖) : UniformContinuous fun g : α →ᵤ[𝔖] β => ofFun 𝔗 (toFun 𝔖 g ∘ f)

views.nl_informal: If `𝔖` covers `α`, then the topology of `𝔖`-convergence is T₂.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformOnFun.t2Space_of_covering [T2Space β] (h : ⋃₀ 𝔖 = univ) : T2Space (α →ᵤ[𝔖] β)

views.nl_informal: The restriction map from `α →ᵤ[𝔖] β` to `⋃₀ 𝔖 → β` is uniformly continuous.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformOnFun.uniformContinuous_restrict_toFun : UniformContinuous ((⋃₀ 𝔖).restrict ∘ toFun 𝔖 : (α →ᵤ[𝔖] β) → ⋃₀ 𝔖 → β)

views.nl_informal:
If `𝔖` covers `α`, the natural map `UniformOnFun.toFun` from `α →ᵤ[𝔖] β` to `α → β` is
uniformly continuous.

In other words, if `𝔖` covers `α`, then the uniform structure of `𝔖`-convergence is finer than
that of pointwise convergence.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformOnFun.uniformContinuous_toFun (h : ⋃₀ 𝔖 = univ) : UniformContinuous (toFun 𝔖 : (α →ᵤ[𝔖] β) → α → β)

views.nl_informal:
If `f : α →ᵤ[𝔖] β` is continuous at `x` and `x` admits a neighbourhood `V ∈ 𝔖`,
then evaluation of `g : α →ᵤ[𝔖] β` at `y : α` is continuous in `(g, y)` at `(f, x)`.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformOnFun.continuousAt_eval₂ [TopologicalSpace α] {f : α →ᵤ[𝔖] β} {x : α} (h𝔖 : ∃ V ∈ 𝔖, V ∈ 𝓝 x) (hc : ContinuousAt (toFun 𝔖 f) x) : ContinuousAt (fun fx : (α →ᵤ[𝔖] β) × α ↦ toFun 𝔖 fx.1 fx.2) (f, x)

views.nl_informal:
If each point of `α` admits a neighbourhood `V ∈ 𝔖`,
then the evaluation of `f : α →ᵤ[𝔖] β` at `x : α` is continuous in `(f, x)`
on the set of `(f, x)` such that `f` is continuous at `x`.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformOnFun.continuousOn_eval₂ [TopologicalSpace α] (h𝔖 : ∀ x, ∃ V ∈ 𝔖, V ∈ 𝓝 x) : ContinuousOn (fun fx : (α →ᵤ[𝔖] β) × α ↦ toFun 𝔖 fx.1 fx.2) {fx | ContinuousAt (toFun 𝔖 fx.1) fx.2}

views.nl_informal:
Convergence in the topology of `𝔖`-convergence means uniform convergence on `S` (in the sense
of `TendstoUniformlyOn`) for all `S ∈ 𝔖`.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformOnFun.tendsto_iff_tendstoUniformlyOn {F : ι → α →ᵤ[𝔖] β} {f : α →ᵤ[𝔖] β} : Tendsto F p (𝓝 f) ↔ ∀ s ∈ 𝔖, TendstoUniformlyOn (toFun 𝔖 ∘ F) (toFun 𝔖 f) p s

views.nl_informal:
Suppose that the topology on `α` is defined by its restrictions to the sets of `𝔖`.

Then the set of continuous functions is closed
in the topology of uniform convergence on the sets of `𝔖`.
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformOnFun.isClosed_setOf_continuous [TopologicalSpace α] (h : IsCoherentWith 𝔖) : IsClosed {f : α →ᵤ[𝔖] β | Continuous (toFun 𝔖 f)}

views.nl_informal: Composing on the left by a uniformly continuous function preserves uniform convergence
views.lean_signature: theorem UniformContinuousOn.comp_tendstoUniformly (s : Set β) (F : ι → α → β) (f : α → β) (hF : ∀ i x, F i x ∈ s) (hf : ∀ x, f x ∈ s) {g : β → γ} (hg : UniformContinuousOn g s) (h : TendstoUniformly F f p) : TendstoUniformly (fun i x => g (F i x)) (fun x => g (f x)) p

views.nl_informal:
If the domain of a `IsUniformInducing` map `f` is a T₀ space, then `f` is injective,
hence it is a `IsUniformEmbedding`.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsUniformInducing.isUniformEmbedding [T0Space α] {f : α → β} (hf : IsUniformInducing f) : IsUniformEmbedding f

views.nl_informal:
If a map `f : α → β` sends any two distinct points to point that are **not** related by a fixed
`s ∈ 𝓤 β`, then `f` is uniform inducing with respect to the discrete uniformity on `α`:
the preimage of `𝓤 β` under `Prod.map f f` is the principal filter generated by the diagonal in
`α × α`.
views.lean_signature: theorem comap_uniformity_of_spaced_out {α} {f : α → β} {s : Set (β × β)} (hs : s ∈ 𝓤 β) (hf : Pairwise fun x y => (f x, f y) ∉ s) : comap (Prod.map f f) (𝓤 β) = 𝓟 idRel

views.nl_informal:
If a map `f : α → β` sends any two distinct points to point that are **not** related by a fixed
`s ∈ 𝓤 β`, then `f` is a uniform embedding with respect to the discrete uniformity on `α`.
views.lean_signature: theorem isUniformEmbedding_of_spaced_out {α} {f : α → β} {s : Set (β × β)} (hs : s ∈ 𝓤 β) (hf : Pairwise fun x y => (f x, f y) ∉ s) : @IsUniformEmbedding α β ⊥ ‹_› f

views.nl_informal: A set is complete iff its image under a uniform inducing map is complete.
views.lean_signature: theorem isComplete_image_iff {m : α → β} {s : Set α} (hm : IsUniformInducing m) : IsComplete (m '' s) ↔ IsComplete s

views.nl_informal:
If `f : X → Y` is an `IsUniformInducing` map, the image `f '' s` of a set `s` is complete
if and only if `s` is complete.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsUniformInducing.isComplete_iff {f : α → β} {s : Set α} (hf : IsUniformInducing f) : IsComplete (f '' s) ↔ IsComplete s

views.nl_informal:
If `f : X → Y` is an `IsUniformEmbedding`, the image `f '' s` of a set `s` is complete
if and only if `s` is complete.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsUniformEmbedding.isComplete_iff {f : α → β} {s : Set α} (hf : IsUniformEmbedding f) : IsComplete (f '' s) ↔ IsComplete s

views.nl_informal: Sets of a subtype are complete iff their image under the coercion is complete.
views.lean_signature: theorem Subtype.isComplete_iff {p : α → Prop} {s : Set { x // p x }} : IsComplete s ↔ IsComplete ((↑) '' s : Set α)

views.nl_informal:
If `f` is a surjective uniform inducing map,
then its domain is a complete space iff its codomain is a complete space.
See also `_root_.completeSpace_congr` for a version that assumes `f` to be an equivalence.
views.lean_signature: theorem IsUniformInducing.completeSpace_congr {f : α → β} (hf : IsUniformInducing f) (hsurj : f.Surjective) : CompleteSpace α ↔ CompleteSpace β

views.nl_informal: A uniform space with a nonarchimedean uniformity is zero-dimensional.
views.lean_signature: theorem TopologicalSpace.isTopologicalBasis_clopens : TopologicalSpace.IsTopologicalBasis {s : Set X | IsClopen s}

views.nl_informal: The projection on the base of a vector bundle created from core is continuous
views.lean_signature: theorem VectorBundleCore.continuous_proj : Continuous Z.proj

views.nl_informal: The projection on the base of a vector bundle created from core is an open map
views.lean_signature: theorem VectorBundleCore.isOpenMap_proj : IsOpenMap Z.proj

views.nl_informal:
Make a `VectorBundle` from a `VectorPrebundle`.  Concretely this means
that, given a `VectorPrebundle` structure for a sigma-type `E` -- which consists of a
number of "pretrivializations" identifying parts of `E` with product spaces `U × F` -- one
establishes that for the topology constructed on the sigma-type using
`VectorPrebundle.totalSpaceTopology`, these "pretrivializations" are actually
"trivializations" (i.e., homeomorphisms with respect to the constructed topology).

views.nl_informal: Rewrite `ContinuousLinearMap.inCoordinates` using continuous linear equivalences.
views.lean_signature: theorem ContinuousLinearMap.inCoordinates_eq {x₀ x : B} {y₀ y : B'} {ϕ : E x →SL[σ] E' y} (hx : x ∈ (trivializationAt F E x₀).baseSet) (hy : y ∈ (trivializationAt F' E' y₀).baseSet) : inCoordinates F E F' E' x₀ x y₀ y ϕ = ((trivializationAt F' E' y₀).continuousLinearEquivAt 𝕜₂ y hy : E' y →L[𝕜₂] F').comp (ϕ.comp <| (((trivializationAt F E x₀).continuousLinearEquivAt 𝕜₁ x hx).symm : F →L[𝕜₁] E x))

views.nl_informal: Rewrite `ContinuousLinearMap.inCoordinates` in a `VectorBundleCore`.
views.lean_signature: theorem VectorBundleCore.inCoordinates_eq {ι ι'} (Z : VectorBundleCore 𝕜₁ B F ι) (Z' : VectorBundleCore 𝕜₂ B' F' ι') {x₀ x : B} {y₀ y : B'} (ϕ : F →SL[σ] F') (hx : x ∈ Z.baseSet (Z.indexAt x₀)) (hy : y ∈ Z'.baseSet (Z'.indexAt y₀)) : inCoordinates F Z.Fiber F' Z'.Fiber x₀ x y₀ y ϕ = (Z'.coordChange (Z'.indexAt y) (Z'.indexAt y₀) y).comp (ϕ.comp <| Z.coordChange (Z.indexAt x₀) (Z.indexAt x) x)
